description.2: PRECIPITATION AND SURFACE WATER FLOWS ARE PROJECTED TO BECOME MORE VARIABLE WITH CONTINUING GLOBAL WARMING, RESULTING IN MORE SEVERE WET AND DRY EVENTS WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR FLOODING AND DROUGHTS. ADDITIONAL WARMING IS PROJECTED TO AMPLIFY THE LOSS OF SEASONAL SNOW COVER FURTHER AND INTENSIFY WATER WITHDRAWALS FOR IRRIGATION IN AGRICULTURAL AREAS. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR IMPROVED PREDICTIONS AND PROJECTIONS OF HOW CLIMATE CHANGE WILL AFFECT NATIONAL WATER AVAILABILITY, QUALITY, AND RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH HYDROLOGICAL HAZARDS ON REGIONAL SCALES THROUGH THE NEXT SEVERAL DECADES (THE 2020S THROUGH 2050S). THIS PERIOD COVERS THE LIFESPAN OF MANY MAJOR PIECES OF INFRASTRUCTURE, THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT, AND POLICY GOALS FOR REACHING CARBON NEUTRALITY.
description.4: PURPOSE:THE PURPOSE OF THIS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT ALGORITHMS, ARCHITECTURES, AND SYSTEMS THAT WILL PROVIDE A FLEXIBLE, SCALABLE, AND USER-FRIENDLY RECORD LINKAGE TECHNOLOGY PLATFORM AS WELL AS A SANDBOX OF MULTIPLE LARGE-SCALE, PUBLIC-DOMAIN DATASETS THAT PROVIDE A BASIS FOR SHARED EVALUATION OF METHODOLOGY AND TECHNOLOGY FOR USERS FROM DIFFERENT INSTITUTIONS.ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED:SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT AND DEPLOYMENT OF AN OPEN-SOURCE RECORD LINKAGE PLATFORM AND A DATABASE OF MULTIPLE LARGE-SCALE, PUBLIC-DOMAIN DATASETS TO USE FOR EVALUATING RECORD LINKAGE TECHNOLOGICAL AND METHODOLOGICAL ADVANCES TO A PUBLIC REPOSITORY ACCOMPANIED BY NECESSARY DOCUMENTATION REGARDING USABILITY. SCHOLARLY WORK REGARDING RECORD LINKAGE TECHNOLOGIES AND SIMULATED DATA CREATION. SCHOLARLY WORK WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO JOURNAL ARTICLES, CONFERENCE AND WORKSHOP PRESENTATIONS, AND ACADEMIC COURSE MATERIALS.EXPECTED OUTCOMES:WORK PERFORMED WILL ADVANCE THE ABILITY TO EXPERIMENT WITH RECORD LINKAGE METHODOLOGIES AND TECHNOLOGIES BY PROVIDING AN EXPERIMENTAL PLATFORM AND LARGE SIMULATED DATA SET. THE AWARD RECIPIENTS WILL RELEASE EACH OF THE DEVELOPMENT TOOLS EARLY IN THE AWARD PERIOD AND THEN INCREMENTALLY IMPROVE BOTH IN CONVERSATION WITH THE CENSUS BUREAU AND OTHER USERS TO BETTER MEET THE NEEDS OF THE ENTIRE RESEARCH COMMUNITY WITH THE FINAL PRODUCT.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES:RECORD LINKAGE PRACTITIONERS AND RESEARCHERS NEEDING TO DEPLOY RECORD LINKAGE TO ADVANCE THEIR WORK IN AREAS SUCH AS SOCIOLOGY, ECONOMICS, AND PUBLIC HEALTH ANALYSIS WILL BENEFIT FROM THESE TOOLS AS THEY WILL ENABLE COLLABORATION ACROSS INSTITUTIONS, WHICH HAS BEEN HAMPERED BY THE INABILITY TO SHARE PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL LARGE DATA SETS OUTSIDE OF SPECIFIC PROTECTED RESEARCH ENCLAVES. THESE PRACTITIONERS WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM THE MODULAR PIPELINE'S ABILITY TO ENABLE RESEARCH ON SPECIFIC ASPECTS OF RECORD LINKAGE WITHIN THE INFRASTRUCTURE OF THE MODULAR RECORD LINKAGE PLATFORM. THIS BENEFIT OCCURS BECAUSE THE PLATFORM WILL DECREASE THE NECESSARY INVESTMENT IN CODE WRITING AND DEVELOPMENT FOR THESE RESEARCH PROJECTS.SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES:THE RECIPIENT WILL SUB-AWARD FUNDS AS NEEDED TO PROCURE ACADEMIC AND TECHNICAL RESOURCES WITH RELEVANT SPECIALIZATIONS.

DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL IS TO UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF STATEWIDE LOCAL ENERGY ACTION NETWORKS (LEANS) IN SUPPORTING AND ADVANCING RENEWABLE ENERGY AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY (REE) IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, WITH COMMUNITY-ENGAGED STATE AND LOCAL PILOT PROJECTS FOCUSING ON INDIGENOUS, RURAL, AND LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES. ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL: 1) IDENTIFY AND COMPARE BARRIERS, OPPORTUNITIES, DECISION DRIVERS OF RENEWABLE ENERGY AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY (REE) ADOPTION FOR INDIVIDUALS, COMMUNITY, AND GOVERNMENT OF UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES; 2) EXAMINE BENEFITS, CHALLENGES, AND EFFECTIVENESS OF STATEWIDE LOCAL ENERGY ACTION NETWORKS (LEANS) IN SUPPORTING REE ADOPTION IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES; AND 3) EXAMINE THE ROLE OF TARGETED INTERVENTIONS (CAPACITY, EDUCATION, OWNERSHIP) IN ADVANCING REE AWARENESS, ENGAGEMENT, AND ADOPTION IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. 

SUBRECIPIENT:SUBAWARDEE PENOBSCOT NATION (PN) TRIBAL GOVERNMENT WILL HAVE A SUSTAINABLE ENERGY COORDINATOR TO SERVE ALL WABANAKI TRIBES, BUILD CAPACITY AND ACCELERATE IMPLEMENTATION OF LOCAL ENERGY SOLUTIONS, OVERSEE PROJECT DEVELOPMENT, ENGAGE COMMUNITY MEMBERS, AND ENGAGE IN RESEARCH ACTIVITIES.  ($307,007)
OUTCOMES:ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE COMMUNITY CO-CREATED RESEARCH INSTRUMENTS AND RESEARCH PRODUCTS INCLUDING REPORTS, BRIEFINGS, ARTICLES, AND PRESENTATIONS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF BARRIERS, OPPORTUNITIES, DECISION DRIVERS RELATED TO SUSTAINABLE ENERGY ADOPTION IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES; EFFECTIVE METHODS FOR ENGAGEMENT AND CO-PRODUCTION OF KNOWLEDGE WITH COMMUNITIES; BEST PRACTICES FOR STATE NETWORKS AND STATE POLICY/PROGRAM DESIGN TO SUPPORT LOCAL SUSTAINABLE ENERGY ADOPTION. ADDITIONAL OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED ADOPTION AND DIFFUSION OF SUSTAINABLE ENERGY IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS IMPROVED RISK MANAGEMENT FOR UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN CLIMATE AND ENERGY RESILIENCE. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE TEN UNDERSERVED INDIGENOUS, LOW-INCOME, AND/OR RURAL MAINE COMMUNITIES, AS WELL AS SIMILAR COMMUNITIES IN OTHER STATES.

BIPARTISAN INFRASTRUCTURE LAW (BIL) - CARBON-STORING INSULATION MANUFACTURING FACILITY IN TEXAS STATE

THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ESTABLISH A 83,000 SQUARE FOOT PRODUCTION FACILITY IN TEXAS TO PRODUCE AN ADVANCED FORM OF CELLULOSE INSULATION FROM RECYCLED CARDBOARD.  THIS INSULATION IS FOR RESIDENTIAL RETROFIT AND NEW CONSTRUCTION APPLICATIONS. THE PRODUCTION FACILITY WILL PROVIDE REGIONAL ACCESS TO A MARKET-READY, DOMESTICALLY SOURCED, LOW-CARBON BUILDING MATERIAL, ADDRESS EMERGING GAPS IN THE DOMESTIC CELLULOSE INSULATION SUPPLY CHAIN, AND REDUCE GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) EMISSIONS BY ENABLING REGIONAL ADOPTION OF A CARBON-NEGATIVE INSULATION SYSTEM.

description.10: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE BALTIMORE CITY DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS (DPW) FOR THE YH20+ PROGRAM DESIGNED TO PROVIDE GREEN JOBS TRAINING TO THE CITY'S YOUTH RELATED PRIMARILY TO THE PROVISION OF SAFE DRINKING WATER.  THE PROGRAM WILL BE EXPANDED TO ADDRESS AND REDUCE OTHER COMMON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES SEEN THROUGHOUT BALTIMORE'S VULNERABLE COMMUNITIES BY STRENGTHENING THE CITY'S YOUTH WORKFORCE THROUGH ON-THE-JOB TRAINING.  THERE WILL BE TWO SOURCES OF FUNDS FOR THIS AWARD - $100,000 FROM THE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN TO FUND ACTIVITIES SPECIFICALLY RELATED TO THE SAFE DRINKING WATER ACT, SECTION 1442(C)(3) AND $100,000 FROM THE ANNUAL APPROPRIATION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE (EJ) TO FUND ACTIVITIES RELATED TO THE: 1) SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL ACT, SECTION 8001(A); 2) CLEAN WATER ACT: SECTION.104(B)(3); AND 3) FEDERAL INSECTICIDE, FUNGICIDE, AND RODENTICIDE ACT, SECTION 20(A).  PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE TRAINING OF YH20+ PROG
description.11: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE CITY OF HARTFORD, CONNECTICUT TO CONDUCT AN INNOVATIVE, RESIDENT-DRIVEN AND RESULTS-ORIENTED STRATEGY TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF LOW INCOME AND MINORITY RESIDENTS REACHED THROUGH A PUBLIC OUTREACH CAMPAIGN ON INDOOR AIR QUALITY.  ADDITIONALLY, AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS TRAINED WILL ADDRESS RESIDENT EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS WHICH CAN CONTRIBUTE TO A DECLINE IN THE INCIDENCE OF ASTHMA-RELATED HOSPITAL VISITS.  ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE: 1) DOCUMENTING PREFERENCES FOR RECEIVING AND/OR ACCESSING ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE INFORMATION INCLUDING CAPACITY TO USE TECHNOLOGY-BASED SOLUTIONS, 2) HOLDING A CIVIC HACKATHON (I.E. EVENT THAT SPARKS CIVIC ENGAGEMENT BY BRINGING TOGETHER COMMUNITY ORGANIZERS WITH SOFTWARE DESIGNERS AND DEVELOPERS) TO IDENTIFY INNOVATIVE, RESIDENT-ORIENTED HIGH-TECH SOLUTIONS AND PROTOTYPES TO SOLVE COMMUNITY NEEDS; AND 3) DEVELOPING TRAINING
description.12: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE CITY OF MADISON, WI TO CARRY OUT A PUBLIC EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAM, INTERVENE AGAINST COVID-19, TO ADDRESS THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND RESPIRATORY HEALTH IMPACTS OF COVID-19 (AN AIRBORNE CONTAMINANT) ON LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES AND COMMUNITIES OF COLOR IN THE CITY. THE KEY OBJECTIVE OF THE PROGRAM IS TO ENCOURAGE COMMUNITY-BASED KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER OF COVID-19 RISK FACTORS, COVID-19 PREVENTION PRACTICES, INTERVENTIONS, AND COMMUNITY RESOURCES.  THE PROGRAM WILL ALSO EDUCATE RESIDENTS ON THE NEXUS BETWEEN COVID-19 AND AIR-RELATED HEALTH CONCERNS WITHIN THESE COMMUNITIES.  ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE: 1) CREATION OF TRAINING VIDEOS AND WRITTEN TRAINING MATERIALS, 2) DIRECT COMMUNITY OUTREACH, RECRUITMENT, AND TRAINING; AND 3) COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS THAT WILL CREATE AND DISSEMINATE LOCAL POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS ADDRESSING THE INTERSECTION OF COVID-19 AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE. description.13: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE CITY OF MILWAUKEE, WI TO COORDINATE THE HEALTHY PEOPLE, HOMES AND NEIGHBORHOODS CAMPAIGN TO CONDUCT OUTREACH AND EDUCATION TO PREDOMINATELY AFRICAN AMERICAN AND LATINX NEIGHBORHOODS FOCUSED ON INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND THE ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS OF URBAN AGRICULTURE.  THE KEY OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO HELP NEIGHBORHOODS TAKE COLLECTIVE ACTION TO IMPROVE ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AT THE NEIGHBORHOOD LEVEL.  ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE: 1) MOBILE RESOURCE TEAMS OF COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS (CHWS) DISTRIBUTING INDOOR AIR QUALITY RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH EDUCATION TO RESIDENTS OF UNDERSERVED NEIGHBORHOODS, 2) DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF A HEALTHY HOMES RESOURCE GUIDE, 3) DEVELOPING AN ECO NEIGHBORHOODS TOOLKIT, AND 4) CONDUCTING COMMUNITY SKILL-BUILDING WORKSHOPS ON URBAN GARDENING AND ITS POSITIVE IMPACT ON LOCAL AIR QUALITY, EXPOSURE TO GREEN JOB OPPORTUNITIES, AND HEALTHY HOMES. description.14: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE MASSACHUSETTS DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH'S (MDPH) ASTHMA PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAM (APCP) TO IMPROVE ASTHMA OUTCOMES IN SEVERAL UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN MASSACHUSETTS THAT ARE THE MOST INEQUITABLY BURDENED BY ENVIRONMENTAL HARMS, AIR POLLUTION, SUBSTANDARD HOUSING, ASTHMA, AND COVID-19.  THROUGH THIS FUNDING, MDPH WILL CONDUCT THE MASSACHUSETTS ASTHMA HOME VISITING COVID-19 ADAPTATION PROJECT. THE PRIMARY ACTIVITIES OF THIS COMMUNITY-INFORMED PROJECT INCLUDE: 1) MEANINGFUL COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT; 2) THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER (CHW) ASTHMA LEARNING COMMUNITY (LC), INCLUDING ACCESS TO CHW MENTORSHIP; 3) A RACIAL JUSTICE REFRAMING OF THE APCP'S COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER PEDIATRIC ASTHMA HOME VISITING PROGRAM PROTOCOL MANUAL AND PROGRAM SUMMARY; AND 4) A RACIAL JUSTICE REFRAMING OF THE ESTABLISHED APCP CHW AND CHW SUPERVISOR ASTHMA HOME VISITING TRAININGS, CONTINUED DE
description.15: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE HOUSING AUTHORITY OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES (HACLA) TO DEVELOP A COMMUNITY HEALTH OUTREACH PUBLIC EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAM BENEFITING THE SECOND LARGEST PUBLIC HOUSING DEVELOPMENT IN THE US. THERE ARE SEVERAL PROJECT ACTIVITIES FROM HACLA AND PARTNERING ORGANIZATIONS. LOS ANGELES DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH (LADPH) AND THE UNIVERSITY OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA (USC) WILL TRAIN COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS (CHW) ON IDENTIFYING RESPIRATORY ILLNESSES CAUSED OR EXACERBATED BY AIR POLLUTION AMONG RESIDENTS AND INFORM THEM OF THE LATEST INFORMATION ON COVID-19 AND ITS PREVENTION AND TREATMENT. CAREER EXPANSION WILL DELIVER OSHA OUTREACH TRAINING CERTIFICATION ENABLING CHWS AND COMMUNITY COACHES TO IDENTIFY INDOOR HEALTH HAZARDS. THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA LOS ANGELES DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH SCIENCES GRADUATE STUDENTS WILL ASSIST HACLA STAFF IN COORDINATION OF OUTREACH AND EDUCATION.
description.16: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE LOUISIANA DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY (LDEQ) TO ENHANCE TWO MOBILE AIR MONITORING STATIONS, NOT CURRENTLY IN USE FOR THIS PROJECT, FOR DEPLOYMENT TO UNDERSERVED, MAJORITY MINORITY AREAS WITHIN THE STATE.  THESE TEMPORARILY LOCATED COMMUNITY (TLC) AIR MONITORS COLLECT AMBIENT AIR QUALITY DATA IN NEIGHBORHOODS USING EPA-APPROVED METHODS AND PROTOCOLS.  THE DATA WILL BE COLLECTED, ARCHIVED, AND RELAYED TO THE LDEQ WEBSITE.  SPECIFIC PROJECT ACTIVITIES ARE AS FOLLOWS: 1) ACQUIRE, INSTALL, AND CERTIFY NECESSARY EQUIPMENT FOR THE TWO MOBILE STATIONS, 2) DEVELOP/RENEW PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE COMMUNITY, INDUSTRY AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT CHOSEN FOR MONITORING TO DETERMINE MONITORING CONCERNS, NEEDS AND SITE LOCATION, 3) NEGOTIATE SITE ACCESS AGREEMENT; DEVELOP SITE (GROUND COVER, ELECTRICITY, FENCING, ETC.), 4) INSTALL MONITORING SITE, CERTIFY AND COMMISSION ALL EQUIPMENT, BEGIN STANDARD MONITOR

DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT AIMS TO USE A COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY APPROACH TO INVOLVE THE LOCAL UNDERSERVED COMMUNITY IN KANSAS CITY, MO IN IDENTIFYING WANTS AND NEEDS OF NEARBY PARK AMENITIES TO REDUCE FLOODING AND INCREASE WATER RETENTION BY CREATING A STRATEGIC PLAN, WHILE EDUCATING THE YOUTH ABOUT CLIMATE CHANGE, WATER QUALITY, ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, AND ADVOCATING FOR CHANGE IN THEIR COMMUNITY. YOUTH WILL ASSIST IN DESIGNING THE GREEN SPACE ON UNITY CAMPUS AND PRESENT THEIR RESULTS TO THE PROJECT LEADERSHIP TEAM AND OTHER PARTNERS AND LOCAL COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS.ACTIVITIES:THE RECIPIENT WILL FIRST COORDINATE WITH PARTNERING ORGANIZATIONS TO: DEVELOP MEMORANDUMS OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN PARTNERING ORGANIZATIONS, CONDUCT REGULAR MEETINGS TO ENSURE PROGRAM GOALS, ASSESS PROGRAM CHALLENGES AND PROGRESS, AND PROBLEM SOLVE ANY ISSUES.
THE COMMUNITY, WITH THE ASSISTANCE FROM ALL PARTNERS WILL LEAD THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STRATEGIC PLAN FOR PARK EQUITY IN KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI. 
THEN THE RECIPIENT WILL WORK WITH AT LEAST 20 YOUTH PARTICIPANTS WHO WILL COMPLETE A SIX-WEEK COURSE WITH GUEST SPEAKERS WHO ARE EXPERTS IN AREAS SUCH AS LANDSCAPE DESIGN, GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE AND WATER RETENTION/RAIN GARDENS, WALK AUDITS, AND OTHER RELATED AREAS GUIDED LESSONS, AND WORK TO CREATE REDESIGN PLANS FOR THE UNITY CAMPUS.
USING INFORMATION ON THE PARK AND WALK AUDITS, THE COMMUNITY, AND STAFF WILL LEAD YOUTH PARTICIPANTS IN REDESIGNING THE CAMPUS TO FACILITATE THE DESIGN AN IDEAL GREEN SPACE ON UNITY CAMPUS THEN PRESENT FINDINGS FROM THEIR PARK AUDITS AND IDEAL PARK CREATIONS TO UNI LEADERSHIP TEAM. 
THE DESIGN WILL FOCUS ON AMENITIES THAT CREATE A SENSE OF COMMUNITY, INCREASE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND INCREASE RETENTION OF STORM WATER TO REDUCE FLOODING IN THE LOCAL NEIGHBORHOODS.
SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT COMPLETION OF THESE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES WILL YIELD THE FOLLOWING EXPECTED OUTCOMES:
1.	INCREASED COMMUNITY CAPACITY: WE EXPECT THAT THIS PROJECT WILL LEAD TO SUSTAINED PARTNERSHIPS TO REDUCE ENVIRONMENTAL INEQUALITIES IN KANSAS CITY, SPECIFICALLY THE WENDELL PHILLIPS NEIGHBORHOOD THROUGH MEETINGS AND EVENTS BETWEEN THE NEIGHBORHOOD, THE YOUTH AND OTHER PROJECT PARTNERS.
2.	CHANGES TO THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT: WE EXPECT IMPROVEMENTS TO THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT, SPECIFICALLY, IMPROVING PARK INFRASTRUCTURE THROUGH SUSTAINED COMMUNITY INPUT AND YOUTH LED PARK PLANNING DESIGNS TO HELP WITH WATER RETENTION.
3.	TRAINED YOUTH LEADERS: WE EXPECT THAT YOUTH WILL BE ENGAGED AND EMPOWERED TO CREATE CHANGE THAT IMPROVES THE LIVES OF THEIR COMMUNITY THROUGH THEIR INCREASE EDUCATION ABOUT ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, GREEN SPACE, WATER QUALITY AND PARK DESIGN.
description.18: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN (ARP) FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO DEVELOP A HOUSING INTERVENTION PROGRAM FOCUSED ON INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND HEALTH CONCERNS IN UNDERSERVED AND VULNERABLE FORT COLLINS, COLORADO COMMUNITY MEMBERS. THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED IN THIS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT ARE TO ENGAGE UNDERSERVED AND VULNERABLE COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND IDENTIFY NEEDS RELATED TO A HOME'S INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND ENERGY USE, ASSESS EXISTING CAPABILITIES, GAPS, BARRIERS AND BEST PRACTICES IN EXISTING HEALTHY HOUSING PROGRAMS, UPDATE EXISTING PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION PLANS AND DEVELOP NEW HOME ASSESSMENT TOOLS AND PILOT IMPLEMENTATION.
description.19:
DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT AIMS TO USE A COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY APPROACH TO IDENTIFY WANTS AND NEEDS OF LOCAL UNDERSERVED COMMUNITY IN KANSAS CITY, MO THROUGH LITTER CLEAN-UPS, CONSERVING ECOSYSTEMS, WHILE EDUCATING COMMUNITY MEMBERS ON  GREEN PRACTICES, PLACING RAIN BARRELS THROUGHOUT HOMES, AND ENGAGING VOLUNTEERS THROUGH ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND ACTIONS IN LEADING CHANGES IN THEIR COMMUNITIES.

ACTIVITIES:THE RECIPIENT WILL FIRST COORDINATE WITH PARTNERING ORGANIZATIONS FOCUSING ON SERVING AND EMPOWERING KANSAS CITY COMMUNITIES IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF HEALTHY GREEN AND PRODUCTIVE TREES. RECIPIENT WILL PROVIDE KNOWLEDGEABLE AND WILLING WORKERS TO AN INDUSTRY RESPONSIBLE FOR QUALITY MAINTENANCE OF KANSAS CITY'S URBAN FOREST CANOPY WITH THE RECOMMENDATION OF IMPROVED MAINTENANCE AND DEVELOPMENT OF KANSAS CITY'S URBAN FOREST CANOPY.  THE RECIPIENT WILL EQUIP WORKERS FOR EMPLOYMENT IN AN INDUSTRY THAT HAS DEMAND FOR KNOWLEDGEABLE AND WILLING WORKERS. DEVELOP POSITIVE ENVIRONMENTAL ATTITUDES IN PARTICIPANTS SUCH AS TO ENCOURAGE INDIVIDUAL ADVOCACY ON BEHALF OF URBAN FORESTS.  THE RECIPIENT WILL WORK WITH AT PARTICIPANTS WHO WILL COMPLETE A SIX MONTH COURSE WITH GUEST SPEAKERS WHO ARE EXPERTS IN AREAS SUCH AS GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE, WATER RETENTION, AND URBAN FOREST CANOPY. BUILD A VIABLE, REPLICABLE JOB TRAINING MODEL FOR URBAN NEIGHBORHOODS, TO IMPROVE LOCAL NEIGHBORHOOD PHYSICAL INFRASTRUCTURE AND TO CREATE A SUCCESSFUL LOCAL 'GREEN JOBS' WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM.  THE DESIGN WILL FOCUS ON AMENITIES THAT CREATE A SENSE OF COMMUNITY AND INCREASE RETENTION OF FOREST CANOPY TO REDUCE FLOODING IN THE LOCAL NEIGHBORHOODS.

SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT COMPLETION OF THESE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES WILL YIELD THE FOLLOWING EXPECTED OUTCOMES: 1. WILL HIGHLY PUBLICIZE PROGRAM AVAILABILITY TO THE TARGET POPULATION SO THAT POTENTIAL BENEFICIARIES ARE REASONABLY INFORMED OF THE PROGRAM. 2. LEARNED ABOUT ARBORICULTURE AS WELL AS UNDERSTANDING THE IMPORTANCE OF TREES. PARTICIPANTS WILL LEARN HOW TO LEAD A COMMUNITY PROJECT. 3. WORK DIRECTLY WITH COMMUNITY ON 'RIGHT PLACE' PLANTING OF TREES AND HOW TO WORK DIRECTLY WITH COMMUNITY NAVIGATING ISSUES LIKE POOR AIR QUALITY, HEAT, AND NEEDS IN THE COMMUNITY. 4. HAVE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR INDIVIDUAL HABITS AND ROLE THEY CAN PLAY IN THE INTERSECTION OF CARBON EMISSIONS, CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE UTILITY BURDEN. 5. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE EQUIPPED TO CONTINUE PRACTICES THEY LEARNED AS WELL AS SECURE EMPLOYMENT. MANAGING AND EDUCATING AT THREE COMMUNITY RECYCLING CENTERS; ORGANIZING LITTER CLEAN-UPS; PLANTING TREES THROUGH HEARTLAND TREE ALLIANCE; CONSERVING ECOSYSTEMS ON 400 ACRES OF KANSAS CITY WILD LANDS; EDUCATING MORE THAN 400 BUSINESSPEOPLE A YEAR ON 'GREEN' PRACTICES; HELPING TO PLACE 200+ RAIN BARRELS AT HOMES EACH YEAR; ENGAGING MORE THAN 1,800 VOLUNTEERS ANNUALLY THROUGH 100+ ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIONS THROUGHOUT KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI, FOCUSING ON LOW LIFE EXPECTANCY ZIP CODES: 64109, 64126, 64127, 64128, 64130, AND 64132 AND LEAST IMPROVEMENT IN LIFE EXPECTANCY ZIP CODES: 64134, 64131, 64117, 64138, 64114, AND 64133 LOCATED ON THE EAST SIDE OF KANSAS CITY, MO.
description.20: THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING FOR THE NEW MEXICO ENVIRONMENT DEPARTMENT, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SAN JUAN COLLEGE AND OTHER ENTITIES IN THE FOUR CORNERS REGION, TO DEVELOP A WORKFORCE RECRUITMENT AND TRAINING PROGRAM FOR DRINKING WATER AND WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT OPERATORS. THE RECIPIENT WILL DEVELOP A COMMUNITY STORMWATER ENHANCEMENT PROJECT THAT FALL UNDER THE STATUTE OF THE SAFE DRINKING WATER ACT, SECTION 1442.  THE EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS ACTIVITIES, AND SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGNS WILL DEMONSTRATE THE IMPORTANCE OF CLEAN WATER AND THE EFFECTS OF CONTAMINANTS ON THE WATER SUPPLY.   SHOWING THE EFFECTS OF CONTAMINANTS ON THE NUMEROUS LAKES, RIVERS, AND STREAMS THAT ARE IN THE CHOCTAW NATION'S TERRITORY WILL HELP EDUCATE THE COMMUNITY ON THE IMPORTANCE OF PROPER WASTE HANDLING AND DISPOSAL AS A MITIGATION EFFORT.  THESE ACTIVITIES WILL ALSO EDUCATE THE COMMUNITY ON HOW TO PROPERLY IDENTIFY POTENTIAL HAZARDS IN THE WATER SYSTEMS AFTER A MAJOR STORM OR FLOODING EVENT.  THIS PROJECT WILL TARGET AN ESTIMATED 20 COMMUNITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES FOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND TRAINING, INCLUDING THE PURCHASE AND DELIVERY OF DRAINAGE CULVERTS FOR INSTALLATION.  THE LAST ASPECT OF THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF AN ESTIMATED 200 UNITS OF SIGNAGE AND PLACARDS FOR DROP INLETS AND STORM DRAINS IN COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE 12 DISTRICTS OF THE CHOCTAW NATION.  THERE WILL NOT BE ANY SUBAWARDS AS PART OF THE PROJECT.

THIS EDUCATION WILL ALSO FOCUS ON IDENTIFYING POTENTIAL SOURCES OF CONTAMINATION BEFORE IT REACHES THESE WATER SUPPLIES. THE GOAL IS TO HELP CITIZENS RECOGNIZE THE CRITICAL ROLE THAT EACH INDIVIDUAL PLAYS IN HELPING IDENTIFY HAZARDS AS WELL AS HOW TO MITIGATE THOSE POTENTIAL HAZARDS. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT THE PROJECT WILL HAVE 40 TOTAL EVENTS, A MIX OF BOTH COMMUNITY EDUCATIONAL AND OUTREACH EVENTS AND MUNICIPALITY OUTREACH AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE EVENTS/MEETINGS. THERE WILL BE COMMUNITY CENTER OUTREACH AND EDUCATIONAL EVENTS.  SURVEYS AND METRIC DATA WILL BE COLLECTED AT THE EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING EVENTS TO ASSIST IN THE REPORTING AND PROJECT EVALUATION. DROP INLET MARKERS AND DRAIN PLACARDS WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO THE IDENTIFIED COMMUNITIES IN DISTRICTS 2, 3, AND 4. THE TARGETED RESULTS OF THESE ACTIVITIES WILL BE THE COMPLETION OF AN ESTIMATED 5 COMMUNITY EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING EVENTS IN CNO DISTRICTS 2, 3, AND 4, THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF 7 MUNICIPALITY ASSISTANCE AND TRAININGS, THE DISTRIBUTION AND COLLECTION OF SURVEYS AND METRIC DATA, THE DISTRIBUTION OF DROP INLET MARKERS AND DRAIN PLACARDS IN THESE DISTRICTS, THE GENERATION OF QUARTERLY METRICS, AND THE COMPLETION OF THE QUARTERLY REPORTS.

DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT IS TO FUND THE OTOE-MISSOURIA RESCUE PLAN PROJECT, WHICH INCLUDES DETERMINING THE EXISTING KNOWLEDGE AND BELIEFS ABOUT THE FOUR MAIN SUBJECTS BEING COVERED IN THIS PROJECT, AIR QUALITY (AMBIENT, INDOOR AND HEALTHY HOMES), CLIMATE CHANGE, SAFE DRINKING WATER, DISASTER RESILIENCY AND PREPAREDNESS. THE TRIBE WOULD ALSO LIKE TO INCORPORATE ANY TRADITIONAL / INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE THAT MIGHT BE GAINED FROM COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN THESE MODULES. INPUT FROM THE OM HISTORICAL PRESERVATION DEPARTMENT COULD BE A RESOURCE FOR THIS TYPE OF KNOWLEDGE. 



ACTIVITIES:OTOE-MISSOURIA ENVIRONMENTAL DEPARTMENT (OMED) STAFF WILL DESIGN AND CREATE BROCHURES, EMAILS, SOCIAL MEDIA, AND NEWSLETTER ARTICLES TO INFORM THE COMMUNITY ABOUT THIS PROJECT AND THE UPCOMING EDUCATIONAL MODULES. OMED WILL USE THESE FORMS OF MEDIA TO GATHER INTERESTED PARTIES FOR THE PROJECT THEN DISTRIBUTE TO THOSE WHO WISH TO PARTICIPATE. 
SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:USING THE INPUT FROM PARTICIPANTS AND THE PROJECT PARTNERS, OMED WILL BEGIN DEVELOPING FOUR EDUCATIONAL MODULES INCLUDING WORKING WITH THE SPECIFIC PROJECT PARTNERS TO EITHER GAIN INPUT OR PLAN THE TIMING AND DETAILS OF THE PRESENTATION. EACH MODULE WILL CONTAIN TRAINING AND DEMONSTRATION MATERIALS AND TOOLS SPECIFIC TO EACH TOPIC. THESE MATERIALS WILL BE DISTRIBUTED AT THE TIME OF THE MODULE. IF THE TOPIC CANNOT BE ADEQUATELY COVERED IN ONE MODULE THE PRESENTER MAY OPT FOR AN ADDITIONAL SESSION TO FURTHER DISCUSS THE TOPIC. PROGRESS ON THIS PROJECT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE OTOE-MISSOURIA ENVIRONMENTAL COORDINATOR AND TO THE REGION 8 EPA PROJECT OFFICER IN QUARTERLY STATUS REPORTS. IN THE FOURTH QUARTER OF THE PROJECT, THE MODULES WILL BE COMPLETED. AN EXIT PROCESS WILL BE DEVELOPED AND COMPLETED BY PARTICIPANTS TO HELP DETERMINE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. A FINAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE EPA. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE OTOE-MISSOURIA TRIBAL AND SURROUNDING COMMUNITY MEMBERS.
description.32: DESCRIPTION: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED GRANT IS TO ALLOW THE MESCALERO APACHE TRIBE TO ADDRESS COVID PANDEMIC IMPACTED PARTICIPATION UNDER THIS ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE SMALL GRANT FUNDED UNDER THE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN. THE TRIBE'S PROJECT FOCUSES ON AIR QUALITY IMPACTS FROM WILD FIRE SMOKE AND PARTICULATE MATTER THAT IMPACTS TRIBAL AND COMMUNITY MEMBER HEALTH, ESPECIALLY LUNG DISEASE AND ASTHMA RATES. THE PROJECT PROVIDES OUTREACH AND EDUCATION TO THE COMMUNITY IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE MESCALERO HIGH SCHOOL COMMUNITY. THE HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, ALONG WITH THE MESCALERO APACHE ENVIRONMENTAL DIRECTOR, WILL DEVELOP A QUALITY ASSURANCE (QA) PROJECT PLAN TO PLACE AND OPERATE PURPLE AIR SENSORS IN AND AROUND THE COMMUNITY TO MONITOR AIR QUALITY. THE ENVIRONMENTAL DATA GATHERED UNDER THE QA  PLAN WILL BE BE UPLOADED TO A WEBSITE FOR LOCAL USE ON POOR AIR QUALITY DAYS. TRIBAL AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL BE ABLE TO CHECK AIR QUALITY IN REAL TIME, DAILY, IN ORDER TO PLAN TO STAY IN DOORS ON POOR AIR QUALITY DAYS TO PROTECT PUBLIC HEALTH. PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EDUCATION AND OUTREACH ON AIR QUALITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACTS FROM WILDFIRE SMOKE. THE PROJECT INVOLVES COLLECTING ENVIRONMENTAL AIR QUALITY DATA AND A QUALITY ASSURANCE PROJECT PLAN (QAPP) WILL BE DRAFTED AND SUBMITTED TO THE EPA FOR APPROVAL PRIOR TO AIR SENSOR PURCHASE OR AIR MONITORING ACTIVITIES IMPLEMENTED. THE PROJECT INVOLVES PARTNERSHIP WITH THE LOCAL HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS FOR BROADER OUTREACH AND SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATH (STEM) EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT. THE PROJECT WILL BE FOUNDATIONAL TO ASSIST THE MESCALERO APACHE TRIBE WITH DEVELOPING AN AIR QUALITY MONITORING PROGRAM. THE PROJECT WILL HELP BREAK DOWN PUBLIC PARTICIPATION BARRIERS THAT INCREASED DUE TO COVID PANDEMIC SHUT DOWNS AND ISOLATION. WEBSITE ACCESS FOR AIR QUALITY STATUS WILL BE CREATED AND SHARED WITH THE COMMUNITY. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:MEMBERS OF THE MESCALERO APACHE TRIBE AND COMMUNITY SURROUNDING THE RESERVATION WILL BE THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT. THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE AN APPROVED QUALITY ASSURANCE PROJECT PLAN FOR AIR QUALITY MONITORING USING PURPLE AIR SENSORS. THE PROJECT DELIVERABLES INCLUDE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF AIR SENSORS AROUND THE COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT OUTCOMES INCLUDE AIR QUALITY MONITORING AND WEBSITE DATA HOSTING FOR THE SENSORS. THE PROJECT OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED PUBLIC PARTICIPATION FOR ALL COMMUNITY AND TRIBAL MEMBERS TO UNDERSTAND AIR QUALITY IMPACTS FROM INCREASED WILDFIRE SMOKE AND PARTICULATE MATTER.
description.33: DESCRIPTION:'CLEAN AIR - HEALTHY HOMES' IS A COLLABORATIVE INITIATIVE TO ADDRESS NEGATIVE HEALTH OUTCOMES DURING EVER-INCREASING WILDFIRE SMOKE EPISODES BY CO-CREATING A WILDFIRE SMOKE READY ACTION PLAN AND PROGRAMS BASED ON OUTREACH, SURVEYS AND INVESTIGATIONS WITH LOCAL INDIGENOUS AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. IT WILL ALSO ADDRESS AIR POLLUTION BY PROVIDING DIRECT ACCESS TO PORTABLE AIR CLEANERS. THE INITIATIVE WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY RESILIENCE BY WORKING WITH PARTNERS TO SURVEY HOW INDIVIDUALS UNDERSTAND THE HEALTH IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE SMOKE AND THEN PREPARE FOR THESE EVENTS. FROM THIS, THE GRANTEE WILL CO-DEVELOP AN ACTION PLAN FOR WILDFIRE EVENTS WITH ACTIVITIES, SHARED RESOURCES, AND MESSAGING. IT BUILDS ON THE GUIDING PRINCIPLES, STRATEGIES, AND PARTNERSHIPS FROM THE RECENTLY ADOPTED COUNTY-WIDE CLIMATE RESILIENCY PLAN, CLIMATE READY MISSOULA AND CLIMATE SMART'S SUMMER SMART INITIATIVE. ACTIVITIES:THE RECIPIENT AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS, INCLUDING ALL NATIONS HEALTH CENTER, WILL HOST 2 PARTNER PLANNING MEETINGS, CO-HOST 8 FOCUS GROUPS, AND HOST 5 POP-UP EVENTS IN KEY NEIGHBORHOODS. THE RECIPIENT WILL DEVELOP A QA PLAN AND QUESTIONNAIRE TO SURVEY 200 COMMUNITY MEMBERS AT POP UP EVENTS. THE PROGRAM WILL GATHER FEEDBACK FROM 150 HOUSEHOLDS WHO RECEIVED AN AIR FILTER. THE HEALTH CENTER WILL CANVAS 70 INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY MEMBERS VIA A PILOT INTAKE PROCESS AND CANVAS 180 HOMES IN KEY NEIGHBORHOODS. THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CREATING 10 MEETING-IN-A-BOX KITS FOR PARTNER USE. THE PROGRAM WILL HOST 2 WORK SESSIONS TO ASSEMBLE DO IT YOURSELF AIR FILTER + BOX FAN COMBINATIONS FOR USE DURING WILD FIRE SEASON. THE PROGRAM AND PARTNERS WILL SHARE INFORMATION REGIONALLY VIA MEDIA, WEBSITES. FINALLY, THE PROGRAM WILL HOST 6 DEBRIEF SESSIONS (FOCUS GROUPS AND PARTNERS) TO GATHER FEEDBACK ON HOW TO IMPROVE FUTURE PROJECT WORK AND GLEAN SUCCESS STORIES. SUBRECIPIENT:SUB-AWARD TO ALL NATIONS HEALTH CENTER TO ADVERTISE FOR AND HOST COMMUNITY MEETINGS.OUTCOMES:RESIDENTS WHO RECEIVED A FILTER REPORT HIGHER COMFORT LEVELS AT HOME (TARGET = 75% REPORT INCREASE IN COMFORT AT HOME) - INCREASED COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF HEALTH IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE SMOKE AND SIMPLE STEPS TO TAKE TO STAY HEALTHY (TARGET = 20% INCREASE IN COMMUNITY AWARENESS) - STRONGER INFORMATION SHARING NETWORK ACROSS PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS AND MEETING IN-A-BOX TOOL (TARGET = 10 ORGANIZATIONS COMMIT TO HOSTING A CLIMATE RELATED MEETING EACH YEAR) - COMMUNITY MEMBERS FEEL EMPOWERED TO CHECK-IN ON NEIGHBORS DURING WILDFIRE SMOKE EVENTS AND SHARE RESOURCES FOR STAYING HEALTH (TARGET = 20 NEIGHBORHOOD AMBASSADORS IDENTIFIED) - ESTABLISH TRACKING SYSTEM FOR SMOKE IMPACTS WITHIN ESTABLISHED EFFORTS, SUCH AS ANNUAL SURVEYS AND INTAKES (TARGET = ALL NATIONS PILOT PROJECT EXPANDED AND DATA COLLECTED FOR INVEST HEALTH) - REGIONAL NETWORK STRENGTHENED FOR WILDFIRE SMOKE READINESS (TARGET = 2 PRESENTATIONS TO CLIMATE READY MONTANA AND MONTANA HEALTH PROFESSIONALS FOR A HEALTHY CLIMATE) - DECREASE IN EMERGENCY ROOM VISITS DURING WILDFIRE SMOKE EVENTS - INVEST HEALTH NEIGHBORHOODS REPORT FEWER POOR PHYSICAL HEALTH DAYS IN 2023 REPORT - COMMUNITY CONSENSUS THAT CLIMATE RESILIENCY PLANNING IS A PRIORITY AND OTHER ENTITIES INCLUDING BUSINESSES GET INVOLVED - 2 OTHER MONTANA COMMUNITIES CREATE A WILDFIRE SMOKE READY PLAN VIA ENGAGEMENT OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES - INDIGENOUS - NON-HISPANIC WHITE MORTALITY GAP DECREASES - DECREASE IN ASTHMA HOSPITALIZATIONS DURING WILDFIRE SMOKE EVENTS - AFFORDABLE HOUSING HAS PROVISIONS FOR CLEAN INDOOR AIR DURING WILDFIRE SMOKE EVENTS - WE HAVE A MORE RESILIENT AND COHESIVE COMMUNITY WHERE HEALTH IS PRIORITIZED FOR EVERYONE. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE INDIVIDUALS IN AND AROUND MISSOULA COUNTY, INCLUDING THOSE WHO TRAVEL TO THE COUNTY FOR HEALTH CARE SERVICES FROM NEARBY RESERVATIONS.
description.34: DESCRIPTION:THE PROPOSAL BEGINS BY CONDUCTING LISTENING SESSIONS (INITIAL, AND SUBSEQUENT CONTINUOUS SESSIONS THROUGHOUT GRANT AWARD PERIOD) TO CONDUCT A NEEDS ASSESSMENT THROUGH EPA'S COMMUNITY ACTION ROADMAP (CAR) OF WHAT THE COMMUNITY NEEDS ARE AND USE THE RESULTS TO ASSESS KNOWLEDGE GAPS REGARDING IMPACTS OF THE INLAND PORT. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO CONDUCT 'EJ PRIMER' TRAININGS WITH THE COMMUNITY TO PROMOTE COORDINATION AND TRAINING RELATED TO THE CAUSES AND POTENTIAL IMPACTS OF THE INLAND PORT (OZONE AND PARTICULATE MATTER). RELATEDLY, THE PROPOSAL WILL DEVELOP EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS (WEBSITE, BROCHURES) TO FURTHER FOSTER EDUCATION AND TRAINING OF THE PUBLIC RELATED TO THE IMPACTS/CAUSES OF AIR POLLUTION. THEREFORE, THE FOCUS IS ON OUTREACH/TRAINING/EDUCATION THROUGH LISTENING SESSIONS AND CONDUCT OF A NEEDS ASSESSMENT FROM THE COMMUNITY. THE OUTCOMES FOR THIS WORK WILL BE A MORE FULLY ENGAGED COMMUNITY ABLE TO SHARE ITS CONCERNS REGARDING THE ENVIRONMENTAL CONSEQUENCES OF THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE INLAND PORT.ACTIVITIES:ACTIVITIES INCLUDE LISTENING SESSIONS, A NEEDS ASSESSMENT USING THE COMMUNITY ACTION ROADMAP, AN ANALYSIS OF THE KNOWLEDGE GAPS REGARDING PORT IMPACTS. ,EJ PRIMER' TRAININGS WITH THE COMMUNITY WILL BE CONDUCTED. THE GRANTEE WILL ALSO DEVELOP AND DISTRIBUTE EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS (WEBSITE, AND BROCHURES) AND USE THESE TO FURTHER EDUCATE THE COMMUNITY RE: ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PORT.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE,: BROCHURE, VIDEOS AND FACT SHEETS, LISTENING SESSION REPORTS, A ROADMAP TO EFFECTIVE COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND A  COMMUNITY OUTREACH GUIDE.  OUTCOMES INCLUDE A MORE INFORMED AND ENGAGED COMMUNITY PREPARED TO ADDRESS AND ARTICULATE COMMUNITY CONCERNS REGARDING PORTS AND OTHER SIGNIFICANT ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERNS.

DESCRIPTION:
THE PROJECT OBJECTIVES ARE: 1) CONDUCT A HEALTHY HOMES SURVEY AND A HEALTH FOCUSED LIFESTYLES SURVEY; 2) ENHANCE THE ONGOING COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM; 3) PERFORM AMBIENT (ATMOSPHERIC) RADON MONITORING AND TO MONITOR FOR OTHER TOXIC AIR POLLUTANTS (E.G., VOLATILE ORGANIC COMPOUNDS (VOCS) AND 4) DEVELOP A WHITE MESA EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDY PLAN, INCLUSIVE OF AMBIENT RADON MONITORING AND INVESTIGATION OF OTHER TOXIC AIR POLLUTANTS. 

 .
ACTIVITIES:
MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY HAVE SUFFERED FROM CANCER AND NATIVE AMERICANS HAVE A HIGHER DEGREE OF ASTHMA THAN THE NATIONAL AVERAGE. THE TRIBE HAS CORRESPONDED WITH THE 
ALBUQUERQUE AREA INDIAN HEALTH BOARD EPIDEMIOLOGY CENTER OVER THE LAST THREE YEARS AND THE INITIAL HEALTHY HOMES AND LIFESTYLES WORK HAS BEEN RECOMMENDED. PAIRING THIS 
WITH PROFESSIONAL EXPERTISE ON EPIDEMIOLOGICAL PLANNING, WE INTEND TO IDENTIFY THE SPECIFIC MECHANISMS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE HEALTH OF THE RESIDENTS OF WHITE MESA AND 
WHETHER THE MILL IS IMPACTING PUBLIC HEALTH. WITH THE FUTURE OF MILL ACTIVITIES UNCERTAIN, BUT LIKELY TO CONTINUE INDEFINITELY INTO THE NEXT DECADES, THIS WILL BE A STARTING POINT FOR 
MORE RIGOROUS INVESTIGATIONS IN THE FUTURE. AFTER APPROVAL TO A PETITION FROM THE TRIBE IN 2019, THE AGENCY FOR TOXIC SUBSTANCES AND DISEASE REGISTRY (ATSDR) HAS BEEN 5
REVIEWING DOCUMENTATION AND TRIBAL AIR MONITORING DATA TO OBTAIN RISK TO HEALTH EFFECTS FROM THE MILL TO THE WHITE MESA COMMUNITY. THE ATSDR REPORT IS EXPECTED TO BE 
FINISHED IN THE NEXT SIX MONTHS. THIS WILL PROVIDE ADDITIONAL CONTEXT IN GUIDING THE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL WORK PROPOSED TO BE PLANNED IN THIS PROJECT.
OUTCOMES:
THE GRANTEE WILL ENGAGE IN A COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM WHICH WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASE IN COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT, AN INCREASE IN INVOLVEMENT WITH LOCAL OFFICIALS AND STAKE HOLDERS.  THE HEALTH EFFECTS FROM URANIUM MILL WILL BE UNDERSTAND BY ALL STAKEHOLDERS. THE GRANTEE WILL COMPLETE A HEALTHY HOMES STUDY (INDOOR RADON) AND COMPLETE A HEALTH-BASED LIFESTYLE SURVEY. ONCE THE RADON TEST IS IMPLEMENTED, THE COMMUNITY WILL HAVE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF POTENTIAL HEALTH IMPACT VECTORS.  ONCE THE DATA IS COLLECTED, INFORMATION SHARED, AND THE GRANTEE WILL HELP IDENTIFY RESOURCES TO ADDRESS IN-HOME HEALTH VECTORS.  THE COMMUNITY WILL HAVE BETTER HOUSING AWARENESS OF IN-HOME HEALTH VECTORS, CHANGES TO HOME HEALTH ISSUES. THE GRANTEE WILL IMPLEMENT AMBIENT AIR QUALITY TESTING.  THE COMMUNITY WILL HAVE A BETTER KNOWLEDGE OF AIR QUALITY RISKS. THE GRANTEE WILL DEVELOP AN EPA LIBRARY AND VIRTUAL MEDIA DEVELOPMENT ON URANIUM HEALTH EFFECTS.  THIS WILL LEAD TO AN INCREASE IN COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT AND AN ACTIVE SPACE TO ARCHIVE MATERIALS TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITY FOR INCREASED KNOWLEDGE. THE GRANTEE WILL BUILD A GROUNDWATER EXHIBIT.  THIS WILL LEAD TO COMMUNITY UNDERSTANDING OF LOCAL GROUNDWATER. THE GRANTEE WILL GATHER URANIUM MILL DATA  AND DO AN UP TO DATE ASSESSMENT OF MILL POLLUTANTS AND REGULATORY ACTIONS.  THIS WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED LINES OF COMMUNICATION WITH REGULATORS, AND CHANGES IN REGULATORY DECISIONS THAT INCORPORATE TRIBAL PERSPECTIVES. FINALLY THE GRANTEE WILL BEGIN THE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDY PLANNING.  THIS RESULT IN THE CONDUCTING OF EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDY OF WHITE MESA RESIDENTS.  THOSE IMPACTED BY THESE ACTIONS INCLUDE, IHS, UTAH HEALTH BOARD, TRIBAL MEMBERS, TRIBAL LEADERS, NON-TRIBAL PARTNERS, REGULATORS WHITE MESA AND LOCAL RESIDENTS.

description.36: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER SECTION 103 OF THE CLEAN AIR ACT TO UTAH CLEAN ENERGY TO BUILD RESILIENCY AND ADDRESSES INDOOR/OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION CHALLENGES THAT HAVE HISTORICALLY BURDENED SALT LAKE CITY&RSQUOANDS WESTSIDE COMMUNITIES.  THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ENGAGING  SALT  LAKE  CITY&RSQUOANDS  WESTSIDE  COMMUNITIES  IN  A  COLLABORATIVE  PROCESS  TO:  1)  BUILD  A  SHARED  UNDERSTANDING  OF  BENEFICIAL  ELECTRIFICATIONAND  2)  DEVELOP  A  COMMUNITY  VISION  OF  WHAT  ASPECTS  OF  ELECTRIFICATION  ARE  MOST  IMPORTANTAND  3) IDENTIFY  THE  UNIQUE  OPPORTUNITIES  AND  BARRIERS  THAT  THE  COMMUNITIES  WILL  FACEAND  4)  BRING  STAKEHOLDERS  (SUCH  AS  THE  ELECTRIC  UTILITY,  SALT  LAKE  CITY,  AND  SERVICE  PROVIDERS)  INTO  LISTENING SESSIONS SO THEY DEVELOP AN UNDERSTANDING OF COMMUNITY NEEDS AND GOALSAND AND 5) CO-DEVELOP STRATEGIES BETWEEN THE COMMUNITIES, GOVERNMENT, UTILITY, AND SERVICE PROVIDERS TO  ENSURE  THAT  COMMUNITY NEEDS  AND  PRIORITIES  ARE  SUCCESSFULLY  INTEGRATED  INTO  PLANNING. EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT ARE INCREASED CLIMATE RESILIENCY IN WESTSIDE COMMUNITIESAND LONG-TERM REDUCTIONS IN INDOOR/OUTDOOR AIR QUALITY POLLUTANTS (PM2.5, CO, NO2)AND IMPROVED HEALTH OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND IMPROVED COMFORT OF HOMES FOR THOSE WHO PARTICIPATEAND AND INCREASED COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO ACCESS RESOURCES AND PARTICIPATE IN FUTURE UTILITY AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT ELECTRIFICATION PROGRAMS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE RESIDENTS OF WESTSIDE COMMUNITIES IN SALT LAKE CITY, UT, WHO ARE PREDOMINANTLY PEOPLE OF COLOR, LOW INCOME, AND LINGUISTICALLY ISOLATED FACING INCREASED LEVELS OF EXPOSURE TO AIR POLLUTION. THE RECIPIENT INTENDS TO ISSUE SUBAWARD AGREEMENTS TO ITS PARTNERS IN COMPLIANCE WITH APPENDIX A OF EPA&RSQUOANDS SUBAWARD POLICY. THE SUB-AWARDEES WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL INSIGHT AND SERVE AS COMMUNITY CONVENORS HOSTING EVENTS, WORKSHOPS, AND LISTENING SESSIONS.
description.37: DESCRIPTION:GROUNDWORK ELIZABETH (GWE), ITS PROJECT PARTNERS AND SUBAWARD RECIPIENT WILL BRING TOGETHER A DIVERSE COALITION OF COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS THAT WILL INCREASE PARTICULATE MATTER (PM) MONITORING, DEFINE PM HEALTH COSTS IN ELIZABETH (NEAR PORT-ELIZABETH MARINE TERMINAL), EXPLORE BIODIESEL AS A STRATEGY TO REDUCE EMISSIONS, AND DEVELOP A COMMUNITY ACTION PLAN FOR REDUCING PM IN THE COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO INCREASE KNOWLEDGE AND AWARENESS OF AIR QUALITY AND ITS HEALTH EFFECTS IN THE COMMUNITY.ACTIVITIES:GROUNDWORK ELIZABETH (GWE) AND ITS SUBAWARD RECIPIENT WILL DEPLOY AIR MONITORS THROUGHOUT THE COMMUNITY TO MONITOR PM LEVELS AROUND THE PORT. THE CONTRACT RECIPIENT WILL MODEL THE IMPACTS OF DIESEL PM WITHIN THE COMMUNITY AND THE BENEFITS OF SWITCHING TO ALTERNATIVE FUELS.  SUBRECIPIENT:THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH SCIENCE INSTITUTE (EOSHI) AND THE CENTER FOR ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURE AND DISEASE (CEED) WITHIN RUTGERS UNIVERSITY WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR IMPROVED CHARACTERIZATION OF LOCAL AIR QUALITY FOCUSED ON PARTICULATE MATTER AND DIESEL EXHAUST AIR POLLUTION. THEY WILL ASSIST WITH DEVELOPMENT OF A QUALITY ASSURANCE PROJECT PLAN (QAPP), TRAINING OF GWE STAFF AND GREEN TEAMS ON FUNDAMENTALS OF AIR POLLUTION AND HEALTH, SITING AND DEPLOYMENT OF PURPLE AIR MONITORS, TROUBLESHOOTING THE MONITORS, AND ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION OF DATA.OUTCOMES:THE PM MONITORING WILL HELP DEFINE PM HEALTH COSTS IN ELIZABETH (NEAR PORT-ELIZABETH MARINE TERMINAL). THE CONTRACTED STUDY WILL EXPLORE BIODIESEL AS A STRATEGY TO REDUCE EMISSIONS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE THE COMMUNITY NEAR THE PORT-ELIZABETH MARINE TERMINAL.
description.38: DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT PROVIDES FUNDING TO VAN CORTLANDT PARK ALLIANCE TO IMPLEMENT ITS PROJECT, WHICH WILL DESIGN, DEMONSTRATE, AND DISSEMINATE ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PRACTICES, METHODS, AND TECHNIQUES, THAT WILL SERVE TO INCREASE ENVIRONMENTAL LITERACY AND ENCOURAGE BEHAVIOR THAT WILL BENEFIT THE ENVIRONMENT IN THE BRONX, NEW YORK. THE GRANTEE WILL DO THIS BY EDUCATING UNDERSERVED STUDENTS' ON HOW AIR QUALITY, WATER QUALITY AND CLIMATE CHANGE IS AFFECTING THEIR COMMUNITY. VAN CORTLANDT PARK ALLIANCE WILL USE A COMBINATION OF CLASSROOM COURSE, HAND-ON ACTIVITIES, AND FIELD TRIPS TO TEACH STUDENT HOW TO MONITOR WATER QUALITY, REDUCE THE GREENHOUSE GASES AND MANAGE FOOD WASTE THROUGH COMPOSTING. THIS PROJECT WILL RAISE THE ENVIRONMENTAL KNOWLEDGE OF PROJECT PARTICIPANTS AND EMPOWER THEM TO THINK CRITICALLY AND DEVELOP CONSERVATION-BASED CAREER EXPERIENCE RELATED TO WATER QUALITY AND AIR QUALITY AS WELL AS INCREASE ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP WITHIN THE AFFECTED UNDERSERVED COMMUNITY.  ACTIVITIES:THIS PROJECT WILL INCREASE PUBLIC AWARENESS AND KNOWLEDGE ABOUT ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES IN THE BRONX, NEW YORK AND PROVIDE UNDERSERVED STUDENTS THE SKILLS NECESSARY TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS AND TO TAKE RESPONSIBLE ACTIONS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED DURING THIS PROJECT PERIOD INCLUDE WATER MONITORING ALONG THE BRONX RIVER, TIBBETTS BROOK AND VAN CORTLANDT'S MILL POND, EXPLORE AND IMPLEMENT PROJECTS TO REDUCE GREENHOUSE GASES AND TEACHING PROJECT PARTICIPANTS THE BENEFITS OF FOOD WASTE MANAGEMENT THROUGH COMPOSTING.  SUBRECIPIENT:VAN CORTLANDT PARK ALLIANCE WILL ISSUE SUBAWARDS AS REQUIRED UNDER THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION ACT. THE SUB AWARDEES WILL PROVIDE COORDINATION OF THE PROJECT, PREPARING EDUCATION MATERIALS FIELD TRIPS AND HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES.  SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT. OUTCOMES:IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THE FOLLOWING DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES: 20 WILL BE EMPOWERED TO THINK CRITICALLY AND DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT PROJECTS TO REDUCE GREENHOUSE GASES; RECRUIT 20 STUDENTS INCREASE THEIR KNOWLEDGE OF WATER QUALITY IN THEIR LOCAL COMMUNITY. 45 STUDENTS TO INCREASE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND SKILL NECESSARY TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ON ADDRESSING CLIMATE CHANGE, IMPROVING AIR QUALITY, ENSURING CLEAN AND SAFE WATER, AND INCREASING THEIR AWARENESS OF GREEN CAREERS AND INTEREST IN ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE STUDENTS LOCATED IN THE BRONX, NEW YORK.
description.39: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT IS TO COLLABORATIVELY DESIGN, CONDUCT, AND SHARE LOCAL COMMUNITY-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL VALUES ADVANCING AT-RISK COMMUNITIES (EVAAC) TRAININGS ON INDOOR AND OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION AND TOXIC CHEMICALS RELATED TO INDOOR AIR POLLUTION THAT WILL PROVIDE COMMUNITIES WITH ON-THE-GROUND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND UTILIZE A CONSENSUS-BASED COMMUNITY MAPPING APPROACH INNOVATED BY REPRESENTABLE TO REFLECT COMMUNITY PRIORITIES. CLEAN AND HEALTHY NEW YORK WILL FORM COLLABORATIVE COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS WITH STAKEHOLDERS AND HOST TRAINING ACTIVITIES TO EDUCATE, ENGAGE, AND EMPOWER THEM ON LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND HEALTH DISPARITIES RELATED TO AIR POLLUTION AND DISCUSS OPTIONS TO ADDRESS OR MITIGATE PRIORITIZED AIR POLLUTION ISSUES.ACTIVITIES:PROJECT ACTIVITIES INVOLVE PUBLIC EDUCATION THROUGH TRAININGS, USE OF THE REPRESENTABLE TOOL TO IDENTIFY AND BUILD COMMUNITIES OF INTEREST, AND EMPOWERING PEOPLE. CLEAN AND HEALTHY NEW YORK, ALONG WITH CAPITAL AREA URBAN LEAGUE AND OTHER COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVES, WILL HOLD 2-3 PRELIMINARY CONVERSATIONS TO SHARE KNOWN INFORMATION ABOUT EXISTING AND POTENTIAL AIR POLLUTION AND TOXICS SOURCES, EXPLORE FEDERAL DATA ON AIR POLLUTION, TOXICS, AND RELATED HEALTH IMPACTS USING THE EPA EJ MAPPER TOOL, AND ASSESS ADDITIONAL COMMUNITY INFORMATION NEEDS SO EXISTING DATA CAN BE COMPILED DURING A LITERATURE REVIEW. 10-20 TRAINING MEETINGS WITH RESIDENTS, ELECTED OFFICIALS, BUSINESS AND RELIGIOUS LEADERS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL BE PLANNED AND HELD TO PRESENT INFORMATION ABOUT AIR POLLUTION AND TOXICS USING A COMBINATION OF PARTICIPANT QUESTIONS, A DEVELOPED SLIDE DECK, AND A PROCESS CREATED BY REPRESENTABLE. 'COMMUNITIES OF INTEREST' AND COMMON PRIORITIES AMONG THE DIFFERENT CHALLENGES FACING THE IMPACTED COMMUNITY WILL BE IDENTIFIED. AFTER THE TRAINING MEETINGS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND HEALTH INFORMATION IDENTIFIED FOR PRIORITIZATION WILL BE CURATED. MAPS, ALONG WITH AN EDUCATIONAL BROCHURE AND INFOGRAPHIC, WILL BE CREATED. CLEAN AND HEALTHY NEW YORK WILL WORK WITH AN ACCREDITED TEACHER TO TRANSLATE TRAINING CONTENT INTO AN EDUCATIONAL CURRICULUM FOR K-12 STUDENTS THAT WILL BE SHARED WITH TEACHERS IN THE CITY AND THE NYS UNITED TEACHERS. THESE MATERIALS AND INFORMATION ABOUT AIR POLLUTION PRIORITIES AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR CHANGE WILL BE SHARED WITH TRAINING MEETING PARTICIPANTS, THEIR ORGANIZATIONS, AND THE BROADER COMMUNITY VIA CLEAN AND HEALTHY NEW YORK'S WEBSITE, SOCIAL MEDIA PAGES, AND TABLES/BOOTHS AT MAJOR CULTURAL EVENTS IN ALBANY, NEW YORK. SUBRECIPIENT:CLEAN AND HEALTHY NEW YORK WILL PROVIDE CAPITAL AREA URBAN LEAGUE, A 501(C)3 ORGANIZATION, A SUBAWARD FOR STAFF TIME TO HELP BRAINSTORM, PLAN TRAININGS, TRAIN PROJECT LEADERS ABOUT THE REPRESENTABLE TOOL FOR COMMUNITY MAPPING, ENGAGE IN OUTREACH AND PARTICIPATE IN/FACILITATE TRAINING MEETINGS WITH STAKEHOLDERS AND TEAM MEMBERS, RECRUIT PARTICIPANTS AND ORGANIZATIONS, REVIEW MATERIALS, AND PROVIDE FEEDBACK. CLEAN AND HEALTHY NEW YORK WILL ALSO PROVIDE SUBAWARDS TO APPROXIMATELY THREE OTHER OTHER COMMUNITY PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS FOR THEIR TIME CONDUCTING WORK SUCH AS PLANNING, ATTENDING EVENTS, PROVIDING FEEDBACK, ENGAGING THEIR MEMBERSHIP, AND HELPING DESIGN AND THEN REVIEW WRITTEN DOCUMENTS.OUTCOMES:ANTICIPATED PROJECT DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A CURATED LITERATURE SEARCH COMPILING PRIORITIZED INDOOR AND OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION DATA, A SLIDE DECK AND REPRESENTABLE QUESTIONS FOR TRAINING MEETINGS, TRAINING MEETING SCHEDULES AND REGISTRATION FORMS, POST-SURVEYS, CALENDARS, A MAP TO ILLUSTRATE PRIORITIZED ENVIRONMENTAL DATA, A MAP TO DOCUMENT THE OUTCOME OF THE REPRESENTABLE PROCESS, LESSON PLANS FOR K-12 STUDENTS, AND MATERIALS (MAPS, BROCHURE, AND INFOGRAPHIC) TO EDUCATE THE PUBLIC ABOUT PRIORITIZED CONCERNS. THE PROJECT IS EXPECTED TO ENABLE COMMUNITY MEMBERS, INCLUDING TEACHERS AND STUDENTS, TO IDENTIFY 'COMMUNITIES OF INTEREST' USING REPRESENTABLE, PLAY AN INTEGRAL ROLE IN PRIORITIZING ENVIR
description.40:
DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT IS FOR ASLF AND ITS PARTNERS TO PLAN, DESIGN, AND INSTALL SIX AGROFORESTRY DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS AND A COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND EDUCATION PROGRAM FOCUSING ON THE MYRIAD ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL BENEFITS ASSOCIATED WITH SAID PRACTICE. FIVE OF THE SIX DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS WILL BE LOCATED IN IMPOVERISHED URBAN SYRACUSE NEIGHBORHOODS AND WILL TAKE THE FORM OF URBAN FOOD FORESTS. THE SIXTH DEMONSTRATION WILL BE INSTALLED ON A FARM OWNED BY THE ONONDAGA NATION AND WILL BE INCORPORATED INTO ITS BRAIDING THE SACRED PROGRAM, WHICH FOCUSES ON PRESERVING INDIGENOUS NATIVE FOOD PLANTS FOR THE PURPOSE OF BUILDING FOOD SOVEREIGNTY. OUTREACH AND EDUCATION WILL FOCUS ON COMMUNICATING THE BENEFITS OF AGROFORESTRY AND NATIVE URBAN TREES AS THEY RELATE TO STORMWATER MITIGATION, AIR QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, FOOD SECURITY, GREENSPACE ACCESS, URBAN HEAT ISLAND MITIGATION, URBAN RESILIENCE, AND PSYCHO-SOCIAL STRESS RELIEF.ACTIVITIES:THIS PROJECT HAS OUTREACH/EDUCATION AND DEMONSTRATION COMPONENTS, AND ACTIVITIES WILL BE BASED ON ACCOMPLISHING OUTCOMES DERIVED FROM THESE. ACTIVITIES ARE DESCRIBED AS FOLLOWS:
- OUTREACH/EDUCATION/ADVANCING AWARENESS - ASLF WILL WORK WITH PARTNERS TO ADVANCE AWARENESS OF HOW AGROFORESTRY AND FOOD FORESTS ARE AN IMPORTANT PART OF RESTORATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, URBAN RESILIENCE, IMPROVING NEARBY GREENSPACES, FOOD SECURITY/SOVEREIGNTY, STORMWATER MITIGATION, AIR QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, URBAN HEAT ISLAND REDUCTION, PSYCHO-SOCIAL STRESS RELIEF, AND PREVENTION OF CHRONIC DISEASE. THIS WILL BE DONE WITH MEETINGS/PRESENTATIONS WITH EACH PARTNER AND THEIR CONSTITUENCY, GENERAL INFORMATIONAL PRESENTATIONS EITHER VIRTUALLY OR IN-PERSON, MEETINGS AT OTHER STAKEHOLDER MEETINGS INVOLVING MUNICIPAL DECISION-MAKERS, NATIVE TREE PLANTING AND CARE WORKSHOPS, DOOR-TO-DOOR OUTREACH, CREATION OF INFORMATIONAL BROCHURES, CREATION OF INFORMATIVE SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS, INFORMATION POSTED ON THE ASLF AND PARTNER WEBSITES, AND A CASE STUDY PAPER WRITTEN ON THE PROJECT. ALL OF THESE OUTREACH ACTIVITIES WILL RESULT IN GREATER AWARENESS OF THE BENEFITS OF AGROFORESTRY AND FOOD FORESTS AT MULTIPLE LEVELS, FROM LAY COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO MUNICIPAL AGENCY DECISION-MAKERS. A MAJOR GOAL IS TO NORMALIZE THE EXPECTATION OF FOOD FORESTS FOR ALMOST EVERY LOCAL PROJECT INVOLVING PUBLICLY-ACCESSIBLE GREENSPACE. AFTER COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT A MUCH GREATER PORTION OF THE LOCAL PUBLIC SHOULD KNOW AND WANT FOOD FORESTS TO BE INTEGRATED INTO THE URBAN FABRIC OF SYRACUSE.

description.42: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT IS TO TRAIN UNDESERVED, DIVERSE STUDENTS AND RESIDENTS OF RIVERHEAD AND RIVERSIDE, NEW YORK ABOUT WATER AND AIR QUALITY ISSUES AFFECTING THEIR COMMUNITY. ALSO, THE RECIPIENT WILL USE EDUCATION AND TRAINING TO INCREASE AWARENESS OF HOW CRITICAL ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES IMPACT THE HEALTH OF RESIDENTS AND THE LOCAL ECOSYSTEMS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND OUTPUTS ARE TO INCREASE COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF THE WATER AND AIR QUALITY ISSUES AND THEIR POTENTIAL HEALTH EFFECTS, DEVELOP EDUCATIONAL CONTENT FOR STUDENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS FOR BOTH IN-PERSON AND ONLINE. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES FOR THIS PROJECT ARE STUDENTS AND RESIDENTS OF RIVERHEAD AND RIVERSIDE, NEW YORK.

DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT AIMS TO EDUCATE THE REFUGEE COMMUNITY LOCATED IN ROCHESTER, NEW YORK ON THE POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES SURROUNDING LOCAL FISH CONSUMPTION. REFUGEE SUBSISTENCE ANGLERS IN THE ROCHESTER EMBAYMENT AREA OF CONCERN ARE DIFFICULT TO REACH WITH TRADITIONAL FISH HEALTH ADVISORY EDUCATIONAL MATERIAL. THIS MEANS THEY, THEIR FAMILIES AND OTHERS WHO CONSUME THE FISH THEY CATCH ARE PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TO THE ILL HEALTH EFFECTS OF MIREX, PCBS, DIOXINS AND OTHER WATER POLLUTANTS FOUND IN THIS AREA WHICH AFFECT HUMAN HEALTH THROUGH FISH CONSUMPTION. 

ROCHESTER REFUGEE RESETTLEMENT SERVICES WILL ENGAGE HIGH SCHOOL AND COLLEGE AGED STUDENTS FROM THE REFUGEE COMMUNITY AS SURVEYORS TO COLLECT DATA ON LOCAL FISH CONSUMPTION AND KNOWLEDGE OF FISH CONSUMPTION HEALTH ADVISORIES. THE SURVEY DATA WILL BE ANALYZED AND USED TO DEVELOP EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH STRATEGIES FOR IMPROVED FISH ADVISORY COMMUNICATIONS WITH THIS COMMUNITY. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE RESIDENTS OF ROCHESTER, NEW YORK.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED ARE: TRAIN 12 STUDENT FISH FLASH CARD SURVEYORS AT ONE 3-HR KICKOFF MEETING; CONDUCT 300 FISH FLASH CARD SURVEYS; COLLECT SURVEY RESULTS FROM SURVEYORS AT 6 BIWEEKLY WORKSHOP MEETINGS; ANALYZE FISH FLASH CARD SURVEYS AT 4 BIWEEKLY WORKSHOP MEETINGS; DEVELOP OUTREACH LESSON PLANS AND DESIGN FORMATS/IDENTIFY LEARNING OBJECTIVES AND DEVELOP OUTREACH STRATEGIES AT 6 BIWEEKLY WORKSHOP MEETINGS; EXECUTE THE DEVELOPED EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH STRATEGIES AT 8 EVENTS, REACHING AN AUDIENCE OF 1000 MEMBERS OF THE REFUGEE COMMUNITY; EVALUATE OUTREACH STRATEGIES.SUBRECIPIENT:THERE ARE TWO SUBAWARDS INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT. ONE SUBAWARD, IN THE AMOUNT OF $8,883 WILL GO TO MARY'S PLACE REFUGEE OUTREACH TO PAY FOR 23% OF THE TIME OF ONE EXPERIENCED EDUCATOR AND OUTREACH COORDINATOR TO ASSIST RECRUITING, COORDINATING, AND ASSISTING TWELVE YOUNG ADULTS FLUENT IN ENGLISH AND THEIR FAMILY'S PRIMARY LANGUAGE TO ACT AS SURVEYORS USING THE 'FISH FLASH CARD' SURVEY. THE MARY'S PLACE EMPLOYEE, ALONG WITH TWO RRRS EMPLOYEES AND THE PROJECT MANAGER, JEFF WYATT, DVM, MPH (UNIVERSITY OF ROCHESTER SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AND DENTISTRY) WILL ASSIST THE 'FISH FLASH CARD' SURVEYORS IN STATISTICAL ANALYSIS OF THE SURVEY DATA. 

A SECOND SUBAWARD, IN THE AMOUNT OF $10,580 WILL GO TO THE SENECA PARK ZOOLOGICAL SOCIETY TO PAY FOR 11.5% OF THE TIME OF TWO EDUCATION SPECIALISTS WHO WILL PROVIDE GUIDANCE ON CRAFTING OUTREACH PLATFORMS TO INFORM THE REFUGEE COMMUNITY OF AGE- AND GENDER-SPECIFIC HEALTH RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH CONSUMING SELECT FISH SPECIES FROM THE ROCHESTER EMBAYMENT AOC AND LAKE ONTARIO. THE TWO SENECA PARK ZOO EDUCATION SPECIALISTS WILL WORK WITH THE TEAM OF SUPERVISORS/MENTORS FROM MARY'S PLACE AND RRRS, THE TWELVE SURVEYORS, DR. WYATT, AND ANTHONY PETRUSO, MD, A PHYSICIAN AT THE CENTER FOR REFUGEE HEALTH (CRH) TO DESIGN AN IMPACTFUL OUTREACH PLATFORM, INCLUDING TARGETED LESSON PLANS, PUBLIC AND WEB-BASED PRESENTATIONS AND PAMPHLETS AND POSTERS FOR THE CRH CLINIC WAITING ROOM ACCESSIBLE TO FAMILIES AND USEFUL FOR HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS TO SHARE DURING PATIENT VISITS. 
OUTCOMES:THE DELIVERABLES FROM THIS PROJECT ARE THE OUTREACH ACTIVITIES THAT ARE DEVELOPED FROM THE SURVEY AND DATA ANALYSIS. OUTREACH STRATEGIES WILL BE DETERMINED BASED ON THE CONCLUSIONS FROM ANALYSIS OF THE SURVEY DATA. THEY ARE EXPECTED TO INCLUDE BROCHURES (IN ENGLISH AND IN REFUGEES' NATIVE LANGUAGES) AND COMMUNITY PRESENTATIONS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE: INCREASED REFUGEE COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF SAFE FISH CONSUMPTION ADVISORIES, DECREASED HAZARDOUS FISH CONSUMPTION BY CHILDREN AND CHILDBEARING AGE WOMEN, REDUCED RISK OF LIFELONG COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS AND ENDOCRINE DISRUPTION FROM CHILDHOOD OR FETAL EXPOSURE TO CONTAMINANTS IN FISH, AND REDUCED CANCER RISK IN WOMEN. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE RESIDENTS OF ROCHESTER, NY.

DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT AGREEMENT IS TO ENABLE WESTERN NEW YORK SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS ROUNDTABLE (SBR) TO PARTNER WITH THE WESTSIDE PROMISE AND BLACK ROCK NEIGHBORHOODS TO BUILD A COLLECTIVE MOVEMENT OF MEANINGFUL ACTION AROUND CLIMATE RESILIENCY. THE APPROACH IS HUMAN-CENTERED, PLACING THE NEEDS, VOICES AND LEADERSHIP OF THOSE WHO ARE MOST IMPACTED AT THE FOREFRONT. THEY WILL BRING TOGETHER THE PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS COMMUNITY OUTREACH CAPACITY AND SBR'S ABILITY TO INFLUENCE BUSINESSES TO BECOME PARTNERS IN ACTION. THE MAIN GOALS ARE TO: 1) EDUCATE RESIDENTS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND CLIMATE VULNERABILITY ISSUES IN THEIR COMMUNITY AND THE RESULTING RISKS; FROM A SHORT- MID-, AND LONG-TERM PERSPECTIVE, 2) CREATE ARENAS FOR DIALOGUE AROUND WHAT TYPE OF MITIGATION AND ADAPTATION MEASURES ARE MOST IMPORTANT FROM A COMMUNITY PERSPECTIVE, AND 3) INVOLVE LOCAL BUSINESSES TO SUPPORT COMMUNITY-LED CLIMATE RESILIENCY ACTION. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A BASE OF ENGAGED RESIDENTS THAT REFLECTS THEIR COMMUNITIES' VOICES, EXPERIENCES, AND PRIORITIES IN CLIMATE RESILIENCY PLANNING, AND A CORE GROUP OF LOCAL, SUSTAINABLE BUSINESSES ASSISTING WITH IMPLEMENTATION OF PRIORITIZED ACTIONS.

NOTE FOR USE OF ARP FUNDS: CAA 103(B)(3): PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED. ACTIVITIES:THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES WILL BE PERFORMED: ANALYZE AND COMPILE COMMUNITY NEEDS TO DRAFT A CLIMATE RESILIENCY PLAN;  CONDUCT TWO WORKSHOPS AT LOCAL BUSINESSES (15-25 ATTENDEES PER WORKSHOP); CREATE AND DISTRIBUTE EVENT SURVEYS TO WORKSHOP ATTENDEES; PRODUCE 4 ELECTRONIC NEWSLETTERS, 2 VIDEOS, 8 SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS AND 1-2 PAID ADVERTISEMENTS; CREATE A FACT SHEET OUTLINING BEST PRACTICES TO SERVE AS A RESOURCE FOR ORGANIZATIONS (LIKE SBR) TO IMPLEMENT COMMUNITY DRIVEN CLIMATE RESILIENCY AND MITIGATION ACTION SUPPORTED BY LOCAL SUSTAINABLE BUSINESSES, WITH THEIR CONSTITUENCIES; RECRUIT A MINIMUM OF 2 COMPANIES TO PARTICIPATE IN COMMUNITY/ CORPORATE SERVICE CLIMATE ACTION DAYS.SUBRECIPIENT:WESTERN NEW YORK SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS (SBR)'S SUB-GRANTEE, BLACK ROCK RIVERSIDE ALLIANCE (BRRA), IS ONE OF TWO MAIN PARTNERS FOR THE PROJECTS. THE PRIMARY ROLE OF BRRA WILL BE TO
PROVIDE CONNECTIONS TO THE RESIDENTS WITHIN THE WEST SIDE COMMUNITIES WHO WILL PARTICIPATE IN DIALOGUES TO INFORM THE CLIMATE RESILIENCE PLANNING EFFORTS. THE SUB-AWARD WILL COVER TIME SPENT BY BRRA ON RECRUITMENT OF RESIDENTS TO ATTEND THE EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS, DISSEMINATION OF MARKETING MATERIALS, USE OF BRRA'S MEETING SPACE FOR ONE OF THE WORKSHOP SERIES AND PRODUCTION AND DATA COLLECTION OF A POST-WORKSHOP SURVEY. BRRA HAS STRONG ROOTS WITHIN THE COMMUNITY, MAKING THEM VALUABLE FOR PROVIDING A BRIDGE BETWEEN THE RESIDENTS AND SBR'S NETWORK OF LOCAL, SUSTAINABLE BUSINESSES. THE OTHER PARTNER, WEST SIDE PROMISE NEIGHBORHOOD PROGRAM (WSPN), IS A NON-FUNDED PARTNER. OUTCOMES:KEY OUTPUTS INCLUDE 300 - 500 INDIVIDUALS INVOLVED IN OUR PROJECT ACTIVITIES, A COMMUNITY-DRIVEN CLIMATE RESILIENCY PLAN AND A FACTSHEET. KEY OUTCOMES INCLUDE CHANGES IN KNOWLEDGE AND AWARENESS AMONG WEST SIDE RESIDENTS AND BUSINESSES, CHANGES IN BUSINESS PRACTICES, AND EQUITY CENTERED POLICIES IN PLACE. WEST SIDE RESIDENTS AND BUSINESSES ARE THE BENEFICIARIES.

description.48: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN / COMMUNITY DRIVEN SOLUTIONS GRANT IS TO EDUCATE THE COMMUNITY OF PORT ARTHUR, TX ON ENERGY POVERTY CONCERNS, COLLECT INFORMATION ON ENERGY EFFICIENCY NEEDS FROM THE COMMUNITY, PUT TOGETHER POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS TO ENERGY EFFICIENCY NEEDS AND PRESENT SOLUTIONS TO STAKEHOLDERS AND THE COMMUNITY.ACTIVITIES:THE RECIPIENT WILL HOST TWO COMMUNITY EDUCATION EVENTS, CREATE A STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES DOCUMENT AND DESIGN A QUESTIONNAIRE ON ENERGY-RELATED HOUSING CONCERNS, DISTRIBUTE THE QUESTIONNAIRE TO 100 RESIDENTS, INTERVIEW 40 RESIDENTS ABOUT THEIR RESPONSES, CONDUCT 10 MORE DETAILED FOLLOW UP INTERVIEWS, IDENTIFY POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS TO MATCH ENERGY NEEDS, CREATE AN ENERGY NEEDS AND ENERGY POVERTY ASSESSMENT, PRESENT RESULTS TO STAKEHOLDERS, AND HOST A COMMUNITY EXPO ON CLEAN ENERGY AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE TWO COMMUNITY EDUCATION EVENTS CONDUCTED, A STANDING OPERATING PROCEDURES AND QUESTIONNAIRE CREATED, DOCUMENTED FEEDBACK FROM OVER 40 RESIDENTS, AN ENERGY NEEDS AND ENERGY POVERTY ASSESSMENT, A STAKEHOLDER MEETING CONDUCTED, AND A COMMUNITY EXPO CONDUCTED. EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE HIGHER AWARENESS BY THE COMMUNITY ON ENERGY EFFICIENCY PROBLEMS AND SOLUTIONS SUCH AS EXPANDED ENERGY EFFICIENCY, WEATHERIZATION, HEATING/AIR CONDITIONING RETROFITS, CLEAN ENERGY, RESIDENTIAL SOLAR, AND SOLAR WATER HEATING. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES ARE RESIDENTS OF PORT ARTHUR, TX.
description.49: DESCRIPTION:THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL DEPLOY PROFESSIONALLY TRAINED DETECTION DOGS TO SURVEY FOR ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS AND COVID-19 IN CULTURALLY SIGNIFICANT LANDSCAPES ON AND SURROUNDING THE BLACKFEET NATION OF NORTH-CENTRAL MONTANA. CONSERVATION DETECTION DOGS TRAINED BY WORKING DOGS FOR CONSERVATION WILL BE USED TO FIND SCAT SAMPLES FROM TWO SENTINEL SPECIES: MINK AND OTTER. BOTH MINK AND OTTER ARE AQUATIC SPECIES EXPLOITING THE INVERTEBRATE AND PISCINE COMPONENTS OF AQUATIC FOOD WEBS, RESPECTIVELY. HEAVY METALS, PHARMACEUTICALS, FLAME RETARDANTS, AND COVID-19 CAN ALL BE RECOVERED FROM THESE TWO MUSTELIDS' SCATS. AS SUCH, THESE SPECIES CAN REVEAL THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF THESE CONTAMINANTS AND DISEASE. ACTIVITIES:K9 DETECTION AND MAPPING OF MINK AND OTTER SCAT.  THIS INCLUDES BASE TRAINING, SO THAT THE DOGS ARE TRAINED AND RELIABLE, FIELD-READY AND THEY WORK WELL WITH THE DOG HANDLER AS A TEAM. THE SECOND PART OF THE ACTIVITY IS A DEMONSTRATION TO COMMUNITY MEMBERS WHERE THE K9 SKILLS AND RELIABILITY ARE OBSERVED BY THE COMMUNITY.  THE FINAL PART OF THE K9 TRAINING IS THE ACTUAL FIELD DEPLOYMENT, WHERE SAMPLES ARE COLLECTED. THE SECOND PART OF THE GRANT WILL BE COMMUNITY INFORMATION DISSEMINATION. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:EFFICIENT SOURCING OF SAMPLES FROM SENTINEL SPECIES (MINK AND OTTER). HIGH QUALITY SAMPLES FOR ANALYSIS, CLEAR IDENTIFICATION OF CONTAMINANT AND DISEASE PATTERNS. TRUST AND BELIEF IN K9 METHODS, ACTION BASED ON SPATIAL/ECOLOGICAL PATTERNS OF CONTAMINATION OR DISEASE OBSERVED. HEALTHIER FOOD. LESS EXPOSURE TO CONTAMINANTS AND DISEASE, HEALTHIER BLACKFEET POPULATION. BETTER RESOURCE COLLECTION AND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS (SPECIFICALLY, AVOIDANCE OF EXISTING CONTAMINATION) CLEANUP OF CONTAMINATED AREAS AND PREVENTION OF FUTURE CONTAMINATION.
description.50: THIS AGREEMENT WILL PROVIDE FUNDING FOR THE STANDING ROCK SIOUX TRIBE TO ENABLE COLLABORATIVE EFFORTS OF THE TRIBE AND ITS PARTNERS TO BRING INTO EACH OF THE LOCAL TRIBAL DISTRICTS SKILL AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT, ALONG WITH SPECIALIZED TRAINING IN RISK AWARENESS AND OIL SPILL HAZARDS. RESPONSE TRAINING WILL BE PROVIDED TO COMMUNITY LEADERS THAT EACH LOCAL DISTRICT IDENTIFIES.  THE TRIBE IS FACING A PRESSING ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUE, THE BUILDING OF THE DAKOTA ACCESS PIPELINE UNDER LAKE OAHE, THE RESERVOIR BASIN CREATED BY THE DAM AND FLOODING OF THE MISSOURI RIVER. MULTIPLE PARTNERS ARE COMMITTED TO PROVIDING PREPARATION AND TRAINING ON EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS FOR POTENTIAL PIPELINE SPILLS AND LEAKS. AS THE COMMUNITY IDENTIFIES THE RISK, THEY CAN PROVIDE BETTER INFORMED DECISIONS TO THE DEVELOPED COMMUNITY PLANS OF ACTION THIS PROPOSAL ENVISIONS FOR OUR EFFECTED COMMUNITIES.

DESCRIPTION:HIGH COUNTRY CONSERVATION CENTER, (HC3) WILL DEVELOP A CLIMATE EQUITY PLAN THAT EMPOWERS SUMMIT COUNTY'S UNDERSERVED RESIDENTS TO PARTICIPATE IN CREATING CLIMATE ACTION SOLUTIONS WHILE IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR ALL RESIDENTS AND DECREASING GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS. - IDENTIFY PRIMARY CONCERNS, NEEDS, AND CHALLENGES FACED BY SUMMIT COUNTY'S UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES

- IMPLEMENT NEW CLIMATE ACTION SOLUTIONS BASED ON INPUT FROM STEERING COMMITTEE AND SUMMIT COUNTY'S UNDERSERVED RESIDENTSSUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:INCREASE IN # OF UNDERSERVED RESIDENTS THAT KNOW ABOUT LOCAL CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS AND THE CLIMATE ACTION PLAN (TARGET: 200)
- INCREASE IN # OF CLIMATE ACTION STRATEGIES AND PROGRAMS DESIGNED WITH UNDERSERVED COMMUNITY MEMBERS' INPUT (TARGET: 4 - 8)
- STRENGTHENED RELATIONSHIPS WITH COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS 
- INCREASED TRUST WITH SUMMIT COUNTY'S UNDERSERVED POPULATION 
- IMPLEMENTATION OF STRATEGIES OUTLINED IN CLIMATE EQUITY PLAN
- INCREASE IN # OF UNDERSERVED RESIDENTS WHO PARTICIPATE IN HC3'S CLIMATE ACTION PROGRAMS
- INCREASE IN COLLABORATION BETWEEN HC3 AND COMMUNITY GROUPS SERVING SUMMIT COUNTY'S UNDERSERVED RESIDENTS
- DECREASE IN GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS FROM PARTICIPATION IN HC3'S CLIMATE ACTION PROGRAMS

- PROGRAM PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN HC3 AND COMMUNITY GROUPS SERVING SUMMIT COUNTY'S UNDERSERVED POPULATION

THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE PARTNERS FOR A HEALTHIER COMMUNITY TO BUILD COMMUNITY LEADERSHIP ON AIR QUALITY, CLIMATE RESILIENCE, ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, URBAN FORESTRY AND COMMUNITY SCIENCE TO ADDRESS HEALTH OUTCOMES THROUGH THE MAINTENANCE AND EXPANSION OF AN AIR QUALITY MONITORING NETWORK IN THE CITIES OF SPRINGFIELD, HOLYOKE, AND CHICOPEE, MASSACHUSETTS. THE PROJECT WILL MAINTAIN AND EXPAND A SET OF AIR MONITORING SENSORS IN COMMUNITIES INCLUDING HOLYOKE, SPRINGFIELD, AND CHICOPEE, MASSACHUSETTS AND CONVENE LOCAL RESIDENT ADVISORS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF AIR QUALITY INFORMATION AND INCREASE ENGAGEMENT ON LOCAL ACTIONS TO IMPROVE AIR QUALITY.
ACTIVITIES:
PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE MAINTAINING AND EXPANDING THE CURRENT PIONEER VALLEY AIR QUALITY MONITORING (PVAQM) NETWORK OF OVER 50 SENSORS COLLECTING DATA ON PARTICULATE MATTER AND OZONE FOCUSING ON NEIGHBORHOODS WITH ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE CONCERNS IN HOLYOKE, SPRINGFIELD, CHICOPEE, AND OTHER NEARBY COMMUNITIES; INCLUSION OF RESIDENT VOICES THROUGH IDENTIFYING AND CONVENING RESIDENT ADVISORS WHO WILL TAKE LEADERSHIP ON EDUCATING THEIR COMMUNITY AND ADVOCATING FOR ACTIONS AND POLICIES THAT ADDRESS AIR POLLUTION, REMOVAL OF POLLUTION SOURCES AND PROMOTE CLIMATE RESILIENCE. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO USE THE INTERNET AND SOCIAL MEDIA TO PROVIDE RESIDENTS REAL-TIME DATA VIA A WEBSITE IN ENGLISH AND SPANISH THAT WILL INCLUDE A 'DASHBOARD' WITH CURRENT AIR QUALITY INFORMATION FROM THE SENSORS ALONG WITH TECHNICAL AND EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES INCLUDING RESPIRATORY DISEASE, CLIMATE CHANGE AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE.
OUTCOMES:
ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE RECRUITING AND TRAINING 10 RESIDENT ADVISORS, CREATING A NEW WEB-BASED PLATFORM FOR SHARING AIR QUALITY SENSOR DATA, DEVELOPING NEW EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS FOR USE IN OUTREACH TO 10 SCHOOLS/COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS EACH YEAR, AND 10 COMMUNITY AND SCHOOL PRESENTATIONS. 

EXPECTED ENVIRONMENTAL OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT ARE IMPROVED AIR QUALITY, A REDUCTION IN EXPOSURE TO AIR POLLUTANTS, INCREASED CLIMATE RESILIENCE, REDUCTION IN ASTHMA, REDUCTION IN CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE MORBIDITY AND AN OVERALL IMPROVEMENT IN HEALTH IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY AS AIR POLLUTANTS DECREASE, AIR QUALITY IMPROVES, AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE MEASURES ARE INSTITUTED. 

DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE RESIDENTS OF SPRINGFIELD, HOLYOKE, AND CHICOPEE, MASSACHUSETTS WHO ARE PREDOMINANTLY BLACK, LATINO, AND/OR LOW INCOME. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: 1) COLLECTING SURVEYS ABOUT RESIDENTS' EXPERIENCES WITH ISSUES INCLUDING TREE INEQUITY, ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH; 2) HOLDING ONE-ON-ONE INTERVIEWS WITH RESIDENTS AND GATHERING THEIR PERSONAL STORIES ABOUT LIVED EXPERIENCES REGARDING TREE INEQUITY AND AIR QUALITY; AND 3) CREATING COMMUNITY WALKS TO EDUCATE ADDITIONAL RESIDENTS ABOUT THE IMPORTANCE OF URBAN TREES. 

THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE COMMUNITY MEETINGS AND TREE WALKS IN THREE BOSTON NEIGHBORHOODS THAT FACE INCREASED ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH BURDENS FROM POLLUTED AIR, LESS GREENSPACE, AND LOW TREE CANOPY COVERAGE. SPEAK FOR THE TREES WILL COLLABORATE WITH PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS TO 1) PREPARE COMMUNITY SURVEYS AND OUTREACH MATERIALS; 2) ENGAGE WITH RESIDENTS THROUGH SURVEYS, INTERVIEWS, AND PRESENTATIONS ABOUT TREE EQUITY AT THREE OR MORE COMMUNITY MEETINGS IN TARGET NEIGHBORHOODS; 3) CREATE MAPS AND EDUCATIONAL CONTENT FOR COMMUNITY TREE WALKS BASED ON SURVEY RESPONSES AND AMERICAN FORESTS' TREE EQUITY SCORE ANALYZER; 4) CONDUCT SIX COMMUNITY TREE WALKS FOR PUBLIC AWARENESS AND INCREASING KNOWLEDGE ABOUT AIR POLLUTION AND THE ROLE OF TREE CANOPY; AND 5) SHARING OF 'ARTIFACTS,' EITHER DIGITAL OR PRINT, CREATED BY EACH NEIGHBORHOOD TO SHARE RESULTS.SUBRECIPIENT:THREE NEIGHBORHOOD ORGANIZATIONS WILL RECEIVE SUBAWARDS TO PROVIDE CONSULTATION AND PARTNERSHIP ON COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND OUTREACH. EACH NEIGHBORHOOD GROUP WILL CO-DEVELOP THE COMMUNITY TREE WALKS, HOST NEIGHBORHOOD MEETINGS, ADVERTISE THE PROJECT TO RESIDENTS, AND ASSIST WITH EVENT PLANNING. EACH GROUP WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ENSURING A MINIMUM OF 20 RESIDENTS ATTEND MEETINGS, THAT ATTENDEES FILL OUT IN-MEETING EVALUATION AND FEEDBACK FORMS, AND THAT 60 RESIDENTS IN TOTAL ATTEND EACH COMMUNITY'S WALKS.

EMVISION AND EVERYDAY BOSTON WILL ASSIST WITH IN-MEETING EVALUATION DESIGN, DEVELOP AND CARRY OUT INTERVIEWS, AND CAPTURE AND CURATE VIDEOS OF RESIDENTS' STORIES AND THE COMMUNITY TREE WALKS. EVERYDAY BOSTON, A LOCAL GRASSROOTS NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION THAT CONNECTS NEIGHBORHOODS THROUGH THE SHARING OF STORIES WILL PROVIDE AND CAPTURE RESIDENT INTERVIEWS. description.65: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN (ARP) FUNDED GRANT IS TO INCREASE UNDERSTANDING OF RESIDENTS' CURRENT EXPERIENCE OF EXTREME HEAT, HOUSING, AND FOOD INSECURITY IN EVERETT, MASSACHUSETTS, IN ORDER TO IMPLEMENT CLIMATE RESILIENCE EFFORTS AND ENSURE THAT POTENTIAL STRATEGIES TO COMBAT THESE ISSUES DO NOT INCREASE SOCIAL INEQUITIES, SUCH AS GENTRIFICATION AND DISPLACEMENT OF LOWER-INCOME AND WORKING-CLASS RESIDENTS. EVERETT HAD ONE OF THE HIGHEST RATES OF COVID INFECTION IN THE STATE, WITH ANALYSIS SHOWING THAT COMMUNITIES OF COLOR WERE PARTICULARLY HARD HIT, AND EVERETT RESIDENTS ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY IMPACTED BY POOR AIR QUALITY. PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN THIS PROJECT AS AUTHORIZED UNDER CAA 103(B)(3), THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO: EXAMINE POLICIES, PLANS AND PROGRAMS THAT WERE ACTIVATED DURING THE PANDEMIC VIA MUNICIPAL AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS IN EVERETT THROUGH PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH; IDENTIFY IF STRATEGIES ARE ADAPTABLE OR CAN BE IMPROVED UPON FOR LONG-TERM CLIMATE RESILIENCE, WITH A PARTICULAR FOCUS ON EXTREME HEAT AND HOUSING AND FOOD INSECURITY; AND DETERMINE RESIDENT-LED POLICY, SYSTEMS AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE STRATEGIES TO COMBAT EXTREME HEAT AND HOUSING AND FOOD INSECURITY.ACTIVITIES:IN ACCORDANCE WITH CLEAN AIR ACT, SECTION 103(B)(3), THIS PROJECT WILL COLLECT DATA AND INFORMATION, CONDUCT A PUBLIC HEALTH ASSESSMENT, AND PROVIDE COMMUNITY EDUCATION TO EXPLORE CAUSES OF EXTREME HEAT AND AIR POLLUTION, HOUSING, AND FOOD INSECURITY, AND EXPLORE STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT LONG-TERM CLIMATE RESILIENCE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: 1) LEADING A COMMUNITY PUBLIC HEALTH ASSESSMENT USING A PARTICIPATORY ACTION RESEARCH (PAR) MODEL FROM THE HEALTHY NEIGHBORHOODS STUDY (HNS) MENTORSHIP PROGRAM, INCLUDING RESEARCH AND TRAINING FOR RESIDENTS AND THE REVIEW OF EXISTING CLIMATE POLICIES; 2) FACILITATING 6 WORKSHOPS WITH THE GREATER BOSTON ANTI-DISPLACEMENT TOOLKIT TO ENGAGE OVER 30 COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN IDENTIFYING STRATEGIES TO COMBAT CLIMATE INTENSIFIED HEALTH RISKS RELATED TO EXTREME HEAT, HOUSING INSTABILITY AND FOOD INSECURITY; AND 3) IDENTIFYING AND PRESENTING 1-2 CLIMATE RESILIENCE STRATEGIES AND PUBLIC HEALTH ASSESSMENT FINDINGS TO A COHORT OF THREE COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS AND AT LEAST 30 RESIDENTS.SUBRECIPIENT:TWO EVERETT-BASED ORGANIZATIONS WILL RECEIVE SUBAWARDS TO COMPLETE ELEMENTS OF THIS PROJECT. EVERETT COMMUNITY GROWERS (ECG), A COMMUNITY-BASED FOOD JUSTICE ORGANIZATION, WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND WILL HIRE A COMMUNITY ORGANIZER TO COORDINATE PROJECT ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. OTHER ECG STAFF, SUCH AS THE YOUTH CREW, WILL PARTICIPATE IN  TRAINING, ASSESSMENT, AND ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. ECG WILL ALSO PROVIDE IN-KIND PROJECT MANAGEMENT SUPPORT THROUGH THEIR PLANNING AND POLICY COORDINATOR AND DEVELOPMENT COORDINATOR. ECG WILL UTILIZE THEIR FARM AND COMMUNITY GARDENS AS COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT SPACE, TO EXEMPLIFY HOW GROWING SPACES COMBAT THE HEAT ISLAND EFFECT WHILE ALSO PROVIDING A SPACE TO GATHER, GROW, AND EXPERIENCE FOOD. ONE EVERETT (OE) IS A COALITION OF COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS (CBOS) AND RESIDENTS ORGANIZING FOR A COMMUNITY THAT VALUES, ACTS AND ADVOCATES FOR JUSTICE, TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY, FIGHTING AGAINST SYSTEMIC RACISM AND XENOPHOBIA. MEMBERS OF OE WILL BE TRAINED TO LEAD THE ACTIVITIES OF THE ASSESSMENT AND ORGANIZE THE COMMUNITY AROUND THE PLANNED ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. MEMBERS WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PARTICIPATING IN TRAINING, COMPLETING THE MODULES ADAPTED FROM THE GREATER BOSTON ANTI-DISPLACEMENT TOOLKIT AND SELECTING A PILOT STRATEGY AS AN OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT.OUTCOMES:THE INTENDED BENEFICIARY OF THIS PROJECT IS THE CITY OF EVERETT, MASSACHUSETTS. EVERETT RESIDENTS ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY IMPACTED BY CORONAVIRUS (COVID) INFECTIONS AND POOR

description.69: THIS ACTION APPROVES AN AWARD OF $120,000 TO MISSISSIPPI BAND OF CHOCTAW INDIAN'S TO DEVELOP AND BEGIN IMPLEMENTATION OF A SUSTAINABLE SOLUTION FOR ILLEGAL DUMPSITES. description.71: THIS PROJECT ENTITLED 'DEVELOPMENT OF A COMMUNITY ACTION PLAN FOR CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION EMPLOYING CLEAN ENERGY TECHNOLOGY,' RELATES TO THE CLEAN AIR ACT AND ADDRESSES ADVERSE CONDITIONS OF AIR QUALITY ATTRIBUTED TO AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES, ELECTRICITY SOURCES GENERATING CARBON DIOXIDE, AND GENERAL CAR EMISSIONS. THIS PROJECT LEVERAGES COMMUNITY, TRIBAL, AND INDUSTRY COLLABORATION TO DEVELOP A COMMUNITY ACTION PLAN TO MITIGATE AIR QUALITY AND REGIONAL CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS THROUGH THE IMPLEMENTING RENEWABLE ENERGY TECHNOLOGY.
