description.72: THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THE PUBLIC HEALTH ASPECTS OF PROVIDING SAFE DRINKING WATER UNDER THE SAFE DRINKING WATER ACT, SECTION 1442(B)(3). IT COMBINES TRAINING, EDUCATION, AND EMPLOYMENT, RELATED TO PUBLIC HEALTH, HELPING COMMUNITY MEMBERS LEARN HOW TO PLAN FOR THEIR FAMILIES IN THE EVENT OF AN EMERGENCY OR NATURAL DISASTER. THE JUNEAU COMMUNITY IS SURROUNDED BY FRESH AND SALTWATER BODIES WITHOUT ROAD ACCESS TO FOOD AND CLEAN WATER IN THE EVENT OF EMERGENCIES OR DISASTERS. THEREFORE, KNOWING HOW TO OBTAIN AND STORE DRINKABLE WATER IS CRUCIAL FOR SURVIVAL OF THE TLINGIT AND HAIDA TRIBES AND SURROUNDING VILLAGES AND COMMUNITIES. THE LONG-TERM OUTCOMES OF THE TWO CONFERENCES INCLUDE CHANGING BEHAVIOR AND/OR KNOWLEDGE OF TRIBAL MEMBERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC.
description.73: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT IS TO INCREASE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO INDOOR AIR HEALTH CONCERNS DUE TO COVID-19 STAY-AT-HOME ORDERS IN THE COTTAGE GROVE AND ADJACENT NEIGHBORHOODS IN GREENSBORO, NORTH CAROLINA. THIS ACTION APPROVES AN AWARD IN THE AMOUNT OF $75,000 TO THE NEW HOPE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT GROUP, INC.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE CONDUCTING INDIVIDUAL AND COMMUNITY TRAINING SESSIONS, DISTRIBUTION OF INFORMATION AND RESOURCES FOR INFORMED CHOICES TO IMPROVE HOME AIR QUALITY. THROUGH TELEPHONE AND FACE-TO-FACE ASSESSMENTS, RESIDENTS WILL BE EVALUATED TO DETERMINE IF THEY HAVE INDOOR AIR ISSUES THAT HAVE INCREASED DUE TO COVID-19.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES ARE ARTICLES FOR COMMUNITY AND PARTNER NEWSLETTERS, MEETINGS, VIDEO, FLYERS, AND PRESENTATIONS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED KNOWLEDGE, IMPROVED HOME ENVIRONMENTS AND REDUCED SOCIAL ISOLATION FOR SENIOR RESIDENTS IN THE COTTAGE GROVE NEIGHBORHOOD IN GREENSBORO, NC.
description.74: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO AMERICAN SAMOA EPA. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES UNDERSERVED RESIDENTS' INCREASED EXPOSURE TO OUTDOOR POLLUTANTS AS AN UNINTENDED CONSEQUENCE OF LOCAL STAY-AT-HOME ORDERS. SPECIFICALLY, PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE THE PURCHASE OF FOUR PERMANENT AIR QUALITY MONITORING STATIONS INSTALLED STRATEGICALLY ACROSS THE ISLAND OF TUTUILA TO MEASURE REAL TIME AIR QUALITY. THESE STATIONS WILL COLLECT AIR QUALITY DATA THAT WILL BE USED TO ASSESS THE AIR QUALITY FOR THE ENTIRE ISLAND AND ASSIST AIR QUALITY REGULATORY AGENCIES, DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND PUBLIC SAFETY ORGANIZATIONS TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS AND DEVELOP PLANS ON HOW TO IMPROVE AIR QUALITY ENFORCEMENT AND ENSURE AIR QUALITY ON THE ISLAND. THE AIR QUALITY INFORMATION WILL MEASURE THE EMISSION OF VARIOUS AIR POLLUTANTS CAUSED BY OPEN BURNING. THE ENVIRONMENTAL OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE USING THE AIR QUALITY DATA FOR PUBLIC EDUCATION TO RAISE AWA
description.75: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO CONTRA COSTA HEALTH SERVICES TO EXPAND ON: 1) CONTRA COSTA ASTHMA HOME VISITING PROGRAM, A PROGRAM THAT PROVIDES CLINICAL ASTHMA TRIGGER ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT, EDUCATION AND TRAINING ON GENERAL HEALTHY HOMES ACTIVITIES TO PREVENT INDOOR AIR POLLUTION FOR ASTHMA PATIENTS INSURED THROUGH MEDICAID AND 2) EXISTING PROMOTORA PROGRAMS DESIGNED TO PROVIDE TRAINING ON AIR QUALITY, AIR POLLUTION MITIGATION AND COMMUNITY ACTION MODEL THAT EMPOWERS PATIENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO BE DECISION-MAKING STAKEHOLDERS IN LOCAL INITIATIVES AND POLICIES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING AN ONGOING PARTNERSHIPS TO CONTINUOUSLY CO-DEVELOP PRIORITIES AND STRATEGIES; LEVERAGING LOCAL RESOURCES TO PROMOTE EDUCATION ON ISSUES RELATED TO HEALTH CONCERNS STEMMING FROM INDOOR AIR POLLUTION AND RELATED ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY; COLLABORATIVELY EMPOWER ASTHMA PATIENTS THROUGH TRAINING TO SERVE AS DECISION-MAKING PARTN
description.76: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED GRANT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER SECTION 104(B)(3) OF THE CLEAN WATER ACT AND SECTION 1442(C)(3) OF THE SAFE DRINKING WATER ACT (SDWA) TO COTTONWOOD GULCH EXPEDITIONS TO EDUCATE LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES OF COLOR LIVING IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO HAZARDOUS WASTE SITES IN ALBUQUERQUE AND GALLUP, NEW MEXICO, ON THE CONNECTION BETWEEN WATER QUALITY AND IMPACTS TO ECOLOGICAL AND HUMAN HEALTH. THE PRIMARY PROJECT OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A DRINKING-WATER QUALITY, PUBLIC HEALTH, AND WATERSHED AWARENESS CURRICULUM FOR 400 EIGHTH-GRADE STUDENTS. CLEAN WATER IS NECESSARY FOR THE PROPER WASHING OF HANDS. HANDWASHING IS A WELL-ACCEPTED APPROACH TO COMBATING THE SPREAD OF COVID-19. SDWA 1442 GRANT PROJECTS CONTRIBUTE TO PROVIDING CLEAN WATER FOR HANDWASHING IN COMBATTING THE SPREAD OF COVID-19.ACTIVITIES:PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: 1) DEVELOPING A NEW CLASSROOM CURRICULUM FOCUSED ON WATERSHEDS, WATER QUALITY, AND DRINKING WATER; 2) CONDUCTING CLASSROOM INSTRUCTION ON WATERSHED MODELING, IDENTIFYING LOCAL SUPERFUND SITES, AND LEARNING ABOUT WATER CONTAMINATION; 3) DEVELOPING A FIELD CURRICULUM FOCUSED ON SURFACE WATER AND DRINKING WATER QUALITY TESTING; 4) FACILITATING SURFACE WATER TESTING IN THE FIELD DURING FIELD-BASED EDUCATION PROGRAMS IN THE WILDERNESS AREA OF NEW MEXICO PUBLIC LANDS; 5) CONDUCTING APPLIED, PRACTICAL TRAINING WITH STUDENTS SO THEY ARE ABLE TO TEST WATER QUALITY BOTH IN THEIR HOMES, IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY, AND IN THE ENVIRONMENT; 6) GENERATING A DATASET TO EDUCATE STUDENTS ON TRENDS AND PATTERNS IN DRINKING AND SURFACE WATER QUALITY; AND 7) CONDUCTING PRE- AND POST-PROGRAM SURVEYS TO ASSESS STUDENTS' UNDERSTANDING OF THESE TOPICS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:PROJECT DELIVERABLES INCLUDE CLASSROOM CURRICULUM FOCUSED ON WATERSHEDS, WATER QUALITY, AND DRINKING WATER AND FIELD CURRICULUM FOCUSED ON SURFACE WATER AND DRINKING WATER QUALITY TESTING. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATHEMATICS (STEM) AS CAREERS THAT ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE (EJ) ISSUES, COMMUNITIES THAT RECOGNIZE THE IMPORTANCE OF WATER QUALITY, AND STUDENT BODIES THAT RECOGNIZE THE LINK BETWEEN WATER QUALITY AND EJ. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES ARE EIGHTH-GRADE STUDENTS IN ALBUQUERQUE AND GALLUP, NEW MEXICO.
description.77: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER SECTION 103(B) OF THE CLEAN AIR ACT TO VISTA COMMUNITY CLINIC (VCC) TO UPDATE AND MODERNIZE AN EXISTING FARMWORKER-SPECIFIC EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN AND TO DESIGN AND DELIVER A CURRICULUM TO TRAIN FARMWORKERS ON EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS, AS WELL AS WILDFIRE AND COVID-19 RISK MITIGATION. FARMWORKERS IN SAN DIEGO COUNTY, CALIFORNIA ARE OFTEN EXPLOITED FOR CHEAP LABOR, AND MANY FACE SIGNIFICANT INSECURITY DUE TO THEIR LACK OF LEGAL IMMIGRATION STATUS. THE TARGETED UNDERSERVED POPULATION OF FARMWORKERS IS PREDOMINANTLY LATINX (82.1%), UNINSURED (35.9%), AND LIVING 200% BELOW THE FEDERAL POVERTY LINE (96.6%). THIS POPULATION ALSO FACES SIGNIFICANT HOUSING INSECURITY, INSUFFICIENT NUTRITIONAL ACCESS, EXPOSURE TO PESTICIDES, AND INCREASED ELEMENTAL EXPOSURE INCLUDING HEAT, SUN, COLD, RAIN, AS WELL IS PERSISTENCE OF HEALTH CONDITIONS SUCH AS RESPIRATORY ISSUES, DIABETES, AND HYPERTENSION. PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED RESPIRATORY ISSUES LIKE ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO  BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.. ACTIVITIES:THE PLANNING FOR THE ROAD AHEAD PROGRAM AIMS TO FIRST CONDUCT A NEEDS-BASED ASSESSMENT FOR THE FARMWORKER POPULATION IN ORDER TO DESIGN HEALTH EDUCATION TOOLS USED TO TRAIN PROMOTORES (CHWS) FOR THE DISSEMINATION OF A FARMWORKER-SPECIFIC EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN THAT ALSO ADDRESSES WILDFIRE RISKS, HEALTHCARE ACCESS, FARMWORKER-SPECIFIC HEALTH DISPARITIES, AND COVID-19. TRAININGS WILL BE CONDUCTED LOCALLY AS WELL AS NATIONALLY USING ONLINE WORKSHOPS. THE EFFECTIVENESS OF TRAINING AND EDUCATION MATERIALS WILL BE EVALUATED BASED ON DOCUMENTATION OF COMPLETION OF CURRICULA, HOW MANY COMMUNITIES USE THE WORKSHOP TO DEVELOP THEIR OWN EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS PLAN (EPP), AND SURVEY DATA COLLECTED FROM WORKSHOP PARTICIPANTS ON THEIR SATISFACTION AFTER TRAINING. SUBRECIPIENT:THE SUBAWARD FUNDS WILL BE USED TO SUPPORT CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT, TO DEVELOP A FARMWORKER EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS PLAN, AND DISSEMINATE PROJECT RESULTS LOCALLY AND NATIONALLY.  SUBAWARD FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TO SUPPORT COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS IN AN ADVISORY ROLE ON THE PROJECT.  COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS WILL SERVE ON THE PROJECT'S ADVISORY BOARD, SHARE THEIR EXPERTISE, AND PROVIDE ACCESS TO COMMUNITIES AND RESOURCES WITHIN THEIR OWN NETWORKS.OUTCOMES:THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE PLANNING FOR THE ROAD AHEAD PROJECT ARE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA FARMWORKERS, FARMWORKERS AROUND THE U.S., AND PROMOTORES THAT OVERSEE THE HEALTH AND SAFETY OF THE WORKERS.

OUTCOMES:
THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL PROGRESS AND FINAL REPORTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: 1) DEMONSTRATION AND VALIDATION OF A NEW APPROACH FOR DETECTION AND QUANTIFICATION FOR PLASTIC ADDITIVES OF EMERGING CONCERN IN PARTICULATE MATTER; AND 2) NEW INSIGHTS AND KNOWLEDGE THAT WILL HELP TO INFORM ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT AND RISK ASSESSMENT ANALYSES OF PLASTIC ADDITIVES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC WHO ARE AFFECTED BY EXPOSURE TO PLASTIC ADDITIVES IN PARTICULATE MATTER.

description.80:
DESCRIPTION:CCLR WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT IN ALASKA TO FACILITATE THE ENGAGEMENT OF DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES 
IN THE EPA ROADSHOW WORKSHOPS ON INFLATION REDUCTION ACT FUNDING TO FACILITATE THEIR ABILITY TO 
PARTICIPATE IN GOVERNMENTAL PROCESSES RELATED TO ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE JUSTICE. THEY WILL 
DO THIS BY VARIOUS MEANS INCLUDING:
(1) BUILDING AND EXPLAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES TO BE ENGAGED IN GOVERNMENTAL 
PROCESSES FOR AWARDING IRA FUNDING ('GOVERNMENTAL PROCESSES') ; (2) LEARN ABOUT IRA FUNDED PROGRAMS SO 
DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES CAN BE MORE INVOLVED IN GOVERNMENTAL PROCESSES THAT IMPACT THEM RELATED TO 
ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE JUSTICE, AND (3) WORKING WITH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROVIDERS TO FACILITATE THE 
ENGAGEMENT OF DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES IN GOVERNMENTAL PROCESSES. EPA WILL WORK WITH CCLR TO 
ENSURE THAT THE WORK IS DESIGNED TO FACILITATE THE ENGAGEMENT OF COMMUNITIES THAT ARE CONSIDERED 
DISADVANTAGED, BASED ON EPAS DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES MAP , IN GOVERNMENTAL PROCESSES.
CCLR WILL BE WORKING IN DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES, AS DESIGNATED ON THE EPA IRA DISADVANTAGED 
COMMUNITIES MAP, AVAILABLE IN EJSCREENACTIVITIES:EPA'S FY 2022-2026 GOAL 2.1 IS TO PROMOTE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND CIVIL RIGHTS AT THE FEDERAL, TRIBAL, STATE, AND LOCAL LEVELS.
THIS PROJECT CONTRIBUTES TO THIS GOAL BY FOCUSING ON COMMUNITY CAPACITY BUILDING, ORGANIZING, AND EDUCATION. SPECIFICALLY, IT
ADDRESSES THE ISSUE OF AVAILABLE TO CONFRONT THE CLIMATE CRISIS AND REDUCE POLLUTION. 
THE PUBLIC WILL DIRECTLY BENEFIT FROM THIS AWARD THROUGH THE ACTIVITIES DESIGNED TO FACILITATE THE ENGAGEMENT OF DISADVANTAGED 
COMMUNITIES IN GOVERNMENTAL PROCESSES. PUBLIC ATTENDEES WILL RECEIVE TRAVEL ASSISTANCE AND MEALS TO OFFSET THE COST OF
PARTICIPATION. ATTENDEES WILL ALSO HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO DIRECTLY ENGAGE WITH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROVIDERS AND POTENTIALLY 
ESTABLISH COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS TO HELP DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES BE INVOLVED IN GOVERNMENTAL PROCESSES.
COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL HAVE A BETTER KNOWLEDGE OF ENVIRONMENTAL REGULATIONS AND THE ROLE EPA PLAYS AS A FEDERAL AGENCY, AND 
HOW THEY CAN HAVE INPUT INTO DECISIONS EPA MAKES, AS WELL AS HOW THEY CAN LEVERAGE FEDERAL RESOURCES AND PROVIDE INPUT ON 
ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE JUSTICE ISSUES. LOCAL LEADERS WILL HAVE A GREATER KNOWLEDGE OF HOW THEY CAN COME TOGETHER AS 
COMMUNITY TO CREATE TANGIBLE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPROVEMENT AND BE MORE INVOLVED IN GOVERNMENTAL DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES. 
IN PERSON AND COMMUNITY-BASED EVENTS SUCH AS THESE HELP PARTICIPANTS FROM DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES. THESE EVENTS WILL 
GENERATE INFORMATION AND RESOURCES THAT ENABLE THE COMMUNITIES TO IDENTIFY AND ACCESS FUNDING FOR ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE 
JUSTICE ACTIVITIES. ALSO, IT GIVES THEM OPPORTUNITIES AND OTHER RESOURCES THAT WILL FACILITATE THEIR ENGAGEMENT IN GOVERNMENTAL 
PROCESSES. EPA WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM CCLR'S WORK BY OBTAINING INPUT FROM MEMBERS OF DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES THAT WILL ASSIST 
EPA IN DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING IRA GRANT PROGRAMS MORE EFFECTIVELY.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:HELP PROVIDE ACCESS, RESOURCES, AND GRANT INFORMATION TO 
DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES SO THEY CAN BE MORE 
INVOLVED IN THE DECISIONS THAT AFFECT THEM.

DESCRIPTION:
THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER SECTION 103 OF THE CLEAN AIR ACT TO BIKEWALKKC TO CONDUCT AN EVALUATION OF THE IMPACTS OF A ZERO-FARE BUS TRANSIT (ZBT) POLICY BASED ON BUS USE, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH FOR RESIDENTS OF KANSAS CITY'S MOST IMPOVERISHED NEIGHBORHOODS. 
ACTIVITIES:
TO ADDRESS HEALTH DISPARITIES AND LIMIT COVID-19 RISKS AMONG THESE RESIDENTS, THE GETTING AROUND KANSAS CITY PROJECT WILL INITIALLY COLLECT DATA REGARDING KANSAS CITY BUS USE, EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF A ZBT POLICY ON RATES OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY USING ACTIVITY-TRACKING BELTS WORN BY PROJECT PARTICIPANTS, IDENTIFY FURTHER BARRIERS TO TRANSPORTATION ACCESS, AND THEN DETERMINE THE VALUE OF A ZBT POLICY FOR LOW-INCOME RESIDENTS BASED ON HOW IT INCREASES PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, LOWERS COVID-19 RISKS, AND IMPROVES HEALTHCARE ACCESS. 


OUTCOMES:
BY INCREASING ACCESS TO A NO-COST BUS SYSTEM, THE GETTING AROUND KANSAS CITY PROJECT ANTICIPATES THE FOLLOWING OUTCOMES: INCREASE ACCESS TO WALKABLE NEIGHBORHOODS AND TO HEALTHCARE FACILITIES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE THE LOW-INCOME AND UNDERSERVED RESIDENTS. 
SUBRECIPIENT:
UMKC&RSQUO;S PLANNED ROLES INCLUDE:

&BULL;	PARTICIPATE IN PLANNING CALLS AND MEETINGS WITH BWKC AND OTHER PARTNERS

&BULL;	LEAD ACCELEROMETER AND GPS TRACKER DATA PROCESSING AND ANALYSES.
&BULL;	CONTRIBUTE TO STATISTICAL ANALYSES.

DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT (FUNDED WITH AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN APPROPRIATIONS) IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO HARTFORD PARENT UNIVERSITY, INC. (HPU) TO PROVIDE TRAINING UNDER SECTION 103 OF THE CLEAN AIR ACT (CAA) AND SECTION 1442 OF THE SAFE DRINKING WATER ACT (SDWA) TO HARTFORD PARENTS SO THAT THEY CAN EDUCATE THE YOUTH OF HARTFORD ON THE DANGERS OF LEAD POISONING IN THE HOME, SCHOOL, AND IN THE DRINKING WATER SUPPLY. HPU PLANS TO INITIALLY FOCUS ON OUTREACH, EDUCATION, AND TRAINING OF PARENTS TO IMPROVE SCREENING AND TESTING FOR LEAD CONTAMINANTS IN WATER AND TO IDENTIFY LEAD PAINT IN HOMES.  HARTFORD HAS MANY RESIDENCES CONSTRUCTED BEFORE 1960, 18 YEARS BEFORE LEAD-BASED PAINTS WERE BANNED FOR USE. THIS INDICATES HIGH USAGE OF LEAD-BASED PAINTS IN EXISTING BUILDINGS IN HARTFORD, TO WHICH COMMUNITY MEMBERS, ESPECIALLY CHILDREN, ARE REGULARLY EXPOSED. WITHIN THEIR TWO-YEAR PLAN, HPU WILL EDUCATE FAMILIES ON THE DANGERS OF LEAD CONTAMINATION AND HOW TO PREVENT LEAD EXPOSURE TO KEEP LOCAL FAMILIES AND CHILDREN SAFE.

CAA 103(B)(3): PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.

SDWA 1442: HANDWASHING IS A WELL-ACCEPTED APPROACH TO COMBATING THE SPREAD OF COVID-19. CLEAN WATER IS NECESSARY FOR THE PROPER WASHING OF HANDS. SDWA 1442 GRANT PROJECTS CONTRIBUTE TO PROVIDING CLEAN WATER FOR HANDWASHING IN COMBATTING THE SPREAD OF COVID-19.
ACTIVITIES:ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE: (1) EDUCATING 1,000 FAMILIES ON LEAD CONTAMINATION DANGERS AND (2) CONDUCT REVIEWS OF HOUSING STOCK TO CREATE A MAP OF 30 LEAD POLLUTED AND AFFECTED BUILDINGS IN HARTFORD TO DIRECTLY PROTECT THE FAMILIES OF HARTFORD, CONNECTICUT (CT) FROM LEAD POLLUTANT EXPOSURES. HARTFORD PARENT UNIVERSITY WILL USE FUNDING TO OPERATE PARENT TRAINING SESSIONS, PAY FOR LEAD TESTING KITS, FUND STAFF TRAVEL, AND PAY FOR COMMUNITY-DISTRIBUTED MATERIALS EDUCATING ABOUT THE DANGERS AND METHODS OF EXPOSURE OF LEAD POLLUTANTS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: (1) 1,000 STAKEHOLDERS ARMED WITH KNOWLEDGE AND AWARENESS ABOUT LEAD POISONING, AND (2) 30 HOMES IN HIGH RISK NEIGHBORHOODS WILL BE EVALUATED FOR LEAD CONTAMINATION IN WATER AND THE ENVIRONMENT. 

INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE DIRECTLY PROTECTING THE FAMILIES OF HARTFORD, CT FROM LEAD POLLUTANT EXPOSURES.  AN INVOLVED AND EDUCATED COMMUNITY IS BETTER EQUIPPED TO PARTICIPATE IN EFFORTS TO PROTECT THEMSELVES AND THE ENVIRONMENT.

DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT AGREEMENT IS TO USE THE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN (ARP) GRANT FUNDING TO CREATE A FUNCTIONING COMMUNITY GARDEN FOR LOW-INCOME SENIORS, NEIGHBORS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS IN NEW HAVEN, CONNECTICUT BY THE TOWERS FOUNDATION. THE PRODUCTIVE GREEN SPACE WILL INCLUDE A COMMUNITY GARDEN AND TEACHING SPACE FOR TOWERS' LOW-INCOME SENIOR CITIZEN RESIDENTS. THE GREEN SPACE WILL IMPROVE AIR QUALITY AND REDUCE THE NEED FOR BUSES TO TRANSPORT PEOPLE TO THE GROCERY STORE FOR FRESH PRODUCE. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO IMPROVE LOCAL RESIDENT AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND PUBLIC HEALTH CONDITIONS RELATED TO LOCAL AMBIENT AIR QUALITY. THIS PROJECT CAN BE FUNDED UNDER SECTION 103(B) OF THE CLEAN AIR ACT (CAA). THE TOWERS FOUNDATION IS THE SUPPORTING ORGANIZATION TO THE TOWERS AT TOWER LANE, THE MAIN HOME FOR GREATER NEW HAVEN'S LOW INCOME ELDERLY AND MINORITY POPULATION SERVICING OVER 300 LOW INCOME, DIVERSE SENIORS. THE TOWERS IS SURROUNDED BY I-95 AND I-91 PUTTING IT IN VERY CLOSE PROXIMITY TO TRAFFIC AND THE PROJECT'S OBJECTIVE IS TO PROVIDE ENVIRONMENTAL AND NUTRITIONAL ASSETS THAT WILL LEAD TO HIGHER QUALITY OF LIFE AND STRONGER COMMUNITY HEALTH. CAA 103(B)(3): PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.
ACTIVITIES:ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE: ASSEMBLE A TASK FORCE OF 12 RESIDENTS, PLAN AND DESIGN A NEW GREEN SPACE WITH GARDEN AND LEARNING SPACES, CREATE SIX RAISED BEDS, GENERATE LOCAL GARDEN PRODUCE, REACH OVER 300 RESIDENTS TO RAISE AWARENESS ON ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES INCLUDING BENEFITS OF GREEN SPACE AND SELECTING HEALTHY FOOD CHOICES AND IMPROVEMENTS IN AMBIENT AIR QUALITY. THE PROJECT WILL TRACK THE AMOUNT OF HARVEST PRODUCED, GREEN SPACE INCREASED AND CONDUCT FOUR EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE AN INCREASED QUALITY OF LIFE AND COMMUNITY HEALTH THROUGH:  1. IMPROVED AIR QUALITY AND GREEN SPACE FROM ADDED TREES, PLANTS, AND SHADE; 2. REDUCED FOOD INSECURITY RESULTING FROM THE INCREASE OF LOCAL, HEALTHY PRODUCE; 3. INCREASED NUTRITIONAL HEALTH FROM CONSUMING LOCAL FRESH PRODUCE THROUGH NEW GARDENS; 4. EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TO LEARN MORE ABOUT LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES INCLUDING AMBIENT AIR QUALITY; AND 5. EXPANDED SOCIALIZATION AND IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE THROUGH ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH ACTIVITIES WITH OTHER RESIDENTS, FAMILIES, FRIENDS, AND NEIGHBORS. INTENDED AND DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE LOW-INCOME SENIOR CITIZENS, NEIGHBORS AND COMMUNITY RESIDENTS IN NEW HAVEN, CONNECTICUT.
description.84: THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO COLLECT DATA ON MERCURY CONCENTRATIONS IN FISH AND CRAYFISH FROM LAKES SUBJECT TO PENOBSCOT INDIAN NATION SUSTENANCE FISHING RIGHTS.  OUTPUTS INCLUDE THE CREATION OF A TRIBAL MERCURY ADVISORY COUNCIL, THE COLLECTION AND MERCURY ANALYSIS OF FISH SPECIES, AND PROVIDING TRIBAL COMMUNITY EDUCATION AND OUTREACH ON THE FINDINGS OF MERCURY CONCENTRATIONS IN FISH AND CRAYFISH.  OVERALL, THE PROJECT WILL DOCUMENT THE VARIABILITY OF MERCURY CONCENTRATIONS IN FISH AND CRAYFISH IN TRIBAL PONDS AND LAKES AND INFORM THE TRIBAL COMMUNITY AND INFLUENCE BEHAVIOR TO MINIMIZE MERCURY EXPOSURE DURING SUSTENANCE FISHING.
description.85: THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CONDUCT TESTING OF DRINKING WATER QUALITY ON THE PASSAMAQUODDY TRIBE OF PLEASANT POINT RESERVATION, AND TO INCREASE COMMUNITY AWARENESS AND INVOLVEMENT RELATING TO DRINKING WATER EDUCATION. OUTPUTS INCLUDE A COMMUNITY DRINKING WATER REPORT, AS WELL AS INSTALLING AN EASILY ACCESSIBLE WATER PURIFICATION STATION FOR THE COMMUNITY TO USE. OVERALL, THE PROJECT WILL EMPOWER PLEASANT POINT RESERVATION COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN UNDERSTANDING THEIR DRINKING WATER ISSUES. WITH THE DATA COLLECTED FROM DRINKING WATER QUALITY TESTING, THE COMMUNITY CAN COLLECTIVELY DISCUSS AND DETERMINE AN ACTION PLAN AS IT PERTAINS TO THEIR DRINKING WATER.
description.86: THE CHILDHOOD LEAD ACTION PROJECT'S COMMUNITY LEAD SAFETY COLLABORATIVE WILL WORK IN PROVIDENCE, RHODE ISLAND (RI)  TO REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF CHILDHOOD LEAD POISONING, IMPROVE THE SAFETY OF RENTAL HOUSING, AND INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF RESIDENTS, LOCAL  GOVERNMENT, HOUSING FUNDING AGENCIES, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS TO ADDRESS THE LEAD ISSUE ON A LOCAL LEVEL. PROVIDENCE HAS A HIGH INCIDENCE OF LEAD POISONING AND IS HOME TO SUBSTANTIAL LOW-INCOME AND MINORITY POPULATIONS. THE PROJECT IS GROUNDED IN EFFECTIVE LEAD PREVENTION PRACTICES INCLUDING: MEANINGFUL INVOLVEMENT AND DIRECTION PROVIDED BY LOCAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS ALREADY ENGAGED IN LEADERSHIP ROLES; A MULTI-STAKEHOLDER GROUP WITH PREVIOUSLY ESTABLISHED RELATIONSHIPS, TRUST, MUTUAL GOALS, AND RESPONSIBILITIES; A PATHWAY FOR FURTHER COMMUNITY MEMBER ENVIRONMENTAL LEARNING AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT THROUGH ACCESSIBLE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES IN ENGLISH, SPANISH, OTHER LANGUAGES, AND USING LOW-LITERACY CURRICULA. BY THE END OF THIS PROJECT

DESCRIPTION:THIS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING TO GREENROOTS, A LOCAL NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION IN CHELSEA, MA.GREENROOTS IS A COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATION DEDICATED TO IMPROVING AND ENHANCING THE URBAN ENVIRONMENT AND PUBLIC HEALTH IN CHELSEA, EAST BOSTON AND SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES. description.92: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE SMALL GRANT IS TO ESTABLISH AN EMPOWERING, SCHOOL CURRICULUM-INTEGRATED ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION PROGRAM FOR YOUNGER STUDENTS PROPELLING THEIR AWARENESS OF PROBLEMS LIKE CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE INJUSTICES THEY CREATE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE LEARNING ABOUT THE ANIMAL, MINERAL, AND PLANT KINGDOMS AND HOW THEY INTERACT AND DEPEND ON ECOSYSTEMS; AND DELVING INTO THE LAWS OF NATURE REGARDING THE MOVEMENT OF LIGHT, WATER, WIND, AND SOIL. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE AN INCREASED SENSE OF RESPONSIBILITY TO TAKE CARE OF THE ENVIRONMENT; INCREASED CONSERVATION OF RESOURCES AT HOME AND SCHOOL; AND A FRAMEWORK FOR THE INTERNATIONAL SCHOOL OF LOUISIANA'S (ISL'S) CURRICULUM ADVISOR AND TEACHERS FOR THEIR THIRD-GRADE SCIENCE PROGRAM, WHICH CAN BE REPLICATED FOR OTHERS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES ARE STUDENTS LIVING IN NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA, ZIP-CODES 70130 AND 70114. ACTIVITIES:ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE PREPPING MATERIALS AND TRAINING STAFF ON TEACHING RESPONSIBLE EARTH EDUCATION'S LOST TREASURE CURRICULUM, PILOTING THE CURRICULUM WITH THIRD GRADE STUDENTS, AND EVALUATING THE SUCCESS OF THE PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE CURRICULUM INCLUDE 50 VISITS OVER 16 WEEKS TO TEACH STUDENTS ABOUT THE ANIMAL KINGDOM AND ANIMAL CHARACTERISTICS, FACILITATING INTERACTIVE CHALLENGES WITH STUDENTS ABOUT ANIMAL SIMILARITIES, AND TAKING STUDENTS ON FIELD TRIPS TO REINFORCE LEARNING.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE AN INCREASED SENSE OF RESPONSIBILITY TO TAKE CARE OF THE ENVIRONMENT; INCREASED CONSERVATION OF RESOURCES AT HOME AND SCHOOL; AND A FRAMEWORK FOR THE INTERNATIONAL SCHOOL OF LOUISIANA'S (ISL'S) CURRICULUM ADVISOR AND TEACHERS FOR THEIR THIRD-GRADE SCIENCE PROGRAM, WHICH CAN BE REPLICATED FOR OTHERS.

SPECIFICALLY, EPA FUNDING WILL BE USED IN INTERNATIONAL DISTRICT ZIP CODE 87108 FOR PROJECT ACTIVITIES ADDRESSING CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE IMPACTS OF COVID-19 ON THE TARGET COMMUNITY THROUGH THE COORDINATION OF A NEIGHBORHOOD FOOD HUB PLAN INCLUDING, 11 COMMITTEE-LED MEETINGS TO SUPPORT LOCAL GARDENERS' CONTRIBUTIONS TO MONTHLY FOOD DISTRIBUTIONS AND FOOD-SHARING NETWORKS; ADDITIONALLY, THE URBAN AG COMMITTEE WILL SUPPORT 2 GARDEN DEMONSTRATION BUILD-OUTS, AND 1 URBAN AG SITE REVITALIZATION PROJECT. PARTNERING WITH TREE NM TO COLLECT AIR QUALITY DATA ON CARBON EMISSIONS, VOC'S, AND TEMPERATURE (HEAT ISLAND INDEX). RESEARCH ON AIR QUALITY, AND IMPACT OF GREEN SPACES ON CITIES. description.95:
DESCRIPTION:
THE PURPOSE OF THIS ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COLLABORATIVE PROBLEM SOLVING (EJCPS) COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE MULTI-MEDIA FUNDING TO FRONT AND CENTERED TO CREATE AN ACCESSIBLE, COMMUNITY-BASED, AND COMMUNITY-DRIVEN ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING, REPORTING, AND ENFORCEMENT SYSTEM IN THREE OF THE MOST ENVIRONMENTALLY COMPROMISED REGIONS IN WASHINGTON STATE: THE DUWAMISH RIVER VALLEY, SKAGIT COUNTY, AND YAKIMA COUNTY. THE COMMUNITIES FACES PERSISTENT ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES INCLUDING: THE DUWAMISH VALLEY NEIGHBORHOODS OF SOUTH PARK AND GEORGETOWN FACE POORER AIR QUALITY THAN THE REST OF SEATTLE BECAUSE OF HIGHER DIESEL PM POLLUTION LEVELS AND OTHER INDUSTRIAL EMISSIONS; HISTORY OF TOXIC CHEMICALS LEACHING INTO DRINKING WATER IN HIGHLY-SENSITIVE AREAS SUCH AS THE DUWAMISH RIVER AND IN AGRICULTURAL REGIONS OF SKAGIT AND YAKIMA COUNTIES; AND PERSISTENT PESTICIDES AND TOXIC CHEMICALS FOUND IN COMMUNITIES. ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING AN ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOL, MODELED AFTER THE SUCCESSFUL IDENTIFYING VIOLATIONS AFFECTING NEIGHBORHOODS (IVAN) SYSTEM. THE RECIPIENT INTENDS TO ISSUE SUB-AWARD AGREEMENTS TO ITS PARTNERS IN COMPLIANCE WITH APPENDIX A OF EPA'S SUB-AWARD POLICY. THE SUB-AWARDEES WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL EXPERTISE IN COORDINATING LISTENING SESSIONS, CREATING EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS IN ENGLISH/SPANISH, DEVELOPING A CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE OUTREACH STRATEGY, AND CREATING SYNERGISTIC OPPORTUNITIES WITH EXISTING PROJECT ACTIVITIES.
ACTIVITIES:
PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING COMMUNITY OUTREACH, EDUCATION, AND ENGAGEMENT IN TARGET COMMUNITIES; CONVENING COMMUNITY PARTNERS, CROSS-JURISDICTIONAL AGENCY REPRESENTATIVES, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS; AND CREATING AND IMPLEMENTING A COMMUNITY/GOVERNMENT WORK GROUP TO RESPOND TO REPORTS OF VIOLATIONS.  
OUTCOMES:
ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING AN ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING TOOL, MODELED AFTER THE SUCCESSFUL IDENTIFYING VIOLATIONS AFFECTING NEIGHBORHOODS (IVAN) SYSTEM.  EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED TOOLS AND PROCESSES FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND REPORTING, INCREASED KNOWLEDGE AND ACCESS TO ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND REPORTING MECHANISMS IN HIGH-IMPACT COMMUNITIES, AND INCREASED ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY IN HIGH-IMPACT COMMUNITIES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES ARE RESIDENTS OF THE KING, YAKIMA, AND SKAGIT COUNTIES OF WASHINGTON STATE. 
SUBRECIPIENT:
IN THIS PROJECT, SUBAWARD STAFF WILL CREATE THE IVAN PLATFORM SPECIFICALLY FOR WASHINGTON STATE. STAFF WILL ALSO ENGAGE IN PROJECT ACTIVITIES TO SHARE LESSONS LEARNED FROM THEIR OUTREACH/EDUCATION WORK IN IMPERIAL VALLEY AND PROVIDE GUIDANCE AND INSIGHT FOR ADAPTING THE IVAN TOOL IN WASHINGTON STATE. OTHER SUBAWARD ACTIVITIES INCLUDE COORDINATING LISTENING SESSIONS, CREATING EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS IN ENGLISH/SPANISH, DEVELOPING AN OUTREACH STRATEGY THAT IS CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE AND CREATING SYNERGISTIC OPPORTUNITIES WITH EXISTING PROJECT ACTIVITIES. FURTHER ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING FACT SHEETS THAT REFLECT THE PROGRESS ON THE PROJECT. THESE FACT SHEETS WILL BE IN COMMUNITY-FRIENDLY LANGUAGE AND WILL HIGHLIGHT INFORMATION OF INTEREST TO THE COMMUNITY. THESE WILL BE TRANSLATED INTO MULTIPLE LANGUAGES (ENGLISH, SPANISH, VIETNAMESE, SOMALI AND KHMER). FINALLY, TECHNICAL EXPERTISE WILL HELP DEVELOP THE QAPP.
description.96:
DESCRIPTION:
THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE SMALL GRANT PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE EDUCATION FOCUSED AT REDUCING FEAR, HESITANCY, AND BARRIERS PREVENTING PEOPLE FROM BEING VACCINATED FOR COVID-19.  THE SCOPE OF THE PROJECT INCLUDES OUTREACH, EDUCATION, MONITORING, PARTICIPANT ASSISTANCE, MILESTONES, AND REPORTING. THIS PROJECT IS IN ACCORDANCE WITH CAA 103(B)(3): PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.
ACTIVITIES:
PROJECT ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE TARGETING THE HOMELESS POPULATION IN SNOHOMISH COUNTY, WA, CONDUCTING OUTREACH, STREET CANVASING, AND COMMUNITY TALK EVENTS.  THIS PROJECT ALSO PROVIDES EDUCATION AND HYGIENE KITS FOR MITIGATING COVID-19 EFFECTS RELATED TO THE CLEAN AIR ACT.  PROJECT ACTIVITIES PROVIDE TRANSPORTATION TO AND FROM VACCINATION SITES AND INCORPORATE PARTICIPANTS' STORIES IN EDUCATION/OUTREACH MATERIALS AND WORKSHOP SESSIONS.
OUTCOMES:
THE GOAL AND ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE INCREASED LEARNING ABOUT COVID-19 AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ISSUES SUCH THAT MEMBERS OF THE HOMELESS POPULATION WILL BECOME VACCINATED AGAINST THE CORONAVIRUS. OTHER OUTCOMES INCLUDE BUILDING PARTNERSHIPS, INCREASING PARTICIPATION IN LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES AND THE USE OF PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT, AS WELL AS INCREASED VACCINATION RATE OF HOMELESS RESIDENTS. IT IS EXPECTED THAT THIS PROJECT WILL HELP TO DECREASE THE SPREAD OF COVID-19, AND HOSPITAL ADMISSIONS OF HOMELESS RESIDENTS DUE TO COVID-19.  DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE HOMELESS AND LOW-INCOME RESIDENTS OF SNOHOMISH COUNTY.
SUBRECIPIENT:
NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.
description.97:
DESCRIPTION:
THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO WORK ALONGSIDE NICKELSVILLE (SELF-MANAGED HOMELESS COMMUNITY) TO CO-ENVISION AN INNOVATIVE TINY HOUSE ECOVILLAGE THAT COMBATS HOMELESSNESS IN AN ENVIRONMENTALLY AND SOCIALLY JUST WAY. THE ANTICIPATED LOCATION OF THE ECOVILLAGE IS THE OTHELLO NEIGHBORHOOD IN SEATTLE, ONE OF THE MOST DIVERSE ZIP CODES IN THE U.S., AN IMMIGRANT AND REFUGEE DESTINATION, AND WHICH HOSTS A LARGE HOMELESS POPULATION. THE GRANTEE WILL WORK WITH THE ECOVILLAGE RESIDENTS TO DETERMINE WHAT THEIR NEEDS ARE AND THEN HELP PLAN, DESIGN, AND BUILD DEMONSTRATION CONCEPTS TO PROMOTE THE HEALTH OF THE RESIDENTS AND REDUCE THE ECOLOGICAL FOOTPRINT OF THE COMMUNITY.
ACTIVITIES:

PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL OCCUR OVER THREE PHASES: 1) INFORMATION GATHERING OF EXISTING CONDITIONS, NEEDS AND PRIORITIES, 2) MASTER PLANNING FOR A NEW NICKELSVILLE TINY HOUSE ECOVILLAGE, AND 3) PROTOTYPING AND DEMONSTRATION OF SELECT ECO-DESIGN COMPONENTS. ADDITIONALLY, THE ECOVILLAGE WILL ALSO BE SUBMITTED FOR CERTIFICATION WITH THE INTERNATIONAL LIVING FUTURE INSTITUTE'S LIVING COMMUNITY CHALLENGE CERTIFICATION.
OUTCOMES:

PROJECT OUTPUTS INCLUDE A MASTERPLAN BOOK AND BUILT PROTOTYPES. ADDITIONALLY, AN OUTCOME OF THE PROJECT WILL BE TO CERTIFY THE VILLAGE WITH THE INTERNATIONAL LIVING FUTURE INSTITUTE'S LIVING COMMUNITY CHALLENGE CERTIFICATION PROCESS. THE COLLABORATIVE DEMOCRATIC PROCESS WILL FACILITATE TRUST-BUILDING, COMMUNICATION AND CO-TRAINING BETWEEN THE PROFESSIONAL TEAM, NICKELSVILLE RESIDENTS, NEIGHBORS, STAKEHOLDERS AND THE PUBLIC TO SUPPORT OUTCOMES THAT A) EXPLORE A UNIQUE SUSTAINABLE SOLUTION TO HOMELESSNESS; B) AMPLIFY THE HOMELESS VOICES AND VISION TO LIVE SUSTAINABLY AND HEALTHILY WITHIN A SUPPORTIVE COMMUNITY SETTING UNIQUE TO PEOPLE FACING HOMELESSNESS; AND C) CHALLENGE HARMFUL HOMELESS STEREOTYPES. TO ACHIEVE THIS, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL FACILITATE PARTICIPATORY WORKSHOPS OVER THREE PHASES AND WORK WITHIN THE INTERNATIONAL LIVING FUTURE INSTITUTE (ILFI)'S LIVING COMMUNITY CHALLENGE CERTIFICATION PROCESS AS AN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE METRICS GUIDE.

SUBRECIPIENT:
NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.

TO ADDRESS THE CURRENT LOW ACCESS TO FOOD BY VALLEJO'S UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES AND REDUCE THE AMOUNT OF LANDFILLED FOOD WASTE THAT CREATES METHANE AND CONTRIBUTES TO CLIMATE CHANGE. THIS PROJECT WILL CONNECT INVESTED COMMUNITY MEMBERS, ORGANIZATIONS AND STAKEHOLDERS IN VALLEJO, CALIFORNIA, TO COORDINATE A ROBUST, HYPER-LOCAL FOOD RESCUE OPERATION. INPUT FROM DIVERSE COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL HELP CUSTOMIZE A MOBILE APP CALLED 'FREEBITES' SO FOOD DONORS (GROCERY/RESTAURANT/GLEANERS) ARE CONNECTED WITH RECIPIENTS (AGENCIES/INDIVIDUALS) IN THEIR COMMUNITIES.
ACTIVITIES:
PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: 1) CUSTOMIZATION OF THE 'FREEBITES' APP; 2) DEVELOPMENT OF THE VALLEJO FOOD RESCUE TOOLKIT (AN IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP FOR OTHER JURISDICTIONS); 3) IMPLEMENTATION OF FOOD RESCUE OPERATIONS (COORDINATING THE MOVEMENT OF FOOD BETWEEN DONORS AND RECIPIENTS); 4) OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT OF ADDITIONAL PARTNERS; 5) OUTREACH/EDUCATION TO FOOD DONORS BUSINESS/INDIVIDUALS); AND 6) OUTREACH/EDUCATION TO COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS/INDIVIDUALS THAT RECEIVE/DISTRIBUTE FOOD. 
OUTCOMES:
THE VALLEJO FOOD RESCUE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT THE RESIDENTS OF ZIP CODES: 94589, 94590, 94591, AND 94592 IN THE CITY OF VALLEJO, CALIFORNIA. THE PROJECT'S ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES ARE ONE COMPLETED 'FREEBITES' APP AND ONE TOOLKIT DOCUMENT. OTHER OUTPUTS INCLUDE: A) POUNDS OF FOOD RESCUED; B) NUMBER OF MEALS/INDIVIDUALS FED; C) NUMBER OF DONORS REACHED AND USING APP; D) NUMBER OF FOOD RECIPIENTS REACHED AND USING APP; E) NUMBER OF RESIDENTS WHO GAINED KNOWLEDGE ABOUT FOOD RESCUE OPERATION THROUGH PUBLIC OUTREACH CAMPAIGN; AND F) NUMBER OF ADDITIONAL PARTNERS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE: A) REDUCTION OF LANDFILLED FOOD WASTE THAT CONTRIBUTES TO CLIMATE CHANGE; B) INCREASED COMMUNICATION AND COLLABORATION AMONG PARTNERS/STAKEHOLDERS; C) INCREASED FOOD SECURITY, RESILIENCY AND BETTER HEALTH IN EJ COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY COVID-19; AND D) RESOURCES AND READINESS TO EXPAND THE PROGRAM TO OTHER JURISDICTIONS IN SOLANO COUNTY.
SUBRECIPIENT:
THE RECIPIENT INTENDS TO ISSUE A SUBAWARD AGREEMENT IN COMPLIANCE WITH APPENDIX A OF EPA&RSQUO;S SUBAWARD POLICY. THE SUB-AWARDEE WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL EXPERTISE IN EXPANDING FOOD MOVEMENT LOGISTICS TO INCLUDE PREPARED FOOD AND COORDINATING THE GLEANING PORTION OF THE PROJECT.

THIS AWARD PROVIDES AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDS TO IMPLEMENT THE BAYVIEW FOOD SOVEREIGNTY AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE PROJECT (BVFSEJP). THE PURPOSE OF THE BAYVIEW FOOD SOVEREIGNTY AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE PROJECT IS TO FORM COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS, EDUCATE THE COMMUNITY, AND ADDRESS AIR QUALITY AND FOOD INSECURITY ISSUES THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEM TO GROW AND DISTRIBUTE LOCALLY GROWN FOOD IN BAYVIEW HUNTERS POINT, ONE OF SAN FRANCISCO'S MOST UNDERSERVED NEIGHBORHOOD WITH THE MOST COVID-19 INFECTIONS AND DEATHS. ACTIVITIES:ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: DEVELOPING PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN NEIGHBORHOOD FARMERS AND MARKETS TO IMPLEMENT A SUSTAINABLE FOOD DISTRIBUTION SUPPLY CHAIN; TRAINING COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO GROW AND MAINTAIN THEIR OWN SUSTAINABLE GARDENS; EDUCATING AND EMPOWERING COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO UNDERSTAND ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES, INCLUDING EDUCATION ON AIR POLLUTION, ACTIVITIES TO IMPROVE AIR QUALITY, AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP.
OUTCOMES:EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: INCREASED EDUCATION AND AWARENESS OF ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH ISSUES, INCLUDING AIR QUALITY AND COVID PROTOCOLS; IMPROVED COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN EFFORTS TO ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES, SUCH AS AIR QUALITY AND SUSTAINABLE FOOD SYSTEMS; BUILDING CONSENSUS AND SETTING COMMUNITY PRIORITIES; IMPROVING AIR QUALITY AND COMMUNITY HEALTH. DESCRIPTION:
OVER A SIX-MONTH PROJECT PERIOD, GROW2ZERO FARMS WILL COLLECT AND RE-PACKAGE 50,000 POUNDS OF RESCUED FOOD AS WELL AS GROW AND DISTRIBUTE AN ADDITIONAL 10,000 POUNDS OF ORGANIC PRODUCE GROWN AT ITS URBAN FARM IN WEST LONG BEACH. THE PROJECT WILL TARGET HOMEBOUND HOUSEHOLDS AND INDIVIDUALS, THOSE ADVERSELY IMPACTED BY SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS RESULTING FROM COVID-19, AS WELL AS THE POLLUTION FROM THE PORT OF LONG BEACH AND SEVERAL LOCAL REFINERIES. 
THE PROJECT WILL REDUCE THE IMPACTS OF METHANE ASSOCIATED WITH FOOD DISPOSAL AND SERVE TO SEQUESTER GHG EMISSIONS FROM THE LOCAL NEIGHBORHOOD. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE AT LEAST 2600 CRATES OF FRESH FOOD THROUGH BOTH DISTRIBUTION AND DIRECT DOOR-TO-DOOR DELIVERY TO PARTICIPATING FAMILIES. DESCRIPTION:
THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED GRANT IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE REGENERATION PROJECT: THE CONGREGATIONS AS RESILIENCY HUBS PROJECT THAT WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A COMMUNITY RESILIENCY HUB FOR AN EAST OAKLAND NEIGHBORHOOD BY PROVIDING ACCESS TO CLEAN AIR DURING WILDFIRES AND BLACKOUTS AT THE FAITH BAPTIST CHURCH. IN CREATING A RESILIENCY HUB, THE REGENERATION PROJECT SHALL ASSESS AND ADDRESS INDOOR AIR POLLUTANTS, AS WELL AS INSTALL AN AIR FILTRATION SYSTEM FOR USE DURING WILDFIRES THE FAITH BAPTIST CHURCH SITE. THE PROJECT WILL HOST TWO COMMUNITY WORKSHOPS DISCUSSING THE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON THEIR NEIGHBORHOOD AND HOW TO ADAPT TO THESE CHANGES. IN ADDITION, THIS PROJECT SHALL DEVELOP A RESOURCE GUIDE SUPPORT OTHER CONGREGATIONS IN BECOMING COMMUNITY RESILIENCY HUBS. 

THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FULL FEDERAL FUNDING OF $75,000. PREAWARD COSTS HAVE BEEN APPROVED BACK TO MARCH 1, 2022.

ACTIVITIES:
THE PRIMARY PROJECT OBJECTIVES ARE:
OBJECTIVE 1: RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES TO HELP FUND A BACK UP BATTERY FOR THE CONGREGATION 
OBJECTIVE 2: IDENTIFY INDOOR AIR POLLUTANTS, SOLICIT AIR FILTRATION UPGRADES, DEVELOP AND DISTRIBUTE PAMPHLETS ABOUT THE RESILIENCY HUB.
OBJECTIVE 3: DEVELOP CURRICULUM FOR INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND HOST WORKSHOPS WITH THE COMMUNITY
OBJECTIVE 4: DEVELOP RESILIENCY HUB GUIDES AND DISTRIBUTE TO THE CONGREGATIONS/CHURCHES
OUTCOMES:
                                                                                                                                                                            
THE ANTICIPATED ACTIVITIES AND DELIVERABLES ARE TO IDENTIFY AND ELIMINATE INDOOR AIR POLLUTANTS AT FAITH BAPTIST CHURCH, PURCHASE PORTABLE AIR PURIFIERS FOR FAITH BAPTIST CHURCH HIRE CONTRACTORS TO INSTALL BACK-UP BATTERIES FOR FAITH BAPTIST SOLAR PANELS AS WELL AS UPDATE THE AIR FILTRATION SYSTEM AT FAITH BAPTIST CHURCH, HOST CLIMATE IMPACT AND PREPAREDNESS WORKSHOPS AND DEVELOP GUIDES FOR CONGREGATION RESILIENCY HUBS, DISSEMINATE INFORMATION ABOUT RESILIENCY HUB TO COMMUNITY MEMBERS THROUGH OAKLAND CITY COUNCIL MEMBER LOREN TAYLOR'S EMAIL LIST, DISTRIBUTE PAMPHLETS ABOUT RESILIENCY HUB AROUND FAITH BAPTIST CHURCH'S NEIGHBORHOOD, AND DISTRIBUTE GUIDES TO CA IPL AND GTC CONGREGATIONS.

SHORT TERM OUTCOMES INCLUDE KNOWLEDGE OF COMMUNITY RESILIENCY HUB FROM HAVENCOURT COMMUNITY MEMBERS, COMMUNITY PREPARATION DURING WILDFIRES, NEIGHBORHOOD ACCESS TO CLEAN AIR DURING WILDFIRES AT COMMUNITY RESILIENCY HUB, CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACT RECOGNITION IN THE HAVENSCOURT/MILLSMONT AREA, AND FORMATION OF CONGREGATIONS IN CA, AND ACROSS THE U.S., TO LEARN ABOUT COMMUNITY RESILIENCY HUB.

INTERMEDIATE OUTCOMES INCLUDE HAVENSCOURT/MILLSMONT NEIGHBORS UTILIZATION OF COMMUNITY RESILIENCY HUB DURING WILDFIRES, INCREASED COMMUNITY CLIMATE CHANGE KNOWLEDGE AND PREPAREDNESS, AND FORMATION OF ADDITIONAL COMMUNITY RESILIENCY HUB CONGREGATIONS ACROSS CA AND U.S.

SUB-GRANT TO GREEN THE CHURCH FOR DEVELOPMENT AND DISTRIBUTION OF COMMUNITY RESILIENCY GUIDE = $11,000

SUB-GRANT TO FAITH BAPTIST CHURCH FOR SECURITY FIRM CONTRACT, OVERHEAD COSTS OF STAFF TIME AND UTILITIES = $7,000

DESCRIPTION:
THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDED GRANT IS TO ASSIST RAIN DC IN CREATING THE CARE RESILIENCE HUB: MAKING HOT SPACES COOL. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON URBAN HEAT INTERVENTIONS IN THE MESA, ARIZONA WATER TOWER IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT, AN UNDERSERVED NEIGHBORHOOD BATTLING INTENSE HEAT AND GENTRIFICATION DUE TO LARGE-SCALE DEVELOPMENT FROM PROPOSED GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS. ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PROJECTS FOCUSED ON DESIGNED SHADE REST STOPS PLACED IN HIGH TRAFFIC/LOW SHADE LOCATIONS, A FRONT YARD BEAUTIFICATION PROJECT, THAT WILL PROVIDE SHADE TREES, AND OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT TO HELP EMPOWER THE COMMUNITY TO BUILD CAPACITY. TWO PROGRAMS WILL BE LAUNCHED AT THE RESILIENCE HUB. THE COMMUNITY GUARDIAN PROGRAM WILL TRAIN NEIGHBORS THROUGH A SERIES OF MONTHLY WORKSHOPS TO ADVOCATE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE SOLUTIONS. A K-12 SUMMER EMERGENCY PROGRAM WILL EDUCATE 250 YOUTH ON HEAT-HEALTH SAFETY, COOL ROUTES, AND POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL CHOICES, SUCH AS ALWAYS CARRYING REUSABLE WATER BOTTLES.  PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.

THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FULL FEDERAL FUNDING IN THE AMOUNT OF $75,000. PRE-AWARD COSTS HAVE BEEN APPROVED BACK TO FEBRUARY 1, 2022. REFER TO TERMS AND CONDITIONS.

ACTIVITIES:
   
THREE ACTIVITIES WILL BE SIMULTANEOUSLY LAUNCHED TO CAPITALIZE SYNERGIES FROM PAST RESEARCH, CURRENTLY FUNDED PROJECTS, AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT PLANS: 1) A DEMONSTRATION PROJECT WILL RESULT IN FOUR COMMUNITY DESIGNED SHADE REST STOPS STRATEGICALLY PLACED IN HIGH TRAFFIC/LOW SHADE AMENITY LOCATIONS, 2) A DEMONSTRATION AND MONITORING PROJECT, A FRONT YARD BEAUTIFICATION PROJECT WILL PROVIDE SHADE TREES ON PRIVATE PROPERTY, CULMINATING IN DATA-DRIVEN COOL CORRIDORS AND 3) A DEMONSTRATION, MONITORING AND PUBLIC EDUCATION PROJECT, ENGAGING AND EMPOWERING RESIDENTS THROUGHOUT THE TRANSFORMATION OF CARE PARTNERSHIP, A TRUSTED COMMUNITY CENTER INTO A RESILIENCE HUB, COMMUNITY-DRIVEN RESILIENCE INCUBATOR FOR EMERGENCY SITUATIONS (HEAT WAVES, BLACKOUTS, WILDFIRES), RECOVERY FROM DISASTERS (COVID), AND CAPACITY BUILDING. TWO PROGRAMS WILL BE LAUNCHED AT THE RESILIENCE HUB. THE COMMUNITY GUARDIAN PROGRAM WILL TRAIN NEIGHBORS THROUGH A SERIES OF MONTHLY WORKSHOPS TO ADVOCATE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE SOLUTIONS. THE EXPECTED OUTPUTS FROM THIS PROJECT ARE: 1) PLANS FOR COMMUNITY SHADE SPACES, 2) A GUIDEBOOK/MAP FOR COOLER SPACES, AND 3) A TEACHING CURRICULUM FOR K-12 STUDENTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE TO EDUCATE THE COMMUNITY ON HEAT MITIGATION MEASURES, AND TO COOL OFF UNDERSERVED NEIGHBORHOODS.

1) SUBGRANT TO CATHOLIC CHARITIES FOR VENUE FEES FOR WORKSHOPS AND ADVOCACY TRAINING, PROVIDING OFFICE SPACE/WORKSTATION FOR URBAN HEAT FELLOW AND RESILIENCE HUB SPECIALIST, PERMISSION FEES FOR SITING OF REST STOPS IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD, FOOD FOR ADVOCACY CONVENINGS. 
2) SUBGRANT TO ARIZONA STATE UNIVERSITY FOR WEATHER STATION INSTALLATION AND MONITORING, ANALYSIS OF PRE/POST SURVEYS, COOL ROUTE OPTIMIZATION ANALYSIS, REST STOP USAGE ANALYSIS.
3) RAIL CDC - ADVOCACY TRAINING PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNITY SPONSORSHIP DEVELOPMENT, EMPLOYER BENEFITS RESPONSIBILITY.
4) STIPEND FOR TWO SEMESTERS ($2,500 EACH) FOR COMMUNITY/DIGITAL ORGANIZERS.

DESCRIPTION:
THIS GRANT PROVIDES FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO THE PURPOSE FOCUSED ALTERNATIVE LEARNING (PFAL) CORPORATION TO IMPLEMENT ITS OWN PROJECT TO NAVAJO 'GREEN JOB CAREER DEVELOPMENT' TO PROVIDE SOLAR EDUCATION, TRAINING, NABCEP CERTIFICATION, AND EMPLOYMENT PROJECTS ON THE NAVAJO NATION. THUS, PROVIDING FOR GREEN-JOB OPPORTUNITIES TO DEPLOY, AND MANAGE OFF-GRID SOLAR FURNACES, AND SOLAR MICROGRID SYSTEMS.

description.108:
DESCRIPTION:THE ROSE FOUNDATION FOR COMMUNITIES AND THE ENVIRONMENT WILL USE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN FUNDS TO IMPLEMENT THE NEW VOICES ARE RISING FOR RESILIENCE PROJECT. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INCREASE COLLABORATION ACROSS COMMUNITIES TO STRENGTHEN RESILIENCE IN THE FACE OF THE TRIPLE THREATS TO COMMUNITY HEALTH POSED BY THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC, CLIMATE CHANGE, AND TOXIC POLLUTION IN LOW-INCOME BAY AREA COMMUNITIES OF COLOR. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THE COMMUNITIES OF BAYVIEW HUNTERS POINT, OAKLAND, RICHMOND/SAN PABLO, AND ANTIOCH/PITTSBURG, WITH A FOCUS ON YOUTH.  CLEAN AIR ACT (CAA) SECTION 103(B)(3):  PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.

THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FULL FEDERAL FUNDING IN THE AMOUNT OF $75,000.  PRE-AWARD COSTS ARE APPROVED BACK TO MARCH 1, 2022.
ACTIVITIES:PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: RECRUITING, TRAINING, AND SUPPORTING COLLABORATION AMONG HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS TO BUILD COMMUNITY LEADERSHIP SKILLS THROUGH PAID FELLOWSHIPS AND INTERNSHIPS; SUPPORTING STUDENTS IN IMPLEMENTING PROJECTS TO ADVANCE FOOD JUSTICE, REDUCE INDOOR EXPOSURE TO WILDFIRE SMOKE, REDUCE COMMUNITY EXPOSURE TO TOXIC POLLUTION, INCREASE ELECTRICITY ACCESS IN EXTREME WEATHER AND WILDFIRE CONDITIONS, OR ADVANCE CREATION OF RESILIENCE HUBS; AND PROMOTING AWARENESS ON VACCINE SAFETY AND AVAILABILITY.SUBRECIPIENT:SUBAWARDS WOULD BE ISSUED TO COMMUNITIES FOR A BETTER ENVIRONMENT AND GREENACTION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE. SUBAWARD ACTIVITIES INCLUDE SUPERVISING AND MENTORING FELLOWS AND INTERNS TO CONDUCT PUBLIC EDUCATION AND COMMUNITY OUTREACH.OUTCOMES:EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: INCREASED KNOWLEDGE OF AIR QUALITY ISSUES AND CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS, REDUCED VACCINE HESITANCY, IMPROVED CROSS-COMMUNITY COLLABORATION ON ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ISSUES,  IMPROVED AIR QUALITY, INCREASED RESILIENCY TO CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS, AND INCREASED COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN AIR QUALITY AND CLIMATE CHANGE PLANNING.

WEST OAKLAND RANKS IN THE 90TH PERCENTILE FOR CALIFORNIA COMMUNITIES OF COLOR EXPOSED TO BLACK CARBON AND TRANSPORTATION EMISSIONS. RESIDENTS ARE SURROUNDED ON ALL SIDES BY FREEWAYS AND SPRAWLING FREIGHT AND LOGISTICS OPERATIONS FROM THE NEARBY PORT OF OAKLAND. TO ADDRESS THE AIR POLLUTION, PUBLIC HEALTH, AND CLIMATE CRISES IN THE REGION, THE WEST OAKLAND SUSTAINABLE PORT COLLABORATIVE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE A FORUM FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO WORK TOGETHER WITH A DIVERSE GROUP OF PARTNERS IN ACADEMIA, LABOR, BUSINESS, INDUSTRY, AND LOCAL AND STATE AGENCIES TO ACCELERATE THE PORT OF OAKLAND'S TRANSITION TO ZERO-EMISSIONS. ACTIVITIES:PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EDUCATING PORT DECISIONMAKERS ON THE FEASIBILITY OF ZERO-EMISSIONS TECHNOLOGY, IDENTIFYING BARRIERS TO ELIMINATING SPECIFIC EMISSIONS SOURCES, AND EMPOWERING RESIDENTS TO PUSH THE PORT TO MAKE SPECIFIC ZERO-EMISSIONS COMMITMENTS. THE GOAL IS TO SHIFT THE DIRECTION OF THE PORT'S MARITIME STRATEGIC PLAN FROM CONTINUOUS GROWTH TO SUSTAINABLE, EMISSION-FREE COMMERCE. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:THE WEST OAKLAND SUSTAINABLE PORT COLLABORATIVE WILL LEAD THE DEVELOPMENT OF A MODEL RESOLUTION INCLUDING ZERO-EMISSIONS RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE PORT OF OAKLAND.  ZERO-EMISSIONS RECOMMENDATIONS WILL BE RESEARCHED BY MEMBERS OF THE COLLABORATIVE INCLUDING COMMUNITY MEMBERS, LOCAL, STATE AND FEDERAL PARTNER AGENCIES, AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS. THE EMISSIONS REDUCTIONS THAT WOULD BE ACHIEVED VIA ADOPTION OF THE ZERO-EMISSIONS RECOMMENDATIONS BY THE PORT OF OAKLAND WOULD BENEFIT THE PUBLIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH OF THE CITIZENS OF WEST OAKLAND COMMUNITIES.
