OUTPUTS ARE GENERALLY PUBLICATIONS IN SCIENTIFIC JOURNALS, PRESENTATIONS AT SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS, AND OCCASIONALLY DEVELOPMENT OF MODELS AND OTHER TOOLS THAT MAY BE USED BY THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND OTHER PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS.
description.238:
DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO BETTER CHARACTERIZE IMPORTANT EXPOSURE PATHWAYS OF PER- AND POLY-FLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFAS) AMONG VULNERABLE GROUPS, IN IMPACTED COMMUNITIES, AND IN THE GENERAL POPULATION.
ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL COLLECT DATA THAT WILL ALLOW THE RECIPIENT TO EVALUATE HOW MUCH VARIABILITY IN PFAS SERUM LEVELS CAN BE EXPLAINED BY WATER CONSUMPTION AND OTHER RESIDENTIAL AND DIETARY EXPOSURE SOURCES/PATHWAYS SUCH AS INDOOR AIR. SUBRECIPIENT:A SUBAWARD WILL BE GIVEN TO INDIANA UNIVERSITY TO PERFORM PFAS ANALYSIS OF 50 PASSIVE INDOOR AIR AND 50 DUST SAMPLES COLLECTED IN PARTICIPANT HOMES, WITH THE ANALYSES TO BE CONDUCTED IN YEAR 1. OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES ARE ANNUAL PROGRESS AND FINAL REPORTS. PROJECT OUTPUTS INCLUDE 1) EXPOSURE MEASUREMENTS (INDOOR AIR CONCENTRATIONS, HOUSEHOLD DUST CONCENTRATIONS) FOR 37 PFAS CHEMICALS AND QUESTIONNAIRE DATA FROM 50 HOMES CONCORDANT WITH BIOMONITORING DATA, 2) TOTAL FLUORINE (TF) AND EXTRACTABLE ORGANOFLUORINE (EOF) CONCENTRATIONS LEVELS IN 50 HOUSE DUST SAMPLES, 3) EVALUATED PROTOCOLS AND SOPS FOR MEASURING A TARGETED SET OF PFAS IN THE RESIDENTIAL ENVIRONMENT, INCLUDING DRINKING WATER; AND 4) PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT OF RESIDENTIAL EXPOSURES, INCLUDING RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MEASURED INDOOR AIR AND HOUSE DUST CONCENTRATIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS WITH HOUSING CHARACTERISTICS AND BEHAVIORS RELATED TO CONSUMER PRODUCTS WITHIN THE HOME. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES ARE STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH MANAGERS, THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY, AND COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY RESIDENTIAL PFAS EXPOSURE.
description.239:
DESCRIPTION:
THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO DEVELOP, CHARACTERIZE, AND DEMONSTRATE A NOVEL TECHNIQUE FOR A LOW-COST WAY OF MEASURING ORGANIC HAZARDOUS AIR POLLUTANTS (HAPS) WITH HIGH SENSITIVITY AND SELECTIVITY AND AT HIGH TIME RESOLUTION. 
ACTIVITIES:
ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: 1) DEVELOPING A NEW MULTIDIMENSIONAL TECHNIQUE FOR IDENTIFYING AND QUANTIFYING HAZARDOUS AIR POLLUTANTS (HAPS); 2) DEMONSTRATING THE USE OF A PROTOTYPE DEVICE IN BOTH THE LABORATORY AND THE FIELD; 3) OPTIMIZING DATA PROCESSING AND INTERPRETATION USING ADVANCED ANALYSIS TECHNIQUES; AND 4) DEVELOPING A MODULAR APPROACH FOR OPTIMIZING MEASUREMENT METHODS TO TARGET SPECIFIC HAPS.
OUTCOMES:
THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES ARE ANNUAL PROGRESS AND FINAL REPORTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE DEVELOPMENT AND DEMONSTRATION OF PROTOTYPE INSTRUMENTS THAT PROVIDE LOW-COST WAYS TO CONDUCT REAL-TIME MONITORING OF HAPS. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY HAPS.
SUBRECIPIENT:
SUBAWARDEE MASSACHUSETTS INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY WILL LEAD THE DEVELOPMENT OF SENSOR ARRAY AND DATA APPROACHES TO INTERPRET THE RESULTS FOR THE PROTOTYPE DEVICE THAT WILL BE DEVELOPED. SUBAWARDEE SOUTH COAST AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT DISTRICT WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE OVERALL DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE LABORATORY TESTING PORTION OF THE PROJECT.
description.240:
DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ESTABLISH A PLATFORM TO QUANTIFY INTRAUTERINE EXPOSURE TO METAL MIXTURES AND DETERMINE THEIR EFFECT ON EPIGENETIC LOCI CHANGES IN NEWBORNS.ACTIVITIES:THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO (1) DEVELOP A STANDARDIZED METHODOLOGY FOR ASSESSING INTRAUTERINE EXPOSURE USING MECONIUM AS A BIOMARKER AND QUANTIFY METAL MIXTURES AMONG AN
URBAN POPULATION, AND (2) EXPLORE AND QUANTIFY THE EFFECT OF METAL MIXTURE EXPOSURE ON METHYLATED GENES FOR THREE ADVERSE BIRTH OUTCOMES: SMALL FOR GESTATIONAL AGE, INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, AND AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDERS. RESEARCHERS WILL DEVELOP A STANDARDIZED METHOD TO QUANTIFY METALS IN MECONIUM AND IMPLEMENT THIS APPROACH TO MEASURE METAL CONCENTRATIONS FROM NEWBORNS DELIVERED IN NEW YORK CITY. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL ALSO COLLECT BUCCAL CELLS FROM MOTHERS AND INFANTS AND IDENTIFY METHYLATED GENES FOR THE ADVERSE BIRTH OUTCOMES. RESEARCHERS WILL THEN INVESTIGATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE METAL MIXTURES AND DNA METHYLATION.SUBRECIPIENT:A SUBAWARD TO UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH CAROLINA ($97,947) WILL DEVELOP A COMPLEX BAYESIAN MIXTURE MODEL TO EVALUATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN METAL MIXTURES AND ADVERSE BIRTH OUTCOMES AND ANALYZE THE DNA METHYLATION IN THE PROPOSED STUDY.

A SUBAWARD TO MEDGER EVERS COLLEGE ($42,395) WILL DEVELOP A STANDARDIZED METHOD FOR ASSESSING METAL CONCENTRATIONS IN MECONIUM AS WELL AS SAMPLE DIGESTION AND PROCESSING FOR ANALYSIS.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS, AS WELL AS THE IDENTIFICATION OF GENE LOCI WHERE METAL MIXTURE EFFECTS RESULT IN CHANGES IN METHYLATION, WHICH COULD ENHANCE THE UNDERSTANDING OF THE PATHWAYS THAT RESULT IN HUMAN HARM. THE RESULTS OF THIS PROJECT MAY LEAD TO STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH ACTIONS TO IDENTIFY AT-RISK INFANTS AND DEVELOP REMEDIATION STRATEGIES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE MOTHERS AND INFANTS IN NEW YORK CITY, INFANTS AT RISK OF HEAVY METALS EXPOSURE, HUMAN HEALTH, THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.241:
DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO DEVELOP A NON-MARKET VALUATION SURVEY ADMINISTERED TO RESIDENTS ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER TO EVALUATE HOW BENEFITS VARY ACROSS SOCIOECONOMIC AND GEOGRAPHIC SCALES AND POPULATIONS OF CONCERN. RESEARCH WILL EVALUATE TRADEOFFS BETWEEN EQUITY AND EFFICIENCY WITH RESPECT TO WATER QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS AND RIVER RESTORATION AND WILL ALSO EXPLORE HOW DIFFERENT METHODS LEAD TO ALTERNATIVE POLICY CONCLUSIONS RESULTING IN BETTER APPROACHES/TOOLS FOR POTENTIAL POLICY ACTIONS. OVERALL, THE RESEARCH WILL EMPOWER COMMUNITIES TO ADVOCATE FOR THEIR PRIORITIES AND WILL LEAD TO IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING OF THE BENEFITS AND DISTRIBUTION OF WATER QUALITY CHANGES. ACTIVITIES:ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE A NON-MARKET VALUATION SURVEY ADMINISTERED TO RESIDENTS OF THE 246 COUNTIES AND PARISHES THAT BORDER OR ARE ADJACENT TO THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER. THE SURVEY WILL ASK RESPONDENTS TO REPORT DAY AND OVERNIGHT TRIPS TO THE RIVER AND WILL INCLUDE A DISCRETE CHOICE REFERENDUM BASED ON PROPOSED CHANGES IN WATERSHED RESTORATION AND MANAGEMENT, RECREATIONAL, CULTURAL, AND/OR ECOLOGICAL VALUES. IN ADDITION TO A 'PUSH TO WEB' APPROACH BASED ON POSTCARD MAILERS TO A RANDOMLY-SELECTED ADDRESS#8208;BASED SAMPLE, POTENTIAL SURVEY PARTICIPANTS WILL BE IDENTIFIED VIA SOCIAL MEDIA PROFILES AND SIGNAGE AT RIVER LOCATIONS WILL DIRECT VISITORS TO AN ONLINE SURVEY. ENGAGEMENT WITH COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS WORKING ON ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ALONG THE RIVER WILL TAKE THE FORM OF PARTICIPATORY WORKSHOPS AND CO-DESIGN OF CITIZEN SCIENCE APPROACHES THAT ADDRESS COMMUNITY-ARTICULATED PRIORITIES FOR RESTORATION OR MANAGEMENT.SUBRECIPIENT:UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON, LEAD PI, SPENCER WOOD
TEAM MEMBERS FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON WILL:
-DEVELOP, TEST, AND DEPLOY APPROACHES FOR USING NEW TECHNOLOGY AND DATA SOURCES TO ELICIT INFORMATION FROM COMMUNITIES WITHIN THE STUDY CORRIDOR.
-STORE AND AGGREGATE RAW DATA TO CHARACTERIZE POPULATIONS
-SUMMARIZE FINDINGS IN REPORTS AND PUBLICATIONS

MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY, LEAD PI, DR. FRANK LUPI
TEAM MEMBERS FROM MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY WILL:
-CONTRIBUTE TO THE DESIGN, TESTING AND IMPLEMENTATION OF WATER QUALITY VALUES USING THE SURVEY DATA AND AVAILABLE SECONDARY DATA
-ADVISE O N AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE ECONOMIC MODELING OF WATER QUALITY VALUES USING THE SURVEY DATA AND AVAILABLE SECONDARY DATA.
-CONTRIBUTE TO AND CO-AUTHOR PROJECT-RELATED PUBLICATIONS.OUTCOMES:GRANT RESULTS INCLUDE NEW METHODS OF ELICITING ENVIRONMENTAL VALUES AND INSIGHTS INTO HOW DIFFERENT METHODS LEAD TO ALTERNATIVE POLICY CONCLUSIONS ACROSS EQUITY AND EFFICIENCY OBJECTIVES. IN ADDITION TO PEER REVIEWED PAPERS AND PRESENTATIONS, THE RESEARCH WILL MAKE CONTRIBUTIONS TO BENEFIT-COST ANALYSES AND WILL  INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEXT-GENERATION INTEGRATED ASSESSMENT MODELS BY TESTING THE GENERALIZABILITY AND SCALABILITY OF NEW METHODS FOR VALUATION ACROSS SPATIAL AND DEMOGRAPHIC GRADIENTS. LAST, THE PROJECT WILL DELIVER BENEFICIAL OUTCOMES TO PARTNER COMMUNITIES ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THE PUBLIC, STATE AND LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL AGENCIES, REGULATORS, AND PARTNER COMMUNITIES ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER.
description.242: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY COMMUNITY STRESSORS AND RESILIENCE-ENHANCING ASSETS THAT SHAPE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN CLIMATE CHANGE-RELATED EXPOSURES [HEAT, OZONE (O3), FINE PARTICULATE MATTER (PM2.5)] AND CHILD HEALTH.ACTIVITIES:THIS PROJECT WILL: 1) WORK WITH NY PEDIATRIC ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH SPECIALTY UNITS (PEHSU) AND COMMUNITY AND GOVERNMENT PARTNERS TO PRIORITIZE STRESSORS AND ASSETS; 2) LEVERAGE COMPLETE PATIENT-LEVEL DATA ON ALL CHILD (AGE 0-17) EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT VISITS AND HOSPITALIZATIONS IN UPSTATE NY OVER 2005-2019; 3) EXAMINE STRESSORS IDENTIFIED BY THE NYS DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION CLIMATE JUSTICE WORKING GROUP, AND APPLY THE RESILIENCE ACTIVATION FRAMEWORK, WHICH ORGANIZES ASSETS IN FIVE DOMAINS (HUMAN, ECONOMIC, SOCIAL, POLITICAL, ENVIRONMENTAL CAPITAL); 4) GENERATE DAILY FINE-SCALE EXPOSURE ESTIMATES FOR HEAT, O3, AND PM2.5, AND EXAMINE VARIATION IN EXPOSURE-HEALTH RELATIONSHIPS USING CASE-CROSSOVER METHODS; AND 5) APPLY CLIMATE PROJECTIONS TO ESTIMATE IMPACTS UNDER VARYING EMISSIONS SCENARIOS, AND, WITH PARTNERS, INTEGRATE FINDINGS INTO LOCAL AND STATE CLIMATE ADAPTATION AND PEDIATRIC CLINICAL INITIATIVES.SUBRECIPIENT:UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURG ($120,551) WILL SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF DATA MANAGEMENT AND GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM (GIS) ANALYSIS FOR THE PROJECT. ICAHN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AT MOUNT SINAI ($527,838) WILL PROVIDE LOCAL CLINICAL EXPERTISE IN CHILD HEALTH OUTCOMES, ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES, AND COMMUNITY ASSETS, INPUT ON USE OF NY CHILDREN'S HEALTH DATA, AND ASSIST ANALYSIS OF ASSET INDICATORS AND ADVISE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF STATISTICAL ANALYSIS.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS AS WELL AS INDICATORS AND MAPS OF CRITICAL ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSORS TO PROVIDE PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES, PEDIATRIC SPECIALISTS, COMMUNITY LEADERS, AND PARENTS WITH EVIDENCE THAT TAILORED INVESTMENTS IN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COMMUNITIES TODAY CAN ALLEVIATE CURRENT AND FUTURE CLIMATE IMPACTS ON CHILDREN'S HEALTH. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PARENTS AND CHILDREN IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN NEW YORK STATE AND SIMILAR COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY.
description.243: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL IS TO ADDRESS AIR POLLUTION AND SUBSEQUENT HEALTH IMPACTS WHILE CONSIDERING THE CHALLENGES FOR ENERGY, MOBILITY, ACCESSIBILITY, AND EQUITABILITY IN FIFTEEN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN THE COLUMBUS METROPOLITAN AREA (CMA). ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL 1) PARTNER WITH UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN THE CMA TO UNDERSTAND THEIR NEEDS FOR ELECTRIFICATION AND MOBILITY AND EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF CURRENT EFFORTS; 2) DEVELOP STRATEGIES TO GUIDE TRANSITION INVESTMENT AND DEPLOYMENT TO IMPROVE HEALTH, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND SOCIAL CONDITIONS OVER TIME FOR THE CMA COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE URBAN-EXURBAN-RURAL GRADIENT; AND 3) UNDERSTAND HOW KNOWLEDGE, PERCEPTION, AND VALUES VARY, AND DESIGN AND EVALUATE INFORMATIONAL INTERVENTIONS THAT INFORM INDIVIDUAL AND DOMICILE-LEVEL DECISIONS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS. OTHER EXPECTED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE: COMMUNITY ASSESSMENTS AND TOOLKITS TO SUPPORT LOCAL AND REGIONAL DECISION-MAKERS ON TRANSITIONS TO ELECTRIFIED ENERGY AND MOBILITY; AND ELECTRICITY AND MOBILITY INFRASTRUCTURE PLANNING WHITE PAPERS AND PRESENTATIONS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE TESTED INFORMATIONAL INTERVENTIONS FOR USE IN HELPING MARGINALIZED COMMUNITIES UNDERSTAND THE DECISIONS FACING THEIR HOUSEHOLDS DURING ELECTRIFIED ENERGY AND MOBILITY TRANSITIONS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN THE COLUMBUS METROPOLITAN AREA AS WELL AS RESEARCHERS WORKING WITH SIMILAR COMMUNITIES TO ADDRESS AIR QUALITY, PUBLIC HEALTH, AND COST CONCERNS ASSOCIATED WITH ELECTRIFIED ENERGY AND TRANSPORTATION SERVICES.
description.244: DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DESIGN A SUSTAINABLE AND AFFORDABLE STRATEGY TO TREAT HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS (HABS) USING SUNLIGHT DRIVEN PHOTOCATALYSTS THAT WILL DEGRADE THE CYANOBACTERIA. RESEARCHERS WILL DEVELOP 3D-PRINTED FLOATING STRUCTURES COATED WITH PHOTOCATALYSTS, WHICH CAN BE DEPLOYED IN WATER BODIES THAT FREQUENTLY EXPERIENCE CYANOBACTERIA-DOMINATED HABS SUCH AS THE INDIAN LAKE IN WORCESTER, MA. ACTIVITIES:THE TEAM WILL DESIGN AND FABRICATE 3D-PRINTED FLOATED SYSTEMS WHICH: 1) HAVE HIGH SPECIFIC SURFACE AREA FOR HIGH EFFICIENCY; 2) ARE COATED WITH A FULLY EXPOSED, UNIFORM LAYER OF PHOTOCATALYST ON THE SURFACE FOR HIGH NUMBER OF EXPOSED ACTIVE SITES; 3) ARE INTENTIONALLY DESIGNED TO BE IN THE SHAPE OF LOCALLY-OCCURRING N LOCAL WILDLIFE; 4) CAN BREAKDOWN CYANOBACTERIA; 5) CAN BE QUICKLY DEPLOYED AT THE SITE-OF-CONCERN AND 6) CAN BE RETRIEVED BY SWIMMING ROBOTS AND REUSED WHEN/WHERE NEEDED.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT IS EXPECTED TO PRODUCE MULTIPLE PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS IN JOURNALS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE A REUSABLE PROTOTYPE PREPARED BY MODIFIED 3D PRINTING PROCESS WHICH CAN BE DEPLOYED INTO WATER BODIES WHEN NEEDED TO CONTROL HAB OUTBREAKS EFFICIENTLY AND RECOVERED AFTER TREATMENT. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE WATER QUALITY MANAGERS, HUMAN HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.245: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND AND PREDICT OCCURRENCE OF DISINFECTION BYPRODUCTS, OPPORTUNISTIC PATHOGENS AND THE ASSOCIATED HEALTH RISK TRADEOFFS POSED BY THEM IN DRINKING WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS (DWDS) ACROSS THE CONTINENTAL U.S.ACTIVITIES:THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A STRATEGIC MONITORING PROGRAM THROUGH PARTNERSHIP WITH PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENTS AND WATER UTILITY MANAGERS AND ANALYSIS OF HISTORIC DATA TO SAMPLE WATER FOR REGULATED AND UNREGULATED DISINFECTION BYPRODUCTS (DBPS) AND PATHOGENS. THE RESEARCH WILL ALSO CONDUCT A CHEMICAL AND QUANTITATIVE MICROBIAL RISK ASSESSMENT AND EVALUATION OF RISK-RISK TRADEOFFS CONSIDERING TEMPORAL, SPATIAL AND POPULATION DYNAMICS.SUBRECIPIENT:OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY ($115,121 EPA, $28,794 COST SHARE) WILL HELP TO COMPLETE THE MICROBIAL RISK ASSESSMENTS AND LEAD THE RISK TRADE-OFF EVALUATION. DREXEL UNIVERSITY ($41,278 EPA, $9,945 COST SHARE) WILL PROVIDE DEEP EXPERTISE AND EXPERIENCE IN WATER DISINFECTION AND RISK ASSESSMENT. THE COLLEGE OF NEW JERSEY ($102,042 EPA, $33,000 COST SHARE) WILL LEAD EFFORTS TO EVALUATE HISTORIC EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND MONITORING DATA TO SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF A STRATEGIC SAMPLING PLAN AND ASSIST WITH THE RISK TRADE-OFF EVALUATION. CLEMSON UNIVERSITY ($716,806 EPA, $178,820 COST SHARE) WILL LEAD THE ANALYTICAL ASSESSMENT OF REGULATED AND UNREGULATED DBPS IN DRINKING WATER SAMPLES COLLECTED IN THE PROJECT TO EVALUATE OCCURRENCE AND CONCENTRATIONS. TULANE UNIVERSITY ($670,129 EPA, $167,431 COST SHARE) WILL LEAD THE MICROBIAL WATER QUALITY ANALYSIS FOR OPPORTUNISTIC PATHOGENS AND OTHER RELEVANT PARAMETERS IN DRINKING WATER SAMPLES COLLECTED IN THE PROJECT TO DETERMINE OCCURRENCE AND CONCENTRATIONS OF SPECIES OF INTEREST. THE NY STATE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH ($46,000 EPA, $11,250 COST SHARE) WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE SELECTION AND EVALUATION OF HEALTH OUTCOME AND MONITORING DATA RELATED TO LEGIONELLA IN NY STATE. THEY WILL PROVIDE RESEARCH DIRECTION ON STRATEGIC SAMPLING IN LOCATIONS WITHIN DWDS THAT MAY BE OF PARTICULAR CONCERN FOR SAMPLING. ADDITIONALLY, THEY WILL COORDINATE SAMPLING WITHIN NY STATE WATER SYSTEMS.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE PUBLICATIONS, RISK MODELS, AND DATA TO INFORM DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO HOST WORKSHOPS AND ONLINE COMMUNICATIONS TO ENGAGE STAKEHOLDERS AS WELL AS DEVELOP TOOLKIT FOR COMMUNICATIONS OUTREACH. THE OUTCOME OF THIS WORK WILL ENABLE MOVEMENT AWAY FROM ROUTINE MONITORING FOR THESE HAZARDS TOWARDS TOOLS FOR MORE COMPREHENSIVE WATER SYSTEM EVALUATION, RISK-BASED AND PRIORITIZED MONITORING STRATEGIES BASED ON DRINKING WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM CHARACTERISTICS, AND THE BIOLOGICAL, CHEMICAL, AND PHYSICAL PARAMETERS MOST LIKELY TO LEAD TO ELEVATED RISKS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE RESIDENTS OF NEW YORK, STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, WATER UTILITY MANAGERS, AND SITE MANAGERS AND OPERATORS.
description.246:
DESCRIPTION:THIS APPLICATION PROPOSES A HIGHLY INNOVATIVE PROJECT TO ASSESS THE TRADEOFFS BETWEEN OPPORTUNISTIC PATHOGENS (OPS) AND DISINFECTION BY-PRODUCTS (DBPS) AND DEVELOP STRATEGIES FOR LIMITING EXPOSURE TO BOTH CLASSES OF WATER CONTAMINANTS VIA U.S. DRINKING WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS. 
ACTIVITIES:THIS PROJECT WILL QUANTIFY AND ASSESS OPS, REGULATED DBPS, AND UNREGULATED DBPS. SUBRECIPIENT:TOWSON UNIVERSITY ($377,267 EPA, $94,320 COST SHARE) WILL PERFORM DBP ANALYSES. JOHNS HOPKINS ($424,851 EPA, $233,427 COST SHARE) WILL PERFORM NON-TARGET DBP ANALYSIS AND TOXICITY TESTING. UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA, FAIRBANKS ($321,820 EPA, $80,455 COST SHARE) WILL PERFORM DATA ANALYTICS AND MODELING.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL PROGRESS AND FINAL REPORTS, PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS, AND CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS.  INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE WATER UTILITIES AND COMMUNITIES SERVED BY WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS THROUGHOUT THE U.S.
description.247: THE OVERALL PROJECT GOAL IS TO DEVELOP AND SCALE UP AN INNOVATIVE BIOREACTOR AND BIOCHAR-SORPTION-CHANNEL (B2) TREATMENT SYSTEM TO EFFECTIVELY CAPTURE NUTRIENTS FROM SUBSURFACE DRAINAGE WATER, RECYCLE NUTRIENT-CAPTURED BIOCHARS AS A SLOW-RELEASE FERTILIZER, AND KEEP NUTRIENTS IN THE CLOSED AGRICULTURAL LOOP. THIS PROJECT WILL OFFER AN INNOVATIVE, FEASIBLE, AND COST-EFFECTIVE PRACTICE TO MITIGATE NUTRIENT POLLUTION IN WATERSHEDS FROM AGRICULTURAL FIELDS, IMPROVE WATER QUALITY, AND THEREBY DIMINISH THE OCCURRENCE OF HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS (HABS).
description.248:
DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EXAMINE CHEMICAL MIXTURES OF INCREASING COMPLEXITY FOR THEIR DEVIATIONS FROM EXPECTED ADIPOGENIC EFFECTS USING CONCENTRATION ADDITION AND INDEPENDENT ACTION MODELS.
ACTIVITIES:THE RECIPIENT WILL INTERROGATE THE COMPARABILITY OF JOINT TOXICITY AS WELL AS THE DEVELOPMENT OF METHODS FOCUSED VARIOUS LEVELS OF BIOLOGICAL ORGANIZATION. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO (1) EVALUATE MIXTURES OF INCREASING COMPLEXITY FOR ABILITY TO PROMOTE ADIPOGENESIS; (2) ASSESS AVAILABLE MIXTURE MODELS THROUGH CONTROLLED ASSESSMENTS OF CONTAMINANTS ACTING THROUGH SHARED, DISTINCT, AND MIXED MECHANISMS; AND (3) PROMOTE A GREATER FUNCTIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF COMPLEX MIXTURE EFFECTS THAT CAN BE UTILIZED TO BOLSTER RISK ASSESSMENTS OF DIVERSE CONTAMINANT EXPOSURES. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS, AS WELL AS A NEW METHOD OF MIXTURE RISK ASSESSMENTS THROUGH USING COMPONENT MECHANISTIC EFFECT LEVELS TO DETERMINE COOPERATIVE EFFECTS ON COMPLEX HEALTH ENDPOINTS AND/OR OUTCOMES. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL UTILIZE ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES (HOUSEHOLD DUST) TO DEVELOP A RECEPTOR BIOACTIVITY COMPONENT MODEL TO PREDICT ADIPOGENIC HEALTH OUTCOMES. THE RESULTS OF THIS PROJECT MAY PROMOTE A GREATER FUNCTIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF COMPLEX MIXTURE EFFECTS THAT CAN BE UTILIZED TO BOLSTER RISK ASSESSMENTS OF DIVERSE CONTAMINANT EXPOSURES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE PEOPLE AT RISK OF METABOLIC HEALTH CONDITIONS, HUMAN HEALTH, THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.249:
DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO ENGAGE S.E. QUEENS RESIDENTS IN THE MEASUREMENTS OF KEY AIR POLLUTANTS (NO2, O3, SO2, PM2.5, TOXIC METALS AND PFAS), THROUGH COMMUNITY-BASED
PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH (CBPR), INCREASING THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF CLIMATIC FACTORS AND AIR POLLUTION IMPACTS ON HEALTH, AND EMPOWERING THEM TO USE SUCH KNOWLEDGE TO INFORM POLICY ON ALLEVIATING CLIMATE IMPACTS AND SUSTAINING GOOD HEALTH.ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT CBPR IS A POWERFUL DRIVER IN PROMOTING AIR POLLUTION REDUCTION WITH THE AIM OF PROTECTING THE HEALTH OF S.E. QUEENS RESIDENTS AND THE ENVIRONMENT. THE PROJECT WILL (1) DEMONSTRATE THE IMPACT OF POLLUTANT EMISSIONS FROM NEARBY WASTE STATIONS ON AIR QUALITY IN S.E. QUEENS THROUGH RESEARCH FIELD MEASUREMENTS; (2) TRAIN RESIDENTS TO DEVELOP COMMUNITY SCIENCE STRATEGIES SUCH AS CROWDSOURCING TOOLS WITH NEW KNOWLEDGE GAINED FROM THE MEASUREMENTS, ENABLING RESIDENTS FACING ENVIRONMENTAL INJUSTICE TO MOBILIZE NEW INNOVATIVE, LOW-COST, REPLICABLE STRATEGIES LEADING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS FOR BETTER MANAGEMENT OF WASTE TRANSFER STATIONS; AND (3) TRANSLATE THE RESEARCH DATA AND COMMUNITY INPUT INTO STATE AND LOCAL CLIMATE AND POLICY SOLUTIONS FOR TRAFFIC EMISSION REDUCTION AND RELIEF FROM CURRENT HEALTH STRESSORS, IMPROVING QUALITY OF LIFE.  SUBRECIPIENT:CUNY-MEDGAR EVERS COLLEGE ($245,629) WILL PROVIDE MEASUREMENT/MONITORING OF AIR POLLUTANTS INCLUDING PM2.5 AND PFAS.

RUTGERS UNIVERSITY ($335,076) WILL (1) LEAD SAMPLING EFFORTS AT THREE SITES TO DETERMINE TOXIC METALS ASSOCIATED WITH PM2.5, (2) PARTICIPATE IN SAMPLING PREPARATION AND ANALYTICAL LAB PROCEDURES, (3) SUPERVISE A GRADUATE STUDENT, AND (4) LEAD LAB TOUR TO PROMOTE COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT.

OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS, AS WELL AS JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS WITH CRITICAL DATA ADDRESSING URGENT ISSUES ASSOCIATED WITH URBAN, MINORITY, AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES THAT HAVE NEVER BEEN INVESTIGATED IN NEW YORK CITY. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED HEALTH AND WELL-BEING FOR RESIDENTS LIVING IN LOW-INCOME URBAN MINORITY COMMUNITIES. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, STATE AND LOCAL POLICY MAKERS, ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGERS, AND COMMUNITY LEADERS.
description.250:
DESCRIPTION:THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO ENGAGE SMALL COMMUNITIES THAT ARE RELIANT ON SMALL WATER SUPPLY SYSTEMS AND EMPOWER THEM TO IDENTIFY STRATEGIES THAT SUSTAIN WATER QUALITY, QUANTITY, AND ACCESSIBILITY AND PROVIDE RESILIENT CONTINUOUS ACCESS TO POTABLE WATER. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE CHALLENGES AND PROBLEMS CLIMATE VARIABILITY AND CHANGE POSE TO WATER DISTRIBUTION AND QUALITY THAT MIGHT IMPACT PUBLIC HEALTH THROUGH WATERBORNE DISEASES. ACTIVITIES:METEOROLOGICAL OBSERVATIONS WILL ESTABLISH CLIMATE RELATIONSHIPS IMPORTANT TO PATHOGEN EXPOSURE AND PROVIDE INFORMATION TO UNDERSTAND HIGH RESOLUTION CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECTIONS FOR
MICROCLIMATES. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT METHODS, KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS, DATA COLLECTION OF RAINFALL, WATER QUALITY, AND SURVEILLANCE OF WATERBORNE PATHOGENS WILL BE CONDUCTED. RESULTS WILL BE SHARED WITH WATER OPERATORS AND STAKEHOLDERS TO DETERMINE COMMUNITY-LED, SCIENCE-BASED SOLUTIONS APPROPRIATE FOR EACH CONTEXT TO MITIGATE HEALTH IMPACTS. OBSERVED FACTORS LIKE NUMBER SERVED, FINANCIAL STATUS, ACCUMULATED RAINFALL, WATER SOURCE, WATER TREATMENT, AND POWER SOURCE WHEN USED WITH HIGH-RESOLUTION CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECTIONS WILL PROVIDE HOLISTIC SOLUTIONS FOR RISK ASSESSMENT AND BUILDING RESILIENCE.SUBRECIPIENT:THE INTER AMERICAN UNIVERSITY ($490,660) WILL PROVIDE EXPERTISE ON WATER SAMPLING DESIGN, COMMUNITY VISITS, DESIGN OF WATER QUALITY RELATED DATA COLLECTION, AND FORMS FOR SELF -REPORTED HEALTH DATA FROM COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND WILL CONDUCT COMMUNITY VISITS AND ANALYZE DATA RELATED TO WATER QUALITY AND HUMAN HEALTH. NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY ($180,649) WILL PROVIDE EXPERTISE ON CLIMATE RELATED DATA COLLECTION AND DESIGN THIS ASPECT OF INFORMATION COLLECTION AND ANALYSES. THIS INCLUDES TRAINING COMMUNITY LEADERS AND MEMBERS TO COLLECT AND REPORT DATA ON RAIN QUANTITY AND FREQUENCY, TEMPERATURE, AND OTHER INDICATORS.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS, AS WELL AS SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION REGARDING WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY RISK ASSESSMENTS FOR CAPACITY BUILDING. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE ADVANCING THE SCIENCE AND UNDERSTANDING OF IMPACTS OF WEATHER AND CLIMATIC CHANGE ON RURAL COMMUNITIES AND MICROCLIMATES. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE RESIDENTS AND RESOURCE MANAGERS IN PUERTO RICO AND OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES.
description.251: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO RESEARCH AND BRING ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE-FOCUSED STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE SEPTIC FAILURES IN COASTAL COMMUNITIES UNDER THE ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS OF RISING SEA LEVELS AND INCREASED FLOODING.ACTIVITIES:RESEARCHERS WILL 1) IDENTIFY AND PARTNER WITH VULNERABLE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES THAT ARE AT RISK OF SEPTIC SYSTEM FAILURES NOW AND IN THE FUTURE DUE TO CLIMATE CHANGES; 2) ADDRESS THE ANTECEDENT CONDITIONS (INCLUDING HISTORICAL SETTLEMENT PATTERNS AND EXCLUSION FROM MUNICIPAL SEWERS) THAT POTENTIALLY EXACERBATE CONTAMINANT EXPOSURE BY COLLECTING PRIMARY DATA ON SEPTIC HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT TO DEVELOP COMPOSITE RISKS; AND 3) EVALUATE WHERE AND HOW SPECIFIC POLICY AND TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS CAN ADDRESS THE COMPOUNDED RISKS, WHILE ENSURING THAT BENEFITS ACCRUE IN A WAY THAT ADDRESSES PAST DISCRIMINATORY PRACTICES.SUBRECIPIENT:RESOURCES FOR THE FUTURE ($477,000) WILL MEASURE THE VALUE OF SEWER AS CAPTURED IN PROPERTY VALUES AND AS MEASURED BY THE PREFERENCES OF LOCAL RESIDENTS AND COMMUNITY LEADERS. GEORGE MASON UNIVERSITY ($226,000) WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FLOOD HAZARDS MODELING COMPONENT OF THE PROPOSED WORK, INCLUDING CLIMATE INDUCED COASTAL FLOODING AND SEA-LEVEL RISE INUNDATION. SOUTHEAST RURAL COMMUNITY ASSISTANCE PROJECT ($117,705) WILL CO-PRODUCE RESEARCH (E.G., GUIDING RESEARCH QUESTIONS TO ENSURE THEY ARE RELEVANT); SUPPORT DATA-SHARING WHERE APPROPRIATE; ADMINISTER A SURVEY OR SUPPORT RESIDENT INTERVIEWS; SUPPORT COLLECTION OF WATER/SOIL SAMPLES; AND SUPPORT RESEARCH OUTREACH.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS AS WELL AS SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS, EDUCATIONAL INFORMATION, AND SOLUTIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES AND COMMUNITY PLANNERS TO PREVENT AND MITIGATE SEPTIC FAILURES IN UNDERSERVED COASTAL COMMUNITIES. EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE PREVENTION OF WATER CONTAMINATION FROM SEPTIC FAILURES AND IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE UNDERSERVED COASTAL COMMUNITIES IN EASTERN MARYLAND, STATE AND LOCAL WATER RESOURCE MANAGERS, AND STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES.
description.252: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL IS TO ANALYZE IMPACTS OF CURRENT ENERGY SYSTEMS AND PATHWAYS FOR ENERGY TRANSITIONS THAT ENHANCE WELL-BEING THROUGH IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH, ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY, AND ENERGY JUSTICE OUTCOMES WITH A FOCUS ON UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING A TRIBAL NATION AND RURAL COMMUNITIES, IN A FOREST-DEPENDENT REGION IN NORTHERN MICHIGAN.ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL: 1) QUANTIFY THE IMPACTS OF WOOD, PAPER, PLASTICS, AND TIRE-DERIVED FUELS (WPPT) ENERGY GENERATION IN TERMS OF ECONOMIC WELL-BEING AT THE HOUSEHOLD AND COMMUNITY SCALE AND OF AIR QUALITY AFFECTING HUMAN HEALTH; 2) EVALUATE THE IMPACTS AND POTENTIAL TRANSITION DRIVERS ASSOCIATED WITH LOCAL USE OF FUELWOOD ALONG WITH IMPROVED VENTILATION AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY OPTIONS; AND 3) ASSESS THE POTENTIAL DECARBONIZATION OF THE ELECTRIC POWER SECTOR TO PROVIDE ECONOMIC BENEFITS AND SECURE ACCESS TO ENERGY SERVICES IN WAYS THAT ENHANCE THE MANUFACTURING SECTOR AS WELL AS COMMUNITY AND HOUSEHOLD WELL-BEING IN TERMS OF AIR QUALITY, PUBLIC HEALTH AND ENERGY JUSTICE.SUBRECIPIENT:SUBAWARDEE CENTER FOR ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT WILL CONTRIBUTE TO PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT IN ALL ASPECTS OF INDOOR AIR QUALITY RESEARCH AND RESIDENTIAL ENERGY AUDIT AND ENERGY ASSESSMENTS. ($135,000)OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS. OTHER EXPECTED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE REPORTS AND JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS DOCUMENTING RESULTS OF THE RESEARCH. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING OF: 1) THE AIR QUALITY IMPACTS OF WPPT ENERGY PRODUCTION FOR UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES; 2) IMPACTS OF CURRENT ENERGY SERVICES PROVISION ON INDOOR AIR QUALITY AND POTENTIAL DRIVERS TO INCREASE ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND USE OF WOOD PRODUCTS IN WAYS THAT DO NOT HAVE NEGATIVE PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACTS; AND 3) POTENTIAL DRIVERS OF A TRANSITION IN FOREST PRODUCT USE THAT CAN SUPPORT JUST ENERGY SERVICES ACCESS AS WELL AS ECONOMIC WELL-BEING FOR HOUSEHOLDS, COMMUNITIES, AND INDUSTRIES THAT ENHANCE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE RURAL COMMUNITIES AND TRIBAL NATIONS IN FOREST DEPENDENT AREAS IN THE GREAT LAKES REGION AS RESEARCHERS WORKING WITH SIMILAR COMMUNITIES TO ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS ASSOCIATED WITH LARGE-SCALE CHANGES IN THE ENERGY SYSTEMS.
description.253: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP AN ENERGY-JUSTICE MODEL FOR FREIGHT VEHICLE ELECTRIFICATION IN AN URBAN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COMMUNITY THAT IS RESPONSIVE TO COMMUNITY NEEDS WHILE ADVANCING SCIENCE IN AIR QUALITY, PUBLIC HEALTH, SOCIOECONOMIC, ORGANIZATIONAL, AND INSTITUTIONAL FACTORS THAT PLAY A ROLE IN ASSESSING BENEFITS AND COSTS OF TRANSITIONING INTO FREIGHT VEHICLE ELECTRIFICATION.ACTIVITIES:THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE: 1) ANALYZE THE SOCIOTECHNICAL REGIME IN WHICH A TRANSITION TO ELECTRIFIED FREIGHT VEHICLES WILL OCCUR; 2) EVALUATE POTENTIAL SCENARIOS FOR SUCH A TRANSITION IN TERMS OF THEIR REDUCTION IN AIR EMISSIONS; AND 3) DETERMINE THE HEALTH BENEFITS OF SUCH A TRANSITION FOR A COMMUNITY THAT IS HEAVILY IMPACTED BY FREIGHT VEHICLE TRAFFIC. SUBRECIPIENT:SUBAWARDEE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS CHICAGO WILL LEAD THE WORK ON BASELINE EXPOSURE ASSESSMENT, ELECTRIFICATION SCENARIO ANALYSIS OF EMISSION MODELING, AIR DISPERSION MODELING, AND EXPOSURE AND HEALTH IMPACTS ASSESSMENT. UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS CHICAGO WILL ALSO BE INVOLVED IN RECRUITING COMMUNITY PARTICIPANTS, MOBILE SENSOR TRAINING, AND BASELINE AIR MONITORING DATA COLLECTION.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS. OTHER EXPECTED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A COMMUNITY AIR MONITORING AND EXPOSURE ASSESSMENT PLAN (AMEAP); COMMUNITY AIR MONITORING GUIDANCE MATERIALS FOR LOW-COST SENSORS; A DATA REPOSITORY THAT CONTAINS A VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND TRAFFIC DATA COLLECTED BY THE PROJECT; A HOLISTIC ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ANALYSIS TOOL KIT; AND AN ONLINE MAPPING TOOL FOR COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE IMPROVED ABILITY TO PREDICT THE POTENTIAL PUBLIC HEALTH AND AIR QUALITY RISK TRADEOFFS IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES DUE TO THE FREIGHT ELECTRIFICATION-RELATED ENERGY TRANSITIONS; AND ENHANCED SOCIOECONOMIC, CULTURAL, AND BEHAVIORAL INSIGHTS THAT CAN INFORM FUTURE ELECTRIFICATION SCENARIOS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE THE RESIDENTS OF THE LITTLE VILLAGE NEIGHBORHOOD IN SOUTHWEST CHICAGO AND SIMILAR COMMUNITIES SITUATED NEAR FREIGHT RAILS AS WELL AS RESEARCHERS WORKING WITH SIMILAR COMMUNITIES TO ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS ASSOCIATED WITH LARGE-SCALE CHANGES IN ENERGY AND TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS.
description.254:
DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO ENGAGE WITH STATE AND TRIBAL WETLAND PROGRAMS TO IDENTIFY EXAMPLES OF EXISTING PLANS, PROGRAMS, TOOLS, AND METHODOLOGIES AND HIGHLIGHT OPPORTUNITIES TO BETTER INTEGRATE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE IN RESTORATION AND PROTECTION PROGRAMS. THE MAIN OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP THE CAPACITY OF STATE, TRIBAL, TERRITORIAL, AND LOCAL WETLAND PROGRAMS TO DEVELOP, FUND, AND IMPLEMENT CONSERVATION AND RESTORATION PROJECTS THAT INCORPORATE COMMUNITY GOALS AND, WHERE APPROPRIATE AND POSSIBLE, PRIORITIZE THE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF VULNERABLE AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES.

TO SUPPORT THIS GOAL, ELI WILL: ASSEMBLE AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE, CONDUCT DESK RESEARCH AND IN-DEPTH INTERVIEWS WITH STATE AND LOCAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS AND WETLAND PROGRAM MANAGERS, DEVELOP A RESEARCH REPORT, RECORD TWO PODCASTS, HOST A WEBINAR, AND WRITE AND PUBLISH AN ARTICLE DETAILING THE FINDINGS OF THE RESEARCH REPORT.
ACTIVITIES:SPECIFICALLY, ELI WILL: 1) ENGAGE WITH EIGHT TO TEN NATIONAL EXPERTS FROM STATE AND TRIBAL WETLAND PROGRAMS; OTHER STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES; ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COMMUNITIES, AND CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS TO GUIDE THE PROJECT; 2) CONDUCT RESEARCH AND INTERVIEWS INCLUDING IDENTIFY AND ANALYZE EXISTING WETLAND AND AQUATIC RESOURCE PLANS, PROGRAMS, ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING METHODOLOGIES, AND PRIORITIZATION TOOLS; 3) DEVELOP A REPORT THAT WILL DESCRIBE EFFECTIVE APPROACHES TO HELP STATE AND TRIBAL WETLAND PROGRAMS DEVELOP, FUND, AND IMPLEMENT CONSERVATION AND RESTORATION PROJECTS THAT BUILD IN COMMUNITY GOALS AND, WHERE APPROPRIATE AND POSSIBLE, PRIORITIZE THE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF VULNERABLE AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES; 4) DEVELOP DETAILED CASE STUDIES OF STATES, TRIBES, AND/OR LOCAL GOVERNMENTS THAT HAVE ENGAGED IN NOTEWORTHY AND INNOVATE APPROACHES FOR ACCOUNTING FOR COMMUNITY INPUT IN MAPPING, PLANNING, AND FUNDING FOR RESTORATION PROJECTS; 5) HOST A WEBINAR AND RECORD TWO PODCAST EPISODES THAT FEATURE THE FINDINGS OF THE RESEARCH REPORT; 6) PUBLISH AN ARTICLE TO REPORT THE RESEARCH FINDINGS MORE BROADLY FOR INTERESTED STAKEHOLDERS; 7) PUBLISH A BLOG POST HIGHLIGHTING KEY THEMES IDENTIFIED IN THE RESEARCH, AND; 8) POST THE RESULTS OF OUR RESEARCH ON ELI'S WETLANDS (WWW.ELI.ORG/WETLANDS-PROGRAM) WEBPAGE.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:THE INTENDED PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE STATES, TRIBES, TERRITORIES AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS WHILE SECONDARY BENEFICIARIES ARE THE INTEREST PUBLIC.

RESULTS OF ACTIVITIES (OUTPUTS) THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THREE OUTPUTS: 
1. FINAL REPORT: ELI WILL PUBLISH A REPORT ON BEST PRACTICES AND CASE STUDIES THAT DEMONSTRATE HOW STATES, TRIBES, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS CAN INTEGRATE COMMUNITY PRIORITIES, PRIORITIZE STAKEHOLDER INPUT, INTEGRATE TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, AND ADDRESS INEQUITIES IN DISTRIBUTION OF RESOURCES AND BENEFITS IN RESTORATION AND CONSERVATION PROJECTS.
2. WEBINAR, PODCASTS, AND BLOG POSTS: THE PROJECT PARTNERS WILL DESIGN AND DELIVER AN IN-DEPTH WEBINAR ON THE FINDINGS OF THE RESEARCH. WE WILL ALSO CREATE TWO PODCASTS AND A BLOG POST ON KEY THEMES THAT EMERGE FROM THE RESEARCH.
3. ARTICLE: ELI WILL DEVELOP FOR PUBLICATION AN ARTICLE IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW REPORTER BASED ON OUR RESEARCH.

ANTICIPATED ENVIRONMENTAL IMPROVEMENT (OUTCOMES) ELI'S PROJECT WILL RESULT IN: 
1) INCREASED KNOWLEDGE OF STATE, TRIBAL, AND LOCAL WETLAND PROGRAMS ON HOW TO INTEGRATE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE IN WETLAND RESTORATION PROGRAMS
2. INCREASED NUMBER OF RESTORATION PLANS, TOOLS, AND METHODOLOGIES THAT BUILD IN STAKEHOLDER PARTICIPATION.
3. INCREASED NUMBER OF CONSERVATION AND RESTORATION PROJECTS IDENTIFIED AND DEVELOPED WITH COMMUNITY GOALS, STAKEHOLDER INPUT, AND TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND CULTURAL CONSIDERATIONS INTEGRATED.
4. INCREASED EQUITY IN DISTRIBUTION OF CONSERVATION AND RESTORATION INVESTMENT.
5. IMPROVED PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF WATERSHEDS AND AQUATIC ECOSYSTEM
description.255:
DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP THE CAPACITY OF STATE AND TRIBAL WETLAND PROGRAMS TO EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS CLIMATE CHANGE IN WETLAND MITIGATION AND RESTORATION PROJECTS TO ENSURE FUNCTIONS LOST TO PERMITTED IMPACTS ARE EFFECTIVELY AND PERMANENTLY REPLACED AND ALL PROJECTS ARE SUSTAINABLE OVER THE LONG TERM.

TO SUPPORT THIS GOAL, ELI WILL: ASSEMBLE AND WORK WITH AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE TO PROVIDE GUIDANCE ON THE WAYS IN WHICH MITIGATION AND RESTORATION PLANS AND PROJECTS ARE IDENTIFYING, DESIGNING WAYS TO AVOID, AND PROVIDING EFFECTIVE TOOLS TO ADAPT TO CLIMATE CHANGE.ACTIVITIES:ELI WILL WORK WITH AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE TO PROVIDE GUIDANCE ON THE WAYS IN WHICH MITIGATION AND RESTORATION PLANS AND PROJECTS ARE IDENTIFYING, DESIGNING WAYS TO AVOID, AND PROVIDING EFFECTIVE TOOLS TO ADAPT TO CLIMATE CHANGE. ELI WILL DESIGN AND HOST 4 - 5 EXPERT TRAINING WEBINARS, CREATE ASSOCIATED RESOURCE MATERIALS, AND RECORD A PODCAST TO DISCUSS KEY THEMES. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF STATES, TRIBES, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO ENSURE ECOLOGICALLY EFFECTIVE AND SUSTAINABLE COMPENSATORY MITIGATION AND RESTORATION PROJECTS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:RESULTS OF ACTIVITIES (OUTPUTS): THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THREE OUTPUTS:
1) 4 -5 EXPERT TRAINING WEBINARS: THE PROJECT PARTNERS WILL DESIGN AND DELIVER 4-5 TRAINING WEBINARS.
2) RESOURCE MATERIALS: ELI WILL DEVELOP RESOURCE MATERIALS TO ACCOMPANY EACH WEBINAR. THE MATERIALS MAY INCLUDE CASE STUDIES, LITERATURE REVIEWS, RESOURCE COMPILATIONS, OR MODEL LANGUAGE FOR BANK OR IN-LIEU FEE PROGRAM INSTRUMENTS OR MITIGATION PLANS.
3) PODCAST: ELI WILL DEVELOP A PODCAST RELATED TO SOME OF THE KEY THEMES IDENTIFIED IN THE WEBINAR SERIES.


ANTICIPATED ENVIRONMENTAL IMPROVEMENTS (OUTCOMES): ELI'S PROJECT WILL RESULT IN (AN):
1) IMPROVED CAPACITY OF STATE AGENCIES SERVING ON IRTS TO ENSURE SUCCESSFUL MITIGATION PROJECTS.
2) INCREASED CAPACITY OF STATE WETLAND RESTORATION PROGRAMS TO INTEGRATE CLIMATE SCIENCE.
3) INCREASED NUMBER OF GUIDANCE DOCUMENTS AND PROCEDURES THAT INCLUDE INFORMATION ON HOW TO EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS CHANGING CONDITIONS - WITH MODELS AND BEST PRACTICES.
4) INCREASED NUMBER OF INSTRUMENTS AND MITIGATION PLANS THAT PROVIDE EFFECTIVE STRATEGIES FOR ADDRESSING CLIMATE CHANGE.
5) INCREASED NUMBER OF SUCCESSFUL MITIGATION PROJECTS.
6) IMPROVED PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF WATERSHEDS AND AQUATIC ECOSYSTEMS.

DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE STATES, TRIBES, THE COMPENSATORY MITIGATION COMMUNITY, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.256: THE PRIMARY OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A GENERAL, SCALABLE APPROACH TOWARDS THE CONSTRUCTION OF CHEMICAL MECHANISMS THAT REPRODUCE THE KEY PROPERTIES AND REACTIVITIES OF ORGANIC COMPOUNDS. THE SPECIFIC FOCUS OF THIS WORK WILL BE A FEW CLASSES OF ORGANIC SPECIES (ALKANES, MONOTERPENES, AND AROMATICS), AND THE STUDY OF THOSE SYSTEMS (E.G., MODEL-MEASUREMENT COMPARISONS, THE DEVELOPMENT OF REDUCED MECHANISMS) IS EXPECTED TO LEAD TO A GREATLY IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR CHEMISTRY.
description.257: THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE BIOCONTAINMENT OF GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MICROBES  (GEMS) IN ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS AND GENERATE A NOVEL GEM KILL SWITCH RELEVANT TO BIOREMEDIATION. CONSISTENT WITH THE STATUTORY AUTHORITIES ABOVE, THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP FUNDAMENTAL SCIENTIFIC SCREENING AND MONITORING TECHNIQUES, AS IN SUBSECTIONS (C) AND (D), TO BETTER UNDERSTAND, ASSESS AND MITIGATE ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS OF WHILE ADVANCING RESEARCH ON THE RELIABILITY OF SUCH TECHNIQUES, AND IMPROVEMENTS ON MONITORING OF GEMS, PARTICULARLY FOR BROADLY USED BIOREMEDIATION APPLICATIONS.
description.258: THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO UNDERSTAND, PREDICT, AND CONTROL THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN NATURAL SOIL MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES (SMCS) AND GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MICROBES (GEMS). SPECIFICALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL APPLY CURRENT UNDERSTANDING OF THE COMPOSITION OF NATURAL SMCS TO CREATE LABORATORY MODEL SMCS TO MEASURE THE SURVIVAL AND PERSISTENCE OF GEMS. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT WILL ASSESS THE CAPACITY OF DOMINANT SMC PHYLOTYPES TO CONTROL THE SURVIVAL AND PERSISTENCE OF GEMS.
description.259: THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO CONDUCT FIELD AND LABORATORY RESEARCH TO ENABLE ACCURATE MODELING OF INTERVENTIONS INTENDED TO REDUCE INDOOR WOODSMOKE EXPOSURES. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF OUTDOOR TO INDOOR AIR POLLUTANT TRANSPORT IN SINGLE-FAMILY DETACHED HOMESAND EVALUATE COMMERCIAL AND LOW-COST AIR-CLEANING APPROACHES FOR PARTICLE AND GAS-PHASE POLLUTANTSAND CHARACTERIZE POLYCYCLIC AROMATIC HYDROCARBONS (PAHS) ON INDOOR SURFACES TO ELUCIDATE HOW INDOOR WOODSMOKE MAY CAUSE LONG-TERM EXPOSURE TO PAHS INDOORS.
description.260: THE PURPOSE OF THIS STUDY IS TO IDENTIFY DECENTRALIZED WASTEWATER TECHNOLOGIES AND MUNICIPAL TREATMENT UNIT PROCESSES CAPABLE OF REMOVING HUMAN ENTERIC VIRUSES TO ALLOW SAFE REUSE OF THE TREATED WASTEWATER AND TO EVALUATE THE USE OF FIVE SURROGATES AS POSSIBLE INDICATORS FOR PRESENCE OF HUMAN ENTERIC VIRUSES DURING TREATMENT PROCESSES. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE USING TWO CULTURABLE AND THREE NON-CULTURABLE SURROGATE INDICATORS FOR HUMAN ENTERIC VIRUSES TO EVALUATE EACH TECHNOLOGY&RSQUOANDS PERFORMANCE AND TO CONCURRENTLY VALIDATE THE USE OF THESE SURROGATES BY PARALLEL MEASUREMENTS OF INDIGENOUS HUMAN ADENOVIRUSES AND HUMAN NOROVIRUSES USING STATE-OF-THE-ART ANALYTICAL METHODS. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A RATING OF EIGHT WASTEWATER TREATMENT PROCESSES WITH RESPECT TO REMOVALS/INACTIVATION OF HUMAN ENTERIC VIRUSES, AND DATA WITH THE OUTCOME OF ULTIMATELY INFORMING POLICIES AND GUIDELINES RELATIVE TO TESTING OF WASTEWATER TREATMENT TECHNOLOGIES BEING CONSIDERED FOR REUSE OF TREATED WASTEWATER. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE WASTEWATER OPERATORS, STATE AND LOCAL REGULATORS, RESIDENTS OF BARNSTABLE COUNTY, MA, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.261:
DESCRIPTION:THE FOCUS OF THIS PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO STUDY WILLINGNESS TO PAY (WTP) FOR WATER QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS IN MIDWESTERN RESERVOIRS. RESEARCHERS WILL BE MEASURING LINKAGES BETWEEN WATER QUALITY AND PROVISION OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES TO INFORM POTENTIAL SCENARIOS AND ECOSYSTEM ATTRIBUTES. WTP WILL BE MEASURED BY INCORPORATING CHOICE EXPERIMENTS TO DETERMINE IMPACTS OF WATER QUALITY RESTORATION ALONG WITH SCENARIOS AND ACCOUNTING FOR ECOSYSTEM SERVICES BUNDLING. LASTLY, RESEARCH WILL EVALUATE DEMOGRAPHIC AND SPATIAL CHARACTERISTICS THAT MAY INFORM THE EXTENT TO WHICH WATER QUALITY CHANGES IMPACT WTP.ACTIVITIES:NON-MARKET VALUATION TECHNIQUES WILL BE USED TO CHARACTERIZE THE MARKET EXTENT. THE GRANTEE WILL ALSO INCORPORATE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES MODELING TO INFORM PLAUSIBLE SCENARIOS AND ECOSYSTEM ATTRIBUTES IN VALUATION QUESTIONNAIRES. FINALLY, THE GRANTEE WILL INTEGRATE DEMOGRAPHIC, AND SPATIAL CHARACTERISTICS THAT MAY INFORM THE EXTENT TO WHICH WATER QUALITY CHANGES IMPACT WTP.SUBRECIPIENT:SUBAWARD TO KANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY. 
CO-PIS DR. TRISHA MOORE AND DR. ALEKSEY SHESHUKOV WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR CREATION, CALIBRATION AND VALIDATION, AND GENERATION OF SCENARIOS AND RESULTS FOR A COUPLED WATERSHED HYDROLOGY-RESERVOIR EUTROPHICATION MODEL. THE MODEL FRAMEWORK DEVELOPED BY MOORE AND SHESHUKOV WILL BE APPLIED TO UP TO 3 STUDY RESERVOIRS.  OUTCOMES:THE EXPECTED OUTCOME WILL BE TO FORECAST THE REALISTIC FUTURE OF MIDWEST RESERVOIRS. THIS INCLUDES PUBLICATIONS DESCRIBING RESEARCH RESULTS AND WILLINGNESS TO PAY ESTIMATES FOR WATER QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. IN ADDITION, SWAT-BATHTUB MODELS FOR THREE RESERVOIRS AND THEIR RESPECTIVE WATERSHED AREAS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THE PUBLIC, STATE AND LOCAL REGULATORS, WATER QUALITY PROGRAM MANAGERS, AND COMMUNITIES LOCATED CLOSE TO THE RESERVOIRS TO BE STUDIED.
description.262: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO BUILD COMMUNITY-LEVEL RESILIENCE AGAINST INCREASED AIR AND WATER POLLUTION DUE TO CLIMATE CHANGES IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN THE MYSTIC RIVER WATERSHED. ACTIVITIES:: THE PROJECT WILL 1) USE A NOVEL MULTI-STRESSOR HEALTH IMPACT ASSESSMENT (HIA) FRAMEWORK TO ENCODE COMMUNITY INSIGHTS INTO A HIGH-RESOLUTION GEOSPATIAL DATABASE CHARACTERIZING CHEMICAL EXPOSURES, VULNERABILITY, AND GEOGRAPHIC/SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC CO-OCCURRENCE OF HAZARDS; 2) DEVELOP IMPACT MODELS TO HIGHLIGHT LOCATIONS PRONE TO CUMULATIVE CLIMATE RISKS AND CHEMICAL EXPOSURES; 3) USE MULTI-STRESSOR EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSES TO EVALUATE CONJOINT OR CASCADING HAZARDS TO VULNERABLE PEOPLE AND NEIGHBORHOODS; AND 4) APPLY THE RESEARCH FINDINGS TO REFINE HEALTH RISKS AND TO INFORM STATE AND LOCAL POLICIES AND INVESTMENTS TO PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT. SUBRECIPIENT:MYSTIC RIVER WATERSHED ASSOCIATION (MYRWA, $180,000) WILL PARTNER WITH BU TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT SURVEY INSTRUMENTS IN THE COMMUNITY, CONVENE MEETINGS OF EXTERNAL STAKEHOLDERS TO ASSESS COMMUNITY PREFERENCES, PROVIDE CONTACT WITH LOCAL DECISION MAKERS TO FACILITATE SOLUTIONS-ORIENTED WORK, AND ENGAGE WITH ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEMBERS TO SOLICIT FEEDBACK ON GRANT PROGRESS.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS AND SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS. OUTPUTS INCLUDE A HIGH-RESOLUTION GEOSPATIAL DATABASE AND MAPPING TOOL THAT IS READILY RESPONSIVE TO COMMUNITY INTERESTS AND CONCERNS. THE TOOL WILL BE USED BY PUBLIC HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND COMMUNITY PLANNERS TO PRIORITIZE OPERATIONAL AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS NEEDED TO PREVENT AND DECREASE CHEMICAL EXPOSURES AND IMPROVE CLIMATE RESILIENCE AMONG VULNERABLE PEOPLE AND NEIGHBORHOODS OVER TIME. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED HUMAN HEALTH OF THE RESIDENTS IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN THE MYSTIC RIVER WATERSHED. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE COMMUNITIES IN THE MYSTIC RIVER WATERSHED AS WELL AS OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE NATION, AS WELL AS PUBLIC HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND STATE AND LOCAL RESOURCE MANAGERS.
description.263: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ASSESS THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN DIVERSE CLIMATE-INDUCED CONCERNS RELATED TO WATER INFRASTRUCTURE AND WATER QUALITY AND THEIR EFFECTS ON HEALTH IN ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT AIMS TO BUILD CAPACITY AGAINST CLIMATE CHANGE RISKS BY ADDRESSING WATER INFRASTRUCTURE ISSUES IN ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES.ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL 1) CONDUCT COMMUNITY-BASED MONITORING (CBM) AND DIRECT SAMPLING TO ASSESS WATER QUALITY; 2) GATHER SURVEYS AND INTERVIEWS AND PHOTOVOICE SUBMISSIONS TO CAPTURE WATER INSECURITY AND LOCAL VULNERABILITIES; 3) ASSESS THE CUMULATIVE EFFECTS OF WATER QUALITY, WATER INSECURITY, AND LOCAL VULNERABILITIES ON HEALTH, MENTAL HEALTH AND NON-WESTERN PERSPECTIVE OF HEALTH USING STATISTICAL ANALYSES AND FUZZY-SET QUALITATIVE COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS; AND 4) BUILD RESILIENT WATER INFRASTRUCTURE CAPACITY.SUBRECIPIENT:UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS ($303,681) WILL IDENTIFY TECHNOLOGY AND TECHNIQUES FOR REDUCING CLIMATE-BASED RISKS TO WATER INFRASTRUCTURE IDENTIFIED IN TASK 1.1. WATER INFRASTRUCTURE AND TASK 3.1 BUILD ADAPTIVE CAPACITY OF WATER INFRASTRUCTURE.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS AS WELL AS (1) HYDRAULIC MODELS OF THE WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM AND OPEN-SOURCE DATA-DRIVEN ALGORITHMS AND CODES FOR LEAK DETECTION AND LOCALIZATION, (2) MAPS OF THE MOST VULNERABLE HOUSEHOLDS AT RISK OF WATER QUALITY AND INSECURITY, AND (3) COMPREHENSIVE MODELS SHOWING THE FACTORS THAT ARE THE MOST SIGNIFICANT IN DETERMINING HEALTH, MENTAL HEALTH AND NON-WESTERN HEALTH OUTCOMES. EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE RESILIENT WATER INFRASTRUCTURES AND IMPROVED HEALTH IN ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE TRIBAL COMMUNITIES, AS WELL AS STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, IN ALASKA.
description.264:
DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY AND EXPAND COMMUNITY WATER AND SOIL TESTING PROGRAMS BY INTEGRATING HISTORICAL DATA WITH LOCAL KNOWLEDGE AND THE COMMUNITY GOALS AND ASSETS, AND FACILITATE DECISION-MAKING FOR TARGETING FUTURE WORK, INCLUDING COMMUNITY VISIONING FOR STORM WATER MANAGEMENT IN THE FACE OF CLIMATE CHANGE. ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL BUILD CAPACITY WITHIN THE UNDERSERVED TRIBAL COMMUNITIES IN DUWAMISH VALLEY SO THEY MAY HAVE OWNERSHIP OVER ENVIRONMENTAL TESTING AND CLEANUP PROCESS THAT TRULY SUPPORT COMMUNITY NEEDS,. THE PROJECT WILL 1) ENSURE THAT THE PROJECT WILL MEET THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITIES BY THOROUGH SURVEYS, INTERVIEWS, AND SHARING OF PREVIOUSLY COLLECTED DATA; 2) DETERMINE THE EXTENT AND DEGREE OF CONTAMINATION AT THE SITE AS WELL AS THE RESEARCH GUIDANCE AND REPORTS THAT WILL BE MOST USEFUL TO COMMUNITY LEADERS; 3) MONITOR SOIL, WATER, AND SEDIMENT CONTAMINANTS (PAH, PCB, METALS, DIOXIN/FURANS) THROUGHOUT THE WATERSHED DURING STORM WATER SURGES TO IDENTIFY AND MAP HIGH-RISK AREAS; AND 4) INFORM COMMUNITIES OF VIABLE SOLUTIONS TO BUILD RESILIENCE AND CAPACITY AGAINST MIGRATION OF WATER CONTAMINANTS. SUBRECIPIENT:DUWAMISH RIVER CLEANUP COALITION ($32,000) WILL CONVENE COMMUNITY SCIENCE WORKSHOPS AND ENSURE THE COMMUNITY NEEDS ARE PRIORITIZED AND CENTERED.

ENVIRONMENTAL COALITION OF SOUTH SEATTLE (ECOSS) ($15,000) - AS A COMMUNITY BASED ORGANIZATION, THEY WILL ASSIST IN CONVENING COMMUNITY SCIENCE WORKSHOPS THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS AS WELL AS DATABASE AND PUBLICATIONS FOR MAKING SOUND EVIDENCE-BASED DECISIONS ON MITIGATING WATER CONTAMINANTS EXACERBATED BY CLIMATE CHANGE. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED HEALTH FOR THE TRIBAL COMMUNITIES AND RESIDENTS IN DUWAMISH VALLEY. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE COMMUNITY DECISION MAKERS, PUBLIC HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, ENVIRONMENTAL CLEANUP MANAGERS, COMMUNITY PLANNERS, AND TRIBAL LEADERS IN THE DUWAMISH VALLEY AND OTHER SIMILAR COMMUNITIES.
description.265:
DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW SOCIAL AND INSTITUTIONAL FACTORS DRIVE INDIVIDUAL AND HOUSEHOLD ELECTRIFICATION DECISIONS IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES AND HOW THESE FACTORS AFFECT ENVIRONMENTAL CO-BENEFITS OF ENERGY-EFFICIENT ELECTRIFICATION.ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL USE COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH (CBPR) APPROACH AND INTEGRATE ETHNOGRAPHIC AND BEHAVIORAL ECONOMIC METHODS WITH ENGINEERING ANALYSIS AND AIR QUALITY TESTING TO: 1) TO UNDERSTAND HOW LOW- AND MODERATE-INCOME (LMI) HOUSEHOLDS AND NEIGHBORHOODS IN AN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COMMUNITY EXPERIENCE AND ENVISION THE 21ST CENTURY ENERGY TRANSITION AND IDENTIFY COMMUNITY PRIORITIES; 2) DEVELOP A ROBUST COMMUNITY-BASED RESEARCH PLATFORM FOR DESIGNING SCALABLE SOLUTIONS TO THE CHALLENGE OF ENERGY-EFFICIENT ELECTRIFICATION OF AGING HOUSING INFRASTRUCTURE; AND 3) WORK WITH LOCAL HOUSING PARTNERS TO IMPLEMENT AND TEST COMMUNITY CO-DESIGNED INTERVENTIONS AND PROTOTYPES TO ASSESS THEIR EFFICACY IN ADDRESSING HOUSEHOLD PRIORITIES, INCLUDING INDOOR AIR QUALITY, COMFORT, AND COST. SUBRECIPIENT:SUBAWARDEE NORTHEASTERN UNIVERSITY WILL OVERSEE THE CO-DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A SERIES OF PARTICIPATORY CAUSAL LOOP DIAGRAMMING (CLD) WORKSHOPS TO INFORM AND FACILITATE STAKEHOLDER-LED INPUT TO IDENTIFY BARRIERS TO JUST ENERGY TRANSITION TOWARDS DECARBONIZATION, TRAIN FACILITATORS FOR THE WORKSHOPS, CO-DESIGN AND SUPERVISE THE EXECUTION OF PARTICIPATORY CLD SESSIONS TO DRAW A SYSTEMS REPRESENTATION OF THE CURRENT ENERGY SYSTEMS; AND CO-DESIGN AND SUPERVISE DEBRIEFING SESSIONS TO IDENTIFY BARRIERS TO JUST TRANSITIONS AND IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES FOR INTERVENTION. THE REQUESTED AMOUNT IS $50,314.

SUBAWARDEE NEIGHBOR TO NEIGHBOR WILL DO RESIDENT RECRUITMENT, HOST GROUP SESSIONS, AND ASSIST IN PLANNING WORKSHOPS, MEETINGS AND
A COMMUNITY FORUM. THE REQUESTED AMOUNT IS $199,720.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS, AS WELL AS CO-DESIGNED SCALABLE, ADAPTABLE SOLUTIONS FOR HOUSEHOLD ELECTRIFICATION. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED KNOWLEDGE REGARDING THE DRIVERS, BARRIERS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CO-BENEFITS OF HOUSEHOLD ELECTRIFICATION IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE LOW- AND MODERATE-INCOME (LMI) HOUSEHOLDS IN MASSACHUSETTS, AS WELL AS RESEARCHERS WORKING WITH SIMILAR COMMUNITIES TO STUDY DRIVERS AND IMPACTS OF HOUSEHOLD ELECTRIFICATION.
description.266: THIS PROJECT WILL ELUCIDATE DETERMINANTS OF INDOOR DUST INGESTION IN 6- TO 24-MONTH-OLD INFANTS. RESEARCHERS WILL TEST IF THE FREQUENCY AND CHARACTERISTICS OF INDOOR DUST AND NON-DUST MOUTHING EVENTS CHANGE WITH AGE AND MOTOR DEVELOPMENT STAGE FOR DIFFERENT MICRO-ENVIRONMENTS, AND HOW HOME CHARACTERISTICS AND DEMOGRAPHIC FACTORS AFFECT INDOOR DUST MASS LOADING AND DUST TOXICANT CONCENTRATION. THE PROJECT ALSO EXAMINES HOW DUST TRANSFER IS INFLUENCED BY DUST PROPERTIES, SURFACE FEATURES, AND CONTACT DYNAMICS; AND CONTRIBUTIONS OF DEVELOPMENTAL, BEHAVIORAL, AND SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS TO DUST AND TOXICANT-RESOLVED DUST INGESTION RATES.
description.267: DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A MORE EFFECTIVE AND SUSTAINABLE METHOD FOR DETECTION AND REMOVAL OF GENX FROM WATER.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES PERFORMED WILL ADDRESS DECREASED SENSITIVITY OF GENX DETECTION DUE TO BACKGROUND LEVELS IN SAMPLE BLANKS AND EFFECTIVE DISPOSAL OF WASTE PRODUCED BY THE CLEANSING OF ANION EXCHANGE RESINS USED IN THE REMOVAL OF GENX AT WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANTS. THE RECIPIENT WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: 1) TREAT WATER USED IN LC-MS/MS BLANK SAMPLES USING PHOTOCATALYTIC DEGRADATION TO REMOVE ANY BACKGROUND CONTAMINANTS THAT WOULD DECREASE INSTRUMENT SENSITIVITY; 2) TREAT THE WASTE PRODUCT OBTAINED FROM CLEANSING OF ANION EXCHANGE RESINS USING PHOTOCATALYTIC DEGRADATION; AND 3) ASSESS THE SUCCESS OF REMOVAL USING LC-MS/MS TO DETECT CHANGES IN LEVELS OF GENX PRE- AND POST-TREATMENT FOR BOTH THE BLANK SAMPLES AND WASTE PRODUCTS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE A FINAL REPORT DOCUMENTING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF PHOTOCATALYTIC DEGRADATION TREATMENT IN REDUCING LEVELS OF GENX IN BLANK SAMPLES AND WASTE PRODUCTS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT OPERATORS, RESEARCHERS, CONTAMINATED SITE MANAGERS, HUMAN HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.268: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO OPTIMIZE AND TEST THE BIOFILTRATION MODULE IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISMS CONTROLLING THE ENHANCED NUTRIENT REMOVAL IN RUNOFF FROM URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL WATERSHEDS. ACTIVITIES:THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1) OPTIMIZE THE BIOFILTER MEDIA TOPOLOGY WITH MULTIPLE OBJECTIVES (E.G., MAX SSA AND VOID RATIO); 2) CHARACTERIZE THE MICROBIAL BIOFILM; AND 3) DEPLOY THE OPTIMIZED BIOFILTERS IN SITU IN SMALL-SCALED WATERSHEDS. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS. THE POTENTIAL OUTCOMES INCLUDE A SET OF ULTRA-HIGH SURFACE AREA DESIGNS, A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIOFILM STRUCTURE, AN INCREASED CAPACITY OF STORMWATER TREATMENT SYSTEMS, AND A SET OF SUSTAINABILITY GUIDELINES FOR ADVANCED MEDIA DESIGNS BASED ON LIFE CYCLE ASSESSMENT. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE RURAL MUNICIPALITIES, COMMUNITIES, AND INDIVIDUALS IN AREAS AFFECTED BY PER- AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES CONTAMINATION, HUMAN HEALTH, THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.269: DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A COST-EFFECTIVE METHOD TO DEGRADE HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS (HABS) SUCH AS MICROCYSTIN LEUCINE ARGININE (MC-LR) IN RECREATIONAL AND DRINKING WATER SOURCES.ACTIVITIES:RESEARCHERS WILL USE AN INNOVATIVE GOLD (AU)-DECORATED METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK (MOF) WHERE THE GOLD NANOPARTICLES PROVIDE THE SOLAR FUNCTION FOR THE PHOTOCATALYST. THE PROJECT'S THREE RESEARCH OBJECTIVES ARE: 1) DESIGN AND FABRICATE AN AU-DECORATED NI-MOF; 2) CHARACTERIZE AND EVALUATE OPTIMAL PARAMETER CONDITIONS; AND 3) CONDUCT A LIFE CYCLE ANALYSIS FOR MC-LR REMOVAL.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS ON THEIR EFFORT TO DESIGN AND FABRICATE A GOLD DECORATED PHOTOCATALYST (AU/NI MOF) FOR ITS ABILITY TO ADVANCE SUSTAINABLE WATER TREATMENT METHODS FOR THE REMOVAL OF MC-LR, WHILE ELIMINATING THE NEED FOR CHEMICAL AND POST-TREATMENT ASSOCIATED WITH CONVENTIONAL TREATMENT METHODS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE SOURCE AND DRINKING WATER MANAGERS AND COMMUNITIES THAT EXPERIENCE MC-LR BLOOMS.
description.270: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EVALUATE THE ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE OF SECOND-GENERATION BIOFUELS PRODUCED VIA HYDROTHERMAL LIQUEFACTION (HTL) CONVERSION OF FOOD WASTE USING A RANGE OF EXPERIMENTAL METHODS AND LIFE-CYCLE AND COST ASSESSMENT TECHNIQUES. ACTIVITIES:THE OBJECTIVES OF THE PROJECT ARE TO: (1) CHARACTERIZE AND OPTIMIZE FOOD WASTE FEEDSTOCKS AND THEIR CORRESPONDING POST-HTL PRODUCTS (I.E., BIOCRUDE, BIOCHAR, AND AQUEOUS CO-PRODUCT (ACP)) AND (2) PERFORM LIFE-CYCLE ASSESSMENT (LCA) AND LIFE-CYCLE COST (LCC) ASSESSMENT OF HYPOTHETICAL REGIONAL COLLECTION AND CONVERSION SYSTEMS FOR BIOCRUDE AND POST-HTL PRODUCTS RECOVERED FROM FOOD WASTE STREAMS. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ASSESS FEASIBILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY OF WASTE-TO-ENERGY SYSTEMS VIA HTL CONVERSION AND DISSEMINATE FINDINGS FROM A FULL-SCALE LCA AND LCC ASSESSMENT MODEL. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE FOOD WASTE STREAMS, THE RENEWABLE ENERGY SECTOR, THE ENVIRONMENT, HUMAN HEALTH, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.271: THIS PROJECT WILL DETERMINE THE METABOLIC ACTIVITIES OF KEY XENOBIOTIC-METABOLIZING ENZYMES IN TRANSGENIC KNOCKOUT ZEBRAFISH, OFTEN USED IN TOXICITY ASSESSMENTS. PARENT AND PRIMARY METABOLITE PROFILES FOR TOP HIT COMPOUNDS WILL BE DETERMINED, AND MORE DETAILED KINETIC ASSAYS WILL BE PERFORMED ON THEM. A NOVEL MULTIPLEXED MULTIDIMENSIONAL GCXGC-MS IDENTIFICATION WILL CHARACTERIZE THE METABOLITE PROFILES FOR SELECTED INDIVIDUAL COMPOUNDS, AND WILL BE USABLE FOR OTHERS.
