description.923: DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ELUCIDATE THE POLICY-MAKING PROCESS TO MITIGATE ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES AND ELEVATE RESIDENT VOICES TO ADDRESS LEGACY POLLUTANTS AND ONGOING CONTAMINANTS THAT RESULT IN NEGATIVE HEALTH OUTCOMES.ACTIVITIES:THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: (1) DEVELOP MODELS OF THE CUMULATIVE HEALTH BURDEN EXPERIENCED BY MARGINALIZED COMMUNITIES TO ADDRESS WHETHER THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN CUMULATIVE SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES AND HEALTH OUTCOMES ARE CONSISTENT ACROSS COMMUNITIES AND DISEASES ALONG COLORADO'S FRONT RANGE AND (2) FACILITATE ROUNDTABLES WHERE RESIDENTS HAVE A DELIBERATE AND MEANINGFUL OPPORTUNITY TO ENGAGE THE STATE AND LOCAL POLICY-MAKING PROCESS REGARDING ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES, PROMOTE THEIR CONCERNS, AND DEVELOP SOLUTIONS IN CONCERT WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE AGENCIES.SUBRECIPIENT:THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS WILL RECEIVE A SUBAWARD FOR $347,608. THEY WILL PROVIDE DATA AND ANALYSIS SUPPORT FOR BOTH THE HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURE DATA ALONG WITH PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR DEVELOPMENT OF PRESENTATIONS AND MANUSCRIPTS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS RESEARCH.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS. A FRAMEWORK WILL BE DEVELOPED THAT WILL ASSESS THE CUMULATIVE BURDEN ATTRIBUTABLE TO MULTIPLE SIMULTANEOUS CHEMICAL AND NON-CHEMICAL STRESSORS IN COLORADO AND TO CREATE SUSTAINABILITY IN THE COMMERCE CITY-NORTH DENVER NEIGHBORHOODS THROUGH MEANINGFUL OPPORTUNITIES FOR ENGAGEMENT, ADVOCACY, AND LEADERSHIP OF RESIDENTS; ELEVATION OF HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES IN STATE AND LOCAL POLICY AND DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE RESIDENTS OF THE COMMERCE CITY-NORTH DENVER NEIGHBORHOODS, HUMAN HEALTH, THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.924:
DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO BUILDING MATERIALS RE-USE ASSOCIATION. THIS PROGRAM IS TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT, ENHANCED STANDARDIZATION AND TRANSPARENCY, AND REPORTING CRITERIA FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCT DECLARATIONS (EPDS) WHICH INCLUDE THE MEASUREMENT OF EMBODIED GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ALL RELEVANT STAGES OF PRODUCTION, USE, AND DISPOSAL, IN CONFORMANCE WITH INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS. THE RECIPIENT WILL DEVELOP A DIGITAL LCA-EPD GENERATOR SOFTWARE TOOL, ENHANCE ITS CAPABILITIES AS A PROGRAM OPERATOR AND CREATE A SUB-CATEGORY PCR FOR SALVAGED AND REPROCESSED CONSTRUCTION PRODUCTS. THE PROJECT WILL GENERATE DATA ON 'AVERAGE' USE, QUALITY, SERVICE LIFESPANS, PAST USES AND END-OF-LIFE IN KEY PRODUCT GROUP CATEGORIES FOR USE IN PRODUCT CIRCULARITY ACTIVITIES SUCH AS DESIGN FOR REUSE AND MATERIALS PASSPORT DEVELOPMENT. ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CAPACITY BUILDING AND EDUCATION SUCH AS OPENLCA SOFTWARE TRAINING, SEATING MEMBERS OF A TECHNICAL COMMITTEE FOR QUALITY ASSISTANCE AND GOVERNANCE AS A PROGRAM OPERATOR. ACTIVITIES ALSO INCLUDE DEVELOPING A PCR FOR SALVAGE AND REUSE CONSTRUCTION PRODUCTS; A DIGITAL LCA-EPD GENERATOR; AND ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCT DECLARATIONS (APPROX 300) FROM 100 DIFFERENT SALVAGE AND REUSE ESTABLISHMENTS.SUBRECIPIENT:BUILD REUSE WILL PROVIDE A SUBAWARD FOR USDA FOREST PRODUCTS LABORATORY FOR PEER REVIEWS AND PUBLICATIONS.OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES FOR TASK 1. CAPACITY BUILDING AND EDUCATION INCLUDE HOSTING A TWO-DAY WORKSHOP AND SESSIONS AT ANNUAL CONFERENCES DEDICATED TO LCA, EPDS AND CARBON LABELING; TRAINING FOR OPENLCA SOFTWARE FOR STAFF; DECLARE AND PUBLISH PROGRAM OPERATOR STATUS AND INFORMATION ON WEBSITE; AND PROPOSED PRESENTATION AND PAPER AT ANNUAL ACLCA CONFERENCE. 

THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES FOR TASK 2. PCR FOR SALVAGE AND REUSE CONSTRUCTION PRODUCTS INCLUDE AN RFP FOR PO PCR SPECIFICATION; CONTRACTING A PO FOR PCR COMMITTEE; SOLICITING AND CONTRACTING AN EXPERT REVIEW PANEL; AND CONDUCTING PCR DEVELOPMENT.

THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES FOR TASK 3. DIGITAL LCA-EPD GENERATOR DEVELOPMENT INCLUDE OPEN EXCEL-BASED DIGITAL LCI DATA COLLECTION TEMPLATES; SOFTWARE DESIGN; DIGITAL GENERATOR TESTING/REFINEMENT; AND INSTRUCTIONAL GUIDANCE FOR GENERATOR. 

THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES FOR TASK 4. EPD DEVELOPMENT INCLUDE EPD PROGRAM WEBINARS; ESTABLISHING SOLICITATION AND PROGRAM GUIDELINES; DEVELOPING LCA MODELS FOR PRINCIPAL SALVAGE AND REUSE PROCESSES; CONDUCTING LCI DATA COLLECTION PROCESSES IN PARTNERSHIP FACILITIES; THIRD-PARTY VERIFICATION OF EPDS; AND PUBLICATION OF EPDS.

THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE OPENLCA TRAINED STAFF; DEDICATED LCA-EPD SESSION AT EACH ANNUAL CONFERENCE FOR PURPOSES OF CROSS-GRANT COORDINATION; ONE OR MORE ONLINE EDUCATION PRODUCTS; ONE REPORT AND ROADMAP DOCUMENTING WORKSHOP AND REPORTING; FIVE PAPERS/PRESENTATIONS TO NATIONAL ACLCA CONFERENCE; DEVELOPMENT OF ONE CORE PCR; AN EPD GENERATOR TOOL; AND APPROXIMATELY 300 EPDS.

THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE ARCHITECTURE, ENGINEERING, AND CONSTRUCTION PROFESSIONALS, LCA PRACTITIONERS, ACADEMIA, AND MATERIAL MANUFACTURERS AND SUPPLIERS.

description.926: THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF PFC'S BFRDP PROJECT IS TO EMPOWER REFUGEE, IMMIGRANT, AND BLACK BEGINNING FARMERS WITH NEEDED RESOURCES, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND OPPORTUNITIES TO ENTER AND CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVE THEIR SUCCESSES IN FARMING BY REFINING PFC'S BEGINNING FARMER TRAINING INITIATIVES IN COLLABORATION WITH CORNELL PARTNERS. ACCORDING TO FEEDBACK AND A SURVEY, THE MOST COMMON METHODS FOR EFFECTIVE LEARNING IDENTIFIED BY REFUGEE, IMMIGRANT, AND BLACK BEGINNING FARMERS ARE PERSONALIZED, HANDS-ON, AND LANGUAGE-ADAPTIVE DEMONSTRATION IN THE FIELD AND TEACHING IN THE CLASSROOM, PLUS THE USE OF VISUAL RESOURCES. FARMERS EXPRESSED NEEDING TO LEARN ABOUT LIVESTOCK AND CROP FARMING PLUS FARM BUSINESS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT. THESE FARMERS PRIORITIZE BUILDING INTER- AND INTRA-COMMUNITY RELATIONSHIPS PLUS EARNING INCOME THROUGH FARMING. INCLUDED IN THEIR DEFINITIONS OF SUCCESS FOR THEIR FARMS ARE BEING ABLE TO FEED THEIR COMMUNITIES AND CONNECT WITH THEIR CULTURE. THUS, OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVESARE TO A) INCREASE PFC STAFF KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY SO STAFF CAN BETTER MEET THE EXPRESSED LEARNING NEEDS OF REFUGEE, IMMIGRANT, AND BLACK FARMERS AND B) EMPOWER SUCH FARMERS TO ENTER OR IMPROVE THEIR SUCCESSES IN FARMING THROUGH ACCESS TO LAND, PERSONALIZED EDUCATION, AND MARKET OPPORTUNITIES WHILE BUILDING COMMUNITY, NOURISHING THEIR COMMUNITIES, AND CONNECTING WITH THEIR CULTURE.TO ACCOMPLISH ITS LONG-TERM GOAL, THE PROJECT WILL EMPLOY METHODS IN WHICH FARMERS ARE SUPPORTED IN CREATING ANNUAL INDIVIDUALIZED EDUCATION PLANS AND PARTNERS AT CORNELL TRAIN PFC STAFF ON TOPIC BASICS. THROUGH FARMERS' EDUCATION PLANS AND INCREASED STAFF KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY, PFC STAFF WILL BETTER PROVIDE BASIC PERSONALIZED EDUCATION AND MENTORSHIP TO FARMERS THAT IS HANDS-ON, LANGUAGE-ADAPTED, AND ONE-ON-ONE OR SMALL-GROUP. PARTNERS WILL LIKEWISE REFERENCE FARMERS' EDUCATION PLANS TO DELIVER ADVANCED INSTRUCTION AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AS WELL AS SUPPORT CURRICULA REFINEMENT AND PRODUCTION OFVISUAL LEARNING MATERIALS. PFC FARMLAND AND RELATIONSHIPS WITH MARKETS SERVING LOW-INCOME, LOW-ACCESS COMMUNITIES WILL BE LEVERAGED THROUGHOUT THE PROGRAM. IN TOTAL, 200 UNDER-RESOURCED FARMERS WILL BE SERVED AND FOUR STAFF MEMBERS WILL BE TRAINED.
description.927: DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP NEW MODELS, METHODS, AND SOFTWARE TOOLS FOR DISCOVERING AND DESIGNING NOVEL REACTION NETWORKS AND PROCESSES THAT ARE ESSENTIAL FOR TRANSFORMING THE US CHEMICALS INDUSTRY TOWARD GREATER SUSTAINABILITY AND CIRCULARITY.ACTIVITIES:SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING, I) AN OPEN-ACCESS MODEL OF THE CURRENT US CHEMICALS INDUSTRY, II) INNOVATIVE METHODS FOR DISCOVERING NOVEL CIRCULAR CHEMICAL REACTION NETWORKS, III) APPROACHES FOR ENGAGING WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND QUANTIFYING  IMPACTS OF CURRENT AND PROSPECTIVE CHEMICAL INDUSTRIES AT SPECIFIC LOCATIONS, IV) A FRAMEWORK FOR EFFICIENTLY GUIDING THE SELECTION AND DESIGN OF BETTER REACTION NETWORKS AND PROCESSES, AND V) APPLICATIONS TO INDUSTRIALLY RELEVANT PRODUCTS SUCH AS METHANOL AND POLYETHYLENE AND USER-FRIENDLY SOFTWARE TOOLS.SUBRECIPIENT:THE SUBAWARD TO UNLIMITED POTENTIAL ($100,000) IS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT EDUCATIONAL PRESENTATIONS, FOCUS GROUPS, AND TRAIN COMMUNITY LEADERS ON ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION.OUTCOMES:ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS WORK INCLUDE A MODEL OF THE U.S. CHEMICALS PRODUCTION AND MANUFACTURING INDUSTRY, NOVEL METHODOLOGY AND FRAMEWORK FOR DEVELOPING REACTION NETWORKS, HIERARCHICAL SCREENING PROCESSES, AND USER-FRIENDLY SOFTWARE TOOLS THAT PROMOTE SUSTAINABILITY AND CIRCULARITY. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THE CHEMICALS MANUFACTURING INDUSTRY, COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURE TO TOXIC CHEMICAL PRODUCTS, THE GENERAL PUBLIC, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH DECISION-MAKERS.
description.928: DESCRIPTION:FUTURE PANDEMICS WILL REQUIRE THAT WASTEWATER SURVEILLANCE FOR POTENTIALLY HARMFUL PATHOGENS SUCH AS SARS-COV-2 (THE VIRUS THAT CAUSES COVID-19) BE DEPLOYED QUICKLY AND EFFECTIVELY AND WITH RESULTS THAT CAN BE APPLIED LOCALLY. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A HIERARCHICAL WASTEWATER SURVEILLANCE SENTINEL SITE IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM FOR DETECTION OF PATHOGENS THAT COULD CAUSE FUTURE PANDEMICS.ACTIVITIES:THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL IDENTIFY WASTEWATER SENTINEL SITES USING DATA-DRIVEN PREDICTIONS OF INFECTION RISK LEVELS AT VARIOUS SPATIAL RESOLUTIONS BASED ON AN INTEGRATED ANALYSIS OF DATA INCLUDING WEATHER, HUMAN MOBILITY, HEALTH CARE, INFRASTRUCTURE, POPULATION DENSITY, SOCIODEMOGRAPHICS, AND DATA FROM THE CURRENT COVID-19 PANDEMIC.SUBRECIPIENT:FUNDS ARE REQUESTED FOR A TOTAL OF $124,902 ($99,996 REQUESTED PLUS $24,906 COST SHARE) FOR A SUBAWARD TO THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA TO DEVELOP A RISK FORECASTING MAP. IN ADDITION, $124,681 ($99,631 REQUESTED PLUS $25,050 COST SHARE) IS REQUESTED FOR A SUBAWARD TO PORTLAND STATE UNIVERSITY TO ANALYZE TRAFFIC NETWORKS AND INCORPORATE THE DATA AND ANALYSIS INTO THE RISK FORECASTING MODEL. IN ADDITION, $70,000 IS BUDGETED FOR A SUBAWARD TO THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF COUNTY AND CITY HEALTH OFFICIALS (NACCHO), TO DEVELOP A STRATEGY TO VERIFY THE SAMPLING METHOD DEVELOPED BY THE GRANTEE AND TO CONTRIBUTE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE COMPUTATIONAL PLATFORM.OUTCOMES:THE RECIPIENT WILL SUBMIT ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS ON THEIR EFFORTS TO DEVELOP A HIERARCHICAL WASTEWATER SENTINEL SITE IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS THAT WASTEWATER SENTINEL SITES WOULD BE IDENTIFIED HIERARCHICALLY FROM THE COUNTY LEVEL, THE CITY/TOWN/VILLAGE LEVEL AND IDEALLY TO BUILDING LEVEL DEPENDING ON PATHOGEN TRANSMISSION CHARACTERISTICS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENTS ACROSS THE U.S., AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.929:
DESCRIPTION:THIS RESEARCH PROJECT AIMS TO FILL EXISTING GAPS IN CUMULATIVE BURDEN ANALYSIS, INCLUDING AIR AND WATER POLLUTION BURDENS, AND TO BETTER INFORM LOCALLY-TAILORED POLICIES AND STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH DISPARITIES IN SELECTED PARTNERING UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN GEORGIA AND NEW MEXICO. ACTIVITIES:THE RESEARCH PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A STATEWIDE CUMULATIVE BURDEN INDEX (CBI) FOR GEORGIA AND NEW MEXICO USING A NOVEL HEALTH IMPACT ANALYSIS METHOD. THE PROJECT WILL THEN INTEGRATE COMMUNITY-DRIVEN PRIORITIES TO DEVELOP LOCAL HIGH-RESOLUTION CBIS FOR BERNALILLO COUNTY, NM AND RICHMOND COUNTY, GA. FINALLY, THE PROJECT WILL APPLY THE ANALYSIS TO CASE STUDY THAT FACILITIES IN EACH COUNTY TO INFORM LOCAL POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS AND IDENTIFY BEST PRACTICES FOR SIMILAR EFFORTS NATIONWIDE.SUBRECIPIENT:UNIVERSITY OF NEW MEXICO ($389,429) - UNM WILL PROVIDE LEGAL AND POLICY ANALYSIS AND SUPPORT ENGAGEMENT WITH COMMUNITY GROUPS AND OVERSEE THE ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES AND QUALITATIVE DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS TASKS, WORKING WITH DR. NUNEZ AND OTHER CO-INVESTIGATORS ON ANALYSES FOR AIM 2.

LOS JARDINES ($389,454) - LOS JARDINES WILL ENGAGE COMMUNITY LEADERS AND HOST GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY WORKSHOPS TO DISSEMINATE RESEARCH AND TO DESCRIBE BROADER RESIDENT'S PERSPECTIVES ON CUMULATIVE BURDENS; CONDUCTING COMMUNITY FOCUS GROUPS; AND HOST PUBLIC CONVENINGS TO VET QUALITATIVE RESEARCH FINDINGS AND SOLIDIFY RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INTEGRATING LOCAL DATA.

GEORGIA WAND ($313,820) - GEORGIA WAND WILL ENGAGE COMMUNITY LEADERS AND HOST GRASSROOTS COMMUNITY WORKSHOPS TO DISSEMINATE RESEARCH AND TO DESCRIBE BROADER RESIDENT'S
PERSPECTIVES ON CUMULATIVE BURDENS; CONDUCTING COMMUNITY FOCUS GROUPS; AND HOST PUBLIC CONVENINGS TO VET QUALITATIVE RESEARCH FINDINGS AND SOLIDIFY RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INTEGRATING LOCAL DATA.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS, PEER REVIEWED JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS, AND SCIENTIFIC REPORTS AS WELL AS EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS AND POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES, ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGERS, HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, AND COMMUNITY PLANNERS AND LEADERS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A REDUCTION OF HARMFUL POLLUTANT EXPOSURES AND A GENERAL IMPROVEMENT IN ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH AMONG RESIDENTS IN THE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN GEORGIA AND NEW MEXICO. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES, ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGERS, HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, COMMUNITY LEADERS, AND VULNERABLE POPULATIONS IN THE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN GEORGIA AND NEW MEXICO.
description.930:
DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT 9 (IRA) TO THE RESEARCH TRIANGLE INSTITUTE (RTI) IN THE AMOUNT OF $7,000,000 AS AUTHORIZED BY CAA 138(B). IN DECEMBER 2023, THE US ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY'S (EPA) OFFICE OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND EXTERNAL CIVIL RIGHTS (OEJECR) SELECTED RESEARCH TRIANGLE INSTITUTE (RTI) TO RECEIVE $100 MILLION FROM THE $3 BILLION APPROPRIATION FROM THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) FOR THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE JUSTICE (ECJ) BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM UNDER CLEAN AIR ACT SECTION 138. 

THIS SELECTION IS A PART OF THE THRIVING COMMUNITIES GRANTMAKER PROGRAM (I.E. 'TCGM' OR 'GRANTMAKER'), WHERE RTI WILL USE $100 MILLION TO 1) MAKE SMALL SUBGRANTS TO ELIGIBLE ENTITIES THROUGH EPA REGIONS 4 - 7 THAT INCLUDE GRASSROOTS NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS AND TRIBAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND 2) PROVIDE ADDITIONAL SUPPORT, COORDINATION, AND OVERSIGHT TO THE SUBGRANTEES, APPLICANTS, AND THE OTHER GRANTMAKERS. AS PART OF THE IRA LEGISLATION, OEJECR ALSO RECEIVED $200 MILLION TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO ELIGIBLE ENTITIES, AS DEFINED IN CAA SECTION 138, RELATED TO ANY GRANTS MADE FROM THE $3 BILLION APPROPRIATION. $20 MILLION OF THIS TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE IS BEING USED TO ESTABLISH AN INTERAGENCY AGREEMENT WITH AMERICORPS TO CREATE THE CLEAN ENVIRONMENT CORPS (CEC) VISTA PROGRAM. OF THIS $20 MILLION, $13 MILLION WILL BE SENT TO AMERICORPS VIA AN INTERAGENCY AGREEMENT AND $7 MILLION WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO RTI AS A NONCOMPETITIVE AWARD ISSUED FOR THE PURPOSE OF SERVING AS THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR FOR ALL THE GRANTMAKERS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES DISCUSSED IN THIS FUNDING RECOMMENDATION WILL PRIMARILY FOCUS ON THOSE COVERED UNDER THE $7 MILLION NONCOMPETITIVE AWARD TO RTI.  
ACTIVITIES:VISTA MEMBERS WITH THE CEC ('CEC VISTA MEMBERS') PROGRAM WILL BE EMBEDDED WITH THE REGIONAL AND NATIONAL GRANTMAKERS TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO COMMUNITIES APPLYING FOR AND RECEIVING FUNDING THROUGH TCGM. THE AMERICORPS - TCGM PARTNERSHIP WILL SUPPORT APPROXIMATELY/UP TO 260 CEC VISTA MEMBERS AND APPROXIMATELY/UP TO 6 CEC VISTA LEADERS OVER A THREE-YEAR PERIOD. MEMBERS OF THE CEC VISTA PROGRAM WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED MEMBERS OF THE AMERICAN CLIMATE CORPS, AN INITIATIVE TO PROVIDE AMERICANS WITH PATHWAYS TO HIGH-QUALITY, GOOD-PAYING CLEAN ENERGY AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE JOBS IN THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS AFTER THEY COMPLETE THEIR YEAR OF SERVICE. 

THE EPA AND AMERICORPS DECIDED THAT ONE NATIONAL GRANTMAKER WILL SERVE AS THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR RESPONSIBLE FOR MANAGING THE ENTIRE CEC PROGRAM ON BEHALF OF ALL THE GRANTMAKERS (BOTH REGIONAL AND NATIONAL). CENTRALIZING THE ADMINISTRATIVE RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE CEC PROGRAM WITH ONE NATIONAL GRANTMAKER, RATHER THAN USING ALL THREE NATIONAL GRANTMAKERS, CREATES ECONOMIES OF SCALE FOR RECRUITMENT AND REPORTING REQUIREMENTS AS WELL AS PROCESS STANDARDIZATION FOR THE ENTIRE PROGRAM. THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR WILL WORK WITH AMERICORPS, THE OTHER GRANTMAKERS, AND ANY PARTNERS TO THE GRANTMAKERS TO IMPLEMENT THE CEC PROGRAM. SECOND, THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR WILL APPLY TO AMERICORPS TO IMPLEMENT A VISTA PROJECT, THEREBY CREATING LESS ADMINISTRATIVE BURDEN FOR AMERICORPS. THIRD, THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR WILL RECRUIT, MANAGE, AND PLACE APPROXIMATELY/UP TO 260 CEC VISTA MEMBERS WITH 11 GRANTMAKERS AND THEIR PARTNERS. LASTLY, THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR WILL IDENTIFY PLACEMENTS FOR CEC VISTA MEMBERS AND ENTER INTO AGREEMENTS WITH GRANTMAKERS AND PARTNERS TO HOST THEM. ONCE THESE PLACEMENTS ARE IDENTIFIED, THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR WILL DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT A RECRUITMENT PROCESS FOR ALL CEC VISTA MEMBERS IN COORDINATION WITH AMERICORPS AND HOSTS. THE INTERMEDIARY SPONSOR WILL ALSO MANAGE THE PROGRAMMATIC, FINANCIAL, AND REPORTING REQUIREMENTS OF THE CEC PROGRAM ON BEHALF OF ALL OTHER HOSTS. 

RTI WILL ENSURE THAT ALL CEC VISTA MEMBERS AND LEADERS WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE RELATED TO GRANTS FUNDED UN
description.931: THIS EDA INVESTMENT SUPPORTS THE CONSTRUCTION OF A SINGLE STORY 5,360SQ.FT. PERFORMANCE AND DANCE BUILDING WITHIN THE TANNERY ARTS CENTER, LOCATED IN THE CITY OF SANTA CRUZ.  THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC HAS TOUCHED ON NEARLY ALL EMPLOYMENT SECTORS IN THE TOURISM INDUSTRY, INCLUDING THE ARTS AND ENTERTAINMENT.  THROUGH THIS PROJECT, THE CITY WILL HELP THE LONG-TERM RECOVERY OF THE ARTS, ENTERTAINMENT, AND RECREATION SECTORS, WHILE ALSO ATTRACTING ADDITIONAL VISITORS TO THE REGION DURING OFF-SEASON TOURISM MONTHS.  THESE AIMS WILL ASSIST IN THE REGION'S RECOVERY AND MAKE IT MORE RESILIENT TO FLUCTUATIONS IN TOURISM, WHICH WILL HELP INCREASE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES, SAVE JOBS, SPUR PRIVATE INVESTMENT, AND ADVANCE ECONOMIC RESILIENCY THROUGHOUT THE REGION.

THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INTEGRATE A COLLECTION OF ADVANCED SURFACE CHEMISTRY, KRAFT PAPER FABRICATION, AND RAPID PROPERTY SCREENING, FOLLOWED BY STANDARD TESTINGS AND PILOT DEMONSTRATION TO PRODUCE MULTIFUNCTIONAL INSULATING KRAFT PAPERS FOR

description.933: THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL DEMONSTRATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF FARM RUNOFF TREATMENT SYSTEMS IN REDUCING NUTRIENT DISCHARGES TO COASTAL WATERWAYS AND PROVIDE A BLUEPRINT FOR SCALING-UP TREATMENT SYSTEMS WITHIN TWO KEY AGRICULTURAL WATERSHEDS OF THE MONTEREY BAY, CA. IN ADDITION, THIS PROJECT WILL EXAMINE THE POTENTIAL LINK BETWEEN AGRICULTURAL NUTRIENT DISCHARGES AND THE GROWTH OF HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS (HABS).
description.934: THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A ROBUST, DATA-DRIVEN MODELING FRAMEWORK THAT WILL ACCURATELY PREDICT THE OUTCOME OF A PRECISION GUIDED SYNTHETIC STERILE INSECT TECHNIQUE (PGSIT) TECHNOLOGY AIMED TO ELIMINATE THE AEDES AEGYPTI MOSQUITO VECTOR RESPONSIBLE FOR DENGUE OUTBREAKS IN THE HAWAII REGION.
description.935: THE PURPOSE OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO STUDY THE EFFECTIVENESS OF SEVERAL METHODS OF SMOKE EXPOSURE REDUCTION. THE RECIPIENT WILL CONDUCT A TWO-YEAR LONGITUDINAL RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL OF 265 SAN FRANCISCO BAY AREA RESIDENTS FROM LOW-INCOME AND NON-ENGLISH SPEAKING COMMUNITIES IN SAN MATEO AND SANTA CLARA COUNTIES. THE PROJECT GOALS ARE TO 1) EVALUATE IF AND HOW MUCH APP-DELIVERED NATIVE LANGUAGE MESSAGING, AIR SEALING, OR PORTABLE HIGH EFFICIENCY PARTICULATE AIR FILTERS CAN EFFECTIVELY REDUCE SMOKE EXPOSURE AND ASSOCIATED HEALTH RISKSAND 2) EVALUATE HOW THE EFFECTIVENESS IS MODERATED BY BEHAVIOR OVER TIMEAND AND 3) EVALUATE HOW AND WHY BEHAVIOR IS AFFECTED BY USE OF THE APP-DELIVERED NATIVE LANGUAGE MESSAGING. THE RESULTS OF THIS STUDY WILL IDENTIFY AFFORDABLE AND ACTIONABLE INTERVENTION STEPS FOR INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES, AND INFORM POLICIES, PROGRAMS AND RISK COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY PARTNERS, LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, AND LOCAL/STATE AGENCIES THAT ARE BEHAVIORALLY REALISTIC FOR THE HARD-TO-REACH COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE. METHODS, RESULTS, AND LESSONS LEARNED FROM THIS PROJECT CAN BE USED TO CONDUCT FUTURE EVALUATIONS OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERVENTIONS FOR WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURE IN OTHER SETTINGS (E.G., MULTI-FAMILY, WORK PLACES) AND AMONG OTHER HARD-TO-REACH POPULATIONS (E.G., RURAL COMMUNITIES, RESERVATIONS) IN CALIFORNIA AND BEYOND. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITYAND STATE AND LOCAL ENTITIES WORKING TO REDUCE WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURESAND AND COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURES. RTI INTERNATIONAL WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL EXPERTISE FOR THE PERSONAL EXPOSURE AND AIR QUALITY ASSESSMENT BY DESIGNING THE EXPOSURE STUDY, TRAINING FIELD STAFF ON AIR SENSOR DEPLOYMENT AND DATA EXTRACTION, ASSESSING THE AIR QUALITY AND EXPOSURES FOR PARTICULATE MATTER, AND ASSESSING SLEEP QUALITY OF A SUB-POPULATION WHO HAS EXISTING HEALTH PROBLEMS.
description.936: DESCRIPTION:THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO ADVANCE THE THEORY AND PRACTICE OF SANITATION JUSTICE (EQUITABLE ACCESS, AGENCY, AND ADAPTIVE CAPACITY FOR SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE) AMIDST INTENSIFYING CLIMATE STRESSORS FOR MARGINALIZED U.S. COMMUNITIES.ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL 1) COMPARE SANITATION-RELATED EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS FOR AN URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITY; 2) PRIORITIZE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE STRESSORS ON SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE AND CONTAMINANT HEALTH IMPACTS IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES; 3) DESIGN AND EVALUATE IMPROVED SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE TO REDUCE EXPOSURE WHILE MAXIMIZING ECONOMIC VIABILITY AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT.SUBRECIPIENT:BAYLOR COLLEGE OF MEDICINE ($340,000) WILL LEAD OBJECTIVE 1, AND IN PARTICULAR TASK 1.1 FOCUSED ON PARASITE QUANTIFICATION. CENTER FOR RURAL ENTERPRISE AND ENVIRONMENTAL (CREEJ) ($340,000) WILL CO-LEAD OBJECTIVES 2 AND 3, SPECIFICALLY THE SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE SURVEY (TASK 2.1), WORKSHOPS FOCUSED ON TECHNOLOGY DOWN-SELECTION (TASK 3.1) AND PILOT-SCALE INVESTIGATIONS (TASK 3.2).OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS AS WELL AS SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION FOR COMMUNITY LEADERS AND PLANNERS REGARDING DEMOGRAPHICS AND CONTAMINANT EXPOSURE, AS WELL AS OPEN-SOURCE DATASETS ON SANITATION QUALITY AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES AND RESIDENTS OF UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES.
description.937: THE GREAT PLAINS ART MUSEUM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF NEBRASKA WILL PHOTOGRAPH AND REHOUSE A COLLECTION OF APPROXIMATELY 550 WORKS OF ART ON PAPER BY ARTIST AND EDUCATOR DWIGHT KIRSCH. A SEMINAL PROFESSOR AND ARTS ADMINISTRATOR, KIRSCH WAS INSTRUMENTAL IN BUILDING THE UNIVERSITY’S ART COLLECTION. FOLLOWING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF A RECENT MUSEUM ASSESSMENT PROGRAM (MAP) REPORT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE ARCHIVAL FOLDERS AND BOXES TO REHOUSE THE COLLECTION AND WILL CONTRACT WITH A PROFESSIONAL PHOTOGRAPHER AND REGIONAL CONSERVATION CENTER TO OFFER A FREE, ONE-DAY HINGING AND MATTING WORKSHOP FOR STAFF, STUDENTS, AND AREA MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS.
description.938: THE CHESAPEAKE CHILDREN’S MUSEUM WILL ESTABLISH A SERIES OF PROGRAMS TO INSPIRE CONNECTIONS AND CREATIVITY BY EXPLORING HISTORY, CULTURE, AND EXPRESSION THROUGH MUSIC. THE MUSEUM WILL OFFER HANDS-ON WORKSHOPS, MUSIC-RELATED ACTIVITIES, CONCERTS, AND PRESENTATIONS ON-SITE AND AT AREA SCHOOLS AND OTHER COMMUNITY SPACES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL INITIATE STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT, FACILITATE PROGRAMMING, AND PURCHASE SUPPLIES AND INSTRUMENTS FOR USE IN WORKSHOPS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL CONTRACT WITH PROFESSIONAL PERFORMERS AND INSTRUCTORS REPRESENTING A RANGE OF CULTURAL AND MUSIC TRADITIONS INCLUDING NATIVE AMERICAN, AFRICAN AMERICAN, WEST AFRICAN, AND LATIN AMERICAN. THE PROJECT AIMS TO PROMOTE CREATIVE THINKING, ENHANCE PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS, AND FOSTER APPRECIATION OF CULTURAL EXPRESSION THROUGH MUSIC. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS, WITH AN EMPHASIS ON CHILDREN, CAREGIVERS, AND FAMILIES THAT ARE ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED.
description.939: THE WIREGRASS MUSEUM OF ART WILL PERFORM A COMPLETE ASSESSMENT OF THE MUSEUM'S PERMANENT COLLECTION. THE COLLECTION OF 735 WORKS OF ART CONSISTS OF 231 DRAWINGS/WATERCOLORS, 259 PRINTS, 66 PHOTOGRAPHS, 147 PAINTINGS, AND 34 SCULPTURES (CERAMICS, TEXTILES, AND ASSEMBLAGES).  STAFF WILL WORK WITH CONSERVATORS TO CONDUCT AN ITEM-BY-ITEM CONSERVATION SURVEY OF OBJECTS. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL WRITE A LONG-TERM COLLECTIONS CARE PLAN TO PRIORITIZE AND RECOMMEND OBJECTS IN NEED OF CONSERVATION TREATMENT. TO INCREASE PUBLIC ONLINE ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION, STAFF WILL PHOTOGRAPH OBJECTS AND DIGITIZE COLLECTION RECORDS FOR THE MUSEUM’S WEBSITE.
description.940: DOOR COUNTY HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL CREATE PERMANENT, OUTDOOR INTERPRETIVE SIGNAGE FOR HERITAGE VILLAGE. THE HISTORICAL SITE FEATURES EIGHT BUILDINGS INCLUDING A GENERAL STORE, SCHOOLHOUSE, FISH HOUSE, AND CHAPEL ARRANGED TO REPRESENT A TYPICAL CROSSROADS VILLAGE FROM 1880-1910. OUTDOOR INTERPRETATION OF THE GROUNDS WILL ENABLE THE MUSEUM TO PROVIDE A HANDS-ON LEARNING OPPORTUNITY FOR VISITORS YEAR-ROUND AS THE BUILDINGS ARE CURRENTLY ONLY OPEN AND STAFFED SEASONALLY. THE MUSEUM WILL DESIGN AND INSTALL 12 ADA-COMPLIANT SIGNS THAT FEATURE INTERACTIVE AUDIO AND TACTILE ELEMENTS. STAFF WILL CONTRACT WITH AN OUTDOOR SIGN FABRICATOR, AN ARTIST TO CREATE TACTILE ELEMENTS, AND AN AUDIO INTERPRETATION SPECIALIST. SOCIETY STAFF WILL SURVEY VISITORS TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE SIGNAGE. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN EXPANDED INTERPRETATION WITH A FOCUS ON PERSONAL LIVED EXPERIENCES AND WILL BENEFIT VISITORS TO HERITAGE VILLAGE AND THE LOCAL COMMUNITY.
description.941: THE ART MUSEUM OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS WILL CONTINUE A MULTI-YEAR PROJECT TO PHOTOGRAPH AND DIGITIZE ITS PERMANENT COLLECTION. BUILDING ON PREVIOUS IMLS GRANTS THAT PRODUCED DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHS FOR OVER 30% OF THE COLLECTION, THIS FINAL PHASE OF THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THE PHOTOGRAPHY OF AN ADDITIONAL 200 TWO-DIMENSIONAL WORKS OF ART. MUSEUM STAFF, WORKING IN TANDEM WITH A CONTRACTED PHOTOGRAPHER AND A PROFESSIONAL ART FRAMER, WILL PHOTOGRAPH ARTWORKS, PRODUCE CONDITION REPORTS, AND REFRAME ARTWORKS AS NECESSARY. STAFF WILL UPLOAD THE IMAGES OF THE ARTWORK TO ITS COLLECTIONS DATABASE AND MAKE THE 200 CATALOG ENTRIES FREELY AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC ONLINE. THIS WILL ALLOW THE MUSEUM TO INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY OF THE COLLECTION FOR THE BENEFIT OF RESEARCHERS AND THE PUBLIC.
description.942: THE PENSACOLA MESS HALL WILL CREATE AND DELIVER HANDS-ON SCIENCE LESSONS FOR SIXTH-GRADE STUDENTS AND PROVIDE TRAINING TO TEACHERS. MESS HALL WILL INITIALLY FOCUS ON TWO SCHOOLS THAT ARE TRANSITIONING SIXTH-GRADE CLASSROOMS TO ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS AS PART OF A PILOT PROGRAM. PARTNERING WITH THE ESCAMBIA COUNTY SCHOOL DISTRICT, MESS HALL WILL DEVELOP LESSONS FOR ALL SEVEN SCIENCE MODULES COVERED IN THE SIXTH-GRADE PACING GUIDE. STAFF WILL DEVELOP AND PURCHASE MATERIALS FOR LESSONS AND CREATE AND CONDUCT EVENING TEACHER TRAINING SESSIONS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN HANDS-ON, OPEN-ENDED INSTRUCTION INTEGRATED WITH SCHOOL CURRICULUM TO ADVANCE SCIENCE PROFICIENCY AND SUPPORT TEACHERS DURING THIS TRANSITION. THE PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO INITIALLY BENEFIT THE STUDENTS DIRECTLY PARTICIPATING IN THE MUSEUM-LED PROGRAMS. A LARGER IMPACT IS EXPECTED FROM TRAINING TEACHERS TO DELIVER THESE ACTIVITIES BEYOND THE PROGRAM PERIOD.
description.943: THE MAINE CENTER FOR COASTAL FISHERIES WILL UNDERTAKE PLANNING TO PREPARE FOR AN EXPANSION OF ITS DISCOVERY WHARF INTERPRETIVE CENTER. LOCATED IN MAINE’S TOP LOBSTER LANDING PORT, THE CENTER ENGAGES AND INFORMS THE PUBLIC ABOUT COASTAL COMMUNITIES, LOCAL FISHERIES, AND THE MARINE ECOSYSTEM. CENTER STAFF WILL PARTNER WITH LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS TO FORM AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE, DEVELOP EXHIBITION THEMES, CREATE A BUSINESS AND STAFFING NEEDS PLAN, AND COMPLETE INTERPRETIVE TRAINING. THE CENTER WILL CONTRACT WITH A MUSEUM CONSULTANT TO ASSIST WITH EXHIBITION DESIGN AND PLANNING. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A COMPREHENSIVE PLAN FOR THE EXPANSION OF DISCOVERY WHARF TO MEET THE DEMANDS OF VISITATION AND SUPPORT COMMUNITY EDUCATIONAL NEEDS. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT INCLUDE CENTER STAFF, LOCAL EDUCATION GROUPS, THE COASTAL MAINE COMMUNITY, AND VISITING TOURISTS.
description.944: THE LA JOLLA HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL DIGITIZE NEARLY 1,800 PHOTOGRAPHS, POSTCARDS, AND ORAL HISTORY RECORDINGS IN ITS COLLECTION. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE HIRING AND TRAINING OF TWO PAID INTERNS. UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF THE COLLECTIONS MANAGER, THE INTERNS WILL DIGITIZE AND ACCESSION THE COLLECTIONS, RESEARCH AND DRAFT DESCRIPTIONS FOR THE CATALOG RECORDS, AND UPLOAD ALL MATERIALS TO THE SOCIETY’S COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. CATALOGING AND DIGITIZING THE COLLECTION WILL ADDRESS THE URGENT NEED TO PRESERVE FIDELITY OF THE DETERIORATING ITEMS IN THE COLLECTION. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO INCREASE THE ACCESSIBILITY OF THE COLLECTIONS FOR GUEST CURATORS, RESEARCHERS, GENEALOGISTS, THE PUBLIC, AND STAFF MEMBERS, WHO WILL USE THE COLLECTIONS TO INFORM FUTURE EXHIBITIONS AND TO RESPOND TO THE ESTIMATED 325 RESEARCH REQUESTS THE SOCIETY RECEIVES ANNUALLY.
description.945: THE KONA HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL ORGANIZE, INVENTORY, AND REHOUSE ITS D. UCHIDA FARM ARCHIVE COLLECTION. THE COLLECTION CONTAINS ARCHIVAL MATERIALS, OBJECTS, AND TEXTILES ASSOCIATED WITH THE SOCIETY’S KONA COFFEE LIVING HISTORY FARM SITE; A HISTORIC FARM HOMESTEADED BY JAPANESE IMMIGRANTS. INFORMED BY A PRESERVATION ASSISTANCE GRANT (PAG), THE SOCIETY’S COLLECTIONS MANAGER WILL PROVIDE STAFF AND VOLUNTEER TRAINING IN COLLECTIONS HANDLING AND PROCEDURES AND OVERSEE THE ORGANIZATION, INVENTORY, AND REHOUSING OF THE COLLECTION. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN GREATER PRESERVATION AND INTELLECTUAL CONTROL OVER THE COLLECTION, ENABLING EXPANDED INTERPRETATION OF THE SITE. THE SOCIETY WILL BE ABLE TO BETTER SERVE ITS COMMUNITY, VISITORS, AND RESEARCHERS BY PROVIDING ACCESS TO THIS COLLECTION THAT DOCUMENTS COFFEE FARMING AND THE JAPANESE IMMIGRANT EXPERIENCE IN KONA, HAWAIʻI.
description.946: THE MUSEUM OF ART FORT COLLINS WILL EXPAND THE SCOPE OF ITS PILOT “MOA FOR ALL” PROGRAM TO PROMOTE INCLUSIVE ENGAGEMENT ACROSS DIVERSE AUDIENCES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EQUIPPING ITS NEW ART ENGAGEMENT CENTER AND IMPLEMENTING A COMMUNITY CURATED ART AND CONVERSATION PROGRAM. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH THE POUDRE SCHOOL DISTRICT, COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY, AND SOCIAL SERVICE/NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS TO CREATE FREE CUSTOMIZED ACCESS PACKAGES TAILORED TO THE UNIQUE NEEDS OF UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITY MEMBERS. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT A FULL-TIME PROGRAM MANAGER AND THE PURCHASE OF EQUIPMENT AND SUPPLIES FOR PROJECT ACTIVITIES. THE OUTCOME WILL BE A MODEL FOR MEANINGFUL COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT THAT CAN BE EASILY REPLICATED BY OTHER MUSEUMS. THE ULTIMATE BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT ARE MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY AT THE MOST RISK OF SOCIAL EXCLUSION FROM THE INFORMAL CULTURAL EDUCATION THAT VISITING AN ART MUSEUM PROVIDES.
description.947: THE EMILY DICKENSON MUSEUM WILL CONCEPTUALIZE, PILOT, AND DESIGN INTERPRETIVE ENHANCEMENTS TO THE HOMESTEAD, EMILY DICKINSON’S HOME AND THE SITE OF HER CREATIVE OUTPUT. INFORMED BY ITS RECENT COMPREHENSIVE INTERPRETATION PLAN, THE MUSEUM WILL EXPAND ITS NARRATIVE TO BE MORE INCLUSIVE AND WELCOMING FOR ALL VISITORS. ENHANCEMENTS WILL INCLUDE VIGNETTES EXPLORING THE POET’S DAILY LIFE, POETRY THROUGH IMMERSIVE MEDIA, SUBTLE SOUNDSCAPES, AND PROJECTION MAPPING. MUSEUM STAFF WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EXHIBITION AND MULTI-MEDIA DESIGN FIRM AND ACCESSIBILITY SPECIALIST TO PRODUCE FULL SCHEMATIC DESIGNS AND WRITTEN NARRATIVES FOR INTERPRETIVE ELEMENTS. IMPROVING ACCESSIBILITY AND HIGHLIGHTING STORIES OF DOMESTIC LABOR AT THE HOMESTEAD WILL BENEFIT ALL VISITORS TO THE SITE AND ENCOURAGE NEW AUDIENCES INCLUDING STUDENTS, LGBTQIA+, AND CONTEMPORARY CREATIVES, ARTISTS, AND WRITERS SEEKING INSPIRATION.
description.948: THE MUSEUM OF CRAFT AND DESIGN WILL CREATE A TRAVELING TEXTILE EXHIBITION “RUGLIFE” AND ACCOMPANYING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING. THE EXHIBIT WILL EXPLORE THE HISTORY OF RUGMAKING, AND FEATURE WORKS BY 14 CONTEMPORARY ARTISTS FROM NINE COUNTRIES. STAFF WILL COMMISSION THREE TACTILE PIECES AND AN AUDIO TOUR TO ACCOMPANY THE EXHIBIT. BUILDING UPON TWO PREVIOUS IMLS PROJECTS, THE MUSEUM WILL OFFER ITS SIGNATURE MAKEART PROGRAMMING TO INCLUDE EIGHT MULTILINGUAL PROJECTS, OVER 100 HANDS-ON PROGRAMS, AND OVER 4,000 FREE MAKEART KITS. THE MUSEUM WILL ALSO CREATE A REPLICABLE MODEL OF ITS MAKEART PROGRAMMING TO SHARE WITH PARTICIPATING MUSEUMS. THE EXHIBIT AND HANDS-ON ART EXPERIENCES WILL ENGAGE BAY AREA RESIDENTS OF DIVERSE BACKGROUNDS, INCOME LEVELS, AND ABILITIES WHILE ENCOURAGING CREATIVITY AND CONNECTION.
description.949: THE ART MUSEUM OF EASTERN IDAHO WILL IMPLEMENT A TEEN TOURS PROGRAM FOR EIGHTH TO TWELFTH-GRADE STUDENTS THAT INCLUDES FIELD TRIPS, INTERACTIVE ART PROJECTS, COMMUNITY PROJECTS, AND MUSEUM CAREER PREPARATION. STAFF WILL DEVELOP FIELD TRIP CURRICULA AND SCHEDULE TOURS, AS WELL AS RECRUIT, TRAIN, AND MENTOR STUDENTS IN THE MUSEUM CAREER PROGRAM. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT TRANSPORTATION FOR FIELD TRIPS, ART SUPPLIES, DIGITAL EQUIPMENT, AND PROGRAM PROMOTION. THE PROJECT WILL FOSTER ART APPRECIATION, PROMOTE CREATIVITY AND PROBLEM-SOLVING, AND IMPROVE COMMUNICATION AND COLLABORATION SKILLS AMONG STUDENT PARTICIPANTS. ADDITIONALLY, STUDENTS SELECTED FOR THE MENTORSHIP PROGRAM WILL DEVELOP LEADERSHIP SKILLS AND GAIN HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE THAT PREPARES THEM FOR A POSSIBLE CAREER IN MUSEUMS.
description.950: THE INSTITUTE OF CONTEMPORARY ART, SAN DIEGO, WILL INITIATE A COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT SERIES TO PROMOTE PHYSICAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL, AND SOCIAL HEALING THROUGH ART IN THE WAKE OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. THE INSTITUTE WILL HOST A SERIES OF EIGHT PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT EVENTS THAT CORRESPOND TO ITS UPCOMING SEASON OF EXHIBITIONS FOCUSED ON PERSONAL AND SOCIETAL HEALING. INSTITUTE STAFF WILL BRING TOGETHER ARTISTS AND CROSS-SECTOR PROFESSIONALS IN PANELS AND SYMPOSIA, OFFER INTERACTIVE ART ACTIVATIONS AND ART-MAKING ACTIVITIES, AND ENHANCE DIGITAL ENGAGEMENT THROUGH PODCASTS, LIVE STREAMS, AND ARCHIVED FOOTAGE. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT STAFF TIME, PROGRAM MARKETING, AND ART SUPPLIES, AS WELL AS STIPENDS AND TRAVEL FOR ARTISTS AND SPEAKERS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN FREE, ACCESSIBLE, AND INCLUSIVE OPPORTUNITIES THAT ENCOURAGE COMMUNITY BUILDING, WELLNESS, AND HEALING FOR THE RESIDENTS OF SAN DIEGO COUNTY.
description.951: THE DUBUQUE MUSEUM OF ART WILL ASSEMBLE A TEAM OF MUSEUM STAFF, VISUAL ARTS EDUCATORS, AND ENGAGEMENT EXPERTS TO DEVELOP, TEST, AND DEPLOY A FORMAL PROCESS FOR EDUCATIONAL ENGAGEMENT FOR PUBLIC-FACING PROGRAMS AT THE MUSEUM. PROJECT STAFF WILL TRAIN WITH CONSULTANTS IN VISUAL LITERACY STRATEGIES. THE MUSEUM WILL CREATE AN IN-DEPTH SET OF STRATEGIES LEVELED FOR CLASSROOM USE AND FACILITATION PRACTICES FOR GALLERY TOURS AT THE MUSEUM. MUSEUM STAFF, BOARD, DOCENTS, AND VOLUNTEERS WILL RECEIVE EDUCATIONAL ENGAGEMENT TRAINING. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL CREATE NEW TRAINING MATERIALS FOR ONBOARDING A GROWING MUSEUM STAFF AS WELL AS VISUAL LITERACY CURRICULUM.
description.952: THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS CHICAGO LIBRARY AIMS TO ENHANCE LIBRARIANS’ KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND APPLICATIONS IN ASSESSING STUDENT SUCCESS AND LIBRARY EXPERIENCES, UTILIZING AN ASSESSMENT TOOL DEVELOPED BY THE PROJECT TEAM IN PREVIOUSLY FUNDED IMLS WORK. DURING THE FIRST YEAR, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DEVELOP, DELIVER, AND FACILITATE A WORKSHOP SERIES TO ENHANCE LIBRARIANS’ PROFICIENCY IN USING ASSESSMENT TOOLS THROUGH ENRICHED LEARNING EXPERIENCES. AFTER COMPLETING THE WORKSHOP SERIES IN THE FIRST YEAR AND THE IMPLEMENTATION PROJECT IN THE SECOND YEAR, PARTICIPANTS WILL BECOME AMBASSADORS FOR A STUDENT SUCCESS ASSESSMENT PROJECT.
description.953: WEST CHESTER UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA WILL PARTNER WITH INDIANA UNIVERSITY BLOOMINGTON, WESTERN MICHIGAN UNIVERSITY, AND DELAWARE COUNTY COMMUNITY COLLEGE TO DEVELOP A CAREERLIT LEARNING MODULE SERIES FOR COLLEGE STUDENTS TO ADVANCE THEIR CAREER INFORMATION LITERACY AND CAREER RESEARCH COMPETENCIES. THIS PROJECT INTENDS TO TRANSFORM THE WAYS THAT LIBRARIES SERVE THE NATION THROUGH A SUBSTANTIVE, LEARNING-CENTERED COLLABORATION MODEL BETWEEN LIBRARIES, CAREER CENTERS, AND COLLEGES. THE MODULE SERIES WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS WITH A STRUCTURED PATHWAY TO IDENTIFY CAREER GOALS THAT ARE ALIGNED WITH THEIR INTRINSIC VALUES AND PERSONAL DEFINITIONS OF SUCCESS. STUDENTS WILL GAIN INSIGHTS INTO CAREER OPTIONS, EXPLORE CAREER RESOURCES AND OPPORTUNITIES, AND CREATE A PERSONALIZED ROAD MAP FOR CAREER SUCCESS. THIS PROJECT WILL TARGET COLLEGE STUDENTS, ESPECIALLY DURING THEIR FIRST OR SECOND YEAR IN COLLEGE, TO FOSTER THEIR SELF-EFFICACY, ADAPTABILITY, AND AGENCY IN EARLY-STAGE CAREER EXPLORATION, PLANNING, AND DECISION MAKING.
description.954: THE URBAN LIBRARIES COUNCIL WILL PARTNER WITH THE SAFE ROUTES PARTNERSHIP AND THE ASSOCIATION FOR RURAL AND SMALL LIBRARIES TO ESTABLISH A PROOF OF CONCEPT FOR SAFE ROUTES TO LIBRARIES, INCREASING THE PHYSICAL ACCESSIBILITY OF PUBLIC LIBRARIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY. THE SAFE ROUTES TO LIBRARIES PLANNING PROJECT WILL COMPLETE A NATIONAL SCAN, BUILDING A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE WORK LIBRARIES ARE ALREADY DOING TO ESTABLISH SAFE PATHS TO THEIR LOCATIONS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL COLLECT FEEDBACK FROM LIBRARIES ON THE SAFE ROUTES PROGRAM THROUGH LISTENING SESSIONS AND SURVEYS AND LEVERAGE EXISTING NATIONAL MODELS FOR SCHOOLS AND PARKS TO CREATE A PROTOTYPE SAFE ROUTES TO LIBRARIES TOOLKIT WITH EXAMPLES FROM RURAL, SUBURBAN, AND URBAN LIBRARIES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL THEN DISSEMINATE THE TOOLKIT AND THEIR INITIAL FINDINGS. THE PLANNING PROJECT WILL CONCLUDE WITH A NATIONAL WEBINAR SHOWCASING THE PROJECT’S LEARNINGS TO DATE AND EXPLORING THE FEASIBILITY OF DEVELOPING A NATIONAL SAFE ROUTES TO LIBRARIES MODEL.
description.955: THE PENNSYLVANIA STATE UNIVERSITY WILL HOST A TWO-DAY NATIONAL FORUM BRINGING TOGETHER SCHOLARS AND PRACTITIONERS TO ESTABLISH CONSENSUS AROUND NATIONAL EDUCATIONAL STANDARDS AND PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES FOR PRIVACY LITERACY EDUCATION IN LIBRARIES. PRIVACY LITERACY IS GAINING TRACTION AS A TOPIC OF LIBRARY PROGRAMMING. IN ADDITION, THERE IS AN EXPRESS NEED FOR COMPREHENSIVE CONSENSUS STANDARDS TO GUIDE THE CREATION AND ASSESSMENT OF PRIVACY LITERACY CURRICULA ACROSS THE K–20 EDUCATIONAL SPECTRUM. BY CONVENING EXPERTS WHO WORK ON PRIVACY LITERACY IN PUBLIC, SCHOOL, AND ACADEMIC LIBRARY CONTEXTS, THIS FORUM WILL ADVANCE AN INTEGRATIVE AND CONSENSUS-BASED MODEL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION, ASSESSMENT, AND STAFFING OF PRIVACY LITERACY EFFORTS. STANDARDS-BASED PRIVACY LITERACY PROGRAMMING WILL ENHANCE THE EFFICACY AND ACCESSIBILITY OF PRIVACY LITERACY EDUCATION FOR DIVERSE PATRON COMMUNITIES. PROJECT RESULTS WILL BE OPEN-LICENSED AND FREELY ACCESSIBLE.
description.956: CARNEGIE MELLON UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP THE PROJECT ON OPEN AND EVOLVING METALITERATURE, A DYNAMIC, EVOLVING, AND SUSTAINABLE COLLECTION OF OPEN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES TO ENHANCE ALGORITHM, DATA, AND MEDIA LITERACY FOR LEARNERS OF HIGH SCHOOL AGE AND ABOVE. THIS PROJECT IS DESIGNED FOR A RANGE OF INSTRUCTOR AND LEARNER AUDIENCES INTERESTED IN PRACTICAL, PEER-REVIEWED OPEN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES DESIGNED TO IMPROVE INFORMATION LITERACY LEVELS AND EMPOWER DIGITAL CITIZENS. THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON THREE AREAS: ALGORITHM, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), AND SOFTWARE LITERACIES; DATA, COMPUTATIONAL, AND ANALYTICAL LITERACIES, AND MEDIA, VISUAL, AND INFORMATION LITERACIES. IT BUILDS UPON THE WORK OF INITIATIVES SUCH AS THE ALGORITHM & DATA LITERACY PROJECT—UNESCO’S WORK DEFINING AI AND DATA COMPETENCY FRAMEWORKS—THE WHITE HOUSE’S BLUEPRINT FOR AN AI BILL OF RIGHTS, THE ASSOCIATION OF COLLEGE & RESEARCH LIBRARIES’ (ACRL) FRAMEWORK FOR INFORMATION LITERACY, AND THE 2021 ACRL FRAMEWORK FOR VISUAL LITERACY IN HIGHER EDUCATION.
description.957: PORTLAND STATE UNIVERSITY GEOGRAPHY DEPARTMENT WILL DEVELOP THE CAPACITY OF PUBLIC LIBRARIES TO SERVE AS KEY PARTNERS IN LOCAL GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM (GIS) DATA ECOSYSTEMS. THE PROJECT WILL RUN AN IN-PERSON AND ONLINE TRAINING FOR TEAMS OF LIBRARIANS AND GIS PROFESSIONALS, ESTABLISH FUNDING AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR LOCAL GIS PROJECTS, AND CREATE A COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE. THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE THE EXISTING ONLINE GIS-MAPPING TOOLKIT THROUGH ADDITIONAL RESOURCES INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT OF A REPOSITORY OF CASE STUDIES. THE PROJECT'S OUTPUTS AND FINDINGS WILL BE WIDELY DISSEMINATED TO LIBRARIES AND ALLIED GROUPS THAT SUPPORT THE PUBLICATION AND USE OF GEOSPATIAL DATA. ULTIMATELY, THE PROJECT WILL CONNECT PUBLIC LIBRARY STAFF WITH GIS LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES AND PATHWAYS THAT BRING GIS AGENCIES, ORGANIZATIONS, AND BUSINESSES TOGETHER TO HELP LIBRARIES AND THEIR PATRONS.
description.958: THE UNIVERSITY OF VIRGINIA LIBRARY, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE INSTITUTE FOR THE STUDY OF KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT IN EDUCATION, WILL DEVELOP A COMMUNITY WEB PORTAL THAT FOCUSES ON HARNESSING GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TECHNOLOGIES TO FOSTER THE CREATION AND ADAPTATION OF OPEN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES (OER). THE PROJECT IS AIMED AT AIDING LIBRARIANS, EDUCATORS, AI PRACTITIONERS, AND STUDENTS FROM K–12 LIBRARIES TO HIGHER EDUCATION. THE PROJECT’S PORTAL IS CONCEIVED AS A DYNAMIC SPACE WHERE INDIVIDUALS CAN COLLABORATE AND SHARE KNOWLEDGE, TOOLS, AND STRATEGIES RELATED TO AI IN THE SERVICE OF OER, SUPPORTED BY A RICH ARRAY OF RESOURCES LIKE A REPOSITORY, DISCUSSION FORUM, AND EVENTS CALENDAR.
description.959: THE AMERICAN LIBRARY ASSOCIATION, WITH MEMBERS OF THE NEW ADULT LITERACY AND LEARNING IMPACT NETWORK, INCLUDING THE BARBARA BUSH FOUNDATION FOR FAMILY LITERACY, NATIONAL CENTER FOR FAMILIES LEARNING, PROLITERACY, AND WORLD EDUCATION, WILL DESIGN ADULT AND FAMILY LITERACY SUPPORT CENTERS FOR LIBRARIES NATIONWIDE. ALTHOUGH LITERACY IS DIRECTLY CONNECTED TO BETTER HEALTH OUTCOMES, REDUCTIONS IN RECIDIVISM FOR RETURNING CITIZENS, AND BETTER LANGUAGE AND LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN WHOSE PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS HAVE HIGHER LITERACY, ACCESS TO LITERACY SKILLS AND SERVICES REMAINS A PERVASIVE CHALLENGE ACROSS THE COUNTRY. THE GRANT WILL DEVELOP AND PILOT MODELS FOR LIBRARY ADULT AND FAMILY LITERACY SUPPORT CENTERS WITH LIBRARY PARTNERS INCLUDING CHARLESTON COUNTY PUBLIC LIBRARY, CHICAGO PUBLIC LIBRARY, AND THE DELAWARE LIBRARY CONSORTIUM. THE PROJECT WILL PRODUCE A COMPREHENSIVE, INTERACTIVE TOOLKIT FOR COMMUNITY LITERACY-BUILDING AND TRAIN-THE-TRAINER MATERIALS FOR REPLICATION IN LIBRARIES NATIONWIDE.
description.960: SIMMONS UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE (LIS) WILL IMPLEMENT A NATIONWIDE CURRICULUM-SHARING SYSTEM OF EQUITY, DIVERSITY, AND INCLUSION (EDI) COURSES TO PROVIDE LIS STUDENTS ACCESS TO COURSES THAT PREPARE THEM TO WORK WITH DIVERSE COMMUNITIES. THE PROGRAM WILL BUILD ON EXISTING INITIATIVES AND INFRASTRUCTURE TO SHARE MATERIALS FOR A HOLISTIC EDI AUDIT OF LIS CURRICULA AND PROVIDE FREE TRAINING ON THOSE TOOLS; LEVERAGE EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE TO DEVELOP A PLATFORM FOR LIS PROGRAMS TO SHARE EDI-FOCUSED COURSES WHERE STUDENTS CAN SEAMLESSLY TAKE AND TRANSFER CREDITS ACROSS PARTICIPATING SCHOOLS; AND ENGAGE STUDENTS FROM HISTORICALLY MARGINALIZED BACKGROUNDS TO PROVIDE CURRICULAR AND PROGRAM FEEDBACK THROUGH A PARTICIPATORY PROCESS THAT RECOGNIZES, HONORS, AND REMUNERATES THEIR VOICES AND EXPERIENCE. THE PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE A NATIONAL PLATFORM FOR SHARING EDI CURRICULA AND TOOLS, AS WELL AS TRAINING MATERIALS FOR INCLUSIVE PEDAGOGY AND ANTI-RACIST EDUCATION.
description.961: THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH CAROLINA AT GREENSBORO WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR DEVELOPING ROBUST INDEPENDENT-MADE (INDIE) DIGITAL VIDEO GAME COLLECTIONS IN ACADEMIC AND PUBLIC LIBRARIES. WHILE LIBRARIES HAVE COLLECTED PHYSICAL COPIES OF VIDEO GAMES FOR A LONG TIME, THEY CURRENTLY LACK METHODS FOR COLLECTING DIGITAL-ONLY GAMES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONDUCT EXPLORATORY RESEARCH TO UNDERSTAND CRITICAL ISSUES, HOST A NATIONAL VIRTUAL FORUM TO SPARK BROADER DISCUSSION, AND COMPOSE A WORKING GROUP TO DEVELOP LEGAL AND SOCIOTECHNICAL ROAD MAPS FOR COLLECTING INDIE DIGITAL GAMES. IN ADDITION TO THE PRODUCTS OF THE WORKING GROUP, THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A RESEARCH ARTICLE, TWO CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, BLOG POSTS, TWO WEBINAR PRESENTATIONS, AND PROCEEDINGS AND RECORDINGS FROM THE FORUM. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF STAKEHOLDER NEEDS, STRATEGIES FOR LEGAL AND TECHNICAL INFRASTRUCTURE, AND INCREASED ACCESS TO INDIE GAMES. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE LIBRARIANS, INDIE GAME DEVELOPERS, AND GAME COLLECTION USERS AT ACADEMIC AND PUBLIC LIBRARIES.
description.962: VIRGINIA TECH’S UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES AND DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER SCIENCE WILL HARNESS THE POWER OF ELECTRONIC THESES AND DISSERTATIONS (ETDS), INTEGRATED WITH LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS), TO IMPROVE DIGITAL LIBRARY SERVICES AND TOOLS FOR ADVANCED INFORMATION DISCOVERY, RESEARCH TREND ANALYSIS, AND PERSONALIZED RESEARCH ASSISTANCE FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL EXPLORE ADVANCED INFORMATION RETRIEVAL TECHNIQUES COMBINED WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TO CREATE A SYMBIOTIC SYSTEM WHEREIN ETDS AND LLMS ENHANCE EACH OTHER’S VALUE. THE PROJECT WILL THEN PROTOTYPE SOFTWARE THAT LEVERAGES THESE INTEGRATED TOOLS AND FOSTERS BROADER UNDERSTANDING AND ADOPTION OF AI TECHNOLOGIES IN THE LIBRARY. THE PROJECT WILL DISSEMINATE KNOWLEDGE THROUGH ACADEMIC PUBLICATIONS, OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE, AND WORKSHOPS GEARED TOWARD RESEARCHERS AND LIBRARY PROFESSIONALS. ULTIMATELY, THE PROJECT WILL MAKE LLMS MORE RELIABLE AND USEFUL FOR ACADEMIC AND SCHOLARLY WORK, ENABLING THEM TO PROVIDE RELEVANT AND TRUSTWORTHY INFORMATION AND INSIGHTS FOR ACADEMIC LIBRARY USERS.
description.963: THE WISCONSIN STATE LIBRARY AGENCY, WASHINGTON STATE LIBRARY, GAME TO GROW, FIELD DAY LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN–MADISON, HEART OF THE DEERNICORN, AND WILS, WITH THE SUPPORT OF THE CHIEF OFFICERS OF STATE LIBRARY AGENCIES (COSLA) AND THE AMERICAN LIBRARY ASSOCIATION’S GAMES & GAMING ROUND TABLE, WILL DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE A COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH REPORT AND DIGITAL TOOLKIT TO GUIDE LIBRARIES IN IMPLEMENTING GAMES-BASED SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL BE STRUCTURED INTO THREE PHASES: 1) INITIAL PILOT PROGRAMMING AND RESEARCH; 2) EXPANSION AND COMMUNITY PRACTICE WORKSHOPS; AND 3) THE CREATION AND DISSEMINATION OF A DIGITAL TOOLKIT. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE AN ANALYSIS OF GAMES-BASED LIBRARY SERVICES AND A TOOLKIT THAT PROVIDES LIBRARIES WITH PRACTICAL RECOMMENDATIONS FOR BUDGETING, FUNDING, METHODOLOGIES, OVERCOMING CHALLENGES, AND ENSURING EQUITY AND ACCESSIBILITY.
description.964: VIRGINIA’S ACADEMIC LIBRARY CONSORTIUM, A STATE-FUNDED CONSORTIUM OF 71 ACADEMIC LIBRARIES, IN COOPERATION WITH SOFTWARE SERVICES BY SCIENTIST.COM (A SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT COMPANY WITH A RECORD OF CONTRIBUTING TO OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE) AND THE ROY ROSENZWEIG CENTER FOR HISTORY AND NEW MEDIA (THE DEVELOPERS OF ZOTERO AND OMEKA), WILL SCALE THE NEXT PHASE OF DEVELOPMENT OF AN OPEN-SOURCE, LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (LMS)-INTEGRATED OPEN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES REPOSITORY FOR ASSESSMENT, HOMEWORK, AND TEST-BANK RESOURCES. THIS NEXT PHASE OF PROJECT DEVELOPMENT, WHICH AIMS TO ENSURE SEAMLESS INTEGRATION WITH THE FOUR MOST POPULAR LMS PLATFORMS, WILL SEED THE REPOSITORY WITH EXTENSIVE CONTENT, STREAMLINE THE USER-TESTED UPLOAD AND PERMISSIONS PROCESSES, AND CONSIDER THE BEST PRACTICES FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) -GENERATED AND VETTED PROBLEM SETS.
description.965: TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY, WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA; THE UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES OF PURDUE; THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, RENO; TEXAS STATE UNIVERSITY; AND PRAIRIE VIEW A&M UNIVERSITY, WILL DEVELOP AN EVIDENCE-BASED RESEARCH DATA MANAGEMENT (RDM) CORE COMPETENCY LEARNING MODULE AND STANDARDIZED MEASURE FOR SOCIAL SCIENCES, FOCUSING ON LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE (LIS) AND EDUCATION. RESEARCHERS WILL USE AN ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN, STUDENT SURVEY, FACULTY INTERVIEWS, AND STUDENT FOCUS GROUPS TO DEVELOP A RDM LEARNING MODULE. THE TEAM WILL DEPLOY THE MODULE IN GRADUATE-LEVEL RESEARCH METHODS COURSES ACROSS THE PARTNER UNIVERSITIES TO INVESTIGATE THE TRAINING’S EFFECTIVENESS. THROUGH RIGOROUS STATISTICAL ANALYSIS, THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL DEVELOP A CORE COMPETENCY MEASURE BASED ON THE INTERVENTION THAT WILL BE EVALUATED ACROSS THE PARTNER INSTITUTIONS. THE RESULTING WIDELY APPLICABLE, STANDARDIZED MEASURE WILL HAVE FAR-REACHING EFFECTS ON THE SOCIAL SCIENCE AND LIS RESEARCH COMMUNITIES, AS WELL AS ON THE QUALITY OF ACADEMIC LIBRARY RDM SERVICES IN SUPPORTING STUDENT SUCCESS.
description.966: THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS AT AUSTIN (UT) HOGG FOUNDATION FOR MENTAL HEALTH, ALONGSIDE THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF STATE MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAM DIRECTORS, THE COUNCIL OF STATE ARCHIVISTS, AND THE UT SCHOOL OF INFORMATION, WILL DEVELOP AND HOST NATIONWIDE, HISTORICAL PUBLIC MENTAL HEALTH RECORDS STAKEHOLDER CONVENINGS. HISTORICAL PUBLIC MENTAL HEALTH RECORDS ARE ADMINISTRATIVE RECORDS AND PATIENT RECORDS WITH INDIVIDUALLY IDENTIFIABLE HEALTH INFORMATION ABOUT A PERSON 50 YEARS FOLLOWING THEIR DEATH. THE PROJECT WILL GATHER ARCHIVISTS, HISTORIANS, RESEARCHERS, GENEALOGISTS, PEOPLE WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE IN PUBLIC PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALS, AND HOSPITAL ADMINISTRATORS TO DISCUSS SHARED CHALLENGES, SUCCESSES, CRITIQUES, AND POTENTIAL COLLABORATIVE SOLUTIONS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF THESE SENSITIVE DOCUMENTS. CURRENTLY, THERE IS NO SPACE FOR THESE COMPLEX DISCUSSIONS, NOR ARE THERE FRAMEWORKS FOR MANAGING HISTORICAL PUBLIC MENTAL HEALTH RECORDS THAT PRACTITIONERS CAN DIRECTLY REFERENCE. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE AND A COMPREHENSIVE PUBLICATION TO FACILITATE ONGOING CONVERSATIONS WITH KEY STAKEHOLDERS ACROSS THE NATION.
description.967: RUTGERS UNIVERSITY, IN COLLABORATION WITH SIMMONS UNIVERSITY AND THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT, WILL ADDRESS THE NEED TO CREATE INTEGRATED, FLEXIBLE, AND COMPREHENSIVE APPROACHES TO PROVENANCE DOCUMENTATION ACROSS TYPES OF COLLECTIONS. PROVENANCE IS THE STORY OF HOW SOMETHING HAS COME TO BE, WHETHER IT BE PHYSICAL, DIGITAL, OR EVEN AN ABSTRACT IDEA. WHILE THE IMPORTANCE OF PROVENANCE CROSSES DISCIPLINARY BOUNDARIES, CURRENT PRACTICE LACKS COLLECTIVE CONVERSATION AND SCHOLARSHIP. THE PROJECT WILL PLAN EVENTS BRINGING TOGETHER 100 RESEARCH AND PRACTITIONER EXPERTS FROM ACROSS MANY DISCIPLINES OVER THE COURSE OF 24 MONTHS. AT THESE EVENTS, PARTICIPANTS WILL SHARE THEIR EXPERTISE ON CURRENT PROVENANCE DEBATES, SUCH AS DISCIPLINARY SILOS, TEMPORALITY, AND PERSUASIVENESS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE TO CLARIFY FOUNDATIONAL PROVENANCE CHALLENGES AND SUPPORT FUTURE WORK ON IMPROVED MODELS AND DOCUMENTARY APPROACHES. ULTIMATELY, THE WORK WILL PROMOTE GREATER TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN THE MANAGEMENT AND CURATION OF CULTURAL HERITAGE, DIGITAL DATA, AND E-SCIENCE COLLECTIONS.
description.968: THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN SCHOOL OF INFORMATION AND THE INTER-UNIVERSITY CONSORTIUM FOR POLITICAL AND SOCIAL RESEARCH (ICPSR) WILL STUDY HOW GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (GENAI) MIGHT ENHANCE DATA CURATION. A PRIOR IMLS-FUNDED STUDY REVEALED THAT NATIONALLY, THE DATA CURATION FIELD IS CHALLENGED WITH THE TIME-INTENSIVE NATURE OF GENERATING EXPERT-CRAFTED, DETAILED METADATA AND ADDRESSING POTENTIAL DISCLOSURE RISKS WHEN SHARING DATA FOR REUSE. THIS RESEARCH PROJECT WILL PURSUE BOTH HOW GENAI CAN AID IN DRAFTING AND EVALUATING METADATA, AS WELL AS HOW COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS CAN ASSIST IN IDENTIFYING AND MANAGING SENSITIVE DATA ELEMENTS. EVALUATION OF GENAI TOOLS’ EFFECTIVENESS WILL INVOLVE CURATOR FEEDBACK, USER STUDIES, TEXT ANALYTICS, AND COMPARISONS WITH ICPSR’S CURRENT METADATA CURATION AND SEARCH INDICES. PROJECT BENEFICIARIES ACROSS THE NATION WILL INCLUDE DATA CURATORS GAINING EFFICIENCY IN THEIR ROLES; DATA REUSERS ENJOYING BETTER DATA ACCESS AND VARIABLE-LEVEL, DETAILED METADATA; AND RESEARCH PARTICIPANTS BENEFITING FROM ENHANCED DATA PRIVACY THROUGH REDUCED DISCLOSURE RISKS.
description.969: TOWSON UNIVERSITY, IN COLLABORATION WITH CENTRAL MICHIGAN UNIVERSITY (CMU) AND GEORGIA STATE UNIVERSITY (GSU), WILL DEVELOP A STUDENT-CENTERED OUTREACH MODEL FOR ACADEMIC ARCHIVES. THIS TWO-YEAR FORUM PROJECT INCLUDES A SERIES OF VIRTUAL FORUMS WITH STUDENTS, FACULTY, AND PRACTITIONERS TO DISCUSS STUDENT-CENTERED OUTREACH PROGRAMMING. THESE FORUMS WILL INFORM A DATA-DRIVEN, COST-EFFECTIVE, AND GENERALIZABLE STUDENT-CENTERED OUTREACH MODEL FOR ACADEMIC ARCHIVES THAT WILL BE DISSEMINATED TO LIBRARIANS, ARCHIVISTS, EDUCATORS, AND UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE STUDENT ENGAGEMENT WITH ARCHIVES, BENEFITING LIBRARIANS, ARCHIVISTS, EDUCATORS, AND STUDENTS NATIONWIDE. SUBRECIPIENT GSU WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT WITH ALL ASPECTS OF PLANNING AND FACILITATING THE FORUMS, AS WELL AS HIRE FOUR CONSULTANTS WHO WILL SERVE AS INCLUSION ADVOCATES FOR THE FORUMS. SUBRECIPIENT CMU ALSO WILL SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE FORUMS AS WELL AS DISSEMINATE PROJECT FINDINGS AND THE OUTREACH MODEL AT TWO PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCES.
description.970: THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND, COLLEGE PARK; THE MARYLAND STATE LIBRARY AGENCY; AND MULTIPLE COMMUNITY PARTNERS DEDICATED TO SUPPORTING CHILDREN AND FAMILIES WILL ADAPT AND EVALUATE THE ORIGINAL HATCHLING PROGRAM TO EMPOWER UNDER-RESOURCED NEW PARENTS TO ENGAGE THEIR BABIES IN EARLY LANGUAGE- AND LITERACY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES BOTH IN AND OUT OF THE LIBRARY. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CREATE A CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE ADAPTATION OF THE ORIGINAL HATCHLING CURRICULUM THAT BETTER MEETS THE NEEDS OF RACIALLY AND ETHNICALLY MARGINALIZED IDENTITIES, IMMIGRANTS, AND ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNERS. THE TEAM WILL THEN EVALUATE THE NEW PROGRAM’S EFFECTS ON PARENTS’ SELF-EFFICACY FOR BUILDING THEIR CHILD’S FOUNDATION OF LANGUAGE AND LITERACY SKILLS, THE NATURALISTIC HOME LANGUAGE ENVIRONMENT, AND FAMILY LIBRARY USE. THIS PROJECT WILL LEVERAGE THE COLLECTIVE, CROSS-DISCIPLINARY EXPERTISE OF LIBRARIANS, RESEARCHERS, EDUCATORS, NEUROSCIENTISTS, SPEECH LANGUAGE PATHOLOGISTS, CHILD DEVELOPMENT EXPERTS, AND OTHER PARTNERS TO ESTABLISH AN OPEN-ACCESS, FLEXIBLE, SCALABLE NATIONAL MODEL SUPPORTING THE FOUNDATIONS OF LANGUAGE AND LITERACY DEVELOPMENT IN YOUNG CHILDREN.
description.971: THE CONSORTIUM OF METROPOLITAN LIBRARIES (COBIMET) WILL PERFORM A DIGITAL PRESERVATION NEEDS ASSESSMENT FOR PUBLIC LIBRARIES AND MUNICIPAL ARCHIVES IN PUERTO RICO’S METROPOLITAN AREA USING THE DIGITAL PRESERVATION COALITION RAPID ASSESSMENT MODEL. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A BILINGUAL, FREE-TO-USE ONLINE DATABASE TO MAKE THE DATA PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE. THIS INITIATIVE AIMS TO ENHANCE DIGITAL PRESERVATION CAPABILITIES, BENEFITING NOT ONLY PUERTO RICO, BUT ALSO OTHER U.S. STATES AND TERRITORIES. KEY DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A COMPREHENSIVE NEEDS ASSESSMENT REPORT, A DATABASE SYSTEM, WEBINARS, AND A WHITE PAPER ON DIGITAL PRESERVATION BEST PRACTICES. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT LONG-TERM PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO PUERTO RICO’S DIGITAL CULTURAL HERITAGE AND HISTORICAL RECORDS.
description.972: THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH TEXAS WILL ENHANCE PUBLIC LIBRARY SERVICES FOR IMMIGRANTS IN TIMES OF CRISIS, STRENGTHEN THE RESILIENCE OF UNDER-RESOURCED IMMIGRANT GROUPS, AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE OVERALL WELL-BEING OF COMMUNITIES THROUGH RESEARCH. USING A MIX OF DATA-DRIVEN AND USER-STUDY METHODS, THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL INVESTIGATE THE INFORMATION NEEDS OF IMMIGRANTS IN UNDER-RESOURCED COMMUNITIES IN CRISIS; THE STATUS OF PUBLIC LIBRARY PRACTICE REGARDING INCLUSIVE SERVICES FOR IMMIGRANTS IN CRISIS; AND INCLUSIVE SERVICES THAT CAN BE RECOMMENDED FOR PUBLIC LIBRARIES TO ADDRESS GAPS IN IMMIGRANTS’ NEEDS IN CRISIS. THE PROJECT WILL PRODUCE AN ONLINE TOOLKIT FOR PUBLIC LIBRARIES THAT PROVIDES GUIDANCE ON IMMIGRANT-INCLUSIVE SERVICES, REPLICABLE SURVEY INSTRUMENTS, AND A NOVEL TRIANGULATION METHOD THAT COMBINES THE USE OF DATA-DRIVEN METHODS WITH USER STUDIES TO INVESTIGATE IMMIGRANTS’ INFORMATION NEEDS IN CRISIS IN UNDER-RESOURCED COMMUNITIES. THE STUDY WILL BETTER PREPARE LIBRARIES TO SUPPORT IMMIGRANT COMMUNITIES WITH CRISIS PREPAREDNESS, RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY, AS WELL AS PROMOTING COMMUNITY RESILIENCE.
description.973: ITHAKA S+R WILL EXAMINE THE NATIONAL LANDSCAPE OF LEGAL INFORMATION ACCESS FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE INCARCERATED, AS WELL AS THE CURRENT STATE OF LAW LIBRARIANSHIP IN FACILITATING LAW ACCESS FOR THE JUSTICE-IMPACTED POPULATION. THE GRANT WILL INVESTIGATE WHAT SERVICE MODELS DEPARTMENTS OF CORRECTIONS USE TO COMPLY WITH THEIR STATUTORY OBLIGATION TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO LEGAL INFORMATION TO INCARCERATED PERSONS; HOW THESE MODELS COMPARE, AND WHICH ARE MOST EFFECTIVE; HOW LAW LIBRARIANS FACILITATE ACCESS TO THE LAW FOR SYSTEM-IMPACTED INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES; AND WHAT TRAINING AND RESOURCES ARE NEEDED TO SUPPORT LAW LIBRARIANS IN PROVIDING EFFECTIVE AND EQUITABLE SERVICES. THE PROJECT SEEKS TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO THE LAW AND LEGAL INFORMATION AMONG PEOPLE WHO ARE INCARCERATED, AS WELL AS COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY THE LEGAL SYSTEM. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN INFORMATION ON BEST PRACTICES AND OUTCOMES REGARDING: 1) STRUCTURAL MODELS FOR ACCESSING AND USING LEGAL INFORMATION AND RESOURCES; AND 2) COORDINATING SERVICES AND TRAINING TO MAXIMIZE EQUITY IN ACCESS AND USE.
description.974: THE CALIFORNIA DIGITAL LIBRARY WILL EXPAND LIBRARY CARPENTRY (LC) ACTIVITIES, WHICH OFFER VITAL EDUCATION FOR LIBRARIANS OF VARIED BACKGROUNDS. BY PROVIDING FOUNDATIONAL CODING AND DATA SCIENCE SKILLS, LC WORKSHOPS ARE KEY TOOLS IN THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF LIBRARY SERVICES AND HAVE BECOME ESSENTIAL LIBRARIAN TRAINING. THIS PROJECT IS AN OPPORTUNITY FOR STRATEGIC REFLECTION AND ACTION TO SECURE A SCALABLE AND ADAPTABLE FUTURE FOR LC. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON TWO AREAS: EXPLORING SCALABLE MEMBERSHIP MODELS TAILORED TO THE NEEDS OF LIBRARIES AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS TO ENSURE ORGANIZATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY, AND CONVENING WORKING GROUPS COMPRISING LEADERS FROM ORGANIZATIONS INSPIRED OR INFLUENCED BY THE LARGER CARPENTRIES PROGRAM. THE WORK WILL ENHANCE LC, PRIORITIZING INCLUSIVITY, INNOVATION, AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY SO IT CAN CONTINUE TO OFFER THE TRAINING AND CURRICULA NECESSARY FOR LIBRARIANS TO CATER TO THE GROWING DATA NEEDS OF THEIR COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY.
description.975: THE QUEENS MEMORY PROJECT AT QUEENS PUBLIC LIBRARY WILL DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE RESOURCE GUIDE WITH CASE STUDIES DESIGNED TO EMPOWER PUBLIC LIBRARIES IN PRESERVING LOCAL HISTORY AND ENHANCE THEIR COMMUNITY ARCHIVING CAPABILITIES. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE LEVERAGING EXISTING COMMUNITY-DRIVEN ARCHIVING TOOLKITS AND OTHER PUBLISHED RESOURCES TO AUDIT QUEENS MEMORY’S DIVERSE ONGOING COLLABORATIONS WITH LOCAL COMMUNITY ARCHIVES PARTNERS TO FIND AREAS FOR EXPANSION AND IMPROVEMENT USING THE TECHNIQUES AND STRATEGIES PUT FORTH BY THE NATIONAL COMMUNITY OF BEST PRACTICE. BY GAINING PERSPECTIVE FROM OUTSIDE EXPERTISE, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE LOCAL PRACTICE IN QUEENS AND PROVIDE USEFUL EXAMPLES FOR CASE STUDIES TO BE PUBLISHED ALONG WITH A HELPFUL RESOURCE GUIDE FOR OTHERS ENGAGED, OR SEEKING TO ENGAGE, IN THIS WORK. IN ADDITION TO THE RESOURCE GUIDE AND CASE STUDIES, EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND ENHANCED DIGITAL ARCHIVING TOOLS. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PUBLIC LIBRARIANS, ARCHIVISTS, AND THEIR LOCAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS.
description.976: THE INTER-UNIVERSITY CONSORTIUM FOR POLITICAL AND SOCIAL RESEARCH (ICPSR) AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN WILL BUILD A STREAMING DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS PIPELINE TO ENHANCE THE FUNCTIONALITY OF THE SOCIAL MEDIA ARCHIVE (SOMAR). SOMAR AIMS TO BALANCE SOCIAL MEDIA DATA PRIVACY AND REUSE BY BUILDING AN ACTIVE DATA COLLECTION SYSTEM AND ENHANCING SEARCH AND ANALYSIS CAPABILITIES WITHIN SOMAR’S VIRTUAL DATA ENCLAVE. BEYOND THE PERIOD OF THE AWARD, THE DATASETS AND SERVICES GENERATED TO DEMOCRATIZE RESEARCHER ACCESS TO SOCIAL MEDIA DATA WILL REMAIN IN THE ICPSR ECOSYSTEM. THE PROJECT TEAM ALSO WILL PRODUCE CODE AND DOCUMENTATION THAT EMPOWER OTHER ARCHIVES TO ADAPT THESE TOOLS FOR THEIR OWN TECHNICAL INFRASTRUCTURES AND UNIQUE DATA CHALLENGES. THE PROJECT WILL TARGET SOCIAL SCIENCE RESEARCHERS WHO CAN EMPLOY SOCIAL MEDIA DATA AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODOLOGIES IN ANALYZING COMPLEX SOCIAL ISSUES NATIONALLY AND INTERNATIONALLY. THIS PROJECT FACILITATES RESEARCH INTO SIGNIFICANT SOCIAL PHENOMENA BY PROVIDING TOOLS FOR LARGE DATASET ANALYSIS WHILE ADDRESSING PRIVACY AND COMPUTATIONAL RESOURCE DISPARITIES.
description.977: THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH TEXAS DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION SCIENCE AND UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE APPLICABILITY OF LOCALLY RUN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS) TO ASSIST THE SUBJECT CATALOGING OF DIGITAL AND PRINT LIBRARY RESOURCES. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL ADDRESS BOTH HOW LLM-BASED MODELS CAN BE DEVELOPED TO GENERATE ACCURATE CATALOGING RESULTS, AS WELL AS HOW THEY CAN BE INTEGRATED INTO CATALOGING PROCEDURES TO ASSIST LIBRARY STAFF. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DEVELOP, ANALYZE, AND SHARE METHODOLOGIES AND CODE FOR THE LLM-BASED MODELS, INPUT AND OUTPUT DATA, SURVEY INSTRUMENTS, AND REPORTS. THE WORK WILL BUILD KNOWLEDGE FOR THE FUTURE DEVELOPMENT AND DEPLOYMENT OF LLM-BASED APPLICATIONS FOR CATALOGING, FURTHERING INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO DIGITAL COLLECTION MANAGEMENT ACROSS INSTITUTIONS AND THEREBY IMPROVING DISCOVERY AND ENSURING THE ACCESSIBILITY OF THESE RESOURCES FOR A BROAD, NATIONWIDE AUDIENCE OF POTENTIAL USERS.
description.978: THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS AT AUSTIN WILL EXPLORE LIBRARIES’ CURRENT AND POTENTIAL ROLE AS MENTAL HEALTH RESOURCES FOR EMERGING ADULTS (18–29 YEARS). USING SURVEYS, INTERVIEWS, AND PARTICIPATORY DESIGN METHODS, THE PROJECT TEA, WILL INVESTIGATE EMERGING ADULTS’ NEEDS FOR AND PRACTICES OF SEEKING HELP FOR MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS AND THEIR PERCEPTIONS OF PUBLIC AND ACADEMIC LIBRARIES AS INFORMATION AND COMMUNITY HUBS FOR MENTAL HEALTH HELP-SEEKING. THE TEAM ALSO WILL EXAMINE PUBLIC AND ACADEMIC LIBRARIANS’ PERCEIVED COMMUNITY NEEDS AROUND MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORT, EFFORTS, AND BARRIERS TO PROVIDING SUCH SUPPORT. FINALLY, THE TEAM WILL EXPLORE POTENTIAL LIBRARY PROGRAMS, SERVICES, AND TOOLS TO PROMOTE MENTAL HEALTH HELP-SEEKING. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A SOCIAL ECOLOGICAL MODEL OF SOURCES FOR MENTAL HEALTH HELP-SEEKING AMONG EMERGING ADULTS; A SOCIOTECHNICAL FRAMEWORK OF LIBRARY MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR EMERGING ADULTS; CASE STUDIES OF EXISTING LIBRARY PROGRAMS AND SERVICES; AND EXAMPLES OF POTENTIAL PROGRAMS AND SERVICES TO SUPPORT LIBRARIANS IN CREATING AND PLANNING MENTAL HEALTH INTERVENTIONS.
description.979: THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS BOARD OF TRUSTEES AND THE CHAMPAIGN-URBANA COMMUNITY FAB LAB, WITH THE AMERICAN LIBRARY ASSOCIATION, NATION OF MAKERS LIBRARY MAKERSPACES WORKING GROUP, AND LIBRARY MAKERS, WILL HOST A FORUM TO SOLIDIFY AND LEVERAGE CURRENT NETWORKS, PROJECTS, AND EXPERTISE IN LIBRARY MAKERSPACES (COLLABORATIVE WORK SPACES FOR MAKING, EXPLORING, LEARNING, AND SHARING) AND CHART FUTURE DIRECTIONS FOR ADVANCING LIBRARY MAKERSPACES. KEY STAKEHOLDERS ENCOMPASS LIBRARY MAKER PROFESSIONALS, PROSPECTIVE LIBRARY MAKER PROFESSIONALS, LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCES EDUCATORS, AND HIGHER EDUCATION RESEARCHERS. THROUGH ONLINE AND IN-PERSON FORUM ACTIVITIES, STAKEHOLDERS WILL ENGAGE IN DIALOGUE, REFLECT ON AND CONSOLIDATE EXISTING KNOWLEDGE, AND ENVISION THE FUTURE OF LIBRARY MAKERSPACES. THE INTENDED PROJECT RESULTS WILL BE A COLLABORATIVELY DEVELOPED VISION AND STRATEGIC DIRECTION FOR LIBRARY MAKERSPACES. THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE THE CAPACITY OF LIBRARY MAKERSPACES TO MEET THE EVOLVING NEEDS OF THEIR COMMUNITIES WHILE ADVANCING THE GOALS OF THE MAKER MOVEMENT ON A NATIONAL SCALE.
description.980: THE UNIVERSITY AT ALBANY LIBRARIES, WITH KANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY AND THE UNIVERSITY OF ALBANY COLLEGE OF EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS, HOMELAND SECURITY, AND CYBERSECURITY, WILL DIGITIZE AND EXPAND AN EXISTING INFORMATION LITERACY INSTRUCTION GAME AND CREATE AN ACCOMPANYING EDUCATOR GUIDE TO FACILITATE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE GAME AT ACADEMIC, SCHOOL, AND PUBLIC LIBRARIES. THE PROJECT WILL COLLABORATE WITH STUDENTS AND INSTRUCTORS IN THE INFORMATICS PROGRAM AT THE UNIVERSITY AT ALBANY TO DESIGN AND PROGRAM A WEB-BASED VERSION OF THE PRINT FORMAT GAME; CONDUCT INTERNAL TESTING WITH FOCUS GROUPS AT BOTH UNIVERSITIES; LAUNCH A BETA VERSION OF THE GAME FOR PROTOTYPE TESTING, USER EXPERIENCE TESTING, ACCESSIBILITY TESTING, AND TROUBLESHOOTING; CONDUCT AN ADDITIONAL ROUND OF FEEDBACK AND ITERATION; DEVELOP FACILITATION AND INSTRUCTION GUIDES ON USING THE GAME; AND LAUNCH THE FINAL VERSION OF THE GAME. THE GAME AND EDUCATOR GUIDE WILL BE MADE FREELY AVAILABLE TO ANYONE WHO WANTS TO INCORPORATE GAMIFICATION AND ACTIVE LEARNING INTO THEIR INFORMATION INSTRUCTION.
description.981: OLD DOMINION UNIVERSITY, WITH VIRGINIA TECH LIBRARIES, WILL EXPLORE HOW TO ENHANCE THE ACCESSIBILITY OF ELECTRONIC THESES AND DISSERTATIONS (ETDS) FOR BLIND AND LOW-VISION (BLV) LIBRARY USERS. THE CURRENT LIMITED ACCESSIBILITY OF ETDS POSES A SIGNIFICANT BARRIER TO BLV USERS’ ACADEMIC AND PROFESSIONAL PURSUITS, HINDERING THEIR ABILITY TO ENGAGE WITH SCHOLARLY RESEARCH AND CONTRIBUTE TO THEIR RESPECTIVE FIELDS. THIS PROJECT WILL CONDUCT EXPLORATORY USER STUDIES WITH DIVERSE BLV PARTICIPANT GROUPS TO UNCOVER THEIR ACCESSIBILITY BARRIERS, BEHAVIOR AND STRATEGIES, AND NEEDS AND PREFERENCES WHEN INTERACTING WITH ETDS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A REPORT ON THE RESEARCH, TECHNICAL, AND IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGES THAT NEED TO BE ADDRESSED TO MAKE ETDS MORE INCLUSIVE FOR BLV USERS; DESIGN REQUIREMENTS FOR FUTURE ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGIES TO INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY OF ETDS; AND PLATFORM-AGNOSTIC ACCESSIBILITY SUGGESTIONS FOR AUTHORS TO MAKE THEIR ETDS MORE USABLE FOR BLV USERS. IN ADDITION TO THE BLV COMMUNITY, THE OUTCOMES WILL BENEFIT STUDENTS, LIBRARY STAFF, ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPERS, AND ACCESSIBILITY RESEARCHERS.
description.982: OLD DOMINION UNIVERSITY WILL LEAD A TEAM INVESTIGATING HOW TO PRESERVE ENDANGERED OPEN ACCESS DATASETS AND SOFTWARE (OADS). OADS ARE PUBLICLY AND FREELY AVAILABLE DIGITAL DATASETS AND SOFTWARE PACKAGES USED FOR REPRODUCING RESEARCH RESULTS REPORTED IN SCHOLARLY PUBLICATIONS. RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF OADS ARE NOT PROPERLY ARCHIVED, WITH THE DISAPPEARANCE OF THESE OADS THREATENING SCIENTIFIC REPRODUCIBILITY ACROSS DISCIPLINES. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP, REPORT ON, AND SOLVE THE FOUNDATIONAL PROBLEMS RELATED TO THE VALUE, STATUS, TRENDS, AND PRESERVABILITY OF OADS IN SCHOLARLY PAPERS AND ELECTRONIC THESES AND DISSERTATIONS. THE TEAM WILL CHARACTERIZE OADS IN TERMS OF AVAILABILITY, OBSERVABILITY, AND ACCESSIBILITY. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL STUDY THE STATUS OF OADS PRESERVATION, DEVELOP PREDICTIVE MODELS FOR ENDANGERED OADS, AND EXPLORE THE TECHNICAL CHALLENGES OF PRESERVING OADS. INVESTIGATING THESE FOUNDATIONAL PROBLEMS RELATED TO OADS WILL BENEFIT EDUCATORS, STUDENTS, RESEARCHERS, DIGITAL ARCHIVISTS, AND LIBRARIANS ACROSS THE COUNTRY.
description.983: DREXEL UNIVERSITY’S COLLEGE OF COMPUTING AND INFORMATICS, IN COLLABORATION WITH OLD DOMINION UNIVERSITY’S DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER SCIENCE, WILL INVESTIGATE HOW BEST TO PRESERVE PERSONALIZED DIGITAL ADVERTISEMENTS VIEWED LIVE BY USERS. THESE ADVERTISEMENTS HAVE ELUDED CONVENTIONAL DIGITAL ARCHIVING METHODS AND ARE NOT TYPICALLY CAPTURED BY ARCHIVAL CRAWLERS. THIS TWO-YEAR APPLIED RESEARCH PROJECT WILL INFORM BEST PRACTICE GUIDELINES AND RECOMMENDATIONS, AS WELL AS THE DEVELOPMENT OF MORE EFFECTIVE TOOLS FOR BOTH RECONSTRUCTING ADS FROM PREVIOUSLY ARCHIVED CONTENT AND ARCHIVING FUTURE WEB CONTENT. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE PERSONA DEVELOPMENT, A DIVERSE DATASET OF ONLINE ADVERTISEMENTS, QUALITATIVE USER STUDIES, AND DISSEMINATION OF FINDINGS THROUGH FORMAL AND INFORMAL PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED DIGITAL ARCHIVING PRACTICES, ENHANCED HISTORICAL RECORDS, AND INCREASED ACCESS TO DIGITAL CULTURAL ARTIFACTS. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT RESEARCHERS, ARCHIVISTS, AND THE PUBLIC. SUBRECIPIENT OLD DOMINION UNIVERSITY WILL LEAD THE SECOND PHASE OF THE PROJECT: AN EVALUATION OF DATA CONCERNING WEB ARCHIVES’ HOLDINGS.
description.984: FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY’S SCHOOL OF INFORMATION WILL RESEARCH THE HIRING PRACTICES AND EVALUATIVE MEASURES OF SOCIAL WORKERS HIRED IN PUBLIC LIBRARIES. IN THE PAST DECADE, PUBLIC LIBRARIES AROUND THE COUNTRY HAVE INCREASINGLY HIRED SOCIAL WORKERS TO PROVIDE SPECIALIZED SERVICES TO THEIR PATRONS AND COMMUNITIES; HOWEVER, THERE HAVE BEEN NO NATIONAL STUDIES ON THIS TOPIC. THE PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE THE PRIMARY SKILLS SOUGHT IN HIRING SOCIAL WORKERS FOR LIBRARIES, AND HOW THESE ARE SKILLS THEN EVALUATED IN PRACTICE; THE SOCIAL NEEDS BEING ADDRESSED BY SOCIAL WORKERS IN LIBRARIES; AND THE PERCEPTIONS OF LIBRARY STAFF ABOUT THE EFFICACY OF SOCIAL WORKERS IN PUBLIC LIBRARIES. THIS RESEARCH WILL INFORM HIRING AND EVALUATION PROCESSES; CREATE A FRAMEWORK OF NEEDS AND PRACTICES FOR LIBRARY STAFF AND LIBRARY SOCIAL WORKERS; EXPOSE WHAT SOCIAL NEEDS OF LIBRARY USERS ARE NOT MET BY TRADITIONAL LIBRARY SERVICES; AND PROVIDE AN OVERVIEW OF THE NON-TRADITIONAL SKILLS THAT ARE NEEDED IN LIBRARIES.
description.985: NORTHWESTERN UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES WILL LEVERAGE THE POWER OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (GENAI) TO REVOLUTIONIZE THE WAY LIBRARIES PROVIDE ACCESS TO KNOWLEDGE. FIRST, THE PROJECT WILL BUILD AN INSTALLABLE, OPEN-SOURCE, SEMANTIC DISCOVERY PRODUCT THAT ALLOWS USERS TO CHAT WITH LIBRARY AND ARCHIVAL COLLECTIONS. SECOND, THE PROJECT WILL TEST AND VALIDATE A TOOLKIT TO AUGMENT METADATA FOR DIGITIZED COLLECTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT THE SEMANTIC CHAT-BASED DISCOVERY TOOL AND AN AUTOMATED METADATA TOOL USING EXISTING GENAI MODELS IN NORTHWESTERN’S DIGITAL COLLECTIONS. TO EXPAND IMPACT NATIONALLY, THE TEAM WILL DEVELOP TOOLKITS COMPRISING RESEARCH METHODS, EXAMPLES, DETAILED DOCUMENTATION, AND OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE PACKAGES SO LIBRARY PROFESSIONALS AND RESEARCHERS ACROSS THE COUNTRY CAN IMPLEMENT THE TOOLS IN THEIR OWN CONTEXTS. BY EXPONENTIALLY EXPANDING ACCESS TO, AND PROVIDING INTERPRETATION OF, INFORMATION FROM PRIMARY RESOURCES, THIS PROJECT WILL INCREASE LIBRARY ACCESS TO KNOWLEDGE AROUND AI TOOLS, ALLOWING LIBRARIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY TO ADAPT AND MEET RAPIDLY CHANGING EXPECTATIONS.
description.986: THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN–MADISON WILL INVESTIGATE MUSEUM AND LIBRARY PRACTITIONERS’ APPROACHES TO PLAY-BASED PROGRAMS AND SPACES AND CO-DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT MATERIALS FOCUSING ON EQUITY, ASSESSMENT, AND ADVOCACY FOR USE IN MUSEUMS AND LIBRARIES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONDUCT A LITERATURE REVIEW AND INTERVIEWS; CONVENE A COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE OF MUSEUMS AND LIBRARIES IN THREE DIVERSE WISCONSIN LOCATIONS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND SUPPORTING PLAY IN THEIR INSTITUTIONS AND CO-DESIGN MATERIALS; AND RECRUIT MUSEUMS AND LIBRARY PARTNERS IN OTHER PARTS OF THE U.S. TO TEST AND REFINE THE MATERIALS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A A DIVERSITY AUDIT TOOL FOR PRACTITIONERS TO EXAMINE THEIR PLAY PROGRAMS AND SPACES FOR DIVERSITY, EQUITY, INCLUSION, ACCESSIBILITY, AND BELONGING CONSIDERATIONS, AS WELL AS A TYPOLOGY OF EXISTING PLAY OFFERINGS FOCUSED ON THE FORMS, PURPOSES, MATERIALS, AND THEORETICAL UNDERPINNINGS OF PLAY THAT ARE SUPPORTED IN MUSEUMS AND LIBRARIES, WITH A SPECIFIC FOCUS ON PLAY OFFERINGS FOR CHILDREN AGES 0–12.
description.987: TOWSON UNIVERSITY’S ALBERT S. COOK LIBRARY, WITH BRANDEIS UNIVERSITY LIBRARY, WILL IMPLEMENT A COMMUNITY PROGRAM FOR EDUCATION ON HOLOCAUST DISINFORMATION, SUPPORTED BY JEWISH CULTURAL RECONSTRUCTION (JCR) BOOKS. THE JEWISH CULTURAL RECONSTRUCTION ORGANIZATION DISTRIBUTED APPROXIMATELY 160,000 OF THE OVER HALF A MILLION BOOKS, PERIODICALS, AND RITUAL OBJECTS THAT HAD BEEN SEIZED FROM JEWISH COMMUNITIES FOLLOWING WORLD WAR II. MANY, HOWEVER, REMAIN UNIDENTIFIED DUE TO INCONSISTENT CATALOGING PRACTICES. THE GRANT WILL DEVELOP, TEST, AND SHARE BEST PRACTICES AND DIGITAL TOOLS FOR BOOK IDENTIFICATION AND CATALOGING, AND PARTNER WITH MUSEUMS, SCHOOLS, UNIVERSITIES, AND OTHER CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS TO CREATE HOLOCAUST EDUCATION PROGRAMMING USING THESE BOOKS. OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE CEMENTED BEST PRACTICES FOR LOCATING, CATALOGING, AND DESCRIBING JCR BOOKS; A SHARED CATALOG OR DATABASE OF JCR MATERIALS; GUIDES AND BEST PRACTICES FOR REACHING OUT TO COMMUNITY MUSEUMS, INSTITUTIONS, AND PARTNERS REGARDING PROGRAM PARTICIPATION, INCLUDING SAMPLE MARKETING MATERIALS; AND A FOUNDATIONAL REPORT SUMMARIZING THE GRANT’S RESULTS.
description.988: THE PRIVATE ACADEMIC LIBRARY NETWORK OF INDIANA (PALNI) WILL COMPLETE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOTYPE OPEN-SOURCE READING LIST SYSTEM, PEARL, THAT CAN BE USED TO CREATE READING LISTS AND EMBED LINKS TO LIBRARY RESOURCES AND OPEN-ACCESS LEARNING MATERIALS WITHIN LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS (LMS). THE PROJECT TEAM WILL RELEASE AN OPEN-SOURCE TOOL THAT CAN CONNECT TO VARIOUS LIBRARY CATALOGS OR DISCOVERY SYSTEMS AND BE INTEGRATED INTO LMS USING THE LEARNING TOOLS INTEROPERABILITY™ STANDARD. THE PROTOTYPE’S CODE WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE AS AN OPEN-SOURCE PROJECT AND WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY DOCUMENTATION FOR INSTALLATION, CONFIGURATION, AND USE; A ROAD MAP FOR FUTURE DEVELOPMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY; AND A PROJECT WEB PAGE AND DOCUMENTATION TOOLKIT TO SUPPORT CONSORTIUM-LEVEL ADOPTION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SOFTWARE. THE PROJECT WILL HAVE FAR-REACHING IMPACT, AS DIVERSE LIBRARIES WILL BE ABLE TO INTEGRATE LIBRARY RESOURCES AND OPEN-ACCESS MATERIALS INTO THEIR LMS, BENEFITING STUDENTS IN VARIED HIGHER EDUCATION ENVIRONMENTS ACROSS THE COUNTRY.
description.989: THE 3D “DIGITAL HERBARIUM” IS A PILOTED, INTERACTIVE 3D DIGITAL EXHIBIT AND LEARNING SYSTEM THAT PROVIDES AN OPEN ACCESS ENVIRONMENT TO LEARN AND RESEARCH BOTANY. THE CAL POLY HUMBOLDT UNIVERSITY LIBRARY WILL TRANSFORM THIS PILOTED, INTERACTIVE LEARNING FRAMEWORK INTO AN OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE SOLUTION. THE PROJECT WILL BUILD A 3D “EXHIBITS4LEARNING” PROTOTYPE AS A CUSTOMIZABLE INTERACTIVE LEARNING SOFTWARE AVAILABLE FOR MANY DISCIPLINES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL PROVIDE PHOTOGRAMMETRY, 3D MODELING TRAINING, AND AN EASY-TO-USE 3D EXHIBIT PROTOTYPE FOR CURATING AND ANNOTATING COLLECTIONS TO PARTICIPATING INSTITUTIONS TO PROVIDE FEEDBACK. CODE REFINEMENT AND THOROUGH TRAINING DOCUMENTATION WILL SUPPORT 3D DIGITIZATION WORKFLOWS AND CURATION INTERESTS FOR INTERACTIVE EXHIBITS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. THIS INNOVATIVE FRAMEWORK WILL ADVANCE LEARNER ACCESS TO SPECIALIZED COLLECTIONS, SUPPORT PROJECT-BASED STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AROUND INVALUABLE SKILLS, AND EXPAND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS OFFERING MEANINGFUL LEARNING EXPERIENCES. LIBRARIES, ARCHIVES, MUSEUMS, AND UNIVERSITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY CAN BENEFIT FROM THIS NEW WAY OF PROVIDING ACCESS TO, AND ENHANCING STUDENT LEARNING WITH, 3D EXHIBIT COLLECTIONS.
description.990: THE UNIVERSITY AT ALBANY, SUNY, WITH THE EMPIRE STATE LIBRARY NETWORK (ESLN), WILL USE ARCLIGHT—A SOFTWARE PLATFORM FOR THE DISCOVERY AND ACCESS OF ARCHIVAL COLLECTIONS—TO DECREASE BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTING ARCHIVAL DISCOVERY AND DELIVERY SYSTEMS AND ENABLE UNDER-RESOURCED INSTITUTIONS TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO DIGITAL OBJECTS. ARCLIGHT WILL INTEGRATE DISCOVERY AND ACCESS TO DIGITAL MATERIALS, METADATA, AND FULL-TEXT CONTENT WITH ARCHIVAL DESCRIPTIONS. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL MODEL WITH THE ARCHIVES COMMUNITY, CREATING AN ARCHIVESSPACE PLUG-IN, AND PILOTING IT ACROSS INSTITUTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE DIGITAL COLLECTIONS ACCESS, REDUCE IMPLEMENTATION BARRIERS AND RESOURCE COSTS FOR SYSTEMS, AND ENABLE REPOSITORIES TO APPLY THE SAME METHODS AND BEST PRACTICES FOR LARGE VOLUMES OF PHYSICAL MATERIALS TO DIGITAL MATERIALS. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE ARCHIVAL REPOSITORIES OF ALL SIZES, AS WELL AS ARCHIVISTS AND RESEARCHERS. ESLN WILL FACILITATE COLLABORATIVE MEETINGS TO DEVELOP THE CONCEPTUAL MODEL, CONDUCT USABILITY TESTING, AND DEVELOP AND PUBLICIZE DOCUMENTATION AND RESULTS.
description.991: THE PARTNERSHIP FOR ACADEMIC LIBRARY COLLABORATION & INNOVATION (PALCI) AND THE PRIVATE ACADEMIC LIBRARY NETWORK OF INDIANA (PALNI) WILL STREAMLINE DEVELOPMENT AND ENSURE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF HYKU, A DIGITAL REPOSITORY SOFTWARE THAT PROVIDES A ROBUST AND FLEXIBLE PLATFORM FOR INSTITUTIONS TO MANAGE, PRESERVE, AND PROVIDE ACCESS TO DIGITAL CONTENT. WITH ACTIVE IMPLEMENTATION RANGING ACROSS FOUR LIBRARY CONSORTIA ENCOMPASSING MORE THAN 30 LIBRARIES, THE SCOPE OF SERVICE MEANS THAT A STRUCTURED DECISION-MAKING PROCESS AND FRAMEWORK HAVE BECOME INCREASINGLY CRITICAL. THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS HYKU’S NEEDS FOR FISCAL AND ORGANIZATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY, EFFICIENCY IN COLLABORATION, AND INCREASED CAPACITY ACROSS PROJECTS SERVING SMALL, LESS-FUNDED INSTITUTIONS. WITH COMMUNITY INPUT AND BUY-IN, THE PROJECT’S DELIVERABLES WILL PROVIDE A FIRM FINANCIAL PLAN, DEFINE WORKING PRACTICES, BUILD EXPERIENCE IN COLLABORATION ACROSS ORGANIZATIONS, AND ADD HUMAN RESOURCES TO SUSTAIN THE HYKU PLATFORM. THE PROJECT WILL ENSURE THE HYKU SOFTWARE’S FUTURE, MEETING LIBRARIES’ NEED FOR AN AFFORDABLE, EASY-TO-USE, MULTI-TENANT DIGITAL REPOSITORY SOLUTION.
description.992: THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAIʻI WILL CONDUCT A ONE-YEAR PLANNING PROJECT TO BETTER SERVE THE RESEARCH NEEDS OF NATIVE HAWAIIAN HULA PRACTITIONERS AND WORK TOWARD IMPROVING RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES AND CULTURAL HERITAGE INSTITUTIONS WITH INDIGENOUS DANCE COLLECTIONS. THE TEAM WILL CONVENE AN ADVISORY BOARD TO ENSURE CULTURAL AND PROFESSIONAL RIGOR IN PROJECT OUTCOMES, CONDUCT FOCUS GROUPS WITH HULA PRACTITIONERS AND INSTITUTIONS HOLDING HULA COLLECTIONS, AND ADMINISTER SURVEYS IN ORDER TO CO-CREATE A STRATEGIC PLAN TO IMPROVE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN HULA PRACTITIONERS AND INSTITUTIONS. OTHER DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE A COMPREHENSIVE DIRECTORY OF HULA COLLECTIONS AND A REPORT OUTLINING PRIORITY RESEARCH SUPPORT NEEDS FOR HULA PRACTITIONERS AND DOCUMENTING THE CURRENT STATE OF COLLECTION MANAGEMENT, DESCRIPTION, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR HULA COLLECTIONS. THE PROJECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE NATIVE HAWAIIAN COMMUNITIES, HULA PRACTITIONERS, AND LIBRARY AND ARCHIVES PROFESSIONALS STEWARDING INDIGENOUS DANCE COLLECTIONS.
description.993: THE SEATTLE ART MUSEUM WILL EXPAND ITS EARLY LEARNER INITIATIVE KNOWN AS ARTFUL BEGINNINGS TO CREATE INCREASED OPPORTUNITIES FOR HANDS-ON ARTS LEARNING AND ENGAGEMENT FOR CHILDREN AGES 2 THROUGH 6, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND EDUCATORS. THE FOCUS IS ON THREE CORE ARTFUL BEGINNINGS PROGRAMS: TINY TOTS WORKSHOPS AND FAMILY FUN STORYTIME, ART ADVENTURES, AND AN ART-BASED OUTDOOR PRESCHOOL CURRICULUM WITH TINY TREES. THE MUSEUM?S THREE LOCATIONS - AS WELL AS COMMUNITY PARTNER FACILITIES IN SOUTH SEATTLE AND SOUTH KING COUNTY ? WILL HOST THE PROGRAMS. PROGRAMMING WILL FOCUS ON ENGAGING TRADITIONALLY UNDERSERVED AND LOWER-INCOME AUDIENCES. THE PROJECT UNDERSCORES THE MUSEUM?S COMMITMENT TO EQUITY AND INCLUSION AND WILL WORK TO ENGAGE ALL AUDIENCES MORE DEEPLY.
description.994: THE MUSEUM OF SCIENCE AND INDUSTRY WILL INCREASE THE GENERAL PUBLIC?S ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTION BY CREATING A NEW ONLINE CATALOG ACCESSIBLE THROUGH THE MUSEUM?S WEBSITE. THEY WILL UPDATE THE COLLECTION DATABASE, CREATE THE ONLINE COLLECTION CATALOG, AND DEVELOP AN INFRASTRUCTURE TO ALLOW FOR REGULAR UPDATES OVER TIME. WHEN LAUNCHED, THE DIGITAL COLLECTION WILL INCLUDE A ROBUST SEARCH ENGINE, CURATED ARTIFACT ?SETS,? AND HIGH-RESOLUTION 360-DEGREE PHOTOGRAPHY. THE MUSEUM?S COLLECTION OF EXHIBITS IS AN ANTHROPOLOGICAL REVIEW OF INDUSTRY AND INGENUITY OVER TIME. THIS PROJECT WILL MAKE A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF THE COLLECTION AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC FOR THE VERY FIRST TIME.
description.995: THE NEW ENGLAND AQUARIUM WILL CREATE CONSERVATION STEM - AN ONLINE CURRICULUM THAT FEATURES ENGAGING VIDEOS AND HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES ALIGNED WITH STATE AND NATIONAL STANDARDS THAT ARE EASILY ACCESSIBLE FOR TEACHERS TO USE IN THE CLASSROOM.
