THE DATABASE WILL CREATE A FOUNDATION THAT ENABLES FURTHER DISEASE RESEARCH, EVALUATION OF POPULATION HEALTH, AND INTEGRATION WITH MEDICAL RECORD KEEPING SOFTWARE, SUPPORTING THE CONTINUED STEWARDSHIP OF LIVING COLLECTIONS AND SPECIES SUSTAINABILITY.
description.1091: THE METROPOLITAN MUSEUM OF ART WILL RESEARCH IMPROVEMENTS TO CALIBRATE TESTS COMMONLY USED TO IDENTIFY MATERIALS TO STORE, DISPLAY, AND TRANSPORT MUSEUM COLLECTIONS AND THEN DEVELOP A LIST OF HARMFUL CHEMICALS AND THEIR DAMAGE THRESHOLDS FOR CULTURAL HERITAGE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE HIRING TWO PH.D. LEVEL RESEARCHERS ALONG WITH TWO CONTRACTORS WHO WILL HELP DEVELOP BENCHMARKING PROTOCOLS AND THEN TEST MATERIALS USING THE NEW PROTOCOLS. RESULTS WILL BE PUBLISHED TO THE MATERIALS TESTING WIKI, AN ONLINE RESOURCE CONTAINING TEST DATA AND GENERAL INFORMATION ABOUT MATERIALS TESTING MAINTAINED BY THE AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF CONSERVATION, ENSURING OPEN-SOURCE ACCESS FOR THE MUSEUM AND CONSERVATION COMMUNITY. THE STANDARDIZATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE CRITERIA AND TOOLS THE MUSEUM FIELD USES TO TEST MATERIALS THAT COME IN CONTACT WITH COLLECTIONS WILL BENEFIT THE COLLECTION MANAGEMENT PRACTICES OF ALL TYPES OF MUSEUMS.
description.1092: THE ROCHESTER INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY (RIT) WILL RESEARCH MUSEUM INTERACTIONS WITH 3D PRINTING, SPECIFICALLY 3D-PRINTED OBJECTS ENTERING COLLECTIONS OR USED FOR PRESERVATION ACTIVITIES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES, LED BY STAFF AND A GRADUATE STUDENT WORKER AT THE IMAGE PERMANENCE INSTITUTE AT RIT, INCLUDE A NATIONAL SURVEY TO DOCUMENT THE EXTENT OF MUSEUM ENGAGEMENT WITH 3D PRINTING, CREATION OF A WEB-BASED RESOURCE TO PRESERVE 3D-PRINTED OBJECTS, DEVELOPMENT OF TWO RESEARCH AGENDAS, AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF 3D-PRINTED RESEARCH COLLECTIONS. THE RESOURCES DEVELOPED FROM THIS RESEARCH WILL BETTER PREPARE THE GLOBAL COMMUNITY OF MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS RESPONSIBLE FOR PRESERVING OBJECTS CREATED BY THESE EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES.
description.1093: THE DISCOVERY CENTER AT MURFREE SPRING, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SIX SCIENCE CENTERS AND MUSEUMS, WILL PROMOTE AND INVEST IN SCIENCE EDUCATION IN RURAL COMMUNITIES WITH LIMITED MUSEUM ACCESS. THIS COALITION WILL WORK WITH TWO COHORTS OF RURAL SCHOOL COMMUNITIES (12 TOTAL) AND FOCUS ON ENGAGING, LEARNING FROM, AND SUPPORTING RURAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS, TEACHERS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES THROUGH RELATIONSHIP BUILDING, ASSET MAPPING, AND THE COLLABORATIVE INTEGRATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MUSEUM RESOURCES. ADDITIONAL ACTIVITIES INCLUDE THE PRODUCTION OF PUBLICATIONS, VIRTUAL PRESENTATIONS, AND A VIRTUAL TOOL KIT. THE PROJECT WILL ILLUSTRATE THE WAYS IN WHICH MUSEUMS CAN COLLABORATE TO SUPPORT STEM AND LITERACY AT THE K-2 LEVEL, ENHANCE TEACHER SELF-EFFICACY, ATTITUDES AND BELIEFS, AND ENGAGE FAMILY AND COMMUNITY, STRENGTHENING SERVICES FOR AMERICANS WHO LIVE IN THE MOST RURAL AREAS.
description.1094: THE DENVER BOTANIC GARDENS, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE AMERICAN PUBLIC GARDENS ASSOCIATION, WILL DEVELOP RESOURCES THAT ADDRESS THE CONTINUED NEEDS AND BARRIERS THAT LIMIT THE ADVANCE OF DIVERSITY, EQUITY, ACCESS, AND INCLUSION (DEAI) WORK IN PUBLIC GARDENS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING A NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND ASSET INVENTORY, DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING A DEAI PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR GARDEN PROFESSIONALS, ESTABLISHING TWO COHORTS OF TEN PUBLIC GARDENS TO PARTICIPATE IN THE TRAINING, AND SUPPORTING TEN PAID STUDENT INTERNSHIPS FOR TRADITIONALLY MARGINALIZED APPLICANTS AT PUBLIC GARDENS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL RESULT IN NEW MODELS AND TOOLS FOR PUBLIC GARDENS STAFF TO ADVANCE DEAI WORK, MAKING THEIR ORGANIZATIONS BETTER PREPARED TO WELCOME AND SUPPORT STAFF OF DIVERSE BACKGROUNDS.
description.1095: THE ASSOCIATION OF AFRICAN AMERICAN MUSEUMS WILL CONDUCT THE FIRST SALARY SURVEY FOCUSED ON PEOPLE WHO WORK, OR RECENTLY WORKED, IN AFRICAN AMERICAN MUSEUMS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL WORK WITH A RESEARCH FIRM TO DEVELOP THE SURVEY INSTRUMENT, TEST IT WITH A SAMPLE OF MUSEUMS, AND THEN LAUNCH THE FULL SURVEY. FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE DATA THAT INFORMS TWO RESEARCH QUESTIONS: 1) WHETHER STAFF AT AFRICAN AMERICAN MUSEUMS DO NOT HAVE COMPENSATION EQUITY WITH THEIR COUNTERPARTS AT OTHER, PREDOMINANTLY WHITE MUSEUMS, AND 2) WHETHER LOW SALARIES ARE LEADING TO HIGH STAFF TURNOVER. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL PUBLISH RESEARCH FINDINGS WIDELY AND, IF THE SURVEY RESULTS SHOW THAT THE HYPOTHESES ARE CORRECT, THEY WILL CREATE A TOOLKIT TO HELP AFRICAN AMERICAN MUSEUMS CREATE MORE EQUITABLE COMPENSATION FOR THEIR STAFF.
description.1096: THE IMAGE PERMANENCE INSTITUTE AT THE ROCHESTER INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY WILL RESEARCH APPROACHES THAT HELP SUPPORT THE PHYSICAL STABILITY OF PLASTICS AND PLASTIC COMPOSITE MATERIALS IN MUSEUM COLLECTIONS. OBJECTS SUCH AS MODERN AND CONTEMPORARY ARTWORKS, DESIGN, FASHION, AND ETHNOGRAPHIC ITEMS OFTEN INCLUDE PLASTICS, AS DO THE STORAGE MATERIALS USED FOR PHOTOGRAPHS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL USE MULTIPLE TYPES OF ANALYSES, INCLUDING A CASE STUDY, TO ASSESS THE EFFECT OF MICROSCOPIC CHANGES IN HUMIDITY ON THE PHYSICAL STRUCTURE OF TWO TYPES OF PLASTICS COMMONLY FOUND IN MUSEUM COLLECTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH SAFE PRESERVATION AND HANDLING CONDITIONS FOR THESE PLASTICS, SPECIFICALLY TEMPERATURE AND RELATIVE HUMIDITY. THEY WILL SHARE FINDINGS THROUGH JOURNAL ARTICLES, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, AND A WEB PUBLICATION.
description.1097: COSI WILL LEAD A MULTI-SITE RESEARCH PROJECT TO EXPLORE MUSEUM VISITORS’ MOTIVATIONS, EXPECTATIONS, AND SATISFACTION, WHICH WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS TO SUPPORT THE DESIGN OF VISITOR-CENTERED EXPERIENCES IN MUSEUMS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DEVELOP, REFINE, AND TEST RESEARCH INSTRUMENTS, AND THEN WILL WORK WITH FOUR MUSEUMS, INCLUDING A SCIENCE CENTER, HISTORY PARK, ZOO, AND AN ART MUSEUM, TO GATHER DATA ABOUT THEIR VISITORS’ EXPERIENCES. THEY WILL COMPARE THE SPECIFIC SITE FINDINGS TO THOSE INSTITUTIONS’ UNDERSTANDINGS OF THE SAME EXPERIENCES. REPRESENTATIVES FROM ALL FOUR SITES WILL DISCUSS THE FINDINGS DURING A REMOTE CONVENING, AND COSI WILL SHARE RESEARCH RESULTS THROUGH A PEER-REVIEWED JOURNAL ARTICLE AND PRESENTATIONS AT CONFERENCES. THE MUSEUM WILL MAKE RESEARCH INSTRUMENTS AVAILABLE THROUGH A DIGITAL TOOLKIT.
description.1098: THE MORTON ARBORETUM WILL LEAD A RESEARCH PROJECT TO SUPPORT ENHANCED MANAGEMENT OF BOTANIC GARDEN METACOLLECTIONS, WHICH ARE THE COMBINED COLLECTIONS OF MANY SEPARATE INSTITUTIONS STEWARDED COLLABORATIVELY TO ACHIEVE BROADER RESEARCH AND CONSERVATION PURPOSES. A CENTRAL CHALLENGE FOR METACOLLECTIONS IS TO EFFICIENTLY AND EFFECTIVELY MANAGE GENETIC DIVERSITY OF HUNDREDS OR THOUSANDS OF PLANTS PER SPECIES ACROSS NUMEROUS INSTITUTIONS. THE PROJECT TEAM INCLUDES 13 PARTNER INSTITUTIONS THAT WILL ADDRESS RESEARCH-FOCUSED OBJECTIVES TO DETERMINE WHEN GIS-BASED METRICS OF COLLECTION BREADTH ARE RELIABLE FOR DECISION MAKING; WHICH ACCESSIONS ARE MOST AND LEAST SECURE, REQUIRING DIFFERENT LEVELS OF CARE; AND HOW HYBRIDIZATION VARIES AMONG SPECIES AND INSTITUTIONS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL SHARE RESULTS THROUGH WEBINARS FOCUSED ON REACHING CURATORS OF LIVING PLANT COLLECTIONS. THE RESEARCH FINDINGS WILL SUPPORT INFORMED DECISION-MAKING LEADING TO INCREASED GENETIC DIVERSITY IN BOTANIC GARDEN COLLECTIONS.
description.1099: MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY WILL LEAD A MULTI-SITE RESEARCH PROJECT TO SUPPORT THE COLLECTIONS CARE AND MANAGEMENT OF AT-RISK AMPHIBIANS IN IMMEDIATE DANGER OF EXTINCTION. THE PROJECT TEAM INCLUDES 23 PARTNER INSTITUTIONS THAT WILL DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE NEW TOOLS TO FACILITATE THE PRESERVATION AND SHARING OF BIOMATERIALS FROM THREATENED AMPHIBIANS FOR THEIR GENETIC MANAGEMENT; TRAIN ZOO STAFF AND STUDENTS ON BIOMATERIAL PRESERVATION OF REPRODUCTIVE MATERIALS; AND CONDUCT FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH ON A ONE-PLAN APPROACH THAT LINKS THE CONSERVATION OF POPULATIONS IN THE WILD AND IN ZOOLOGICAL FACILITIES THROUGH BIOMATERIAL BANKING FOR IMPROVED SUSTAINABILITY. PROJECT FINDINGS WILL HELP REDUCE THE RISK OF POPULATION COLLAPSE OF THE LIVING COLLECTIONS AND MAXIMIZE GENETIC DIVERSITY THROUGH STORAGE OF KEY REPRODUCTIVE CELLS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL SHARE RESULTS IN PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS, CONFERENCES, VIDEO TUTORIALS, PODCASTS, WEBSITES, AND SOCIAL MEDIA AS WELL AS THROUGH ADVANCED TRAINING WORKSHOPS.
description.1100: THE CONSERVATION CENTER FOR ART AND HISTORIC ARTIFACTS WILL PARTNER WITH LYRASIS TO DEVELOP A SUITE OF RESOURCES TO SUPPORT SUCCESSION PLANNING FOR COLLECTIONS CARE STAFF AND RELATED VOLUNTEER POSITIONS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL BEGIN WITH LISTENING SESSIONS WITH MUSEUMS, LIBRARIES, AND ARCHIVES TO LEARN ABOUT THE NUANCES OF SUCCESSION PLANNING STRATEGIES. FINDINGS WILL INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS SUCH AS TECHNICAL BULLETINS, RESOURCE LISTS, CHECKLISTS, FACT SHEETS, INFOGRAPHICS, BIBLIOGRAPHIES, AND VIDEOS. THE CENTER WILL OFFER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TO PRESENT STRATEGIES TO PREPARE FOR STAFFING TRANSITIONS AND WILL DISSEMINATE MATERIALS ONLINE AND THROUGH CONFERENCE SESSIONS AND WEBINARS. THE PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO ASSIST MUSEUM LEADERSHIP AND GOVERNING BODIES IN UNDERSTANDING THE COMPLEXITY OF COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT AND STEWARDSHIP ROLES, TO SUPPORT MUSEUM LEADERS IN FOSTERING GROWTH IN THESE POSITIONS, AND TO HELP ENSURE THE CONTINUITY OF CARE FOR MUSEUM COLLECTIONS.
description.1101: THE FOUNDATION FOR ADVANCEMENT IN CONSERVATION WILL INCORPORATE USER FEEDBACK TO DEVELOP NEW FEATURES FOR ITS WEB-BASED CONNECTING TO COLLECTIONS CARE (C2C) RESOURCE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE DEVELOPING 33 NEW WEBINARS AND SIX ONLINE COURSES WITH ENHANCED ACCESSIBILITY THROUGH THE ADDITION OF CLOSED-CAPTIONING AND TRANSCRIPTIONS IN ENGLISH AND SPANISH. SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS WILL MONITOR ONLINE FORUMS TO ENSURE PROMPT ANSWERS AND TRUSTED ADVICE FOR PARTICIPANTS. TECHNICAL IMPROVEMENTS TO THE C2C WEBSITE WILL ENHANCE SEARCH FUNCTIONALITY, ENSURE ADA COMPLIANCE, AND MAKE IT MOBILE-ADAPTIVE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL MEASURE SUCCESS THROUGH INDIVIDUAL PROGRAM SURVEYS, PARTICIPATION DATA, AND A USER NEEDS ASSESSMENT. PARTICIPATION AT STATE, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL MUSEUM CONFERENCES WILL BUILD AWARENESS FOR THE C2C RESOURCE. THE PROJECT WILL PARTICULARLY BENEFIT ORGANIZATIONS WITH LIMITED PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT BUDGETS BY ENHANCING THEIR KNOWLEDGE OF COLLECTIONS CARE PRACTICES.
description.1102: THE ASSOCIATION OF CHILDREN’S MUSEUMS WILL CONDUCT A RESEARCH PROJECT TO INVESTIGATE PROMISING PRACTICES FOR VIRTUAL PROGRAMS OFFERED BY CHILDREN’S MUSEUMS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES, CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH TWO RESEARCH FIRMS, WILL INCLUDE COLLECTING DATA FROM CHILDREN’S MUSEUMS TO ASSESS VIRTUAL PROGRAMMING ASSETS AS WELL AS FROM PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND EDUCATORS TO IDENTIFY AUDIENCE NEEDS. FINDINGS WILL INFORM THE CREATION OF A PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TOOL THAT IDENTIFIES KEY ASPECTS OF EFFECTIVE VIRTUAL PROGRAMS. THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT, THE TEAM WILL DISSEMINATE RESEARCH FINDINGS THROUGH A SERIES OF 18 ONLINE REPORTS. THE PROJECT TEAM ALSO WILL DEVELOP A WIREFRAME OF AN ONLINE PLATFORM WHERE CHILDREN’S MUSEUMS CAN SHARE VIRTUAL PROGRAMS WITH ONE ANOTHER AND THE PUBLIC. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN DATA AND TOOLS THAT CHILDREN’S MUSEUMS CAN USE TO ENSURE THAT THEIR VIRTUAL PROGRAMMING BEST MEETS THE NEEDS OF THEIR COMMUNITIES.
description.1103: THE INTERNATIONAL COALITION OF SITES OF CONSCIENCE WILL WORK WITH 10 PARTNER MUSEUMS TO CREATE A SUITE OF TOOLS TO HELP MUSEUMS SYSTEMATICALLY IDENTIFY AND DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE ABSENCES IN REPRESENTATION IN THEIR OPERATIONS AND IN THEIR COLLECTIONS AND PROGRAMS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DEVELOP FRAMEWORKS TO ASSESS COLLECTIONS, PROGRAMMING, AND EMPLOYMENT AND OPERATIONS POLICIES, AS WELL AS COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS. WITH THE SUPPORT OF A MENTOR, EACH MUSEUM WILL STRENGTHEN RELATIONSHIPS WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS BY DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING PLANS TO ADDRESS MISSING NARRATIVES IN THEIR INSTITUTIONS. EACH MUSEUM WILL PRODUCE A PUBLIC PROGRAM OR EXHIBIT ABOUT THEIR WORK. PROJECT OUTPUTS WILL INCLUDE A REPORT, A SERIES OF WEBINARS, A TOOLKIT, AND ARTICLES IN PEER-REVIEWED JOURNALS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS WITH SKILLS TO PROACTIVELY EXPAND THE STORIES THEIR MUSEUMS TELL THROUGH NEW PROGRAMMING AND EXHIBITIONS.
description.1104: CHILDREN’S MUSEUM OF PITTSBURGH (CMP) WILL USE A PARTICIPATORY DESIGN RESEARCH APPROACH TO IDENTIFY AND REINVENT EDUCATIONAL PRACTICES THAT HINDER A SENSE OF BELONGING AMONG MINORITIZED VISITORS AND STAFF. THE PROJECT WILL BEGIN WITH AN EQUITY AUDIT OF CURRENT AND HISTORIC INSTITUTIONAL PRACTICES AT BOTH CMP AND THE MADISON CHILDREN’S MUSEUM. WORKING GROUPS AT EACH SITE WILL ENGAGE WITH OTHER PARTNERS, USING THE FINDINGS TO DEVELOP A PRELIMINARY FRAMEWORK OF LEARNING PRACTICES FOCUSED ON BELONGING. THEY THEN WILL CONDUCT EXPERIMENTS DESIGNED TO OPERATIONALIZE THE LEARNING PRACTICES AND USE WORKSHOPS WHERE RESEARCHERS, EDUCATORS, AND YOUNG PEOPLE SWAP ROLES AND WORK TOGETHER TO STUDY, REVISE, AND LEAD EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES THAT ENACT THE LEARNING PRACTICES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DISSEMINATE A TOOLKIT OF RESEARCH ACTIVITIES THAT OTHER SITES CAN USE TO CREATE COLLABORATIVELY DEFINED LEARNING PRACTICES THAT HELP MORE LEARNERS TO THRIVE.
description.1105: THE AMERICAN ALLIANCE OF MUSEUMS WILL EMBED THE PRINCIPLES OF DIVERSITY, EQUITY, ACCESSIBILITY, AND INCLUSION (DEAI) INTO ITS FIELDWIDE ASSESSMENT AND ACCREDITATION PROGRAMS AND RELATED STANDARDS AND ETHICS FOR MUSEUMS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE ASSESSMENT OF EXISTING PROGRAMS AND PROVIDING CLEAR GUIDANCE AND TRAINING FOR MUSEUM STAFF AND VOLUNTEERS ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROGRAMS. A RESEARCH FIRM WILL ANALYZE DEMOGRAPHIC AND SOCIAL FACTORS OF THE PROGRAMMING TO IDENTIFY VARIANCES IN PROGRAM OUTCOMES. A TASK FORCE WILL USE THE RESULTS TO RECOMMEND CHANGES, WHICH PROJECT STAFF AND BODIES SUCH AS THE ACCREDITATION COMMISSION MAY INCORPORATE INTO STANDARDS, PEER REVIEWER TRAINING, AND RELATED ASSESSMENT PROGRAMMING. THE ASSOCIATION WILL SHARE PROGRESS THROUGH STATUS REPORTS, BLOG POSTS, AND CONFERENCE SESSIONS. A PROJECT EVALUATION WILL PROVIDE A MODEL FOR OTHER ORGANIZATIONS WORKING THROUGH A MULTI-YEAR, SYSTEM-WIDE PROCESS TO EMBED DEAI FUNDAMENTALS AT A STRUCTURAL LEVEL.
description.1106: THE ONEIDA INDIAN NATION WILL USE FUNDS FOR THE LIBRARY ADMINISTRATOR'S SALARY TO CONTINUE EXISTING OPERATIONS AND MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR THE COMMUNITY. LOCATED IN THE RAY ELM CHILDREN & ELDERS CENTER IN THE NATION'S VILLAGE OF THE WHITE PINES HOUSING COMMUNITY, THE ONEIDA NATION LIBRARY WILL PROVIDE OUTREACH TO THEIR USER BASE INCLUDING PROVIDING CHILDREN AND THEIR CAREGIVERS ASSOCIATED WITH THE EARLY LEARNING CENTER WITH WEEKLY THEMATIC BOOKS AND PROVIDING SENIORS WITH MATERIALS TO HELP MAINTAIN MENTAL SHARPNESS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE ONEIDA INDIAN NATION COMMUNITY WITH AN EMPHASIS ON CHILDREN FROM THE EARLY LEARNING CENTER, ELDERS, AND NATION EMPLOYEES.
description.1107: THE PONCA TRIBE OF NEBRASKA WILL SUPPORT ITS EXISTING LIBRARY OPERATIONS AND MAINTAIN ITS CORE LIBRARY SERVICES ACROSS FIVE LOCATIONS WITHIN THEIR FIFTEEN COUNTIES OF SERVICE AREA FOR THEIR TRIBE. FUNDING WILL SUPPORT THE PURCHASE OF NEW BOOKS, SUBSCRIPTION RENEWALS, AND LIBRARY FURNITURE AS NEEDED TO CREATE WELCOMING LIBRARY SPACES. THE LIBRARY OFFERS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, HEALTHCARE, EDUCATION, AND CULTURAL RESOURCES TO HELP COMMUNITY MEMBERS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THEIR COMMUNITY MEMBERS WITHIN THEIR SERVICE DELIVERY AREA.
description.1108: THE CATAWBA NATION'S COMMUNITY LIBRARY AND ARCHIVES WILL PURCHASE BOOKS AND OTHER LIBRARY COLLECTIONS TO PRESERVE, PROMOTE, AND MAINTAIN CULTURAL AND HISTORICAL COLLECTIONS REGARDING THE CATAWBA PEOPLE. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE SALARY SUPPORT FOR THE TRIBAL ARCHIVIST TO ENHANCE EXISTING OPERATIONS. CATAWBA COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND RESEARCHERS ALIKE WILL BENEFIT FROM BOTH THE MATERIALS AND STAFF EXPERTISE MADE AVAILABLE THROUGH THIS PROJECT. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE IMPROVED CORE LIBRARY AND ARCHIVAL MATERIALS AND SERVICES FOR THE CATAWBA PEOPLE.
description.1109: THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF PORT LIONS WILL PURCHASE CHILDREN’S BOOKS AND OTHER LIBRARY SUPPLIES, PROVIDE INTERNET ACCESS, AND SUPPORT THE SALARY OF THE TRIBAL LIBRARIAN TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES AND ENHANCE EXISTING OPERATIONS FOR ITS COMMUNITY. THE COMMUNITY HAS A LARGE POPULATION OF PREKINDERGARTEN CHILDREN AND SO THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PURCHASE AN EARLY EDUCATION LITERACY STATION TO ASSIST WITH EARLY LITERACY AND DIGITAL SKILLS FOR YOUNG CHILDREN IN THE COMMUNITY. THE FOCUS OF THE PROJECT FOR THE YEAR WILL BE TO ENHANCE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES THROUGH THE TRIBAL LIBRARY. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT NATIVE VILLAGE OF PORT LIONS COMMUNITY MEMBERS.
description.1110: THE CRAIG TRIBAL ASSOCIATION HISTORICAL LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE LIBRARY SUPPLIES, FURNITURE, AND BOOKS TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. THE TRIBAL HISTORIC LIBRARY ENDEAVORS TO CONNECT THE CRAIG TRIBAL ASSOCIATION TRIBAL CITIZENS AND THE PRINCE OF WALES COMMUNITY TO LIBRARY AND ARCHIVAL MATERIALS RICH IN TRADITIONS, CULTURES, AND LANGUAGE OF ALASKA'S FIRST PEOPLES TO WIDEN THE WORLD VIEW OF THEIR COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND ENHANCE LEARNING. THE GOAL OF THESE PROJECTS IS TO PROVIDE MATERIALS AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT FOR TRIBAL CITIZENS AS WELL AS THE 5,200 RESIDENTS OF COMMUNITIES LOCATED AROUND THE ISLAND.
description.1111: THE TONKAWA TRIBE OF OKLAHOMA WILL MAKE AVAILABLE TO THE COMMUNITY, LIBRARY PROGRAMMING IN THE FORM OF A COMPUTER LAB, AFTERSCHOOL TUTORING, COMPUTER SUPPLIES, NEW BOOKS AND MAGAZINES. THE PROGRAMMING WILL INCORPORATE A DAY TRIP TO ONE OF THE AREA SCIENCE MUSEUMS TO HELP CHILDREN HAVE ACCESS TO A SPACE WHERE THEY CAN LEARN TO USE THEIR CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS AND PROBLEM SOLVING. THE TONKAWA TRIBE PLANS TO DO MORE STORYTELLING SESSIONS, AS WELL AS INTERACTIVE ACTIVITIES WITH THE CHILDREN/YOUTH ON HISTORY, SCIENCE, ETC. THE NEW BOOKS WILL BE USED IN THE SUMMER READING PROGRAM AND WILL INCLUDE CULTURAL BOOKS AND STEM MATERIALS.
description.1112: THE OUNALASHKA CORPORATION AND THE UNALASKA PUBLIC LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE ADDITIONAL CIRCULATING AND REFERENCE MATERIALS, INCLUDING MATERIALS DETAILING THE HISTORY AND ETHNOGRAPHY OF THE ALEUTIAN REGION, WHICH WILL BE ACCESSIBLE TO THE ENTIRE COMMUNITY AND ALSO TO PATRONS THROUGHOUT THE STATE OF ALASKA VIA INTERLIBRARY LOAN. THIS WILL IMPROVE SHAREHOLDERS’ LIVES BY ADDING MATERIALS TO LOCAL LIBRARY COLLECTIONS, MINIMIZING THE NEED TO INDIVIDUALLY ACQUIRE MATERIALS WHICH DETAIL TRIBAL HISTORY
description.1113: KOOTZNOOWOO, INC. WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ACCESSIBILITY TO THE TRADITIONAL ARTIST'S LIBRARY AND RESOURCE CENTER IN THE VILLAGE OF ANGOON, FOR LOCAL RESIDENTS, VISITORS, AND ARTISTS. FUNDS WILL BE USED TO PURCHASE BOOKS AND VIDEOS THAT FOCUS ON VARIOUS TYPES OF TLINGIT ART AND DESIGN. IN ADDITION, THE PURCHASE OF ADDITIONAL SHELVING, SO THAT THE RESOURCE MATERIALS ARE SECURELY STORED, AND ACCESSIBLE TO LOCAL RESIDENTS AND PAY A PORTION OF THE UTILITY AND STAFFING COSTS TO EXPAND HOURS OF OPERATION.
description.1114: THE SANTA ROSA BAND OF CAHUILLA INDIANS WILL INCREASE THE LOVE OF BOOKS AND TRADITIONAL STORIES AMONG CHILDREN. THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY INCREASING THE AVAILABILITY OF THE LEAD LIBRARIAN, THE PURCHASE OF SUPPLIES, LIBRARY BOOKS, AND SUBSCRIPTIONS TO PERIODICALS THAT ARE OF INTEREST TO CHILDREN. IN ADDITION TO DEVELOPING A HEIGHTENED LOVE OF BOOKS AND LEARNING, CHILDREN WILL ALSO LEARN THE CAHUILLA LANGUAGE DURING MANY ACTIVITIES THROUGHOUT THE YEAR.
description.1115: THE CHILKAT INDIAN VILLAGE WILL IMPROVE SERVICES FOR LEARNING AND ACCESSING INFORMATION IN A VARIETY OF FORMATS TO SUPPORT NEEDS FOR EDUCATION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, ECONOMIC AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT, HEALTH INFORMATION, CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS AND OTHER TYPES OF LITERACY SKILLS. THE LIBRARY WILL ALSO SUPPORT THE ACQUISITION OF LIBRARY-RELATED MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, SERVICES AND FEES AND ALLOW STAFF TO RECEIVE TRAINING TO CONTINUE IMPROVING SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE RELATED TO GENERAL LIBRARY AND ARCHIVAL WORK. THE TRIBAL MEMBERS HAVE EXPRESSED INTEREST IN PARTICIPATING IN MORE CULTURAL AND COMMUNITY CENTERED PROGRAMING AT THE LIBRARY, SO THEY WILL CONTINUE TO PARTNER WITH TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE BEARERS AND OTHER CONSULTANTS WHO HAVE EXPERTISE IN RELEVANT FIELDS TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR IN-PERSON LEARNING THROUGH WORKSHOPS AS WELL AS ASYNCHRONOUS LEARNING THROUGH SHORT FILMS ABOUT SPECIAL TOPICS.
description.1116: THE PETERSBURG INDIAN ASSOCIATION WILL OFFER VARIOUS PROGRAMS AND ACTIVITIES FOR THE COMMUNITY, WITH A FOCUS ON ENHANCING THEIR COLLECTION OF HIGH INTEREST DVD’S AND BOOKS TO ADD TO THE COLLECTION. THE LIBRARY STAFF WILL ADOPT A CUSTOMER-CENTRIC APPROACH TO COLLECTION DEVELOPMENT. THIS STRATEGY INVOLVES INCORPORATING NEW MATERIALS IN RESPONSE TO CUSTOMER REQUESTS, ANALYZING COLLECTION USAGE PATTERNS, AND ANTICIPATING FUTURE NEEDS. A ROBUST COLLECTION IS CRUCIAL FOR THE REMOTE ISLAND COMMUNITY, WHERE LIMITED ACCESS TO RESOURCES PERSISTS AS A SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGE.
description.1117: THE QUAPAW NATION WILL PROVIDE RESOURCES TO IMPROVE LITERACY SKILLS, MAINTAIN A COLLECTION OF NATIVE AMERICAN MATERIALS, AND MEET THE INFORMATIONAL AND RECREATIONAL NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY. THE GOAL IS TO INCREASE ITS COLLECTION OF MATERIALS RELATING TO THE QUAPAW NATION AND NEIGHBORING TRIBES IN THE REGION, AS WELL AS ENSURING THEY MAINTAIN A CORE COLLECTION OF CURRENT BESTSELLING NON-FICTION AND FICTION MATERIALS FOR ALL AGES. IN ADDITION, QUAPAW NATION WILL CONTINUE ITS PARTICIPATION IN THE OKLAHOMA VIRTUAL LIBRARY, HOSTING A SUMMER READING PROGRAM, AS WELL AS A STORYTIME PROGRAM FOR DAYCARE CENTERS.
description.1118: THE CENTRAL COUNCIL OF TLINGIT AND HAIDA INDIAN TRIBES OF ALASKA WILL INCREASE HOLDINGS AS RESOURCES FOR ITS TRIBAL CITIZENS AS IT WORKS TO STRENGTHEN TRIBAL AND COMMUNITY LANGUAGES, ARTS, AND CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE ACQUISITION OF LIBRARY-RELATED MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, FURNISHINGS, AND SERVICES. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE COVERAGE OF EXPENSES RELATED TO STAFF PARTICIPATION AT PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCES. MANY RESOURCES SPECIFIC TO TLINGIT AND HAIDA CULTURES ARE OUT OF PRINT, COST-PROHIBITIVE, OR DIFFICULT TO FIND. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO RESOURCES BECAUSE MANY EXISTING TLINGIT AND HAIDA RESOURCES ARE CURRENTLY INACCESSIBLE.
description.1119: THE CRAIG PUBLIC LIBRARY OF CRAIG ALASKA IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SHAAN SEET INCORPORATED WILL FOCUS ON COLLECTION CARE AND MANAGEMENT. THE LIBRARY WILL CONTINUE TO BUILD A BODY OF MATERIALS THAT ADVANCE SHARED KNOWLEDGE AND LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR ALL. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE ACQUISITION OF LIBRARY-RELATED MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, FURNISHINGS, AND SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON REVAMPING LIBRARY SHELVES WITH COMPELLING, HIGH-INTEREST TITLES. THE ALASKA COLLECTION TAKES CENTER STAGE, WITH A FOCUS ON NATIVE ART, CULTURE, AND HISTORY. ADDITIONALLY, THE LIBRARY WILL ENHANCE THE ALASKA DIGITAL LIBRARY BY ACQUIRING POPULAR EBOOKS AND AUDIOBOOKS, AIMING TO MINIMIZE HOLD WAIT TIMES AND MAXIMIZE READER SATISFACTION.
description.1120: THE SEALASKA CORPORATION IN JUNEAU, ALASKA WILL HAVE A GREATER EMPHASIS ON IMPROVING DIGITIZATION EFFORTS THAT WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SEALASKA’S GOAL TO PRESERVE AND ENHANCE ITS COLLECTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, SEALASKA WILL CONTINUE TO IMPLEMENT ITS ONGOING GOAL TO ENSURE ITS LIBRARY RESOURCES REMAIN CURRENT, VIABLE, AND OF VALUE TO THE NATIVE AND NON-NATIVE PATRONS. THE PRIMARY AIM OF SEALASKA’S PRESERVATION EFFORTS WILL BE DIGITIZING VULNERABLE COLLECTIONS TO ALLOW FOR CONTINUED ACCESS WHILE GUARDING AGAINST DETERIORATION. TO ENSURE ITS RESOURCES REMAIN CURRENT, VIABLE, AND OF VALUE TO ITS PATRONS, SEALASKA WILL PURCHASE NEW BOOKS AND PUBLICATIONS ON TLINGIT, HAIDA, AND TSIMSHIAN CULTURE, HISTORY, AND LANGUAGE.
description.1121: GALENA VILLAGE WILL PROVIDE CORE LIBRARY SERVICES TO ITS COMMUNITY BY MAINTAINING LIBRARY HOURS AFTER-SCHOOL AND DURING THE SUMMER AND PROVIDING ENRICHMENT TO TRIBAL MEMBERS THROUGH PROGRAMMING. CHARLES EVANS COMMUNITY LIBRARY IS THE ONLY PUBLIC LIBRARY SERVICE IN THE RURAL COMMUNITY OF GALENA AND PROVIDES ESSENTIAL YEAR-ROUND PROGRAMS AND ACTIVITIES TO ITS COMMUNITY. THE LIBRARY WILL OFFER NUMEROUS PROGRAMS INCLUDING THE SUMMER READING PROGRAM CLUB, AFTERSCHOOL LIBRARY SERVICES, TODDLERS LIBRARY, ADULT BOOK CLUB, LITERACY NIGHT, AND GAME TIME. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO TRIBAL CITIZENS OF ALL AGES WITHIN ITS SERVICE AREA.
description.1122: ELK VALLEY RANCHERIA WILL SUPPORT EXISTING LIBRARY OPERATIONS, EXPAND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS, AND SUPPORT PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR STAFF. THE TRIBE WILL PURCHASE NEW BOOKS, PERIODICALS, AND ELECTRONIC RESOURCES TO ADD VARIETY TO EXISTING COLLECTIONS TO INCREASE INTEREST TO USERS. THE TRIBE WILL IMPROVE THE CHILDREN’S READING NOOK BY HONORING TRIBAL MEMBERS AND CHILDREN WHO GRADUATED FROM THE TRIBE’S HIGHER EDUCATION PROGRAM TO INSPIRE OTHER CHILDREN SEEKING EDUCATION. FINALLY, THE TRIBE WILL SUPPORT STAFF SALARY AND ENABLE THE TRIBAL LIBRARIAN TO ATTEND THE 2024 INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE OF INDIGENOUS ARCHIVES, LIBRARIES, AND MUSEUMS FOR PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS SERVICE AREA.
description.1123: FOREST COUNTY POTAWATOMI COMMUNITY (FCPC) WILL ACQUIRE NATIVE AMERICAN-FOCUSED MATERIALS, HOST DIVERSE LIBRARY PROGRAMS, AND COLLABORATE WITH LOCAL SCHOOLS AND THE TRIBE’S COMMUNITY CENTER TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS, MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES, EXPAND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND ENHANCE YOUTH PROGRAMMING AT FCPC. ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A MORE EXTENSIVE COLLECTION, INCREASED PATRONAGE, AND ENHANCED CULTURAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR FCPC YOUTH, BOLSTERING POTAWATOMI HERITAGE PRESERVATION. THE ENRICHED RESOURCES AND ENGAGING PROGRAMMING WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS PROJECT SERVICE AREA, ESPECIALLY YOUTH, EDUCATORS, AND RESIDENTS INTERESTED IN NATIVE AMERICAN CULTURE AND HISTORY.
description.1124: THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF TETLIN’S TETLIN SCHOOL LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE COMFORTABLE FURNITURE TO CREATE A WELCOMING SPACE AND EXPAND THE COLLECTION OF ALASKAN-THEMED BOOKS TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. IT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH A COLLABORATION BETWEEN THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF TETLIN, TETLIN SCHOOL, AND ALASKA GATEWAY SCHOOL DISTRICT. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT STUDENTS THROUGH A CONDUCIVE LEARNING ENVIRONMENT, EXPANDED ACCESS TO ALASKAN-THEMED MATERIALS, AND ENHANCED ENGAGEMENT IN LIBRARY ACTIVITIES. THE LIBRARY WILL PROVIDE ENRICHED LEARNING EXPERIENCES FOR CHILDREN ENROLLED IN SCHOOL ON THE RESERVATION WITH A FOCUS ON THOSE ACTIVITIES THAT WILL PREPARE THEM TO MOVE TO THE NEXT LEVEL.
description.1125: THE EASTERN SHOSHONE TRIBE WILL COMBAT LITERACY CHALLENGES BY PROVIDING ACCESS TO READING MATERIALS AND EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES YEAR-ROUND THROUGH ITS BOOKMOBILE PROGRAM. THEY WILL ALSO PURCHASE BOOKS AND OTHER MATERIALS TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. IT WILL ALSO SUPPORT TRIBAL STAFF INVOLVED IN LITERACY OUTREACH AND PROVIDE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES TO EXPAND THEIR SKILLS. THE LIBRARY WILL CONTINUE TO BUILD A BODY OF MATERIALS THAT ADVANCE SHARED KNOWLEDGE AND LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR ALL. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS SERVICE AREA
description.1126: PUEBLO OF POJOAQUE WILL OFFER EXTENDED LIBRARY EVENING AND WEEKEND HOURS TO ACCOMMODATE WORKING PARENTS AND STUDENTS TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. IT WILL SUPPORT TRAVEL FOR LIBRARY STAFF TO ATTEND SKILL-ENHANCING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT MEETINGS AND CONFERENCES TO ENHANCE ACCESS TO LIBRARY RESOURCES. ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED PATRONAGE DURING EXTENDED HOURS, IMPROVED STAFF SKILLS, AND ENHANCED COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS WITH TRIBAL DEPARTMENTS, LOCAL BUSINESSES, AND EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE POJOAQUE COMMUNITY, INCLUDING WORKING PARENTS, STUDENTS, AND RESIDENTS SEEKING ACCESS TO INFORMATION AND EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES.
description.1127: THE WRANGELL COOPERATIVE ASSOCIATION’S IRENE INGLE PUBLIC LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE PLAYAWAY AND WONDERBOOK AUDIOBOOK DEVICES AS WELL AS RENEW ITS ALASKA DIGITAL LIBRARY SUBSCRIPTION TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. IT WILL ALSO SUPPORT TRAVEL FOR ITS LIBRARY WORKFORCE TO THE SKILL-ENHANCING ALASKA LIBRARY ASSOCIATION CONFERENCE SO THAT STAFF MAY IMPROVE ACCESS TO INFORMATION AND PROMOTE LITERACY SKILLS AMONG PATRONS, PARTICULARLY THROUGH EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AND DIGITAL RESOURCES. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO TRIBAL CITIZENS OF ALL AGES WITHIN ITS SERVICE AREA.
description.1128: THE OUZINKIE TRIBAL MEDIA CENTER LIBRARY IN OUZINKIE, ALASKA (SPRUCE ISLAND) WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS RELATIVELY ISOLATED COMMUNITIES. THE LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE LIBRARY-RELATED MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, FURNISHINGS, SERVICES TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. IT WILL SUPPORT TRAVEL FOR ITS LIBRARY WORKFORCE TO SKILL-ENHANCING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT MEETINGS AND CONFERENCES AND WILL OFFER LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES TO COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN A VARIETY OF FORMATS TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND IMPROVE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS RELATED TO SPECIFIC TOPICS AND CONTENT AREAS OF INTEREST TO LIBRARY USERS AND COMMUNITY-BASED USERS.
description.1129: THE OJIBWE LEARNING CENTER AND LIBRARY OF THE SAULT SAINT MARIE TRIBE OF CHIPPEWA INDIANS IN SAULT SAINT MARIE, MICHIGAN WILL INCREASE SERVICES AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAMS THROUGH THE WORK OF ITS STAFF AND LIBRARY AIDE BY OFFERING COMPENSATION FOR SALARY AND WAGES. THE LIBRARY AIDE MAINTAINS THE LIBRARY DATABASE, OVERSEES ESSENTIAL LIBRARY FUNCTIONS, ANSWERS ALL LIBRARY-RELATED QUESTIONS, AND PARTICIPATES IN COMMUNITY EVENTS RELATED TO LIBRARY SERVICES. THE SAULT TRIBE WILL MAINTAIN THE LIBRARY AS A LEARNING SPACE, WHICH IS ACCESSIBLE AND OPEN TO SAULT TRIBE DEPARTMENTS, TRIBAL AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS.
description.1130: THE PUEBLO OF TESUQUE WILL HIRE A PART-TIME LIBRARY AIDE POSITION TO ENSURE CONSISTENT HOURS OF OPERATION AND GIVE PATRONS CONTINUED ACCESS TO THE LIBRARY'S AVAILABLE RESOURCES. NEW CULTURAL MATERIALS WILL BE PURCHASED TO SUPPORT A VARIETY OF PROGRAMS SUCH AS ARTS & CRAFTS, STEM ACTIVITIES, AND READING PROGRAMS. CULTURAL CLASSES WILL BE OFFERED IN THE LIBRARY, WITH MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY INVITED TO TEACH AND TO BE OFFERED STIPENDS FOR THIS WORK. THE LIBRARY WILL ALSO STRENGTHEN ITS GENERAL COLLECTION BY PURCHASING BOOKS, DVDS, AND MAGAZINES.
description.1131: THE NONDALTON VILLAGE WILL CONTINUE TO GROW ITS COLLECTION OF BOOKS, MAGAZINES, DVDS, CDS, AND OTHER ELECTRONIC FORMATS. IN ADDITION, THEY WILL HIRE A PART-TIME LOCAL LIBRARIAN WITH THE GOAL OF KEEPING INVENTORY OF LIBRARY COLLECTIONS, RESEARCHING OTHER LIBRARY FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES, ORGANIZING LIBRARY COLLECTIONS, ORDERING REQUESTED LIBRARY MATERIALS AND OPENING THE LIBRARY TO THE PUBLIC. FUNDS WILL ENSURE THAT COMMUNITY MEMBERS ARE READING AND THAT FAMILIES STAY CONNECTED. FUNDS WILL ALSO SUPPORT LIBRARY STAFF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES DURING THE YEAR.
description.1132: THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF AFOGNAK'S NADIA MULLAN ALUTIIQ HERITAGE LIBRARY WILL INCREASE THE COLLECTION OF MATERIALS RELATING TO THE TRIBE, THE ALUTIIQ LANGUAGE AND CULTURE, AS WELL AS OTHER TRIBES IN ALASKA AND THROUGHOUT THE UNITED STATES. THE LIBRARY WILL ALSO FACILITATE INTERACTIVE CULTURAL ACTIVITIES THAT WILL PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES CONNECTING THEM TO THE ALUTIIQ LANGUAGE, CRAFTS, CULTURE, OR EXPERIENCES. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO OVER 800 TRIBAL MEMBERS AND NEARLY 3,400 ALASKA NATIVE PEOPLE WITHIN THE PROJECT SERVICE AREA.
description.1133: THE ALEUT COMMUNITY OF ST. PAUL ISLAND WILL SUSTAIN ITS WEBSITE, PROVIDING CULTURAL INFORMATION ON, BY, AND FOR THE UNANGAN (ALEUTS). FOR CITIZENS WITHOUT COMPUTER AND/OR INTERNET CAPABILITY, THE TANAX̂ UNAAĜIM MAQAX̂SINGIN (OFFICE OF CULTURAL AFFAIRS) MAINTAINS A COMPUTER WORKSTATION THAT LIBRARY VISITORS CAN USE TO ACCESS THE WEBSITE AND MAKES PAPER OR DIGITAL COPIES AVAILABLE. THE PROJECT DIRECTOR WILL WORK WITH LOCAL LIBRARY EMPLOYEES WHO WILL CURATE THE CONTENT OF THE WEBSITE. THE TWO CURATORS WILL WORK AN AVERAGE OF 1-2 HOURS A WEEK EACH TO UPLOAD PHOTOS, TEXT, AUDIO RECORDINGS, AND OTHER ITEMS OF INTEREST AS DIRECTED BY THE PROJECT DIRECTOR.
description.1134: THE MUSCOGEE CREEK NATION WILL PURCHASE NEW BOOKS AND MATERIALS TO SUPPORT THE COLLEGE’S DEGREE PROGRAMS THAT INCLUDE NATIVE AMERICAN STUDIES, TRIBAL SERVICES, CRIMINAL JUSTICE, GENERAL STUDIES, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND GAMING. THESE WILL PROVIDE NEW TOOLS FOR STUDENTS WHEN CONDUCTING RESEARCH FOR CLASSWORK. FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TOWARDS THE PURCHASE OF EIGHT LAPTOPS TO ENHANCE THE LAPTOP LENDING PROGRAM. THIS WILL EMPOWER STUDENTS IN THEIR ACADEMIC PURSUITS AND HELP BRIDGE THE DIGITAL DIVIDE.
description.1135: THE IOWA TRIBE OF OKLAHOMA, INC. WILL PROVIDE REMOTE, AND SOCIAL DISTANCING IN-PERSON ACCESS TO LIBRARY LITERATURE AND RESOURCES FOR LIBRARY PATRONS AND TEACH SKILLS AND DIGITAL LITERACY EDUCATION TO LIBRARY PATRONS FOR EASE OF ACCESS TO LIBRARY RESOURCES. THE IOWA TRIBE OF OKLAHOMA LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE A TUMBLE BOOK SUBSCRIPTION THAT WILL INCLUDE AUDIO, GUIDED READING, AND EASY TO READ CHAPTER BOOKS BEGINNING IN AUGUST. STAFF WILL OPERATE THE LIBRARY AND ITS RESOURCES HELPING PATRONS IMPROVE EDUCATION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, DIGITAL LITERACY SKILLS, AND OTHER TYPES OF ENGAGEMENT. TUMBLE BOOKS COLLECTION WILL HELP EARLY, YOUNG, AND STRUGGLING READERS BY PROVIDING REMOTE INTERACTIVE READING MATERIALS. THE EDUCATION ASSISTANT WILL PROVIDE GUIDED TRAINING AS NEEDED TO IMPROVE USAGE OF LIBRARY RESOURCES FOR PATRON’S USE OF NEW AND CURRENT LIBRARY RESOURCES.
description.1136: BARONA BAND OF MISSION INDIANS WILL ENHANCE EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES FOR BARONA INDIAN CHARTER SCHOOL STUDENTS AND THE NATIVE COMMUNITY BY EXPANDING CHILDREN'S LITERATURE COLLECTIONS, FOSTERING PARTNERSHIPS, AND IMPLEMENTING ENGAGING PROGRAMMING, ULTIMATELY AIMING TO INCREASE BOOK CHECK-OUT RATES AND LITERACY WHILE CREATING AN INCLUSIVE AND CULTURALLY RICH ENVIRONMENT. THE LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE BOOKS RELATING TO SEASONS, HOLIDAYS, AS WELL AS MULTI-CULTURAL CELEBRATIONS AS THOSE ARE FREQUENTLY REQUESTED BY STAFF AND HELP RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT DIFFERENT CULTURES. TWO LIBRARY STAFF MEMBERS WILL RECEIVE CONTINUED PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH ATTENDANCE AT THE ASSOCIATION FOR TRIBAL ARCHIVES, LIBRARIES, AND MUSEUMS 2024 CONFERENCE; THE CONFERENCE HAS ALWAYS PROVIDED VALUABLE INFORMATION ABOUT TRIBAL LIBRARIES THROUGH SESSIONS AND WORKSHOPS.
description.1137: THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF CANTWELL WILL PURCHASE BOOKS, SUBSCRIPTIONS, AND AUDIO/VISUAL MATERIALS TO ADDRESS EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT NEEDS IN THIS ALASKAN COMMUNITY. THE LIBRARY WILL IMPROVE SERVICES FOR LEARNING AND ACCESSING INFORMATION IN A VARIETY OF FORMATS TO SUPPORT NEEDS FOR EDUCATION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, ECONOMIC AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT, HEALTH INFORMATION, CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS AND OTHER TYPES OF LITERACY SKILLS. FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TOWARDS THE ACQUISITION OF LIBRARY-RELATED MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, SERVICES AND FEES. THIS WILL ALLOW STAFF TO RECEIVE TRAINING TO CONTINUE IMPROVING THEIR SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE RELATED TO GENERAL LIBRARY AND ARCHIVAL WORK. FUNDS WILL ALLOW STAFF TO PARTICIPATE IN TRAININGS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT CONFERENCES, TO BETTER SERVE PATRONS AND IMPROVE LIBRARY OPERATIONS.
description.1138: WITH THIS GRANT, KCL IS CONTINUING TO FOCUS ON PROVIDING LIBRARY MATERIALS IN A VARIETY OF FORMATS, INCLUDING DIGITAL EBOOKS AND AUDIOBOOKS, PERIODICALS, AND BEST SELLERS FOR ALL AGE LEVELS.
description.1139: THIS GRANT WILL SUPPORT INTERNET SUBSCRIPTIONS FOR OGLALA LAKOTA COLLEGE LEARNING RESOURCE CENTER/$3000 FOR PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR LIBRARY STAFF DEVELOPMENT.
description.1140: THE YAVAPAI PRESCOTT INDIAN TRIBE LIBRARY  WILL SUPPORT THE SALARIES AND TRAINING OF LIBRARY STAFF TO BETTER SERVE THEIR COMMUNITY AND INCREASE THE OVERALL CAPACITY OF THE LIBRARY FOR THE ENHANCEMENT AND BETTERMENT OF ALL THEY SERVE.
description.1141: "THE OTTAWA TRIBAL LIBRARY IS SET-UP AS A HISTORICAL RESEARCH LIBRARY AND THE LIBRARY WILL GIVE CONTINUED ACCESS TO CURRENT, RELEVANT RESOURCES ON NATIVE AMERICAN TOPICS, SO THAT COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN SATISFY THEIR FORMAL AND INFORMAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS.
description.1142: THE HUNA TOTEM CORPORATION WILL ADVANCE COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP AND ACCESS THROUGH INNOVATIVE MEANS BY ENGAGING OUR PATRONS IN A BLEND OF OUTREACH APPROACHES AND METHODS OF ENGAGEMENT. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH THE FOLLOWING SIMPLE MEASURES THAT WILL ENABLE OUR AUDIENCES TO EXPAND THE EXPERIENCES AND ENJOYMENT OF OUR LIBRARY AND ARCHIVAL MATERIALS, SERVICES, AND RESOURCES.
description.1143: JAMES S’KLALLAM TRIBE WILL OFFER A VARIETY OF PROGRAMS SUCH AS TRADITONAL FOODS, CRAFTS, ARCHAELOGY AND HISTORY DUE TO THEIR IMPROVED FACILITIES AND DEDICATED EXHIBIT SPACE SINCE THEIR REOPENING IN FEBRUARY 2024. FUNDS WILL ALLOW FOR OPPORTUNITIES FOR IN-PERSON PROGRAMMING AND RESEARCH SUPPORT THAT WILL EDUCATE COMMUNITY MEMBERS ON HISTORICAL AND CONTEMPORARY CULTURAL PRACTICES OF THE TRIBE. FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TOWARDS LIBRARY STAFF SALARY AS THEY MAINTAIN LIBRARY SERVICES AND OVERSEE DAILY OPERATIONS OF THE LIBRARY INCLUDING COLLECTION DEVELOPMENT, ADMINISTERING THE LIBRARY WEBSITE, AND CONTENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS.
description.1144: SHOALWATER BAY INDIAN TRIBE WILL CONTINUE TO OFFER SERVICES AND PROGRAMS THAT ENHANCE PUBLIC EDUCATION THROUGH A VARIETY OF MEANS. FUNDS WILL BE USED TO SUPPORT THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF LIBRARY STAFF WHO WILL BRING VALUABLE KNOWLEDGE BACK TO THE TRIBE. THE LIBRARY PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE EDUCATION, INCLUDING CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE EDUCATION AND OTHER OPTIONS, TO THE SURROUNDING COMMUNITY AND STAFF. FUNDS WILL BE USED TO PURCHASE MORE MEDIA AND FURNISHINGS FOR THE LIBRARY, WITH THE INTENT OF CREATING A COMFORTABLE AND WELL-EQUIPPED LEARNING ENVIRONMENT. THIS PROGRAM IS CORE TO THE TRIBE’S CULTURE AND HERITAGE AND BRINGS STRENGTH AND RESOLUTION TO ITS COMMUNITY, AND BINDING THE COMMUNITY TOGETHER.
description.1145: THE SELDOVIA VILLIAGE TRIBE WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITS TRIBAL LENDING LIBRARY COLLECTON AND INCREASE THE NUMBER OF READERS ACROSS AGE GROUPS. THE TRIBAL LENDING LIBRARY OFFERS A COLLECTION OF ALASKA NATIVE BOOKS ON CULTURE AND HERITAGE, WITH THE GOAL OF KEEPING STORIES AND TRADITIONS ALIVE. IT PROVIDES TOOLS AND SPACE TO HELP OLD AND NEW COMMUNITY MEMBERS LEARN, TEACH, SHARE, AND EXPERIENCE TOGETHER. IN SUPPORT OF THE ART OF READING, LISTENING, AND STORYTELLING, FUNDS WILL BE USED TO CREATE A DEDICATED COMMUNITY LEARNING CENTER WITHIN THE LIBRARY, ALLOWING MORE SPACE FOR THE STAFF TO HOST VARIOUS EVENTS FOR CHILDREN AND YOUTH TO HEAR STORIES FROM ELDERS AND OTHER ADULTS THROUGH READING, STORYTELLING, MULTIMEDIA, OR TRADITIONAL ALASKA NATIVE ART FORMS.
description.1146: THE NOOKSACK TRIBAL WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL NEEDS FOR LIBRARY OPERATIONS, MAINTAIN CORE SERVICES, AND EXPAND THEIR LIBRARY MISSION. THE LIBRARY WILL PROMOTE COMMUNITY, LITERACY, EDUCATION, EMPLOYMENT, AND ON-GOING READING ENJOYMENT FOR PATRONS BY PROVIDING CULTURALLY-RELEVANT MATERIALS, SERVICES, AND PROGRAMS. THIS WILL SUPPORT NOOKSACK LIFEWAYS LEARNING AND NATIVE AMERICAN RESEARCH. FURTHERMORE, THE LIBRARY WILL CONTINUE ITS PARTICIPATION IN THE WASHINGTON STATE SUMMER READING PROGRAM, USING GRANT FUNDS FOR THE PURCHASING OF RECOMMENDED READING TITLES.
description.1147: THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF PORT GRAHAM WILL PROVIDE SERVICES TO THEIR COMMUNITY AND BUILD BACK THEIR PATRON NUMBERS AFTER CLOSURE DUE TO THE IMPACT OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. FUNDS WILL BE USED TO SUPPORT WAGES FOR THE PART-TIME LIBRARIAN FOR THE YEAR, AS WELL AS FOR COSTS RELATED TO INTERNET CONNECTIVITY OF LIBRARY COMPUTERS, AND THE PURCHASE BOOKS AND DVDS FOR THE LIBRARY. THIS WILL ALLOW THOSE WITHOUT INTERNET CONNECTIVITY IN THEIR HOMES TO STILL ACCOMPLISH NECESSARY ONLINE BUSINESS AT THE LIBRARY. FUNDS WILL ALSO CONTINUE TO SUPPORT READING COMPETITIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN A MAJOR PART OF THE COMMUNITY FOR THE YOUTH COMMUNITY.
description.1148: THE WASHOE TRIBE’S WOODFORDS INDIAN EDUCATION CENTER HOUSES THE HÚNGALELTI LIBRARY WHICH WILL FOCUS ON NEW COLLECTION ACQUISITIONS RELATED TO INDIGENOUS LITERATURE. LIBRARY STAFF WILL INTRODUCE COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO THE DIGITAL LITERACY TOOLS ON SITE, AND TRAIN VOLUNTEERS WHO ARE WILLING TO LEARN HOW TO CATALOGUE NEW TITLES FOR THE DIGITAL LIBRARY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TO INSTALL TWO SMALL “FREEDOM LIBRARIES” OUTSIDE THEIR BUILDING, TO BE FILLED WITH BOOKS FOR ALL AGES, AND THAT WILL PROMOTE LIFELONG LEARNING OF DIVERSE AND QUALITY CONTENT.
description.1149: ALEUTIAN PRIBILOF ISLAND ASSOCIATION (APIA), INC WILL WORK IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE CONSTITUENT COMMUNITIES TO STRENGTHEN, PRESERVE AND ENSURE THE UNITY OF THE UNANGAX PEOPLE BY PROVIDING ACCESS TO CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE AND INFORMATION, CREATING LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES, AND HOSTING EVENTS TO SUPPORT COMMUNITY CONNECTIONS. APIA’S PRIORITIES FOR THE YEAR INCLUDE COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND EDUCATION, DIGITIZATION AND ACCESS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR CULTURAL HERITAGE (CH) STAFF. THE STAFF WILL SHARE ONGOING WORK WITH TRIBAL MEMBERS AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS AS WELL AS THE GENERAL PUBLIC.
description.1150: HEALY LAKE VILLAGE’S LIBRARY WILL EXPAND THEIR BOOK AND DVD COLLECTION, AND PROVIDE INTERNET AND COMPUTER ACCESS TO THE COMMUNITY. FUNDS WILL BE USED TOWARDS THE HIRING OF NEW LIBRARY STAFF, AND THE IMPROVEMENT OF THE LIBRARY SPACE SUCH AS IN THE ADDITION OF NEW SHELVES. AS HEALY LAKE IS A REMOTE COMMUNITY WITH LIMITED RESOURCES, THIS WILL ALLOW THE LIRARY TO REACH THEIR GOAL FOR ALL TRIBAL CITIZENS TO BE ABLE TO ENGAGE IN HEALTHY ACTIVITIES THAT ALLOWS THEM TO EXPAND THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND TEACH THEIR KNOWLEDGE TO OTHERS. LIBRARY PROGRAMMING WILL AIM TO IMPROVE TRIBAL CITIZEN ENGAGEMENT IN MEETINGS, ESPECIALLY ONES CONCERNING DECISIONS THAT WILL AFFECT THE TRIBAL COMMUNITY.
description.1151: THE GULKANA VILLAGE COUNCIL WILL PROVIDE LIBRARY SERVICES TO THE COMMUNITY THAT INCLUDE CHECKING OUT BOOKS AND MATERIALS TO PATRONS, PROVIDING INTERNET ACCESS, AS WELL AS PRINTING, FAXING AND SCANNING SERVICES. FUNDS WILL GO TOWARDS DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING A YOUTH SUMMER READING PROGRAM THAT MAY INCLUDE HOSTING ADDITIONAL YOUTH OR COMMUNITY EVENTS AS TIME ALLOWS. EXAMPLES OF POSSIBLE COMMUNITY EVENTS INCLUDE CHILDREN’S STORY HOURS, COMMUNITY GAME NIGHTS, CRAFTING PROJECTS, MOVIE NIGHTS, AND CULTURAL LANGUAGE WORKSHOPS/CULTURAL ACTIVITIES. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE COMMUNITY, GIVING RESIDENTS THE OPPORTUNITY TO ENRICH THEIR MINDS THROUGH THE POWER OF READING.
description.1152: THE HO-CHUNK NATION OF WISCONSIN DID NOT HAVE AN OPERATIONAL LIBRARY PRIOR TO 2023, THUS GRANT FUNDS WILL ENHANCE THEIR EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES AND REMOTE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES, PROMOTE LITERACY, AND INSPIRE MEMBERS OF THEIR COMMUNITY TO BECOME LIFELONG LEARNERS. LIBRARY STAFF WILL BE GROWING THEIR COLLECTIONS OF NATIVE AUTHORED BOOKS FOR YOUTH AGED KINDERGARTEN THROUGH GRADE 12, AS WELL AS FOR ADULTS. DEDICATED LIBRARY SPACE WILL BE PROVIDED FOR MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY WHO MAY CHOOSE TO COMPLETE THEIR ART PROJECTS SUCH AS PAINTING, SEWING, CRAFTING, AND CARVING. FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TO PURCHASE PERIODICALS AND SUBSCRIPTIONS, AND TO ACCOMMODATE THEIR GROWING BOOK COLLECTIONS BY ADDING NEW SHELVING, AND PURCHASING ADDITIONAL RESOURCES SUCH AS OFFICE SUPPLIES, ETC.
description.1153: THE GRAND TRAVERSE BAND OF OTTAWA AND CHIPPEWA INDIANS’ HERITAGE LIBRARY WILL FOCUS ON PROVIDING AND MAINTAINING EXISTING LIBRARY SERVICES FOR THE COMMUNITY. GRANTS FUNDS WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR PEOPLE TO ACCESS AND USE ELECTRONIC INFORMATION, PROMOTE COMMUNITY INTERACTION AND INCLUSION, AND DELIVER A MIX OF RESOURCES, ACTIVITIES, AND SERVICES DESIGNED TO BENEFIT THEIR PATRONS. GRANT FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TOWARDS PURCHASES THAT WILL INCREASE AND REPLENISH BOOKS, RESOURCES AND COLLECTIONS OF MATERIALS RELATING TO THE NATIVE AMERICAN COMMUNITIES AND THE GRAND TRAVERSE BAND OF OTTAWA AND CHIPPEWA INDIANS. SPECIFICALLY, PURCHASES INCLUDE PERIODICALS, SUBSCRIPTIONS, EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS, AND CHILDREN’S BOOKS. THESE BOOK AND RESOURCE PURCHASES WILL WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO ITS COMMUNITY, AS THEY WILL BE BASED ON COMMUNITY MEMBERS' INTERESTS AND ONGOING RESEARCH BY LIBRARY STAFF THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT YEAR.
description.1154: THE VILLAGE OF ANIAK WILL SUPPORT A LIBRARIAN AND LIBRARY AIDE TO SUSTAIN AND ENHANCE CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS REMOTE COMMUNITY. STAFF WILL FOCUS ON IMPROVING ELECTRONIC ACCESS, PROVIDING FREE WI-FI, AND EXPANDING RESOURCES SUCH AS LAPTOPS, TABLETS, BOOKS, AND MEDIA. THEY WILL ALSO PLACE SPECIAL EMPHASES ON FOSTERING LITERACY AMONG YOUTH THROUGH A SUMMER READING PROGRAM AND OFFERING MATERIALS RELEVANT TO RURAL ALASKA AND TRIBAL ISSUES. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED LIBRARY USAGE AND ENGAGEMENT, PARTICULARLY AMONG YOUNG READERS, CONTRIBUTING TO COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND ENRICHMENT. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE 526 TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS PROJECT SERVICE AREA.
description.1155: THE CHIPPEWA CREE TRIBE WILL PURCHASE SUBSCRIPTIONS TO THE JUNIOR LIBRARY GUILD, NEWSBANK, MONTANALIBRARY2GO, AND ANCESTRY.COM/HERITAGE QUEST TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP IMPROVE CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR THEIR CORE COMMUNITY.
description.1156: THE HUSLIA VILLAGE TRIBAL LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE INTERNET, BOOKS, DVDS, A PUBLIC USE COMPUTER AND ACCESSORIES TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND TO MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS REMOTE ISOLATED COMMUNITY. IT WILL ALSO PURCHASE SUPPLIES FOR A NEWLY ESTABLISHED SUMMER READING PROGRAM TO PROVIDE ENRICHED LEARNING EXPERIENCES FOR CHILDREN. BY BOLSTERING LIBRARY RESOURCES AND OFFERING ESSENTIAL SERVICES SUCH AS INTERNET ACCESS, THE PROJECT SEEKS TO BRIDGE GAPS IN INFORMATION ACCESS AND PROMOTE LITERACY FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS, PARTICULARLY CHILDREN. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE 314 TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS PROJECT SERVICE AREA.
description.1157: THE VILLAGE OF ILIAMNA WILL PURCHASE BOOKS, DVDS, OTHER MATERIALS, AND SHELVING TO SUPPORT ITS EXISTING OPERATIONS AND MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. ANTICIPATED RESULTS INCLUDE A BETTER ORGANIZED AND MAINTAINED LIBRARY, ENRICHED WITH INFORMATION ON LOCAL HISTORY AND LANGUAGE RESOURCES, BETTER SERVING THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE 110 TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS PROJECT SERVICE AREA.
description.1158: THE BLUE LAKE RANCHERIA’S SYLVIA DANIELS MEMORIAL LIBRARY WILL PURCHASE BOOKS, PERIODICALS, AND SOFTWARE SUBSCRIPTIONS TO EXPAND THE COLLECTION AS WELL AS PROGRAM SUPPLIES FOR YOUTH PROGRAMS. THE LIBRARIAN WILL DEVELOP PROGRAMS INCLUDING PAINTING, CRYSTAL MAKING, STEAM PROGRAMS, AND GAME AND MOVIE NIGHTS TO ENGAGE YOUTH. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS PROJECT SERVICE AREA BY EXPANDING SERVICES TO ALL MEMBERS, AND ESPECIALLY STUDENTS.
description.1159: THE NEW KOLIGANEK VILLAGE COUNCIL WILL SUPPORT BOOKS, JOURNALS, SUPPLIES, AND SOFTWARE SUBSCRIPTIONS TO DELIVER CORES LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO BE USED TO SUPPORT TRAVEL FOR ITS LIBRARY WORKFORCE TO THE ASSOCIATION OF TRIBAL ARCHIVES, LIBRARIES, AND MUSEUMS ANNUAL CONFERENCE TO PARTICIPATE IN PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND LEARN FROM OTHER TRIBAL LIBRARIANS. THE LIBRARY WILL CONTINUE TO BUILD AND CATALOG A BODY OF MATERIALS THAT ADVANCE SHARED KNOWLEDGE FOR ALL AND ENRICH LEARNING EXPERIENCES FOR CHILDREN.
description.1160: THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF NAPAIMUTE WILL MAINTAIN AND ENHANCE ITS CORE LIBRARY SERVICES TO MEET THE DIVERSE NEEDS OF ITS PATRONS BY PURCHASING GENERATOR FUEL AND INTERNET SERVICE TO KEEP ITS LIBRARY OPEN EXTRA HOURS AND PROVIDE 24/7 INTERNET ACCESS THROUGHOUT THE SUMMER. NAPAIMUTE IS A REMOTE COMMUNITY IN SOUTHWEST ALASKA WHERE RESIDENTS OFTEN RELY ON THE LIBRARY AS THEIR ONLY ACCESS TO COMPUTER AND INTERNET SERVICES. BY PROVIDING ACCESS TO ESSENTIAL SERVICES AND RESOURCES SUCH AS BOOKS, INFORMATION, RESEARCH, AND FREE WI-FI, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT BENEFIT TO THE TRIBAL CITIZENS WITHIN ITS PROJECT SERVICE AREA.
description.1161: THE PALA BAND OF MISSION INDIANS WILL PURCHASE LIBRARY BOOKS, MATERIALS, EDUCATIONAL ITEMS, AND SUPPLIES TO SUPPORT YOUTH LITERACY AND MAINTAIN CORE LIBRARY SERVICES FOR ITS COMMUNITY. THE LIBRARY WILL ALSO RENEW CRUCIAL LIBRARY SOFTWARE. THE LIBRARY WILL DEVELOP YOUTH PROGRAMS, HOLD STORY TIMES, AND SUPPORT STUDENTS. ITS LIBRARY WORKFORCE WILL PARTICIPATE IN SKILL-ENHANCING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT MEETINGS AND CONFERENCES.
