description.2966: I-CORPS: TRANSLATION POTENTIAL OF AN ONLINE HEALTHCARE INFORMATION (OHI) TRUST BADGE -THE BROADER IMPACT OF THIS I-CORPS PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN ONLINE KNOWLEDGE RECOMMENDER TOOL AND TRUST BADGE FOR CONSUMERS. HEALTH MISINFORMATION REMAINS A SERIOUS SOCIETAL THREAT. SINCE THE EMERGENCE OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC, REPORTS SHOW ON AVERAGE THAT 8 OUT OF 10 AMERICANS SEARCH FOR ONLINE HEALTHCARE INFORMATION (OHI), AND 4 OUT OF 10 AMERICANS CANNOT CORRECTLY IDENTIFY FALSE HEALTHCARE CLAIMS. THE GOAL OF THE NEW TECHNOLOGY IS TO HELP ALLEVIATE CONFUSION AMONGST CONSUMERS CAUSED BY THE OVERWHELMING AMOUNT OF OHI, AND TO HELP OHI PROVIDERS BOOST THEIR REPUTATION AS A TRUSTWORTHY SOURCE. THE TOOL IS DESIGNED TO COMBAT MISINFORMATION BY PROACTIVELY SERVING A WIDE SPECTRUM OF STAKEHOLDERS WHO REGULARLY DEAL WITH OHI CONTENT. THE I-CORPS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON THE SPECIFIC ISSUES AND PUBLIC CHALLENGES OF ENDORSEMENTS IN ADDITION TO FACT CHECKING OF OHI CONTENT AND CONTRIBUTING TO A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE NEEDS OF PEOPLE WHO USE AND/OR PROVIDE OHI CONTENT. THIS SOLUTION SERVES AS A FOUNDATION FOR A CONSULTANCY SERVICE PROVIDING PLATFORM OFFERING ADVICE PLUS TRAINING TO OHI CONSUMERS AND OHI PROVIDERS. THIS I-CORPS PROJECT UTILIZES EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING COUPLED WITH A FIRST-HAND INVESTIGATION OF THE INDUSTRY ECOSYSTEM TO ASSESS THE TRANSLATION POTENTIAL OF A SOFTWARE TOOL THAT WILL SERVE ONLINE HEALTHCARE INFORMATION (OHI) USERS BY PROVIDING MACHINE LEARNING-BASED CLASSIFICATION AND CERTIFICATION OF OHI CONTENT TRUSTWORTHINESS. RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT MACHINE LEARNING-BASED CLASSIFIERS CAN PROCESS OHI CLAIMS AND CLASSIFY THEM AS FACT OR FAKE, BUT SUCH SOLUTIONS HAVE NOT BEEN DIRECTLY INTEGRATED INTO WEB BROWSERS AND HAVE BEEN TRAINED WITH PRIMARILY TEXTUAL CUES FROM MOSTLY UNIMODAL DATASETS. THIS TECHNOLOGY ADDRESSES THESE LIMITATIONS AND IS DESIGNED AS A MACHINE LEARNING DRIVEN ONLINE KNOWLEDGE RECOMMENDER TOOL, PROTOTYPED AS A WEB EXTENSION UTILITY, WHICH CAN BE DIRECTLY EMBEDDED INTO WEB BROWSERS TO SEAMLESSLY REPORT TRUSTWORTHINESS OF ANY OHI CONTENT. THE SOLUTION IS DESIGNED AS A TRUST BADGE MODEL FOR EASY CERTIFICATION OF WEB CONTENT AND CAN FUNCTION BOTH AS AN ONLINE CONTENT CLASSIFIER. THIS CAPABILITY MAY ALLOW BOTH OHI CONSUMERS AND OHI PROVIDERS TO VALIDATE AND TAG OHI WEBSITES' TRUSTWORTHINESS. ADDITIONALLY, THE SOLUTION IS TRAINED WITH MULTIMODAL DATA, THAT INCLUDES BOTH TEXTUAL AND VISUAL CUES (E.G., IMAGE ELEMENTS, GRAPHIC CONTENTS, AND INFOGRAPHICS), UNLIKE EXISTING SOLUTIONS THAT DO NOT INCLUDE VISUAL CUES OR IMAGE ARTIFACTS. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.
description.2967: COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: PLANNING: TRACK 1 FOR CATALYZING A PARADIGM SHIFT TOWARDS AN INCLUSIVE ENGINEERING FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT -THIS PLANNING GRANT WILL ENABLE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A COMPETITIVE AND COLLABORATIVE CENTERS FOR EQUITY IN ENGINEERING (CEE) PHASE I PROJECT PROPOSAL. THE CENTER PROPOSAL SEEKS TO ENABLE THE RESEARCH AND PRACTICE OF AN ENGINEERING FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (ECD) THAT PROVIDES TRANSFORMATIONAL EXPERIENCES TO ALL STUDENTS, ESPECIALLY STUDENTS OF COLOR. THROUGH CREATING A DISTRIBUTED CENTER ACROSS SELECTED PARTNER INSTITUTIONS, WE ARE SEEKING TO INITIATE AND SUSTAIN A SHIFT WITHIN ECD TOWARDS THE PRINCIPLES OF INCLUSIVE PEDAGOGY. SUCH A SHIFT WILL ELIMINATE THE LIMITATIONS OF TRADITIONAL ECD, WHICH CAN OFTEN EXCLUDE GROUPS OF PEOPLES, REINFORCE STEREOTYPES, AND LEAVE PARTNER COMMUNITIES WANTING MORE. REPLACEMENT WITH AN INCLUSIVE ECD CAN SPECIFICALLY PROVIDE FOR STUDENTS OF COLOR, THEIR ASSETS, AND THEIR NEEDS WHILE POSITIVELY IMPACTING PARTNER COMMUNITIES TO STRENGTHEN EFFORTS OF BROADENING PARTICIPATION IN ENGINEERING. IN CONDUCTING THIS RESEARCH, WE WILL UNDERSTAND THE WAYS IN WHICH THE LIMITATIONS OF SERVICE-LEARNING?S ABILITY TO EQUITABLY EDUCATE ALL STUDENTS CAN BE OVERCOME. MORE SPECIFICALLY, IF SERVICE-LEARNING IS GOING TO SUPPORT THE EDUCATION OF STUDENTS FROM MINORITIZED BACKGROUNDS, THEN WE MUST RESEARCH ECD WITH RESPECT TO THE SPECIFIC NEEDS OF STUDENTS FROM THESE VARIOUS BACKGROUNDS. THIS WORK WILL IMPACT STUDENTS, COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION THROUGH PROMOTING ECD THAT IS INCLUSIVE TO ALL, WHERE STUDENTS FROM HISTORICALLY MINORITIZED DEMOGRAPHICS WILL BE SUPPORTED THROUGH TRANSFORMATIONAL EXPERIENCES THAT ENCOURAGE THEM TO REMAIN AND SUCCEED IN ENGINEERING. THROUGH STRENGTHENING AND CREATING A BROAD ARRAY OF INCLUSIVE AND CULTURALLY RELEVANT ECD APPROACHES, CONTEXTS, AND DATA COLLECTION METHODS THE RESEARCH PERFORMED BY THE CENTER WILL ENABLE EFFORT ACROSS THE RESEARCH-TO-PRACTICE CYCLE THAT SYSTEMATICALLY INCLUDES HISTORICALLY MARGINALIZED STUDENTS AND COMMUNITIES INTO ECDINITIATIVES. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL AND MAXIMIZE THE CHANCES OF A FUNDED PROPOSAL, THE FOLLOWING PRIMARY OBJECTIVES WILL BE MET WITHIN THE PLANNING PROPOSAL: ALIGN CORE TEAM THROUGH REGULAR VIRTUAL MEETINGS; ARTICULATE CORE CONCEPT OF RESEARCH; DEVELOP INITIAL DELPHI PROMPTS; PLAN AND PERFORM DISCOVERY PHASES OF A DELPHI METHOD; CONDUCT AN INTENSIVE TWO DAY WORKSHOP; AND WRITE AND REFINE PROPOSAL USING INFORMATION FROM FIRST TWO PHASES OF DELPHI. THIS EFFORT WILL PRODUCE NEW KNOWLEDGE ON WHAT AN INCLUSIVE ECD IS AND HOW IT CAN BE ACCOMPLISHED IN PRACTICE. THROUGH SUPPORTING INCLUSIVE AND CULTURALLY RELEVANT ECD PRACTICE, STUDENTS FROM HISTORICALLY MINORITIZED DEMOGRAPHICS WILL BE SUPPORTED TO OBTAIN TRANSFORMATIONAL OUTCOMES WITHIN ECD INITIATIVES AND BY EXTENSION INCREASE THE LIKELIHOOD TO REMAIN AND SUCCEED IN ENGINEERING. ULTIMATELY, AS PROMOTED BY THE OFFICE OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY POLICY OF THE WHITE HOUSE, FEDERALLY FUNDED RESEARCH WILL, MOVING FORWARD, TRY TO INCLUDE COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE AND INTEREST FROM ITS INCEPTION (GENERATING RESEARCH QUESTIONS) TO ITS CONCLUSION (RESEARCH DELIVERABLES) (NATIONAL ACADEMIES, 2022). HENCE, THIS INCLUSION OF COMMUNITIES IN RESEARCH AND DESIGN THAT ECD OFFERS WILL CHALLENGE STEM (SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING AND MATHEMATICS) EDUCATION AT LARGE TO DEVELOP A STUDENT WORKFORCE CAPABLE OF EFFECTIVELY INTERACTING AND CO-DEVELOPING WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND BEING DIVERSE ENOUGH TO EMPATHIZE WITH THE REALITIES AND CHALLENGES OF RACIALLY, ETHNICALLY, AND SOCIO-ECONOMICALLY DIVERSE COMMUNITIES. THROUGH DEVELOPING AND EXPLORING INCLUSIVE AND CULTURALLY RELEVANT ECD CONTEXTS, THIS PLANNING GRANT, AND IN TURN, THE FULL GRANT, CAN ENABLE THE USE OF ECD PROBLEM DOMAINS AND CONTEXTS THAT CRITICALLY ENGAGE ISSUES OF MARGINALIZATION AND SOCIAL JUSTICE TO PROMOTE DIVERSE AND EQUITABLE ECD PARTICIPATION WITHIN ENGINEERING EDUCATION. COLLECTIVELY, THESE IMPACTS WILL STRENGTHEN ENGINEERING INSTITUTIONS? ABILITY TO SERVE AS VEHICLES FOR BROADENING PARTICIPATION. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.
description.2968: DEVELOPING CHAMPIONS OF DIVERSITY WITH APPRECIATIVE INQUIRY AND COMPUTATIONAL SIMULATION (CHAMPIONS) -THE CHAMPIONS (DEVELOPING CHAMPIONS OF DIVERSITY WITH APPRECIATIVE INQUIRY AND COMPUTATIONAL SIMULATION) PROJECT AIMS TO ADDRESS THE PERSISTENT LACK OF DIVERSITY IN THE GEOSCIENCES FIELD BY TAKING A UNIQUE AND INCLUSIVE APPROACH. BY EMBRACING THE PRINCIPLES OF BELONGING, ACCESSIBILITY, JUSTICE, EQUITY, DIVERSITY, AND INCLUSION (BAJEDI), THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO EMPOWER GEOSCIENCES FACULTY TO BECOME CATALYSTS FOR CHANGE WITHIN THEIR DEPARTMENTS. THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS PROJECT LIES IN ITS BOTTOM-UP APPROACH, WHICH EMPHASIZES COMPASSION, EMPATHY, AND THE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF INDIVIDUAL FACULTY MEMBERS. BY CREATING A POSITIVE AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT THAT VALUES DIVERSE VIEWPOINTS AND EXPERIENCES, THE PROJECT AIMS TO FOSTER A SENSE OF EMPOWERMENT FOR UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITY (URM) FACULTY, ENABLING THEM TO LEAD FROM WITHIN AND DRIVE SUSTAINED PROGRESS IN BROADENING PARTICIPATION OUTCOMES. THE CHAMPIONS PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH A THREE-STEP PROCESS. 1) CONVENE AN APPRECIATIVE INQUIRY SUMMIT THAT ENGAGES GEOSCIENCES FACULTY IN IDENTIFYING CHALLENGES AND DESIRED BAJEDI OUTCOMES WITHIN THEIR DEPARTMENTS. THIS QUALITATIVE APPROACH ALLOWS FOR A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE SPECIFIC OBSTACLES AND OPPORTUNITIES THAT EXIST IN EACH UNIQUE CONTEXT. 2) DEVELOP A COMPUTATIONAL SIMULATION MODEL THAT WILL BE INFORMED BY THE DATA COLLECTED FROM THE SUMMIT. THE MODEL WILL SIMULATE THE LONG-TERM IMPACTS OF BOTTOM-UP INTERVENTIONS ON BAJEDI OUTCOMES IN THE GEOSCIENCES. 3) DEPLOY THE MODEL TO SERVE AS A DECISION-MAKING TOOL, TRAINING FACULTY IN SYSTEMIC AND LONG-TERM THINKING WHEN ADDRESSING BAJEDI ISSUES. BY ENABLING FACULTY TO VISUALIZE THE POTENTIAL EFFECTS OF THEIR INTERVENTIONS, THE PROJECT AIMS TO FOSTER INTENTIONAL AND EFFECTIVE STRATEGIES. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.
description.2969: COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: A QUALITATIVE INQUIRY INTO SEX/GENDER NARRATIVES IN UNDERGRADUATE BIOLOGY AND THEIR IMPACTS ON TRANSGENDER, NON-BINARY, AND GENDER NON-CONFORMING STUDENTS -THIS PROJECT EXAMINES HOW A MORE ACCURATE CURRICULUM ABOUT THE DIVERSITY OF SEXES FOUND ACROSS SPECIES, THE ROLE OF THE ENVIRONMENT IN SEX DETERMINATION, AND THE COMPLEX RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SEX AND GENDER CAN CREATE A MORE INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT FOR TRANSGENDER, NON-BINARY, AND GENDER NON-CONFORMING (TNG) STUDENTS IN UNDERGRADUATE BIOLOGY COURSES. RESEARCH INDICATES THAT RATHER THAN EMPHASIZING THE DIVERSITY OF STRATEGIES AND EXPERIENCES THAT ORGANISMS HAVE AROUND SEX, GENDER, AND ORIENTATION, BIOLOGY COURSES OFTEN INACCURATELY CATEGORIZE SEX AND GENDER AS BINARY. THE OVERSIMPLIFICATION OF SEX AND GENDER INTO BINARY CATEGORIES CAN MAKE BIOLOGY CLASSROOMS PARTICULARLY CHALLENGING FOR TNG STUDENTS. EARLY DATA SUGGEST THAT HOW SEX AND GENDER TOPICS ARE REPRESENTED IN THE BIOLOGY CURRICULUM IMPACTS TNG STUDENTS? SENSE OF BELONGING AND INTEREST IN BIOLOGY. UNDERSTANDING TNG STUDENTS? EXPERIENCES WITH BIOLOGY CONTENT WILL SUPPORT THE DESIGN OF INTERVENTIONS AND CURRICULUM INCLUSIVE OF BOTH TNG AND INTERSEX STUDENTS. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO HELP ALL BIOLOGY STUDENTS DEVELOP INCLUSIVE AND SCIENTIFICALLY ACCURATE UNDERSTANDINGS OF SEX AND GENDER. FINALLY, THIS WORK WILL POSITIVELY IMPACT THE CAREER COMPETENCIES OF ALL BIOLOGY MAJORS WHO WILL NEED SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE TO WORK WITH DIVERSE PATIENTS, STAKEHOLDERS, AND TEAMS. GUIDED BY MASTER NARRATIVE THEORY, THE GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO: 1) EXPLORE HOW SEX AND GENDER ARE CURRENTLY REPRESENTED IN THE UNDERGRADUATE BIOLOGY CONTENT, 2) DESCRIBE THE IMPACT THIS CONTENT HAS ON CLASSROOM CLIMATE AND BELONGING FOR TNG STUDENTS, AND 3) CHARACTERIZE THE CURRENT EFFORTS OF BIOLOGY INSTRUCTORS TO CREATE A MORE INCLUSIVE CLIMATE FOR TNG STUDENTS. MASTER NARRATIVE THEORY DECIPHERS HOW MESSAGES IN THE CULTURAL ENVIRONMENT BECOME INTERNALIZED AND IMPACT THE DEVELOPMENT OF PERSONAL IDENTITY. THE SAMPLE WILL INCLUDE TNG STUDENTS WITH DIVERSE RACIAL/ETHNIC AND SOCIAL IDENTITIES ALONG WITH BIOLOGY INSTRUCTORS RECRUITED FROM A VARIETY OF INSTITUTIONS. DATA COLLECTED WILL INCLUDE PARTICIPANT INTERVIEWS (RECORDED AND TRANSCRIBED), PARTICIPANT BASELINE DEMOGRAPHIC SURVEYS, COURSE OBSERVATIONS (E.G., VIDEO RECORDINGS), AND COURSE ARTIFACTS (E.G., LESSON PLAN, ASSESSMENT QUESTIONS). FEMINIST PHENOMENOLOGY, QUALITATIVE CONTENT ANALYSIS, AND DOCUMENT ANALYSIS WILL BE USED TO ANALYZE THE DATA. THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE (A) IDENTIFYING ASPECTS OF BIOLOGY CONTENT THAT COULD INFLUENCE THE SENSE OF BELONGING OF TNG STUDENTS AND IMPACT THE CAREER COMPETENCY OF ALL BIOLOGY MAJORS, (B) DESCRIBING FACTORS THAT CAN HELP OR HINDER INSTRUCTORS AS THEY TRY TO CREATE MORE INCLUSIVE AND ACCURATE BIOLOGY CURRICULA RELATED TO SEX AND GENDER, AND (C) CREATING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT MATERIALS TO SUPPORT INSTRUCTORS WHO DESIGN LESSONS AROUND BIOLOGY TOPICS RELATED TO SEX AND GENDER. THIS PROJECT IS SUPPORTED BY NSF'S EHR CORE RESEARCH (ECR) PROGRAM. THE ECR PROGRAM EMPHASIZES FUNDAMENTAL STEM EDUCATION RESEARCH THAT GENERATES FOUNDATIONAL KNOWLEDGE IN THE FIELD. INVESTMENTS ARE MADE IN CRITICAL AREAS THAT ARE ESSENTIAL, BROAD AND ENDURING: STEM LEARNING AND STEM LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS, BROADENING PARTICIPATION IN STEM, AND STEM WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT. THE PROGRAM SUPPORTS THE ACCUMULATION OF ROBUST EVIDENCE TO INFORM EFFORTS TO UNDERSTAND, BUILD THEORY TO EXPLAIN, AND SUGGEST INTERVENTION AND INNOVATIONS TO ADDRESS PERSISTENT. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

description.3149: THE MBDA CAPITAL READINESS PROGRAM (PROGRAM) IS DESIGNED TO HELP CLOSE THE ENTREPRENEURSHIP GAP BETWEEN SOCIALLY AND ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED INDIVIDUALS (SEDI) AND NON-SEDI. description.3260: THE COMMUNITY FOOD MOBILIZATION IN CHICAGO (CF-MOB) PROJECT INVESTIGATES MECHANISMS TOTRANSFORM THE STRUCTURES OF FOOD PRODUCTION AND DISTRIBUTION IN WAYS THAT CENTER RACIAL JUSTICE,SOVEREIGNTY AND COMMUNITY FOOD ACCESS. IT AIMS TO ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF PUBLIC PROCUREMENT'S ROLE IN INVESTING IN LOCAL, EQUITABLE FOOD SUPPLY CHAIN DEVELOPMENT, WHILE EMPOWERING AND CREATING SPACE FOR BLACK, INDIGENOUS AND PEOPLE OF COLOR (BIPOC) FOOD STAKEHOLDERS TO SELF-DETERMINE THEIR PARTICIPATION IN IT. CF-MOB LEVERAGES STRONG MULTI-SECTORAL PARTNERSHIPS AMONG FOOD PRODUCERS, WORKERS, EATERS, ADVOCATES AND PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS AROUND THE METRO CHICAGO GOOD FOOD PURCHASING INITIATIVE (GFPI). GFPI AIMS TO REORIENT PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS' LARGE SPENDING ON FOOD TOWARDS PRODUCTS ALIGNED WITH FIVE GOOD FOOD VALUES AND ANCHORS RESOURCES FOR BIPOC STAKEHOLDERS TO BENEFIT FROM IT. THIS MASSIVE CHALLENGE REQUIRES TARGETED RESEARCH TO IDENTIFY MECHANISMS FOR OVERCOMING RESOURCE APARTHEID AND ARTICULATING STRATEGIC ROLES FOR PUBLIC PROCUREMENT IN THIS PROCESS. THE TEAM WILL RESEARCH STRUCTURAL BARRIERS AND PRACTITIONER EXPERIENCES ALONG THE FOOD SUPPLY CHAIN, INCLUDING THE COMMUNITY'S DIVERSE VISIONS TO DESIGN A SET OF INNOVATIVE, FOOD MOBILIZATION PATHWAYS. THEY WILL IDENTIFY A SHORTLIST OF HIGH-IMPACT, SUSTAINABLE FOOD PRODUCTS AVAILABLE IN THE 300-MILE RADIUS CHICAGO FOODSHED, IDENTIFY AND MAP SUPPLY CHAIN GAPS FOR GFPI-ALIGNED PRODUCTS, AND MODEL BUDGETARY SCENARIOS AND PROCUREMENT PROCESS REFORMS ENABLING INTEGRATION OF LOCAL FOOD SUPPLIERS, ESPECIALLY BIPOC, INTO INSTITUTIONAL PROCUREMENT PROCESSES. THEY WILL DEVELOP A DIGITAL PLATFORM--METRO CHICAGO GOOD FOOD DASHBOARD--TO SHARE INFORMATION ABOUT FOOD PROCUREMENT AND MOBILIZATION OPPORTUNITIES, AND CONNECT THE DIVERSE CONSTITUENCIES ACROSS CHICAGOLAND.

description.3274:
THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS (MDOC) IS COMMITTED TO A NEW MODEL OF CORRECTIONS, PROMOTING THE SAFETY AND WELL-BEING OF STAFF AND RESIDENTS, WHILE ENSURING RESIDENTS AND COMMUNITY CLIENTS SEE FEWER BARRIERS AS THEY ENGAGE WITH REHABILITATIVE-FOCUSED SERVICES. THIS PHILOSOPHY, KNOWN AS THE MAINE MODEL OF CORRECTIONS, IS FOUNDED ON PRINCIPLES OF NORMALIZATION AND HUMANIZATION, WITH EMPHASIS ON DESTIGMATIZATION, RESPECT, AND MODERNIZATION. SIMPLY, THE GOAL IS TO REBUILD AND TRANSFORM LIVES. 

THE NATIONAL STATE OF EMERGENCY WILL END MAY 2023, A SIGNIFICANT NUMBER OF MDOC RESIDENTS WHO QUALIFY FOR MAINECARE UPON RELEASE WILL NO LONGER BE ELIGIBLE. THE HEALTH CARE MARKETPLACE WILL PROVIDE A OPTION FOR HEALTH INSURANCE, BUT INCARCERATED PERSONS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE TO APPLY UNTIL AFTER RELEASED INTO THE COMMUNITY. WITHOUT HEALTH INSURANCE, THE ABILITY TO COVER TREATMENT AND MEDICATION FOR COMMUNITY-BASED OPIOID USE DISORDER TREATMENT SERVICES WILL BE LIMITED OR NON-EXISTENT. AS STUDIES SHOW, THE RISK OF DEATH FROM AN OPIOID OVERDOSE TWO WEEKS AFTER COMMUNITY REENTRY IS GREATER THAN 40% COMPARED TO THE RISK OF DEATH IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. AT ONE-YEAR POST-RELEASE THE RISK OF OPIOID-RELATED FATAL OVERDOSE FOR FORMERLY INCARCERATED INDIVIDUALS IS 11% GREATER THAN THE RISK FOR THOSE IN THE GENERAL POPULATION.

TO REDUCE OVERDOSE AND RELAPSE, MDOC WILL PARTNER WITH GROUPS RECOVER TOGETHER FOR COUNSELING, TREATMENT, AND MEDICATION FOR RESIDENTS UP TO 8-WEEKS POST-RELEASE. A RESEARCH AND EVALUATION PARTNER WILL BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH A REQUEST FOR APPLICATIONS (RFA) TO COMPETE MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, AND YEARLY ANALYSIS OF THE PROJECT. THE TARGET POPULATION WILL INCLUDE RESIDENTS RECEIVING MEDICATIONS FOR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (MSUD) TREATMENT, THOSE RELEASING FROM THE REENTRY CENTERS, AND THOSE WHO DO NOT HAVE ACCESS TO MAINECARE AT TIME OF RELEASE. 

THE PROJECT IDENTIFIES FIVE GOALS: 1) INCREASED ACCESS TO COMMUNITY-BASED MSUD SERVICES FOR RESIDENTS REENTERING FROM SECURE CONFINEMENT; 2) REDUCE BARRIERS TO MSUD TREATMENT INCLUDING ACCESS TO INTERNET, PHONES, TRANSPORTATION; 3) REDUCE RISK OF FATAL OVERDOSE UPON RELEASE FROM SECURE CONFINEMENT; 4) REDUCE OVERALL RECIDIVISM OVER THREE-YEARS BY 2%; AND 5) REDUCE SUBSTANCE USE CRIME RECIDIVISM OVER THREE-YEARS BY 2%.

THE DEPARTMENTS MISSION IS TO MAKE OUR COMMUNITIES SAFER BY REDUCING HARM THROUGH SUPPORTIVE INTERVENTION, EMPOWERING CHANGE, AND RESTORING LIVES. THIS PROJECT WILL ENSURE THAT RESIDENTS RECEIVING OR IN NEED OF MSUD TREATMENT WILL RECEIVE IT WITH DIGNITY AND RESPECT. 




[1] SHABBAR I. RANAPURWALA ET AL. OPIOID OVERDOSE MORTALITY AMONG FORMER NORTH CAROLINA INMATES: 20002015, AMERICAN JOURNAL OF PUBLIC

description.3277:
NEW ENGLAND ARAB AMERICAN ORGANIZATION (NEAAO), A NON-PROFIT 501C3 ETHNIC-BASED ORGANIZATION, WILL COLLABORATE WITH UNIFIED ASIAN COMMUNITIES AND EQUALITY MAINE TO IMPLEMENT MAKING MAINE A PLACE WITHOUT HATE, A STATE-WIDE EFFORT TO IMPROVE RESPONSE TO HATE CRIME, INCREASE REPORTING, ENHANCE VICTIM SERVICES, AND ESTABLISH HATE CRIME AS A PRIORITY AMONG LAW ENFORCEMENT, JUSTICE SYSTEMS, AND WITHIN OUR COMMUNITIES AND NEIGHBORHOODS.  THROUGH THIS PROJECT PARTNERS WILL ESTABLISH A TASK FORCE AGAINST HATE CRIME THAT BRINGS TOGETHER MAINE'S DIVERSE COMMUNITIES, DISTRICT ATTORNEYS, CIVIL RIGHTS SPECIALISTS AND DETECTIVES, MEMBERS OF THE MAINE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S OFFICE, AND A WIDE VARIETY OF STAKEHOLDERS.  THE PARTNERSHIP OF THE THREE ORGANIZATIONS REFLECTS PRIMARY COMMUNITIES IN MAINE THAT HAVE BEEN TARGETED OVER THE LAST FIVE YEARS, AND WHO ALSO HAVE HISTORIES OF WORKING EFFECTIVELY WITHIN SYSTEMS THAT PROSECUTE HATE-FUELED CRIMES AND INCIDENTS.  

MAKING MAINE A STATE WITHOUT HATE BUILDS ON NEAAO'S CURRENT WORK ADDRESSING HATE CRIME THROUGH A FUTURES WITHOUT VIOLENCE COMMUNITY IMPACT GRANT.  THE BJA GRANT WILL ENABLE NEAAO TO PARTNER WITH COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO CONTINUE BUILDING RELATIONSHIPS AMONG DISTRICT ATTORNEYS, THE MAINE ATTORNEY GENERALS OFFICE, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT. TASK FORCE EFFORTS WILL ALSO SUPPORT A MAJOR PUBLIC INFORMATION CAMPAIGN COMPRISED OF PSAS, SOCIAL MEDIA, MUNICIPAL SIGNAGE AND WIDESPREAD OUTREACH TO IMMIGRANT, LGBTQI+ AND BIPOC COMMUNITIES TO ENCOURAGE REPORTING.  BETWEEN 2019 AND 2021, THE NUMBER OF HATE CRIME REPORTS INCREASED FROM 19 TO 83, WITH THE BULK OF CRIMES TARGETING PEOPLE OF COLOR, ASIAN AMERICANS, MUSLIMS AND LGBTQ+ INDIVIDUALS.  MAINE ALSO CONTENDS WITH SOME VERY ACTIVE WHITE SUPREMACY GROUPS, INCLUDING PATRIOT FRONT AND NSC-13.

THE PROJECT TAKES A THREE-PRONG APPROACH TO PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION:  1) BUILD RELATIONSHIPS AND UNDERSTANDINGS THROUGH A MONTHLY TASK FORCE AGAINST HATE CRIME;  2) ENGAGE IN CULTURALLY AND LINGUISTICALLY APPROPRIATE OUTREACH TO TARGETED COMMUNITIES  TO INCREASE REPORTING AND BUILD TRUST; AND 3) DEVELOP A STRONG AND WELL-RESOURCED VICTIM SERVICE NETWORK THAT CAN RESPOND QUICKLY AND ALSO PROMOTE HEALING. 

WHILE MAKING MAINE A STATE WITHOUT HATE INVOLVES THREE MAJOR PARTNERS, THERE ARE MORE THAN 60 ORGANIZATIONS, POLICE DEPARTMENTS, AND JUSTICE PROFESSIONALS WHO WILL BE INVOLVED IN GROWING THE PROGRAM OVER THREE YEARS AND ENSURING SUCCESS.
description.3278: THE MAINE STATISTICAL ANALYSIS CENTER (SAC), PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT A CORE CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT: INCREASING ACCESS TO MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA THROUGH BUILDING A FOUNDATIONAL DATA WAREHOUSE INFRASTRUCTURE. INNOVATIONS IN DATA MANAGEMENT AND ANALYSIS SYSTEMS NOW MAKE IT POSSIBLE TO COLLECT, PROCESS, AND REPORT MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA GENERATED BY NUMEROUS STATE AGENCIES IN AN ACCURATE, PROMPT, AND ACCESSIBLE FASHION. HOWEVER, MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA ARE HOUSED IN A MULTITUDE OF LOCATIONS AND A SOLE REPOSITORY DOES NOT CURRENTLY EXIST. THEREFORE, THIS PROPOSED ONE-YEAR PROJECT AIMS TO INCREASE ACCESS TO MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA BY DEVELOPING A FOUNDATIONAL DATA STORAGE AND MANAGEMENT INFRASTRUCTURE TO DO JUST THAT. THE MAINE SAC SEEKS TO USE STRUCTURED QUERY LANGUAGE SERVER TO CREATE A MAINE SAC DATA WAREHOUSE THAT WILL BE CAPABLE OF STORING, MANIPULATING, AND MANAGING CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA IN ONE SCALABLE ENVIRONMENT. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE USING NATIONAL INCIDENT-BASED REPORTING SYSTEM DATA AND MAINE PROSECUTORIAL DATA TO BUILD APPROPRIATE TABLES AND SCHEMA THAT WILL BE CAPABLE OF EFFICIENTLY INCORPORATING NEW DATA IMPORTS AND UPDATING EXISTING DATA. ONCE BUILT, THE MAINE SAC DATA WAREHOUSE WILL BE DIRECTLY LINKED TO POWER BI SO THAT CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA CAN BE EFFECTIVELY VISUALIZED THROUGH TOPIC-SPECIFIC, PUBLIC-FACING DATA DASHBOARDS ON THE MAINE SAC WEBSITE. THIS CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORT WILL MAKE THE MAINE SAC WELL-POSITIONED FOR FUTURE COLLABORATIONS WITH MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE AGENCIES THAT SEEK TO USE INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS FOR COMPLEX DATASETS AND MAKE MEANINGFUL DATA AVAILABLE TO A WIDE AUDIENCE.
description.3279: THE LONG AND DIVERSE BORDERLINE OF THE U.S. POSES A GREAT CHALLENGE FOR HSE TO MANAGE IT IN AN EFFICIENT WAY. ONE PROMISING DIRECTION TO EXPLORE IS UTILIZATION OF UNMANNED VEHICLES (UVS) TO HELP TO SECURE AND MANAGE THE BORDERS. TO FULLY UNLEASH THE POTENTIAL OF UVS TO IMPROVE THE OPERATION EFFICIENCY ON BORDER SECURITY, IT IS NECESSARY TO LEVERAGE RECENT PROGRESSES IN AI FOR UV CONTROL AND USE DIFFERENT TYPES OF UVS TO FORM A SWARM. THE RESEARCH COMPONENT OF THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON THREE ASPECTS OF BUILDING SUCH SYSTEM FOR HSE TASKS: AI-BASED SWARM CONTROL, GRAPH THEORY FOR FORMATION CONTROL, AND SECURITY OF AI-DRIVEN SWARM, INCLUDING THEIR APPLICATIONS IN COUNTER-DRONE. THE EDUCATION COMPONENT IS INTEGRATED WITH THE RESEARCH TASKS. BY COLLABORATING WITH A WIDE RANGE OF STAKEHOLDERS (DHS COES, INDUSTRY PARTNERS, AND COMMUNITY COLLEGES), THE PROJECT WILL EXPOSE STUDENTS FROM CSUN AND PARTNER COMMUNITY COLLEGES TO CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCHES ON SWARM FOR HS TASKS, AND OBTAINING INTERNSHIPS OPPORTUNITIES. THESE EXPERIENCES HELPS THEM TO PURSUE HIGHER DEGREES AND FINALLY ENHANCE THE DIVERSITY OF HIGH QUALITY HSE WORKFORCE.
description.3280: THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE) IS FACING A SIGNIFICANT TASK IN DEVELOPING A SKILLED AND DIVERSE WORKFORCE THAT CAN ADDRESS THE COMPLEX AND EVOLVING THREATS TO NATIONAL SECURITY. TO BE READY FOR FUTURE CHALLENGES, HSE REQUIRES A DIVERSE AND COMPETENT WORKFORCE THAT SPECIALIZES IN AREAS SUCH AS COUNTER TERRORISM, BORDER SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY, SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT. THERE IS A PARTICULAR NEED IN THE LOS ANGELES AND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA REGION, WHERE THE BORDER, MAJOR PORTS (LONG BEACH AND LA) AND INTERNATIONAL AIRPORTS (LAX) PRESENT CRITICAL SECURITY CHALLENGES SUCH AS INTERNATIONAL TRADE AND IMMIGRATION. THE REGION ALSO HAS A HIGH LIKELIHOOD OF EXPERIENCING NATURAL HAZARDS LIKE WILDFIRE, EARTHQUAKE, DROUGHT, HEATWAVES, AND FLOODS, WITH VULNERABLE POPULATIONS AND LOCATIONS ESPECIALLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO THESE DISASTERS. AS A MINORITY SERVING INSTITUTION (MSI) IN THE REGION, CSUDH CAN PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN TRAINING A QUALIFIED, MORE DIVERSE HS WORKFORCE BY CREATING EVIDENCE-BASED CAREER PATHWAYS FROM COMMUNITY COLLEGES TO OUR CAMPUS, ON TO USC AND BEYOND, AS WELL AS CONDUCTING STATE-OF-THE-ART RESEARCH ALONGSIDE STUDENTS ON INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS TO INFORM REGIONAL HSE STAKEHOLDERS.WE PROPOSE LAUNCHING THE HOMELAND SECURITY INITIATIVE AT CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, DOMINGUEZ HILLS (CSUDH) TO BUILD OUR UNIVERSITY CAPACITY IN INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT FOR HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE) TO SERVE THE LOS ANGELES REGION. THE INITIATIVE HAS THREE MAJOR GOALS: 1) RECRUIT AND SUPPORT STUDENTS TOWARDS COMPLETING SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATHEMATICS (STEM) OR HOMELAND SECURITY (HS) RELATED DEGREES THROUGH IMPROVED HS-RELEVANT CURRICULA, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND INTEGRATED RESEARCH  2) BUILD RESEARCH CAPACITY IN HSE TOPICS AT CSUDH THROUGH SUPPORTING INNOVATIVE, INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROJECTS AND FUNDING DEVELOPMENT  3) DEVELOP A DIVERSE AND QUALIFIED WORKFORCE THAT IS READY FOR THE FUTURE HS CHALLENGES, ESPECIALLY IN THE LOS ANGELES REGION.       THE FIRST GOAL OF EDUCATIONAL OUTCOMES IS ACHIEVED THROUGH THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES: 1) DEVELOPING 4 NEW COURSES FOR HSE THAT ARE DESIGNED TO THE LATEST PEDAGOGICAL STANDARDS, INCORPORATE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, AND FACILITATE CULTURAL COMPETENCY  2) UPDATING 17 EXISTING HOMELAND SECURITY-RELATED COURSES IN VARIOUS DEGREE PROGRAMS TO MEET THESE SAME STANDARDS  3) STUDENT RECRUITMENT AT PARTNERING COMMUNITY COLLEGES  4) AWARDING 20 DHS SLA SCHOLARSHIPS OVER FIVE YEARS TO SUPPORT STUDENT LEARNING 5) HOSTING 3 SERIES OF EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND TRAINING PROGRAMS.FOR OUR SECOND GOAL OF BUILD RESEARCH CAPACITY IN HSE, WE WILL LAUNCH 1) 14 IMPACTFUL INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROJECTS, WHICH COVERS TOPICS INCLUDING CYBERSECURITY, MARITIME SECURITY, SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTION, SYSTEM ENGINEERING, DISASTER MANAGEMENT, COUNTERTERRORISM AND SOCIAL MEDIA ANALYTICS  2) INTEGRATION OF STUDENTS AND FACULTY IN PROPOSED RESEARCH PROJECTS WITH 30 STUDENT RAS  3) RESEARCH COLLABORATION WITH DHS COE, USC CENTER FOR RISK AND ECONOMIC ANALYSIS OF THREATS AND EMERGENCIES (CREATE) TO SUPPORT CSUDH STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND FACULTY DEVELOPMENT  4) INCENTIVES FOR GRANT DEVELOPMENT, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS AND OTHER CAPACITY BUILDING ACTIVITIES.THE THIRD GOAL IS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT WITH A FOCUS IN THE LA REGION. WE WILL DEVELOP: 1) STUDENT INTERNSHIP PROGRAM WITH REGIONAL PARTNERS (TOTAL OF 15 INTERNSHIP STIPENDS)  2) MENTORSHIP PROGRAM  FOR HSE WORKING PROJECTS TO PROVIDE CAREER GUIDANCE TO CSUDH AND LASC STUDENTS  3) CAREER TRAINING AND APPRENTICESHIP OPPORTUNITIES WITH SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD (SBWIB) IN AREAS SUCH AS CYBER SECURITY  4) PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND NETWORKING EVENTS HELD REGULARLY ON CAMPUS.
description.3281: THE ALASKA PARTE (PROGRAM FOR ARCTIC RESEARCH, TRAINING AND EDUCATION) SERVES TO GREATLY ASSIST THE RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATION INTERNSHIP PROGRAMS THAT EXIST WITHIN THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKAS (UA), ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) AND APPLIED ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH CENTER (AERC). THESE CENTERS SHARE A MISSION THAT ENCOMPASS PROGRAMS DESIGNATED FOR CAREER DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES AND DIRECTLY ENGAGE WITH UA COMMUNITY CAMPUSES AND CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS. ADDITIONALLY, THE EXPECTATION FOR STUDENTS INCLUDES FILLING ESSENTIAL ROLES IN RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT SUPPORT THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) AND DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (DOD) MISSIONS WHILE ENGAGING STUDENTS IN STEM RELATED ACTIVITIES AND RELATED DISCIPLINES.IN 2022, THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA ANCHORAGE, APPLIED ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH CENTER (AERC) AND ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) INTEGRATED THEIR STUDENT FELLOWSHIP PROGRAMS TO ENHANCE EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES AND SERVE A GREATER NUMBER OF STUDENTS INCLUDING TARGETING UNDERREPRESENTED CLASSES. WHILE BOTH AERC AND ADAC ARE HOUSED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA ANCHORAGE, THEY SUPPORT THE ENTIRE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA (UA) SYSTEM. THE AERC OPERATES ONE OF THE FIRST FEDERALLY AUTHORIZED REGISTERED APPRENTICESHIP TRAINING PROGRAMS FOR RESEARCHERS APPROVED BY THE US DEPARTMENT OF LABOR. MERGING THIS STUDENT SUCCESS INITIATIVE WITH ADACS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, FELLOWSHIP AND ARCTIC SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM PROVIDES A CENTRALIZED UNIT UNDER THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA SYSTEM DESIGNATED TO SUPPORT OUR FEDERAL PARTNERS AND SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTE TO THE UNIVERSITYS MISSION OF TRANSFORMING LIVES THROUGH TEACHING, RESEARCH, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND CREATIVE EXPRESSION IN A DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT. ALASKAS PARTE WILL PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS TO ASSIST THE DHS AND DOD MISSIONS BY ACTIVELY ENGAGING STUDENTS IN RESEARCH PROJECTS ASSOCIATED WITH: ADVANCED DATA ANALYSIS AND VISUALIZATION  ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH CLIMATE CHANGE  COMMUNICATIONS AND INTEROPERABILITY  COMMUNITY (TO INCLUDE ALASKA NATIVE AND RURAL PROBLEMS AND CONCERNS)  COMMERCE  INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE  EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE  MARITIME AND PORT SECURITY  NATURAL DISASTERS AND RELATED GEOPHYSICAL STUDIES  SEARCH AND RESCUE  ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS  BORDER SECURITY  AND DECISION SCIENCES. THE AERC ADAC HAS BEEN PROACTIVE AT ASSISTING EDUCATIONALLY DISADVANTAGED AND UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS IN POSTSECONDARY EDUCATION AS WELL AS MINORITY STUDENTS WITH ASSOCIATE, BACHELORS AND OR ADVANCED DEGREES FOR ALMOST A DECADE. BOTH OF THE CENTERS WERE ESTABLISHED IN 2014, THE ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) IS RECOGNIZED AS A CENTER OF EXCELLENCE (COE) IN MARITIME RESEARCH BY DHS AND BRINGS A WEALTH OF KNOWLEDGE TO SUPPORT STUDENT SUCCESS INITIATIVES. THE AERC CONSISTS OF A DIVERSE NETWORK OF ARCTIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY ACADEMICS AND CURRENTLY HAS MORE THAN A DOZEN PROJECTS FUNDED BY THE UNITED STATES ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS AND PROVIDES PATHWAYS FOR STUDENTS TO PARTICIPATE IN NUMEROUS DOD FUNDED PROJECTS PERTAINING TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE RELATED RESEARCH. BOTH CENTERS HOST STRONG ORGANIZATIONAL AND FISCAL LEADERS AND ADMINISTRATORS THAT SERVE TO CREATE ENRICHING OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS WHILE BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF GOVERNMENT LEADERS AND SCIENTISTS.
description.3282: THIS PROJECT AIMS TO PROVIDE SOUTH TEXAS STUDENTS IN THE COASTAL BEND REGION AS WELL AS INDUSTRY PROFESSIONALS, OPPORTUNITIES IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE EDUCATION. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP INTENSIVE ACCELERATED TRAINING IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE (IAT-CI) FOR HIGH SCHOOL, COMMUNITY COLLEGE, AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AT THE FRESHMAN AND SOPHOMORE LEVELS. TO REACH BROADER AUDIENCES, THE PROGRAM WILL DEVELOP AN ONLINE CERTIFICATE PROGRAM IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE (OCP-CI) THAT ATTRACTS INDUSTRY PROFESSIONALS. THIS WILL GIVE TEXAS A M UNIVERSITY-KINGSVILLE (TAMUK) THE VISIBILITY AND THE CAPABILITY TO PREPARE AND CREDENTIAL PROFESSIONALS TO JOIN THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) WORKFORCE BY PROVIDING CYBER INTELLIGENCE EDUCATION, TRAINING, RESEARCH EXPERIENCES, AWARENESS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO INCREASE THE INVOLVEMENT AND NUMBER OF MARGINALIZED UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITIES AVAILABLE AND QUALIFIED TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE DHS WORKFORCE IN THE FIELD OF CYBER INTELLIGENCE. THIS MULTI-TIERED EDUCATION IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE WILL BE OFFERED BY THE COMPUTER SCIENCE FACULTY AT TAMUK. THE IAT-CI AND OCP-CI PROGRAMS WILL BE OPEN TO ALL STEM AND NON-STEM FIELDS. THE EXISTING PARTNERSHIP WITH THE DHS CBTS COE AT TEXAS A M UNIVERSITY COLLEGE STATION (TAMU) WILL BE LEVERAGED TO MENTOR THE CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT PROCESS FOR THE IAT-CI AND OCP-CI PROGRAMS. THE NEW PARTNERSHIPS WITH DHS CINA COE AT GEORGE MASON UNIVERSITY (MSU) AND LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY (LSU) CAE-CO WILL GROW THE EXPERTISE IN THE CYBER INTELLIGENCE IN THIS PROGRAM. EARLY-CAREER AND RESEARCH FACULTY AND SELECTED STUDENTS FROM TAMUK WILL PARTICIPATE IN CBTSS SUMMER RESEARCH PROGRAM.MOREOVER, THE EARLY-CAREER AND RESEARCH FACULTY WILL DEVELOP A WORLD-CLASS RESEARCH PROGRAM IN AI-BASED CYBER INTELLIGENCE LEVERAGING THE COLLABORATIONS WITH CBTS COE AT TAMU, LSU CENTER OF ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE IN CYBER OPERATIONS (CAE-CO), TEXAS A M UNIVERSITY-SAN ANTONIO, UNIVERSITY OF NORTH TEXAS, AND XAVIER UNIVERSITY OF LOUISIANA. EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES WITH FINANCIAL SUPPORT WILL BE PROVIDED TO ELIGIBLE AND QUALIFIED TAMUK STUDENTS WHO HAVE ALREADY COMPLETED THE IAT-CI TRAINING AND ARE PURSUING A COMPUTER SCIENCE DEGREE OR THE MINOR OR CERTIFICATE PROGRAMS IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE. THE FUNDED POSITIONS WILL INCLUDE SUMMER RESEARCH ASSISTANTSHIPS, FELLOWSHIPS, AND INTERNSHIPS AT TAMU CBTS COE, LSU CAE-CO, NATIONAL LABS, AND PRIVATE INDUSTRIES. MOREOVER, THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A CYBER INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH LAB (CIRL) TO FACILITATE THE PLANNED TRAINING, ONLINE CERTIFICATION, AND UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE RESEARCH IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE. THE EARLY CAREER AND RESEARCH FACULTY WILL LEAD CYBER INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH PROJECTS USING THE CIRL LAB.
description.3283: THERE IS A DEARTH OF STUDENTS, AND PARTICULARLY OF MINORITIZED STUDENTS (E.G., THOSE WHO IDENTIFY AS WOMEN, BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN, AND OR HISPANIC OR LATINX) IN COMPUTING, AND ESPECIALLY THOSE WHO ARE QUALIFIED FOR PROFESSIONS IN HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE). TO BROADEN PARTICIPATION  ENHANCE EDUCATION, RESEARCH, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT IN THE HOMELAND SECURITY SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATHEMATICS (HS-STEM) AREAS  AND BUILD CAPACITY FOR COLLEGE STUDENTS, UNIVERSITY STUDENTS, AND FACULTY TO MAKE CONNECTIONS WITH HSE, FLORIDA INTERNATIONAL UNIVERSITY (FIU) PROPOSES THE CREATION OF THE ADVANCED EDUCATION AND RESEARCH FOR MACHINE LEARNING-DRIVEN CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE (ADMIRE) CENTER. THE ADMIRE CENTER IS EXPECTED TO PROVIDE AN INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EDUCATION FRAMEWORK WITH A SPECIAL FOCUS ON THREE OF THE DHS OPERATIONAL TOPICS OF INTEREST, I.E., CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE, CYBERSECURITY, AND MACHINE LEARNING (ML). THE CENTER BENEFITS FROM COLLABORATIONS WITH MIAMI DADE COLLEGE (MDC), THREE DHS CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE (COE), AND OTHER HSE PARTNERS TO ENRICH THE PROPOSED EDUCATION AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES FOR FIU AND MDC STUDENTS, AS WELL AS FACULTY. THE PROJECT WILL INVOLVE A TEAM OF SEVEN HIGHLY PRODUCTIVE FACULTY MEMBERS (FOUR OF WHOM ARE EARLY CAREER FACULTY) AT FIUS KNIGHT FOUNDATION SCHOOL OF COMPUTING AND INFORMATION SCIENCES AND THE SCHOOL OF UNIVERSAL COMPUTING, CONSTRUCTION, AND ENGINEERING EDUCATION, WHO HAVE STRONG EXPERTISE IN HS-STEM TOPICS, AS WELL AS COMPUTING AND ENGINEERING EDUCATION AND RESEARCH. IN ORDER TO EDUCATE, TRAIN, AND MENTOR STUDENTS AND EARLY CAREER FACULTY, THE CENTER WILL CONDUCT THE FOLLOWING EDUCATION AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES: (1) THE CENTER WILL PROVIDE SCHOLARSHIPS TO CREATE A SUSTAINABLE PIPELINE FOR 2-YEAR MDC STUDENTS TO TRANSITION TO FIU, AS WELL AS OFFERING SCHOLARSHIPS TO FIU UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS SPECIALIZED IN HS-STEM AREAS TO PREPARE THEM FOR HSE CAREERS, PROVIDE THEM WITH EDUCATION, MENTORING, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT RESOURCES, ASSIST THEM WITH INTERNSHIP AND CAREER PLACEMENT AT RESEARCH AND GOVERNMENT LABS, AND AT OUR PARTNER DHS COES  (2) THE CENTER WILL DEVELOP AND INTEGRATE HS-STEM TEACHING MODULES AND RESEARCH OUTCOMES IN EXISTING COMPUTER SCIENCE, INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, CYBERSECURITY, DATA SCIENCE, AND ENGINEERING COURSES AT FIU, AND DEVELOP NEW COURSES TO EXPLORE INNOVATIVE AREAS OF DEPLOYING ML FOR CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE AND SECURITY  (3) STRONG TEAMS OF RESEARCHERS WILL CONDUCT INNOVATIVE RESEARCH PROJECTS IN IMPORTANT AREAS OF CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE AND SECURITY USING ADVANCED ML TECHNIQUES  (4) THE CENTER WILL BUILD CAPACITY FOR RESEARCH AND EDUCATION ON HS-STEM TOPICS BY ENGAGING EARLY CAREER FACULTY WITH THE SUPPORT MENTORSHIP FROM SENIOR FACULTY PARTICIPANTS, EACH WITH PRIOR ENGAGEMENT WITH DHS, AND IN COLLABORATION WITH THREE DHS COES AND OTHER HSE PARTNERS  (5) THE CENTERS RESEARCH OUTCOMES WILL ENLIST TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER ACTIVITIES FOR HSE SUPPORTED BY STARTUP FIU AND OUR INDUSTRY PARTNERS AND THE EDUCATION AND RESEARCH OUTCOMES WILL BE DISSEMINATED TO OTHER INSTITUTIONS FOR INTEGRATION IN THEIR CURRICULUM AND ENSURE SCALABILITY OF OUR HS-STEM EDUCATION EFFORTS.THE CENTER WILL PARTNER WITH THREE DHS COES. THE CENTERS ACTIVITIES ALIGN WELL WITH THE COES GOALS ON HS-STEM EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND WILL PROVIDE RESOURCES FOR PROMOTING THE ACTIVE INVOLVEMENT OF MINORITIZED GROUPS IN THESE COES. WE HAVE DEVELOPED AND DEFINED QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE EVALUATION METRICS TO MONITOR AND EVALUATE THE PROGRAM AND ITS IMPACT ON CAPACITY BUILDING FOR FIU AND MDC, AND SHARE THE PERFORMANCE METRICS WITH THE DHS AND OUR EXTERNAL ADVISORY BOARD FOR EVALUATION AND FEEDBACK. INDEPENDENT EVALUATION WILL ALSO BE PERFORMED PERIODICALLY TO ENSURE PROGRAMMATIC ALIGNMENT WITH DHS GOALS.
description.3284: THE DHC-CREST CENTER AT NCCU AIMS TO ADVANCE INSTITUTIONAL RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL CAPABILITIES IN STEM DISCIPLINES RELATED TO DHS AT NCCU AND STRENGTHEN THE PIPELINE FOR THE ADVANCEMENT OF UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITIES IN DHS STEM DISCIPLINES. THIS WILL BE DONE IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE SENTRY COE AND WILL LEVERAGE THE ASSETS OF BOTH INSTITUTIONS TO ENABLE SIGNIFICANT INCREASES IN MINORITY PARTICIPATION IN MATERIAL SCIENCE AND AT THE SAME TIME PRODUCE RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL OUTCOMES THAT HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT BEYOND THE TIME LIMITS OF THIS FUNDING. THE VISION OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ESTABLISH NCCU AS A PREMIER INSTITUTION IN DHS DETECTOR SCIENCE WITH THE ACCOMPANYING INFRASTRUCTURE AND HUMAN CAPITAL NECESSARY FOR SUCH A TRANSFORMATION. THE RESEARCH THRUST AT THE CORE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS HIGH SELECTIVITY AND HIGH SENSITIVITY LABEL FREE BIOCHEMICAL SENSOR FOR CONTINUING DETECTION BASED ON QUANTUM CONFINEMENT. THE DETECTION PRINCIPLE ALLOWS FOR CONTINUOUS MONITORING WITHOUT DETECTOR REFRESHING, WHICH COULD BE A SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTION TO DHS. THE DETECTOR IS IN MANY WAYS SIMILAR TO THE SENTRY DETECTOR, WHICH CONTINUOUSLY DETECTS TRACES OF TRIACETONE TRIPEROXIDE OR TATP. THAT WILL ALLOW OUR TEAM TO GET VALUABLE EXPERIENCE WORKING FIRST ON THE ELEMENTS OF THE SENTRY DETECTOR AND LATER INCORPORATING OUR DETECTOR INTO THE SENTRY PLATFORM. THE PROPOSED PARTNERSHIP ADDRESSES A KEY EDUCATIONAL CHALLENGE MANIFESTED IN THE LOW PARTICIPATION OF UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITIES IN MATERIAL SCIENCE. THE VISION IS NOT MERELY TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR NCCU STUDENTS TO PARTICIPATE IN THE SENTRY PROGRAM AND THEREBY CORRECT SUCH A DISPARITY. THE INTELLECTUAL MERIT OF THIS PROPOSAL LIES IN THE QUALITY OF THE OPPORTUNITIES PROVIDED AND THE OUTCOMES THAT WILL RESULT. THE FOUR-TIERED PLAN CONSISTS OF A) RECRUITMENT STRATEGIES TARGETED AT THE BEST AND BRIGHTEST HIGH SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY COLLEGE TRANSFER STUDENTS IN THE REGION BY HIGHLIGHTING THE CENTRAL ROLE OF DHS STEM SCIENCE IN THE 21ST CENTURY, B) ACADEMIC ENRICHMENT PROGRAMS FOCUSED ON DHS STEM SCIENCE, C) EFFECTIVE MENTORING PROGRAM WHICH WILL PAIR MINORITY PARTICIPANTS IN THE NCCU WITH MENTORS AT SENTRY AND NCCU, AND D) PRODUCTIVE RESEARCH EXPERIENCES AT THE FRONTIERS OF DHS-STEM SCIENCE SUPPORTED BY CLOSE MENTORING BY BOTH NCCU AND SENTRY FACULTY AND RESEARCHERS AT ALL LEVELS.   THE UNDERLYING FRAMEWORK THAT WILL ENABLE PRODUCTIVE RESEARCH IS THE BROAD AND DEEP LINKS BETWEEN THE INDIVIDUAL RESEARCH THRUSTS AND ONGOING PROJECTS IN THE SENTRY. THESE LINKS WILL LEVERAGE THE EXPERTISE AND RESOURCES IN THE SENTRY TO GENERATE IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC ADVANCES IN THE SHORT TERM AS WELL AS CREATE SUSTAINABLE RESEARCH PROGRAMS AT NCCU IN THESE AREAS AT THE END OF FIVE YEARS.   THE KEY SCIENTIFIC CHALLENGE THAT IS ADDRESSED IN THIS PROPOSAL IS THE ABILITY TO CONTROL TUNNELING BETWEEN A TARGETED ANALYTE AND DETECTOR NANOSTRUCTURE AND TO USE THAT PHENOMENON FOR ANALYTE DETECTION. MANY TECHNICAL PROBLEMS MUST BE SOLVED TO ACHIEVE THAT GOAL, WHICH WILL EXPOSE STUDENTS AND FACULTY TO FIELDS OF ELECTRONICS, DATA ACQUISITION SYSTEMS, MACHINE LEARNING, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, COMPUTER SIMULATIONS, AND MAKING ALGORITHMS, AND SOFTWARE FOR DATA ANALYSIS AND DISPLAY OF DATA. THE FACILITIES AND EXPERTISE AVAILABLE VIA OUR PARTNERS AT SENTRY WOULD BE CRITICAL FOR US HERE AT NCCU TO BE ABLE TO TRANSITION TO A LEVEL WHERE THESE ACHIEVEMENTS CAN BE UTILIZED IN ACTUAL DEVICES.          THE PROJECT WILL CREATE A MULTIDISCIPLINARY DHS SCIENCE COMMUNITY AT NCCU THAT WILL INCREASE PUBLIC AWARENESS OF THE FIELD, RECRUIT TALENTED MINORITY STUDENTS TO THIS FIELD, PREPARE THESE STUDENTS FOR FUTURE CAREERS IN THE FIELD THROUGH COMPREHENSIVE ACADEMIC AND RESEARCH PROGRAMS, AND INCREASE RATES OF MATRICULATION OF MINORITY STUDENTS FROM NCCU TO DHS SCIENCE DOCTORAL PROGRAMS AT SENTRY AND ELSEWHERE. THIS PARTNERSHIP WILL ENABLE US TO ATTAIN A HIGHER LEVEL OF RESEARCH CAPABILITY, ENABLING US TO SUSTAIN A NATIONAL REPUTATION.
description.3285: THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT MULTI-YEAR EFFORTS TO DEVELOP A SUSTAINABLE COMPUTER SCIENCE EDUCATION AND CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH PROGRAM, AND ENHANCE COLLABORATIONS WITH THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE), AND PREPARE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO FIND A STEM CAREER IN HSE DOMAIN AND ALSO TO SURVIVE THE RIGORS OF GRADUATE STUDIES, AND INCREASE THE DIVERSITY IN THE HSE COMMUNITY, AND PROVIDE CREATIVE LEADERSHIP IN DEVELOPING PATHWAYS TO BREAKTHROUGHS IN THE DOMAIN OF DISASTER RESILIENCE AND NATURAL HAZARDS RESEARCH. THIS COLLABORATIVE PROJECT BETWEEN JOHNSON C. SMITH UNIVERSITY (JCSU) AND STANLY COMMUNITY COLLEGE (SCC) WILL DEVELOP A CULTURE OF LEADING-EDGE INNOVATIVE RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT AND TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS WITH RELEVANT EXPERTISE THROUGH EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING   HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE SO AS TO PREPARE STUDENTS TO BE READY FOR CAREERS IN HSE DOMAIN AND GRADUATE SCHOOL IN STEM. THE NEED FOR COMPUTER SCIENCE PROFESSIONALS AND GRADUATES TO FILL THESE NEW JOBS, AND THE REQUISITE TRAINING AND CODING LITERACY, HAS BECOME A MATTER OF NATIONAL IMPORTANCE. THERE ARE MANY PUBLIC STUDIES WHICH ALSO SUGGESTED THAT EDUCATION PROGRAMS COULD BETTER PREPARE STUDENTS FOR A COMPUTER SCIENCE BASED HSE STEM CAREER BY PROVIDING MORE HANDS-ON EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES  INTEGRATING THEORETICAL AND INDUSTRY-STANDARD THEMES IN THE CURRICULUM  AND PROVIDING BETTER CAREER DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT. THE PROPOSED PROGRAM SEEKS TO BRIDGE THE GAP BETWEEN COMPUTER SCIENCE EDUCATION, ENHANCING THE RESEARCH CAPABILITY AND THE WORKFORCE PREPARATION, BY OFFERING ACADEMIC AND RESEARCH SOLUTIONS GEARED TOWARD MEETING CURRENT AND FUTURE MARKET DEMANDS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE LED BY FACULTIES FROM JCSU AND SCC WITH VARIOUS RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDING OVERSEEING FACULTY AND STUDENTS IN RELATIONS TO BUILDING RELATIONS, WHILE ENGAGING ACTIVITIES INVOLVING OTHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, PROGRAM ENTITIES, AS WELL INTERNAL INTERACTIONS WITHIN THE UNIVERSITY. THE PI, CO-PI AND THE PROJECT TEAM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR DEVELOPING CURRICULUM AND RESEARCH PROJECTS, MANAGING STUDENTS ACTIVITIES, AND COLLECTING PROGRAM DATA.
description.3286: THE PROJECT S FUNDING WILL BE USED FOR CYBERSECURITY RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR UNDERREPRESENTED UNDERGRADUATES AND EARLY-CAREER FACULTY MEMBERS  AS WELL AS THE CREATION OF CYBERSECURITY EDUCATION PATHWAYS FOR COMMUNITY COLLEGES AND CERTIFICATE PROGRAMS TO ENHANCE CYBERSECURITY SKILLS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE SUMMER RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATES IN AREAS SUCH AS CYBER-ETHICS, PRIVACY, TRUST AND FRAUD INVESTIGATION, BLOCKCHAIN, CYBER DATAMINING AND MACHINE LEARNING, AND WEB APPLICATION AND GAME DEVELOPMENT. FACULTY, INCLUDING EARLY CAREER JUNIOR MEMBERS, WILL RESEARCH CYBER DATA ANALYTICS, MACHINE LEARNING (ML), ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), MALWARE ANALYSIS, SOFTWARE ASSURANCE, AND MOBILITY WITH CRITICAL CYBERINFRASTRUCTURES INCLUDING ENERGY, AGRICULTURE, AND HEALTHCARE SERVICES. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL DEVELOP NOVEL SOFTWARE TOOLS WITH ALGORITHMS, PROTOTYPES, MODELS, AND MAINTENANCE. THE TEAM WILL ALSO DESIGN MODERN CYBERSECURITY COURSES AND CERTIFICATE PROGRAM FOR ALL STEM STUDENTS IN THE DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION SCIENCE. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL CREATE A PATHWAY FOR COMMUNITY COLLEGE STUDENTS TO TRANSFER TO THE FOUR-YEAR PROGRAM AT UNT--PROVIDING OPPORTUNITIES FOR RE-SKILLING OR UP-SKILLING TOWARDS CYBERSECURITY CAREERS AFTER COMPLETING AN ASSOCIATE DEGREE AT THEIR COMMUNITY COLLEGE.
description.3287: JOBS IN STEM ARE SOME OF THE FASTEST GROWING IN THE WORKFORCE, YET MINORITIES REMAIN UNDERREPRESENTED IN THESE JOBS AT A NATIONAL LEVEL, PARTICULARLY IN THE FIELD OF HOMELAND SECURITY (HS). FIU, WITH COLLABORATIONS FROM MIAMI DADE COLLEGE, GEORGE MASON UNIVERSITYS DHS CENTER OF EXCELLENCE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS AND NETWORK ANALYSIS (DHS COE CINA), AS WELL AS ADDITIONAL HS RESEARCH ENTITIES, WILL ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM BY ENGAGING DIVERSE STUDENTS AND FACULTY IN RESEARCH AND GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE-LEVEL CURRICULA THAT WILL SUPPORT THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE). FLORIDA INTERNATIONAL UNIVERSITY (FIU) IS A MULTI-CAMPUS PUBLIC RESEARCH UNIVERSITY OFFERING A BROAD ARRAY OF UNDERGRADUATE, GRADUATE, AND PROFESSIONAL PROGRAMS. AS A MINORITY-SERVING INSTITUTION (MSI), 85  OF FIU STUDENTS ARE HISPANIC, BLACK, ASIAN OR PACIFIC ISLANDER, OR OTHER MINORITY GROUPS. FIU IS ALSO RANKED R1 (DOCTORAL UNIVERSITIES  VERY HIGH RESEARCH ACTIVITY), THE HIGHEST LEVEL AWARDED IN THE CARNEGIE CLASSIFICATION OF INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION. AS THE LARGEST PRODUCER OF STEM DEGREES FOR HISPANICS IN THE US, FIU HAS ESTABLISHED ITSELF AS A LEADING MSI WORKING TO ADVANCE DIVERSITY IN STEM. THROUGH ITS TWO PREEMINENT PROGRAMS, THE GLOBAL FORENSIC JUSTICE CENTER (GFJC) AND THE STEM TRANSFORMATION INSTITUTE (STEM TI), FIU PROPOSES THE TRANSFORMING FORENSIC CHEMISTRY EDUCATION AND RESEARCH TO SERVE THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE AND ESTABLISH A DIVERSE WORKFORCE PROGRAM. THROUGH THIS ROBUST PROGRAM, FIU WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH TO IMPROVE DETECTION OF CONCEALED THREATS BY INSTRUMENTS AND CANINE, BROADEN THE REACH OF OUR ESTABLISHED FORENSIC PROGRAM TO INCLUDE HS TOPICS, AND CREATE AN EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT TO ENCOURAGE MINORITY PARTICIPATION IN STEM AND HS-RELATED RESEARCH NEEDS. OUR TEAM PROPOSES TO STRENGTHEN DHS APPROACHES STRATEGICALLY AND SCIENTIFICALLY IN BORDER SECURITY, COUNTERING BIOTHREATS IN SUPPLY CHAINS, LAW ENFORCEMENT INVESTIGATIONS, TRANSPORTATION SECURITY AND SCREENING, AND TERRORISM PREVENTION. CO-DIRECTED BY GFJCS PROFESSOR OF FORENSIC CHEMISTRY, DR. LAURYN DEGREEFF, AND STEM TIS PROFESSOR OF CHEMISTRY EDUCATION RESEARCH, DR. JUSTIN CARMEL, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE THE MISSION OF DHS AT THE HIGHEST LEVELS. THE OBJECTIVES OF FIUS SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP AWARD PROPOSAL ARE TO 1) PROVIDE RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS AND FACULTY IN AREAS RELATING TO HS WITH A FOCUS ON PREVENTION OF TERRORISM AND SECURING OUR BORDERS THROUGH VARIOUS METHODS OF THREAT DETECTION  2) RETHINK TRADITIONAL COURSEWORK TO INCLUDE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES FOR STUDENTS AT ALL POST-SECONDARY LEVELS IN ORDER TO PREPARE THEM FOR CAREERS IN THE FIELD OF HS, 3) ENGAGE WITH MIAMI DADE COLLEGE TO BRING CAREER-RELEVANT INFORMATION TO THEIR DOORSTEP AND PROMOTE PATHWAYS TOWARD STEM DEGREE COMPLETION AND TRANSITION FROM 2-YEAR TO 4-YEAR INSTITUTIONS, AND 4) ENGAGE WITH DHS COE CINA AND ADDITIONAL HSE RESEARCH COLLABORATORS TO ENSURE THE PROGRAM EFFECTIVELY SUPPORTS THE HSE. OUR VISION IS THAT THESE AREAS OF RESEARCH AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT WILL BRING FURTHER ALIGNMENT OF PRACTICES AND CAPABILITIES TO MAKE IMMEDIATE, NOTABLE, AND MEASURABLE IMPACTS TO DETECT AND DETER TERRORISM AND INCREASE SECURITY FOR ALL OUR CITIZENS, AS WELL AS BUILD A PREPARED, KNOWLEDGEABLE, AND DIVERSE WORKFORCE FOR THE HSE.

description.3310: THE CHILDREN'S MUSEUM OF PITTSBURGH, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE ASSOCIATION OF CHILDREN’S MUSEUMS, WILL EXPAND A PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM TO FOSTER INNOVATIVE EXHIBIT DESIGN FOR MUSEUMS CATERING TO CHILDREN AND YOUTH.  THE PROJECT WILL CONDUCT TWO VERSIONS OF THE PROGRAM WITH 100 MID-CAREER STAFF THAT WORK DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY WITH EXHIBITS TO SPARK LOCAL, COMMUNITY-RESPONSIVE INNOVATION THROUGH CURATED CREATIVE EXPERIENCES.  TRAINING ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE IN-PERSON GATHERINGS, VIRTUAL LEARNING, MENTORSHIPS, AND THE CREATION OF ACTION PLANS AND PROTOTYPES BY PARTICIPANTS.  THE PROJECT WILL RE-INVIGORATE THE MUSEUM WORKFORCE THROUGH A CREATIVE APPROACH TO TEACHING INNOVATIVE EXHIBIT DESIGN THAT WILL GENERATE NOVEL EXPERIENCES FOR MUSEUM VISITORS.
description.3311: THE VERMONT HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL WORK WITH LOCAL HISTORICAL SOCIETIES AND MUSEUMS AROUND VERMONT TO HELP DEVELOP SKILLS AMONG THE WORKFORCE AT MOSTLY ALL-VOLUNTEER ORGANIZATIONS.  THE PROJECT AIMS TO ENGAGE UP TO 300 MUSEUM STAFF AND VOLUNTEERS IN USING AN ACTIVE COLLECTIONS FRAMEWORK THAT ENCOURAGES SMALLER AND MORE FOCUSED MUSEUM COLLECTIONS.  PROJECT COMPONENTS INCLUDE FOUR ONE-DAY WORKSHOPS, AND MONTHLY VIRTUAL MEETINGS WITH TWO COHORTS OF HISTORICAL SOCIETIES TO PROVIDE TRAINING, RESOURCES, AND DIRECT ASSISTANCE ON SELF-SELECTED COMPONENTS OF COLLECTIONS-BASED PROJECTS. AN ONLINE RESOURCE CENTER WILL BE CREATED THAT WILL INCLUDE CONTENT FROM THE PROJECT, SUCH AS TRAINING MATERIALS AND COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT RESOURCES THAT MAY SERVE SIMILAR VOLUNTEER-BASED ORGANIZATIONS IN OTHER STATES DEVELOP THE SKILLS OF THEIR VOLUNTEER STAFF TO INCREASE INSTITUTIONAL SUSTAINABILITY AND ENSURE THE CONTINUING PRESERVATION OF LOCAL HISTORY.
description.3312: THE SCIENCE MUSEUM OF MINNESOTA WILL SUPPORT TRANSFORMATIVE CHANGE TOWARD INCLUSION, DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND ACCESS AMONG UPPER MIDWEST MUSEUMS BY CREATING A DURABLE COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE.  USING A FIELD-TESTED MODEL OF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, THE MUSEUM WILL COLLABORATE WITH 20 SMALL, UNDERSERVED MUSEUMS, ACROSS MINNESOTA, IOWA, NORTH DAKOTA, SOUTH DAKOTA, AND WISCONSIN, TO BRING TOGETHER 48 STAFF AND RESEARCHERS, VIRTUALLY AND IN-PERSON, OVER A PERIOD OF TWO YEARS TO LEARN ABOUT THEORIES, METHODS, AND TOOLS RELATED TO EQUITY AND FIND WAYS TO ADAPT THESE IDEAS TO THEIR MUSEUMS AND PROFESSIONAL NETWORKS.  THROUGH ONGOING COMMUNICATION AND CONSULTATION, THE PROJECT WILL GENERATE A LEADERSHIP COHORT OF INDIVIDUALS WITH A SOLID GROUNDING IN COMPLEX EQUITY ISSUES.  THE PROJECT WILL NOT ONLY DEVELOP RESOURCES, SKILLS, TOOLS, AND MINDSETS TO CREATE MORE INCLUSIVE STAFF AND INSTITUTIONS, BUT ALSO MORE INCLUSIVE LOCAL AND REGIONAL COMMUNITIES OF PROFESSIONALS.
description.3313: THE CONSERVATION CENTER FOR ART AND HISTORIC ARTIFACTS (CCAHA) WILL DEVELOP A PILOT WORKFORCE TRAINING PROGRAM FOR CONSERVATION TECHNICIANS.  THE PROJECT RESPONDS TO AN IDENTIFIED NEED TO EXPAND CAREER PATHWAYS IN CONSERVATION FOR PROFESSIONALS WITHOUT A GRADUATE DEGREE.  CCAHA WILL PARTNER WITH DREXEL UNIVERSITY’S LENFEST CENTER FOR CULTURAL PARTNERSHIPS TO CONNECT UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS WITH EXPERIENTIAL TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES WORKING ON DREXEL COLLECTIONS AS CONSERVATION TECHNICIANS. UNDER THE DIRECTION OF CCAHA STAFF, STUDENTS WILL LEARN KEY COMPETENCIES RELATED TO THE HANDLING, TREATMENT AND CARE OF MUSEUM OBJECTS, AS WELL AS SPECIFIC SKILLS RELATED TO THE DIGITIZATION OF MUSEUM COLLECTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A TOOLKIT FOR IMPLEMENTING SIMILAR INITIATIVES BETWEEN HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS AND CONSERVATION LABORATORIES, SO THAT UNDERGRADUATES AT OTHER COLLEGES MAY ALSO BENEFIT.
description.3314: THE FIVE COLLEGE CONSORTIUM WILL BUILD A PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TRAINING PROGRAM THAT CREATES OPPORTUNITIES FOR MUSEUM STAFF AS WELL PATHWAYS FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE INTERNS ENTERING THE MUSEUM WORKFORCE.  THE PROJECT PARTNERS INCLUDE THE CONSORTIUM OF FIVE COLLEGES ALONG WITH SEVEN CAMPUS MUSEUMS AND THREE AFFILIATED MUSEUMS IN WESTERN MASSACHUSETTS.  PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND TRAININGS WITH MUSEUM STAFF BASED ON WORK AREAS AND CAREER INTERESTS TO DEVELOP PATHS FOR GAINING SKILLS AND HELPING GROW THE NEXT GENERATION OF MUSEUM LEADERS.  THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN TRAINING 210 PROFESSIONALS AND OVER 100 UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE INTERNS, FELLOWS, AND ASSISTANTS TO MEET THE CHANGING NEEDS OF MUSEUMS IN ADMINISTRATION, EDUCATION, EXHIBITION DEVELOPMENT, AND COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT.
description.3315: THE GEORGIA O'KEEFFE MUSEUM WILL CREATE A PAID APPRENTICESHIP PROGRAM TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR EMERGING MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS IN NORTHERN NEW MEXICO TO GAIN HANDS ON TRAINING IN COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT AND ART PREPARATION.  MUSEUMS THROUGHOUT THE STATE HAVE EXPERIENCED A SHORTAGE OF QUALIFIED REGISTRARS AND ART HANDLERS WHO RESIDE IN THE COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE.  BUILDING ON A SUCCESSFUL PILOT PROJECT WITH THE INSTITUTE OF AMERICAN INDIAN ARTS, THE MUSEUM WILL EXPAND THE PROGRAM TO INCLUDE OUTREACH AND RECRUITMENT AT A RANGE OF LOCAL HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS.  THE PROJECT IS INTENDED TO FOSTER IMMERSIVE LEARNING EXPERIENCES FOR RECENT GRADUATES ENTERING THE MUSEUM WORKFORCE.  IN ADDITION TO THE APPRENTICESHIPS, THE MUSEUM WILL PROVIDE INFORMATIONAL WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR CURRENT STUDENTS ENROLLED AT PARTNER INSTITUTIONS.  THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN NEW PATHWAYS FOR EMERGING PROFESSIONALS IN THE ARTS AND CULTURE FIELD.
description.3316: HISTORIC NEW ENGLAND WILL PILOT A CROSS-DISCIPLINARY, COHORT-BASED, PAID INTERNSHIP PROGRAM TO ENHANCE EQUITY AND OPPORTUNITY WITHIN THEIR ORGANIZATION AND GENERATE A MODEL FOR SIMILAR ORGANIZATIONS SEEKING TO SUPPORT A MORE DIVERSE AND EMPOWERED MUSEUM WORKFORCE.  THE PROGRAM WILL SEEK TO RECRUIT 76 STUDENTS WHO ARE CURRENTLY ENROLLED IN UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE-LEVEL PROGRAMS, OR THOSE WHO HAVE COMPLETED A DEGREE PROGRAM WITHIN THE LAST 24 MONTHS.  THE INTERNS WILL CONVENE WEEKLY, AS A COHORT, TO RECEIVE TRAINING AND SUPPORT ON MUSEUM OPERATIONS AND NAVIGATING EMPLOYMENT.  AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STUDENTS WILL GAIN TECHNICAL SKILLS, CONNECTIONS WITH PEERS, AND UNDERSTANDING OF MUSEUM OPERATIONS AND THE JOB MARKET.  IN ADDITION, THE PILOT PROJECT WILL CULMINATE IN A WHITE PAPER THAT OUTLINES LESSONS LEARNED AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR IMPLEMENTING PAN-INSTITUTIONAL COHORTS AT PEER INSTITUTIONS, WITH AN EYE TOWARD CREATING SAFE AND MEANINGFUL PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCES FOR PEOPLE OF ALL BACKGROUNDS.
description.3317: THE RUBIN CENTER FOR THE VISUAL ARTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS AT EL PASO WILL EXPAND ITS INTERNSHIP PROGRAM FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN SUPPORT OF EMERGING MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS. WORKING WITH AN OUTSIDE EVALUATOR AND AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE CONSISTING OF FORMER RUBIN CENTER INTERNS, THE MUSEUM TEAM WILL UNDERTAKE A ROBUST REVIEW OF THE 15 YEAR-OLD PROGRAM. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE DEPLOYING A YEARLY RECRUITMENT PLAN AND MATCHING STUDENTS WITH AN INTERNSHIP ALIGNED TO THEIR LEARNING OBJECTIVES. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT SIX PAID UNDERGRADUATE POSITIONS, TRAVEL TO A REGIONAL PARTNER MUSEUM SITE, AND A SERIES OF SPEAKERS FEATURING LATINO MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS. THE OUTCOME OF THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THE PUBLICATION OF AN EVIDENCE-BASED EVALUATION ON THE EFFORTS AND IMPACT OF INTERNSHIPS FOR EMERGING MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS.
description.3318: THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH TEXAS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE MEXICAN AMERICAN CIVIL RIGHTS INSTITUTE WILL CREATE A NEW INTERNSHIP PROGRAM FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE RECRUITING A COHORT OF SIX STUDENTS EACH YEAR, SUPPORTING THEIR COMPLETION OF THE NEW CULTURAL HERITAGE STEWARDSHIP CERTIFICATE, PROVIDING MENTORSHIP AT THE MEXICAN AMERICAN CIVIL RIGHTS INSTITUTE, AND CONDUCTING A PROGRAM EVALUATION. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT STIPENDS FOR STUDENTS, AND COMPENSATION FOR MUSEUM-BASED MENTORS AND FACULTY. THE RESULTING DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW CERTIFICATE PROGRAM IN CULTURAL HERITAGE STEWARDSHIP WILL PREPARE STUDENTS IN MUSEUM STUDIES FOR CAREERS IN THE MUSEUM FIELD.
description.3319: THE UNIVERSITY OF PUERTO RICO-RIO PIEDRAS CAMPUS WILL PARTNER WITH THE MUSEO DE HISTORIA, ARTE Y ANTROPOLOGÍA AND THE MUSEO DE ARTE DR. PIO LÓPEZ MARTÍNEZ TO DEVELOP AN ACADEMIC-STRUCTURED, EMPLOYMENT-ORIENTED HANDS-ON INTERNSHIP EXPERIENCE FOCUSING ON PUERTO RICO AND ITS DIASPORA. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PROVIDING RESOURCES FOR STAFF TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT OF MUSEUM STUDIES CURRICULA WITH A FOCUS ON DEPLOYING CLIMATE CHANGE RELATED SAFETY MEASURES IN COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THIS INTERNSHIP WILL SUPPORT STUDIES IN PRESERVATION, REVITALIZATION, AND DISSEMINATION OF ART OBJECTS HELD WITHIN PARTNER MUSEUM COLLECTIONS. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF CURRICULUM WITH PARTNERING MUSEUMS AS WELL AS ACCESS TO MENTORS IN CURATORIAL, PRESERVATION, AND EXHIBITION DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES. INTERNSHIP PARTICIPATION WILL RESULT IN THE PRESENTATION OF 25 TO 30 MICROPROJECTS RELATING TO BEST PRACTICE MUSEUM METHODOLOGY.
description.3320: THE MUSEUM OF LATIN AMERICAN ART IN PARTNERSHIP WITH UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA IRVINE, CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY LONG BEACH, UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA LOS ANGELES, AND UNIVERSITY OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA–WILL DEVELOP THE LATINO MUSEUM RESEARCH AND FELLOWSHIP CONSORTIUM, A PAID FELLOWSHIP FOR MASTERS AND POSTDOCTORAL STUDENTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE CREATION OF AN ADVISORY COUNCIL TO STEER INTERNSHIP ACTIVITIES AND DEVELOP PANEL SESSIONS, PURCHASE PROFESSIONAL COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE, AND PROVIDE DIGITIZATION TRAINING. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT FOUR PAID FELLOWS THAT WILL DIGITIZE OVER 300 OBJECTS FROM THE MUSEUM’S PERMANENT COLLECTION. THE RESULTING OUTCOME OF THE FELLOWSHIPS WILL EXPAND THE DIGITAL ARCHIVE OF THE MUSEUM’S PERMANENT COLLECTION AND CONTRIBUTE TO ACADEMIC AND CURATORIAL INQUIRY OF THE FELLOWS.
description.3321: THE NATIONAL MUSEUM OF MEXICAN ART IN PARTNERSHIP WITH DEPAUL UNIVERSITY AND THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS AT CHICAGO WILL DEVELOP A YEARLONG INTERNSHIP PROGRAM FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE PLACEMENT OF INTERNS IN DISTINCT DEPARTMENTS INCLUDING EDUCATION, YOUTH INITIATIVES, PERMANENT COLLECTION, AND VISUAL ART EXHIBITIONS. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT COMPUTER AND SOFTWARE FOR INTERN ACTIVITIES, YEARLY PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WORKSHOPS, TRANSIT COSTS, AND MENTORSHIP OPPORTUNITIES. THE RESULTING OUTCOME WILL BE AN ONGOING INTERNSHIP STRUCTURE WITH DETAILED PROGRAM PLANS TO CONTINUE GROWING WITH OTHER ORGANIZATIONS.
description.3322: THE MEXIC-ARTE MUSEUM IN PARTNERSHIP WITH CENTRAL TEXAS UNIVERSITIES WILL IMPROVE AND FORMALIZE THEIR LATINO MUSEUM INTERNSHIP PROGRAM. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE HANDS-ON TRAINING FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN DISTINCT AREAS SUCH AS EXHIBITION DEVELOPMENT, CURATORIAL, EDUCATION, AND SOCIAL AND DIGITAL MEDIA. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT COMPENSATION FOR COLLEGE AND UNIVERSITY INTERNS AND MENTORS AS WELL AS THE HIRING OF AN EDUCATION CURATOR WHO WILL OVERSEE INTERN PERFORMANCE AND EXPERIENCE. EACH OF THE INTERNS WILL COMPLETE A PROJECT IN THEIR RESPECTIVE MUSEUM DEPARTMENT RANGING FROM THE PRODUCTION OF AN EXHIBITION TO THE DIGITIZATION AND MAINTENANCE OF THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION METADATA.
description.3323: THE MOVIMIENTO DE ARTE Y CULTURA LATINO AMERICANA (MACLA) IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE SAN JOSE STATE UNIVERSITY AND THE SANTA CLARA UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP CURATORIAL FELLOWSHIPS FOR PARTICIPANTS AT AMERICAN LATINO MUSEUMS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE PLANNING, RESEARCH, AND INSTALLATION OF EXHIBITIONS SHOWCASED AT MACLA, AND CONDUCTING EXHIBITION RESEARCH ON LATINO CONTEMPORARY ARTISTS. THE THREE CURATORIAL FELLOWS WILL BE MENTORED BY PROFESSIONAL CURATORS AND ARTISTS AND ENGAGE IN FACILITATED CONVERSATIONS WITH OTHERS IN THE FIELD OF CONTEMPORARY LATINO ART. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WILL CONNECT ASPIRING CURATORS TO OTHER PROFESSIONALS IN AMERICAN LATINO MUSEUMS AND PRODUCE 12 MAJOR VISUAL ART EXHIBITIONS.
description.3324: THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS RIO GRANDE VALLEY WILL CREATE AND SUPPORT A NEW MUSEUM-BASED UNDERGRADUATE INTERNSHIP AND GRADUATE FELLOWSHIP PROGRAM IN PARTNERSHIP WITH AMERICAN LATINO MUSEUMS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE CREATION OF A NEW TRANSDISCIPLINARY MUSEUM STUDIES COURSE, EXPANSION OF OUTREACH FOR STUDENTS TO ENROLL IN INTERNSHIPS AND FELLOWSHIPS, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FAMILY ENGAGEMENT PLAN TO INVOLVE STUDENTS’ FAMILIES IN THE INTERNSHIP APPLICATION PROCESS. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT THE RECRUITMENT AND SUPPORT STAFF FOR THE FORMATION OF A STUDENT ADVISORY BOARD AND A FAMILY ADVISORY BOARD. THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE MUSEUM-BASED COURSEWORK WILL RESULT IN THE CREATION OF A NEW MUSEUM-FOCUSED ACADEMIC COURSE, AND A HANDBOOK FOR STUDENTS PARTICIPATING IN INTERNSHIPS AT AMERICAN LATINO MUSEUMS.
description.3325: THE VINCENT PRICE MUSEUM AT THE EAST LOS ANGELES COLLEGE WILL INCREASE ITS CAPACITY TO FACILITATE MUSEUM INTERNSHIPS AT MUSEUMS AND CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS FOR STUDENTS ENROLLED IN THEIR MUSEUM STUDIES CERTIFICATE TRACK. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE THE CREATION OF NEW PARTNERSHIPS AND EXPANSION OF ITS ROSTER OF PARTICIPATING MUSEUMS, PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO STUDENTS, AND OFFER SUPPORT FOR INTERNS. THE PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT STUDENT STIPENDS, ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS AT HOSTING INSTITUTIONS, AND OUTREACH AND STUDENT ENGAGEMENT. THE RESULTING OUTCOME IS A WIDER AND FURTHER ENHANCED INTERNSHIP EXPERIENCE FOR STUDENTS IN THE MUSEUM STUDIES PROGRAM.
description.3326: THE HUMANITIES INSTITUTE AT UC SANTA CRUZ WILL PARTNER WITH THE MUSEUM OF ART AND HISTORY TO CREATE AN INTERNSHIP EXPERIENCE FOR THREE GRADUATE AND THREE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE TRAINING IN PUBLIC PROGRAMMING, CURATORIAL AND EXHIBITION DEVELOPMENT, AND MENTORSHIP. THE FELLOWS WILL DEVELOP AN EXHIBITION EXPLORING LANGUAGE SCIENCE, INDIGENOUS OAXACAN LANGUAGES AND THE HISTORY OF MONTEREY BAY, CALIFORNIA. THE PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT COSTS, EXHIBITION DESIGN EQUIPMENT AND LABOR, AND A PROJECT EVALUATION. THE RESULTING OUTCOMES INCLUDE THE CREATION OF A PUBLIC EXHIBITION, LEARNING CURRICULA, PUBLIC PROGRAMMING, AND BILINGUAL MATERIAL.
description.3327: THE ARIZONA STATE UNIVERSITY ART MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH THE HISPANIC RESEARCH CENTER TO CREATE THE LATINX ART & CULTURE CURATORIAL FELLOWS AND INTERNSHIP PROGRAM. THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND FELLOWSHIP AND INTERNSHIPS OPPORTUNITIES, CREATE A FULLY ILLUSTRATED AND BILINGUAL TEXT ON CHICANO/A/X PRINTS AND OBJECTS, AND DEVELOP A CROSS-DISCIPLINARY ONLINE COURSE ON CHICANO/A/X ART HISTORY. THE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT THE PURCHASE OF EXHIBITION MATERIALS AND EQUIPMENT, THE PUBLICATION OF A TEXT PREPARED BY THE FELLOWS, TRAVEL TO ENGAGE WITH A NETWORK OF CURATORS, AND THE PRODUCTION OF AN ONLINE COURSE. THE RESULTING OUTCOMES INCLUDE AN EXPANSION AND DIVERSIFYING OF THE MUSEUM CURATORIAL FIELD THROUGH JOB SKILL AND PROFESSIONAL NETWORK DEVELOPMENT.
description.3328: ARTE AMÉRICAS: THE MEXICAN ART CENTER WILL PARTNER WITH THE STATE CENTER COMMUNITY COLLEGE DISTRICT, THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA MERCED, AND CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY FRESNO TO IMPLEMENT A MUSEUM-BASED UNDERGRADUATE INTERNSHIP PROGRAM. THE INTERNSHIP PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AT SEVEN CAMPUSES ACROSS FIVE COUNTIES IN CALIFORNIA’S CENTRAL VALLEY. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE FIELD TRIPS TO CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS ACROSS THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, THE PRODUCTION OF SEASONAL PUBLIC PROGRAMS, AND MENTORSHIP WITH PROFESSIONAL MUSEUM STAFF. THE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT THE PURCHASE OF MUSEUM EQUIPMENT FOR INTERNS TO USE, STUDENT STIPENDS, TRAVEL COSTS, ONE FULL-TIME INTERNSHIP COORDINATOR. THE RESULTING OUTCOMES INCLUDE THE PRODUCTION OF A DIGITAL INVENTORY FOR ARTE AMÉRICAS’ COLLECTION OF MASKS, A DIGITIZATION OF THE “CAMINOS” EXHIBITION WITH THE FRESNO STATE SPECIAL COLLECTIONS TEAM, ALONG WITH PROFESSIONAL HANDS-ON MUSEUM SKILL DEVELOPMENT FOR PARTICIPANTS.
description.3329: TWIN LAKES LIBRARY SYSTEM WILL PARTNER WITH GEORGIA COLLEGE AND STATE UNIVERSITY TO INTENTIONALLY AND SENSITIVELY DOCUMENT THE ORAL HISTORY OF CENTRAL STATE HOSPITAL, WHICH WAS ONCE THE LARGEST MENTAL HEALTH HOSPITAL IN THE WORLD. TWIN LAKES LIBRARY SYSTEM WILL ASSEMBLE AN ADVISORY BOARD OF FORMER HOSPITAL STAFF, PATIENTS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO HELP GUIDE THE COLLECTION OF STORIES FROM COMMUNITY MEMBERS AFFILIATED WITH THE HOSPITAL. THE LIBRARY WILL ALSO SPONSOR STATEWIDE HARVEST DAYS TO DIGITIZE CENTRAL STATE HOSPITAL MATERIALS FROM INDIVIDUALS? PERSONAL ARCHIVES. INTERVIEWS AND MATERIALS WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO AN EXHIBIT THAT WILL TRAVEL ACROSS GEORGIA TO EDUCATE INDIVIDUALS ABOUT THIS LITTLE-KNOWN STATE HISTORY AND DESTIGMATIZE MENTAL HEALTH.
description.3330: PROVIDENCE CHILDREN'S MUSEUM WILL EXPAND A SUCCESSFUL PILOT COLLABORATION FIRST ESTABLISHED IN 2020 WITH THE RHODE ISLAND DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO ADVANCE ENGAGING, HANDS-ON, AND PERSONALIZED DIGITAL INCLUSION PROGRAMS FOR CHILDREN K-3. THE MUSEUM IS PROVIDING TRAINING TO TEACHERS TO DEVELOP VIRTUAL OR IN-CLASS LESSON PLANS AND PROGRAMMING AND OFFERING A SERIES OF PLAY-BASED ONLINE ENRICHMENT COURSES. AS CHILDREN RETURN TO SCHOOL AND TEACHERS ADDRESS LEARNING LOSS RESULTING FROM SCHOOL CLOSURES AND REMOTE LEARNING DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC, THESE PROGRAMS WILL BENEFIT STUDENTS WHO HAVE NOT BEEN IN THE CLASSROOM ROUTINELY AND/OR NEED HIGHLY INTERACTIVE AND ENGAGING LESSONS AND EXPERIENCES FROM REMOTE ENRICHMENT, DISTANCE, OR IN-PERSON LEARNING.
description.3331: THE CENTRAL RAPPAHANNOCK REGIONAL LIBRARY IN FREDERICKSBURG, VIRGINIA, WILL INVEST IN AN OUTREACH VEHICLE TO BRING TECHNOLOGY RESOURCES INTO UNDERSERVED AREAS OF RURAL WESTMORELAND COUNTY. COVID-19 AFFECTED OPEN LIBRARY HOURS, AND WITH LONG DRIVING DISTANCES BETWEEN BRANCHES AND LIMITED HOME ACCESS TO INTERNET-ENABLED DEVICES, THE LIBRARY NEEDED A MOBILE SOLUTION. THE LIBRARY ON THE GO VAN WILL REGULARLY VISIT SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY GATHERING PLACES TO OFFER RESIDENTS ACCESS TO TABLETS, LAPTOPS, WIRELESS PRINTING, AND WI-FI. IN ADDITION TO TECHNOLOGICAL RESOURCES, THE OUTREACH VEHICLE WILL OFFER A PRINT COLLECTION, LIBRARY CARD SIGN-UPS, READERS’ ADVISORY SERVICES, AND SPECIAL PROGRAMMING. BY PROVIDING SERVICES IN THIS WAY, THE LIBRARY WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO TRADITIONAL LIBRARY SERVICES IN THE RURAL COUNTY AND SERVE NEW PATRONS OF ALL AGES WHO MAY BE UNABLE OR UNWILLING TO COME TO THE LIBRARY BRANCHES.
description.3332: DISCOVERY SCIENCE CENTER OF ORANGE COUNTY IN SANTA ANA, CALIFORNIA, WILL REHIRE AND TRAIN ESSENTIAL STAFF TO SUPPORT AN OCEAN-BASED FIELD TRIP DESIGNED TO BRING STUDENTS TO THE COAST WHO COULD NOT OTHERWISE HAVE THIS EXPERIENCE. THE PROJECT WILL OFFER 36 FREE FIELD TRIPS FOR TITLE I SCHOOLS AND DIRECTLY BENEFIT K-12 STUDENT POPULATIONS THAT HAVE ALL BEEN DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTED BY LEARNING LOSS DUE TO THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC, INCLUDING LOW-INCOME ETHNIC OR RACIAL MINORITY POPULATIONS, IMMIGRANTS, AND STUDENTS WITH MENTAL OR PHYSICAL CHALLENGES AND DISABILITIES. STUDENTS WILL EXPERIENCE HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES THAT WILL TEACH THEM TO MAKE REAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO ONGOING CITIZEN SCIENCE PROJECTS.
description.3333: THE YAKAMA NATION LIBRARY IN TOPPENISH, WASHINGTON, WILL EXPAND ITS CAPABILITY TO PROVIDE INTERNET CONNECTIVITY FOR TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS WHO DO NOT HAVE ACCESS AT HOME. THE LIBRARY WILL HIRE A TECHNOLOGY REVIEW CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT A TECHNOLOGY SITE SURVEY SO IT CAN PLAN AND EVALUATE THE BEST APPROACH FOR IMPLEMENTING THE EXPANDED INTERNET PROJECT AND SUSTAINING A ROBUST ONLINE ENVIRONMENT. THEY ALSO PLAN TO EXPAND WI-FI ACCESS BY PURCHASING UPGRADED EQUIPMENT THAT ENABLES FASTER, BROADER CONNECTIVITY. EXISTING TV WHITE SPACE EQUIPMENT WILL PROVIDE WI-FI TO NEARBY TRIBAL COMMUNITY HOUSING AREAS AND BUILDINGS. THE PROJECT WILL ASSIST WITH COVID-19 RECOVERY BY FILLING INTERNET ACCESS GAPS THAT ARE ESSENTIAL FOR EDUCATION, EMPLOYMENT AND HEALTH-RELATED NEEDS.
description.3334: THE WYANDOTTE NATION CULTURAL CENTER AND MUSEUM IN OKLAHOMA WILL EXPAND ITS OUTREACH TO BROADER COMMUNITIES BY CREATING AN ONLINE EXHIBIT FEATURING PHOTOGRAPHS, PAINTINGS, AND OTHER WYANDOTTE ARTIFACTS. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A MUSEUM TECHNICIAN WHO WILL RECEIVE INSTRUCTION FROM THE STATE HISTORICAL SOCIETY ON BEST PRACTICES IN ONLINE EXHIBITS. THE ONLINE EXHIBIT WILL ALLOW THE MUSEUM TO SERVE WYANDOTTE CITIZENS ALL OVER THE COUNTRY, PROVIDING THEM WITH ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTION AND RELATED EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS. THE PROJECT WILL HELP COMMUNITIES RECOVER FROM THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC BY ALLOWING CITIZENS TO PRACTICE SOCIAL DISTANCING WHILE CREATING A DIGITAL COMMUNITY. IN ADDITION TO INCREASING ACCESS TO TRIBAL HERITAGE, THE MUSEUM'S ONLINE PRESENCE WILL ENHANCE CONNECTIONS WITH THE TRIBE AND TRIBAL CITIZENS NATIONWIDE.
description.3335: THE MENOMINEE INDIAN TRIBAL ARCHIVES AND THE MENOMINEE CULTURAL MUSEUM IN KESHENA, WISCONSIN, WILL COLLABORATE ON A PROJECT TO IMPROVE MANAGEMENT, CARE, AND TRIBAL MEMBER ACCESS TO ARCHIVAL AND ETHNOGRAPHIC COLLECTIONS. THEY WILL HIRE AND TRAIN TWO PART-TIME STAFF TO SELECT, CATALOG, AND REHOUSE COLLECTION MATERIALS. OTHER MUSEUM STAFF WILL RECEIVE TRAININGS ON ARCHIVAL SOFTWARE AND COLLECTIONS CARE AND MANAGEMENT. THE TRIBAL ARCHIVIST WILL MANAGE THE PROJECT, WHICH IS PART OF A LONG-TERM EFFORT TO PROVIDE TRIBAL MEMBERS WITH DIGITAL ACCESS TO A BROAD ARRAY OF CULTURAL HERITAGE MATERIALS, AND WAS DELAYED AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC'S EFFECTS ON COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP.
description.3336: THE FAIRBANKS NORTH STAR BOROUGH PUBLIC LIBRARIES WILL MAKE AVAILABLE 25 LAPTOPS AND MIFI DEVICES (HOTSPOTS) FOR RESIDENTS TO BORROW. THE RURAL NATURE OF THE AREA MEANS THERE ARE LIMITED CELL TOWERS AND INTERNET ACCESS POINTS BEYOND THE PUBLIC LIBRARY. THESE INTERNET ACCESSIBLE LAPTOPS WILL INCLUDE INSTRUCTIONAL VIDEOS, APPLICATIONS TO ASSIST WITH RESUME CREATION, VIRTUAL EDUCATION, LINKS TO LOCAL, STATE, AND FEDERAL RESOURCES FOR ASSISTANCE, AND LITERACY SOFTWARE TO THOSE PATRONS WHO NEED ADDITIONAL ACCESS TO RESOURCES FROM HOME. THE EXTRA DEVICES WILL NOT ONLY PROVIDE SERVICES TO UNDESERVED LIBRARY PATRONS BUT WILL ALSO HELP ALLEVIATE DEMAND ON LIBRARY COMPUTERS.
description.3337: TAMASTSLIKT CULTURAL INSTITUTE WILL ENHANCE ITS DIGITAL CONTENT AND REMOTE WORK CAPABILITIES, PROVIDE SALARY SUPPORT FOR PROJECT-RELATED STAFF AND TASKS, AND INCREASE SAFEGUARDS SPECIFIC TO COVID-19 WITHIN THE FACILITY. THROUGH WWW.TAMASTSLIKT.ORG, THEY WILL INCREASE OFFERINGS TO THE PUBLIC SO THAT THEY CAN BENEFIT FROM THE COLLECTIONS, EXHIBITS, AND PROGRAMS FROM THE SAFETY OF THEIR HOME OR OFFICE. VIRTUAL TOURS, ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS, AND LIVE STREAMING WILL MAKE IT POSSIBLE TO LEARN MORE ABOUT THE HISTORY AND CULTURES OF THE PEOPLES NOW KNOWN AS THE CONFEDERATED TRIBES OF UMATILLA?THE CAYUSE, UMATILLA, AND WALLA WALLA?WHILE SOCIAL DISTANCING.
description.3338: IN A TIME OF UNCERTAINTY, THE NAVAJO NATION MUSEUM WILL CREATE PROGRAMMING THAT SAFELY BRINGS FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES TOGETHER THROUGH AN ANIMATED NAVAJO COYOTE STORIES SERIES?CLASSIC TRADITIONAL TEACHINGS THAT ARE USUALLY TOLD DURING THE WINTER MONTHS. THE MUSEUM WILL CREATE THIS SERIES IN THE NAVAJO LANGUAGE WITH AN OPTION FOR ENGLISH SUBTITLES AND ORGANIZE THE SCREENS USING A DRIVE-IN THEATER FORMAT. THEY WILL HOLD THESE SHOWINGS ACROSS THE NAVAJO NATION AT CHAPTER HOUSES AND COMMUNITY CENTERS SO THAT FAMILIES CAN ENJOY AND LEARN THE NAVAJO COYOTE STORIES FROM THE SAFETY OF THEIR VEHICLES.
description.3339: THE KENTUCKY MUSEUM AT WESTERN KENTUCKY UNIVERSITY WILL IMPROVE THE LONG-TERM CARE OF ITS COLLECTIONS BY UPGRADING THE MECHANICAL SYSTEM AT THE MUSEUM?S OFF-SITE, ON-CAMPUS STORAGE FACILITY. THEY WILL INSTITUTE A PROGRAM TO MONITOR THE TEMPERATURE OF INTERIOR SURFACES OF EXTERNAL WALLS AND INVESTIGATE POINTS OF EXTERNAL AIR FILTRATION IN THE BUILDING. THE UPGRADED SYSTEM AND RELATED EFFORTS WILL HELP PRESERVE THE MUSEUM?S COLLECTION OF 30,000 ARTIFACTS FOR FUTURE EXHIBITIONS, PROGRAMS, INSTRUCTIONAL OPPORTUNITIES, STUDENT WORK OPPORTUNITIES, AND RESEARCH.
description.3340: THE ALABAMA MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALABAMA WILL REHOUSE, DIGITIZE, AND IMAGE THE HISTORIC INVERTEBRATE PALEONTOLOGY AND TYPE COLLECTIONS. THE PALEONTOLOGY COLLECTION IS ONE OF THE LARGEST COMPONENTS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF ALABAMA MUSEUMS COLLECTION, CONSISTING OF AT LEAST 500,000 SPECIMENS, REPRESENTING 500 MILLION YEARS OF TIME. FOUR GRADUATE STUDENTS FROM THE UNIVERSITY?S MUSEUM STUDIES PROGRAM WILL BE RECRUITED TO ASSIST THE PROJECT, PROVIDING CAREER DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES. ENHANCED ACCESSIBILITY TO THE COLLECTIONS WILL BENEFIT MUSEUM AND UNIVERSITY FACULTY, STAFF, AND STUDENTS AS WELL AS NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL RESEARCHERS AND STUDENTS.
description.3341: THE UNIVERSITY AND JEPSON HERBARIA AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, BERKELEY WILL DEVELOP A SERIES OF VIRTUAL WORKSHOPS THAT PROMOTE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND DISCOVERY IN THE FIELDS OF BOTANY, ECOLOGY, AND CONSERVATION BIOLOGY. THE WORKSHOPS AND ACCOMPANYING RECORDINGS WILL ADDRESS CRITICAL ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES. GEARED TOWARD LIFELONG LEARNERS, RECORDINGS OF THE LECTURE PORTIONS OF THE TWELVE WORKSHOPS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE ONLINE AND FREE OF CHARGE. THE WORKSHOPS AND VIDEOS WILL PROVIDE HIGH-QUALITY, MUSEUM-BASED EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THAT DEMONSTRATE THE VALUE OF MUSEUM COLLECTIONS AND HOW THOSE COLLECTIONS ARE USED IN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION. BY BRINGING ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION TO A BROADER AUDIENCE, THIS PROGRAM WILL EDUCATE PARTICIPANTS ABOUT HOW EACH MEMBER OF A COMMUNITY CAN CONTRIBUTE TO LOCAL EFFORTS TO PROTECT NATURAL RESOURCES.
description.3342: ECOEXPLORATORIO: MUSEO DE CIENCIAS DE PUERTO RICO'S IN-STEM: AN INCLUSIVE STEM MUSEUM EXHIBITION PROJECT WILL PROVIDE STEM EDUCATIONAL MATERIAL SPECIFICALLY FOR AUDIENCES WITH VISUAL AND HEARING DISABILITIES. IN ADDITION TO AN INCLUSIVE SUMMER MOON TO MARS EXHIBIT, THE MUSEUM WILL OFFER TOURS WITH AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGES (ASL) INTERPRETERS AND ADAPTATIONS FOR THE VISUALLY IMPAIRED. ACCESSIBLE ONLINE, THE MUSEUM WILL PRODUCE TEN STEM ACTIVITY VIDEOS. BY BEING INCLUSIVE OF PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES, SPECIFICALLY FOCUSING ON PEOPLE THAT ARE DEAF OR HARD OF HEARING AND BLIND OR VISUALLY IMPAIRED, THE MUSEUM SEEKS TO PROMOTE LIFELONG ACCESS TO STEM EDUCATION.
description.3343: THE GRAND BAY COASTAL RESOURCES CENTER WILL IMPLEMENT “VISUALIZING INTERPRETIVE SPACE THROUGH INTEGRATIVE TEAMWORK” (VISIT), A NEW INITIATIVE TO DEVELOP A REDESIGN PLAN FOR ITS EXHIBIT SPACE THROUGH MULTI-LEVEL COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT. THE CENTER WILL INITIATE THE PROJECT BY DISTRIBUTING A SURVEY, HOLDING FOCUS GROUPS, AND TRAVELING TO LOCAL MUSEUMS TO COLLECT FEEDBACK ON THE EXISTING SPACE. THE CENTER WILL THEN CONTRACT WITH AN EXHIBIT DESIGNER TO PERFORM AN ON-SITE EXHIBIT ASSESSMENT. THE PROJECT TEAM AND EXHIBIT DESIGNER WILL CONVENE AN ADVISORY PANEL OF CLASSROOM TEACHERS, INFORMAL EDUCATORS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE IN A WORKSHOP TO CREATE THE ACTION PLAN FOR THE EXHIBIT SPACE. BY NAVIGATING THE REDESIGN PROCESS WITH COMMUNITY INPUT, THE CENTER WILL CREATE A LEARNING ENVIRONMENT THAT APPEALS TO VARIOUS AUDIENCES AND PARTICIPANTS WILL FEEL A SENSE OF PRIDE AND OWNERSHIP IN THE FUTURE SPACE.
description.3344: VICTORIA MANSION WILL IMPROVE THE DOCUMENTATION OF ACCESSION RECORDS FOR ITS COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING FURNITURE, SCULPTURE, CARPETING, PAINTINGS, AND GLASS AND CERAMIC ARTS OBJECTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL FOCUS ON SYSTEMATICALLY IDENTIFYING AND CORRECTING INACCURACIES, DUPLICATIONS, AND OMISSIONS IN THE PHYSICAL COLLECTIONS RECORDS. THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH TOUR GUIDES TO ASSESS THEIR NEEDS FOR DIGITAL ACCESS TO IN-DEPTH INFORMATION ABOUT THE COLLECTION IN ORDER TO ANSWER VISITOR QUESTIONS AND CONDUCT RESEARCH. THE MUSEUM WILL MAKE PROGRESS IN COMPLETING A DIGITAL DATABASE TO MAKE DETAILED INFORMATION ABOUT ITS COLLECTIONS READILY ACCESSIBLE TO STAFF AND DOCENTS, ULTIMATELY ENRICHING INTERPRETATION OF THE HOUSE FOR VISITORS.
description.3345: THE PRATT MUSEUM WILL CREATE A SERIES OF PROGRAMS AND EXHIBITS TO STRENGTHEN ENGAGEMENT WITH ALASKA NATIVE CULTURE-BEARERS AND FAMILIES WITH YOUNG CHILDREN AND LIMITED INCOME. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A DIRECTOR OF LIFELONG LEARNING EXPERIENCES, WHO WILL BE OUTWARDLY FOCUSED TO ENSURE THAT PROGRAMMING IS PRIORITIZING DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION. THE NEW POSITION WILL BE CHARGED WITH COLLABORATING WITH KEY COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS TO DEVELOP THREE TO FIVE EXHIBITS AND ACCOMPANYING PROGRAMS, CRAFTING A STRATEGIC PLAN FOR BUILDING FUTURE PROGRAM CONTENT AND PARTNERSHIPS, AND RE-ESTABLISHING THE MUSEUM AS A GATHERING PLACE FOR ALL. THE PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO RESULT IN NEW AND RENEWED EXHIBITS, PROGRAMS, AND RELATIONSHIPS THAT ARE TRANSFORMATIVE FOR THE MUSEUM AND COMMUNITY. A PROFESSIONAL EVALUATOR WILL MEASURE THE MUSEUM’S SUCCESS AT ACHIEVING THE PROJECT GOALS.
description.3346: THE STAR GAZING ROOM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA WILL PREPARE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO DEVELOP EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS FOR K–12 STUDENTS AND YOUTH AUDIENCES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL TRAIN COHORTS OF PAID, UNDERGRADUATE PLANETARIUM EDUCATORS IN INFORMAL SCIENCE EDUCATION AND ROLE MODEL ENGAGEMENT AS WELL AS CONDUCT TEAM BUILDING AND MENTORSHIP ACTIVITIES. THE STUDENT EDUCATORS WILL DEVELOP CREATIVE CONTENT AND LEAD PLANETARIUM SHOWS AND ASTRONOMY OUTREACH TO K–12 SCHOOLS AND YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS IN THE MISSOULA REGION, INCLUDING FROM THE NEARBY FLATHEAD RESERVATION. THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL HELP CULTIVATE THE UNDERGRADUATE EDUCATORS’ SELF-EFFICACY AND SENSE OF BELONGING IN STEM AND HIGHER EDUCATION WHILE ALSO POSITIVELY INFLUENCING K–12 STUDENTS’ KNOWLEDGE OF, AND INTEREST IN, ASTRONOMY. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE STAR GAZING ROOM’S WORKFORCE AND ENHANCE ITS ABILITY TO REACH K–12 AND PUBLIC AUDIENCES.
description.3347: MUNCIE CHILDREN'S MUSEUM WILL FABRICATE AND INSTALL THE WHITE RIVER WATER TABLE EXHIBIT TO PROVIDE A LEARNING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH CHILDREN AGES 10 AND UNDER CAN PRACTICE THE SKILLS OF COLLABORATION, COMMUNICATION, CRITICAL THINKING, AND PROBLEM-SOLVING. THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH AN EXHIBIT DESIGN FIRM TO CRAFT THE NEW EXHIBIT COMPONENT BASED ON RECENT CONCEPT DEVELOPMENT AND SCHEMATIC DESIGN PLANNING. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE EFFORTS OF EAST CENTRAL INDIANA—A 9 COUNTY REGIONAL COALITION-- TO CREATE A CULTURE OF EDUCATION THAT PROVIDES RESIDENTS WITH AN EDUCATIONAL ATTAINMENT LEVEL TO BE SUCCESSFUL IN SCHOOL AND THE WORKPLACE. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH OTHER COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS INVOLVED IN THIS EFFORT TO DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK OF EVALUATION TO CAPTURE MEASURABLE OUTCOMES THAT ARE IMPORTANT TO GUIDING FUTURE EDUCATIONAL PLANNING.
description.3348: THE CHILDREN’S MUSEUM OF WILMINGTON WILL IMPROVE THE VISITOR EXPERIENCE FOR SPANISH SPEAKING VISITORS AND THOSE WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENTS BY ADDRESSING LANGUAGE BARRIERS AND ACCESSIBILITY ISSUES. WORKING WITH PROFESSIONAL TRANSLATORS, THE MUSEUM WILL CREATE BILINGUAL AND BRAILLE SIGNAGE FOR EXHIBITS AND OTHER MUSEUM SPACES. THE MUSEUM WILL ALSO PROVIDE SPANISH AND BRAILLE FOR FLYERS AND MARKETING AND INFORMATIONAL MATERIALS. COMMUNITY PARTNERS WILL EVALUATE THE SIGNAGE AND MATERIALS FOR EASE OF READING AND UNDERSTANDING. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE MUSEUM’S ONGOING WORK TO EMBED DEAI (DIVERSITY, EQUITY, ACCESSIBILITY, AND INCLUSION) PRACTICES WITHIN ALL OF ITS OPERATIONS BY FOSTERING RELATIONSHIPS WITH ORGANIZATIONS THAT WORK WITH DIVERSE GROUPS AND REACHING NEW AUDIENCES THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY FELT EXCLUDED FROM ITS SERVICES.
