description.3349: LED BY THE WATKINS MUSEUM OF HISTORY, FIVE HERITAGE SITES IN DOUGLAS COUNTY, KANSAS, WILL COLLABORATE TO DEVELOP A SERIES OF ONLINE LEARNING RESOURCES UNITING THE HISTORIES OF THE SITES UNDER THE THEME, "SEEKING A MORE PERFECT UNION: THE ENDURING STRUGGLE FOR FREEDOM AND CIVIL RIGHTS.” BASED ON A NEWLY DEVELOPED FIELD TRIP PROGRAM AND A NEEDS ASSESSMENT OF K–12 TEACHERS, THIS SERIES OF LESSON PLANS, STUDENT WORKBOOKS, AND CLASSROOM RESOURCES WILL CONNECT STORIES THAT EMPHASIZE HOW ISSUES OF FREEDOM, RACE, JUSTICE, EQUALITY, AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY AFFECTED PEOPLE’S LIVES FROM THE MID-1800S TO THE PRESENT. THE PROJECT WILL ENSURE THAT TEACHERS AND STUDENTS CONTINUE TO BENEFIT FROM THE ADVANTAGES OFFERED BY LEARNING IN A MUSEUM SETTING, IN ADDITION TO PROVIDING A MORE ACCESSIBLE OPTION FOR THOSE WHO CANNOT TRAVEL TO THE SITES.
description.3350: THE MUSEUM OF BOULDER WILL IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT AND CARE OF ITS COLLECTIONS BY IMPLEMENTING A PILOT PROGRAM TO CONDUCT AN INVENTORY AND ANALYSIS OF ITS COSTUME COLLECTION. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A COLLECTIONS ASSISTANT TO WORK WITH ITS COLLECTIONS MANAGER TO PHOTOGRAPH AND EVALUATE ITEMS AND UPDATE DIGITAL RECORDS, WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF STUDENT INTERNS. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS 15 PERCENT OF THE 11,000 ARTIFACTS IN THE COLLECTION, WHICH SPANS 150 YEARS OF BOULDER’S DRESS HISTORY. THE MUSEUM WILL ENGAGE A TEXTILE CONSERVATOR TO REPAIR OR PRESERVE 10 ARTIFACTS THAT RANK HIGHLY AS HISTORICALLY SIGNIFICANT AND ARE MOST IN NEED OF CONSERVATION THE PILOT PROJECT WILL PROVIDE FOUNDATIONAL KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE COSTUME COLLECTION AND CREATE A BLUEPRINT FOR A FUTURE PRESERVATION STUDY OF THE FULL COLLECTION, LEADING TO ITS INCREASED ACCESS AND USE FOR STAFF, RESEARCHERS, AND OTHER INSTITUTIONS.
description.3351: THE CHARLES SUMNER SCHOOL MUSEUM AND ARCHIVES WILL STABILIZE A COLLECTION OF NEGATIVES AND PHOTOGRAPHS DOCUMENTING 40 YEARS OF WASHINGTON, DC PUBLIC SCHOOL HISTORY. THE MUSEUM WILL ALSO DIGITIZE A PORTION OF THE COLLECTION AS A PILOT PROJECT TO PLAN FOR THE DIGITIZATION OF ITS ENTIRE COLLECTION. INFORMED BY A COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH COLLECTIONS AND DIGITIZATION CONSULTANTS, HIGH SCHOOL INTERNS, AND GRADUATE STUDENTS TO REHOUSE, ACCESSION, TRANSCRIBE, SCAN, AND DIGITIZE IMAGES, AS WELL AS DEVELOP COLLECTION METADATA. THE DIGITIZATION CONSULTANT WILL DEVELOP A DIGITIZATION PLAN FOR THE MUSEUM AND PROVIDE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE PROJECT TEAM. THE PROJECT WILL CREATE A FRAMEWORK FOR BUILDING THE MUSEUM’S DIGITAL COLLECTIONS DATABASE AND MAKING ITS COLLECTIONS MORE WIDELY ACCESSIBLE AS AN EXAMPLE OF COLLECTING AND PRESERVING THE HISTORY OF AN URBAN PUBLIC SCHOOL SYSTEM.
description.3352: THE MUSEO DEL WESTSIDE, OPERATED BY THE ESPERANZA PEACE AND JUSTICE CENTER, WILL IMPROVE THE CARE AND MANAGEMENT OF ITS COLLECTIONS AND MAKE THEM PUBLICLY SEARCHABLE ONLINE. THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION OF OVER 3,000 PHOTOGRAPHS, ORAL HISTORIES, AND ARCHITECTURAL ARTIFACTS DOCUMENT THE HISTORY OF SAN ANTONIO’S WESTSIDE NEIGHBORHOOD, WHICH BECAME THE PRIMARY SAN ANTONIO NEIGHBORHOOD HOUSING WORKING-CLASS TEJANOS (TEXANS OF MEXICAN DESCENT) AND MEXICAN IMMIGRANTS IN THE LATE 19TH CENTURY. MUSEUM STAFF WILL TRANSFER THE COLLECTION INTO NEW COLLECTION STORAGE AREAS AND COMPLETE THE ASSOCIATED DATA ENTRY. IN PARTNERSHIP WITH LOCAL SCHOOLS AND SENIOR CENTERS, STAFF WILL RECRUIT AND TRAIN VOLUNTEER DOCENTS AS WELL AS HOST WORKSHOPS TO ENGAGE THEM WITH THE USE OF THE COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE IMPROVED ACCESS TO OBJECTS FOR FUTURE EXHIBITIONS AND MAKE THE COLLECTIONS PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE THROUGH THE MUSEUM WEBSITE.
description.3353: THE DELAWARE CONTEMPORARY WILL EXPAND UPON ITS SUCCESSFUL AFTERSCHOOL TEEN PROGRAM, CREATIVE ARTS CLUB, BY ADDING VOCATIONAL EXPLORATION OF MUSEUM AND CREATIVE INDUSTRY CAREERS THROUGH A SERIES OF NEW LEARNING EXPERIENCES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL PARTNER WITH TITLE 1 HIGH SCHOOLS IN NEW CASTLE COUNTY TO RECRUIT STUDENTS WITH LIMITED ACCESS TO ARTS OPPORTUNITIES. THROUGH CROSS-DISCIPLINARY LEARNING METHODS AND ENGAGEMENT WITH THE MUSEUM’S TEACHING ARTISTS AND A DIVERSE GROUP OF CREATIVES-IN-RESIDENCE, STUDENTS WILL CREATE THEIR OWN WORKS OF ART USING A VARIETY OF ART MEDIA, VISIT CREATIVE INDUSTRY WORKSPACES AND CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS, AND PARTICIPATE IN CIVIC ENGAGEMENT PROJECTS. THE PROGRAM WILL CULMINATE IN AN EXHIBITION AND POP-UP RETAIL OPERATION TO SHOWCASE STUDENTS’ ARTWORK. THESE OPPORTUNITIES WILL HELP STUDENTS TO DEVELOP PROFESSIONAL SKILLS, PROMOTE JOB PREPAREDNESS, BROADEN CAREER HORIZONS, AND OVERCOME BARRIERS TO SUCCESS.
description.3354: THE WALTER W. STIERN LIBRARY’S HISTORICAL RESEARCH CENTER AT CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, BAKERSFIELD WILL DEVELOP AN EXHIBIT OF IMAGES AND EPHEMERA ABOUT BASQUE SHEEPHERDERS IN THE CENTRAL VALLEY REGION OF CALIFORNIA, AND THEIR ARBORGLYPHS, OR STORY-TELLING ART CARVED INTO TREES. FOR OVER A HUNDRED YEARS, BASQUE IMMIGRANTS ARRIVED TO WORK IN ISOLATED CONDITIONS IN THE WESTERN DESERTS AND THE SIERRA NEVADA HIGH COUNTRY, AND WERE KNOWN FOR THEIR SKILLS AT MOVING AND WATCHING OVER VAST SHEEP HERDS. A TEAM OF STUDENT VOLUNTEERS, UNIVERSITY FACULTY, AND STAFF WILL DEVELOP THE EXHIBIT FLOOR PLAN, COLLECT PHOTOGRAPHS AND EPHEMERA PRIMARILY THROUGH THE LOCAL BASQUE CLUB, AND DEVELOP 3D MODELS OF SELECTED ARBORGLYPHS. THE MULTI-MEDIA EXHIBIT WILL PROVIDE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN THE BAKERSFIELD METRO AREA AND THE SURROUNDING SAN JOAQUIN VALLEY.
description.3355: THE INDIAN ARTS RESEARCH CENTER WILL USE FUNDS TO IMPROVE THE STEWARDSHIP OF ITS COLLECTION OF SOUTHWEST NATIVE AMERICAN ART, WHICH CONSISTS OF OVER 12,500 OBJECTS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL INVENTORY AND BARCODE OBJECTS IN THE COLLECTION, WHICH WILL RESULT IN EFFICIENT AND ACCURATE KNOWLEDGE OF OBJECT LOCATION AND CONDITION. STAFF WILL RECEIVE TRAINING ON THE NEW COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM AND INVENTORY PROCESS. IMPROVED COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT WILL ALLOW STAFF TO ACCESS THE COLLECTION MORE EASILY FOR EXHIBITION AND PROGRAMMATIC PURPOSES.
description.3356: THE CASTELLANI ART MUSEUM OF NIAGARA UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP A TRAVELING EXHIBITION, “OLD/NEW THREADS” ABOUT THE INTERSECTIONS OF TRADITIONAL ART, ECONOMY, AND COMMUNITY-BUILDING. THE EXHIBITION WILL EXPLORE THIS TOPIC THROUGH THE CASE STUDY OF STITCH BUFFALO, A TEXTILE ARTS-BASED ORGANIZATION SERVING PRIMARILY REFUGEE WOMEN WITHIN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT A PROJECT MANAGER AND A PAID INTERN, WHO, IN CONSULTATION WITH HUMANITIES EXPERTS, WILL CONDUCT NEW ETHNOGRAPHIC FIELDWORK, DEVELOP INTERPRETIVE PANELS AND AN EXHIBIT CATALOG, CREATE SHORT-FORM VIDEOS, AND DESIGN ACCOMPANYING PUBLIC PROGRAMS SUCH AS ARTIST-LED WORKSHOPS, DEMONSTRATIONS, AND COMMUNITY CELEBRATIONS. AS A RESULT, THIS PROJECT WILL RECOGNIZE THE EFFORTS OF DIVERSE INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANIZATIONS THAT IMPLEMENT THESE OPPORTUNITIES FOR DISADVANTAGED MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY IN THE REGION, AND CONTRIBUTE TO IMPROVED REFUGEE PROSPERITY THROUGH INCREASED VISIBILITY AND AWARENESS.
description.3357: THE HAITIAN AMERICAN MUSEUM OF CHICAGO WILL IMPROVE THE CARE OF ITS COLLECTION RELATED TO THE HISTORY OF HAITIANS IN THE GLOBAL AFRICAN DIASPORA. STAFF WILL ESTABLISH A PRESERVATION PLAN FOR THE MUSEUM'S COLLECTION AND LIBRARY THAT INCLUDES POLICIES, PROCEDURES, AND A DISASTER PLAN. STAFF WILL THEN IMPLEMENT THE PRESERVATION PLAN AND UPDATE THE COLLECTION AND LIBRARY CATALOGS WITH MORE ACCURATE LABELS, DESCRIPTIONS AND METADATA. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, MUSEUM STAFF AND THE PUBLIC WILL HAVE IMPROVED ACCESSIBILITY TO THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION AND LIBRARY FOR RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT INCLUDE HAITIAN AND AFRICAN AMERICANS, AS WELL AS STUDENTS, EDUCATORS, AND MUSEUM VISITORS.
description.3358: DIASPORA VIBE CULTURAL ARTS INCUBATOR WILL ADVANCE SHARED KNOWLEDGE AROUND MATERNAL FIGURE HOOD THROUGH AN EXHIBITION OF WORKS BY KATRINA COOMBS AND IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE HARVEY B. GANTT CENTER FOR AFRICAN AMERICAN ARTS AND CULTURE. THIS EXHIBITION WILL ADDRESS THE NEED IN EXHIBITING MORE FIBER ARTISTS AND TEXTILE ART, WHICH IS OFTEN RELATED TO A “HOBBY CRAFT,” AND WILL BRING AWARENESS TO THIS MEDIUM, WHILE ELEVATING THE WORK AND LABOR OF WOMEN ARTISTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE EXHIBIT CONTENT DEVELOPMENT, COORDINATING WITH THE ARTIST ON SELECTING AND SHIPPING ARTWORKS, AND DEVELOPING PUBLIC PROGRAMS WITH THE GANTT CENTER. THE RESULTS WILL INCLUDE AN INCREASED AWARENESS OF THE WORK OF AFRO-DIASPORIC AND CARIBBEAN ARTISTS, AND A GREATER UNDERSTANDING AND FUTURE SCHOLARSHIP ON THE AFRICAN DIASPORA, THE CARIBBEAN, AND LATIN AMERICA.
description.3359: THE INTERNATIONAL MUSEUM OF ART AND SCIENCE WILL IMPROVE COLLECTION STEWARDSHIP AND ACCESSIBILITY FOR APPROXIMATELY 5,600 WORKS OF MEXICAN AND LATIN AMERICAN FOLK ART IN ITS COLLECTION. DURING THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL WORK WITH PAID INTERNS TO PHOTOGRAPH, CATALOG, AND INPUT DATA INTO A COLLECTIONS SOFTWARE DATABASE IN ORDER TO PROVIDE INTERNAL AND ONLINE ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION. LOCAL AND NATIONAL PROJECT ADVISORS WILL INFORM RESEARCH ACTIVITIES AND ASSIST STAFF IN REVIEWING SPANISH AND ENGLISH TEXT TRANSLATIONS RELATED TO THE OBJECTS.
description.3360: LINDSAY WILDLIFE EXPERIENCE WILL CREATE THREE NEW AVIARY ANIMAL ENCLOSURE EXHIBITS IN THE NATURE COVE, AN OUTDOOR PROGRAM PRESENTATION AREA. ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE UPGRADING THE AREA TO MAKE THE OUTDOOR EXHIBIT FULLY ADA ACCESSIBLE AND DEVELOPING INTERACTIVE SIGNAGE IN MULTIPLE LANGUAGES. THIS PROJECT IS PART OF A LARGER INITIATIVE TO PROVIDE INTERACTIVE OPPORTUNITIES FOR PEOPLE OF ALL AGES TO LEARN ABOUT WILDLIFE AND CONSERVATION IN A SAFE, OUTDOOR LOCATION WHERE VISITORS WILL FEEL COMFORTABLE VISITING EVEN DURING A PANDEMIC. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL HAVE AVIARIES THAT EXCEED CURRENT CALIFORNIA FISH AND WILDLIFE REGULATIONS ON HOUSING LIVE, WILD ANIMALS, AND THE ANIMAL AMBASSADORS WILL HAVE A SAFE AND NATURAL HOME THAT WILL VASTLY IMPROVE THEIR WELFARE.
description.3361: THE DAURA MUSEUM OF ART WILL DIGITALLY DOCUMENT AND CATALOG WORKS FROM ITS PERMANENT COLLECTION TO IMPROVE COLLECTION MANAGEMENT, PRESERVATION, AND ACCESSIBILITY FOR APPROXIMATELY 2,500 WORKS OF ART. THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION SERVES AS AN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCE FOR TEACHING THROUGH THE INTERPRETATION AND EXHIBITION OF WORKS OF ART AND INCLUDES PAINTINGS, DRAWINGS, WORKS ON PAPER, SCULPTURE, AND ETHNOGRAPHIC ARTIFACTS. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A REGISTRAR TO CONDUCT AN INVENTORY OF THE COLLECTION, TRANSFER METADATA TO A COLLECTIONS DATABASE, AND PHOTO DOCUMENT THE COLLECTION. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE STUDENTS, FACULTY, AND RESEARCHERS, AS WELL AS THE SURROUNDING REGIONAL COMMUNITY.
description.3362: THE MEETEETSE MUSEUMS WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTIONS BY SCANNING AND DIGITIZING ITS COLLECTION OF OVER 100 BOUND MATERIALS, INCLUDING A SCRAPBOOK OF PHOTOGRAPHER CHARLES BELDEN. BY DIGITIZING OBJECTS WITH A NEW OVERSIZE BOOK SCANNER, THE INSTITUTION WILL REDUCE THE HANDLING OF OBJECTS AND PREVENT STRAIN ON BINDINGS. THE INSTITUTION WILL ALSO MAKE THE LARGE FORMAT SCANNER AVAILABLE FOR USE BY OTHER RURAL MUSEUMS IN NORTHWESTERN WYOMING. PROJECT STAFF WILL WORK WITH DIGITAL COLLECTIONS INTERNS TO UPLOAD THE RECORDS TO A PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE ONLINE DATABASE.
description.3363: THE BREVARD ZOO WILL IMPLEMENT A 12-WEEK PAID ANIMAL KEEPER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM FOR FIVE MINORITY STUDENTS OR RECENT GRADUATES DESIGNED TO INCREASE DIVERSITY IN THE ANIMAL CARE FIELD. THE PROGRAM, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH BETHUNE-COOKMAN UNIVERSITY, WILL PROVIDE HANDS-ON PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE, ONE-ON-ONE MENTORING, AND TRAINING FROM EXPERIENCED ANIMAL CARE STAFF, AND WILL SUPPORT PARTICIPANT HOUSING, TRANSPORTATION, AND STIPENDS. THIS PROGRAM WILL NURTURE EACH PARTICIPANT’S PASSION FOR ANIMAL CARE AND CONSERVATION AND INCREASE CONFIDENCE IN, AND COMMITMENT TO, THE ANIMAL CARE FIELD. LONG-TERM OUTCOMES OF THIS INTERNSHIP PROGRAM INCLUDE FUTURE EMPLOYMENT IN THE ZOOLOGICAL OR ANIMAL CARE FIELDS AND CONTRIBUTE TO GROWING A DIVERSE WORKFORCE THAT HAS A WIDER RANGE OF EXPERIENCE AND VIEWPOINTS, BETTER PREPARING THE ZOO AND THE FIELD TO ENGAGE DIVERSE AUDIENCES.
description.3364: THE SCIENCE ZONE WILL FABRICATE A SERIES OF TRAVELING EXHIBITIONS, KNOWN AS FLEXCART, TO REACH UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE STATE OF WYOMING. THE CARTS ARE MOBILE AND SMALL ENOUGH TO BE PUSHED THROUGH A CLASSROOM DOOR, AND FOCUS ON TEACHING STEM TOPICS USING A HANDS-ON INTERACTIVE APPROACH. FLEXCARTS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE FOR BOOKING BY FAMILY-SERVING AGENCIES ACROSS THE STATE, AS WELL AS NATRONA COUNTY SERVICE PROVIDERS. THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF STATEWIDE PARTNERSHIPS, CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES IN RURAL COMMUNITIES WILL GET TO EXPERIENCE HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES AND MUSEUM QUALITY STEM EXHIBITS AT NO COST.
description.3365: THE SAN DIEGO CHILDREN’S DISCOVERY MUSEUM WILL EMBARK ON THE BUILDING, CREATING, AND EXPANSION PHASE OF THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES PROJECT TO STRENGTHEN STAFF AND VISITOR'S CULTURAL APPRECIATION AND UNDERSTANDING OF THE CITY OF ESCONDIDO’S FIRST PEOPLES, THE KUMEYAAY NATION AND LUISEÑO TRIBES. MUSEUM STAFF AND TRIBAL CONSULTANTS WILL OFFER ONSITE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS AND STORYTELLING PROGRAMS, STAFF DEVELOPMENT AND TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES, AND FREE ACCESS TO THE MOBILE STEM WORKSHOPS FOR LOCAL TRIBAL SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL SOLIDIFY NEW PARTNERSHIPS AND ENGAGE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES PARTNERS TO HELP ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, AND CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS WILL DEVELOP AN APPRECIATION FOR NATURAL RESOURCES THROUGH THE LENS OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES.
description.3366: INFORMED BY THE FINDINGS OF A CONSERVATION ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, THE PINAL COUNTY HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL HIRE A PART-TIME COLLECTIONS MANAGER TO WORK WITH PAID INTERNS ON PROJECT ACTIVITIES THAT WILL INCLUDE A COMPREHENSIVE INVENTORY AND AN UPDATE THEIR COLLECTIONS RECORDS.  AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL IMPROVE COLLECTION STEWARDSHIP AND MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR FUTURE COLLECTIONS CARE, INCLUDING LONG-TERM PLANNING AND DEACCESSIONING. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL BE THE LOCAL COMMUNITY OF FLORENCE, ARIZONA, WHICH INCLUDES MEMBERS OF THE TOHONO O’ODHAM NATION, AND MEXICAN AND AFRICAN AMERICAN POPULATIONS.
description.3367: THE SEE SCIENCE CENTER WILL INCREASE ITS ABILITY TO WELCOME VISITORS WITH DISABILITIES BY REMOVING BARRIERS IN THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT AND THROUGH A NEW INCLUSIVE CUSTOMER SERVICE STAFF TRAINING PROGRAM. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING TWO UNIVERSAL DESIGN PRINCIPLES STAFF TRAININGS FOR SEE’S ACCESS TEAM; SELECTING, ORDERING, AND INSTALLING NEW ACCESSIBLE EQUIPMENT AND FURNISHINGS; CREATING AN ACOUSTIC MITIGATION REPORT; AND DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING NEW INCLUSIVE STAFF CUSTOMER SERVICE TRAINING BASED ON UNIVERSAL DESIGN PRINCIPLES. THE PROJECT WILL INVOLVE ENGAGING A CONSULTANT TO SERVE AS SEE’S ACCESSIBILITY AND INCLUSION ADVISOR AND TRAINER. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A MORE WELCOMING AND ACCESSIBLE SPACE FOR ALL VISITORS INCLUDING THOSE WITH PHYSICAL AND NEUROSENSORY DISABILITIES.
description.3368: THE BLACK MOUNTAIN COLLEGE MUSEUM AND ARTS CENTER WILL CATALOG APPROXIMATELY 2,000 OBJECTS FROM ITS COLLECTION RELATED TO THE HISTORIC BLACK MOUNTAIN COLLEGE. FOR THE PROJECT, THE INSTITUTION WILL HIRE A PART-TIME COLLECTIONS ASSISTANT TO WORK WITH PAID INTERNS ON DATA ENTRY AND COLLECTIONS STAFF WILL TRAIN INTERNS ON OBJECT HANDLING AND CATALOGUING. AFTER DATA ENTRY AND PHOTO DOCUMENTATION OF OBJECTS IS COMPLETE, STAFF WILL MAKE RECORDS ACCESSIBLE TO THE PUBLIC ONLINE. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL HAVE INCREASED INTELLECTUAL CONTROL OVER THE COLLECTION.
description.3369: SEA TURTLE INC. WILL INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY TO ITS ONSITE SCHOOL PROGRAMS BY DESIGNING A STATE-OF-THE-ART EDUCATION CLASSROOM IN ORDER TO PROVIDE QUALITY SCIENCE-BASED EDUCATION PROGRAMS IN ALIGNMENT WITH TEXAS STATE SCIENCE STANDARDS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE OUTFITTING THE CLASSROOM WITH UPDATED EQUIPMENT AND TECHNOLOGY, AND DEVELOPING CURRICULUM FOR 5TH-12TH GRADE SCHOOL GROUPS WITH A FOCUS ON THE RIO GRANDE VALLEY. THROUGH HANDS-ON, INTERACTIVE ACTIVITIES, STUDENTS WILL LEARN ABOUT AN ARRAY OF SCIENTIFIC TOPICS INCLUDING: CLASSIFICATION, ADAPTATIONS, ANATOMY, WATER QUALITY, PH, SALINITY, AND CURRENT CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS. AN EVALUATION PLAN WILL INCLUDE SURVEYING WORKSHOP PARTICIPANTS TO ENSURE THAT STUDENTS LEARN ABOUT THE IMPORTANCE OF THE MARINE ENVIRONMENT, WHICH WILL HELP FOSTER THE NEXT GENERATION OF OCEAN STEWARDS.
description.3370: THE SKID ROW HISTORY MUSEUM AND ARCHIVE WILL CREATE THE MULTI-DISCIPLINARY PROJECT, “WELCOME TO THE VAGABOND HOTEL.” THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON THE INTERPERSONAL AND HOLISTIC PANDEMIC RESPONSE DEVELOPED ON-THE-FLY BY HEALTH WORKERS WHO RAN LOS ANGELES COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT’S EMERGENCY QUARANTINE AND ISOLATION SITES CREATED FOR HOUSELESS COVID PATIENTS AND PEOPLE EXPOSED TO COVID IN SHELTERS. THE MUSEUM AND A TEAM OF COLLABORATORS, INCLUDING ARTISTS FROM SKID ROW, WILL PRODUCE THEATRICAL PERFORMANCES, AN EXHIBITION, AND TRANSFORM THE GALLERY INTO A REPLICA OF A QUARANTINE AND ISOLATION SITE. SKID ROW COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND HOUSING ADVOCATES, AS WELL AS POLICY MAKERS, JOURNALISTS, SCHOLARS, AND PUBLIC AUDIENCES WILL BENEFIT FROM KNOWLEDGE GAINED ABOUT THE WAYS COMPASSIONATE PRACTICES CAN LEAD TO BETTER OUTCOMES FOR INDIVIDUALS AND SOCIETY.
description.3371: THE GOLD NUGGET MUSEUM WILL CONDUCT STAFF TRAINING AND DEVELOP MUSEUM OPERATIONAL MANUALS TO HELP THE MUSEUM REBUILD AFTER LOSING ITS ORIGINAL LOCATION, NEARLY ITS ENTIRE COLLECTION, AND ALL RECORDS TO CALIFORNIA’S 2018 CAMP FIRE WILDFIRE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE PROFESSIONAL TRAINING FOR MUSEUM STAFF, INCLUDING WORKSHOPS, CLASSES, AND WEBINARS TO BUILD INTERNAL INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY. ONCE THE TRAINING IS COMPLETE, STAFF WILL CREATE FOUR POLICY AND PROCEDURES MANUALS INCLUDING A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT MANUAL, EXHIBIT DEVELOPMENT AND INSTALLATION MANUAL, EMERGENCY PLAN, AND A VISITOR SERVICES/DOCENT MANUAL. THE PROJECT WILL GUIDE THE PROFESSIONAL OPERATION OF THE MUSEUM AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE AND ENGAGING EXHIBITS AND PROGRAMMING FOR MUSEUM VISITORS.
description.3372: THE SCIENCE MILL WILL EXPAND THE IMLS-FUNDED PILOT PROJECT, SUMMER STEM CAREER INITIATIVE (SCI) CAMPS PROGRAM, INTO THE BIG BEND REGION OF FAR WEST TEXAS, AN UNDERSERVED RURAL TEXAS COMMUNITY. THE EXPANSION WILL CONSIST OF OFFERING IMMERSIVE SUMMER STEM CAMPS, SUPPORTED BY THE MUSEUM’S MOBILE STEM VAN INITIATIVE TO 3RD-8TH GRADE STUDENTS. IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SUL ROSS STATE UNIVERSITY, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DEVELOP AND OFFER ONE-WEEK LONG CAMPS BASED IN REAL-WORLD STEM CAREER SCENARIOS INCLUDING CODING AND PROGRAMMING, ENGINEERING, LIFE SCIENCES, ROBOTICS, AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP. AS A RESULT, RURAL STUDENTS WILL INCREASE THEIR INTEREST IN STEM LEARNING AND SEE THEMSELVES AS PART OF A FUTURE 21ST CENTURY SKILLED WORKFORCE. STUDENT OUTCOME AND IMPACT WILL BE MEASURED THROUGH ANALYSIS OF SURVEY RESPONSES AND WILL TRACK A VARIETY OF METRICS SPECIFIC TO CAMPER EXPERIENCE.
description.3373: THE LIVINGSTON COUNTY HISTORICAL MUSEUM WILL USE FUNDS TO PURCHASE AND INSTALL ARCHIVAL STORAGE EQUIPMENT. THE PROJECT BUILDS UPON PLANNING DOCUMENTS CREATED BY A TEAM OF MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS, ARCHITECTS, AND ENGINEERS, AND WILL ADDRESS ISSUES OF OVERCROWDING AND INACCESSIBILITY OF OBJECTS IN THE CURRENT STORAGE SPACE. INFORMED BY A PREVIOUS COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL CONSULT WITH A CONSERVATOR TO IMPLEMENT BEST PRACTICES FOR COLLECTION STORAGE. IMPROVED COLLECTIONS CARE WILL BENEFIT VISITORS AND RESEARCHERS, INCLUDING THE RESIDENTS OF LIVINGSTON COUNTY AND THE WESTERN NEW YORK REGION.
description.3374: THE DANFORTH ART MUSEUM AT FRAMINGHAM STATE UNIVERSITY WILL REHOUSE AND IMPROVE THE SAFETY OF OBJECTS IN ITS PERMANENT COLLECTION OF OVER 3,600 WORKS OF ART. MUSEUM STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CURATORIAL FELLOW TO IMPLEMENT THE COLLECTION PRESERVATION AND ACCESSIBILITY PROJECT. THE FIRST PHASE OF THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE ARCHIVAL REHOUSING OF OBJECTS, INCLUDING SCULPTURES AND PORTRAITS. THE SECOND PHASE WILL IMPROVE THE SAFETY OF OBJECTS FOR DISPLAY BY REPLACING HANGING MATERIALS AND ADDING PROTECTIVE BACKINGS. THE THIRD PHASE WILL IMPROVE STORAGE SPECIFICALLY FOR FRAMES IN THE COLLECTION. INCREASED SAFETY AND ACCESSIBILITY OF COLLECTIONS IN STORAGE WILL BENEFIT STAFF, RESEARCHERS, AND COLLEGE CLASSES.
description.3375: THE CHILDREN’S MUSEUM OF BROWNSVILLE WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO PLAY-BASED STEM EXPERIENCES THROUGH A NEW EXHIBIT TITLED, “REACH FOR THE STARS.” THE INTERACTIVE EXHIBIT WILL FOCUS ON MIXED AIR TRAVEL SUCH AS AIRPLANES, BLIMPS, ROCKETS, AND DRONES WHILE MAKING A CONNECTION BETWEEN PAST, PRESENT, AND FUTURE TO DEMONSTRATE THE ADVANCEMENTS IN SCIENTIFIC TECHNOLOGY AND THE POTENTIAL THAT IT HOLDS FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. THE MUSEUM WILL ENGAGE WITH DOSEUM IN SAN ANTONIO TO CREATE EXHIBITION SCHEMATICS AND SERVE AS THE FABRICATION PROJECT MANAGER. BY ENCOURAGING A NEW GENERATION OF STUDENTS, MAINLY YOUNG GIRLS, TO DEVELOP AN INTEREST IN PROBLEM-SOLVING, COLLABORATION, COMMUNICATION SKILLS, AND DISCOVERY, THE MUSEUM WILL PROVIDE VISITORS WITH A MEANINGFUL DIRECTION REGARDING THEIR FUTURE STUDIES AND CAREERS.
description.3376: THE CAYUGA MUSEUM OF HISTORY AND ART WILL COMPLETE THE RESEARCH PHASE OF THE MUSEUM’S PLANNED PERMANENT EXHIBIT EXPLORING THE COMPREHENSIVE HISTORY OF CAYUGA COUNTY. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT HIRING A NEW CURATOR AND A PAID INTERN WHO WILL CREATE A NEW INTERPRETIVE PLAN WHICH WILL BE USED AS THE FRAMEWORK TO INFORM THE EXHIBIT PLAN AND FINAL IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NEW EXHIBIT. THROUGH THIS PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL ACTIVELY EXPLORE THE NARRATIVE OF HISTORICALLY EXCLUDED COMMUNITIES WITH THE GOAL TO CREATE AN INVITING SPACE FOR CONSISTENT ENGAGEMENT WITH REGIONAL HISTORY.
description.3377: HISTORIC SARANAC LAKE WILL CREATE CATALOG RECORDS FOR APPROXIMATELY 2,500 OBJECTS AND ARCHIVAL MATERIALS TO GAIN INTELLECTUAL AND PHYSICAL CONTROL OVER ITS COLLECTION. INFORMED BY A PREVIOUS IMLS-FUNDED PILOT PROJECT TO CATALOG RECORDS FOR APPROXIMATELY 2,000 PHOTOGRAPHS AND POSTCARDS FROM THE MUSEUM'S COLLECTIONS, THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO INCLUDE PHOTO DOCUMENTATION OF OBJECTS AND THE CREATION OF A PLAN FOR MOVING THE COLLECTION TO A NEW STORAGE SPACE. PROJECT STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONSULTANT TO COMPLETE AND EVALUATE THE PROJECT. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE INSTITUTION WILL PRODUCE A COMPREHENSIVE MOVING PLAN FOR THE COLLECTION, PUBLISH CATALOG RECORDS AND IMAGES, AND INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY TO THE COLLECTION. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT STUDENTS, RESEARCHERS, AND STAFF PREPARING FOR EXHIBITS AND PROGRAMS.
description.3378: CHESTERWOOD, A HISTORIC SITE OF THE NATIONAL TRUST FOR HISTORIC PRESERVATION, WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL MUSEUM-QUALITY STORAGE CABINETS FOR OBJECTS AND ARCHIVAL FILES, AND ALLOW SPACE FOR SCHOLARLY RESEARCH IN THE NEWLY CREATED CHESTERWOOD COLLECTIONS AND RESEARCH CENTER. AS THE FORMER HOME, STUDIO, AND GARDENS OF SCULPTOR DANIEL CHESTER FRENCH (1850-1931), CHESTERWOOD HAS THE LARGEST COLLECTION OF ART BY FRENCH, IN ADDITION TO WORKS BY OTHER ARTISTS, HISTORIC DOCUMENTS, AND PHOTOGRAPHS. THE PROJECT WILL MAXIMIZE NEWLY RENOVATED SPACE THROUGH THE INSTALLATION OF A HIGH-DENSITY MOBILE SHELVING SYSTEM, CREATING OPTIMAL AND EFFICIENT STORAGE THAT WILL ENSURE THE LONGEVITY OF THE COLLECTION AND INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY FOR STUDENTS, ARTISTS, RESEARCHERS, CURATORS, MEMBERS OF THE GENERAL PUBLIC, AND STAFF.
description.3379: THE LAFAYETTE HISTORY MUSEUM WILL CONDUCT AN INVENTORY OF ITS COLLECTION OF APPROXIMATELY 4,000 ARTIFACTS AND INCREASE DIGITAL ACCESS TO THE MATERIAL. THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION INCLUDES AGRICULTURAL AND COAL MINING TOOLS, TEXTILES, ARCHIVAL DOCUMENTS, ORAL HISTORIES, MAPS, AND PHOTOGRAPHS PERTAINING TO THE HISTORY OF LAFAYETTE, COLORADO. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A COLLECTIONS ASSISTANT TO HELP COMPLETE THE INVENTORY AND TRAIN VOLUNTEER AND PAID STUDENT INTERNS IN OBJECT HANDLING AND DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL UPLOAD DIGITIZED RECORDS TO AN ONLINE COLLECTIONS DATABASE. ONCE COMPLETED, THE UPDATED DATABASE WILL ALLOW FOR THE PUBLIC AND RESEARCHERS TO ACCESS THE COLLECTION MORE EASILY.
description.3380: BIG CAR WILL INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY TO ITS EXHIBITIONS AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS FOR THE RESIDENTS OF SOUTH INDIANAPOLIS WITH A FOCUS ON REACHING THE GROWING SPANISH-SPEAKING POPULATION. THE INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM WILL WORK WITH LOCAL AND INTERNATIONAL ARTISTS TO OFFER ARTIST TALKS, WORKSHOPS, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAMS TO SUPPLEMENT FOUR EXHIBITIONS. THE CONTENT WILL ALSO BE BROADCAST THROUGH THE MUSEUM-RUN FM RADIO STATION THAT IS ALSO AVAILABLE THROUGH ONLINE PLATFORMS. THE SOUND PIECES — SHARED IN SPANISH AND ENGLISH — WILL ALLOW PEOPLE TO HEAR DIRECTLY FROM A DIVERSE ARRAY OF NOTABLE ARTISTS FROM AROUND THE WORLD. BY REMOVING THE PHYSICAL, CULTURAL, AND LINGUISTIC BARRIERS, VISITORS AND LISTENERS WILL FEEL WELCOMED IN THE GALLERY SPACES, AND HAVE ACCESS TO BILINGUAL PROGRAMS AND MATERIALS.
description.3381: THE GAITHERSBURG COMMUNITY MUSEUM WILL BUILD ON THE CITY’S GAITHERSBURG HISTORY PROJECT BY DEVELOPING AN INTERPRETATIVE FRAMEWORK FOR COMMUNICATING THE STORIES OF GROUPS THAT COMPRISE GAITHERSBURG’S CULTURALLY-DIVERSE COMMUNITY WITH A FOCUS ON BLACK AND LATINX RESIDENTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE ASSESSING SHARED AND POTENTIAL RESOURCES, HIRING A PROJECT MANAGER AND AN INTERPRETIVE PLANNER, AND DEVELOPING INTERPRETATIVE PRODUCTS FOR EACH IDENTIFIED CULTURAL GROUP. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A COMPREHENSIVE INTERPRETATIVE PLAN WITH A SUITE OF EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES INCLUDING TRAVELING EXHIBITS, DIGITAL STORYTELLING, AND EDUCATIONAL AND COMMUNITY OUTREACH PROGRAMS. MUSEUM VISITORS AND LOCAL OFFICIALS WILL BE BETTER ABLE TO CONNECT WITH THE RESIDENTS OF GAITHERSBURG BY LEARNING ABOUT THEIR STORIES AND CHALLENGES.
description.3382: THE HALF MOON BAY HISTORY ASSOCIATION WILL LEAD A PROJECT TO ASSESS ITS EDUCATION PROGRAMS AND FORMULATE PLANNING DOCUMENTS TO SHAPE FUTURE PREK–12 EDUCATION PROGRAMS WITH AN EMPHASIS ON INCORPORATING MATERIALS TO REACH BILINGUAL AND LATINX STUDENTS IN SAN MATEO COUNTY. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE HIRING A MUSEUM EDUCATION CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF EXISTING PROGRAMS, CREATE A PLAN FOR UPDATING THE PROGRAMS AND DEVELOPING NEW PROGRAMS, AND BUILD AN EVALUATION FRAMEWORK. FOLLOWING THE ASSESSMENT AND PLAN DEVELOPMENT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL IMPLEMENT THE PROGRAMS AND SHARE THE PLAN FOR REPLICATION BY OTHER MUSEUMS. THROUGH THIS PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION PROJECT, VISITORS WILL HAVE A GREATER UNDERSTANDING OF COASTSIDE HISTORY, FROM OHLONE TIMES TO THE RECENT PAST.
description.3383: THE SOMALI MUSEUM OF MINNESOTA WILL ENGAGE MULTIGENERATIONAL AUDIENCES OF SOMALI-AMERICANS AND NON-SOMALI MINNESOTANS IN HANDS-ON CULTURAL PROGRAMMING BY EXPANDING ITS MOBILE CULTURE SHOW AND CULTURAL WORKSHOPS. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS AN ONGOING DEMAND FOR IN-PERSON AUDIENCE EXPERIENCES, INCLUDING THOSE WHICH INTRODUCE NEWCOMERS TO SOMALI CULTURAL ART FORMS, AND THOSE THAT REINFORCE A CONNECTION BETWEEN ELDER GENERATIONS AND YOUTH. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE HIRING AND TRAINING FOUR PROGRAM COORDINATORS, COACHING MUSEUM STAFF IN PROGRAM FACILITATION, WORKING WITH THE RESIDENT ARTISTS TO EXPAND PROGRAM OFFERINGS, AND DEVELOPING A MONTHLY SCHEDULE OF FREE AND ACCESSIBLE WORKSHOPS OFFERED BOTH ON-SITE AND AT COMMUNITY PARTNER LOCATIONS. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE OF SOMALI HERITAGE ART FORMS AND CULTURAL HISTORY, AND STRENGTHEN CONNECTIONS BETWEEN SOMALI-AMERICAN GENERATIONS.
description.3384: CHINESE CULTURE CENTER OF SAN FRANCISCO WILL EXPAND THE PILOT PROJECT, “41 ROSS ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE,” LOCATED AT THE CENTER’S OFFSITE STOREFRONT ALLEYWAY PROJECT SPACE IN SAN FRANCISCO’S CHINATOWN. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE SELECTING THREE ARTISTS FOR THREE-MONTH RESIDENCIES, ORGANIZING PUBLIC PROGRAMS, AND OFFERING PARTICIPATORY OPEN STUDIOS AND FREE WORKSHOPS. CENTER STAFF WILL MATCH SELECTED ARTISTS WITH A MENTOR, AND PROVIDE SUPPORT THROUGHOUT THE RESIDENCY INCLUDING ACCESS TO MARKETING AND OUTREACH CHANNELS, TRANSLATION SERVICES, AND VIDEO DOCUMENTATION. COMMUNITY MEMBERS LIVING AND WORKING IN CHINATOWN WILL BE THE TARGET AUDIENCE, MANY OF WHOM ARE NEW IMMIGRANTS, WORKING CLASS, LOW INCOME, YOUTH, AND SENIORS. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE EXISTING AND EMERGENT STRUCTURAL ISSUES FACING CHINATOWN AND ASIAN AMERICAN CONSTITUENTS TODAY, SUCH AS ANTI-ASIAN HATE, LACK OF CULTURAL RESOURCES, AND THE NEED TO SHIFT DOMINANT NARRATIVES.
description.3385: THE CLARK COUNTY HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL INVENTORY, REHOUSE, AND UPDATE ARTIFACT RECORDS IN A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE FOR ITS COLLECTION OF HISTORIC TEXTILES, MEDICAL TOOLS, PINS, AND FASHION ITEMS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL ADDRESS PREVIOUS DAMAGE TO COLLECTIONS STORAGE CAUSED BY WATER INTRUSION. STAFF WILL PURCHASE NEW SHELVING AND REHOUSING MATERIALS, SUPERVISE THE SHELVING INSTALLATION, AND INPUT DATA INTO A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE TO MAINTAIN ACCURATE OBJECT LOCATION AND INVENTORY INFORMATION. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL HAVE INCREASED ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION FOR THE PURPOSES OF EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING, EXHIBITION, AND RESEARCH.
description.3386: THE NATIONAL CANAL MUSEUM WILL DEVELOP AN EDUCATIONAL GRAPHIC NOVEL BASED ON THE LIFE EXPERIENCES OF CAPTAIN JAMES “JIMMY” BROWN, A BLACK CANAL BOATMAN THAT WORKED ON THE DELAWARE AND LEHIGH CANAL SYSTEM IN EASTERN PENNSYLVANIA IN THE EARLY 1900S. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE ASSEMBLING A MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ADVISORY GROUP, CONTRACTING AN ILLUSTRATOR, REVIEWING AND REVISING GRAPHIC NOVEL TEXT AND ARTWORK, AND WORKING WITH A GRAPHIC DESIGNER ON THE BOOK LAYOUT. THE GRAPHIC NOVEL, ALONG WITH ASSOCIATED RESOURCES, WILL BE ALIGNED TO MEET STATE AND NATIONAL CURRICULUM STANDARDS, AND WILL BE PILOTED OVER THE COURSE OF TWO SEMESTERS IN MIDDLE SCHOOLS WITHIN THE DELAWARE AND LEHIGH NATIONAL HERITAGE CORRIDOR. DATA COLLECTED FROM BOTH PILOTS WILL BE USED TO FINALIZE THE TEACHING RESOURCES AND AN EDUCATOR TRAINING SESSION. LOCAL MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENTS AND THEIR FAMILIES, AND PARTICULARLY PEOPLE OF COLOR WILL BENEFIT FROM THE PROJECT BY SEEING THEMSELVES PORTRAYED IN LOCAL AND U.S. HISTORY. THE PROJECT WILL SHARE A MORE DIVERSE NARRATIVE THAN HAS BEEN TRADITIONALLY TOLD WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF AMERICAN CANAL HISTORY AND WILL PROVIDE AN ENGAGING MEANS FOR STUDENTS TO LEARN ABOUT THEIR REGIONAL HISTORY AND STRENGTHEN THEIR LITERACY.
description.3387: THE SHELTON MCMURPHEY JOHNSON HOUSE WILL INCREASE MUSEUM STAFF CAPACITY TO OFFER FAMILY AND YOUTH EDUCATION PROGRAMS, AND CONDUCT OUTREACH ACTIVITIES TARGETED TO 4TH GRADE STUDENTS IN RURAL COMMUNITIES FURTHER THAN 10 MILES FROM THE MUSEUM OR AT LOW-INCOME SCHOOLS WITHIN THE EUGENE/SPRINGFIELD METRO AREA. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT A NEW POSITION FOR A PART-TIME FAMILY AND YOUTH EDUCATION COORDINATOR TO LEAD EXISTING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING AND GROW MUSEUM OFFERINGS TO REACH CHILDREN AND FAMILIES IN LANE COUNTY. THE EDUCATION COORDINATOR’S PRIMARY DUTIES WILL INCLUDE DEVELOPING CURRICULUM, MANAGING PROGRAMS, LAUNCHING A SERIES OF ONSITE CAMPS, CONDUCTING OUTREACH, AND SHARING THE MUSEUM’S RESOURCES BEYOND THE PROPERTY BOUNDARIES. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL HAVE AN EXPANDED PORTFOLIO OF EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES TO MAKE AVAILABLE TO THE RESIDENTS OF EUGENE AND THE SURROUNDING AREA.
description.3388: PUGET SOUND ESTUARIUM WILL EXPAND ITS PARTNERSHIP WITH THE 21ST CENTURY COMMUNITY LEARNING CENTER AND OFFER A SUITE OF OUT-OF-SCHOOL PROGRAMS FOR K-12 STUDENTS IN THURSTON COUNTY, WASHINGTON, INCLUDING FIELD TRIPS TO BUDD INLET AND HENDERSON INLET. THE ESTUARIUM’S STEM AFTER SCHOOL PROGRAM, SPRING TIDES CAMP, AND ESTUARY EXPLORERS SUMMER CAMPS ARE DESIGNED TO SUPPORT STEM FUNDAMENTALS, AND ARE ALIGNED WITH NEXT GENERATION SCIENCE STANDARDS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS WITH HANDS-ON, ESTUARINE ECOLOGY EDUCATION IN THE CLASSROOM, AT THE ESTUARIUM FACILITY, AND IN THE FIELD, AND TEACHERS WILL BE PROVIDED WITH ESTUARY LEARNING KITS FOR USE IN CLASSROOMS. THE ESTUARIUM WILL HIRE A PART-TIME INTERN TO SUPPORT EDUCATION STAFF AND FILL IN AS THE FIELD LEAD WHEN NECESSARY. AS A RESULT, K-12 YOUTH WILL BE EMPOWERED TO BECOME THE NEXT GENERATION OF STEWARDS, SCIENTISTS, AND CONSERVATIONISTS OF OUR WATERSHEDS IN THE SOUTH PUGET SOUND REGION, THE SALISH SEA AT LARGE, AND BEYOND.
description.3389: BUILDING UPON A PREVIOUS IMLS PROJECT, THE MUSEUM OF CRAFT AND DESIGN WILL EXPAND THE MOBILE MAKEART PROJECT TO CREATE AND DISTRIBUTE FREE, MULTILINGUAL INSTRUCTIONAL ART KITS TO OVER 8,000 PEOPLE IN THE BAY AREA. ADDITIONALLY, THE MUSEUM WILL CONSULT WITH LOCAL DISABILITY ORGANIZATIONS AND DEVELOP AN ACCESSIBILITY ROADMAP AND EXHIBITION-RELATED AUDIO AND TOUCH TOURS TO BE EXPERIENCED INSIDE THE MUSEUM, ONLINE, AND AT PARTNER SITES, INCLUDING PUBLIC SCHOOLS, LIBRARIES, AND PARKS. EVALUATION BY MOBILE MAKEART PARTICIPANTS AS WELL AS INPUT SOUGHT FROM SPECIFIC DISABILITY AGENCY PARTNERS WILL INFORM COURSE CORRECTION DURING THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ACCESSIBILITY INITIATIVES. MUSEUM STAFF WILL SURVEY PARTICIPANTS AND PARTNERS, AND GATHER FEEDBACK FROM DISABILITY ADVOCACY GROUPS TO ASSESS THE EFFICACY OF THESE NEWLY DEVELOPED TOOLS. THESE HANDS-ON ART EXPERIENCES WILL ENCOURAGE CREATIVITY, CONNECTION, AND KNOWLEDGE OF CRAFT AND DESIGN, AS WELL AS ENGAGE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, SUCH AS PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES, LOW-INCOME CHILDREN AND FAMILIES, THE UNHOUSED, AND BIPOC COMMUNITIES.
description.3390: LA CASA DEL LIBRO BOOK MUSEUM WILL LAUNCH AN EXHIBITION SERIES AND RELATED PROGRAMMING TO REACH EXISTING AND NEW AUDIENCES THAT WERE ADVERSELY AFFECTED BY CATASTROPHIC WEATHER EVENTS AND, MORE RECENTLY, THE PANDEMIC. COMMUNITY INPUT GATHERED DURING POST-COVID EVENTS HAS SHOWN THAT VISITORS, PARTICULARLY STUDENTS AND SENIORS, ARE INTERESTED IN ACCESSING IN-PERSON OPPORTUNITIES TO LEARN ABOUT THE MUSEUM COLLECTION. THIS PROJECT WILL INVOLVE HIRING A PART-TIME EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM COORDINATOR TO ASSIST MUSEUM STAFF WITH REBUILDING IN-PERSON PROGRAMS TO PRE-PANDEMIC LEVELS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PRESENTING THREE EXHIBITIONS, HOSTING EIGHT IN-PERSON FORUMS, AND SCHEDULING 12 ARTLAB WORKSHOPS. IN ADDITION, THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE PLANNING FOR THE MUSEUM TO HOST AN EXHIBITION CELEBRATING PUERTO RICAN AFRO-DESCENDANT ARTISTS IN COLLABORATION WITH THE INTERDISCIPLINARY AND MULTICULTURAL INSTITUTE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PUERTO RICO AT RÍO PIEDRAS. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL BE BETTER POSITIONED CARRY OUT ITS MISSION AND WILL BUILD RELATIONSHIPS WITH ITS COMMUNITY PARTNERS.
description.3391: ISLAND SPACE WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A YEARLONG EXHIBIT AND CULTURAL PROGRAMMING SERIES THAT CONSISTS OF THREE THEMATIC CULTURAL EXHIBITS, FOUR QUARTERLY ART EXHIBITS, AND 12 MONTHLY CULTURAL EVENTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING PROGRAMMATIC ELEMENTS, CONDUCTING COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND PROGRAM PROMOTION THROUGH PRODUCTION PARTNER NETWORKS, CAPTURING AND BROADCASTING CONTENT CREATED THROUGH PROJECT ACTIVITIES, AND COLLECTING REGULAR EVALUATIONS TO GAUGE AUDIENCE FEEDBACK, GROWTH, AND ENGAGEMENT. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS EFFORTS TO RAISE AWARENESS OF THE PROGRAM AS WELL AS SUPPORT TECHNICAL EQUIPMENT UPGRADES. THE PROJECT WILL ENGAGE VISITORS VIRTUALLY AND IN-PERSON, PROVIDING DYNAMIC REPRESENTATION OF CARIBBEAN THEMES, STORIES, AND CONVERSATIONS CONTRIBUTING TO A GREATER APPRECIATION OF THE REGION.
description.3392: THE LORAIN HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL INITIATE AN ORAL HISTORY PROJECT TO COLLECT AND SHARE STORIES OF OLDER ADULTS AND FOSTER DIALOGUE WITH AREA YOUTH. THE PROJECT BUILDS UPON TWO SUCCESSFUL ORAL HISTORY PROJECTS FOCUSED ON LORAIN’S LATINO AND BLACK RESIDENTS. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH A MULTI-MEDIA DESIGN FIRM TO DEVELOP A DIGITAL ORAL HISTORY KIOSK THAT WILL FEATURE APPROXIMATELY 76 SHORT-FORM DIGITAL ORAL HISTORIES AND ACCOMPANYING PHOTOGRAPHS. STAFF WILL MAKE THE ARCHIVE AVAILABLE ON A DEDICATED WEBSITE, WHICH WILL SERVE AS A PRIMARY SOURCE FOR RESEARCH PURPOSES. THE PROJECT WILL BUILD ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY AND ADVANCE INTERGENERATIONAL KNOWLEDGE FOR THE BENEFIT OF MUSEUM VISITORS, LOCAL RESIDENTS, SCHOLARS, EDUCATORS, AND STUDENTS.
description.3393: THE BAYOU TECHE MUSEUM IN LOUISIANA WILL PRESERVE ITS ORAL HISTORY COLLECTION BY DIGITIZING APPROXIMATELY 300 AUDIO CASSETTES AND VHS TAPES. THE ORAL HISTORIES DOCUMENT THE LIVES OF RESIDENTS OF NEW IBERIA, A COMMUNITY RICH IN HISTORY AND HERITAGE THAT IS A BLEND OF SPANISH, FRENCH, NATIVE AMERICAN, AND AFRICAN CULTURES. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE HIRING OF A PART-TIME ARCHIVIST TO CONVERT AND DIGITIZE AUDIO AND VIDEO TAPES AND ORGANIZE DIGITAL FILES. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE COMPUTERS AND CONVERSION EQUIPMENT TO CARRY OUT THE PROJECT. THE DIGITIZED ORAL HISTORY INTERVIEWS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE ON KIOSKS AT THE MUSEUM, ENABLING COMMUNITY MEMBERS, RESEARCHERS, AND THE PUBLIC TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THIS UNIQUE COMMUNITY THROUGH RESIDENTS’ LIVED EXPERIENCES.
description.3394: THE BARLOW PLANETARIUM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN WILL EXPAND ITS PROGRAMMING AND STUDENT OUTREACH BY BRINGING THE PLANETARIUM EXPERIENCE TO SCHOOLS AND THE LOCAL COMMUNITY. BARLOW STAFF WILL PURCHASE A PORTABLE PLANETARIUM, TRAIN STAFF IN ITS USE, AND SCHEDULE AND PROVIDE SCIENCE-BASED ASTRONOMY SHOWS FOR AREA SCHOOLS AND AT PUBLIC GATHERINGS. THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND SCIENCE EDUCATION WHILE PROVIDING A FUN LEARNING EXPERIENCE FOR STUDENTS WHO ARE CURRENTLY UNABLE TO VISIT THE PLANETARIUM DUE TO DISTANCE AND LIMITED ACCESS TO TRANSPORTATION. THE PLANETARIUM WILL EXTEND ITS REACH AND BUILD CAPACITY BY OFFERING ENGAGING ASTRONOMY PROGRAMMING OUTSIDE THE CONFINES OF ITS BUILDING. THE ULTIMATE BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE STUDENTS IN RURAL AND NORTHERN WISCONSIN AND THE UPPER PENINSULA SCHOOL DISTRICTS, AS WELL AS THE LOCAL COMMUNITY.
description.3395: THE L. C. BATES MUSEUM, A NATURAL HISTORY MUSEUM ON THE CAMPUS OF GOOD WILL-HINCKLEY HOMES, WILL PRESERVE AND SAFEGUARD 25 HISTORIC TAXIDERMY MOUNTS IN ITS COLLECTION. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH A PROFESSIONAL CONSERVATOR TO CARRY OUT TREATMENTS ON 21 BIRD MOUNTS, A LARGE WHITE MARLIN, AND THREE SMALL FISH MOUNTED BY NATURALIST AND TAXIDERMIST FRED C.N. PARKE. THE MOUNTS SELECTED FOR TREATMENT WERE INFORMED BY PREVIOUS COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) PROGRAM AND MUSEUM ASSESSMENT PROGRAM (MAP) RECOMMENDATIONS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL ALSO PROVIDE GUIDED TOURS TO EDUCATE VISITORS ABOUT THE PROJECT AND GENERAL COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP. CONSERVATION TREATMENT OF THE MOUNTS WILL ENSURE THEIR LONG-TERM PRESERVATION AND USE FOR RESEARCHERS, THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY, STUDENTS, AND MUSEUM VISITORS.
description.3396: THE CHILDREN'S CREATIVITY MUSEUM WILL DESIGN AN IMMERSIVE, SCIENCE-BASED EXHIBITION SPACE TO EXPLORE CALIFORNIA WATER RESOURCES AND USE THROUGH PLAYFUL, COLLABORATIVE LEARNING. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE EQUIPMENT AND SUPPLIES INCLUDING A THREE-TIERED WATER TABLE, ICE TABLE, BENCHES, FLOORING, AND INTERPRETIVE EXHIBIT ELEMENTS. THE MUSEUM WILL ENGAGE A WATER POLICY ADVISOR TO INFORM SCIENCE COMMUNICATIONS AND WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EXTERNAL EVALUATOR TO ASSESS VISITOR SATISFACTION. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN AN EXHIBITION THAT EDUCATES ON COMPLEX, REAL-WORLD CHALLENGES THROUGH PLAY. CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS WHO VISIT THE MUSEUM WILL BENEFIT FROM THE EXHIBITION’S SENSORY PLAY COMPONENTS. FINDINGS FROM EXTERNAL EVALUATION WILL HELP INFORM OTHER CHILDREN’S MUSEUMS THAT WISH TO EDUCATE ON WATER RESOURCES THROUGH HANDS-ON, INFORMAL LEARNING.
description.3397: THE WESTERN MUSEUM OF MINING AND INDUSTRY WILL DESIGN AND INSTALL A NEW PERMANENT, INTERACTIVE EXHIBITION ON MINERS TO EXPAND AND DIVERSIFY ITS CURRENT INTERPRETATION. THE EXHIBITION “WHO WERE MINERS?” WILL EXPLORE STORIES OF THE LATINO, NATIVE AMERICAN, ASIAN, BLACK, CORNISH, AND ITALIAN MEN AND WOMEN WHO PARTICIPATED IN THE WESTERN MINING DISTRICTS FROM 1849 TO THE PRESENT. STAFF AND INTERNS HAVE CONDUCTED PRELIMINARY RESEARCH AND IDENTIFIED STORYLINES. AS A NEXT STEP, THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EXHIBITION AND INTERPRETIVE DESIGN/PLANNING FIRM TO DESIGN AND INSTALL THE EXHIBITION. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A MORE INCLUSIVE AND ENGAGING NARRATIVE, BENEFITING MUSEUM VISITORS, AND IN PARTICULAR VISITORS FROM THE REPRESENTED COMMUNITIES.
description.3398: THE ROGER TORY PETERSON INSTITUTE WILL PURCHASE EQUIPMENT TO ENHANCE PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO THE APPROXIMATELY 80 FRAMED WORKS OF ART IN ITS COLLECTION. THE INSTITUTE HOLDS THE LARGEST COLLECTION OF WORKS BY THE ARTIST-NATURALIST AND CREATOR OF THE WELL-KNOWN PETERSON FIELD GUIDES. INFORMED BY A 2022 COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL POWDER-COATED CABINETS AND WALL-MOUNTED SCREENS TO STORE ITS FRAMED ARTWORK COLLECTION. STAFF WILL ALSO TAKE THE OPPORTUNITY TO PHOTOGRAPH AND COMPLETE CONDITION REPORTS FOR EACH PIECE AS IT IS BEING REHOUSED. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO THE FRAMED ART IN THE COLLECTION AND THE CREATION OF MORE FUNCTIONAL SPACE FOR COLLECTION CARE SUPPORT ACTIVITIES.
description.3399: FRIENDS OF ZOO BOISE WILL PRODUCE AND INSTALL 27 INTERPRETATIVE SIGNS FOR ANIMAL EXHIBITS IN ITS NEW EDUCATION FACILITY AND RENOVATED SMALL ANIMAL KINGDOM. VISITORS WILL LEARN ABOUT THE ANIMALS LIVING IN THESE EXHIBITS, HOW THE ZOO ENSURES ANIMAL WELL-BEING, AND WAYS TO PROTECT ANIMALS IN THE WILD. THE INTERPRETIVE ELEMENTS ARE GROUNDED IN BEST PRACTICES FOR FOSTERING EMPATHY FOR WILDLIFE. THE MUSEUM WILL PURCHASE ALUMINUM COMPOSITE SIGNS FOR INDOOR USE AND HIGH-PRESSURE LAMINATE SIGNS FOR OUTDOOR SPACES AND WILL CONTRACT WITH THE VENDOR FOR SIGN INSTALLATION. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONDUCT SURVEYS AND EVALUATIONS TO MEASURE LEARNING AND BEHAVIOR CHANGE OUTCOMES OF VISITORS AND PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS. THE NEW SIGNAGE WILL BENEFIT ZOO GUESTS AND EDUCATION PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS AND WILL INCREASE THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF, AND EMPATHY FOR, THE ANIMALS LIVING AT ZOO BOISE.
description.3400: THE SKID ROW HISTORY MUSEUM AND ARCHIVE WILL CREATE AN EXHIBITION AND RELATED PROGRAMMING TO EXAMINE THE HISTORY AND DECLINE OF RESIDENTIAL HOTEL HOUSING IN SKID ROW. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING ORAL HISTORIES AND HOSTING AN EXHIBITION, THEATRICAL PERFORMANCE, AND PUBLIC FORUMS. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT STAFF AND PROJECT PERFORMERS AND SPEAKERS. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH VISUAL ARTISTS AND INSTALLERS TO DESIGN AND REALIZE THE EXHIBITION AND A BOOK DESIGNER FOR A PROJECT PUBLICATION. THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO CREATE GREATER AWARENESS OF THE HOUSING CRISIS AND SHED LIGHT ON VIABLE SOLUTIONS THAT EXIST AND HAVE BEEN IMPLEMENTED IN THE PAST, BENEFITING SKID ROW RESIDENTS, CITY LEADERS, JOURNALISTS, ACADEMICS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3401: THE DELAWARE MUSEUM OF NATURE AND SCIENCE WILL REHOUSE APPROXIMATELY 10,500 CLUTCHES OF SONGBIRD EGGS IN ITS COLLECTION, CONTRIBUTING TO THEIR LONG-TERM PRESERVATION. THE MUSEUM HAS THE SECOND LARGEST COLLECTION OF EGGS IN NORTH AMERICA REPRESENTING OVER 2,000 BIRD SPECIES. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE ARCHIVAL BOXES AND PAPER AND HIRE AND TRAIN AN INTERN TO ASSIST WITH REHOUSING. PROVIDING ACID-FREE STORAGE FOR THE EGG COLLECTION WAS IDENTIFIED AS A HIGH CONSERVATION PRIORITY IN THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) PROGRAM REPORT, AS THIS WILL HELP STABILIZE AND PROTECT IT FROM BYNE’S DISEASE, A CHEMICAL REACTION THAT CAN DAMAGE EGGSHELLS. PRESERVATION OF THE SPECIMENS WILL ENSURE THEIR INTEGRITY FOR RESEARCH AND ADVANCEMENTS IN SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE AND ENHANCE ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION.
description.3402: VICTORIA COLLEGE'S MUSEUM OF THE COASTAL BEND IN VICTORIA, TEXAS, WILL PROVIDE TWO PAID INTERNSHIP OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS TO ASSIST IN MIGRATING CATALOG DATA TO A NEW COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. VICTORIA COLLEGE IS A HISPANIC SERVING INSTITUTION (HSI) WITH OVER HALF OF ITS STUDENT POPULATION IDENTIFYING AS LATINO. BUILDING UPON A PREVIOUS IMLS PROJECT, THIS IS THE SECOND PHASE OF A STEWARDSHIP INITIATIVE TO DIGITIZE AND CATALOG COLLECTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE HANDS-ON SKILLS AND TRAINING TO STUDENTS AND PUTS THE MUSEUM ONE STEP CLOSER TO PROVIDING AN OPEN DATABASE. DIGITIZING ITS COLLECTION WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS, RESEARCHERS, AND THE PUBLIC WITH ACCESS TO ARTIFACTS FROM THE LAST 13,000 YEARS AND INSIGHT INTO THE HISTORY OF THE COASTAL BEND.
description.3403: THE UNDERGROUND RAILROAD HISTORY PROJECT OF THE CAPITAL REGION WILL DEVELOP A MUSEUM STUDIES TEEN PROGRAM FOR JUNIOR AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS. THE ORGANIZATION WILL OFFER A COMPREHENSIVE OUT-OF-SCHOOL PROGRAM TO PREPARE STUDENTS FROM LOW-INCOME AND/OR MARGINALIZED BACKGROUNDS FOR A CAREER IN THE MUSEUM FIELD. STAFF WILL HIRE A FULL-TIME PROGRAM MANAGER, INITIATE PARTNERSHIPS FOR MENTORSHIP, DEVELOP CURRICULUM WITH INPUT FROM EXTERNAL CONSULTANTS, AND RECRUIT PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A READY-TO-IMPLEMENT PLAN THAT CAN BE SHARED WITH OTHER SMALL MUSEUMS WISHING TO REPLICATE THE PROGRAM AT THEIR INSTITUTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY, ENGAGE COMMUNITY YOUTH, AND HELP DIVERSIFY THE MUSEUM WORKFORCE, BENEFITING STUDENT PARTICIPANTS AND THE MUSEUM FIELD AS A WHOLE.
description.3404: THE CANSA'YAPI CULTURAL DEPARTMENT AT THE LOWER SIOUX COMMUNITY COUNCIL WILL INCREASE HISTORIC KNOWLEDGE OF NATIVE AMERICAN AND DAKOTA CULTURAL TRADITIONS THROUGH EDUCATIONAL EVENTS. THE DEPARTMENT IS A REPOSITORY FOR DAKOTA CULTURAL ARTIFACTS, INCLUDING STONE TOOLS, PROJECTILE POINTS, AND HISTORIC CULTURAL MATERIALS SUCH AS MOCCASINS, PIPE BAGS, AND HISTORIC PHOTOS. TO INCREASE ACCESS TO CULTURAL HISTORY AND ARTIFACTS, THE DEPARTMENT WILL HIRE A PART-TIME STAFF MEMBER TO PLAN AND HOST EDUCATIONAL EVENTS AND HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES FOR THE LOWER SIOUX AND SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES. PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE CHILDREN, FAMILIES, ELDERS, RETURNEES, AND RELATIVES.
description.3405: THE MANCHESTER HISTORIC ASSOCIATION WILL ORGANIZE AND REHOUSE ITS TEXTILE COLLECTION TO IMPROVE PRESERVATION AND ACCESS. THE COLLECTION INCLUDES OVER 5,000 ARTICLES OF PERIOD CLOTHING AND ACCESSORIES FROM THE 18TH THROUGH THE 20TH CENTURIES AND DOCUMENTS MANCHESTER’S ROLE AS A MAJOR TEXTILE PRODUCTION CENTER AND CONTRIBUTOR TO THE AMERICAN INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION. THIS PROJECT IS CRITICAL AS THE TEXTILES ARE CURRENTLY OVERCROWDED, INACCESSIBLE, AND AT RISK OF DETERIORATION. PROJECT STAFF WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL STORAGE RACKS AND CABINETS, ARCHIVAL BOXES AND SUPPLIES, AND MATERIALS TO IMPLEMENT INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT. AS PART OF THE PROJECT, THE CONDITION OF THE TEXTILES WILL BE ASSESSED, AND ITEMS WILL BE REHOUSED, CATALOGED, AND PHOTOGRAPHED.
description.3406: THE MATSON MUSEUM OF ANTHROPOLOGY AT PENNSYLVANIA STATE UNIVERSITY WILL IMPROVE COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP BY CATALOGING ITS COLLECTION OF ARCHAEOLOGICAL AND ETHNOGRAPHIC ARTIFACTS. INFORMED BY RECOMMENDATIONS FROM A COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, STAFF WILL REHOUSE COLLECTION ITEMS AND PREPARE THEM FOR AN UPCOMING MOVE INTO A NEW LOCATION. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL DIGITIZE COLLECTIONS TO CREATE A REFERENCE RESOURCE IN THE FORM OF A PUBLIC-FACING COLLECTIONS WEBPAGE AND SEARCH PORTAL. THE MAIN BENEFICIARIES OF PROJECT WILL BE STUDENTS, FACULTY, AND PUBLIC RESEARCHERS WHO WILL HAVE INCREASED ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION THROUGH EXPANDED PUBLIC PROGRAMMING, EXHIBITS, AND ONLINE RESOURCES.
description.3407: THE DELAWARE AGRICULTURAL MUSEUM WILL CREATE A SERIES OF OUTDOOR EXHIBITS THAT EXPLORE THE USE OF RENEWABLE ENERGY IN AGRICULTURE AND RURAL LIFE. THE MUSEUM WILL CREATE INTERACTIVE EXHIBITIONS THAT INCORPORATE WATER, WIND, SOLAR, AND ORGANIC MATTER TO DEMONSTRATE THAT RENEWABLE ENERGY IS PART OF THE FUTURE OF FARMING, AS WELL AS ITS PAST. COMPANION EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS AND ONLINE CONTENT WILL BE DEVELOPED TO INCREASE THE LEARNING POTENTIAL OF THE PROJECT. MUSEUM STAFF WILL CONTRACT WITH A CURATOR, EXHIBIT DESIGNER, AND WEB DESIGNER TO ASSIST WITH THE PROJECT. THE RESULTS WILL BE NEW EXHIBITS THAT SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF ECONOMIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, HEALTH, SOCIAL, AND HISTORICAL LITERACIES AND FOSTER A NEW UNDERSTANDING OF AGRICULTURE AND ENERGY FOR VISITORS OF ALL AGES.
description.3408: THE DENNOS MUSEUM CENTER, ON THE CAMPUS OF NORTHWESTERN MICHIGAN COLLEGE, WILL PURCHASE POWDER-COATED ART STORAGE BINS TO IMPROVE PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO APPROXIMATELY 225 FRAMED WORKS OF ART IN ITS COLLECTION. INFORMED BY A 2022 COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL REPLACE NON-ARCHIVAL PARTICLEBOARD PAINTING BINS WITH NEW ARCHIVAL UNITS. THE MUSEUM PURCHASED AND INSTALLED TWO OF THE UNITS AS A TRIAL, AND THIS PROJECT WILL ENABLE THE PURCHASE OF ADDITIONAL UNITS AND INTERLEAVING MATERIAL TO HOUSE THE ENTIRE FRAMED ART COLLECTION WITH ROOM FOR EXPANSION. THE NEW ADJUSTABLE ART STORAGE BINS WILL PROVIDE IMPROVED STORAGE AND MITIGATE DAMAGE TO WORKS OF ART WHEN ACCESSING THEM FOR STUDENTS, FACULTY, STAFF, RESEARCHERS, AND EXHIBITIONS.
description.3409: THE AVA GARDNER MUSEUM WILL DIGITIZE AND REHOUSE ITS COLLECTION OF OVERSIZED PAPER-BASED MATERIALS INCLUDING FILM POSTERS, LARGE-FORMAT PHOTOGRAPHS, AND SCRAPBOOKS THAT DOCUMENT THE ICONIC FILM LEGEND. THE MUSEUM IDENTIFIED THIS COLLECTION IN NEED OF IMPROVED PRESERVATION AS PART OF A PREVIOUS IMLS INVENTORY AND CATALOGING PROJECT. THIS DIGITIZATION AND REHOUSING PROJECT WILL SUPPORT MUSEUM STAFF TO MANAGE AND OVERSEE THIS IMPROVEMENT AND PURCHASE CAMERA EQUIPMENT, A FLAT-FILE STORAGE CABINET, AND ARCHIVAL SUPPLIES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL PARTNER WITH THE JOHNSTON COUNTY HERITAGE CENTER TO DIGITIZE A PORTION OF THE COLLECTION USING THEIR LARGE-FORMAT SCANNER. THE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT WILL BE IMPROVED PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION THROUGH VIRTUAL EXHIBITIONS AND AN ONLINE CATALOG, BENEFITING RESEARCHERS, FILM HISTORIANS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3410: THE BESS BOWER DUNN MUSEUM OF LAKE COUNTY WILL INITIATE A COMMUNITY-LED PROJECT TO INTEGRATE LATINO HISTORY AND CULTURE INTO THE MUSEUM’S PERMANENT EXHIBITION THROUGH NEW INTERPRETATION, DISPLAYS, AND SPANISH LANGUAGE AUDIO GUIDES. MUSEUM STAFF WILL IDENTIFY AND WORK TO FILL GAPS IN THE COLLECTION, PURCHASE EXHIBITION SUPPLIES AND MATERIALS, AND CONTRACT WITH A PROJECT ADVISOR AND AUDIOVISUAL CONSULTANT. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH THE COLLEGE OF LAKE COUNTY’S LATINO ALLIANCE STUDENT ORGANIZATION AND THE LATINO ADVISORY GROUP TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE VIEWPOINTS, VALUES, AND NEEDS OF THE LOCAL LATINO COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE THE ACCESSIBILITY AND RELEVANCE OF THE MUSEUM AND ITS OFFERINGS AND HELP TELL A MORE COMPREHENSIVE LAKE COUNTY STORY FOR ALL VISITORS.
description.3411: THE CASS COUNTY HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL PROCESS, CATALOG, AND REHOUSE ITS BACKLOG OF NEW ACCESSIONS TO ENHANCE PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTION. THE SOCIETY PRESERVES THE CULTURAL HERITAGE OF CASS COUNTY, MISSOURI, AND IS THE PRIMARY REPOSITORY FOR COLLECTIONS RELATED TO ITS HISTORY. INFORMED BY A RECENT COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, SOCIETY STAFF WILL PURCHASE STORAGE SHELVING AND ARCHIVAL MATERIALS TO PROCESS AND REHOUSE ITS BACKLOG OF NEW DONATIONS. THE SOCIETY WILL HIRE AND PROVIDE TRAINING TO TWO PAID INTERNS TO ASSIST WITH CATALOGING AND REHOUSING. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED PRESERVATION AND INTELLECTUAL CONTROL OF THE COLLECTION AND WILL ENABLE STAFF TO ENHANCE EXHIBITIONS AND PROGRAMMING.
description.3412: THE GREENVILLE MUSEUM OF ART WILL UPDATE ITS PERMANENT COLLECTIONS STORAGE AREA BASED ON RECOMMENDATIONS IN ITS RECENT CONSERVATION ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE TEMPORARILY RELOCATING ARTWORK, THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF HIGH-DENSITY STORAGE SYSTEMS, REHOUSING THE COLLECTION, AND ENHANCING CATALOG RECORDS. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH EAST CAROLINA UNIVERSITY TO PROVIDE TWO PAID SUMMER INTERNSHIPS TO SUPPORT PROJECT ACTIVITIES AND DEVELOP INTERPRETIVE AND EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED LONG-TERM STORAGE AND INCREASED CAPACITY FOR RESPONSIBLE GROWTH OF THE COLLECTION, BENEFITING STAFF, UNIVERSITY STUDENTS AND FACULTY, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3413: THE NEW MEXICO STATE UNIVERSITY MUSEUM WILL COMPLETE AN INVENTORY AND ASSESSMENT OF ITS ARCHAEOLOGICAL HOLDINGS TO IMPROVE INTELLECTUAL CONTROL AND PUBLIC ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION. REPRESENTING HUMAN HABITATION OF THE SOUTHWEST FROM THE EARLIEST KNOWN PALEOINDIAN OCCUPATION THROUGH THE LATE 1800S, THE COLLECTION INCLUDES REGIONAL POTTERY AND PROJECTILE POINT STYLES KEY IN MAKING IDENTIFICATIONS AND TRAINING STUDENTS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL HIRE AND MENTOR A GRADUATE ASSISTANT AND INTERNS TO ASSIST WITH THE INVENTORY, ASSESSMENT, AND PHOTOGRAPHY OF OBJECTS. THE RESULTING CATALOG DATA WILL BE ENTERED INTO THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM AND ONLINE DATABASE. AS A HISPANIC SERVING INSTITUTION, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE HANDS-ON TRAINING TO STUDENTS AND CONTRIBUTE TO AMPLIFYING THE MUSEUM WORKFORCE. GAINING INTELLECTUAL CONTROL OVER ITS ARCHAEOLOGICAL HOLDINGS AND MAKING THEM ACCESSIBLE WILL ENABLE STAFF TO BETTER USE AND DEVELOP THE COLLECTION, BENEFITING STUDENTS, FACULTY, AND RESEARCHERS.
description.3414: THE TOMAQUAG MUSEUM WILL UNDERTAKE A PROJECT TO CREATE AN INTERACTIVE OUTDOOR EXHIBITION OF A MISHOON, A DUGOUT CANOE TRADITIONALLY USED BY SOUTHEASTERN NEW ENGLAND'S INDIGENOUS TRIBES. AS PART OF THE PROJECT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL SELECT UP TO TEN NATIVE YOUTH ARTISTS TO LEARN TRADITIONAL MISHOON-MAKING SKILLS. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH A SPECIALIZED EXHIBITION DESIGN FIRM AND WAMPANOAG TRIBAL ARTISAN WHO WILL BUILD THE MISHOON, PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL TRAINING FOR STAFF, AND MENTOR YOUTH ARTISTS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN HANDS-ON TRAINING FOR INDIGENOUS YOUTH, TRAINING FOR MUSEUM STAFF, AND THE CREATION OF A WEATHERIZED, OUTDOOR MISHOON EXHIBIT, BENEFITING STAFF, THE TRIBES OF SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND, AND VISITORS.
description.3415: THE COASTAL INTERPRETIVE CENTER WILL UPDATE ITS CURRENT HABITAT ROOM INTO AN INTERACTIVE WATERSHED ECOSYSTEMS EXHIBITION, LINKING NATURAL AND HUMAN DIMENSIONS WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF WATERSHEDS OF WASHINGTON’S PACIFIC COAST. CENTER STAFF WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL TWO DIGITAL TOUCH TABLES AND CONTRACT WITH AN ARTIST TO PAINT A DIORAMA ILLUSTRATING EACH ECOSYSTEM OF THE WATERSHED. THE MUSEUM WILL CREATE FORMATIVE EVALUATIONS AND SOLICIT FEEDBACK FROM VISITORS, TEACHERS, AND STUDENTS THAT WILL INFORM THE FINAL EXHIBITION CONTENT. THE NEW EXHIBITION WILL RESULT IN AN INTERACTIVE AND ENGAGING DISPLAY THAT ADVANCES STEM KNOWLEDGE THROUGH INFORMAL SCIENCE EDUCATION, BENEFITING REGIONAL VISITORS, TEACHERS, AND STUDENTS.
description.3416: THE BERNARD A. ZUCKERMAN MUSEUM OF ART AT KENNESAW STATE UNIVERSITY WILL ENGAGE IN A PROJECT TO EXPLORE HOW ART MUSEUMS CAN CONTRIBUTE TO THE ADVANCEMENT OF HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. IN RESPONSE TO THE RECENT RISE IN LEVELS OF DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, AND LONELINESS IN UNIVERSITY AND COMMUNITY POPULATIONS, THE MUSEUM HOPES TO DEMONSTRATE THE POTENTIAL OF MUSEUMS TO SUPPORT MENTAL AND PHYSICAL WELL-BEING. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN AN EXHIBITION, ASSOCIATED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING, AND AN ACADEMIC CONVENING ON ADVANCING HEALTH AND WELL-BEING THROUGH THE ARTS. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH CAMPUS AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS TO DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK OF EVALUATION TO CAPTURE MEASURABLE OUTCOMES. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS, EDUCATORS, HEALTH PRACTITIONERS, AND STUDENTS SEEKING ALTERNATIVE METHODS TO REDUCE STRESS AND ANXIETY.
description.3417: THE MONTCLAIR HISTORY CENTER WILL UPDATE ITS CURRENT COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM TO IMPROVE WORKFLOW AND ENHANCE PUBLIC ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTION. THE CENTER’S OVER 15,000 ARTIFACTS AND ARCHIVAL MATERIALS PRESERVE THE HISTORY OF MONTCLAIR AND SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES AND SERVE AS A CRITICAL RESOURCE FOR THE PUBLIC. THE CENTER WILL TRANSITION TO A DATABASE WITH PUBLIC ACCESS, COMBINING ITS CURRENT SYSTEMS INTO ONE STREAMLINED MANAGEMENT TOOL. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE STAFF EFFICIENCY AND THE QUALITY AND QUANTITY OF SEARCHABLE COLLECTIONS ONLINE, ENABLING THE COMMUNITY AND THE PUBLIC TO CONNECT MORE DEEPLY WITH MONTCLAIR’S HISTORY.
description.3418: THE WEST END MUSEUM WILL EXPAND ITS REACH BY OFFERING APPROXIMATELY 100 TARGETED PILOT PROGRAMS AND EVENTS. OVER THE TWO-YEAR PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH STAKEHOLDERS TO ASSESS AND REVISE CURRENT OFFERINGS AND EXPLORE, DEVELOP, AND EVALUATE NEW PROGRAMS TO BETTER ENGAGE THE GREATER BOSTON COMMUNITY. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE PROGRAMMING SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT, MARKETING MATERIALS, AND RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONTRACT WITH A COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT FACILITATOR AND A RANGE OF PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS INCLUDING PERFORMERS, HISTORIANS, AND INSTRUCTORS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A PORTFOLIO OF SUSTAINED PROGRAM OFFERINGS REFLECTING THE NEEDS AND INTERESTS OF THE MUSEUM’S AUDIENCES, AND A ROBUST METHODOLOGY FOR THEIR ASSESSMENT. PROGRAMS WILL EDUCATE VISITORS, BRING TOGETHER COMMUNITY MEMBERS, AND ENGAGE NEW AUDIENCE MEMBERS IN THE MUSEUM’S URBAN-PLANNING-FOCUSED MISSION.
description.3419: BUILDING UPON A PREVIOUS IMLS PROJECT, PROVIDENCE COLLEGE GALLERIES WILL UNDERTAKE ACTIVITIES TO EXPAND DIGITAL ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTION AND DEEPEN ENGAGEMENT WITH MEMBERS OF ITS COMMUNITY WHO IDENTIFY AS DISABLED. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE TRAINING STAFF IN UNIVERSAL DESIGN LEARNING PRINCIPLES AND ALT-TEXT CAPTIONING AND ADDING ALT-TEXT TO 874 IMAGES ON THE GALLERIES’ WEBSITE AND ART COLLECTION DATABASE. MUSEUM STAFF WILL HIRE STUDENTS AND CONTRACT WITH A WRITER/EDITOR TO CREATE CAPTIONING AND AN ALT-TEXT GUIDE. AN ACCESS FOCUS GROUP WILL BE FORMED TO BUILD RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN THE MUSEUM AND THE DISABILITY COMMUNITY ON AND OFF CAMPUS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED ONLINE ACCESSIBILITY AND WILL SERVE DIVERSE POPULATIONS, CULTIVATE COMMUNITY CONNECTIONS, AND SUPPORT LOCAL AND INTERNATIONAL ARTISTS.
description.3420: THE FLOW CHART FOUNDATION WILL PARTNER WITH THE INFORMATION SCIENCES DEPARTMENT AT THE UNIVERSITY AT ALBANY TO CREATE A PAID INTERNSHIP PROGRAM AT THE ASHBERY RESOURCE CENTER (ARC). ARC IS THE FOUNDATION’S REPOSITORY AND SPECIAL COLLECTION LIBRARY DEDICATED TO THE SCHOLARLY RESEARCH OF THE 20TH-CENTURY AMERICAN POET, JOHN ASHBERY, AND THE BROADER NEW YORK SCHOOL OF POETS AND PAINTERS. THREE PART-TIME INTERNS WILL BE HIRED AND TRAINED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE ARC ’S ARCHIVIST/LIBRARIAN TO ASSIST WITH PROCESSING, CATALOGING, DIGITIZING, AND REHOUSING UNDOCUMENTED COLLECTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT MUSEUM AND LIBRARY WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT BY PROVIDING INTERNS WITH HANDS-ON TRAINING IN COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT AND ARCHIVAL PROCESSING. THE WORK COMPLETED BY INTERNS WILL ENHANCE PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION FOR STUDENTS, VISITORS, AND RESEARCHERS AND EXPAND DOCUMENTATION FOR USE IN EXHIBITIONS AND PROGRAMMING.
description.3421: THE CHILDREN'S MUSEUM OF GREEN BAY WILL PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING AND FREE MUSEUM ADMISSION TO SUPPORT READING PROGRAMS AT RURAL LIBRARIES IN NORTHEAST WISCONSIN. FOSTERING LITERACY IS A CRITICAL NEED, WITH ONLY 35% OF WISCONSIN THIRD-GRADE STUDENTS MEETING READING PROFICIENCY TARGETS. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH FIVE REGIONAL LIBRARIES TO OFFER A SERIES OF OUTREACH PROGRAMS, SIX MINI-TRAVELING EXHIBITIONS, AND FREE MUSEUM PASSES. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT EDUCATION STAFF TIME AND TRAVEL, THE PURCHASE OF PROGRAM AND EXHIBITION SUPPLIES AND MATERIALS, AND MUSEUM ADMISSION FEES. THE PROJECT WILL ADVANCE READING PROFICIENCY AND PROMOTE POSITIVE FAMILY INTERACTIONS IN RURAL COMMUNITIES. CHILDREN AND FAMILIES WILL BENEFIT BY HAVING MORE CONSISTENT ACCESS TO FUN AND EDUCATIONAL ART AND STEM ACTIVITIES. THE MUSEUM WILL TRACK PROJECT RESULTS THROUGH POST-OUTREACH PROGRAM LOGS, EVALUATION SURVEYS, ASSESSMENT MEETINGS, AND ATTENDANCE RECORDS.
description.3422: THE CENTER FOR PHOTOGRAPHY AT WOODSTOCK WILL IMPLEMENT AN EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM TO ENGAGE LOCAL HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS ENROLLED IN THE ENGLISH AS A NEW LANGUAGE PROGRAM. CENTER STAFF WILL PARTNER WITH KINGSTON HIGH SCHOOL TO ORGANIZE FIELD TRIPS AND WEEKLY IN-SCHOOL CLASSES DESIGNED TO HELP STUDENTS IMPROVE LANGUAGE SKILLS THROUGH PHOTOGRAPHY. THE PROGRAM WILL CULMINATE IN A STUDENT-PRODUCED PUBLIC ART PIECE AND A PUBLICATION. THE CENTER WILL CONTRACT WITH AN ARTIST TEAM THAT HAS FACILITATED SIMILAR COMMUNITY PROJECTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE TO BUILD STUDENTS’ SENSE OF SELF-WORTH AND FOSTER A WIDER DISCUSSION ABOUT THE NEIGHBORING LATIN AMERICAN COMMUNITY. THE CENTER RECENTLY RELOCATED TO KINGSTON, AND ENGAGEMENT WITH ITS NEW COMMUNITY WILL HELP IT BUILD CAPACITY AND ESTABLISH NEW AUDIENCES. PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE PARTICIPATING STUDENTS, THEIR FAMILIES, AND THE LOCAL COMMUNITY.
description.3423: THE FISHER MUSEUM AT HARVARD UNIVERSITY’S SCHOOL OF FORESTRY WILL CREATE A MULTIMEDIA EXHIBITION CENTERING THE VOICES OF THE NIPMUC PEOPLE WHOSE ANCESTRAL LAND IS OCCUPIED BY THE MUSEUM. THE EXHIBIT WILL ACKNOWLEDGE INDIGENOUS STEWARDSHIP LEGACIES AND ITS POTENTIAL FOR FUTURE LAND RESILIENCE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONDUCT ARCHIVAL RESEARCH AND INTERVIEW NIPMUC TRIBAL INDIVIDUALS, PRODUCE A SERIES OF SHORT FILMS, AND DESIGN AND INSTALL A DIGITAL INSTALLATION. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH A NIPMUC ARTIST AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZER TO CO-CURATE THE EXHIBIT. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE DIGITAL EQUIPMENT, PROVIDE TWO PAID INTERNSHIPS AND A GRADUATE STUDENT ASSISTANTSHIP, AND OFFER PAID HONORARIUMS FOR NIPMUC PARTICIPANTS. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH A VIDEO EDITOR AND EVALUATION SPECIALIST. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN AN INDIGENOUS-LED, TRAVELING, MULTIMEDIA EXHIBITION THAT WILL BENEFIT THE NIPMUC TRIBE AND PUBLIC, STUDENT, AND PROFESSIONAL VISITORS.
description.3424: EN FOCO IN THE BRONX, NEW YORK, WILL INVENTORY, REHOUSE, AND DIGITIZE MATERIALS CHRONICLING ITS 50-YEAR EXHIBITION HISTORY. FOUNDED AS A COLLECTIVE OF PHOTOGRAPHERS FROM THE PUERTO RICAN DIASPORA, EN FOCO’S EXHIBITION RECORDS DETAIL THE CULTURAL LEGACY OF PHOTOGRAPHERS OF COLOR. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE HIRING OF A FULL-TIME DIGITAL LIBRARIAN TO RESEARCH, ORGANIZE, DIGITIZE, AND REHOUSE THE EXHIBITION’S ARCHIVE. THE DIGITIZED COLLECTION WILL BE AVAILABLE ONSITE AT THE NUEVA LUZ STUDY CENTER AS WELL AS DIGITALLY ONLINE. ARCHIVE STAFF WILL PURCHASE A COMPUTER, DOCUMENT SCANNER, AND ARCHIVAL SUPPLIES. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN GREATER PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION AND WILL SERVE AS A CRUCIAL RESOURCE FOR THE BRONX COMMUNITY OF LATINO ARTISTS AND ARTISTS OF COLOR. PROVIDING ONLINE ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION WILL BENEFIT ARTISTS, SCHOLARS, WRITERS, CURATORS, GALLERISTS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3425: EDELMAN PLANETARIUM AT ROWAN UNIVERSITY WILL ENHANCE THE QUALITY AND ACCESS OF ITS PROGRAMS FOR FAMILIES AND PATRONS WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER AND SENSORY NEEDS. PLANETARIUM STAFF WILL COMPLETE TRAINING, CERTIFICATION, AND ON-SITE REVIEW TO BECOME A CERTIFIED AUTISM CENTER THROUGH THE INTERNATIONAL BOARD OF CREDENTIALING AND CONTINUING EDUCATION STANDARDS. WITH INPUT FROM ON-SITE REVIEWERS AND EXPERTS, THE PLANETARIUM WILL PURCHASE MATERIALS TO BUILD KITS TO ASSIST VISITORS WITH SENSORY NEEDS. SPECIALIZED STAFF TRAINING WILL ENABLE THE PLANETARIUM TO PROVIDE A MORE WELCOMING AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT AND WILL BENEFIT FAMILIES AND VISITORS WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM AND SENSORY PROCESSING DISORDERS.
description.3426: THE SAN LUIS OBISPO MUSEUM OF ART WILL HOST A BILINGUAL EXHIBITION AND RELATED PROGRAMMING HIGHLIGHTING EMERGING LATINA ARTIST DEANNA BARAHONA. THE PROJECT ALIGNS WITH A KEY GOAL NOTED IN THE MUSEUM’S RECENT MUSEUM ASSESSMENT PROGRAM (MAP) REPORT TO DIVERSIFY ITS EXHIBITIONS AND PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERREPRESENTED ARTISTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EXHIBITION INSTALLATION, DEVELOPING A SERIES OF ADULT AND FAMILY-FRIENDLY WORKSHOPS AND PROGRAMS, AND ORGANIZING SCHOOL GROUP TOURS.  THE MUSEUM WILL BUILD UPON ITS PARTNERSHIP WITH CALIFORNIA POLYTECHNIC STATE UNIVERSITY’S LATINX/E CENTER FOR ACADEMIC SUCCESS AND ACHIEVEMENT AND THE LATINO OUTREACH COUNCIL TO CREATE JOINT PROGRAMMING. THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND THE MUSEUM’S PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT AND OFFER VISITORS NEW PERSPECTIVES ON THE LATINO EXPERIENCE IN AMERICA.
description.3427: THE PACIFIC GROVE MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY WILL DEVELOP AN INTERPRETIVE MASTER PLAN ALIGNED WITH ITS STRATEGIC PLAN AND NEW MISSION TO STRENGTHEN ITS EMPHASIS ON CULTURAL HISTORY AND COMMUNITY BUILDING. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL IDENTIFY INTERPRETIVE THEMES, DEFINE ITS AUDIENCES AND PARTNERS, AND STRATEGIZE ITS REACH AND MODE OF ENGAGEMENT WITH LOCAL COMMUNITIES. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH COMMUNITY LEADERS, A GRAPHIC ARTIST, AND A CONSULTANT TO HELP FACILITATE AND DEVELOP THE INTERPRETIVE MASTER PLAN. COMPLETION OF THE INTERPRETIVE PLAN WILL RESULT IN INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL CAPACITY BUILDING AND WILL SERVE AS A COMMUNICATION AND PLANNING TOOL FOR THE ENTIRE INSTITUTION. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE STAFF, VISITORS, AND THE RESIDENTS OF MONTEREY COUNTY, PARTICULARLY THOSE PREVIOUSLY UNDERSERVED BY THE MUSEUM, INCLUDING LOCAL INDIGENOUS GROUPS, CHINESE AMERICANS, AND THE LATINO COMMUNITY.
description.3428: THE NEWPORT HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL USE FUNDS TO HIRE A FULL-TIME RESEARCH ASSISTANT TO CONTINUE WORK ON ITS DATABASE OF RECORDS REPRESENTING BLACK AND INDIGENOUS INDIVIDUALS. SINCE THIS WORK FIRST BEGAN IN 2021, THE SOCIETY HAS IDENTIFIED AND RECORDED MORE THAN 1,700 NAMES OF PEOPLE OF AFRICAN AND INDIGENOUS DESCENT FROM THE ARCHIVES. THE RESEARCH ASSISTANT WILL CONTINUE THE REVIEW OF THE COLLECTION, DIGITIZE RECORDS, CREATE BIOGRAPHIES OF AFRICAN, AFRICAN AMERICAN, AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLE WHO LIVED AND WORKED IN NEWPORT DURING THE ERA OF SLAVERY, AND MAKE THESE RESOURCES AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC THROUGH THE SOCIETY’S ONLINE DATABASE, ALLOWING RESEARCHERS AND THE PUBLIC TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE CITY’S ROLE IN THE TRANSATLANTIC SLAVE TRADE AND SERVE AS A TOOL FOR DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES TO RESEARCH THEIR ANCESTORS.
description.3429: GREAT EXPLORATIONS CHILDREN’S MUSEUM WILL DESIGN AND FABRICATE NEW EXHIBIT SPACE TO ENHANCE THE WELL-BEING AND IMPACT OF ITS LIVING COLLECTION. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE SUPPLIES AND MATERIALS TO CREATE NEW ENCLOSURES FOR ITS LIVING COLLECTION THAT INCLUDE SPECIES-SPECIFIC ENVIRONMENTS THAT ENCOURAGE ANIMAL BEHAVIOR COMMONLY SEEN IN THE WILD. THE NEWLY DESIGNED SPACE WILL INCLUDE AN ANIMAL ENRICHMENT WALL, A WATER-FILTRATION SYSTEM, A HYDROPONIC GARDEN, AND FOOD STORAGE AND PREPARATION AREAS. THE MULTIPURPOSE SPACE WILL ENABLE STAFF TO CONDUCT DAILY DEMONSTRATIONS AND HANDS-ON ANIMAL ENCOUNTERS AND PROMOTE STREAM-BASED LEARNING THROUGH ANIMAL AND NATURE-THEMED PROGRAMMING. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN OVERALL IMPROVED CARE AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR THE MUSEUM’S LIVING COLLECTION. THE NEW EXHIBIT SPACE WILL ENRICH THE OVERALL EXPERIENCE OF MUSEUM VISITORS, PRIMARILY FAMILIES WITH YOUNG CHILDREN, AND ENCOURAGE INTERACTIVE, HANDS-ON LEARNING TO FOSTER GREATER KNOWLEDGE OF THE NATURAL WORLD.
description.3430: THE DC HISTORY CENTER WILL DEVELOP AND INSTALL A SEMI-PERMANENT EXHIBITION EXPLORING THE HISTORY OF BLACK EDUCATION IN WASHINGTON, DC. THE EXHIBITION WILL EXPLORE THEMES THAT ARE RELEVANT TODAY: WHO HAS ACCESS TO EDUCATION AND HOW; THE ROLE OF ACTIVISM IN CREATING CHANGE; AND THE BLACK COMMUNITIES’ AGENCY IN RESISTING RACIST SYSTEMS AND STRUCTURES. THE CENTER WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE ANACOSTIA COMMUNITY MUSEUM AND THE CHARLES SUMNER SCHOOL MUSEUM AND ARCHIVES ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE EXHIBIT. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE PURCHASE OF EXHIBITION EQUIPMENT AND MATERIALS, AND THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EVALUATION CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT A POST-OPENING ANALYSIS. THE GOAL OF THE EXHIBITION IS TO ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE OF BLACK EDUCATIONAL HISTORY IN THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA AND ITS LEGACY. TELLING THIS LOCALLY AND NATIONALLY IMPORTANT STORY WILL BENEFIT FAMILIES, TEACHERS, STUDENTS, AND VISITORS TO THE NATION’S CAPITAL.
description.3431: THE ARLINGTON HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL BUILD UPON A PREVIOUS IMLS PROJECT TO INVENTORY, DIGITIZE, AND REHOUSE OVER 16,000 OBJECTS THAT ARE CURRENTLY AT THE MOST AT RISK FOR POTENTIAL COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT ISSUES. THIS SUBSET OF THE MUSEUM'S COLLECTION INCLUDES ARCHIVAL MATERIALS, PHOTOGRAPHS, BOOKS, CERAMICS GLASS, AND TEXTILES. PLANNED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE THE INSTALLATION OF HIGH-DENSITY ROLLING STORAGE UNITS, DIGITIZING ITEMS, UPDATING CATALOG RECORDS, AND REHOUSING COLLECTIONS. DIGITIZED ITEMS AND THEIR ASSOCIATED METADATA WILL BE ADDED TO THE MUSEUM'S COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM AND UPLOADED TO AN ONLINE PLATFORM PERMITTING INCREASED ACCESS FOR EDUCATORS, RESEARCHERS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3432: THE BURWELL SCHOOL HISTORIC SITE IN HILLSBOROUGH, NORTH CAROLINA, WILL PRODUCE A SERIES OF BIOGRAPHICAL COMIC BOOKS AND CORRESPONDING LESSON PLANS TO ENGAGE FOURTH- AND FIFTH-GRADE STUDENTS WITH UNITED STATES HISTORY. EACH BOOK WILL SPOTLIGHT A LOCAL FIGURE FROM THE 1800S WHO ACHIEVED PROMINENCE DESPITE FACING ADVERSITY. BURWELL SCHOOL STAFF WILL COLLABORATE WITH LOCAL CHILDREN’S AUTHORS AND ARTISTS TO WRITE AND ILLUSTRATE FOUR BOOKS. AN EDUCATIONAL CONSULTANT WILL BE CONTRACTED TO DEVELOP LESSON PLANS THAT ALIGN WITH FOURTH AND FIFTH-GRADE HISTORY CURRICULUM. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN FREE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES, AVAILABLE IN BOTH PRINT AND DIGITAL FORMATS, BENEFITING TEACHERS AND STUDENTS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS INITIATIVE WILL BROADEN COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF LOCAL HISTORY, FOSTERING A DEEPER CONNECTION TO THE REGION'S PAST.
description.3433: THE NATIONAL HISPANIC CULTURAL CENTER WILL PURSUE INTERNAL CAPACITY BUILDING TO STRENGTHEN ITS IMPACT WITHIN THE ORGANIZATION AND THE LARGER COMMUNITY. THE CENTER WILL INVEST IN PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TO ENHANCE AND UPDATE PROFESSIONAL MUSEUM PRACTICES, BUILD STAFF KNOWLEDGE AND CONFIDENCE THROUGH TRAINING AND CONFERENCES, AND DEVELOP SUSTAINABLE WORK MODELS TO MEET STAFF NEEDS. IN ADDITION, IT WILL IMPLEMENT PROGRAM EVALUATION FOCUSED ON VISITOR EXPERIENCE, BELONGING, AND CULTURAL CONNECTEDNESS. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT STAFF TRAVEL TO ATTEND CONFERENCES, HOSTING OF COMMUNITY LISTENING SESSIONS, AND CONTRACTING WITH CONSULTANTS TO FACILITATE SPECIALIZED TRAINING. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN INSTITUTIONAL COHESION, EMPOWER STAFF, AND ADVANCE CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE, VISITOR-INFORMED PROGRAMS AND EXHIBITIONS, BENEFITING BOTH STAFF AND VISITORS.
description.3434: THE MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN-STEVENS POINT WILL IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY TO ITS EXHIBITS WITH NEW DISPLAYS HIGHLIGHTING ITS ROCK, MINERAL, AND FOSSIL COLLECTIONS. THE MUSEUM WILL PURCHASE NEW EXHIBIT CASES, DIGITAL DISPLAY EQUIPMENT, AND A HANDS-ON ACTIVITY CART FOR INSTALLATION IN ITS NEWLY RENOVATED SPACE IN THE SCIENCE BUILDING. STAFF WILL HIRE TWO PAID INTERNS FOR THE TWO-YEAR DURATION OF THE PROJECT. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN GREATER ACCESS TO A WIDER RANGE OF VISITORS, INCLUDING AUDIENCES WHO HAVE BEEN UNDERREPRESENTED IN PREVIOUS MUSEUM DESIGN AND PROGRAMMING. IT WILL ALSO PROVIDE STUDENT INTERNS WITH HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE WORKING WITH COLLECTIONS AND CREATING INTERPRETIVE MEDIA. THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTIONS ARE USED IN OVER 20 CLASSES AND BY MORE THAN 1,350 STUDENTS EACH YEAR AND MORE ENGAGING AND ACCESSIBLE DISPLAYS WILL BENEFIT FACULTY, RESEARCHERS, STUDENTS, AND MUSEUM VISITORS.
description.3435: HANFORD MILLS MUSEUM AT EAST MEREDITH WILL DRAFT AND IMPLEMENT AN UPDATED INTERPRETIVE MASTER PLAN TO HEIGHTEN CONNECTIONS BETWEEN THE SITE’S HISTORY AND LARGER GLOBAL SYSTEMS AND CONDITIONS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL CONTRACT WITH A CONSULTANT TO ASSIST IN WRITING THE PLAN, BUILDING UPON ITS RECENT INTERPRETIVE AUDIT AND DRAFT FRAMEWORK. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DRAFT INTERPRETATION AND EVALUATION PROCESSES AND PROTOCOLS AND PROVIDE INTERPRETIVE WORKSHOPS FOR STAFF, OTHER SMALL MUSEUMS, AND STUDENTS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A MASTER PLAN TO GUIDE AND EXPAND INTERPRETATION, INCLUDING AN UPDATED ORIENTATION SCRIPT AND MILL TOUR. THE PLANNING PROCESS, RESULTING DOCUMENTS, AND WORKSHOPS WILL INCREASE INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL CAPACITY AND STAFF KNOWLEDGE. PROJECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE MUSEUM STAFF AND BOARD MEMBERS, STAFF FROM SURROUNDING SMALL MUSEUMS, NEARBY MUSEUM STUDIES PROGRAMS, AND ULTIMATELY VISITORS TO THE SITE.
description.3436: THE ONEIDA COMMUNITY MANSION HOUSE (OCMH) WILL INVENTORY AND CATALOG APPROXIMATELY 850 OBJECTS IN ITS CARE TO PRESERVE AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTION AND ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE OF THE ONEIDA COMMUNITY AND ITS RELEVANCE IN UNITED STATES HISTORY. OCMH STAFF WILL HIRE A PART-TIME COLLECTIONS MANAGER TO INVENTORY AND PHOTOGRAPH OBJECTS, CREATE AND UPDATE DIGITAL CATALOG RECORDS, AND IMPLEMENT A COLLECTION STORAGE PLAN AND LOCATION SYSTEM FOR TWO COLLECTIONS STORAGE AREAS. COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN INCREASED INTELLECTUAL AND PHYSICAL CONTROL OVER THE COLLECTION. IMPROVING PRESERVATION AND ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION WILL BENEFIT VISITORS, STUDENTS, RESEARCHERS, HISTORIANS, AND ONEIDA COMMUNITY DESCENDANTS.
description.3437: THE HARTFORD ART SCHOOL GALLERIES LOCATED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF HARTFORD WILL CONDUCT A FULL INVENTORY OF THE APPROXIMATELY 2,100 ART OBJECTS IN ITS COLLECTION TO IMPROVE STEWARDSHIP AND ACCESSIBILITY. INFORMED BY A MUSEUM ASSESSMENT PROGRAM (MAP) REPORT, THE GALLERIES WILL CONTRACT WITH A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT EXPERT TO CONDUCT A FULL INVENTORY OF TWO STORAGE SPACES, UPDATE PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL COLLECTION RECORDS, AND PHOTOGRAPH AND LABEL OBJECTS. THE UNIVERSITY WILL ALSO OFFER A PAID INTERNSHIP FOR THE YEARLONG PROJECT. THE RESULTS OF THIS AWARD WILL BE IMPROVED INTELLECTUAL CONTROL AND ONLINE ACCESSIBILITY OF THE COLLECTION, BENEFITING STUDENTS, FACULTY, STAFF, AND VISITORS.
description.3438: THE LAC COURTE OREILLES TRIBAL MUSEUM AND VISITOR CENTER WILL UNDERTAKE A CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT TO STRENGTHEN OPERATIONS AND ENHANCE SUSTAINABILITY. THE MUSEUM SERVES AS A COMMUNITY ARCHIVE AND PRESERVES THE HISTORY, CULTURE, TRADITIONS, AND VALUES OF THE LAC COURTE OREILLES ANISHINAABE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE REVIEWING AND UPDATING COLLECTIONS AND FACILITY POLICIES AND PROCEDURES AND DEVELOPING A PUBLIC RELATIONS PLAN, CAPITAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN, AND 5-YEAR STRATEGIC PLAN. MUSEUM STAFF AND ADVISORY BOARD MEMBERS WILL ATTEND ONLINE TRAINING COURSES AND ENGAGE WITH A CONSULTANT TO FACILITATE STRATEGIC PLANNING. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN MUSEUM-TRAINED STAFF, INCREASED USE OF MUSEUM RESOURCES, AND A BROADER BASE OF SUPPORT TO SUSTAIN FUTURE GROWTH. THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS, MUSEUM VISITORS, AND RESEARCHERS.
description.3439: THE DELAWARE CONTEMPORARY WILL CONTINUE ITS SUCCESSFUL AFTERSCHOOL TEEN ARTS PROGRAM THROUGH A SERIES OF LEARNING EXPERIENCES TO FOSTER EXPLORATION OF MUSEUM AND CREATIVE INDUSTRY CAREERS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL PARTNER WITH TITLE 1 HIGH SCHOOLS IN NEW CASTLE COUNTY TO RECRUIT STUDENTS WHO HAVE LIMITED ACCESS TO ARTS OPPORTUNITIES. THROUGH CROSS-DISCIPLINARY LEARNING METHODS AND ENGAGEMENT WITH THE MUSEUM’S TEACHING ARTISTS AND A DIVERSE GROUP OF CREATIVES-IN-RESIDENCE, STUDENTS WILL CREATE THEIR OWN WORKS USING A VARIETY OF ART MEDIA, VISIT CREATIVE INDUSTRY WORKSPACES AND CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS, AND PARTICIPATE IN CIVIC ENGAGEMENT PROJECTS. THE PROGRAM WILL CULMINATE IN AN EXHIBITION AND POP-UP RETAIL OPERATION TO SHOWCASE STUDENTS’ ARTWORK. THESE OPPORTUNITIES WILL HELP STUDENTS DEVELOP PROFESSIONAL SKILLS, PROMOTE JOB PREPAREDNESS, BROADEN CAREER HORIZONS, AND OVERCOME BARRIERS TO SUCCESS. PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL BE TRACKED THROUGH INFORMAL OBSERVATION, PROGRAM SURVEYS, AND COLLABORATION WITH EDUCATORS.
description.3440: SIGAL MUSIC MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH GREENVILLE COUNTY SCHOOLS TO PROVIDE LOCAL MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL MUSIC DEPARTMENTS WITH DIGITAL VERSIONS OF 12 HISTORIC KEYBOARD INSTRUMENTS IN ITS COLLECTION, INCLUDING A 1761 HARPSICHORD PLAYED BY A YOUNG MOZART. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH AN AUDIO ENGINEER TO CREATE A SOFTWARE PLUG-IN THAT DIGITALLY REPLICATES THE INSTRUMENTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF DIGITAL KEYBOARDS, COMPUTER EQUIPMENT, AND SOFTWARE FOR 10 PARTICIPATING SCHOOLS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PROVIDE TUTORIALS, TRAINING, AND LESSON PLANS FOR ASSOCIATED PROGRAMMING. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT STUDENTS, EDUCATORS, MUSICIANS, AND SCHOLARS BY EXPANDING THE STUDY OF THESE INSTRUMENTS TO PLAYABLE EXPERIENCES.
description.3441: THE PORT TOWNSEND MARINE SCIENCE CENTER WILL PROTOTYPE AND EVALUATE POP-UP EXHIBITIONS TO INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF PERMANENT EXHIBITS PLANNED FOR ITS NEW DOWNTOWN LOCATION. BUILDING UPON A PREVIOUS IMLS PROJECT TO DEVELOP AN EXHIBITION MASTER PLAN, THIS SECOND PHASE WILL TEST AND REFINE THE PLAN TO ENSURE IT MEETS COMMUNITY NEEDS AND RESONATES WITH VISITORS. THE CENTER WILL CONVENE STAKEHOLDER GROUPS TO REVIEW THEMES AND WILL DEVELOP AND INSTALL THREE TEMPORARY POP-UP EXHIBITS FOR TESTING AND EVALUATION. STAFF WILL PURCHASE EXHIBIT SUPPLIES AND MATERIALS, AND CONTRACT WITH AN EXHIBIT DESIGNER AND EXTERNAL EVALUATOR. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN DEEPER COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND EXPANDED ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY. EVALUATION OF PROTOTYPE EXHIBITS WILL ENSURE PERMANENT EXHIBITS ARE ENGAGING AND ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE AND STEWARDSHIP OF THE VITAL MARINE ECOSYSTEMS OF THE SALISH SEA, BENEFITING THE COMMUNITY AND MUSEUM VISITORS.
description.3442: EAST CENTRAL UNIVERSITY?S LINSCHEID LIBRARY?IN PARTNERSHIP WITH OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES, REDLANDS COMMUNITY COLLEGE, AND THE OKLAHOMA COUNCIL OF ONLINE LEARNING EXCELLENCE? PROPOSES A THREE-YEAR PROJECT TO CREATE AND DISSEMINATE A RESEARCH METHODOLOGY FOR EVALUATING THE EFFICACY OF OPEN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES (OER) IN INCREASING LIFELONG LEARNING COMPETENCIES. THE GOALS OF THE PROJECT ARE TO DEVELOP A RESEARCH TOOLKIT FOR STUDYING THE EFFICACY OF OER ON INCREASING LIFELONG LEARNING COMPETENCIES AND TO DEVELOP AN OER FOR LIBRARIANS ON HOW TO CREATE ROBUST RESEARCH METHODOLOGIES FOR STUDYING TEACHING AND LEARNING. THE PROJECT WAS CREATED TO ADDRESS THE LACK OF ROBUST RESEARCH METHODOLOGY IN OER EFFICACY STUDIES AND THE LACK OF LIBRARIAN KNOWLEDGE IN CONDUCTING RESEARCH.
description.3443: FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY WILL PARTNER WITH THE STATE LIBRARY OF FLORIDA, THE PANHANDLE LIBRARY AREA NETWORK (PLAN), CHIEF OFFICERS OF STATE LIBRARY AGENCIES, PUBLIC LIBRARY ASSOCIATION, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT OFFICERS, AND NATIONAL DISASTER EXPERTS TO EXPLORE EXISTING LIBRARY DISASTER PREPAREDNESS, RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY AND CONTINUITY OF OPERATIONS PLANS AND DISTILL EVIDENCE-BASED PROCESSES, RECOMMENDATIONS, AND MODELS FOR SMALL AND RURAL PUBLIC LIBRARIES THROUGHOUT FLORIDA AND THE NATION. THE MAIN GOAL IS TO DEVELOP COMMUNITY-CENTERED, MULTI-DISCIPLINARY, SMART, AND CONNECTED DISASTER MODELS INFORMED BY LIBRARIANS AND GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM ANALYSES TO STRENGTHEN SMALL AND RURAL LIBRARIES? CAPACITY TO PREPARE LIBRARY PERSONNEL TO MEET LOCAL NEEDS AND SAFEGUARD LIBRARY RESOURCES. THE RESEARCH GRANT WILL BUILD OFF OF IMLS-FUNDED RESEARCH FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS AND INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF LIBRARIES NATIONWIDE TO SUPPORT COMMUNITIES DEALING WITH NATURAL DISASTERS, COVID-19 OR OTHER WIDESPREAD HEALTH ISSUES, AND OTHER TYPES OF COMMUNITY EMERGENCIES.
