THE PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE MUSEUM’S EFFORTS TO SHARE VAN DER ZEE’S ARCHIVE—MUCH OF WHICH HAS NEVER BEEN SEEN PUBLICLY—ONLINE VIA THE MUSEUM’S WEBSITE, WHICH REACHES MORE THAN 37.8 MILLION USERS AROUND THE WORLD ANNUALLY. THE AVAILABILITY OF THIS WORK WILL OFFER SCHOLARS AND THE PUBLIC A MORE COMPREHENSIVE ACCOUNT OF THE HISTORY OF AMERICAN PHOTOGRAPHY WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY CELEBRATING BLACK AMERICAN CULTURE FROM THE FIRST DECADE OF THE 20TH CENTURY TO THE EARLY 1980S.
description.3611: MYSTIC SEAPORT MUSEUM WILL STABILIZE AND IMPROVE THE CONDITION OF FILM NEGATIVES FROM ITS COLLECTION THAT HAVE BEEN AFFECTED BY A FORM OF SEVERE DETERIORATION KNOWN AS VINEGAR SYNDROME. MUSEUM STAFF WILL EVALUATE, SELECT, TREAT, DIGITIZE, REHOUSE, AND CATALOG THOUSANDS OF IMAGES FROM THE COLLECTION. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE AND TRAIN AN ADDITIONAL CONSERVATION TECHNICIAN TO ASSIST IN CATALOGING AND RECOVERY OF THE OBJECTS IN COMPLIANCE WITH PROFESSIONAL CONSERVATION STANDARDS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL CREATE A SUSTAINABLE MODEL FOR THE ONGOING IN-HOUSE TREATMENT OF NEGATIVES AFFECTED BY VINEGAR SYNDROME AND WILL SHARE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT ONLINE AND THROUGH PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCES.
description.3612: THE YERBA BUENA CENTER FOR THE ARTS (YBCA) WILL LAUNCH ITS YBCA CO-OP MEMBERSHIP PROGRAM, A RECENTLY PILOTED MEMBERSHIP FRAMEWORK THAT CENTERS ARTISTS AND COMMUNITIES AS INTRINSIC TO AUDIENCE BUILDING, ONGOING ENGAGEMENT, AND ONSITE PROGRAMMING. THE MUSEUM WILL CONVENE REGULARLY WITH FOCUS GROUPS TO COLLECT FEEDBACK TO STRENGTHEN THE PROGRAM BY ENSURING IT DIRECTLY SERVES THE NEEDS OF ARTISTS, AS WELL AS EXPAND OUTREACH TO A GREATER NUMBER OF ARTISTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS FROM ACROSS THE BAY AREA. PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL HAVE ACCESS TO ONGOING USE OF THE MUSEUM’S REHEARSAL, STUDIO, AND MEETING SPACES, GENERATING INCREASED COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT THROUGH ART PROTOTYPING FESTIVALS, CONVENINGS, EXHIBITIONS, PERFORMANCES, LECTURES, AND SCREENINGS. BY CO-CREATING THIS PROGRAM WITH AND FOR ARTISTS AND COMMUNITIES, THE MUSEUM HOPES TO REACH THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN HISTORICALLY MARGINALIZED FROM OR UNABLE TO PARTICIPATE IN TRADITIONAL MUSEUM MEMBERSHIP PROGRAMS.
description.3613: THE JAPANESE AMERICAN NATIONAL MUSEUM WILL CATALOG AND CONSERVE ITEMS FROM ITS COLLECTION OF ART AND ASSOCIATED EPHEMERA OF JAPANESE AMERICAN ARTIST HENRY SUGIMOTO. THE MUSEUM WILL CONTRACT WITH PROFESSIONAL CONSERVATORS TO CONDUCT CONDITION ASSESSMENTS OF PAINTINGS, WOODBLOCK PRINTS, DOCUMENTS, AND OTHER MATERIALS AND TO PERFORM CONSERVATION WORK ON THOSE ITEMS IN NEED OF IMMEDIATE ATTENTION. THE MUSEUM WILL PURCHASE ARCHIVAL STORAGE BOXES, AND CONSERVATION TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT TO SUPPORT THIS WORK. MUSEUM STAFF WILL INVENTORY, CATALOG, AND REHOUSE ITEMS IN THE COLLECTION AND WORK WITH A CONTRACTED PHOTOGRAPHER TO DIGITIZE UP TO 600 ARTIFACTS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THE COMPLETE INVENTORY AND CATALOGING OF THE COLLECTION, WHICH WILL BE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC THROUGH THE MUSEUM’S ONLINE COLLECTIONS DATABASE.
description.3614: THE PORTLAND ART MUSEUM WILL PRODUCE THE EXHIBITION BLACK ARTISTS OF OREGON, WHICH WILL HIGHLIGHT AND CELEBRATE THE WORK OF BLACK ARTISTS, INCLUDING WORKS IN THE MUSEUM’S PERMANENT COLLECTION THAT HAVE BEEN HISTORICALLY UNDER-EXHIBITED AND UNDER-RESEARCHED. THE MUSEUM WILL ENGAGE A GUEST CURATOR AND THE EXHIBITION WILL BUILD UPON BOTH HER LIVED EXPERIENCE AND HER RESEARCH EXPLORING THE LINEAGE AND LEGACY OF BLACK ARTISTS IN OREGON AND THE IMPACT, HISTORY, AND PRESENCE OF BLACK ARTISTS AND ARTS COLLECTIVES IN THE REGION. A CATALOG WILL ACCOMPANY THE INSTALLATION, AND A SERIES OF PUBLIC PROGRAMS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS WILL HIGHLIGHT THE FEATURED ARTISTS’ CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE REGION AND THE NATION. PROGRAMS WILL INCLUDE DOCUMENTING AND DISTRIBUTING ORAL HISTORIES THROUGH VIDEOS AND PODCASTS, ARTIST STUDIO VISITS, AND INTERGENERATIONAL ARTIST CONVERSATIONS.
description.3615: THE ARMORY CENTER FOR THE ARTS WILL IMPLEMENT THE SOWING SEEDS INITIATIVE, A THREE-YEAR SERIES OF COMMUNITY-DRIVEN, MULTI-GENERATIONAL ARTS EDUCATION PROGRAMS. THE INITIATIVE WILL INCLUDE BOTH IN-SCHOOL AND OUT-OF-SCHOOL PROGRAMS CENTERING ON THE WAYS SEEDS ARE USED AND SHARED BY DIVERSE COMMUNITIES IN THE PAST, PRESENT, AND FUTURE. WITH THE HIRE OF A FULL-TIME ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE, THE MUSEUM WILL ENGAGE WITH COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND THE PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT TO PLAN AND PRODUCE THE PROGRAMS FOR ADULTS, FAMILIES, AND YOUNG PEOPLE IN A VARIETY OF DIFFERENT LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH A TONGVA CULTURAL ADVISOR TO ENSURE INCLUSION OF FIRST WORLD VOICES IN THE CURRICULUM. PARTICIPANTS THROUGHOUT THE GREATER SAN GABRIEL VALLEY WILL CONNECT WITH THE LAND AND THE TONGVA COMMUNITY, LEARN ABOUT THE FLORA AND FAUNA, AND BUILD NEW SKILLS TO PROTECT NATURE AND THE ENVIRONMENT.
description.3616: THE TAUBMAN MUSEUM OF ART WILL DEVELOP THE “HAPPY HEARTS” THERAPEUTIC ART PROGRAM TO SUPPORT INDIVIDUALS WITH INTELLECTUAL, PHYSICAL, AND EMOTIONAL DISABILITIES IN SOUTHWEST VIRGINIA. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH 17 SOCIAL SERVICES ORGANIZATIONS REPRESENTING A RANGE OF INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES AND A PROFESSIONAL ART THERAPIST TO IDENTIFY PARTICIPANT NEEDS AND DEVELOP PROGRAMS. GRADUATE STUDENT INTERNS FROM RADFORD UNIVERSITY’S OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY PROGRAM WILL ASSIST IN DEVELOPING CURRICULA AND LEADING THERAPEUTIC ART SESSIONS. THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH AN EXTERNAL EVALUATOR THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT TO MEASURE PROGRAM EFFICACY AND SUPPORT ITS LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY. PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL LEARN NEW SKILLS TO ENHANCE SELF-ESTEEM; DEVELOP TECHNICAL ABILITIES TO ENABLE VISUAL SELF-EXPRESSION; ENHANCE CREATIVE CAPABILITIES TO SUPPORT SELF-ACTUALIZATION; AND BUILD RELATIONSHIPS WITH OTHERS THROUGH SOCIAL INTERACTION.
description.3617: THE DENVER MUSEUM OF NATURE AND SCIENCE WILL CONDUCT A THREE-YEAR PROJECT TO ADVANCE COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP FOR LOGISTICALLY CHALLENGING LARGE BONES OF DINOSAURS IN THE MORRISON FORMATION FOSSIL COLLECTION. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO THESE SCIENTIFICALLY SIGNIFICANT SPECIMENS—INCLUDING HOLOTYPE SPECIMENS—FOR SCHOLARS AND THE PUBLIC. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE REPAIRING, PREPARING, REHOUSING, ARCHIVAL CRADLING, AND 3D SCANNING THE SPECIMENS. IT ALSO WILL SUPPORT PURCHASING 3D SCANNING EQUIPMENT FOR LARGE SPECIMENS. THE PROJECT WILL OFFER NUMEROUS OPPORTUNITIES FOR EARLY-CAREER PALEONTOLOGISTS THROUGH A TERM PREPARATOR POSITION AND THREE PAID INTERNSHIPS THAT WILL MAKE SIGNIFICANT SPECIMENS AVAILABLE FOR STUDY FOR THE FIRST TIME. THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED CARE OF THIS COLLECTION, ENHANCED COLLECTIONS ACCESS, AND A WIDER DISSEMINATION OF THE COLLECTION AND ITS SIGNIFICANCE FOR MUSEUM VISITORS, THE GENERAL PUBLIC, RESEARCHERS, AND COMMUNITIES WHERE THE FOSSILS ORIGINATED.
description.3618: THE BRONX MUSEUM OF THE ARTS WILL ENHANCE A SERIES OF COMMUNITY PROGRAMS DESIGNED TO PROMOTE EQUITY AND SOCIAL JUSTICE THROUGH THE ARTS. ACTIVITIES WILL FOCUS ON ENHANCING ACCESS THROUGH PUBLIC PROGRAMS, NURTURING LOCAL ARTISTS THROUGH COMMISSIONS AND RESIDENCIES, AND DEEPENING COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND PARTNERSHIPS. GUIDED BY A REVITALIZED COMMUNITY ADVISORY COUNCIL, THE MUSEUM WILL IMPROVE EXISTING PROGRAMS, INCLUDING CULTURAL EVENTS, STORYTELLING PROGRAMS, SENIOR PROGRAMS, AND VIRTUAL PLATFORMS WITH DIGITALLY ACCESSIBLE LEARNING MATERIALS. THE MUSEUM WILL PROVIDE FREE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SEMINARS FOR EMERGING ARTISTS, AS WELL AS OFFERING A RESIDENCY PROGRAM FOR ARTISTS TO ENGAGE WITH ISSUES EXPRESSED BY LOCAL BIPOC (BLACK, INDIGENOUS, AND PEOPLE OF COLOR) COMMUNITIES THROUGH OPEN STUDIO DAYS, TALKS, AND WORKSHOPS. ADDITIONAL PROJECT RESULTS WILL INCLUDE IMPROVED MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENTS AND EVALUATION REPORTS AND PHOTO AND VIDEO PROGRAM DOCUMENTATION SHARED THROUGH SOCIAL MEDIA AND THE MUSEUM’S WEBSITE.
description.3619: THE NEW-YORK HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL WORK WITH A SCHOLAR IN NATIVE AMERICAN STUDIES TO ASSESS ITS COLLECTIONS THAT PERTAIN TO INDIGENOUS HISTORY FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF NATIVE AMERICAN AND U.S. HISTORY. THE CONSULTING SCHOLAR WILL WORK WITH MUSEUM AND LIBRARY STAFF TO UPDATE COLLECTION DESCRIPTIONS, CREATE NAVIGATION TOOLS, AND TRAIN STAFF TO INTEGRATE INDIGENOUS HISTORIES, MATERIALS, AND PERSPECTIVES INTO THEIR WORK WITH COLLECTIONS AND RELATED PROGRAMMING. TWO ADDITIONAL CONSULTING SCHOLARS WILL ALSO AID STAFF IN GENERATING CARE PROTOCOLS FOR SENSITIVE ITEMS AND DEVELOPING STAFF GUIDANCE MATERIALS, INCLUDING IDENTIFYING INSTANCES WHERE OTHER SCHOLARS AND TRIBAL REPRESENTATIVES SHOULD BE CONTACTED FOR FURTHER CONSULTATION. THE PROJECT WILL MAKE A COLLECTIONS GUIDE AND DIGITIZED IMAGES AND INFORMATION ABOUT THE COLLECTION AVAILABLE ONLINE, BRINGING TO LIGHT AND MAKING ACCESSIBLE MATERIAL THAT HAS BEEN LARGELY IGNORED, MISUNDERSTOOD, AND INVISIBLE.
description.3620: THE GEORGE EASTMAN MUSEUM WILL SEEK TO EXPAND ITS OUTREACH TO NEW AUDIENCES BY CREATING TWO NEW EXHIBITIONS ABOUT THE HISTORY OF PHOTOGRAPHER GEORGE EASTMAN AND PHOTOGRAPHIC TECHNOLOGY. INFORMED BY COMMUNITY SURVEYS AND FOCUS GROUPS, THE REINTERPRETATION OF GEORGE EASTMAN WILL ENGAGE VISITORS WITH THEMES AROUND SINGLE-PARENT FAMILIES; CONDITIONS FOR THE WORKING POOR OF HIS TIME; HIS SUPPORT FOR STEM EDUCATION; AND HIS DONATIONS TO BLACK COLLEGES CONTRASTED WITH THE CHALLENGES OF ORGANIZATIONAL DISCRIMINATION. THE STEM-FOCUSED EXHIBITION TRACING THE EVOLUTION OF PHOTOGRAPHIC TECHNOLOGY WILL INTEGRATE HISTORIC OBJECTS FROM THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION. MUSEUM STAFF WILL PRODUCE AN AUDIO TOUR AND WORK WITH A TECHNOLOGY CONSULTANT TO DEVELOP INTERACTIVE DIGITAL ACTIVITIES THAT UTILIZE MOBILE APPLICATIONS. A WEBSITE WILL ACCOMPANY THE EXHIBITION, INCLUDING A VIRTUAL TOUR, EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES, AND VIDEO CONTENT GEARED TOWARD AUDIENCES OF ONLINE VISITORS, STUDENTS, TEACHERS, DOCENTS, AND RESEARCHERS.
description.3621: GOGGLEWORKS CENTER FOR THE ARTS WILL IMPLEMENT THE “COMO CRECEMOS (HOW WE GROW)” PROJECT, EXPANDING ON ITS SUCCESS SERVING HISPANIC AND LATINX AUDIENCES BY DESIGNING EQUITABLE, INCLUSIVE EXHIBITIONS, PROGRAMS, AND COMMUNICATIONS. THE MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH THREE COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS—BARRIO ALEGRÍA, CENTRO HISPANO, AND THE READING ARTIST COLLECTIVE—WHO ARE COMMITTED TO SUPPORTING THE LATINX POPULATION AND ADVANCING DIVERSITY IN THE LOCAL ARTS COMMUNITY. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CREATING TWO MAJOR EXHIBITIONS FEATURING THE WORKS OF CONVENTIONALLY MARGINALIZED ARTISTS AND A COMMUNICATIONS PROGRAM DESIGNED TO ENGAGE NEW AUDIENCES FROM HISPANIC AND LATINX BACKGROUNDS BY PRIORITIZING LISTENING, STORYTELLING, GRASSROOTS OUTREACH, AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY. THE MUSEUM WILL ALSO HIRE A MANAGER OF INCLUSIVE PROGRAMS TO IMPLEMENT PROGRAMS SUCH AS OUTDOOR ARTS ACTIVITIES, EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS, AND A PUBLIC FASHION SHOW. THE PROJECT WILL FOSTER CROSS-CULTURAL COLLABORATION, AMPLIFY MARGINALIZED VOICES, AND EXPAND LATINX ARTS ACCESS AND REACH.
description.3622: PERALTA HACIENDA HISTORICAL PARK WILL DESIGN, FABRICATE, AND INSTALL NEW INTERPRETIVE EXHIBITS ABOUT THE OHLONE, THE ORIGINAL PEOPLE IN THE HUCHIUN AREA WHERE THE PARK STANDS TODAY. EXHIBITS WILL WEAVE TOGETHER THE HISTORY OF THE LANDOWNING PERALTA FAMILY WITH THAT OF THE INDIGENOUS WORKERS ON THE SPANISH AND MEXICAN-ERA RANCHO, AND THEIR PAST AND CURRENT PRESENCE IN THE REGION. MUSEUM STAFF WILL WORK WITH OHLONE ARTISTS AND DESIGNERS TO FINALIZE DESIGNS AND FABRICATE AND INSTALL INTERPRETIVE ELEMENTS, INCLUDING OBJECTS, SCULPTURES, VIDEOS, TEXT, AND IMAGES. THE MUSEUM WILL INCORPORATE NEW RESEARCH TO REVISE, FIELD-TEST, AND LAUNCH ITS SCHOOL FIELD TRIP PROGRAM TO BETTER REFLECT INDIGENOUS AND LATINX COMMUNITY VOICES. THE EXHIBITS ARE DESIGNED TO HELP INDIGENOUS GROUPS UNDERSTAND AND CELEBRATE THEIR OWN CULTURES, WHILE HELPING NON-NATIVES LEARN ABOUT INDIGENOUS HISTORY AND ITS IMPACT ON THE REGION TODAY.
description.3623: THE SANTA CRUZ MUSEUM OF ART AND HISTORY WILL PARTNER WITH THE LONDON NELSON LEGACY INITIATIVE AND THE SANTA CRUZ BLACK HEALTH MATTERS INITIATIVE TO RESEARCH AND SHARE THE STORIES OF TWELVE PRE-1900S BLACK PIONEERS BURIED AT EVERGREEN CEMETERY IN SANTA CRUZ COUNTY, CALIFORNIA. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL PRODUCE AND ORGANIZE HISTORY AND ART EXHIBITIONS, DOCUMENTARY FOOTAGE OF THE RESEARCH PROCESS, AND PUBLIC MURALS. ADDITIONAL EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING WILL INCLUDE A PANEL DISCUSSION, AN HISTORIC WALKING TOUR, A COMMUNITY EVENT, AS WELL AS THE DEVELOPMENT OF A RELATED K-12 CURRICULUM. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE RESIDENTS OF SANTA CRUZ COUNTY WILL HAVE INCREASED ACCESS TO LOCAL HISTORICAL KNOWLEDGE, A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW TO RESEARCH OTHER HIDDEN HISTORIES, AND A STRONGER SENSE OF CROSS-CULTURAL CONNECTIONS AMONG COMMUNITY MEMBERS.
description.3624: SAVE THE BAY WILL IMPLEMENT A FELLOWSHIP PROGRAM THAT PROVIDES HANDS-ON TRAINING AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES AT THE AQUARIUM CREATING A SCHOOL-TO-CAREER PATHWAY FOR THOSE UNDERREPRESENTED IN ENVIRONMENTAL CAREERS FOCUSING ON THE OCEAN. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RECRUITING AND ONBOARDING TWO NEW FELLOWS ANNUALLY, TRAINING AND MENTORING FELLOWS, AND WORKING WITH EACH FELLOW TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A YEAR-LONG PROJECT. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A ROBUST SUSTAINABLE CAREER PATHWAY THAT EXPANDS ORGANIZATIONAL INCLUSION AND ENCOURAGES GREATER INVOLVEMENT IN AQUARIUM CAREERS FOR THOSE WHO ARE NOT WELL-REPRESENTED IN THE FIELD.
description.3625: THE SOLOMON R. GUGGENHEIM MUSEUM WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTIONS AND ONLINE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES FOR VISITORS WITH DISABILITIES THROUGH A TWO-PRONGED APPROACH: CREATION OF A NEW DIGITAL MUSEUM MAP OF THE FRANK LLOYD WRIGHT BUILDING, AND AN IN-DEPTH REVIEW AND REMEDIATION OF THE WEBSITE DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND CONTENT TO ENSURE USABILITY. THE MUSEUM’S DIGITAL EXPERIENCE TEAM WILL START THE MAP REDESIGN PROCESS WITH USER RESEARCH BEFORE PROCEEDING TO DESIGN AND RELEASE. A PART-TIME PROJECT MANAGER WILL BE HIRED TO OVERSEE THE WEBSITE REMEDIATION, AND WILL CONDUCT WEBSITE QUALITY ASSURANCE FROM AN ACCESSIBILITY STANDPOINT, ADD ACCESS CONTENT, PROVIDE CROSS-DEPARTMENTAL TRAINING, AND SERVE AS THE POINT OF CONTACT FOR BEST PRACTICES IN USER ACCESSIBILITY. AS A RESULT, VISITORS WILL HAVE ACCESS TO A VARIETY OF DIGITAL PLATFORMS, SUCH AS WEBSITES AND APPS THAT SUPPORT USE BY SCREEN READERS OR OTHER ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY; AND ACCESSIBLE CONTENT, SUCH AS VERBAL DESCRIPTION AUDIO AND AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE VIDEO.
description.3626: THE BURKE MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY AND CULTURE WILL CATALOG AND REHOUSE APPROXIMATELY 9,000 PALEOBOTANICAL SPECIMENS IN THE COLLECTION, INCLUDING FOSSIL LEAVES, FLOWERS, SEEDS, FRUITS, WOOD, PLANT MICROFOSSILS, AND FOSSIL INSECTS, AND WILL UNDERTAKE DATA CLEANUP OF APPROXIMATELY 20,000 SPECIMENS. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT A PAID INTERN, SEVERAL WORK STUDY POSITIONS FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS, AND A GRADUATE RESEARCH ASSISTANT POSITION. STAFF WILL ALSO BUILD NEW AND STRENGTHEN EXISTING RELATIONSHIPS WITH REGIONAL TRIBES THROUGH ENGAGEMENT AND CONSULTATION FOCUSED ON LEARNING AND KNOWLEDGE SHARING OF WASHINGTON STATE’S PALEONTOLOGICAL RESOURCES.
description.3627: GROUNDS FOR SCULPTURE WILL EXPAND ITS WELLNESS INITIATIVE PROGRAMMING TAILORED FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS OF VARYING PHYSICAL AND MENTAL ABILITIES, SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS, AND SENIORS. INFORMED BY A PREVIOUS CONVENING OF COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS FOCUSED ON HEALTH, ARTS, NATURE, ACCESSIBILITY, AND WELLNESS NEEDS, THE MUSEUM WILL SCALE UP AND REFINE ITS CURRENT PROGRAMMATIC OFFERINGS AND PARTNERSHIPS UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF ITS WELLNESS ADVISORY COUNCIL. A NEW WELLNESS PROGRAM MANAGER WILL BE HIRED TO SUPERVISE, MANAGE, AND GROW THIS INITIATIVE AND WORK WITH AN EVALUATION CONSULTANT TO ASSESS PROGRAM SUCCESS. BY OFFERING A BROAD SUITE OF WELLNESS-CENTERED PROGRAMS AND EVENTS, SUCH AS AN ANNUAL WELLNESS FAIR, THE MUSEUM WILL CONTINUE TO SERVE THE NEEDS OF ITS DIVERSE PUBLIC AS A CORNERSTONE FOR WELLNESS IN THE COMMUNITY.
description.3628: THE BROOKLYN MUSEUM WILL SUPPORT 55 PAID INTERNSHIPS FOR STUDENTS AND EARLY CAREER PROFESSIONALS INTERESTED IN CAREERS IN THE ARTS AND CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS. THE PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES, THAT PUT THE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF THESE YOUNG PEOPLE, WHOSE IDENTITIES ARE OFTEN UNDERREPRESENTED IN THE ARTS AND MUSEUM SECTOR, AT THE CENTER OF THEIR WORK. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE FACILITATING DEPARTMENTAL PLACEMENTS, WHERE INTERNS WILL DEVELOP HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE THROUGH REAL-WORLD PROJECTS WITH THE GUIDANCE OF MUSEUM STAFF; CONDUCTING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SEMINARS; AND DEVELOPING AN INTERN MENTOR PROGRAM TO HELP INTERNS ACHIEVE THEIR CAREER GOALS. PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL DEVELOP THE SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE NECESSARY FOR FUTURE EMPLOYMENT AND LEAVE WITH NEW PROFESSIONAL RELATIONSHIPS AND A STRUCTURE TO FOSTER THEM.
description.3629: ZOO ATLANTA WILL ADVANCE THE MANAGEMENT AND CARE OF ITS ANIMAL COLLECTION BY UPGRADING ITS CURRENT ANIMAL MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION VAN TO A CUSTOMIZED VETERINARY SERVICES VEHICLE. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE NEED FOR IMPROVED TRANSPORTATION FOR ANIMALS UNDERGOING ROUTINE CARE AND OFF-GROUNDS SPECIALIZED TREATMENTS AS WELL AS IMPROVED RESPONSE TIMES FOR STAFF ADDRESSING ANIMAL EMERGENCIES. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE NEW VEHICLE WILL IMPROVE THE EFFICIENCY OF THE VETERINARY MEDICINE TEAM AND RESULT IN SAFER METHODS FOR THE ZOO TO TRANSPORT ANIMALS.
description.3630: THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN MUSEUM OF ART WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT PROGRAMMING TO EDUCATE YOUNG VOTERS WITH THE GOAL OF ENGAGING THEM IN DIALOGUE ACROSS DIFFERING IDEOLOGIES AND INCREASING CIVIC UNDERSTANDING AND PARTICIPATION. THE MUSEUM WILL WORK IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE CITY OF ANN ARBOR, THE NON-PARTISAN UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN CREATIVE CAMPUS VOTING PROJECT, ARTIST PHILIPPA PHAM HUGHES, AND OTHER CAMPUS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO ENGAGE STUDENTS AND THE PUBLIC ON VOTING RIGHTS. PAID UNDERGRADUATE STUDENT INTERNS AND GRADUATE STUDENT ASSISTANTS WILL WORK WITH MUSEUM STAFF TO PRODUCE PROGRAMS, INCLUDING CROSS-POLITICAL DINNERS, DISCUSSIONS, LECTURES, AND INTERACTIVE ART EXPERIENCES, INFORMED BY A COMMUNITY ADVISORY GROUP. THE PROJECT WILL DEMYSTIFY THE VOTING PROCESS, ENERGIZE VOTERS, AND ENCOURAGE MEANINGFUL DIALOGUE ACROSS THE POLITICAL SPECTRUM WHILE EXPANDING THE MUSEUM’S COMMITMENT TO CIVIC RESPONSIBILITY.
description.3631: THE SHELBURNE MUSEUM WILL CONDUCT CONSERVATION SURVEYS IN THE ELECTRA HAVEMEYER WEBB MEMORIAL BUILDING, WHICH HOUSES IMPRESSIONIST PAINTINGS, ASIAN ART, AMERICAN AND ENGLISH DECORATIVE ARTS, AND HISTORIC INTERIORS. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A PROFESSIONAL CONSERVATOR WHO WILL CONDUCT CONDITION AND ILLUMINATION SURVEYS, CONSIDER ENERGY AND VISIBILITY IMPROVEMENTS, UPDATE CONDITION INFORMATION FOR THE COLLECTIONS, AND CREATE A PLAN FOR PROTECTING THE COLLECTIONS WHILE WORK IS UNDERTAKEN ON THE BUILDING. THE ILLUMINATION SURVEY WILL INFORM FUTURE PLANNING FOR LIGHTING IMPROVEMENTS TO BALANCE PRESERVATION AND VISITOR ACCESS.
description.3632: THE SAN FRANCISCO BOTANICAL GARDEN WILL EXPAND PUBLIC ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTIONS OF THE GARDENS OF GOLDEN GATE PARK, A NEW ENTITY LAUNCHED TO ELEVATE THE EXPERIENCES OF VISITORS TO THE THREE BOTANICAL GARDENS IN GOLDEN GATE PARK. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE CREATING A UNIFIED COLLECTIONS POLICY FOR ALL THREE GARDENS, EXPANDING THE CAPACITY OF THE COLLECTIONS TEAM, AND INTEGRATING AND EXPANDING THE COLLECTIONS DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES THE NEED TO PROVIDE THE PUBLIC, INCLUDING VISITORS, STUDENTS, AND RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS, WITH REAL-TIME AND ACCURATE INFORMATION ABOUT THE LIVING AND HISTORICAL COLLECTIONS IN THE CONSERVATORY OF FLOWERS, JAPANESE TEA GARDEN, AND SAN FRANCISCO BOTANICAL GARDEN.
description.3633: THE CARNEGIE MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY WILL CONSERVE, REHOUSE, AND DIGITIZE 15,000 ARCHIVAL LETTERS AND DOCUMENTS THAT COMPOSE THE HOLLAND CORRESPONDENCE ARCHIVE. SPANNING FROM 1896 TO 1913, THE ARCHIVE INCLUDES CORRESPONDENCE BETWEEN THE MUSEUM’S FIRST DIRECTOR, WILLIAM J. HOLLAND, AND COLLEAGUES, PARTNERS, AND RESEARCHERS. STAFF WILL WORK WITH CONSERVATORS TO ADDRESS IMMEDIATE THREATS TO THE ARCHIVE AS WELL AS REHOUSE AND STORE THE COLLECTION. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A FULLY DIGITIZED, SEARCHABLE, PARTIALLY TRANSCRIBED, AND PROPERLY SECURED ARCHIVE THAT WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO THE MUSEUM’S EARLIEST YEARS, COLLECTING IDEOLOGIES AT THE TURN OF THE 20TH CENTURY, AND FOUNDATIONAL MUSEUM OPERATION PRACTICES.
description.3634: THE NEW ENGLAND AQUARIUM WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A NEW APPRENTICE PROGRAM TO PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND CAREER PATHWAY ACCESS TO STEM CAREERS BY REDUCING ACCESS BARRIERS FOR HISTORICALLY UNREACHED AND UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITIES IN THE GREATER BOSTON AREA. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE IDENTIFYING AND ENGAGING A VARIETY OF COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO DEVELOP THE PROGRAM AND REACH NEW AUDIENCES, EVALUATING INTERNAL CULTURE TO ENSURE THAT THE AQUARIUM IS READY TO ENGAGE APPRENTICE COHORTS, DEVELOPING CURRICULUM AND TRAINING FUTURE MENTORS, RECRUITING AND TRAINING APPRENTICE COHORTS, AND CONDUCTING PROGRAM EVALUATION. THE EIGHT APPRENTICES WHO GRADUATE FROM THE PROGRAM WILL DEVELOP THE SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED TO START A STEM CAREER INCREASING THE LIKELIHOOD OF VIABLE EMPLOYMENT AT THE AQUARIUM OR BEYOND.
description.3635: THE BOTANICAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF TEXAS, A SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND CONSERVATION CENTER THAT ALSO MANAGES THE FORT WORTH BOTANIC GARDEN, WILL MIGRATE LIVING COLLECTION RECORDS FROM THEIR CURRENT COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE TO AN ENHANCED PLATFORM TO FACILITATE THE ACCESSIONING OF EXISTING AND FUTURE PLANT MATERIALS. FUNDS WILL BE USED TO HIRE A PLANT RECORDS MANAGER WHO WILL CONDUCT PLANT INVENTORIES, CATALOG MATERIAL, PERFORM DATA VALIDATION, AND TRAIN STAFF. THIS PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A LIVING COLLECTIONS STRATEGIC PLAN AND THE ADVANCEMENT OF AN INTEGRATED, COLLECTIONS-FOCUSED APPROACH TO PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT, RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND SPECIES CONSERVATION.
description.3636: THE MUSEUM OF ARTS AND DESIGN WILL USE FUNDS TO UPGRADE ITS PRIMARY CONTENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (CMS) AND PHOTOGRAPH, REVIEW, AND UPDATE ITS COLLECTION RECORDS TO SUPPORT GREATER ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTION. THIS PROJECT WILL CONVERT THEIR CURRENT SYSTEM TO A CLOUD-BASED CMS, PHOTOGRAPH NEW ACQUISITIONS, AND SUPPORT A FULL INVENTORY OF THEIR COLLECTIONS TOWARD COMPLETE RECORD CONSOLIDATION. AT THE END OF THE PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL HAVE A FUNCTIONAL AND USER-FRIENDLY, PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE DATABASE OF ITS COLLECTION WITH ARTIFACT-BASED PROGRAMMING FOR K-12 AUDIENCES AND LIFELONG LEARNERS OF ALL AGES.
description.3637: THE JUDD FOUNDATION WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO A COLLECTION OF APPROXIMATELY 21,000 IMAGES RELATED TO THE LIFE AND WORK OF AMERICAN ARTIST DONALD JUDD. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON DIGITIZING IMAGES THAT DOCUMENT THE ARTIST’S WORK, ARCHITECTURE, FURNITURE, DESIGN PRACTICES, AND EXHIBITIONS, AS WELL AS HIS PERSONAL LIFE AND TRAVELS. BY SUPPORTING THE CATALOGING, DATABASE MANAGEMENT, AND IMPROVED DIGITAL IMAGE FILE PRESERVATION, THIS PROJECT LAYS ESSENTIAL GROUNDWORK FOR THE STAFF TO EXPAND AND DIVERSIFY ITS AUDIENCE THROUGH DIGITIZATION INITIATIVES, ONLINE ACCESS, PUBLIC PROGRAMS, AND TO FACILITATE SCHOLARLY RESEARCH.
description.3638: THE WILLOWBROOK WILDLIFE CENTER WILL DESIGN AND DEVELOP A PLAN TO PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL AND ACTION-ORIENTED MESSAGES TO ADDRESS GAPS IN PUBLIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE MEDICAL SCIENCE BEHIND WILDLIFE REHABILITATION, THE IMPACT OF HUMAN ACTIVITIES ON HABITAT, AND PROVIDE SOLUTIONS TO HEALTHY CO-EXISTENCE OF PEOPLE AND WILDLIFE THAT CAN CONTRIBUTE TO A SUSTAINABLE FUTURE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE GRAPHIC DESIGN AND PRODUCTION OF INTERPRETIVE PANELS FOR THE VISITOR CENTER AND OUTDOOR INTERACTIVE TRAILS EXPERIENCE; DEVELOPMENT OF CURRICULUM-BASED GUIDED AND SELF-GUIDED SCHOOL FIELD TRIPS; A CLASSROOM LOAN BOX WITH LESSON PLANS, AND A FAMILY DISCOVERY BACKPACK FOR VISITORS; AND EVALUATION OF BOTH THE INTERPRETIVE VISITOR EXPERIENCE AND THE CURRICULUM-BASED AND FAMILY LEARNING MATERIALS. THE RESULTING NEW VISITOR EXPERIENCE WILL ENCOURAGE INFORMED ACTION SO LOCAL AND REGIONAL VISITORS CAN LEARN WHAT THEY CAN DO TO HELP PREVENT AND RESPOND APPROPRIATELY TO HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT.
description.3639: THE STRONG NATIONAL MUSEUM OF PLAY WILL USE FUNDS TO IMPROVE THE DOCUMENTATION, PRESERVATION, AND ACCESSIBILITY OF 15,000 TRADE CATALOGS FROM THE TOY, DOLL, PUZZLE, AND GAME INDUSTRIES. PROJECT STAFF WILL MAKE COLLECTIONS-RELATED INFORMATION ACCESSIBLE AND SEARCHABLE ONLINE THROUGH ITS OWN WEBSITE AS WELL AS THROUGH AN EXTERNAL COLLECTION WEBSITE. ENHANCED DOCUMENTATION, PRESERVATION, AND ACCESSIBILITY OF THE COLLECTION WILL ADVANCE THE MUSEUM’S MISSION AND BENEFIT HISTORIANS AND RESEARCHERS OF AMERICAN TOY AND GAME PRODUCTION.
description.3640: THE LONG ISLAND CHILDREN’S MUSEUM WILL LAUNCH THE THIRD PHASE OF THE DEVELOPMENT OF “SALTWATER STORIES: THE SEA AND ME,” A NEW PERMANENT EXHIBITION THAT WILL ENGAGE FAMILY AND SCHOOL AUDIENCES IN AN EXPLORATION OF THE LOCAL MARITIME TRADITIONS THAT HAVE SHAPED THE HISTORICAL, CULTURAL, AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF LONG ISLAND. BUILDING ON PREVIOUS GRANTS, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL INCORPORATE FINDINGS FROM THE SECOND PHASE TO FABRICATE EXHIBITION COMPONENTS WITH AN OUTSIDE CONTRACTOR, DEVELOP SEASONALLY INFORMED PROGRAMS AND MATERIALS FOR FAMILIES, DEVELOP WEBSITE CONTENT, FINALIZE AND IMPLEMENT THE EXHIBITION MARKETING PLAN, AND UTILIZE A REMEDIAL EVALUATION OF THE INSTALLED EXHIBITION TO MAKE ADJUSTMENTS. EXHIBITION CONTENT WILL CORRELATE TO SEVERAL NEW YORK STATE NEXT GENERATION LEARNING STANDARDS, AND WILL EXTEND THE REACH OF HUMANITIES PROGRAMMING TO KEY AUDIENCES, INCLUDING UNDERSERVED OR RECENTLY IMMIGRATED POPULATIONS FROM COASTAL COMMUNITIES IN MEXICO, CENTRAL AMERICA, AND ASIA. AS A RESULT, VISITORS TO THE MUSEUM WILL INCREASE THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF LONG ISLAND’S MARITIME HISTORY AND CULTURE THROUGH PARTICIPATING IN EDUCATIONAL AND INTERGENERATIONAL EXPERIENCES.
description.3641: THE PAINE ART CENTER AND GARDENS WILL USE FUNDS TO CREATE A HISTORIC PRESERVATION PLAN TO HELP SUSTAIN THE LONG-TERM CARE OF THE HISTORIC ESTATE’S ARCHITECTURE AND COLLECTIONS. INFORMED BY A PREVIOUS MUSEUM ASSESSMENT PROGRAM (MAP) REPORT THAT RECOMMENDED PRIORITIZING THE NEED FOR PRESERVATION AND MAINTENANCE PLANS, THE ORGANIZATION WILL WORK WITH AN HISTORIC PRESERVATION ARCHITECT AND A HISTORIC RESTORATION FIRM TO ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE HISTORIC PRESERVATION PLAN AND A CYCLICAL MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE NEW PRESERVATION PLAN WILL GUIDE THE CURATORIAL AND FACILITIES STAFF IN PLANNING FOR FUTURE PRESERVATION AND MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES OF THE ESTATE’S ARCHITECTURE AND COLLECTIONS.
description.3642: CLOCKSHOP WILL ENGAGE IN A CULTURAL ASSET MAPPING PROCESS TO DOCUMENT THE DIVERSE AND CHANGING NEIGHBORHOODS NEAR THE SITE OF A PLANNED 18-ACRE STATE PARK IN NORTHEASTERN LOS ANGELES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL GATHER ORAL HISTORIES, WRITE NEIGHBORHOOD NARRATIVES, CAPTURE PROFESSIONAL PHOTOGRAPHIC IMAGERY, AND PRODUCE MINI DOCUMENTARIES TO RECORD UNDERREPRESENTED CULTURAL PRACTICES, PERSONAL HISTORIES, AND LIVED EXPERIENCES OF LOCAL WORKING-CLASS COMMUNITIES OF COLOR. CLOCKSHOP WILL HIRE A FULL-TIME COMMUNITY PROGRAMS MANAGER AND WILL ENGAGE ARTISTS, PROGRAM FACILITATORS, LANGUAGE INTERPRETERS, AND A PROJECT ARCHIVIST TO PRODUCE THE BILINGUAL CULTURAL ASSET MAP AS WELL AS SUPPORT PUBLIC PROGRAMS AND TEMPORARY PUBLIC ART PROJECTS. A NEIGHBORHOOD ADVISORY COUNCIL COMPRISED OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL INFORM STRATEGIC PLANNING AND PROGRAMMING, WHILE ONGOING COLLABORATION WITH CALIFORNIA STATE PARKS WILL RESULT IN THE INTEGRATION OF THESE COMMUNITIES’ STORIES AND CULTURES INTO THE INTERPRETATION OF THE FUTURE PARK.
description.3643: THE MORRIS CENTER FOR LOWCOUNTRY HERITAGE WILL PARTNER WITH LOCAL EDUCATORS TO CREATE A NEW FOURTH-GRADE SCHOOL FIELD TRIP PROGRAM THAT INCLUDES MUSEUM VISITS AND PRE- AND POST-TRIP LESSON PLANS SERVING EVERY FOURTH-GRADE STUDENT IN THE MUSEUM’S FOUR SURROUNDING COUNTIES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RECRUITING AND ONBOARDING A NEW SCHOOL PROGRAMS COORDINATOR, DEVELOPING FIELD TRIP RESOURCES; TRAINING DOCENTS; PILOTING, EVALUATING, AND REFINING PROGRAMS; AND IMPLEMENTING IMPROVED FIELD TRIP PROGRAMS. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE 3,400 FOURTH-GRADE STUDENTS AND 120 TEACHERS BY PROVIDING INTERACTIVE AND ENGAGING CROSS-DISCIPLINARY PROGRAMS COVERING THE LOCAL HISTORY, ARTS, AND CULTURE OF THE AREA.
description.3644: THE AMERICAN MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY WILL BROADEN ACCESS TO ITS VERTEBRATE PALEONTOLOGY ARCHIVE BY CREATING DETAILED FINDINGS AIDS FOR EIGHT OF ITS COLLECTIONS. THE ARCHIVE CONSISTS OF 820 LINEAR FEET OF MATERIALS IN 43 COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING PHOTOGRAPHS, CORRESPONDENCE, AND FIELD NOTES. BUILDING ON WORK FUNDED BY PREVIOUS IMLS GRANTS, THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A PROJECT ARCHIVIST AND TWO PAID STUDENT INTERNS TO PROCESS, REHOUSE, AND DIGITIZE COLLECTIONS MATERIALS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, RESEARCHERS FROM A VARIETY OF DISCIPLINES WILL BE ABLE TO DIRECTLY ACCESS CATALOG RECORDS DESCRIBING THE CONTENTS OF THE VERTEBRATE PALEONTOLOGY ARCHIVE COLLECTIONS. PROJECT STAFF WILL SHARE THE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT ONLINE AND AT PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCES.
description.3645: THE CAMERON ART MUSEUM WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO THE MUSEUM FOR PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES, PARTICULARLY THOSE LIVING WITH VISUAL, HEARING, AND COGNITIVE DIFFERENCES. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS ACCESSIBILITY FOR PROGRAMS, EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES, EXHIBITIONS, AND VIRTUAL INITIATIVES. PROGRAMMING WILL INCLUDE ARTISTS AND MUSICIANS WORKING WITH PARTICIPANTS LIVING WITH DISABILITY, ASL INTERPRETATION, AND INCORPORATE NEW MEANS OF ACCOMMODATION SUCH AS SENSORY BAGS AND SOUND BLOCKING HEADPHONES. STAFF WILL RECEIVE TRAINING ON ACCESSIBILITY BEST PRACTICES, AND PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL BE INFORMED BY A NEWLY FORMED ADVISORY COMMITTEE CONSISTING OF MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY WHO HAVE LIVED EXPERIENCE IN EACH AREA OF ACCESSIBILITY FOCUS. THIS COLLABORATIVE, INSTITUTION-WIDE INITIATIVE WILL REMOVE BARRIERS TO ENGAGEMENT AND BUILD THE MUSEUM’S CAPACITY TO BETTER MEET THE NEEDS OF VISITORS OF ALL ABILITIES.
description.3646: THE HANDS ON CHILDREN’S MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH LOCAL LOW-INCOME AND RURAL SCHOOLS, YOUTH ORGANIZATIONS, AND TRIBES TO EXPAND ITS MAKER PROGRAMS FOR YOUNG CHILDREN BY BRINGING TAILORED PROGRAMMING TO OFF-SITE COMMUNITY-BASED LOCATIONS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE HIRING A NEW COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT MANAGER WHO WILL OVERSEE THE PROGRAM, DEVELOPING CURRICULUM AND STAFF TRAINING MATERIALS FOR THE NEW PROGRAMS, IMPLEMENTING THE OUTREACH PROGRAMMING AT OFF-SITE LOCATIONS, AND EVALUATING THE NEW PROGRAM MODELS. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES COVID-19 PANDEMIC-RELATED LOSSES IN LEARNING AND SOCIAL EMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WHILE INCREASING THE MUSEUM’S CAPACITY TO MEET THE GROWING DEMAND FOR OFF-SITE STEM ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES.
description.3647: SITE SANTA FE WILL INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY TO ITS DIGITAL CONTENT BY CREATING A DYNAMIC, BILINGUAL WEBSITE. BUILT IN 1996 WITH A 2012 RENOVATION TO ADAPT TO MOBILE USAGE, THE CURRENT WEBSITE HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY OUTDATED AND INADEQUATE IN REPRESENTING THE WORK OF CONTEMPORARY ARTISTS AND RESOURCES AVAILABLE THROUGH THE MUSEUMS PUBLIC PROGRAMMING AND PLACE-BASED ACTIVATIONS. A WEBSITE CONTENT MANAGER WILL BE HIRED TO WORK WITH THE PROJECT TEAM ON ASSESSING THE MUSEUM’S CURRENT RESOURCES, WORKING WITH A WEB DESIGN FIRM ON THE NEW WEBSITE, AND CREATING CONTENT. A TWO-YEAR FELLOWSHIP WILL BE CREATED TO ASSESS THE DIGITAL ASSETS FROM PREVIOUS EXHIBITIONS AND CONVERT OLDER FORMAT RECORDINGS OR IMAGES. AS A RESULT, WEBSITE USERS WILL EXPERIENCE AN ACCESSIBLE, STREAMLINED SITE WITH ENGAGING CONTENT AND INTUITIVE NAVIGATION, WHILE STAFF WILL BENEFIT FROM EFFICIENT OPERATIONS.
description.3648: THE ALBUQUERQUE MUSEUM FOUNDATION WILL IMPROVE THE STEWARDSHIP OF ITS COLLECTIONS OF ART, HISTORY, AND PHOTOGRAPHY ARCHIVES FOUND WITHIN THEIR MUSEUM, AS WELL AS CASA SAN YSIDRO: THE GUTIÉRREZ/MINGE HOUSE, A HISTORIC STRUCTURE ADMINISTERED BY THE FOUNDATION. DURING THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL CREATE CONDITION REPORTS, INVENTORY COLLECTIONS, ENTER DATA INTO THEIR COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, AND WORK WITH A PHOTOGRAPHER TO DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL SHARE DIGITIZED COLLECTIONS RECORDS ONLINE THROUGH A SEARCHABLE COLLECTIONS DATABASE.
description.3649: THE OKEFENOKEE SWAMP PARK WILL IMPROVE ITS ABILITY TO SERVE THE PUBLIC BY CREATING A MASTER INTERPRETIVE PLAN THAT UTILIZES INCLUSIVE AND EQUITABLE ENGAGEMENT STRATEGIES ACROSS DIVERSE AND HISTORICALLY UNDER-REPRESENTED AUDIENCES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONTRACT WITH MASTER INTERPRETIVE PLANNING CONSULTANTS TO SET THE FOUNDATIONAL WORK, WHICH WILL INCLUDE REGULAR MEETINGS, VISITS TO CONDUCT SITE AUDITS AND COLLECT DATA, BEFORE DRAFTING THE PRELIMINARY PLAN. COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL PROVIDE INPUT THROUGHOUT THE PROCESS THROUGH COLLECTION OF ORAL HISTORIES, VISITOR SURVEYS, AND PUBLIC WORKSHOPS OR CHARRETTES. THE RESULTING MASTER INTERPRETIVE PLAN WILL SERVE AS A ROAD MAP FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ALL FUTURE EXHIBITS AND EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES AT THE NATURE CENTER.
description.3650: THE NATIONAL MUSEUM OF TOYS AND MINIATURES WILL EXPAND THE DOCUMENTATION AND ACCESSIBILITY OF 1,250 OBJECTS FROM ITS COLLECTION OF TOYS AND FINE-SCALE MINIATURES. STAFF WILL WORK WITH UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE FELLOWS TO CONDUCT RESEARCH AND DEVELOP COLLECTIONS-RELATED CONTENT FOR THE MUSEUM WEBSITE. PROJECT STAFF WILL WORK WITH K-12 AND UNIVERSITY STAKEHOLDERS, WHO WILL SELECT THE OBJECTS TO BE INCLUDED ON THE WEBSITE AND PARTICIPATE IN PROJECT WORKSHOPS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, INCREASED ACCESSIBILITY TO THE OBJECTS AND THEIR ASSOCIATED METADATA WILL PROVIDE LOCAL EDUCATORS WITH RESOURCES TO INCORPORATE COLLECTIONS-RELATED CONTENT INTO THEIR TEACHING.
description.3651: THE MUSEUM OF THE ROCKIES AT MONTANA STATE UNIVERSITY WILL DESIGN AND LAUNCH DISCOVER SCIENCE!, A PALEONTOLOGY EDUCATION INITIATIVE THAT WILL IMMERSE VISITORS IN PROCESSES OF SCIENTIFIC INQUIRY OF 71-82 MILLION YEAR OLD PREHISTORIC ENVIRONMENTS BY ENGAGING THEM WITH PALEONTOLOGY SPECIMENS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PRODUCING K-12 CURRICULUM, DEVELOPING TEACHER TRAINING PROGRAMS TO BE OFFERED VIRTUALLY AND IN PERSON, AND OFFERING A POP UP MUSEUM SERVICE THAT WILL INCLUDE OUTREACH KITS FOR CLASSROOMS AND A TRAVELING MUSEUM EDUCATOR. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A PART-TIME STAFF PERSON TO LEAD THE POP UP MUSEUM SERVICE WITH A FOCUS ON REACHING TITLE 1 AND RESERVATION SCHOOLS. THE RESULTING SUITE OF PROGRAMS WILL LEAVE AN OUTDATED, SELF-GUIDED TOUR APPROACH BEHIND AND REPLACE IT WITH MORE INQUIRY-BASED AND INTERACTIVE APPROACH THAT WILL BETTER SERVE THE MUSEUM'S RURAL COMMUNITY.
description.3652: THE NEVADA MUSEUM OF ART WILL USE FUNDS TO SUPPORT THE REHOUSING OF ITS ART AND LIBRARY COLLECTIONS IN A NEW AND EXPANDED 50,000 SQUARE FOOT EDUCATION AND RESEARCH CENTER. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON REHOUSING ENVIRONMENTAL PHOTOGRAPHY AND WORK BY CONTEMPORARY INDIGENOUS ARTISTS AS WELL AS 10,000 LIBRARY VOLUMES AND SPECIAL COLLECTIONS OBJECTS. STAFF WILL SUPERVISE THE INSTALLATION OF MOVABLE STORAGE SCREENS FOR ARTWORKS AND SHELVING FOR LIBRARY COLLECTIONS AS WELL AS ENGAGE IN COLLECTIONS CARE ACTIVITIES, SUCH AS REFRAMING ARTWORK. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, COLLECTIONS STORAGE WILL BE MORE ACCESSIBLE TO STAFF FOR EXHIBITION, RESEARCH, AND COLLECTIONS CARE PURPOSES.
description.3653: HISTORIC HUDSON VALLEY WILL UNDERTAKE A PROJECT TO DIGITIZE AND FULLY CATALOG THEIR COLLECTION OF 3,500 MANUSCRIPTS, TRANSCRIBE SELECTIONS FROM THE COLLECTION, AND CREATE AN ONLINE PORTAL THAT WILL MAKE THE COLLECTION PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE. AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT, STAFF WILL BE ABLE TO BETTER UNDERSTAND, CARE FOR, AND UTILIZE THE MANUSCRIPT COLLECTION WHILE REDUCING THE RISKS OF PHYSICAL DAMAGE ASSOCIATED WITH REGULARLY HANDLING SENSITIVE ARCHIVAL MATERIALS. ADDITIONALLY, THE COLLECTIONS PORTAL WILL BENEFIT RESEARCHERS, STUDENTS, EDUCATORS, AND CURATORS WHO WILL NOW HAVE THE ABILITY TO SEARCH AND DISCOVER DIGITIZED AND TRANSCRIBED MANUSCRIPTS.
description.3654: THE GEORGIA O’KEEFFE MUSEUM WILL EXPLORE NEW WAYS TO ENGAGE THE PUBLIC IN LEARNING ABOUT THE ART AND LIFE OF GEORGIA O’KEEFFE, ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT ARTISTS OF THE 20TH CENTURY. A USER-FRIENDLY SEARCHABLE BROWSER WILL PROVIDE FREE ACCESS TO ALL KNOWN ARTWORKS BY THE ARTIST, INCLUDING 1,009 WORKS IN THE O’KEEFFE’S COLLECTION, AS WELL AS 498 WORKS HELD BY AN ADDITIONAL 145 ORGANIZATIONS, WITH RELATED IMAGES, EXHIBITION HISTORIES, ARCHIVAL MATERIALS, AND OTHER DATA ASSOCIATED WITH THE ARTIST’S CATALOG. THE PROJECT WILL BRING GREATER MEANING AND CONTEXT TO THE COLLECTIONS HELD BY THE MUSEUM AND INSTITUTIONS ACROSS THE COUNTRY, AND PRESENTS OPPORTUNITIES FOR FUTURE RESEARCH, COLLABORATION, AND ENGAGEMENT.
description.3655: THE MUSEUM OF CONTEMPORARY PHOTOGRAPHY WILL DIGITIZE ARTWORKS AND ENTER COLLECTIONS METADATA FOR APPROXIMATELY 6,000 ITEMS FROM ITS PERMANENT COLLECTION. THE MUSEUM WILL ALSO CATALOG AND REHOUSE OBJECTS AND UPDATE METADATA RELATED TO THE OBJECTS. STAFF WILL HIRE AND TRAIN TWO GRADUATE CURATORIAL ASSISTANTS WHO WILL RESEARCH AND WRITE UPDATED ARTIST BIOGRAPHIES AND CATALOG CONTENT THAT ARE INFORMED BY SURVEYS COMPLETED BY ARTISTS, THEIR AGENTS, AND FAMILIES. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE PUBLIC WILL HAVE INCREASED ACCESS TO THOUSANDS OF SEARCHABLE, HIGH-RESOLUTION IMAGE FILES ONLINE THROUGH THE MUSEUM’S WEBSITE.
description.3656: THE DISCOVERY CHILDREN’S MUSEUM WILL REFRESH CONTENT AND RENOVATE WATER WORLD, ONE OF THE ORIGINAL AND MOST POPULAR PERMANENT EXHIBITIONS. BASED ON RECOMMENDATIONS FROM A 2020 EXHIBIT MASTER PLANNING REPORT, STAFF WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EXHIBITION FABRICATOR, A PROJECT MANAGER, AND AN EVALUATOR TO TAKE EXISTING DESIGNS THROUGH FABRICATION, TESTING, INSTALLATION, AND REMEDIAL EVALUATION. A CROSS-DEPARTMENTAL STAFF TEAM WILL COLLABORATE ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROGRAMS, COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, REVISED K-7TH GRADE CURRICULUM-BASED MATERIALS, CREATION OF ONLINE CONTENT FOR EDUCATORS, AND A TIMELAPSE VIDEO OF THE EXHIBITION INSTALLATION. AS A RESULT, VISITORS WILL ENJOY A PERMANENT EXHIBITION THAT REQUIRES SIGNIFICANTLY LESS WATER TO OPERATE, WITH IMPROVED SAFETY AND ENGAGEMENT FEATURES AND NEW NEVADA-SPECIFIC CONTENT AROUND WATER CONSERVATION.
description.3657: THE CHILDREN’S MUSEUM OF INDIANAPOLIS WILL MARK ITS CENTENNIAL IN 2025 WITH AN EXHIBITION THAT TELLS STORIES ABOUT THE WAYS IN WHICH PEOPLE OF ALL BACKGROUNDS, BELIEFS, AND ABILITIES FROM ALL ACROSS THE WORLD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE MUSEUM, COMMUNITY, AND SOCIETY. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE SELECTING OBJECTS WITH FINAL CONCEPTUALIZATION AND INPUT GATHERED FROM THE COMMUNITY, CONSULTING WITH ADVISORS ON STORYLINE DEVELOPMENT, CLEANING AND STABILIZING OBJECTS FOR DISPLAY, PRODUCING COMPLEMENTARY PROGRAMS, AND CONDUCTING A FORMATIVE AND REMEDIAL EVALUATION. THE EXHIBITION WILL ELEVATE UNDERHEARD VOICES, CELEBRATE MUSEUM AND COMMUNITY MILESTONES, AND EXPLORE THE SOMETIMES-DIFFICULT STORIES BEHIND THESE OBJECTS WHILE ENVISIONING THE ROLE THE MUSEUM WILL PLAY IN SOCIETY OVER THE NEXT CENTURY. THE PROJECT WILL RAISE AWARENESS OF THE IMPORTANCE OF COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP, TURNING VISITORS INTO AMBASSADORS WHO WILL SUPPORT CENTENNIAL CAMPAIGN EFFORTS TO FUND COLLECTIONS INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS TO SAFEGUARD THESE ICONIC OBJECTS FOR GENERATIONS TO COME.
description.3658: THE ACADEMY OF NATURAL SCIENCES OF DREXEL UNIVERSITY WILL PARTNER WITH MANTUA CIVIC ASSOCIATION TO CREATE THE MANTUA YOUTH AMBASSADOR PROGRAM, A COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM THAT SEEKS TO CONNECT YOUTH AGES 8-16 IN PLACE-BASED ARTS AND CIVIC ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES THROUGH ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP OF COMMUNITY GREEN SPACE. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT A COMMUNITY HORTICULTURE EDUCATOR AND A UNIVERSITY STUDENT INTERN IN THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION, AND OVERSIGHT OF THE PROGRAM, AS WELL AS STIPENDS FOR THE PHILADELPHIA YOUTH AMBASSADOR PARTICIPANTS. THROUGH THEIR PARTICIPATION IN A CURRICULUM OF EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES INTEGRATING ARTS, STEM, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE, THE YOUTH AMBASSADORS WILL DEVELOP LEADERSHIP SKILLS AND A DEEPENED SENSE OF CIVIC ENGAGEMENT. THIS INITIATIVE WILL ADDRESS AN URBAN COMMUNITY’S NEED FOR YOUTH CIVIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSIBILITY, AS WELL AS SERVE AS A MODEL FOR FUTURE ENGAGEMENT OF INFORMAL STEM LEARNERS AND YOUTH COMMUNITY LEADERS WITHIN PHILADELPHIA.
description.3659: THE DYCKMAN FARMHOUSE MUSEUM WILL TRANSFORM ITS WINTER KITCHEN INTO AN IMMERSIVE SPACE THAT INVITES GUESTS TO MORE FULLY UNDERSTAND THE HISTORY OF ENSLAVEMENT IN THE NORTHERN UNITED STATES. BUILDING ON AN IMLS-FUNDED INTERPRETIVE PLANNING PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL ENGAGE WITH A CONSULTANT TO CREATE AN IMMERSIVE PROJECTION ON ONE OR MORE WALLS OF THE WINTER KITCHEN. IMAGES WILL INCLUDE ORIGINAL FOOTAGE OF HISTORIC CHARACTERS, CONTEMPORARY COMMUNITY MEMBERS, ARCHIVAL IMAGES, AND ILLUSTRATIONS. GRADUATE STUDENT INTERNS WILL ASSIST MUSEUM STAFF WITH RESEARCH, IMPLEMENTATION, AND OUTREACH. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL ADVANCE ITS MISSION TO SUPPORT THE PRESERVATION OF THE HISTORIC SITE, TO BE A CATALYST FOR ENGAGING, ADVENTURESOME PROGRAMMING AND TO BE A GOOD NEIGHBOR AND A DYNAMIC RESOURCE FOR THE COMMUNITY BY PROVIDING NEW AND FRESH INCLUSIVE NARRATIVES IN AN ENGAGING AND ACCESSIBLE MANNER.
description.3660: THE FLEISHER ART MEMORIAL WILL WORK WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO EXPAND PROGRAMS AND RESOURCES FOR IMMIGRANT COMMUNITIES OF SOUTHEAST PHILADELPHIA. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE VISUAL ART EXHIBITIONS AND PRESENTATIONS, COMMUNITY EVENTS, AND PUBLIC PROGRAMMING SUCH AS FREE ART WORKSHOPS. PROGRAM DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION WILL BE INFORMED COMMUNITY COLLABORATORS AND A COMMUNITY PLANNING COMMITTEE, WHILE MUSEUM STUDIES STUDENTS FROM A LOCAL COLLEGE WILL BE RECRUITED TO ASSIST STAFF AND GAIN PRACTICAL EXPERIENCE. THROUGH OFFERING A CONTINUUM OF WELCOMING, ACCESSIBLE, AND CULTURALLY RELEVANT ARTS PROGRAMMING, THE MUSEUM WILL DEEPEN COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS AND ADVANCE CROSS-CULTURAL UNDERSTANDING WITHIN THEIR INCREASINGLY CONNECTED COMMUNITIES.
description.3661: THE SOUTH DAKOTA SCHOOL OF MINES AND TECHNOLOGY’S MUSEUM OF GEOLOGY WILL CATALOG AND REHOUSE SPECIMENS FROM ITS MINERALOGY AND PETROLOGY COLLECTIONS THAT DOCUMENT THE MINERAL DIVERSITY OF THE BLACK HILLS AND INCLUDE ORES OF MANY STRATEGIC MINERALS. STAFF WILL TRAIN AND WORK WITH TWO GRADUATE STUDENTS AND ONE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENT TO IDENTIFY, CURATE, AND REHOUSE SPECIMENS AS WELL AS DIGITIZE COLLECTION RECORDS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL PROVIDE PUBLIC ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION THROUGH AN ONLINE COLLECTIONS DATABASE THAT WILL INCLUDE PHOTOGRAPHY AND 3D SCANS OF CURATED MINERALS FOR THE BENEFIT OF FACULTY, STUDENTS, STAFF, AND VISITING RESEARCHERS OF MINERALOGICAL SCIENCES.
description.3662: THE PENNSYLVANIA ACADEMY OF THE FINE ARTS WILL EXPAND ITS ONGOING PARTNERSHIP WITH ECONOMICALLY UNDERSERVED ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS IN THE PHILADELPHIA NEIGHBORHOODS OF KENSINGTON AND FELTONVILLE TO CONTINUE PROVIDING FREE ARTS-BASED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING TO EDUCATORS, STUDENTS, AND FAMILIES. THE ACADEMY WILL HIRE TWO PART-TIME ART EDUCATORS AND ADD A FOURTH PARTNER SCHOOL TO THE EXISTING YEAR-ROUND BI-LINGUAL SERVICES IT PROVIDES, WHICH INCLUDE STUDENT FIELD TRIPS, TEACHER PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNITY AND PARENT WORKSHOPS, VIRTUAL TOURS, AND FAMILY FESTIVAL EVENTS. PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS, THE MAJORITY OF WHOM ARE NEWLY IMMIGRATED TO THE UNITED STATES, WILL GAIN LITERACY, CRITICAL THINKING, AND EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE SKILLS THROUGH FLEXIBLE, RESPONSIVE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES THAT ARE DESIGNED BY AND FOR THE CITIZENS THEMSELVES.
description.3663: THE CENTER FOR CRAFT WILL INSTALL A MATERIALS LIBRARY, AN INTERACTIVE, FLEXIBLE COLLECTION OF TRADITIONAL AND INNOVATIVE CRAFT MATERIALS, IN ITS ENGAGEMENT STUDIO, A HANDS-ON EDUCATIONAL AREA THAT ENCOURAGES INTERACTION WITH CRAFT THROUGH APPROACHABLE ACTIVITIES AND RESOURCES. THE MATERIALS LIBRARY WILL OFFER THE CENTER’S VISITORS THE OPPORTUNITY FOR TACTILE ENGAGEMENT WITH APPROXIMATELY 100 SAMPLES OF TRADITIONAL, INNOVATIVE, AND SUSTAINABILITY-MINDED MATERIALS HOUSED IN A CUSTOM DISPLAY SHELF ALONG WITH CORRESPONDING INFORMATION ABOUT THE MATERIALS’ PROPERTIES ACCESSIBLE THROUGH A DIGITAL RADIO FREQUENCY IDENTIFICATION (RFID) SCANNER AND INTERACTIVE DISPLAY. THE RESULTING PUBLIC-FACING RESOURCE WILL SCAFFOLD THE PUBLIC’S UNDERSTANDING OF WHAT CRAFT IS AND WHAT IT CAN BE, SHIFTING PAST PERCEPTIONS OF CRAFT AND ENCOURAGING CONSIDERATION OF ITS POTENTIAL. THE MATERIALS LIBRARY WILL ALSO SERVE AS A PILOT FOR THE KIND OF COLLABORATIVE, RADICALLY ACCESSIBLE INSTALLATION THE MUSEUM PLANS TO CONTINUE EXPLORING THROUGH THE PLATFORM OF THE ENGAGEMENT STUDIO.
description.3664: THE DUBUQUE COUNTY HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL LAUNCH A STAKEHOLDER-ENGAGED INTERPRETIVE PLANNING INITIATIVE THAT WILL PRODUCE A MASTER PLAN ALIGNED TO THE RECENTLY EXPANDED MUSEUM CAMPUS. THROUGH COLLABORATIVE ACTIVITIES BETWEEN STAFF, BOARD OF DIRECTORS, VOLUNTEERS, VISITORS, COMMUNITY MEMBERS, STAKEHOLDERS, AND AN INTERPRETIVE PLANNING FIRM, THE MUSEUM WILL PRODUCE A NEW MASTER INTERPRETIVE PLAN INCLUDING RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INTERPRETIVE PRACTICES AND COMPREHENSIVE SIGNAGE. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL GAIN AN INCREASED UNDERSTANDING OF VISITOR KNOWLEDGE, BEHAVIORS, AND ATTITUDES, REFLECT COMMUNITY NEED AND CONNECTIVITY, INFORM EVALUATION PRACTICES TO BEST SERVE THE COMMUNITY, CREATIVELY INTEGRATE THE GOALS OF BOTH HISTORIC AND LIVING COLLECTIONS IN EXHIBITS AND PROGRAMS, AND CREATE A MORE COHESIVE STORYLINE TO BETTER JOIN ITS 14-ACRE CAMPUS AND 2-ACRE HERITAGE SITE.
description.3665: THE KIDZU CHILDREN’S MUSEUM WILL DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK FOR SUPPORTING REFUGEES INCLUDING REGULAR FAMILY PROGRAMMING AT THE MUSEUM, A SKILLS-DEVELOPMENT VOLUNTEER PROGRAM FOR TEENAGE REFUGEES, AND A BEST PRACTICES TOOLKIT DESIGNED TO HELP OTHER INFORMAL LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS AND CULTURAL CENTERS IMPLEMENT SIMILAR PROGRAMS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE THE FACILITATION OF TARGETED, FREE PROGRAMMING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH LOCAL REFUGEE COMMUNITIES; AN AUDIT OF MUSEUM SPACE AND PROGRAMMING; THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A SKILLS-DEVELOPMENT VOLUNTEER PROGRAM FOR TEENAGE REFUGEES; AND THE CREATION OF A BEST PRACTICES TOOLKIT TO BE SHARED WITH OTHER MUSEUMS AND CENTERS. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE 300 FAMILIES AND UP TO 40 TEEN VOLUNTEERS AND HELP BOTH PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS AND PROJECT PARTNERS BUILD A FEELING OF BELONGING AND ATTACHMENT TO THE COMMUNITY.
description.3666: THE BAKKEN MUSEUM WILL ENHANCE ITS CAPACITY TO CONDUCT EVALUATIONS BY DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING A NEW INTERNAL EVALUATION SYSTEM AND TRAINING STAFF ON RESEARCH AND EVALUATION TOOLS AND PRACTICES. THROUGH AN ITERATIVE AND COLLABORATIVE APPROACH, PROJECT STAFF AND PAID COMMUNITY ADVISORY GROUP MEMBERS WILL DESIGN AND TEST THE NEW SYSTEM, WHICH WILL POSITION THE MUSEUM TO BETTER UNDERSTAND AND RESPOND TO VISITORS’ NEEDS. STAFF WILL RECEIVE TRAINING ON TECHNIQUES FOR COMMUNITY OUTREACH-BASED EVALUATION METHODS, SUCH AS SURVEY DEVELOPMENT, OBSERVATIONS, AND INTERVIEWS, AND WILL ATTEND CONFERENCES TO FURTHER THEIR PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND SHARE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT. AS A RESULT, THE BAKKEN MUSEUM WILL BE BETTER SITUATED TO SERVE ITS CONSTITUENTS AND STAFF WILL BE EMPOWERED TO ASSESS PROGRAM IMPROVEMENTS, COMMUNICATE SUCCESSES AND CHALLENGES, AND FOSTER ONGOING ENGAGEMENT.
description.3667: THE WISCONSIN STATE HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL ENGAGE IN A STATE-WIDE PUBLIC HISTORY PROJECT THAT WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO THE SOCIETY’S COLLECTIONS AND RESOURCES BY BRINGING COMMUNITY-BASED PROGRAMMING INTO ALL 72 WISCONSIN COUNTIES. PROJECT STAFF WILL PROTOTYPE STRATEGIES FOR DESIGNING AND DELIVERING LOCALIZED PROGRAMMING IN COLLABORATION WITH APPROXIMATELY 120 COMMUNITY PARTNERS, PARTICULARLY IN RURAL AREAS. THE SOCIETY WILL HIRE A DIRECTOR OF EXPERIENCE DESIGN, CONTRACT WITH LOCAL VENDORS TO CREATE MOBILE EXHIBITS, AND CONDUCT PUBLIC PROGRAMMING FEATURING THE SOCIETY’S COLLECTION, BANNER EXHIBITS, SPEAKERS BUREAU PRESENTATIONS, AND SIGNATURE EVENTS TAILORED TO INDIVIDUAL COMMUNITIES. AS A RESULT, COMMUNITY PARTNERS WILL HAVE AN INCREASED KNOWLEDGE AND SENSE OF OWNERSHIP OF WISCONSIN STATE HISTORICAL SOCIETY RESOURCES AND GREATER TRUST FOR FUTURE COLLABORATIONS, SUPPORTING THE SOCIETY’S LONG-TERM GOAL OF BECOMING A HUB FOR COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT.
description.3668: THE UNIVERSITY OF ALABAMA’S DEPARTMENT OF BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES WILL REHOUSE AND DIGITIZE ITS COLLECTION OF DECAPODS, WHICH CONTAINS APPROXIMATELY 20,000 CRAYFISH SPECIMENS. DEPARTMENT STAFF WILL HIRE AND TRAIN PAID AND VOLUNTEER STUDENT WORKERS WHO WILL CATALOG, LABEL, AND SHELVE SPECIMENS. STAFF WILL ALSO CONDUCT DATABASE CLEANUP FOR CRAYFISH LOTS FROM WATERBODIES ACROSS ALABAMA, UPDATING TAXONOMY AND GEOREFERENCING FOR INCREASED ACCURACY. TO ADVANCE THE SCIENTIFIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE DISTRIBUTION AND BIODIVERSITY OF CRAYFISHES AND HERPETOFAUNA IN THE ECOSYSTEMS IN THE SOUTHEASTERN UNITED STATES, STAFF WILL MAKE SPECIMEN DATA AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC BY SHARING INFORMATION WITH ONLINE DATA REPOSITORIES FOR NATURAL HISTORY COLLECTIONS.
description.3669: HOLDEN FORESTS & GARDENS WILL WORK WITH A CONSULTING FIRM TO CREATE A MAPPING APPLICATION THAT SHOWCASES THE LIVING COLLECTIONS AT THEIR CLEVELAND BOTANICAL GARDEN AND HOLDEN ARBORETUM CAMPUSES. THIS PROJECT WILL MERGE THEIR CURRENT PLANT RECORDS SYSTEM WITH A MODERN GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM (GIS) AND PRODUCE THEIR FIRST INTERACTIVE, PUBLIC MAPPING APPLICATION. THIS WORK WILL ALLOW STAFF TO ACCESS AND UPDATE DATABASES FROM MULTIPLE PLATFORMS, INCLUDING MOBILE DEVICES, AND PROVIDE DIGITAL ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS INFORMATION TO EXTERNAL AUDIENCES. THE CREATION OF A PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE WEB PORTAL THAT CONNECTS THE STAKEHOLDERS WITH INFORMATION ABOUT THEIR PLANTS AND TREES WILL SUPPORT THE ORGANIZATION'S STRATEGIC GOALS.
description.3670: THE BUFFALO MUSEUM OF SCIENCE WILL GAIN INTELLECTUAL AND PHYSICAL CONTROL OVER ITS FLUID-PRESERVED ICHTHYOLOGICAL COLLECTION THAT DOCUMENTS THE POPULATION OF FRESHWATER FISHES IN REGIONAL WATERWAYS. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A COLLECTIONS ASSISTANT TO WORK WITH STUDENT INTERNS AND VOLUNTEERS TO CREATE A COHESIVE CATALOG AS WELL AS REHOUSE, PHOTOGRAPH, AND DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION. STAFF WILL ALSO CREATE AND INSTALL PANELS AT FRESHWATER CONSERVATION AREAS IN WESTERN NEW YORK TO PROMOTE EDUCATION ABOUT FRESHWATER FISH AT LOCAL WATERWAYS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL MAKE THE NEWLY COMPLETED CATALOG OF THE COLLECTION PUBLICLY AVAILABLE THROUGH OPEN-ACCESS COLLECTION PORTALS FOR RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES.
description.3671: THE MISSOURI HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL DIGITIZE, CATALOG, AND PROCESS 52 LINEAR FEET OF PANORAMIC NEGATIVES AND PRINTS CREATED BY THE SIEVERS COMMERCIAL PHOTOGRAPHY STUDIO, WHICH OPERATED IN DOWNTOWN ST. LOUIS, MISSOURI FROM 1917 TO 1989, RESULTING IN AN ESTIMATED 4,745 DIGITIZED AND CATALOGED IMAGE RECORDS. TO COMPLETE THIS WORK, THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A FULL-TIME DIGITIZATION SPECIALIST AND A PART-TIME CATALOGER. THE DIGITIZATION SPECIALIST WILL DIGITIZE AND PROPERLY REHOUSE AN ESTIMATED 3,245 ORIGINAL PANORAMIC NEGATIVES AND DIGITIZE 1,500 PRINTS. THE CATALOGER WILL CREATE CATALOG RECORDS FOR EACH DIGITIZED IMAGE, ARRANGE AN ESTIMATED 16,300 PRINTS, AND MONITOR THE CONDITION OF THE FILM.
description.3672: THE PHILADELPHIA MUSEUM OF ART WILL USE FUNDS TO SUPPORT AN ONGOING EFFORT TO CATALOGUE, PHOTOGRAPH, DIGITIZE, RESEARCH, AND REHOUSE DRAWINGS FROM THEIR PRINTS, DRAWINGS, AND PHOTOGRAPHY DEPARTMENT. THE PROJECT WILL PHOTOGRAPH 7,832 SMALL- TO MID-SIZED DRAWINGS, CONFIRM AND VALIDATE DATA IN THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, CONDUCT IN-DEPTH CATALOGUING THAT WILL ADD PROVENANCE RESEARCH, DESCRIPTION, AND PUBLICATION AND EXHIBITION HISTORIES FOR SELECT WORKS, ADD ALL DIGITIZED WORKS TO THE MUSEUM’S ONLINE COLLECTION SITE; AND REHOUSE WORKS AS NEEDED.  AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE PRODUCTS OF THE CATALOGUING AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES FOR THESE FRAGILE AND LIGHT-SENSITIVE WORKS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE FOR PUBLIC ACCESS THROUGH THE MUSEUM’S ONLINE COLLECTIONS.
description.3673: ZOO NEW ENGLAND WILL FABRICATE AND INSTALL 25 CONSERVATION EDUCATION GRAPHICS AND FIVE INTERACTIVE EXPERIENCES IN THE NEW AFRICAN EXPERIENCE EXHIBIT. IN ADDITION TO TRADITIONAL GRAPHICS, A “PENGUIN RESCUE STATION” WILL ENABLE GUESTS TO ROLE-PLAY SAVING PENGUINS FROM AN OIL SPILL IN A BOAT WITH AUDIO AND VISUAL COMPONENTS OF A RESCUE IN ACTION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE FINALIZING THE DESIGN OF GRAPHICS AND INTERACTIVES, PRODUCING AND EVALUATING PROOFS AND MODELS, REVISING DESIGNS AS NEEDED, FABRICATING THE FINAL GRAPHICS, AND INSTALLING IN THE ZOO. THE RESULTING SIGNAGE AND INTERACTIVES WILL CREATE A NEW LEVEL OF ENGAGEMENT FOR VISITORS, WHO WILL GAIN A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE NATURAL WORLD, A DEEPER CONNECTION WITH THE SPECIES IN IT, AND A COMMITMENT TO TAKE SOME ACTION ON BEHALF OF THE ENVIRONMENT.
description.3674: VICTORIA MANSION WILL CONSERVE THE PAINTED FINISHES IN THE SECOND STORY OF ITS GRAND CENTRAL STAIR HALL THAT DATE BACK TO 1859-1860. THE STAIRCASE PAINTINGS WERE COMPLETED BY GIUSEPPE GUIDICINI, AN ITALIAN-BORN ARTIST WHO EMIGRATED TO THE UNITED STATES IN 1832 AND LATER HELPED TO DISSEMINATE A TASTE FOR ITALIANATE FRESCO-STYLE DECORATION IN THE NATION’S OPERA HOUSES AND THEATERS. PROJECT CONSERVATORS WILL ADDRESS AT-RISK AREAS BY STABILIZING AND CLEANING THE SECOND STORY STAIR HALL PAINT AND REVERSIBLY IN-PAINTING SMALL AREAS OF LOSS. CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES WILL TAKE PLACE IN PUBLIC VIEW TO FURTHER THE MUSEUM’S EFFORT TO PROMOTE EDUCATION ABOUT CONSERVATION PRACTICES.
description.3675: THE UNIVERSITY MUSEUM AT SOUTHERN ILLINOIS UNIVERSITY WILL IMPROVE THE STEWARDSHIP OF ITS COLLECTIONS AND INVENTORY APPROXIMATELY 11,000 OBJECTS FROM THE SOUTH AND CENTRAL AMERICAN COLLECTIONS, AMERICAN HISTORY COLLECTIONS, AND 3-DIMENSIONAL CONTEMPORARY ARTWORK COLLECTIONS. INFORMED BY A MUSEUM ASSESSMENT PROGRAM (MAP) REPORT AND PREVIOUS IMLS AWARDS, MUSEUM STAFF WILL RECEIVE TRAINING IN COLLECTIONS CARE AND CONDUCT DATA ENTRY TO IMPROVE THE ACCURACY OF COLLECTION INFORMATION. DURING THE INVENTORY PROCESS, STAFF WILL CONDITION REPORT, COMPLETE DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHIC DOCUMENTATION, AND IMPROVE BASIC STORAGE STABILIZATION.
description.3676: THE SAINT LOUIS ZOO WILL ESTABLISH A SECOND BIOBANKING LOCATION AT THE ZOO’S WILDCARE PARK TO ENSURE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A COLLECTION OF GENETICALLY SIGNIFICANT AND VALUABLE SPECIMENS FOR REPRODUCTIVE RESEARCH AND MANAGEMENT OF ANIMALS AT THE PARK. ONCE COMPLETED, IT WILL ALLOW THE ZOO TO EXPAND PARTICIPATION IN CONSERVATION AND RECOVERY PROGRAMS FOR ENDANGERED UNGULATE SPECIES, SUCH AS BANTENG AND ADDAX. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, BIOMATERIALS WILL BE AVAILABLE FOR RESEARCH, PROPAGATION, AND CONSERVATION PURPOSES TO OTHER ORGANIZATIONS, SUCH AS ZOOS AND UNIVERSITIES.
description.3677: THE SAN DIEGO AIR & SPACE MUSEUM WILL IMPROVE ITS COLLECTION CARE PROCESSES AND DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT FOR ITS COLLECTION OF ARTIFACTS RELATED TO AIR AND SPACE HISTORY AND TECHNOLOGY. THIS PROJECT WILL ENABLE THE MUSEUM TO IMPLEMENT A NEW INTEGRATED COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (CMS) ACROSS ALL ITS COLLECTIONS: CURATORIAL, LIBRARY, ARCHIVES, WITH THEIR CURRENT DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (DAMS). THIS HIGH-LEVEL UPGRADE WILL MEET THE GROWING NEEDS OF STAFF AND COLLECTION RECORDS, SAVE TIME AND MONEY BY ELIMINATING DUPLICATE WORKFLOWS, CENTRALIZE THE MUSEUM’S REGISTRATION PROCESS, AND CREATE A UNIFIED PUBLIC PORTAL TO DRAMATICALLY INCREASE DISCOVERABILITY AND ACCESS TO THEIR COLLECTION.
description.3678: THE SCIENCE MUSEUM OF MINNESOTA WILL EXPAND ON RECENT EFFORTS TO BUILD EVALUATION CAPACITY ACROSS THE MUSEUM BY ENGAGING IN COMMUNITY-WIDE CONVERSATIONS ABOUT EQUITY AND CLIMATE ACTION IN THE TWIN CITIES AND THE UPPER MIDWEST. USING A WIDE VARIETY OF DATA COLLECTION STRATEGIES, ONGOING DATA REPORTING, AND THREE DAY-LONG SUMMITS TO REFLECT ON THE BREADTH OF DATA GATHERED, THE MUSEUM WILL DEVELOP NEW INSIGHTS INTO WHAT ITS ROLE CAN AND SHOULD BE IN SUPPORTING CLIMATE-RELATED COMMUNITY CONVERSATIONS. THE PROJECT WILL BUILD ON THE MUSEUM’S EXISTING CLIMATE AND EQUITY WORK, INFORM FUTURE EXHIBITS AND PROGRAMMING, AND SUPPORT DEEPER ENGAGEMENT WITH ONSITE VISITORS AS WELL AS WITH NEIGHBORING COMMUNITIES WHO ARE INTERESTED IN OR COMMITTED TO WORK ON EQUITY AND CLIMATE CHANGE.
description.3679: THE FRANK LLOYD WRIGHT HOME AND STUDIO WILL EXPAND THE TEACHING BY DESIGN TEACHER PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM TO INCLUDE ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE CLASSES WITH VISITING ARCHITECTS, DESIGNERS, VISUAL ARTISTS, MUSICIANS, AND NATURALISTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING 12 PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SEMINARS, RECRUITING GUEST EDUCATORS AND FOUR RESIDENT ARTISTS, AND DEVELOPING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING THE ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE PROGRAM. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE IDENTIFIED NEED FOR INCREASED ARTS ACCESS IN UNDERSERVED SCHOOLS AND FOR LOCAL PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN ARTS INTEGRATION. TEACHER PARTICIPANTS WILL DEMONSTRATE INCREASED CONFIDENCE, MOTIVATION, AND USE OF DESIGN-BASED INQUIRY IN THEIR TEACHING.
description.3680: THE FINE ARTS WORK CENTER WILL EXPAND ITS SUMMER VISUAL ARTS AND CREATIVE WRITING PROGRAM TO INCLUDE AN ADDITIONAL 270 PARTICIPANTS, REACHING WIDER AUDIENCES BY REDUCING BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING OUTREACH TO RAISE AWARENESS OF THE PROGRAM, DEVELOPING NEW COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS TO REACH WIDER AUDIENCES, CONDUCTING STAFF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TO INCREASE CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT THIS EXPANDED PROGRAM, COORDINATING THE SUMMER PROGRAM, AND CONDUCTING A PROGRAM EVALUATION. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT PARTICIPANT HOUSING, TRAVEL, AND PROGRAM COSTS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN INCREASED PARTICIPATION BY MORE YOUNG ARTISTS AND WRITERS WHILE BUILDING INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT PROGRAMS AND CREATE A NURTURING COMMUNITY.
description.3681: EXPLORA WILL PARTNER WITH LOCAL COMMUNITY GROUPS AND LIBRARIES TO INCREASE THE MUSEUM’S RELEVANCE FOR BLIND AND LOW-VISION VISITORS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL HOST LISTENING SESSIONS AND DESIGN CHARRETTES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE ASPIRATIONS OF THE BLIND COMMUNITY; MAKE MODIFICATIONS TO THE EXHIBIT FLOOR THAT UTILIZE ADVISORS’ EXPERTISE AND BEST PRACTICE FROM OTHER MUSEUMS TO IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY FOR BLIND AND LOW-VISION VISITORS; EMPLOY BLIND AND LOW-VISION TEENS TO WORK AS NEAR-PEER MENTORS WITH YOUNGER BLIND STUDENTS IN CO-CREATED OUT-OF-SCHOOL TIME PROGRAMS; TRAIN THE FRONTLINE MUSEUM STAFF TO SUPPORT BLIND VISITORS AT THE MUSEUM; AND ENHANCE THE MUSEUM’S WEBSITE TO IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY FOR BLIND AND LOW-VISION USERS. THE OUTCOME OF THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL BE ENHANCEMENTS TO THE MUSEUM’S EXHIBITS, PROGRAMS, AND ONLINE RESOURCES THAT MAKE THEM MORE RELEVANT TO THE BLIND COMMUNITY AS WELL AS INCREASE ACCESS TO EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES THAT SUPPORT PATHWAYS TO STEAM COURSES AND CAREERS.
description.3682: THE FRANK LLOYD WRIGHT FOUNDATION WILL USE FUNDS TO PURCHASE NEW HIGH-DENSITY COMPACT STORAGE FOR ITS EXTENSIVE COLLECTIONS. THIS REHOUSING WILL INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF THE COLLECTIONS AREA AND SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE STORAGE CONDITIONS BY REDUCING OVERCROWDING AND REPLACING INADEQUATE AND INAPPROPRIATE STORAGE FURNITURE. THE NEW STORAGE CABINETRY ALLOWS THE FOUNDATION TO MAXIMIZE SUSTAINABILITY BY IMPROVING AND INCREASING COLLECTION STORAGE WITHIN THE EXISTING BUILDING RATHER THAN ADDING NEW SPACE, MINIMIZE UNNECESSARY HANDLING AND MOVEMENT OF ARTWORK, AND RESULT IN SAFER STORAGE CONDITIONS OVER THE LONG TERM.
description.3683: AMAZEMENT SQUARE WILL PARTNER WITH FIVE CENTRAL VIRGINIA LIBRARIES TO PROVIDE THE STEAM LIBRARY MAKERS PROGRAMS DESIGNED FOR AT-RISK EARLY LEARNERS NOT ENROLLED IN EARLY LEARNING FACILITIES TO HELP THEM DEVELOP THE SKILLS THEY NEED TO ENTER KINDERGARTEN AND EMPOWER THEIR CAREGIVERS TO HELP THEM LEARN AT HOME. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING, IMPLEMENTING, EVALUATING, AND REFINING THE MONTHLY STEAM PROGRAMS AND PROVIDING STEAM MAKER EDUCATION TRAINING FOR LIBRARY STAFF. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT FABRICATING MOBILE MAKER SPACES FOR EACH PARTNER LIBRARY, PROGRAM MATERIALS, AND PAID COLLEGE INTERNSHIPS. PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL DEVELOP A LOVE FOR LEARNING AND CURIOSITY WHILE DEVELOPING SKILLS THAT WILL HELP PREPARE THEM FOR KINDERGARTEN.
description.3684: THE DENVER ZOO WILL INCORPORATE INTERPRETIVE EXPERIENCES ACROSS ALL 12 ZONES WITHIN ITS TROPICAL DISCOVERY BUILDING THAT USE BEST PRACTICES AND INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO ENGAGE GUESTS AND MOTIVATE THEM TO CONSERVE TROPICAL HABITATS. IN TROPICAL DISCOVERY, GUESTS WALK THROUGH AN IMMERSIVE SPACE – FROM CAVE HABITATS TO RAINFORESTS AND CORAL REEFS – AND, FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 30 YEARS, THEY WILL ENCOUNTER A BACKWARDS-DESIGNED INTERPRETIVE EXPERIENCE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DEVELOP INTERPRETIVE SIGNAGE, OFFER LIVE INTERPRETATION PROGRAMS, CREATE NON-LIVE INTERPRETIVE ELEMENTS LIKE TACTILES AND COMMUNITY ART, AND INCORPORATE A CONSERVATION ACTION EXHIBITION TO SHOWCASE CONCRETE CONSERVATION ACTIONS THAT VISITORS CAN TAKE AS THEY DEPART THE BUILDING. FINDINGS FROM THE PROJECT WILL BE APPLIED TO EXHIBITS AND PROGRAMS ACROSS THE 84-ACRE CAMPUS.
description.3685: THANKSGIVING POINT INSTITUTE WILL PARTNER WITH TWO COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS BY ESTABLISHING “CURIOSITY CENTERS” WITHIN THEIR FACILITIES AND PROVIDING FREE STEM PROGRAMMING TO UNDERSERVED PRE-K AND K-12 YOUTH. GRANT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT TWO FULL-TIME AND TWO PART-TIME STEM EDUCATORS WHO WILL FACILITATE PROGRAMS ON TOPICS SUCH AS CODING, MAKING, ROBOTICS, ENTOMOLOGY, PALEONTOLOGY, ANIMAL AND EARTH SCIENCES, AND CAREER EDUCATION EXPERIENCES, ALL OF WHICH WILL ALIGN WITH UTAH STATE SCIENCE STANDARDS. THIS PILOT PROJECT WILL RESPOND TO COMMUNITY PARTNERS’ REQUESTS TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL ON-SITE STEM PROGRAMMING TO INCREASE THE ACCESSIBILITY OF HANDS-ON SCIENCE EDUCATION FOR THEIR COMMUNITIES. IT WILL RESULT IN A FRAMEWORK AND TOOLKIT FOR DELIVERING STEM PROGRAMMING TO YOUTH WITHIN ORGANIZATIONS THAT ALREADY HAVE AN ESTABLISHED RELATIONSHIP OF TRUST WITH THE FAMILIES AND YOUTH THEY SERVE.
description.3686: THE MEMPHIS BROOKS MUSEUM OF ART WILL REIMAGINE ITS INTERACTIVE FAMILY GALLERY THROUGH A DESIGN AND FABRICATION PROCESS THAT SUPPORTS EFFORTS TO PROVIDE ENRICHING, INTERACTIVE, AND ACCESSIBLE ARTS-BASED EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES TO VISITORS. THE NEW EXHIBITION DESIGN WILL BE DEDICATED TO VISUAL LITERACY, AND WILL OFFSET DECLINING PUBLIC ACCESS TO ARTS EDUCATION, WHICH DISPROPORTIONATELY IMPACTS COMMUNITIES WITH HIGHER-THAN-AVERAGE POVERTY RATES, LIKE MEMPHIS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL BEGIN WITH RESEARCH INTO BEST PRACTICES FOR DEVELOPING INTERACTIVE FAMILY SPACES, THEN WORK WITH ARTS AND EDUCATION PROFESSIONALS TO GUIDE THE DESIGN PROCESS, AND LEAD FOCUS GROUPS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE NEEDS AND EXPECTATIONS OF LOCAL FAMILIES. AN EVALUATION PARTNER WILL SUPPORT EACH STEP OF THE PROCESS, INCLUDING A SECOND ROUND OF FOCUS GROUP SURVEYS DURING A SOFT OPENING TO BEST UNDERSTAND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE NEW SPACE. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN AN UPDATED EXHIBITION FOR MULTIGENERATIONAL ENGAGEMENT WHERE FAMILIES WILL BE INSPIRED, DISCUSS ART, EXPERIMENT WITH VARIOUS PROCESSES, EXERCISE THEIR CREATIVITY, AND SHARE MEANINGFUL TIME TOGETHER.
description.3687: BROOKLYN CHILDREN’S MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH ELEMENTARY SCHOOL EDUCATORS TO CREATE SCHOOL PROGRAMS FOR NATURE’S ENGINEERS, A NEW STEM MAKER SPACE FOR CHILDREN AGES 5-10 THAT EXPLORES BIOMIMICRY (HOW NATURE INFLUENCES HUMAN DESIGN) THROUGH HANDS-ON PROJECTS AND ENGAGEMENT WITH THE 14,000 OBJECTS IN THE MUSEUM’S NATURAL SCIENCE COLLECTION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CREATING AN EDUCATOR ADVISORY COUNCIL, DEVELOPING FIVE NEW STEM MAKER FIELD TRIP PROGRAMS, DELIVERING THOSE PROGRAMS TO CENTRAL BROOKLYN PUBLIC ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS AT NO CHARGE, PROVIDING TEACHER PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS, AND EVALUATING THE PROGRAMS FOR THEIR EFFECTIVENESS ON LEARNING OUTCOMES AND BEHAVIORS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN CENTRAL BROOKLYN STUDENTS MAKING CONNECTIONS BETWEEN ENGINEERING AND NATURE THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THEIR CONSTRUCTED NARRATIVES ABOUT SCIENCE, HUMAN DESIGN, AND THE IMPORTANCE OF OUR NATURAL WORLD.
description.3688: THE INTREPID SEA, AIR AND SPACE MUSEUM WILL PILOT INSPIRATION ACADEMY, A NEW TEACHER TRAINING AND RESOURCES PROGRAM DESIGNED TO HELP K—12 EDUCATORS TEACH INCLUSIVE STEM, HISTORY, AND SOCIAL STUDIES, BUILT ON THE MUSEUM’S DECADE-LONG EXPERIENCE DEVELOPING TEACHER PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND PROVIDING OF CONTINUING EDUCATION CREDITS TO TEACHERS IN NEW YORK STATE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RECRUITING EARLY-CAREER TEACHERS FROM TITLE 1 SCHOOLS; IMPLEMENTING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES, INCLUDING IN-PERSON AND VIRTUAL SEMINARS AND INSTITUTES; AND CONDUCTING A PROGRAM EVALUATION. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS EARLY-CAREER TEACHER ATTRITION RATES BY FOSTERING A SENSE OF BELONGING IN THE PROFESSION AND REKINDLING THE JOY AND INSPIRATION WHICH BROUGHT INDIVIDUALS TO TEACH.
description.3689: THE TAMPA MUSEUM OF ART WILL PARTNER WITH KING’S KIDS CHRISTIAN ACADEMY, A NEEDS-BASED PRIVATE SCHOOL TO EXPAND ITS ART THERAPY-INFORMED PROGRAM, ART SPACE, TO THREE NEW CAMPUSES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING ART THERAPY-INFORMED LESSON PLANS AND THEN PILOTING, EVALUATING, AND REFINING THE SCHOOL AND MUSEUM VISITS. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT HIRING TWO PART-TIME OUTREACH PROGRAMS ASSISTANTS WHO WILL LEAD THE MUSEUM VISITS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS WITH CREATIVE INTERVENTIONS TO AUGMENT EXISTING SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL LEARNING USED BY THE SCHOOLS WHILE LEARNING COPING SKILLS AND EXPLORING EMOTIONAL EXPRESSION.
description.3690: THE CHILDREN’S MUSEUM OF PITTSBURGH WILL COLLABORATE WITH A TEAM OF PARTNERS AND LOCAL ADVISORS TO EXPAND THE GENIUS, JOY AND LOVE PROGRAM TO INCORPORATE CO-LEARNING EXPERIENCES IN WHICH HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS AND TEACHERS PARTICIPATE IN THREE TYPES OF ACTIVITIES: RESEARCH-BASED WORKSHOPS ABOUT EDUCATION PRACTICES THAT VALUE STUDENTS’ EXPERIENCES OUTSIDE SCHOOL AS ASSETS; ART AND MAKING ACTIVITIES; AND SUPPORTED ACTION PLANNING. THE PROJECT WILL BE CONDUCTED IN THREE PHASES. PHASE ONE WILL CARRY OUT A VERSION OF THE PROGRAM WHERE ADULTS AND YOUTH ARE BALANCED CO-LEARNERS, PHASE TWO WILL REVIEW EVALUATION RESULTS FROM PHASE ONE AND DEVELOP NEW MODULAR PROGRAMS, AND PHASE THREE WILL EMBED THE PROGRAM AS A REGULAR PART OF THE MUSEUM’S MISSION-ALIGNED PROGRAMMING. THE PROJECT WILL RAISE AWARENESS OF EQUITY-BASED APPROACHES TO EDUCATING, SUPPORT MEANINGFUL COLLABORATION, AND EMPOWER PARTICIPANTS WITH ACTION PLANS TO RECOGNIZE AND ADDRESS INJUSTICE SO THAT PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS FEELING ENERGIZED AND MOTIVATED TO RECLAIM EDUCATION.
description.3691: THE BUILDING FOR KIDS WILL OFFER PROGRAMMING AIMED AT MAKING MEANINGFUL CHANGE IN THE FOOD CULTURE OF ITS COMMUNITY. MUSEUM STAFF WILL HOST FAMILY COOKING WORKSHOPS AS WELL AS FIELD TRIPS FOR CHILDREN AND THEIR GROWN-UPS TO DEVELOP KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AROUND SOURCING, PREPARING, AND CONSUMING A VARIETY OF NUTRITIONALLY VALUABLE FOODS. A DIVERSE ADVISORY GROUP WILL HELP GUIDE PROJECT ACTIVITIES, WHILE COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS WILL INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN EXHIBIT ABOUT FOOD CULTURE. THE MUSEUM WILL ALSO HIRE LOCAL UNIVERSITY STUDENTS TO SERVE AS RESEARCH ASSISTANTS AND ASSIST IN PROGRAM EVALUATION. AS A RESULT, PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW THEY VIEW AND ENGAGE WITH THE FOOD THEY EAT AND TAKE PRIDE IN AND OWNERSHIP OVER THEIR CHOICES AND PREPARATION OF HEALTHY MEALS.
description.3692: THE WALTERS ART MUSEUM WILL DEVELOP "ETHIOPIA AT THE CROSSROADS," AN EXHIBITION THAT CELEBRATES THE ARTISTIC TRADITIONS OF ETHIOPIA FROM ANTIQUITY TO THE PRESENT. THIS EXHIBITION WILL EXPLORE THE CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE AND HUMANISTIC LEGACY OF ETHIOPIA THROUGH NEW, BROADENED LENSES, INCLUDING COMMUNITY VOICES AND INTERACTIVE EXPERIENCES, AND WILL EXAMINE HOW ETHIOPIA EMBODIES THE IDEA OF "CROSSROADS" GEOGRAPHICALLY, HISTORICALLY, AND CULTURALLY. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE FINALIZING THE EXHIBITION DESIGN AND INSTALLATION, WORKING WITH NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS AND PRIVATE COLLECTIONS TO SHIP LOANED ARTWORKS, AND WORKING WITH A COMMUNITY ADVISORY GROUP TO DEVELOP A SUITE OF RELATED PUBLIC PROGRAMS. AS A RESULT, VISITORS TO THE MUSEUM AND PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS WILL INCREASE THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF THE COMPLEX EXCHANGE OF VISUAL CULTURE BETWEEN ETHIOPIA AND THE WORLD.
description.3693: THE SCIENCENTER WILL ADDRESS ITS COMMUNITY’S NEED FOR OUTDOOR FAMILY LEARNING EXPERIENCES AND INCREASE ACCESS TO HANDS-ON STEM EDUCATION THROUGH THE CREATION OF FOUR OUTDOOR EXHIBIT AREAS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL USE COMMUNITY INPUT TO DRIVE THE DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE EXHIBIT AREAS, AND CREATE AND TEST PROTOTYPES WITH A FOCUS ON ACCESSIBLE PLAY-BASED ACTIVITIES TO ADDRESS LEARNING DECLINES RESULTING FROM THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE MEETING WITH THE COMMUNITY AND GATHERING INPUT TO DEFINE THE LEARNING GOALS, FABRICATING SELECTED COMPONENTS OF THE EXHIBITS, CONSULTING WITH ADVISORS AND ACCESSIBILITY EXPERTS AND TESTING PROTOTYPES, AND CONTINUING EVALUATION AFTER THE EXHIBITS OPEN TO THE PUBLIC. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM’S ROLE AS A RELEVANT AND WELCOMING RESOURCE FOR SCIENCE LEARNING WILL BE EVIDENT, AND LOCAL CHILDREN AND FAMILIES WILL INCREASE THEIR SOCIAL SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE OF THE SCIENCE PROCESS.
description.3694: THE PHILBROOK MUSEUM OF ART WILL GROW STORAGE CAPACITY AND EFFICIENCY BY CONVERTING A CURRENT LIBRARY SPACE INTO A MODERN, EFFICIENT STORAGE ROOM THAT WILL ALLEVIATE THE URGENT PROBLEM OF OVERCROWDING IN THE MUSEUM'S PERMANENT STORAGE SPACE. PROJECT STAFF WILL ASSESS THE CONDITION OF EACH PAINTING MOVED AND FLAG ANY NEEDING STABILIZATION, UPDATE THEIR COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM WITH TEMPORARY LOCATION AND CONDITION, AND WORK WITH THIRD-PARTY VENDOR TO INSTALL 31 PULL-OUT STORAGE RACKS. AS A RESULT, THIS PROJECT WILL INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY TO THE PAINTINGS BY COLLECTIONS STAFF AND GREATLY REDUCE THE FREQUENCY WITH WHICH WORKS NEED BE HANDLED.
description.3695: THE RUBIN MUSEUM OF ART WILL EXPAND KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING OF HIMALAYAN ART AND CULTURES THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FLEXIBLE TRAVELING EXHIBITION THAT PRESENTS THE ICONOGRAPHY, MATERIALS, AND ARTISTIC AND CULTURAL PRACTICES OF THE HIMALAYAN REGION. PRESENTED IN THREE MODULES WITH A VARIETY OF THEMATIC ACCESS POINTS, DIFFERENT MUSEUM COMMUNITIES WILL HAVE THE ABILITY TO MODIFY THE EXHIBITION ACCORDING TO THEIR NEEDS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE WORKING WITH FIVE UNIVERSITY MUSEUMS TO ADAPT THE EXHIBITION, TRANSPORTING AND INSTALLING THE EXHIBITION AT THE HOST SITE, AND REFINING AN OPEN-ACCESS DIGITAL PLATFORM TO ACCOMPANY THE EXHIBITION. THE PUBLIC WILL LEARN ABOUT THE FUNDAMENTAL ART FORMS AND IMPORTANT UNIVERSAL IDEAS FROM THE HIMALAYAN REGION, SUCH AS COMPASSION, KARMA, THE CYCLICAL NATURE OF EXISTENCE, AND THE INTERDEPENDENCE OF THINGS.
description.3696: THE PARRISH ART MUSEUM WILL EVALUATE, IMPROVE, AND EXPAND AN EXISTING GALLERY EXPERIENCE AND ART-MAKING PROGRAM THAT SERVES INDIVIDUALS WITH SPECIAL NEEDS, INCLUDING COGNITIVE DIVERSE INDIVIDUALS WITH INTELLECTUAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES, INDIVIDUALS ON THE AUTISM SPECTRUM, PEOPLE WITH PHYSICAL DISABILITIES, AND PEOPLE WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED SEVERE TRAUMA. THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH AN EXTERNAL EVALUATOR TO DEVELOP AN EVALUATION PLAN AS WELL AS A COMMUNITY ADVISORY PANEL WITH MEMBERS FROM THE PROGRAM’S TARGET AUDIENCES AND PARTNERING HUMAN SERVICE AGENCIES TO GUIDE THE PROJECT. PROGRAM EVALUATION WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT AND EXPANSION OF FUTURE COMMUNITY-INFORMED MUSEUM PROGRAMMING TO SERVE A WIDER AUDIENCE AND WILL LEVERAGE LESSONS LEARNED TO IMPROVE THE MUSEUM’S OVERALL SERVICE TO SPECIAL AUDIENCES IN ALL OF ITS PROGRAMS.
description.3697: THE CLYFFORD STILL MUSEUM WILL PARTNER WITH COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO ART CRAWL, A PROGRAM FOR INFANTS AND THEIR CAREGIVERS, TO INCLUDE MUSEUM-BASED SESSIONS AND PROGRAMMING IN COMMUNITY-BASED EARLY LEARNING CENTERS THAT REACH AUDIENCES TRADITIONALLY EXCLUDED FROM ARTS-BASED EDUCATION EXPERIENCES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE AUDIENCE EVALUATION TO LEARN FROM THE COMMUNITY, IMPROVE QUALITY, AND ENSURE THE PROGRAMS ARE INCLUSIVE AND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE; AND UPDATING THE LEARNING ENVIRONMENT SO THAT IT CREATES A SENSE OF BELONGING AND WELL-BEING. THE PROJECT WILL REMOVE BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATION AND HELP THE COMMUNITY SEE THE MUSEUM AS A RESOURCE FOR INFANTS AND FAMILIES AND WILL RESULT IN WELCOMING ART-BASED EARLY CHILDHOOD PROGRAMMING THAT PROVIDES OPPORTUNITIES FOR CAREGIVERS TO IMPACT THEIR BABY’S LEARNING BY INCREASING LANGUAGE, LITERACY, AND COGNITIVE SKILLS.
description.3698: THE AMERICAN FOLK ART MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH NEURODIVERSE ARTISTS WHOSE ARTWORK IS PART OF THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION AND CREATE AN ONLINE RESOURCE WITH INFORMATION ABOUT NEURODIVERSE ARTISTS. A COLLECTIONS ASSOCIATE HIRED FOR THE PROJECT WILL RECEIVE TRAINING ON THE COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM AND ASSIST WITH DIGITIZATION AND COLLECTIONS PHOTOGRAPHY. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO INCLUDE A CONVENING OF INDUSTRY EXPERTS TO DEVELOP A WHITE PAPER THAT WILL SERVE AS A GUIDE FOR MUSEUMS COLLECTING AND EXHIBITING WORKS OF ART BY NEURODIVERSE ARTISTS.
description.3699: THE BISHOP MUSEUM IN HONOLULU WILL LAUNCH KA ˊULA WENA: OCEANIC RED, AN EXHIBITION ORGANIZED BY NATIVE HAWAIIAN CURATORS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A COMMUNITY OF HAWAIIAN AND PACIFIC KNOWLEDGE-HOLDERS. THE EXHIBITION WILL HIGHLIGHT RARELY SEEN CULTURAL OBJECTS FROM THE MUSEUM COLLECTIONS AND NEVER-SEEN-IN-HAWAII OCEANIC OBJECTS ON LOAN FROM AROUND THE WORLD THAT ALL CARRY SOME ASPECT OF THE COLOR RED, AND WILL COINCIDE WITH THE MUSEUM HOSTING THE 13TH FESTIVAL OF PACIFIC ARTS AND CULTURE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL ENGAGE ‘ŌLELO HAWAIʻI (HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE) SPEAKERS AS CONTENT EXPERTS TO PREPARE BILINGUAL TEXT PANELS AND OTHER EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS, AND WILL TRAIN EDUCATORS, DOCENTS, AND MUSEUM STAFF TO LEAD THE SERIES OF INTERACTIVE AND BILINGUAL PROGRAMS. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL HONOR NATIVE HAWAIIANS AND OTHER PEOPLE OF THE PACIFIC THROUGH AN EXHIBITION OF THEIR CULTURE WHILE GROWING VISITORS' UNDERSTANDING OF THE MARRIAGE BETWEEN OBJECTS AND STORIES, AND HOW MUSEUMS HAVE A RESPONSIBILITY TO ENSURE BOTH OF THESE ASPECTS OF CULTURE ARE PERPETUATED.
description.3700: THE WILD CENTER WILL CONDUCT A TWO-YEAR OUTREACH AND SUMMER PROGRAM INITIATIVE TO TRAIN A COHORT OF TEEN CLIMATE EDUCATORS IN CLIMATE LITERACY, ENABLING THEM TO COMMUNICATE CLIMATE CHANGE SCIENCE AND IMPACTS AS WELL AS CLIMATE JUSTICE AND SOLUTIONS TO MUSEUM VISITORS USING THE MUSEUM’S SCIENCE ON A SPHERE AND CLIMATE SOLUTIONS EXHIBIT. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RECRUITING AND ONBOARDING THE EDUCATORS, DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING TRAINING AND MENTORING PLANS, ENHANCING THE VISITOR EXPERIENCE THROUGH EXHIBIT-BASED ENGAGEMENT, WORKING WITH THE TEENS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT CLIMATE ACTION PROJECTS FOR THEIR SCHOOL OR COMMUNITY, AND PLANNING AND HOSTING THE ADIRONDACK YOUTH CLIMATE SUMMIT. PROJECT FUNDS WILL ALSO SUPPORT PURCHASING HIGH-QUALITY PROJECTORS AND TWO BACK-OF-THE-HOUSE COMPUTERS TO RUN THE SCIENCE ON A SPHERE EXHIBIT. THE TEEN CLIMATE EDUCATORS WILL LEAD INTERPRETIVE PROGRAMMING, BECOME ACTIVE IN COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND CIVIC ENGAGEMENT, AND SUPPORT THE YOUTH-LED PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ADIRONDACK YOUTH CLIMATE SUMMIT.
description.3701: THE WHITNEY MUSEUM OF AMERICAN ART WILL LAUNCH A THREE-PHASE PROJECT TO ASSESS, UPDATE, AND DEPLOY INTERPRETATION STRATEGIES GEARED TOWARD VISITORS WITH DISABILITIES, PARTICULARLY THOSE WHO IDENTIFY AS D/DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING, BLIND AND WITH LOW VISION, WITH AMBULATORY DISABILITIES, NEURODIVERGENT, AND MORE. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP NEW STANDARDS FOR ACCESSIBLE DIGITAL INTERPRETATION AND IMPLEMENT THEM ACROSS NEW MATERIALS FOCUSED ON APPROXIMATELY 50 TIME-BASED MEDIA WORKS. A CROSS DEPARTMENTAL MUSEUM TEAM WILL WORK WITH AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE, FOCUS GROUPS, AND AN EVALUATOR TO CARRY OUT A USER-CENTERED ITERATIVE EVALUATION PROCESS, INCLUDING COMPLETING A NEEDS ASSESSMENT. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL HAVE INSTITUTIONAL GUIDELINES FOR ACCESSIBLE INTERPRETATION AND STANDARDS FOR PRESERVING THESE DIGITAL MATERIALS. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO INFORM THE MUSEUM’S FUTURE ACCESSIBLE DIGITAL INTERPRETATION FOR TIME-BASED MEDIA AND ALL OTHER FORMS OF ART.
description.3702: THE EMILY DICKINSON MUSEUM WILL IMPROVE COLLECTIONS DOCUMENTATION BY DIGITIZING INSTITUTIONAL RECORDS RELATED TO ITS APPROXIMATELY 8,000 ARTIFACTS PERTAINING TO THE FAMILY OF AMERICAN POET EMILY DICKINSON. MUSEUM STAFF WILL SCAN PHYSICAL RECORDS AND UPLOAD AND MANAGE THE DIGITIZED FILES IN THEIR DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. PROJECT STAFF WILL ALSO TRAVEL TO OTHER REPOSITORIES OF DICKINSON-RELATED ARCHIVAL INFORMATION AND, WITH STAFF FROM THOSE PARTNERING ORGANIZATIONS, CONDUCT SURVEYS OF PRIMARY SOURCES RELATED TO COLLECTIONS OBJECTS. THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN MORE COMPLETE COLLECTIONS INFORMATION MANAGEMENT, ENABLING THE MUSEUM TO INTERPRET THE POET’S LIFE AND TIMES MORE FULLY, AND PROVIDE PUBLIC AND SCHOLARLY ACCESS TO AN IMPORTANT CULTURAL COLLECTION.
description.3703: THE NEW YORK TRANSIT MUSEUM WILL DEVELOP A COMMUNITY-INFORMED MODEL FOR CREATING ADULT PUBLIC PROGRAMS AND SUSTAINING AUDIENCE ENGAGEMENT. MUSEUM STAFF WILL WORK WITH CONSULTANTS TO CONDUCT AN AUDIENCE ASSESSMENT AS WELL AS DEVELOP PLANS FOR IMPROVED DIGITAL COMMUNICATIONS. A FULL-TIME OUTREACH COORDINATOR WILL BE HIRED TO SUPERVISE THE PROJECT AND IDENTIFY EXTERNAL STAKEHOLDERS TO SERVE AS ADVISORS FOR PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. THIS STAKEHOLDER ADVISORY COMMITTEE AND PARTNERING DOWNTOWN BROOKLYN CULTURAL ORGANIZATIONS WILL INFORM THE RESULTING PROGRAM PLANNING FRAMEWORK, HELPING THE MUSEUM BETTER-UNDERSTAND AND ENGAGE WITH ITS EXISTING ADULT AUDIENCES, IDENTIFY POTENTIAL AUDIENCES THAT ARE NOT YET ENGAGED, AND COLLABORATIVELY DESIGN PROGRAMS THAT INCLUDE COMMUNITY VOICES AND INPUT.
description.3704: THE CHILDREN’S MUSEUM TUCSON WILL EXPAND ITS STEAM PROGRAM OFFERINGS FOR FAMILIES AND YOUNG LEARNERS ONSITE AND THROUGH VIRTUAL AND IN-PERSON OUTREACH THROUGHOUT PIMA AND SANTA CRUZ COUNTIES. BUILDING ON “APRENDEMOS,” AN IMLS-FUNDED INITIATIVE, THE MUSEUM WILL CREATE A NEW POSITION FOR A BILINGUAL STEAM SPECIALIST, WHO WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE PROJECT TEAM TO EXPAND EXISTING PROGRAMS BY OFFERING THEM IN SPANISH, CREATE SPANISH-LANGUAGE TOURS, AND DESIGN NEW PROGRAMS AND EDUCATIONAL COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT THAT ORIGINATE IN SPANISH, AS WELL AS CONTINUING TRANSLATION OF EXISTING PROGRAMS. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL BE AN INCLUSIVE, WELCOMING PLACE FOR CHILDREN WHO HAVE HISTORICALLY BEEN EXCLUDED FROM EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS, AND ENABLE ALL CHILDREN IN SOUTHERN ARIZONA TO BUILD, CREATE, IMAGINE, EXPLORE, AND DISCOVER.
description.3705: THE WASHINGTON STATE HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL INSTALL A NEW PERMANENT EXHIBITION THAT EXPLORES THE HISTORY OF THE MORE THAN 29 TRIBES OF WASHINGTON STATE WITH AN EMPHASIS ON INTERPRETING TRIBAL SOVEREIGNTY. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EXHIBITION FABRICATOR TO BUILD OUT DESIGNS THAT WERE DEVELOPED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH TWO NATIVE CURATORS AND GUIDED BY A 10-PERSON NATIVE ADVISORY COMMITTEE. THE EXHIBITION WILL INCLUDE INDIGENOUS ARTISTS SELECTED THROUGH AN OPEN CALL, WHO WILL CREATE WORKS THAT COMMENT ON AND INTERPRET GALLERY THEMES.
