THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A PART-TIME PHOTO ARCHIVIST AND CONTRACT WITH A DIGITAL ASSET MANAGER, POLICY WRITER, AND CONSERVATOR WHO, ALONG WITH EXISTING VOLUNTEERS, WILL CATALOG AND DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING A CONSERVATION ASSESSMENT; CREATING COLLECTIONS AND PRESERVATION POLICIES; CATALOGING, REHOUSING, AND DIGITIZING PHOTOGRAPHS AND NEGATIVES; AND CREATING AN ONLINE COLLECTIONS DATABASE. AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT, THE COLLECTION WILL BE MORE ACCESSIBLE FOR USE BY RESEARCHERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS.
description.3887: THE WHITNEY PLANTATION WILL EXPAND ITS EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH TO LOCAL AND NATIONAL AUDIENCES BY IMPLEMENTING A DISTANCE LEARNING PROGRAM AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM ON THE HISTORY AND LEGACIES OF ENSLAVED AFRICANS, AFRICAN AMERICANS, AND CREOLES OF COLOR IN SOUTHEAST LOUISIANA. ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES WITH LOCAL AUDIENCES WILL INCLUDE A TEACHER OPEN HOUSE, A JUNETEENTH COMMUNITY DAY, HOSTING THE SLAVE DWELLING PROJECT, AND DEVELOPING THE “MUSEUM IN A BOX” PROGRAM, WHICH WILL EXPLORE SLAVERY THROUGH THE LENS OF HISTORY, ART, AND SCIENCE FOR OFFSITE LEARNING. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT A DIGITAL PROGRAMS COORDINATOR, WHO WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT VIRTUAL PROGRAMS AND ASSOCIATED OUTREACH TO NATIONAL AUDIENCES. THESE ACCESSIBLE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS FOR BOTH TRADITIONAL AND NONTRADITIONAL LEARNING SPACES AND AUDIENCES WILL FURTHER BUILD THE CAPACITY OF WHITNEY PLANTATION AS AN INNOVATIVE MUSEUM THAT NARRATES THE HISTORY OF SLAVERY FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF ENSLAVED PEOPLE.
description.3888: THE MEEK-EATON SOUTHEASTERN REGIONAL BLACK ARCHIVES RESEARCH CENTER AND MUSEUM (MEBA) AT FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY WILL BUILD ITS DIGITAL CAPACITY BY ENHANCING MANAGEMENT, CARE, AND ACCESS FOR ITS COLLECTIONS AND EXPANDING ITS PUBLIC SERVICES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE HIRING A FULL-TIME PROJECT ARCHIVIST TO ASSIST WITH INVENTORYING, ACCESSIONING, CATALOGING, AND REHOUSING COLLECTIONS; CREATING AND UPDATING FINDING AIDS; CREATING A DIGITAL PLATFORM FOR PUBLIC ACCESS; AND HOSTING PROGRAMS TO INTRODUCE THE PUBLIC TO NEW ONLINE METHODS FOR ACCESSING THE COLLECTIONS. PROJECT FUNDING WILL ALSO ENABLE MEBA TO REACTIVATE ITS STUDENT TRAINING PROGRAM INSPIRING AUTHORITIES IN MUSEUM MANAGEMENT. PAID INTERNSHIPS FOR TWELVE STUDENTS WILL PROVIDE TRAINING IN ARCHIVAL MANAGEMENT AND DIGITIZATION TO SUPPORT PROJECT ACTIVITIES. THROUGH THIS PROJECT, MEBA WILL ESTABLISH LONG-TERM ARCHIVAL MANAGEMENT POLICIES, EXPAND THE USE OF ITS COLLECTION BY RESEARCHERS, AND BUILD PROFESSIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND NETWORKS FOR EMERGING PROFESSIONALS.
description.3889: THE JIM CROW MUSEUM OF RACIST IMAGERY AT FERRIS STATE UNIVERSITY WILL DESIGN AND INSTALL A NEW PERMANENT EXHIBIT ON ITS BIG RAPIDS, MICHIGAN CAMPUS TO CREATE MORE ACCESSIBLE, ENGAGING, AND ROBUST EXPERIENCES FOR STUDENTS, EDUCATORS, RESEARCHERS, AND THE PUBLIC. THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH AN EXHIBIT CONSULTANT TO DESIGN AND FABRICATE A NEW EXHIBIT THAT WILL INCLUDE NEW STORIES FOCUSED ON JIM CROW AND CIVIL RIGHTS IN MICHIGAN AND BUILDING A MORE JUST SOCIETY. THE EXHIBIT WILL EXPAND THE MUSEUM’S CAPACITY TO SERVE A BROADER AND MORE DIVERSE AUDIENCE THROUGH EXPANDED PHYSICAL SPACE AND IN-PERSON PROGRAMMING. THE NEW EXHIBITION WILL ENABLE THE JIM CROW MUSEUM OF RACIST IMAGERY TO ENHANCE ITS ROLE AS A FORUM FOR DIFFICULT DISCUSSIONS AS GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS SEEK TO UNDERSTAND THE HISTORY OF RACE AND RACISM IN AMERICA.
description.3890: THE ASSOCIATION OF AFRICAN AMERICAN MUSEUMS (AAAM) WILL EXPAND ITS EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP TRAINING PROGRAM IN COLLABORATION WITH THE HOWARD UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF BUSINESS. BUILDING ON A SUCCESSFUL PILOT PROGRAM, AAAM WILL OFFER THE LEADERSHIP TRAINING PROGRAM TO 25 PARTICIPANTS PER YEAR SELECTED FROM MID-LEVEL AND SENIOR-LEVEL MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS AND LEADERS. THE PROGRAM INCLUDES IN-PERSON ACTIVITIES AT THE ANNUAL CONFERENCE, ENGAGEMENT IN SIX STRATEGIC MODULES, AND A COLLABORATIVE CAPSTONE PROJECT. PARTICIPANTS WILL GAIN KNOWLEDGE AND INSIGHTS ABOUT NON-PROFIT MANAGEMENT AND LEADERSHIP AND EXPAND THEIR NETWORK OF COLLEAGUES AND FACULTY MEMBERS FOR LIFE-LONG LEARNING AND SUPPORT. PARTICIPANTS WHO COMPLETE THE PROGRAM WILL RECEIVE A JOINT CERTIFICATE FROM AAAM AND HOWARD UNIVERSITY. THE PROJECT ENABLES AAAM TO PROVIDE HIGH-QUALITY, AFFORDABLE EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP TRAINING FOR MUSEUM STAFF TO HELP THEM LEAD THEIR INSTITUTIONS TO A STRONGER, MORE SUSTAINABLE FUTURE.
description.3891: THE HOSANNA SCHOOL MUSEUM WILL BUILD CAPACITY TO EXPAND ACCESS TO ITS SITES AND COLLECTIONS BY HIRING A NEW FULL-TIME ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR POSITION AND CREATING A PAID INTERNSHIP PROGRAM. THE INCREASED STAFF CAPACITY WILL LEAD TO THE CREATION OF GRADE-SPECIFIC MATERIALS COVERING THE PERIOD OF SLAVERY TO RECONSTRUCTION IN HARFORD COUNTY AND ACROSS THE NATION; A RELATED TRUNK SHOW FOR IN-CLASS PRE-VISIT PRESENTATIONS; TRAVELING EXHIBITIONS FOR SCHOOLS AND PUBLIC BUILDINGS; EXPERIENTIAL BUS TOURS; UNDERGROUND RAILROAD IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCES; FIELD TRIPS TO RELEVANT SITES OF MEMORY; WALKING TOURS THROUGH HISTORICALLY IMPACTFUL COMMUNITIES; FILM SCREENINGS; PANEL DISCUSSIONS; AND DOCENT TRAINING. THROUGH EXPANDED PROGRAMMING AND NEW EXHIBITS THIS PROJECT WILL ENGAGE THE PUBLIC IN LEARNING ABOUT AFRICAN AMERICANS’ QUEST FOR EDUCATION IN THE RECONSTRUCTION ERA AFTER THE AMERICAN CIVIL WAR AND PROVIDE CONSISTENT ACCESS TO THE HOSANNA SCHOOL MUSEUM AND MCCOMAS INSTITUTE, A LANDMARK FREEDMEN’S BUREAU SCHOOLHOUSE SITE.
description.3892: ELIZABETH CITY STATE UNIVERSITY (ECSU) WILL RESEARCH, DESIGN, FABRICATE, AND INSTALL EXHIBITS THAT WILL INTERPRET AFRICAN AMERICANS’ COMMITMENT TO EDUCATION AS A CIVIL RIGHT AND THE STRUGGLE FOR EQUALITY THROUGH THE PURSUIT OF EDUCATION IN NORTHEASTERN NORTH CAROLINA. THE EXHIBITS WILL BE INSTALLED IN A REHABILITATED ROSENWALD SCHOOL BUILDING AND PRINCIPAL’S HOUSE, BOTH BUILT IN 1922, WHICH ARE NOW PART OF THE ECSU CAMPUS. THE EXHIBITS WILL INTERPRET THE FOLLOWING THEMES: AFRICAN AMERICAN EDUCATION FROM RECONSTRUCTION TO THE CIVIL RIGHTS ERA; ROSENWALD SCHOOL BUILDING PROGRAM; TEACHER EDUCATION AT ELIZABETH CITY STATE COLORED NORMAL SCHOOL; AND ECSU ROSENWALD SCHOOL BUILDING HISTORY. EXHIBIT CREATION WILL INCLUDE AN EDUCATIONAL COMPONENT THAT WILL BENEFIT ECSU FACULTY, LIBRARY STAFF, AND STUDENTS WHO WILL DEVELOP SKILLS RELATED TO RESEARCHING AND DESIGNING INTERPRETIVE EXHIBITS.
description.3893: THE CLEMSON AREA AFRICAN AMERICAN MUSEUM (CAAAM) WILL EXPAND STAFF CAPACITY AND SUPPORT PAID INTERNSHIPS TO COLLECT, PRESERVE AND MAKE AVAILABLE ORAL HISTORIES FROM AFRICAN AMERICANS IN PICKENS COUNTY, SOUTH CAROLINA. THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE HOSTING TWO WORKSHOPS ON FAMILY LEGACY PRESERVATION AND FIVE OPEN FORUM DISCUSSIONS DESIGNED TO ENCOURAGE COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND OWNERSHIP OF THE ORAL HISTORY PROJECT. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A DIGITIZED AND TRANSCRIBED SET OF ORAL HISTORIES DOCUMENTING AFRICAN AMERICANS IN UPSTATE, SC. STAFF WILL USE THESE ORAL HISTORIES AS THE CORE OF A NEW TRAVELING EXHIBIT, PUBLISH SELECTIONS AS A BOOKLET OF THE STORIES COLLECTED AND MAKE THESE RESOURCES AVAILABLE TO RESEARCHERS. CAAAM HOPES TO INSPIRE AND ENCOURAGE COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO PRESERVE THEIR FAMILY HISTORY BY PROVIDING FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING OF BEST PRACTICES FOR THE PRESERVATION OF THEIR FAMILY’S LEGACY.
description.3894: THE HAMPTON UNIVERSITY MUSEUM WILL INCREASE THE VISIBILITY AND ACCESSIBILITY OF THE AFRICAN ART COLLECTION BY IMPLEMENTING THE NEXT PHASE OF ITS COLLECTION MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE PROJECT. A COLLECTIONS DATA MANAGER WILL BE HIRED TO WORK WITH MUSEUM STAFF AND PAID INTERNS TO MANAGE THE PROCESS OF MOVING FROM A PAPER-BASED RECORD KEEPING SYSTEM TO AN EFFICIENT, UPDATED DIGITAL SYSTEM. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING A FULL INVENTORY OF THE AFRICAN COLLECTION, PHOTOGRAPHING INDIVIDUAL ITEMS, SCANNING CURATORIAL RECORDS, ADDING DATA AND RECORDS TO THE COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, AND CREATING TWO ONLINE EXHIBITIONS. AS A RESULT, THE MUSEUM WILL HAVE THE ABILITY TO SHARE COLLECTIONS ONLINE, WHILE KEEPING DATA SAFE AND SECURE, AND ACCESSIBLE FOR EDUCATORS, STUDENTS, OTHER MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3895: THE NATIONAL BLUES MUSEUM (NBM) WILL UNDERTAKE A COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND STRATEGIC PLANNING PROCESS TO IDENTIFY MUSEUM SERVICES AND PROGRAMMING BEST ALIGNED WITH THE NEEDS AND INTERESTS OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS. NBM WILL HIRE A MANAGER OF COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT TO LEAD THE PROJECT AND WORK IN COLLABORATION WITH RESEARCH AND STRATEGIC PLANNING CONSULTANTS. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE A COMMUNITY SURVEY, THE DEVELOPMENT OF PILOT PROGRAMS AND ENHANCEMENTS TO CURRENT PROGRAMS, AND CODIFYING DIFFERENT COMMUNITY NEEDS TO MEASURE SUCCESSFUL ENGAGEMENT. A FOLLOW-UP COMMUNITY SURVEY WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TOWARD THE END OF THE PROJECT TO GATHER DATA ON THE SUCCESS OF NEW PROGRAMS AND THE MUSEUM’S COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT ON A LARGE SCALE. THESE INTERRELATED FORMS OF DATA AND TESTIMONY WILL INFORM A NEW COMPREHENSIVE STRATEGIC PLAN. NBM’S PLAN WILL REFLECT THE GROWING ROLE OF MUSEUMS AS SITES FOR COMMUNITY BUILDING, SERVICE, AND CIVIC ENGAGEMENT.
description.3896: THE SPELMAN COLLEGE MUSEUM OF ART PROPOSES A PROJECT TO CARE FOR THE COLLECTION OF ART WHILE OFFERING OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS OF HBCUS TO GAIN EXPERIENCE IN COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT AND CARE. MUSEUMS STAFF WILL INVENTORY AND APPRAISE WORKS, CREATE PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL OBJECT FILES, RE-ORGANIZE ART STORAGE, AND ADD DATA AND IMAGES TO A SEARCHABLE ONLINE DATABASE. WORK STUDY AND INTERNSHIP OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS AT THE ATLANTA UNIVERSITY CENTER WILL OFFER HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE CATALOGING AND ORGANIZING THE COLLECTION. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE CONSULTANTS AND EDUCATORS TO FOSTER COLLABORATIONS WITH INSTITUTIONS AND CULTIVATE COLLECTION FOCUSED EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES TO TRAIN STUDENTS IN CONSERVATION ETHICS, MUSEUM BEST PRACTICES, AND COLLECTIONS CARE. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO THE SPELMAN MUSEUM COLLECTION AND CREATE OPPORTUNITIES FOR GREATER DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION IN THE COLLECTIONS CARE AND MANAGEMENT PROFESSION.
description.3897: THE HARRIS COUNTY CULTURAL ARTS COUNCIL (HCCAC) WILL ENGAGE THE EAST HARRIS COUNTY COMMUNITY IN EXPLORING THE RITUALS, CUSTOMS, TRADITIONS, AND HISTORY OF AFRICAN AMERICAN FUNERALS. HCCAC WILL COLLABORATE WITH WRITERS AND ARTISTS TO DEVELOP A VISUAL EXHIBIT AND STAGE PLAY THAT WILL PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE PUBLIC TO LEARN THE HISTORY ASSOCIATED WITH FUNERAL RITUALS AND EXPAND UNDERSTANDING ABOUT AN IMPORTANT ELEMENT OF AFRICAN AMERICAN CULTURE. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT INTERVIEWS, CONTENT RESEARCH AND RELATED DIGITAL PRODUCTS WILL BE DEVELOPED IN YEAR ONE WITH PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS TAKING PLACE IN YEAR TWO. PANEL DISCUSSIONS WILL BE HELD WITH PROFESSIONALS IN THE FUNERAL INDUSTRY, CLERGY, AND THE GENERAL COMMUNITY AS PART OF THE OVERALL PROGRAM. THE COMMUNITY WILL BENEFIT FROM INCREASED PUBLIC DIALOGUE AND ENGAGEMENT AND A BROADENED UNDERSTANDING OF AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY AND CULTURE.
description.3898: THE WILLOW HILL HERITAGE AND RENAISSANCE CENTER IN COLLABORATION WITH THE GEORGIA SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF HISTORY WILL INCREASE DIGITIZATION AND ENSURE GREATER ACCESSIBILITY TO ITS COLLECTION OF 15,000 AFRICAN AMERICAN FUNERAL PROGRAMS. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT TWO PAID STUDENT INTERNS AND A PAID COMMUNITY ARCHIVES MANAGER TO DIGITIZE, DESCRIBE, AND UPLOAD FUNERAL PROGRAMS TO THE DIGITAL COMMONS AT GEORGIA SOUTHERN, AN OPEN-ACCESS ONLINE REPOSITORY. INTERNS WILL RECEIVE TRAINING IN SCANNING TECHNIQUES AND CREATING METADATA FOR EACH DOCUMENT, WHICH OFTEN CONTAIN SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION NOT AVAILABLE ELSEWHERE, SUCH AS WORKPLACE, EDUCATION HISTORY, CHURCH AFFILIATION, AND ORGANIZATION MEMBERSHIP. STAFF WILL MENTOR THE STUDENT INTERNS FOR FUTURE JOBS AS PROFESSIONAL MUSEUM PERSONNEL. THE PROJECT PROVIDES A TRAINING OPPORTUNITY FOR STUDENTS AND GENERATES A SIGNIFICANT INCREASE IN ACCESS TO THIS UNIQUE COLLECTION OF PRIMARY SOURCE MATERIALS.
description.3899: THE WORLD BEAT CULTURAL CENTER WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, EXPAND ACCESS TO ARCHIVAL DATA, AND PRESERVE RECORDINGS OF THE CULTURAL TRADITIONS AND DIALECTS OF MAROON SOCIETIES THAT PROVIDED SANCTUARY FOR BLACK SEMINOLES AND MASCOGOS WHO FLED TO MEXICO FOR THEIR FREEDOM. WBCC WILL DEVELOP A MODULAR EXHIBITION OF THE UNDERGROUND RAILROAD SOUTH THAT CENTERS THE EXPERIENCE OF BLACK SEMINOLE, GULLAH GEECHEE, MASCOGOS, AND MAROON SOCIETIES. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT MUSEUM STAFF AND PAID UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE INTERNS IN GATHERING ARCHIVAL DATA THROUGH MULTIGENERATIONAL INTERVIEWS THAT WILL DOCUMENT CULTURAL TRADITIONS AND LINGUISTIC VARIATIONS. THROUGH THESE COMMUNITY-BASED RESEARCH ACTIVITIES AND THE RESULTING EXHIBITION, THE WBCC INTENDS TO EDUCATE, ENRICH, AND EMPOWER MUSEUM VISITORS AS WELL AS THE DESCENDANTS OF EACH GROUP WHILE ARCHIVING AND PRESERVING LINGUISTIC AND CULTURAL DATA.
description.3900: THE LAWNSIDE HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL DIGITIZE ITS ARCHIVE OF DOCUMENTS AND DEVELOP COLLECTIONS FINDING AIDS FOR ITS COLLECTIONS RELATED TO AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY, INCLUDING UNDERGROUND RAILROAD, CIVIL RIGHTS, AND GREEN BOOK HISTORIES. STAFF WILL WORK WITH LOCAL UNIVERSITY STUDENTS TO DIGITIZE THE ARCHIVE AND UTILIZE A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM TO CATALOG MATERIALS, PRIORITIZING THE DIGITIZATION OF PHYSICALLY UNSTABLE DOCUMENTS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL MAKE DIGITIZED COLLECTIONS AND FINDINGS AIDS ACCESSIBLE TO THE PUBLIC ONLINE. PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL BE SCHOLARS OF AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY AND GENEALOGICAL RESEARCHERS.
description.3901: DIASPORA VIBE CULTURAL ARTS INCUBATOR WILL IMPROVE ORGANIZATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY THROUGH INCREASED HIRING AND THE CREATION OF ORGANIZATIONAL GUIDES. THE INSTITUTION WILL HIRE A PART-TIME GRADUATE STUDENT TO RECEIVE TRAINING, CREATE ORGANIZATIONAL AND TECHNICAL GUIDANCE, AND WORK CLOSELY WITH STAFF ON PROGRAMMATIC ACTIVITIES FOCUSING ON THE LATIN AND CARIBBEAN DIASPORA. INFORMED BY DIASPORA VIBE CULTURAL ARTS INCUBATOR’S STRATEGIC PLAN, STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONSULTANT TO CREATE AN ORGANIZATIONAL EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS PLAN FOR ONGOING SUSTAINABILITY. STAFF WILL ATTEND CONFERENCES FOR PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND SHARE PROJECT RESULTS., BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE STAFF, BOARD OF DIRECTORS, AND ARTIST INTERNS.
description.3902: THE AMISTAD RESEARCH CENTER WILL INCREASE PUBLIC ACCESS TO AND ENHANCE STEWARDSHIP OF ITS COLLECTIONS OF ARCHIVAL, DIGITAL, AND LIBRARY HOLDINGS. FOR THE PROJECT, THE INSTITUTION WILL HIRE A FULL-TIME REFERENCE ARCHIVIST TO ASSIST RESEARCH SERVICES AND ADDRESS A BACKLOG IN COPY AND ORIGINAL CATALOGING OF BOOKS AND RARE PUBLICATIONS. THE INSTITUTION WILL ALSO HIRE A FULL-TIME METADATA SPECIALIST TO ADDRESS COLLECTIONS METADATA REMEDIATION FOR THE LEGACY DIGITAL AMERICAN MISSIONARY ASSOCIATION PHOTOGRAPHS COLLECTION. STAFF WILL RECEIVE TRAINING ON CATALOGING PROCEDURES AND PROTOCOLS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE DIGITIZED ARCHIVES AND LIBRARY COLLECTIONS DOCUMENTING OVER 150 YEARS OF AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY AND CULTURE WILL BE AVAILABLE ONLINE FOR PUBLIC ACCESS.
description.3903: THE LEGACY MUSEUM AT TUSKEGEE UNIVERSITY WILL IMPROVE THE STEWARDSHIP OF ITS COLLECTION BY REHOUSING OBJECTS IN ITS ART AND BIOETHICS COLLECTIONS. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTOR TO PURCHASE AND INSTALL ARCHIVAL SHELVING UNITS AND STORAGE SYSTEM. STAFF WILL REHOUSE OBJECTS USING ARCHIVAL MATERIALS AND ACCESSION COLLECTIONS AS THEY BECOME PHYSICALLY ACCESSIBLE. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, IMPROVED STORAGE WILL ALLOW FOR INCREASED ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION AND WILL CREATE ADDITIONAL SPACE FOR STAFF TO PERFORM ROUTINE COLLECTIONS PRESERVATION AND EXHIBITION PREPARATION ACTIVITIES. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE FACULTY, STUDENTS, STUDENT INTERNS, AND OUTSIDE RESEARCHERS.
description.3904: THE CHRISTIANSBURG INSTITUTE WILL IMPLEMENT PROGRAMMING IN LOCAL HIGH SCHOOLS AND CREATE AN INTERNSHIP PROGRAM. THE CHRISTIANSBURG INSTITUTE (1866-1966) WAS FOUNDED AS A SCHOOL, LED BY BOOKER T. WASHINGTON. TODAY, THE CHRISTIANBURG INSTITUTE HOLDS THOUSANDS OF RECORDS THAT REPRESENT THE EXPERIENCES OF AFRICAN AMERICANS IN SOUTHWEST VIRGINIA. WORKING WITH HISTORICALLY BLACK COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES (HBCUS), CHRISTIANSBURG INSTITUTE WILL OFFER PAID, REMOTE INTERNSHIPS FOR STUDENTS TO LEARN DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT AND CATALOG THE INSTITUTE’S COLLECTION. PROGRAMMING DEVELOPED FOR LOCAL HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS WILL INCLUDE INTERNSHIPS, WORKSHOPS, IN-CLASSROOM VISITS, AND NEWLY CREATED LESSON PLANS. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL ALSO DEVELOP A TRAVELING EXHIBIT RELATED TO CHRISTIANBURG INSTITUTE TO BE HOSTED AT VARIOUS HBCUS.
description.3905: THE ANDERSON CENTER FOR THE ARTS WILL CREATE A TRAVELING EXHIBITION AND FREE BOOK EXCHANGE LIBRARY FEATURING WORKS WRITTEN BY BLACK AUTHORS. WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS, THE ANDERSON CENTER FOR THE ARTS WILL ORGANIZE EXHIBITIONS AND PROGRAMS AT PARTNER SITES, SUCH AS AUTHOR TALKS, PERFORMANCES, BOOK AND POETRY READINGS, AND VISUAL ART EXHIBITIONS. THE FREE BOOK EXCHANGE LIBRARY WILL BE INSTALLED FOR A YEAR AT A PARTNER SITE. THE INSTITUTION WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTED CURATOR TO ORGANIZE THE TRAVELING EXHIBITIONS AND MANAGE THE BOOK EXCHANGE, INCLUDING DEVELOPING A LENDING SYSTEM AND CATALOGING AND TRACKING BOOKS.
description.3906: THE ISLAND SOCIETY FOR THE PROMOTION OF ARTISTIC AND CULTURAL EDUCATION (ISLAND SPACE) WILL PRODUCE PROGRAMS TO EDUCATE AUDIENCES ABOUT THE ARTS, CULTURE, AND HISTORY OF THE CARIBBEAN REGION, IN SOUTH FLORIDA AND THE BROADER DIASPORA COMMUNITY. IN COLLABORATION WITH OTHER CARIBBEAN CULTURAL ORGANIZATION PARTNERS, THE INSTITUTION WILL PRODUCE A SERIES OF PROGRAMMATIC EVENTS, SUCH AS WORKSHOPS, PANEL DISCUSSIONS, AND PERFORMANCES. IN PARTNERSHIP WITH CARIBBEAN CONSULATES, STAFF WILL HOST A BOOK FAIR FEATURING LOCAL CARIBBEAN AUTHORS AND WILL LIVE STREAM THE PROGRAM TO ENCOURAGE VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION AND EXPAND PROGRAM AUDIENCES. ISLAND SPACE WILL ALSO HOST A CHILDREN’S READING FESTIVAL DURING CARIBBEAN-AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH. PROGRAM PARTNERS WILL INCLUDE MEMBERS OF THE ENGLISH, SPANISH, FRENCH, AND DUTCH-SPEAKING CARIBBEAN.
description.3907: THE BANNEKER-DOUGLASS MUSEUM WILL IDENTIFY LINEAL DESCENDANTS OR COMMUNITIES THAT ARE CULTURALLY AFFILIATED WITH THE REMAINS OF 13 INDIVIDUALS OF AFRICAN DESCENT THAT ARE CURRENTLY HOUSED AT THE MARYLAND ARCHAEOLOGICAL CONSERVATION LABORATORY IN CALVERT COUNTY, MARYLAND. IN COLLABORATION WITH MARYLAND HISTORICAL TRUST, MARYLAND COMMISSION ON AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY AND CULTURE STAFF WILL CONDUCT DNA ANALYSIS AND RESEARCH LOCAL HISTORY TO DETERMINE LINEAL DESCENDANTS. WITH THE PERMISSION OF DESCENDANTS, PROJECT STAFF WILL COMMISSION FACIAL RECONSTRUCTIONS OF THE DECEASED INDIVIDUALS AND COORDINATE REBURIAL CEREMONIES. A UNIVERSITY RESEARCH FELLOW WILL ASSIST PROJECT STAFF IN CREATING A LOCAL HISTORY RESEARCH REPORT, WHICH WILL BE MADE ACCESSIBLE ONLINE FOR A PUBLIC AUDIENCE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL INVITE DESCENDANTS TO ASSOCIATED PROGRAMMING AND LEAD PUBLIC WORKSHOPS ON HOW TO CONDUCT GENEALOGICAL RESEARCH.
description.3908: THE MICHIGAN STREET AFRICAN AMERICAN HERITAGE CORRIDOR COMMISSION WILL INCREASE STAFF CAPACITY AND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS FOR FIVE HISTORIC LOCATIONS: THE MICHIGAN STREET BAPTIST CHURCH, NASH HOUSE MUSEUM, HISTORIC COLORED MUSICIANS CLUB AND JAZZ MUSEUM, WUFO 1080 AM BLACK RADIO HISTORY COLLECTIVE, AND MICHIGAN STREET AFRICAN AMERICAN HERITAGE CORRIDOR. FOR THE PROJECT, THE ORGANIZATION WILL HIRE A NEW FULL-TIME MUSEUM COLLECTIONS AND INTERPRETIVE ASSISTANT TO IMPROVE COLLECTIONS CARE AND ACCESS. THE MUSEUM COLLECTIONS AND INTERPRETIVE ASSISTANT WILL ALSO DEVELOP AND COORDINATE EXHIBITION CONTENT AND PROGRAMMING. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE LOCAL RESIDENTS, STUDENTS, AND RESEARCHERS OF ABOLITIONIST AND AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORIES OF BUFFALO.
description.3909: THE HARVEY B. GANTT CENTER FOR AFRICAN-AMERICAN ARTS + CULTURE WILL IMPROVE COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP BY MIGRATING ITS COLLECTIONS INVENTORY INTO A NEW COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE AND CUSTOMIZING ARTIFACT STORAGE. THE COLLECTION INCLUDES PAINTINGS, WORKS ON PAPER, PHOTOGRAPHS, BOOKS, AND HISTORICAL DOCUMENTS. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL PURCHASE AND IMPLEMENT THE NEW COLLECTIONS DATABASE SYSTEM, WHICH WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION FOR EXHIBITION AND RESEARCH PURPOSES. STAFF WILL ALSO PURCHASE CUSTOM CRATES TO PROTECT AND STORE OBJECTS FROM THE PERMANENT COLLECTION AND EXPAND THE INSTITUTION’S CAPACITY TO LOAN OBJECTS FOR EXHIBITION TO OTHER INSTITUTIONS.
description.3910: THE CENTER FOR AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY & CULTURE AT VIRGINIA UNION UNIVERSITY WILL DIGITIZE AND PROVIDE PUBLIC ACCESS TO THE HARTSHORN MEMORIAL COLLEGE COLLECTION FROM THE ARCHIVES AND SPECIAL COLLECTIONS AT THE L. DOUGLAS WILDER LIBRARY. THE COLLECTION DOCUMENTS THE HISTORY OF HARTSHORN MEMORIAL COLLEGE, A WOMEN’S COLLEGE AND HISTORICALLY BLACK COLLEGE THAT MERGED WITH VIRGINIA UNION UNIVERSITY IN 1932, AND CONTAINS ARCHIVAL MATERIALS AND PRIMARY RESOURCES SUCH AS DOCUMENTS, CATALOGS, PHOTOGRAPHS, AND CORRESPONDENCE. PROJECT STAFF WILL TRAIN AND WORK WITH PAID STUDENT INTERNS TO DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION AND PROVIDE PUBLIC ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION THROUGH AN ONLINE DATABASE. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE RESEARCHERS AND SCHOLARS OF HBCU AND WOMEN’S HISTORY.
description.3911: THE PAULI MURRAY CENTER FOR HISTORY & SOCIAL JUSTICE WILL CREATE AN EXHIBIT ABOUT PAULI MURRAY, A CIVIL RIGHTS AND LGBTQ+ ACTIVIST. WITHIN MURRAY’S CHILDHOOD HOME, THE MULTIMEDIA EXHIBIT WILL HIGHLIGHT MURRAY’S LEADERSHIP ROLES IN LEGAL ADVOCACY IN CASES SUCH AS BROWN V. BOARD OF EDUCATION AND THE 1964 CIVIL RIGHTS ACT. STAFF WILL CONDUCT INTERPRETIVE COMMUNITY PROGRAMS AND DEVELOP EDUCATIONAL CURRICULUM RELATED TO THE EXHIBIT. THE INSTITUTION WILL HIRE A PART-TIME PUBLIC HISTORIAN, AND STAFF WILL WORK WITH PAID, GRADUATE STUDENT INTERNS. STAFF WILL SHARE THE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT AT A PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCE.
description.3912: THE ALEXANDRIA BLACK HISTORY MUSEUM WILL DIGITIZE MATERIALS DOCUMENTING ALEXANDRIA’S AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY, INCLUDING APPROXIMATELY 1,500 RECORDS FROM ITS OBJECT COLLECTION AS WELL AS THE CATALOG OF APPROXIMATELY 4,000 VOLUMES IN THE WATSON READING ROOM. FOR THE PROJECT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL UPDATE AND STANDARDIZE INFORMATION AND DOCUMENTATION ACROSS DIGITAL AND PHYSICAL FORMATS AS WELL AS ADD RECORDS AND PHOTOGRAPHS TO MISSING OR INCOMPLETE MATERIALS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL MAKE COLLECTIONS MATERIALS SUCH AS PHOTOGRAPHS, DOCUMENTS, AND RARE BOOKS ACCESSIBLE ONLINE. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE EDUCATORS, SCHOLARS, AND PUBLIC RESEARCHERS.
description.3913: THE AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY RESEARCH CENTER AT HOUSTON PUBLIC LIBRARY WILL DIGITIZE AND MAKE ACCESSIBLE VULNERABLE MATERIALS FROM ITS COLLECTION RELATED TO THE AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY OF HOUSTON, INCLUDING ARCHIVED AUDIO, VIDEO, AND ORAL HISTORY RECORDINGS. FOR THE PROJECT, THE INSTITUTION WILL HIRE A FULL-TIME CONTRACT PROJECT ARCHIVIST WHO WILL COORDINATE WITH AN EXTERNAL VENDOR TO PROCESS AND DIGITIZE OVER 1,400 AUDIOVISUAL ITEMS FROM THE ARCHIVE. STAFF WILL PROVIDE TRAINING TO THE PROJECT ARCHIVIST ON METADATA STANDARDS AND THE CREATION OF ORAL HISTORY TRANSCRIPTS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL SHARE AND MAKE THE PRESERVED MATERIALS AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC THROUGH LIBRARY AND MUSEUM EXHIBITS, COMMUNITY EVENTS, AND ONLINE AND PRINTED PUBLICATIONS.
description.3914: THE DRISKELL CENTER WILL INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY OF THREE OF ITS ARCHIVAL COLLECTIONS FROM AFRICAN AMERICAN ARTISTS. THE COLLECTIONS CONTAIN THE PAPERS OF ARTIST ALONZO DAVIS, FOCUSING ON DAVIS’ PERSONAL ART CAREER AND PUBLIC ART COMMISSIONS; INTERVIEWS, FIELD NOTES, AND PHOTOGRAPHIC PRINTS OF ARTIST AND SCHOLAR MICHAEL D. HARRIS, FOCUSING ON HARRIS’ STUDY IN ILE-IFE, NIGERIA; AND THE DOCUMENTS OF ARTIST ROBIN HOLDER PERTAINING TO THE ARTIST’S CAREER IN PRINTMAKING, PUBLIC ART, AND ART EDUCATION IN NEW YORK CITY. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL TRAIN AND WORK WITH EIGHT PAID GRADUATE STUDENTS FROM THE UNIVERSITY’S LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE PROGRAM TO CATALOG AND DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION FOR ONLINE PUBLIC ACCESS. PROJECT STAFF WILL REHOUSE OBJECTS IN ARCHIVAL STORAGE CONTAINERS TO IMPROVE LONG-TERM PRESERVATION OF THE COLLECTION.
description.3915: THE EVANSVILLE AFRICAN AMERICAN MUSEUM WILL OFFER EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS FOR YOUTH IN GRADES 6–12 WITH VISUAL, PERFORMING, AND LITERARY ARTISTS AND EDUCATORS. THE PROGRAM, CALLED THE COVE (CONNECTION, OPPORTUNITY, VISUAL ARTS, EXPRESSION) PROJECT WILL INCLUDE 25 YOUTH PARTICIPANTS, WHO WILL PARTICIPATE IN COMMUNITY-BASED ARTS.  STAFF WILL WORK WITH TWO PAID COLLEGE STUDENT INTERNS TO DEVELOP AND COORDINATE THE PROGRAMS. PROJECT STAFF WILL PROVIDE YOUTH PARTICIPANTS WITH INDIVIDUALIZED AND SMALL GROUP INSTRUCTION IN VARIOUS TYPES OF INSTRUMENTATION, VOCAL TRAINING, AND HANDS-ON VISUAL ARTS AS WELL AS FACILITATE YOUTH PARTICIPANT RECITALS, PLAYS, AND EXHIBITIONS.
description.3916: WEEKSVILLE HERITAGE CENTER WILL COMPLETE A COMPREHENSIVE COLLECTIONS INVENTORY AND INCREASE PUBLIC ACCESS BOTH ONSITE AND ONLINE TO ITS COLLECTIONS DOCUMENTING THE HISTORY OF WEEKSVILLE, ONE OF THE LARGEST FREE BLACK COMMUNITIES IN PRE-CIVIL WAR AMERICA. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL HIRE A NEW COLLECTIONS ASSOCIATE POSITION AND TWO PAID INTERNS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE COMPILING EXISTING INVENTORIES, CATALOGING ITEMS THAT ARE NOT YET ACCESSIONED, IMPROVING SAFE COLLECTIONS STORAGE, RESTRUCTURING DIGITAL RECORDS, AND DIGITIZING HIGH-PRIORITY ITEMS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL EXPAND PUBLIC ACCESS TO THE COLLECTIONS VIA A PUBLIC DATABASE PORTAL, ENHANCED EXHIBITION DISPLAYS, AND AN ONSITE RESOURCE CENTER WITH EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES FOR RESEARCHERS, MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS.
description.3917: THE LEWIS LATIMER HOUSE MUSEUM WILL HIRE STAFF TO IMPROVE COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT AND CREATE A DIGITAL EXHIBITION FROM THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION. IN PARTNERSHIP WITH QUEENS PUBLIC LIBRARY, MUSEUM STAFF WILL DIGITIZE THE LATIMER FAMILY PAPERS. FOR THE PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A COLLECTIONS DIGITIZATION MANAGER, WHO WILL TRAIN AND SUPERVISE PAID INTERNS ON DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. THE MUSEUM WILL ALSO HIRE A DIGITIZATION SPECIALIST TO IMPLEMENT COLLECTIONS DIGITIZATION SOFTWARE. STAFF WILL TRAVEL TO CONDUCT COLLECTIONS RESEARCH, WHICH WILL INFORM THE CREATION OF A DIGITAL EXHIBITION OF THE MUSEUM’S PERMANENT COLLECTION. THE DIGITAL EXHIBITION WILL BE AVAILABLE ON THE MUSEUM’S WEBSITE AS A FREE, PUBLIC RESOURCE.
description.3918: THE ALABAMA AFRICAN AMERICAN CIVIL RIGHTS HERITAGE SITES CONSORTIUM (AAACRHSC) WILL EXPAND ITS SUMMER INTERNSHIPS AND YOUTH LEADERSHIP COLLABORATIVE INITIATIVES. STAFF WILL WORK WITH REGIONAL HIGH SCHOOLS TO RECRUIT 30 HIGH SCHOOL INTERNS IN BIRMINGHAM, MONTGOMERY, AND SELMA. UPON COMPLETION OF THEIR INTERNSHIPS, INTERNS WILL BE INVITED TO JOIN THE GATEWAY YOUTH LEADERSHIP COLLABORATIVE AND COLLABORATE WITH STAFF AND THEIR FELLOW COHORTS TO RESEARCH, WRITE, AND PRODUCE TRAVELING MUSEUM EXHIBITIONS. THE EXHIBITIONS WILL ADDRESS CIVIL RIGHTS HISTORY, INCLUDE ORAL HISTORIES, AND FEATURE TOPICS SUCH AS THE VOTING RIGHTS ACT OF 1965 IN SELMA, AND THE INTERSTATE COMMERCE ACT OF 1885 IN MONTGOMERY.
description.3919: THE BASTROP COUNTY AFRICAN AMERICAN CULTURAL CENTER WILL BUILD STAFF CAPACITY FOR PROGRAMMING AND EXHIBITION DEVELOPMENT. FOR THE PROJECT, THE CENTER WILL HIRE A PART-TIME PROGRAMS COORDINATOR TO MANAGE COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAMS, INCLUDING A BLACK BASTROP HISTORY WALKING TOUR. STAFF WILL WORK WITH VOLUNTEERS AND A PAID INTERN TO COLLECT TWELVE ORAL HISTORIES FROM BASTROP DESCENDANT COMMUNITY ELDERS, WHICH WILL BE UTILIZED IN EXHIBITIONS AND PROGRAMMING. ADDITIONALLY, DESCENDANT FAMILIES WILL BE INVITED TO BRING FAMILY LETTERS, PHOTOGRAPHS, OR DOCUMENTS TO BE PROFESSIONALLY SCANNED FOR HISTORIC PRESERVATION. EXHIBITIONS WILL FEATURE A TOUCH-SCREEN COMPUTER TO MAKE THE ORAL HISTORIES AVAILABLE TO VISITORS, AND ORAL HISTORIES WILL BE FEATURED IN AUDIO NARRATIVE DESCRIPTIONS GENERATED FOR THE WALKING TOUR.
description.3920: MOTOWN HISTORICAL MUSEUM WILL IMPROVE THE ARCHIVAL REPOSITORY FOR ITS COLLECTION OF OVER 20,000 OBJECTS THAT DOCUMENT MOTOWN HISTORY. FOR THE PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A REGISTRAR AND A PREPARATOR TO WORK WITH STAFF TO UPDATE COLLECTIONS RECORDS, CONDUCT ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING, AND SUPERVISE THE INSTALLATION OF ARCHIVAL STORAGE UNITS. BY RELOCATING THE OBJECTS INTO THE ARCHIVAL STORAGE UNITS IN A NEW LOCATION, THE MUSEUM WILL MITIGATE ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS TO THE COLLECTION AND IMPROVE THE ACCESSIBILITY OF THE COLLECTION FOR MUSEUM STAFF. BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE SCHOLARS, MUSICIANS, AND PUBLIC RESEARCHERS OF MOTOWN HISTORY.
description.3921: THE NATIONAL UNDERGROUND RAILROAD FREEDOM CENTER WILL CREATE A NEW PERMANENT EXHIBITION EXAMINING THE HISTORICAL ROOTS OF SOCIAL JUSTICE MOVEMENTS IN THE UNITED STATES, FROM TIME OF THE UNDERGROUND RAILROAD TO THE PRESENT DAY. STAFF WILL WORK WITH AN ARCHITECTURAL FIRM TO PRODUCE EXHIBIT MATERIALS, SUCH AS EXHIBIT FURNITURE, GRAPHICS, AND AUDIOVISUAL DISPLAYS. TO DEVELOP THE EXHIBITION, STAFF WILL ENGAGE THREE PANELS OF HISTORIANS, SCHOLARS, ARTISTS, ACTIVISTS, AND COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS OVER THE COURSE OF THREE YEARS. COINCIDING WITH THE OPENING OF THE EXHIBITION, AN ACCOMPANYING ONE-DAY SYMPOSIUM WILL FEATURE GUEST SCHOLAR SPEAKERS. STAFF WILL SHARE PROJECT RESULTS AT BOTH A REGIONAL AND A NATIONAL CONFERENCE.
description.3922: THE WITHERS COLLECTION MUSEUM AND GALLERY WILL ENHANCE STEWARDSHIP OF ITS COLLECTION BY ARCHIVALLY STORING AND DIGITIZING PHOTOGRAPHS FROM ITS COLLECTION TAKEN BY PHOTOJOURNALIST EARNEST C. WITHERS THAT DOCUMENT CIVIL RIGHTS HISTORY AS WELL AS AFRICAN AMERICAN LIFE AND CULTURE. FOR THE PROJECT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL PURCHASE COLLECTIONS STORAGE AND UPDATE PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL ARCHIVES. STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTOR TO DIGITIZE APPROXIMATELY 4,000 IMAGES AND UPLOAD THEM TO AN ONLINE, PUBLIC PLATFORM. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL MAKE THE PHOTOGRAPHS MORE ACCESSIBLE FOR BOTH INTERNAL USE AS WELL AS USE FOR PUBLIC PROGRAMMING, EXHIBITIONS, AND RESEARCH.
description.3923: THE MUSEUM OF AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY WILL DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT EXPERIENTIAL TOURS AND PROGRAMS FOR SCHOOLS, FAMILIES AND ADULTS IN BOSTON AND ON THE ISLAND OF NANTUCKET. FOR THE PROJECT, THE INSTITUTION WILL HIRE ONE FULL-TIME OUTREACH POSITION AND THREE FULL-TIME EDUCATION POSITIONS. STAFF WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A SCHOOL FIELD TRIP PROGRAM, CREATE INTERPRETIVE MATERIALS FOR MUSEUM EXHIBITS, AND CONDUCT PROGRAMS AT EACH OF THE MUSEUM’S FOUR HISTORIC SITES. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL PRODUCE A COMMUNICATION PLAN, CURRICULUM MATERIALS, PROGRAM MODELS, AND INTERPRETIVE PLANS AND DEVICES FOR ADULT AND FAMILY PROGRAMS.
description.3924: THE CHARLES H. WRIGHT MUSEUM OF AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY WILL CREATE LEADERSHIP PROGRAMS FOR EMERGING MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS. THESE OPPORTUNITIES WILL INCLUDE AN EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP FELLOWSHIP AND A COLLECTIONS AND ARCHIVES FELLOWSHIP. FOR THE EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP FELLOWSHIP, STAFF WILL CONSULT WITH EXPERIENCED ARTS LEADERS TO RESEARCH AND DESIGN THE FELLOWSHIP FRAMEWORK. THE COLLECTIONS AND ARCHIVES FELLOW WILL ASSIST IN THE MANAGEMENT OF THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION AS WELL AS EXHIBITION PLANNING. STAFF WILL ALSO LAUNCH TRAINING MODULES FOR CROSS-DEPARTMENTAL TRAINING FOR GRADUATE STUDENT FELLOWS AS WELL AS PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL TRAINING FOR MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS ACROSS THE COUNTRY.
description.3925: THE DUSABLE BLACK HISTORY MUSEUM & EDUCATION CENTER WILL CREATE A DIGITAL CATALOG AND FINDING AID FOR ITS COLLECTION OF OVER 1,000 BOXES OF MATERIALS RELATED TO THE HISTORY OF CIVIC ENGAGEMENT OF AFRICAN AMERICANS IN CHICAGO. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL MOVE MATERIALS OUT OF STORAGE AND REHOUSE MATERIALS IN A CLIMATE-CONTROLLED ENVIRONMENT. STAFF WILL ALSO WORK WITH VOLUNTEERS, INTERNS, AND A PAID ARCHIVIST FELLOW. AN ARCHIVIST CONSULTANT WILL PROCESS AND CATALOG ARCHIVED MATERIALS AS WELL AS TRAIN STAFF ON THE MAINTENANCE OF DIGITAL SYSTEMS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL HAVE INCREASED ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION FOR USE IN PROGRAMMING AND EXHIBITIONS, AS WELL AS PROVIDING INCREASED ACCESS FOR PARTNER ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3926: THE JACK HADLEY BLACK HISTORY MUSEUM WILL DEVELOP AND PRODUCE AUDIO GUIDES AND MUSEUM EXHIBITS TO ENGAGE YOUTH AUDIENCES WITH THE AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY OF SOUTHWEST GEORGIA. BASED ON NEEDS IDENTIFIED IN A PREVIOUS AUDIENCE ASSESSMENT AND IN PREVIOUS VISITOR SURVEYS, STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTED DESIGN FIRM TO CREATE EXHIBITS THAT UTILIZE AUDIO-VISUAL TECHNOLOGY FOR A CUSTOMIZABLE AND IMMERSIVE VISITOR EXPERIENCE. FOR EXHIBITION CONTENT, STAFF WILL BUILD UPON WORK COMPLETED IN A PREVIOUS IMLS GRANT TO COLLECT THE ORAL HISTORIES OF JACK HADLEY AS MATERIAL. STAFF WILL PRESENT AT PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCES TO SHARE THE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT WITH THE MUSEUM FIELD. PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL BE SCHOOL GROUPS VISITING THE MUSEUM.
description.3927: THE CROW TRIBE WILL LAUNCH A STRATEGIC PLANNING INITIATIVE TO GUIDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A CULTURAL CENTER ON THE CAMPUS OF LITTLE BIG HORN COLLEGE. A MASTER PLANNER AND AN ARCHITECT WILL LEAD THE PROCESS, AND EACH STAGE WILL INVOLVE STUDENTS, FACULTY AND STAFF, CROW COMMUNITY MEMBERS, AND OTHER INTERESTED PARTIES THROUGH SURVEYS AND COMMUNITY MEETINGS. BEYOND STAKEHOLDERS' INPUT, ROTATING MEMBERS OF THE PLANNING COMMITTEE WILL VISIT FOUR CULTURAL CENTERS TO SEE FIRST-HAND HOW OTHER INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES HAVE DEVELOPED THEIR CULTURAL CENTERS. THE WORK TEAM WILL USE THE ACCUMULATED DATA TO GUIDE THE PRODUCTION OF A STRATEGIC PLAN AND THE FINAL CONCEPT PLAN. THE CULTURAL CENTER WILL SERVE AS AN ACCESS POINT ALONG WITH THE TRIBAL LIBRARY AND ARCHIVES TO PERPETUATE CROW CULTURE AND HISTORY THROUGH ROTATING DISPLAYS AND CULTURAL ACTIVITIES ON A REGULAR BASIS.
description.3928: THE HAWAII STATE ARCHIVES WILL IMPROVE THE PRESERVATION AND ACCESSIBILITY OF ITS COLLECTION OF NEGATIVES DOCUMENTING THE HISTORY, HERITAGE, AND CULTURE OF NATIVE HAWAIIANS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DIGITIZE OVER 22,000 FRAGILE AND DETERIORATING 19TH AND EARLY 20TH CENTURY NEGATIVES, MANY OF WHICH HAVE BEEN PULLED FROM PUBLIC ACCESS DUE TO DAMAGE AND SIGNS OF SEVERE DETERIORATION. THE DIGITAL IMAGES WILL LIVE IN A FREELY ACCESSIBLE, CENTRALIZED, BI-LINGUAL (''LELO HAWAI'I'HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE'AND ENGLISH), SEARCHABLE ONLINE PUBLIC ACCESS DATABASE. TWO HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE GRADUATE STUDENT INTERNS WILL ASSIST WITH DIGITIZATION WORK AND TRANSCRIBING DESCRIPTIVE METADATA.
description.3929: BUILDING ON COMPLETED STRATEGIC AND ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR A TRIBAL CULTURAL CENTER/MUSEUM, THE TWENTY-NINE PALMS BAND OF MISSION INDIANS WILL CREATE AN EXHIBIT PLAN AS THE NEXT STEP IN ITS EFFORTS TO RETAIN TRADITIONAL CULTURE AND SHARE ITS HISTORY WITH THE LOCAL COMMUNITY AND OTHERS. THE TRIBE WILL WORK WITH A MUSEUM CONSULTING FIRM AND CONDUCT A COMMUNITY SURVEY TO DEVELOP A DRAFT PLAN FOR EXHIBIT CONFIGURATION. THE TRIBE WILL ALSO ESTABLISH COOPERATIVE RELATIONSHIPS WITH A VARIETY OF PARTNERS TO RECEIVE SHARED CONTENT, EXHIBITS, OR ARTIFACTS WHICH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE CULTURAL CENTER/MUSEUM’S EXHIBITS TO PROVIDE A HOLISTIC VIEW OF THE BREADTH OF CHEMEHUEVI CULTURE. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN A COMPREHENSIVE EXHIBIT PLAN AND ASSOCIATED DESIGN BOARDS FEATURING THE CORE CONCEPTS OF THE EXHIBITS AS WELL AS DESIGN ELEMENTS SUCH AS FONTS, MATERIALS, COLOR PALETTE, TEXTURES, AND CULTURAL MOTIFS.
description.3930: THREE CHIEFS CULTURE CENTER OF THE CONFEDERATED SALISH AND KOOTENAI TRIBES WILL RESTORE AND REHOUSE ARTIFACTS DAMAGED BY AN ARSON FIRE IN 2020. THE PROJECT WILL FUND OBJECT CONSERVATION, ENVIRONMENTAL IMPROVEMENTS, AND FIRESAFE STORAGE FOR THE COLLECTION. A CONSERVATOR AND AN APPRAISER WILL ASSIST STAFF IN THE RESTORATION AND PRESERVATION OF DAMAGED CULTURAL RESOURCES OF THE BITTERROOT SALISH, UPPER PEND D’OREILLE, AND KOOTENAI PEOPLE. STAFF WILL UPDATE THE COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT POLICY, PARTICIPATE IN DATABASE TRAINING, DIGITIZE RECORDS AND COLLECTION MATERIALS, TRANSFER VIDEO AND DIGITAL MEDIA, CONDUCT APPRAISALS, AND COMPLETE THE CATALOGING OF RECORDS. THIS PROJECT WILL ENHANCE THE TRIBE’S ABILITY TO CARE FOR ITS COLLECTIONS, BENEFITTING BOTH TRIBAL AND NON-TRIBAL COMMUNITIES.
description.3931: THE YAVAPAI-APACHE NATION CULTURAL CENTER WILL STRENGTHEN ITS SERVICES BY IMPLEMENTING IMPROVEMENTS IN COLLECTIONS CARE AND PROGRAMMING. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE AN EVALUATION OF THE CENTER’S CLIMATE CONTROL SYSTEM TO ENSURE THE LONG-TERM PRESERVATION OF COLLECTION ITEMS IN STORAGE AND ON DISPLAY. STAFF WILL UPGRADE SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT TO SUPPORT ONGOING LANGUAGE PRESERVATION AND ORAL HISTORY PROGRAMMING. TRIBAL MEMBERS WILL ALSO TRAVEL TO FIVE DIFFERENT LOCATIONS AROUND THE COUNTRY TO RESEARCH, IDENTIFY, AND EXAMINE ITEMS THAT HAVE THE POTENTIAL FOR REPATRIATION AND CARE BY THE NATION. REPAIRS TO THE CENTER’S POTTERY WHEEL WILL SUPPORT ITS USE FOR DEMONSTRATIONS, CLASSES, AND POTTERY MAKING. VISITORS, INCLUDING TRIBAL MEMBERS, THE LOCAL VERDE VALLEY COMMUNITY, AND NON-LOCAL TOURISTS, WILL BENEFIT FROM INCREASED ACCESS TO THE NATION’S PRESERVED HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL MATERIALS.
description.3932: THE KANZA MUSEUM AND THE KANZA LIBRARY AND LEARNING CENTER WILL PROVIDE A SERIES OF PROGRAMS FOCUSED ON INCREASING NATIVE COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT THROUGH THE TEACHING OF TRADITIONAL ARTS AND CRAFTS. A TRIBAL ELDER WILL TEACH CULTURAL HISTORY TO PARTICIPANTS, AS WELL AS TRADITIONAL METHODS OF MAKING TRIBAL ITEMS AND REGALIA, INCLUDING MOCCASINS, FRINGE SHAWLS, JEWELRY, RIBBON SKIRTS, AND SHIRTS. THEY WILL INFUSE THE PROGRAMS WITH KAÁⁿZE ÍE, THE KAW LANGUAGE, AND DISPLAY CRAFTED ITEMS MADE BY PARTICIPANTS AT FASHION SHOWS AND CULTURAL EVENTS. PARTICIPATING KAW TRIBAL CITIZENS AND INTERESTED NON-NATIVE COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL LEARN TRIBAL LANGUAGE, HISTORY, AND CULTURE, INCREASING A SENSE OF TRIBAL COMMUNITY AND PRIDE, AND HELPING PRESERVE TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE.
description.3933: THE DELAWARE NATION WILL PARTNER WITH THE 3D SCANNING LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA LIBRARIES TO PRODUCE HIGH-QUALITY, HIGH-RESOLUTION 3D MODELS OF THE NATION’S ARCHIVAL AND MUSEUM ARTIFACTS. A CLOUD-BASED STORAGE SYSTEM AND DIGITAL CATALOG WILL PROVIDE CITIZENS AND RESEARCHERS ONLINE ACCESS TO THE IMAGES OF THE 3D MODELS, WHICH WILL ALSO BE DISPLAYED ON-SITE FOR VISITORS TO THE DELAWARE NATION LIBRARY. THE DIGITIZATION OF ARTIFACTS WILL PROVIDE BROADER ACCESS TO INFORMATION ABOUT THE COLLECTION AND THE CULTURAL HISTORY OF THE LENAPE PEOPLE, AND WILL SERVE AS THE FOUNDATION FOR A FUTURE, FULLY INTERACTIVE ONLINE MUSEUM.
description.3934: THE NEZ PERCE TRIBE WILL CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE FEASIBILITY STUDY IN ORDER TO GAIN AN UNDERSTANDING OF POTENTIAL OPTIONS FOR UTILIZING A NEWLY ACQUIRED PROPERTY AS THE FUTURE SITE OF THE TRIBE’S FIRST MUSEUM AND CULTURAL CENTER. THE AM’SAÁXPA (“PLACE OF BOULDERS”) PROPERTY, LOCATED IN THE HEART OF THE NEZ PERCE TRIBE’S TRADITIONAL HOMELAND, IS A HISTORIC PROPERTY IN JOSEPH, OREGON, FORMERLY A NEZ PERCE TRIBAL VILLAGE SITE OCCUPIED BY CHIEF JOSEPH, WHO IS BURIED NEARBY. ADDITIONAL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PURCHASING EXHIBIT CASES AND DEVELOPING A TEMPORARY EXHIBIT OF REPLICA ARTIFACTS, WHICH WILL INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF THE TRIBE TO SERVE ITS MEMBERS, THE LOCAL PUBLIC, AND ALL THOSE INTERESTED IN LEARNING ABOUT THE NEZ PERCE PEOPLE.
description.3935: THE AH-TAH-THI-KI MUSEUM OF THE SEMINOLE TRIBE OF FLORIDA WILL RESEARCH AND DIGITALLY CATALOG A COLLECTION OF HISTORIC NEWSPAPERS FROM THE 18TH AND 19TH CENTURIES. BUILDING ON AN EARLIER GRANT AWARD TO IMPROVE CATALOG RECORDS AND CREATE A FINDING AID, THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A RESEARCH ASSISTANT TO SCAN AND GENERATE HIGH-RESOLUTION, SEARCHABLE IMAGES FOR HUNDREDS OF NEWSPAPERS, WHICH WILL THEN BE MADE PUBLICLY AVAILABLE TO NATIVE AND WORLDWIDE RESEARCH COMMUNITIES AS A ROBUST DIGITAL ARCHIVE. THE UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA ACCESS 3D LAB WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL TRAINING AND ACCESS TO THE EQUIPMENT NECESSARY TO COMPLETE THE PROJECT. A MUSEUM NEWSLETTER WILL SHARE PROJECT UPDATES AND RESULTS RELATED TO THE PRESERVATION AND ACCESS OF THIS HISTORIC MATERIAL.
description.3936: THE WIYOT TRIBE WILL DEVELOP MAPS OF THE PLACE NAMES OF ANCESTRAL TERRITORY IN THE NATIVE WIYOT LANGUAGE OF SOULATLUK. UTILIZING MAPPING AND ANALYTICS SOFTWARE, A PUBLIC-FACING MAP WILL CONTAIN PLACE NAMES AND LOCATIONS THAT ARE NOT CULTURALLY SENSITIVE, WHILE A SEPARATE TRIBAL-USE VERSION WILL CONTAIN ALL DOCUMENTED PLACE NAMES. FOCUSED ARCHIVAL AND FIELD RESEARCH TO RECOVER THESE PLACE NAMES AND ACCURATELY LOCATE THEM WITHIN ANCESTRAL LANDS WILL RESULT IN PUBLISHED BROCHURES AND LARGE FORMAT PRINTED MAPS FOR EXHIBITION. THE MAPS WILL SERVE AS AN ONGOING RESOURCE FOR TRIBAL MEMBERS TO RECLAIM AND CARE FOR THEIR LANGUAGE AND ANCESTRAL LANDS AS WELL AS FOR RESIDENTS OF THE ANCESTRAL WIYOT TERRITORY TO LEARN ABOUT WIYOT LAND STEWARDSHIP, CULTURE, AND THE SOULATLUK LANGUAGE.
description.3937: THE TWENTY-NINE PALMS BAND OF MISSION INDIANS WILL CONTINUE AN ONGOING PROJECT TO DEVELOP A CULTURAL CENTER AND MUSEUM THAT WILL SERVE AS A PLACE WHERE ITS MEMBERS CAN COME TOGETHER TO PRACTICE, CELEBRATE, AND PASS ON THEIR CULTURAL HERITAGE. THE TRIBE WILL SELECT AND HIRE A CONSULTANT TO DEVELOP A FINANCIAL PLAN THAT WILL GUIDE MUSEUM OPERATIONS AND INTEGRATE ITS MISSION, VISION, AND VALUES WITH SHORT- AND LONG-TERM FINANCIAL PLANNING, FUNDRAISING, AND MARKETING. PLANNING FOR STABLE FISCAL MANAGEMENT FOR THE MUSEUM WILL ENABLE MUSEUM LEADERS TO LEVERAGE RESOURCES AND MAKE DECISIONS WITH GREATER CONFIDENCE. THE FUTURE MUSEUM WILL SERVE TRIBAL AND LOCAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS WHILE PRESERVING THE CULTURAL LEGACY, LIVING TRADITIONS, KNOWLEDGE, AND LANGUAGE THAT MAKE UP CHEMEHUEVI CULTURE.
description.3938: NINILCHIK VILLAGE WILL IMPLEMENT A PLANNING PROJECT THAT SUPPORTS THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE TRIBE’S NEW CULTURAL INSTITUTION, THE Q’ESCHIŁ HERITAGE CENTER. ESTABLISHING A TRIBALLY OWNED AND OPERATED MUSEUM AND CULTURAL CENTER WILL ENABLE NINILCHIK VILLAGE TO MAINTAIN AND MANAGE ITS OWN VOICE TO EDUCATE AND COMMUNICATE ITS HISTORY, CULTURE, AND IDENTITY TO THE COMMUNITIES OF THE LOWER KENAI PENINSULA REGION AND BEYOND. PROJECT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT STAFF AS THEY DEVELOP POLICY AND GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE PLANS, LAUNCH HERITAGE OUTREACH EFFORTS, AND FINALIZE EXHIBIT DESIGN PLANS IN PREPARATION FOR THE CULTURAL CENTER'S CONSTRUCTION.
description.3939: THE BUENA VISTA RANCHERIA OF ME-WUK INDIANS WILL ORGANIZE THE ARCHEOLOGICAL COLLECTIONS HOUSED AT THE UPUSANI CULTURAL CENTER TO AID IN THE CURATION AND EXHIBITION OF COLLECTIONS. THEY WILL HIRE A COLLECTIONS SPECIALIST TO HELP PROCESS, CATALOG, AND PRESERVE THE ARCHEOLOGICAL COLLECTION UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE TRIBAL HISTORIC PRESERVATION OFFICER AND AN ADVISORY BOARD. THE TRIBE WILL HOLD PROGRAMMATIC EVENTS ASSOCIATED WITH THE COLLECTION THROUGHOUT THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT FOR TRIBAL MEMBERS, GUESTS, AND THE SURROUNDING COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE ARCHEOLOGICAL COLLECTION AS A RESOURCE IN BOTH PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL FORMATS, AND RESULT IN THE PROTECTION AND ADVANCEMENT OF TRIBAL HISTORICAL KNOWLEDGE AND CULTURAL PRACTICES.
description.3940: THE OJIBWE LEARNING CENTER AND LIBRARY (OLCL) WILL DEVELOP AN ARTS PROGRAM TO IDENTIFY AND SUPPORT ANISHINAABE ART AND ARTISTS TO STRENGTHEN THEIR ABILITY TO BUILD, MAINTAIN, AND PRESERVE CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING AN ARTS NEEDS ASSESSMENT SURVEY, ESTABLISHING AN ARTS ADVISORY GROUP, AND DEVELOPING ART WORKSHOP PROGRAMMING. THE PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE UNDER-SERVED AND UNDER-RECOGNIZED ANISHINAABE ARTISTS WITH PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES, HELP BUILD THEIR SKILLS WHILE DEVELOPING AVENUES FOR FINANCIAL SUPPORT, CONNECT MENTORS AND MENTEES, AND ENCOURAGE THE EMERGENCE OF A NEW GENERATION OF ANISHINAABE ARTISTS. AS A RESULT, THE OLCL WILL FURTHER ITS MISSION TO EDUCATE THE COMMUNITY ABOUT THEIR CULTURE, SUPPORT CULTURAL PRESERVATION EFFORTS, AND PROVIDE A PLATFORM FOR REMATRIATING CULTURAL AND ARTISTIC PRACTICES.
description.3941: THE KAHOʻOLAWE ISLAND RESERVE COMMISSION (KIRC), UNDER THE HAWAII DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES, WILL ADVANCE STEWARDSHIP AND ACCESS TO ITS COLLECTIONS, WHICH INCLUDE NATURAL, CULTURAL, HISTORICAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND ARCHEOLOGICAL RESOURCES. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE UPGRADING HARDLINE SERVICES AND TECHNICAL HARDWARE TO A CLOUD-BASED SYSTEM AND INCREASING ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY BY PROVIDING STAFF WITH THE ABILITY TO WORK BOTH ON-SITE AND REMOTELY FROM THREE DIFFERENT ISLANDS. THE UPGRADES WILL ENABLE THE KIRC TO OFFER INCREASED ACCESS TO DIGITAL RESOURCES, SUCH AS THE LIVING LIBRARY PLATFORM AND DATABASE, THE KAHOʻOLAWE ISLAND GUIDE APP, LIVE-STREAMING VIDEO, AND A KAHOʻOLAWE VIRTUAL REALITY HUAKAʻI. AS A RESULT, LOCAL AND NATIVE HAWAIIAN COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS THE GENERAL PUBLIC WILL HAVE SAFE AND MEANINGFUL PHYSICAL AND VIRTUAL ENGAGEMENT WITH THE KIRC’S RESOURCES.
description.3942: THE BAD RIVER BAND OF LAKE SUPERIOR TRIBE OF CHIPPEWA INDIANS WILL INITIATE OPERATIONS AND COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT PROCEDURES TO SUPPORT THE OPENING OF ITS NEW MOKA'AANGIIZIS (“RISING SUN”) TRIBAL MUSEUM. THE TRIBE WILL HIRE A MUSEUM MANAGER WHO WILL LEAD THE MUSEUM THROUGH ITS GRAND OPENING, DEVELOP INITIAL POLICIES AND PROCEDURES, AND ESTABLISH A VOLUNTEER VISITOR SERVICES PROGRAM. ADDITIONAL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A COLLECTIONS DATABASE AND THE PRODUCTION OF VIRTUAL MUSEUM RESOURCES, SUCH AS WEBSITE UPDATES, AN ONLINE NEWSLETTER, AND A VIRTUAL EXHIBIT. COUPLING THESE EFFORTS WITH ONGOING LONG-RANGE PLANNING WILL BUILD AND SUSTAIN PROFESSIONAL MUSEUM ACTIVITIES AND HELP ESTABLISH THE MUSEUM AS A VIBRANT CULTURAL CENTER FOR THE BAD RIVER BAND TRIBAL COMMUNITY AND BEYOND.
description.3943: THE CITIZEN POTAWATOMI NATION CULTURAL HERITAGE CENTER WILL CREATE TEN OUTDOOR EDUCATIONAL DISPLAYS AT SITES OF HISTORICAL OR CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE AROUND THE NATION’S PUBLIC GROUNDS. THE SIGNAGE WILL BE EQUIPPED WITH QR CODES TO ACCESS A SELF-DIRECTED ALTERNATE REALITY (AR) CONTENT DELIVERY PLATFORM, PROVIDING INFORMATION ON POTAWATOMI HISTORY AND CULTURE VIA VISITORS’ PERSONAL DEVICES. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT DESIGNING, PRINTING, AND INSTALLING THE TEN DISPLAYS, AS WELL AS PRODUCING 2D AND 3D CONTENT FOR USE IN THE AR PLATFORM. AS A RESULT OF THE NEW DISPLAYS, POTAWATOMI TRIBAL MEMBERS, OTHER NATIVE AMERICAN COMMUNITY MEMBERS, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC WILL INCREASE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING OF POTAWATOMI ORIGINS, HISTORY, AND CULTURE.
description.3944: ELK VALLEY RANCHERIA WILL IMPROVE THE CARE, MANAGEMENT, AND LONG-TERM PRESERVATION OF ITS COLLECTION OF ETHNOGRAPHIC ITEMS, LITHICS AND STONE TOOLS, DOCUMENTS, AND BOOKS. DRAWING ON RECOMMENDATIONS FROM A 2015 CONSERVATION SURVEY AND ASSESSMENT, THE TRIBE WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL MUSEUM-QUALITY DISPLAY CASES THAT PROTECT THE COLLECTIONS FROM CHANGES IN TEMPERATURE, RELATIVE HUMIDITY, AND ULTRAVIOLET LIGHT. HOUSING THE TRIBE’S CULTURAL MATERIALS, WHICH INCLUDE OVER 100 HISTORICAL BASKETS, IN NEW CASES WILL PRESERVE THEM FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS AND ENABLE BOTH NATIVE AND NON-NATIVE MEMBERS OF THE SURROUNDING COMMUNITY TO CONTINUE TO VISIT AND LEARN ABOUT THE LIFEWAYS, VALUES, AND HISTORY OF ELK VALLEY RANCHERIA.
description.3945: KONIAG, INC. WILL DESIGN AND PUBLISH A BOOK THAT CELEBRATES THE LIVING ARTISTIC TRADITIONS OF THE KODIAK ALUTIIQ PEOPLE BY SHARING THE CONTEMPORARY NATIVE ART COLLECTIONS OF TWO COMMUNITY MUSEUMS – THE ALUTIIQ MUSEUM AND THE KODIAK HISTORY MUSEUM. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL IDENTIFY ARTISTS AND ARTWORKS FOR INCLUSION IN THE BOOK, PHOTOGRAPH AND PROCESS IMAGES, OBTAIN USE PERMISSIONS, RESEARCH AND WRITE ARTIST BIOGRAPHIES AND SHORT ESSAYS, AND DESIGN THE LAYOUT. UPON PUBLICATION, 1000 COPIES WILL BE PRINTED AND DISTRIBUTED FOR FREE THROUGHOUT THE COMMUNITY AND A DIGITAL COPY WILL BE SHARED ON THE ALUTIIQ MUSEUM’S WEBSITE. THE RESULTING BOOK WILL ILLUSTRATE THE RICH ARTISTIC TRADITIONS OF ALUTIIQ HISTORY, CULTURE, AND EXPERIENCE, WHILE SUPPORTING NATIVE ARTISTS, INCREASING PUBLIC AWARENESS OF CONTEMPORARY NATIVE ARTS, AND ENHANCING THE DOCUMENTATION OF THESE COLLECTIONS.
description.3946: KAW NATION’S KANZA MUSEUM WILL IMPROVE THE CARE AND MANAGEMENT OF ITS COLLECTION BY IMPLEMENTING A COLLECTIONS INVENTORY AND CATALOGING PROJECT TO PRESERVE AND PROTECT KANZA ARTIFACTS, PHOTOS, GLASS SIDES, AND OTHER ITEMS OF CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE HIRING AND MENTORING A NEW COLLECTIONS CARE SPECIALIST WHO WILL INVENTORY THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION, CREATE AND IMPLEMENT A CATALOG SYSTEM, AND PROCURE ARCHIVAL QUALITY MATERIALS TO REHOUSE AND STORE ITEMS. AS A RESULT, THE TRIBE WILL BE BETTER ABLE TO SAFEGUARD AND PRESERVE THE ITEMS AND THEIR RELATED HISTORICAL INFORMATION ON THE KANZA PEOPLE FOR FUTURE REFERENCE, EXHIBITION, AND USE BY MUSEUM STAFF, TRIBAL MEMBERS, AND THE COMMUNITY.
description.3947: THE BISHOP MUSEUM WILL IMPLEMENT A PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR MUSEUM STAFF AT SMALL AND MID-SIZED MUSEUMS IN HAWAI‘I TO ADDRESS THE NEED FOR MENTORSHIP AND TRAINING AND TO BUILD AN ONGOING NETWORK FOR PEER LEARNING AND SUPPORT FOR MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS IN HAWAI‘I. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DESIGNING, DEVELOPING, AND DELIVERING A MENTORSHIP PROGRAM TO COHORTS OF MULTIPLE PARTICIPANTS THAT IS TARGETED TOWARDS UNDERSTANDING THE NON-PROFIT CULTURE IN HAWAI‘I, AND CUSTOMIZED TO THE NEEDS OF NATIVE HAWAIIANS AND HAWAI‘I-BASED MUSEUMS. PARTICIPANTS IN THE PROGRAM WILL DEVELOP KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND CAPACITY IN THE WORK THEY DO, ENABLING THEM TO STRENGTHEN PROGRAMS AND INCREASE SUPPORT FOR THE COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE.
description.3948: HUI MAULI OLA WILL PARTNER WITH NATIVE HAWAIIAN HEALING MASTERS TO ETHICALLY GATHER, STORE, ORGANIZE, CURATE, AND MAKE ACCESSIBLE DOCUMENTS AND RESOURCES PERTAINING TO TRADITIONAL NATIVE HAWAIIAN HEALING PRACTICES VIA A DIGITAL ARCHIVE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING PROTOCOLS FOR ETHICAL DATA STEWARDSHIP DETERMINED BY THE NATIVE HAWAIIAN HEALING COMMUNITY; COLLECTING AND DIGITIZING MATERIALS FOR INCLUSION IN THE DATABASE; AND DEVELOPING AND PUBLISHING THE DIGITAL ARCHIVE. THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A FOUNDATIONAL SYSTEM OF DOCUMENTING AND TRACING NATIVE HAWAIIAN TRADITIONAL HEALING KNOWLEDGE WHILE INCREASING NATIVE HAWAIIAN ARCHIVAL INFRASTRUCTURE CAPACITY, BENEFITING STUDENTS, THE COMMUNITY OF HAWAI‘I, NATIVE HAWAIIANS, AND OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDERS.
description.3949: THE BAY MILLS INDIAN COMMUNITY WILL RECRUIT AND HIRE A FULL-TIME STAFF PERSON TO ORGANIZE, CATALOG, AND DIGITIZE THE TRIBAL HISTORY DEPARTMENT'S COLLECTION OF ARTIFACTS, PHOTOS, AND DOCUMENTS. ONCE INVENTORIED AND ORGANIZED, THE HISTORICAL COLLECTIONS WILL BE MORE ACCESSIBLE TO TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND WILL BE USED TO SHARE ACCURATE AND CULTURALLY RELEVANT HISTORY WITH VISITORS AT THE POINT IROQUOIS LIGHTHOUSE MUSEUM. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL ALSO DEVELOP A POLICIES AND PROCEDURES MANUAL FOR HANDLING, INVENTORYING, AND FILING HISTORICAL DOCUMENTS, RESULTING IN THE TRIBE BEING BETTER-ABLE TO PROTECT AND CONSERVE IMPORTANT CULTURAL AND HISTORIC ASSETS.
description.3950: THE FOREST COUNTY POTAWATOMI COMMUNITY CULTURAL CENTER, LIBRARY & MUSEUM WILL FABRICATE AND INSTALL TWO NEWLY DESIGNED OUTDOOR EXHIBITS AND PROVIDE RELATED PROGRAMMING TO RE-ENGAGE THE COMMUNITY IN THE WAKE OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. THE MUSEUM WILL FABRICATE AN AUTHENTIC MEDICINAL GARDEN AND TEACHING LODGE EXHIBIT USING TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNIQUES AS WELL AS COLLABORATE WITH TRIBAL ELDERS TO DEVELOP CULTURALLY SPECIFIC HANDS-ON EXPERIENCES FOR THE NEW SPACES. BY PROVIDING NEW IMMERSIVE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES ABOUT LIVING POTAWATOMI CULTURE AND TRADITIONS, THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASE IN COMMUNITY MEMBER PARTICIPATION IN MUSEUM PROGRAMMING AND WILL BENEFIT TRIBAL MEMBERS, DESCENDANTS, AND THEIR FAMILIES.
description.3951: KAWAIAHA'O CHURCH, HOUSED IN THE FIRST CHRISTIAN CHURCH BUILT ON OʻAHU, WILL HIRE AN ARCHIVIST TO OVERSEE THE MANAGEMENT OF ITS HISTORICAL SITES AND ARCHIVE LIBRARY AS THE CHURCH UNDERTAKES A MOLD REMEDIATION PROJECT. THE ARCHIVIST WILL HELP COORDINATE THE RELOCATION OF THE ARCHIVAL COLLECTION, OVERSEE CONTRACTORS PERFORMING MOLD REMEDIATION, AND WORK WITH THE PROJECT TEAM TO CONTINUE PROCESSING THE COLLECTIONS THROUGH ACTIVITIES SUCH AS CATALOGING, DIGITIZATION, AND RE-HOUSING. THEY WILL ALSO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT ARCHIVAL COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT POLICIES AND PROCEDURES TO SUPPORT THE LONG-TERM PRESERVATION AND CARE OF THIS HISTORICAL COLLECTION. AS A RESULT, NATIVE HAWAIIANS AND THE LARGER HAWAIʻI COMMUNITY WILL HAVE INCREASED ACCESS TO IMPORTANT CULTURAL AND HISTORICAL RECORDS, WHICH WILL BE BETTER PRESERVED FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS.
description.3952: THE INSTITUTE FOR NATIVE PACIFIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE (INPEACE) WILL DEVELOP AND DESIGN PLANS FOR A NEW LAWAIʻA (FISHING) STEM EXHIBIT THAT WILL HIGHLIGHT AND REINTRODUCE NATIVE HAWAIIAN FISHING TOOLS, STRATEGIES, AND TECHNIQUES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONSULTING WITH CULTURAL EXPERTS AND RESEARCHERS TO GATHER INFORMATION TO CREATE A REPOSITORY OF MATERIALS ABOUT NATIVE HAWAIIAN FISHING PRACTICES; CREATE A DESIGN REFERENCE GUIDE; DEVELOP CONCEPTUAL PLANS WITH COMMUNITY AND DESIGN EXPERTS; AND REFINE AND COMPLETE EXHIBIT LAYOUTS, SPECIFICATIONS, AND MATERIALS. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE OF THE TRADITIONAL AND CONTEMPORARY SCIENCE OF NATIVE HAWAIIAN FISHING PRACTICES WHILE SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN CULTIVATING STRATEGIES TO DEVELOP CULTURALLY RELEVANT AND INFORMED STEM EXPERIENCES.
description.3953: HULA PRESERVATION SOCIETY WILL DEVELOP FIVE VIRTUAL EXHIBITIONS THAT WILL ENABLE INCREASED INSIGHT AND UNDERSTANDING OF THE 20TH CENTURY IN HAWAIʻI. PROJECT STAFF AND PAID INTERNS WILL GATHER CONTENT AND DEVELOP THE DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE FIVE VIRTUAL EXHIBITS USING THE EXTENSIVE RESOURCES AVAILABLE IN THE SOCIETY’S DIGITAL ARCHIVES, DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT ASSOCIATED PUBLIC PROGRAMMING, AND LAUNCH A RELATED SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP ADDRESS MISCONCEPTIONS ABOUT HAWAIʻI HISTORY AND CULTURE BY PROVIDING INCREASED ACCESS TO AND INTERPRETATION OF OVER 700 MULTI-FORMAT PRIMARY SOURCE MATERIALS AND WILL BENEFIT NATIVE AND NON-NATIVE HAWAIIANS ALIKE BY PROVIDING AN OPPORTUNITY TO EXPERIENCE HAWAIʻI THROUGH THE EYES, HEADS, AND HEARTS OF NATIVE HAWAIIANS.
description.3954: THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF KWINHAGAK, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE NUNALLEQ MUSEUM IN QUINHAGAK, AK, WILL CREATE A DIGITAL MUSEUM GUIDE TO FACILITATE ON-SITE VISITOR EXPERIENCE OF THE MUSEUM’S ARCHAEOLOGICAL COLLECTION. THE DIGITAL GUIDE WILL FEATURE A RESPONSIVE MOBILE APPLICATION CONTAINING A SELECTION OF INTERACTIVE 3D ARTIFACTS FROM THE COLLECTION TOGETHER WITH CO-CURATED INTERPRETATIVE CONTENT FROM CLIMATE SCIENTISTS, ARCHAEOLOGISTS, YUP’IK CULTURE BEARERS, ARTISTS, AND ELDERS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE GATHERING RESOURCES FOR INCLUSION IN THE GUIDE, DEVELOPING THE BACK-END DATA STRUCTURE, PROTOTYPING AND BETA TESTING THE MOBILE APPLICATION, AND COLLECTING COMMUNITY FEEDBACK. AS A RESULT, THIS HISTORICALLY AND SCIENTIFICALLY SIGNIFICANT COLLECTION OF YUP’IK MATERIALS WILL BE BETTER PRESERVED, WHILE ALSO MORE ACCESSIBLE AND ENGAGING FOR MUSEUM VISITORS.
description.3955: THE GUN LAKE TRIBE WILL DEVELOP AND ENHANCE EXISTING AND UNDERUTILIZED EXHIBIT AREAS WITHIN THREE TRIBAL FACILITIES WITH THE DUAL GOAL OF IMPROVING THE CARE OF AND INCREASING COMMUNITY ACCESS TO MATERIALS FROM THE TRIBE’S ARCHIVES AND COLLECTIONS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE PURCHASING AND INSTALLING CLIMATE-CONTROLLED DISPLAY CASES, INSTALLING UV PROTECTION ON WINDOWS IN PUBLIC EXHIBIT AREAS, UPDATING EXHIBIT CONTENT WITH COMMUNITY INPUT, UPGRADING TO DIGITAL SIGNAGE, AND IDENTIFYING NEW OBJECTS FOR DISPLAY. THE UPDATED EXHIBITS WILL BETTER PROTECT AND PRESERVE THE TRIBE’S CULTURAL AND HISTORICAL COLLECTIONS, AS WELL AS INCREASE AWARENESS OF AND ENGAGEMENT WITH THE COLLECTIONS FOR TRIBAL CITIZENS, COMMUNITY MEMBERS, AND NON-TRIBAL VISITORS.
description.3956: THE NOTTAWASEPPI HURON BAND OF THE POTAWATOMI WILL PARTNER WITH THE BATTLE CREEK REGIONAL HISTORY MUSEUM IN BATTLE CREEK, MI TO CREATE A NEW CULTURAL HERITAGE LOBBY AT THE MUSEUM TO ADDRESS A GENERAL LACK OF EDUCATION AND AWARENESS ABOUT LOCAL TRIBAL HISTORY AND CULTURAL HERITAGE. THE RE-DESIGNED LOBBY WILL DISPLAY AN ORIGINAL MURAL BY A POTAWATOMI ARTIST, AS WELL AS THREE KIOSKS SET WITHIN CUSTOMIZED DECORATIVE BASES, SHOWCASING DIGITAL IMAGES AND CONTENT DISCUSSING POTAWATOMI HISTORY, LANGUAGE, AND LIFEWAYS. PROJECT FUNDS WILL COVER EXHIBITION CONTENT AND GRAPHIC DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, REVIEW, AND APPROVAL, AS WELL AS THE KIOSK FABRICATION AND INSTALLATION. BY FEATURING NATIVE VOICES AND MATERIALS, THE NEW LOBBY EXHIBIT WILL HELP INCREASE KNOWLEDGE AND UNDERSTANDING OF LOCAL TRIBAL HISTORY AND CULTURE FOR BOTH TRIBAL AND NON-TRIBAL CITIZENS OF SOUTHWESTERN MICHIGAN.
description.3957: THE IOWA TRIBE OF KANSAS AND NEBRASKA WILL ADDRESS CHALLENGES IT FACES IN OPERATING ITS NEWLY OPENED IOWA AND SAC & FOX MISSION MUSEUM, NAMELY, LACK OF ACCESS TO ARTIFACTS RELATED TO THE MISSION AND TRIBE’S HISTORY. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL IDENTIFY AND DOCUMENT CULTURALLY SIGNIFICANT ITEMS AND ARTWORK HELD BY NON-TRIBAL ENTITIES AND PARTNER WITH THOSE ENTITIES TO PHOTOGRAPH AND DIGITIZE THOSE ITEMS. MUSEUM STAFF WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN TRAINING AND PURCHASE NECESSARY COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE AND EQUIPMENT, BUILDING THE TRIBE’S CAPACITY TO PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL MUSEUM SERVICES. THE RESULTING VIRTUAL REPOSITORY WILL BENEFIT TRIBAL MEMBERS, STUDENTS, EDUCATORS, AND RESEARCHERS BY PROVIDING GREATER ACCESS TO IOWA AND SAC & FOX HISTORICAL INFORMATION AND MATERIAL CULTURE.
description.3958: THE CHOCTAW CULTURAL CENTER WILL PRESERVE COLLECTIONS AND PERPETUATE TRADITIONAL CULTURAL PRACTICES BY RECREATING AT-RISK TEXTILES AND PROVIDING PROGRAMMING FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO LEARN ABOUT CHOCTAW TEXTILE PRACTICES. THE CENTER WILL COLLABORATE WITH CHOCTAW TRADITIONAL ARTISANS, WHO WILL CREATE 10 TO 15 DUPLICATE TEXTILE ITEMS TO BE USED FOR DISPLAY ROTATION, HELPING TO COMBAT DETERIORATION AND STRAIN ON TEXTILES FEATURED IN THE CENTER’S PERMANENT EXHIBIT. THE CENTER WILL ALSO EXPAND UPON ITS CURRENT PUBLIC PROGRAMMING BY OFFERING MASTERCLASS OPPORTUNITIES WITH THE ARTISANS AND ADDITIONAL EDUCATIONAL SEMINARS AND DEMONSTRATIONS FOR TRIBAL MEMBERS, STUDENTS, TEACHERS, AND THE COMMUNITY. AS A RESULT, COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL BE MORE KNOWLEDGEABLE ABOUT TRADITIONAL CHOCTAW TEXTILES AND THE LIVES OF CURRENT COLLECTION ITEMS WILL BE EXTENDED FOR CONTINUED DISPLAY.
description.3959: THE MYAAMIA HERITAGE MUSEUM & ARCHIVE WILL REVAMP AND INSTALL ITS COMMUNITY CURATED MYAAMIA RIBBONWORK EXHIBIT. FIRST DISPLAYED AT THE MIAMI UNIVERSITY ART MUSEUM, THE EXHIBIT’S ORIGINAL RUN WAS CUT SHORT BY THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT PHYSICAL IMPROVEMENTS TO THE TRIBAL MUSEUM’S EXHIBITION GALLERY, INCLUDING UPGRADING LIGHTING AND PURCHASING AND INSTALLING NEW DISPLAY CASES, IN ORDER TO SAFELY EXHIBIT EARLY 19TH CENTURY RIBBONWORK OBJECTS. ADDITIONAL PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE SECURING LOANS OF HISTORIC RIBBONWORK OBJECTS, PLANNING AND INSTALLING THE EXHIBITION, AND ENGAGING THE COMMUNITY THROUGH OUTREACH ACTIVITIES AND EDUCATIONAL EVENTS. THE EXHIBIT WILL BENEFIT THE CITIZENS OF THE MIAMI TRIBE OF OKLAHOMA BY CREATING AN ADDITIONAL OPPORTUNITY TO SHARE CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE AND WILL CONTINUE COMMUNITY EFFORTS TO REVITALIZE MYAAMIA RIBBONWORK.
description.3960: THE BAD RIVER BAND OF LAKE SUPERIOR TRIBE OF CHIPPEWA INDIANS WILL CONTINUE ITS EFFORTS TO ESTABLISH ITS NEW MOKA’AANGIIZIS-IBAN (RISING SUN) TRIBAL MUSEUM BY IMPLEMENTING A COMMUNITY-DRIVEN INSTITUTIONAL PLANNING AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT PROJECT. THE MUSEUM MANAGER WILL CREATE A 5-YEAR STRATEGIC PLAN AND DRAFT POLICIES THAT ESTABLISH A STRONG FOUNDATION FOR MUSEUM ORGANIZATION, COLLECTIONS STEWARDSHIP, EDUCATION AND INTERPRETATION, AND COMMUNITY AND AUDIENCE ENGAGEMENT. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RESEARCHING BEST PRACTICES, INFORMATION GATHERING THROUGH COMMUNITY SURVEYS AND FOCUS GROUPS, AND CONDUCTING SITE VISITS TO MUSEUMS OF SIMILAR SCOPE AND MISSION. DEVELOPING THESE FOUNDATIONAL DOCUMENTS WILL INCREASE THE MUSEUM’S CAPACITY TO SERVE ITS COMMUNITY AND CREATE A PATH FORWARD FOR MUSEUM OPERATION AND GROWTH THAT IS ROOTED IN TRIBAL VALUES.
description.3961: KAʻALA FARM WILL DEVELOP AND PROVIDE FIBER ARTS WORKSHOPS THAT DISCUSS THE ROLE OF FIBER ARTS IN HAWAIIAN HISTORY AND MOʻOLELO (STORIES) AND OFFER HANDS-ON OPPORTUNITIES TO GAIN SKILLS IN THIS IMPORTANT NATIVE HAWAIIAN ART FORM. PROJECT STAFF WILL IDENTIFY AND HIRE FIBER ARTS PRACTITIONERS TO LEAD PROGRAMS, COORDINATE RECRUITMENT FOR PARTICIPATION IN PILOT WORKSHOPS, AND EVALUATE AND REFINE THE CONTENT BEFORE LAUNCHING IT TO WIDER AUDIENCES. THE RESULTING PROGRAMS WILL CREATE OPPORTUNITIES FOR A BROADER AND DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF THE ANCESTRAL AND CONTEMPORARY HISTORY OF NATIVE HAWAIIANS IN GENERAL, AND THE NATIVE HAWAIIAN COMMUNITY OF WAIʻANAE IN PARTICULAR. THROUGH THIS PROJECT, STUDENTS, ELDERS, FAMILIES, AND OTHER PARTICIPANTS WILL HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO ENGAGE WITH HAWAIIAN HISTORY AND THIS ART FORM FROM A NATIVE HAWAIIAN PERSPECTIVE.
description.3962: THE LĀNAʻI CULTURE AND HERITAGE CENTER WILL CONDUCT A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT PROJECT TO ENHANCE THE CARE OF AND ACCESS TO 2,500 NATIVE HAWAIIAN CULTURAL OBJECTS IN ITS COLLECTION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT POLICY; CONDUCTING A COMPREHENSIVE COLLECTIONS INVENTORY; CATALOGING AND DIGITIZING THE INVENTORIED COLLECTION; ACQUIRING AND INSTALLING COMPACT MOBILE SHELVING; AND REHOUSING THE COLLECTIONS. PROJECT FUNDS WILL ALSO SUPPORT THE PURCHASE OF NECESSARY SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT, THE RECRUITMENT AND TRAINING OF PAID INTERNS, AND THE ENGAGEMENT OF A CONSULTING ARCHIVIST WHO WILL TRAVEL TO THE CENTER TO PROVIDE OVERSIGHT ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF CATALOGING PROTOCOLS AND STANDARDS FOR DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN INCREASED PHYSICAL AND INTELLECTUAL CONTROL OF THE COLLECTION, BENEFITTING BOTH THE LOCAL LĀNAʻI COMMUNITY, AND THE BROADER NATIVE HAWAIIAN COMMUNITY.
description.3963: THE KAHO‘OLAWE ISLAND RESERVE COMMISSION WILL DEVELOP A DIGITAL APPLICATION TO COLLECT AND MANAGE RELEVANT CULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION RELATED TO THE RESTORATION OF KAHO‘OLAWE ISLAND. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING, TESTING, AND IMPLEMENTING COLLECTION PROTOCOLS FOR GATHERING DATA THROUGH CULTURAL AND TRADITIONAL PRACTICES, DEVELOPING THE DIGITAL APPLICATION AND DATA MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, AND PROVIDING STAFF TRAINING ON DATA COLLECTION, MANAGEMENT, AND DIGITAL APPLICATION USE. THE RESULTING APP AND RELATED PROTOCOLS WILL ALLOW USERS TO RECORD, COLLECT, AND ORGANIZE CONSISTENT AND ACCURATE DATA IN REAL TIME, AND IN A STANDARDIZED FORMAT, MAKING IT MORE MANAGEABLE AND EASIER TO ANALYZE BY CURRENT AND FUTURE CULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDS OF KAHO‘OLAWE. AS A RESULT, THE OVERALL CARE, MANAGEMENT, AND USE OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL, HISTORICAL, ARCHEOLOGICAL, AND CULTURAL RESOURCES ON KAHO‘OLAWE WILL IMPROVE.
description.3964: THE ILANKA CULTURAL CENTER WILL FURTHER ITS MISSION TO EDUCATE ITS COMMUNITY AND VISITORS WHILE PERPETUATING THE TRADITIONS, SKILLS, AND CULTURES OF THE NATIVE VILLAGE OF EYAK BY CREATING SIX CHILDREN'S PICTURE BOOKS DEPICTING TRADITIONAL EYAK AND CHUGACH LEGENDS. PROJECT STAFF WILL HIRE SIX TRIBAL ARTISTS TO PROVIDE ILLUSTRATIONS FOR THE LEGENDS AND WILL OVERSEE DESIGN AND PUBLICATION OF APPROXIMATELY 450 COPIES OF THE BOOKS. THE PUBLISHED BOOKS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE AT THE CULTURAL CENTER, AS WELL AS DISSEMINATED FREE OF COST THROUGHOUT THE COMMUNITY, INCLUDING TO TRIBAL HOUSEHOLDS WITH YOUTH AND THE CORDOVA PUBLIC LIBRARY. AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT, TRIBAL FAMILIES WILL HAVE A NEW ENGAGING MEDIUM FOR PASSING DOWN ORAL TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND TRIBAL ARTISTS’ WORK WILL BE SUPPORTED AND SHOWCASED.
description.3965: THE CENTRAL COUNCIL TLINGIT AND HAIDA INDIAN TRIBES OF ALASKA WILL SUPPORT ONGOING COLLECTIONS CARE AND ACCESS EFFORTS FOR HISTORIC SACRED AND CEREMONIAL ITEMS THAT HAVE BEEN REPATRIATED TO THE TRIBE. THE PROJECT WILL ENABLE THE PURCHASE OF MUSEUM SUPPLIES AND HIGH-QUALITY PROTECTIVE CASES SO THE REPATRIATED OBJECTS CAN BE SAFELY TRANSPORTED TO CULTURAL EVENTS IN THEIR RESPECTIVE SOUTHEAST ALASKAN COMMUNITIES. PROJECT FUNDS WILL ALSO SUPPORT THE TRIBE’S CULTURAL RESOURCES SPECIALIST, WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CARETAKING AND TRANSPORT OF THESE OBJECTS, SOME OF WHICH DATE TO THE 1800’S AND EARLIER. AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT, TLINGIT AND HAIDA PEOPLES OF SOUTHEAST ALASKA WILL HAVE INCREASED ACCESS TO THEIR CULTURAL ITEMS, HELPING PRESERVE AND PERPETUATE TRADITIONAL CEREMONIES AND LIFEWAYS, WHILE THE ITEMS THEMSELVES WILL BE BETTER PROTECTED FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS.
description.3966: THE CATAWBA CULTURAL CENTER, COMPRISED OF THE CATAWBA INDIAN NATION’S MUSEUM, LIBRARY, AND ARCHIVES, WILL DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT A SERIES OF PROGRAMS TO PROMOTE THE IMPORTANCE OF PRESERVING AND CELEBRATING TRADITIONAL CATAWBA CULTURE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING A SUMMER READING PROGRAM FOR CATAWBA CHILDREN, LAUNCHING A YEAR-ROUND CULTURAL HERITAGE PROGRAMMING SCHEDULE FOR CATAWBA COMMUNITY MEMBERS OF ALL AGES, AND PURCHASING NECESSARY EQUIPMENT, SOFTWARE, AND SUPPLIES TO DIGITIZE OBJECTS USING 3D PHOTOGRAMMETRY TECHNOLOGY. DIGITIZED OBJECTS WILL BE MADE ACCESSIBLE ONLINE, ALLOWING GREATER ACCESS FOR RESEARCH AND PROGRAMMING PURPOSES WHILE REDUCING PHYSICAL HANDLING, WHICH WILL IN TURN SUPPORT PRESERVATION EFFORTS. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP BUILD A FOUNDATION FOR LIFELONG LEARNING, INCREASE UNDERSTANDING OF CATAWBA CULTURE AND HERITAGE, AND HELP PRESERVE THAT HERITAGE FOR THE CATAWBA COMMUNITY.
description.3967: THE MECHOOPDA INDIAN TRIBE WILL UNDERTAKE EFFORTS TO PRESERVE AND PERPETUATE THE MAIDU LANGUAGE IN RESPONSE TO THE LOSS OF ONE OF THE TRIBE’S LAST FLUENT MAIDU SPEAKERS TO COVID-19. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT HIRING A FULL-TIME PROJECT COORDINATOR WHO WILL COLLECT AND CREATE NEW CONTENT FOR THE TRIBE’S FREE MAIDU LANGUAGE APP; DEVELOP NEW MAIDU CLASSES, WORKSHOPS, AND PROGRAMS; AND UPDATE SIGNAGE IN EXHIBITS AND DISPLAYS AT THE TRIBAL ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICES TO INCLUDE MAIDU. THIS TIMELY INITIATIVE TO DOCUMENT, SHARE, AND INCORPORATE MAIDU BEFORE MORE KNOWLEDGE IS LOST WILL HELP PRESERVE AND PERPETUATE THE MAIDU LANGUAGE FOR THE NEXT GENERATION OF MECHOOPDA PEOPLE.
description.3968: HIʻIPAKA LLC WILL DESIGN AND FABRICATE A MULTI-SENSUAL MUSEUM EXHIBIT AT A RESTORED TRADITIONAL HAWAIIAN LIVING SITE IN WAIMEA VALLEY, FEATURING SEVEN HALE (TRADITIONAL HOUSES OR STRUCTURES) STAGED WITH TRADITIONAL IMPLEMENTS AND AUDIO RECORDINGS OF DAILY LIFE, HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE, AND EXPOSITORY NARRATION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ENGAGING LOCAL ARTISANS TO REPRODUCE TRADITIONAL TOOLS FOR DISPLAY IN THE RESTORED HALE AS WELL AS DRAFTING AND RECORDING AUDIO NARRATIVES FOR THE HALE. THE RESULTING EXHIBITS WILL PROVIDE A MORE INCLUSIVE EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCE THAT ENGAGES ALL FIVE SENSES, CREATING AN IMMERSIVE AND AUTHENTIC OPPORTUNITY TO LEARN ABOUT NATIVE HAWAIIAN CULTURE FOR K-12 STUDENTS, LOCAL RESIDENTS, AND WAIMEA VALLEY VISITORS.
description.3969: THE TWENTY-NINE PALMS BAND OF MISSION INDIANS WILL CONTINUE ITS PLANNING EFFORTS FOR A FUTURE CULTURAL CENTER AND MUSEUM BY DEVELOPING AN ORGANIZATIONAL PLAN THAT ADDRESSES THE GOVERNANCE, OPERATIONS, AND STAFFING NEEDS FOR THE MUSEUM. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ENGAGING A PROFESSIONAL MUSEUM CONSULTANT WHO WILL CONVENE AND COORDINATE AN ORGANIZATIONAL COMMITTEE COMPRISED OF TRIBAL STAFF, TRIBAL MEMBERS, CULTURAL PRACTITIONERS, AND ORGANIZATIONAL PARTNERS TO DEVELOP THE ORGANIZATIONAL PLAN. THE RESULTING PLAN WILL BE USED TO BUILD THE FOUNDATION OF A MUSEUM THAT IS SUSTAINABLY OPERATED, HELPING TO ENSURE THAT IT CAN SUCCESSFULLY BECOME A PLACE OF LEARNING, PRESERVATION, AND HEALING FOR THE TRIBE AND THE VISITING PUBLIC.
description.3970: THE HAWAIʻI STATE ARCHIVES WILL DIGITIZE OVER 100,000 NEGATIVES FROM TWO OF THE PREMIER ARCHITECTURAL PHOTOGRAPHERS OF THE LATTER 20TH CENTURY, DAVID FRANZEN AND NANCY BANNICK, AND MAKE THEM FREELY ACCESSIBLE IN A BILINGUAL (HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE AND ENGLISH) ONLINE DATABASE. THREE PAID GRADUATE STUDENT INTERNS WILL BE HIRED AND TRAINED TO CREATE HIGH RESOLUTION DIGITAL FILES FOR OVER 40 BOXES OF PHOTOGRAPHS, SLIDES, AND PRINTS AS WELL AS CLEAN, TRANSCRIBE, AND TRANSLATE DESCRIPTIVE METADATA. THIS NEWLY DIGITIZED BILINGUAL ARCHIVE WILL SERVE AS A VISUAL RECORD OF THE “HAWAIʻI THAT WAS,” PROVIDING WORLDWIDE ACCESS TO HAWAIIAN ARCHITECTURAL HISTORY AND HERITAGE, AS WELL AS PROTECTING THESE IRREPLACEABLE MATERIALS FROM CONTINUED DETERIORATION AND EVENTUAL LOSS.
description.3971: THE CONFEDERATED TRIBES OF THE UMATILLA INDIAN RESERVATION WILL COMMEMORATE THE 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE OPENING OF ITS TAMASTSLIKT CULTURAL INSTITUTE (TCI) BY UPDATING OUTDATED SECTIONS OF ITS PERMANENT EXHIBITION, ENHANCING COLLECTIONS CARE AND ACCESS, AND INVESTING IN THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF ITS STAFF. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT HIRING A CONSERVATION TECHNICIAN, PURCHASING ARCHIVAL SUPPLIES TO PROPERLY STORE AND DISPLAY COLLECTION ITEMS, AND SUBSCRIBING TO A NEW COLLECTIONS SOFTWARE OPTION THAT WILL ALLOW TCI TO SHARE ITS COLLECTIONS ONLINE. PROJECT FUNDS WILL ALSO BE USED TO INVEST IN TECHNOLOGY ENHANCEMENTS, SUPPORT TRAINING FOR NEWLY HIRED STAFF MEMBERS, AND CONTRACT WITH AN EXHIBITION DESIGN FIRM THAT WILL DESIGN, FABRICATE, AND INSTALL FRESH CONTENT AND DISPLAYS FOR TCI’S PERMANENT EXHIBITION. ALL OF THESE ACTIVITIES WILL IMPROVE TCI'S CAPACITY TO PROVIDE MUSEUM SERVICES TO TRIBAL MEMBERS, STUDENTS, TEACHERS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.3972: KONIAG, INC. WILL PARTNER WITH THE ALUTIIQ MUSEUM TO COMPLETE A COMMUNITY-LED PLANNING AND DESIGN PROCESS TO ENHANCE THE MUSEUM’S NEWLY EXPANDED GALLERY SPACE THROUGH EXHIBITIONS THAT CELEBRATE THE KODIAK ALUTIIQ PEOPLE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL RECRUIT AND HIRE AN APPRENTICE TO ASSIST WITH THE DEVELOPMENT AND FABRICATION OF 13 DISPLAYS HIGHLIGHTING THE ALUTIIQ HARVESTING TRADITION, COMMUNITY LIFE, AND SPIRITUALITY THROUGH ARTIFACTS, ARTWORK, IMAGES, AND TEXT. THE NEW EXHIBITION SPACE WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO MUSEUM COLLECTIONS AND STRENGTHEN AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF THE HISTORY AND LIVING CULTURE OF THE ALUTIIQ PEOPLE.
description.3973: THE RAPPAHANNOCK TRIBE WILL UNDERGO A CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT TO ENHANCE THE TRIBE’S ABILITY TO PRESERVE AND PROTECT ITS CULTURAL HERITAGE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE: INCREASING STAFF CAPACITY BY HIRING A NEW MUSEUM GENERALIST AND PROVIDING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES; INCREASING ACCESS BY DIGITIZING AND CATALOGING THE COLLECTION; DEVELOPING INTERPRETIVE AND STRATEGIC PLANS FOR THE ARCHIVES, LIBRARY, AND MUSEUM; DEVELOPING A VIRTUAL EXHIBIT; AND EVALUATING THE CARE AND MANAGEMENT OF COLLECTIONS BY AUDITING PAPER RECORDS, CONDUCTING CONDITION ASSESSMENTS ON ARTIFACTS, AND EVALUATING MUSEUM AND LIBRARY PROGRAMS. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP TRIBAL CITIZENS REBUILD CONNECTIONS TO THEIR CULTURE AND ANCESTRAL HOME ON THE RAPPAHANNOCK RIVER AND HELP THE PUBLIC BETTER UNDERSTAND TRIBAL HISTORY AND CONTEMPORARY CULTURE.
description.3974: THE SAGINAW CHIPPEWA INDIAN TRIBE OF MICHIGAN’S ZIIBIWING CENTER OF ANISHINABE CULTURE AND LIFEWAYS WILL DIGITIZE MOUNT PLEASANT INDIAN INDUSTRIAL BOARDING SCHOOL DECIMAL FILES LOCATED AT THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES AND RECORDS ADMINISTRATION (NARA) IN CHICAGO, ILLINOIS TO INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY TO THESE HISTORICAL DOCUMENTS. PROJECT STAFF WILL CONDUCT MULTIPLE TRIPS TO THE NARA FACILITY TO DIGITIZE THE RECORDS RELATED TO THE MOUNT PLEASANT INDIAN BOARDING SCHOOL AND THE GREAT LAKES INDIAN AGENCY. THE DIGITAL FILES WILL BE CROSS-REFERENCED WITH THE TRIBE’S EXISTING BOARDING SCHOOL STUDENT DATABASE, THE ACCOMPANYING METADATA WILL BE UPDATED, AND THE RECORDS WILL BE ADDED TO THE ZIIBIWING REPOSITORY FOR COMMUNITY USE. THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN INCREASED ACCESS TO THESE RECORDS FOR TRIBAL MEMBERS, DESCENDANTS OF THOSE WHO ATTENDED THE SCHOOL, AND THE PUBLIC, HELPING TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND PROVIDE A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF WHAT HAPPENED IN THIS BOARDING SCHOOL.
description.3975: THE INSTITUTE FOR NATIVE PACIFIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE (INPEACE) WILL DEVELOP AND DESIGN PLANS FOR A SELF-DIRECTED HALE (HOUSE) BUILDING EXHIBIT THAT WILL HIGHLIGHT AND REINTRODUCE NATIVE HAWAIIAN TRADITIONAL HALE BUILDING KNOWLEDGE, STRATEGIES, AND TECHNIQUES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONSULTING WITH CULTURAL EXPERTS TO GATHER INFORMATION AND CREATE A REPOSITORY OF MATERIALS AND ORAL HISTORIES ABOUT NATIVE HAWAIIAN HALE BUILDING PRACTICES; CREATING A DESIGN REFERENCE GUIDE; DEVELOPING CONCEPTUAL DESIGN LAYOUTS AND BLUEPRINTS; AND REFINING AND COMPLETING THE EXHIBIT DESIGN AND LAYOUT. A VIDEOGRAPHER WILL BE HIRED TO CAPTURE ORAL HISTORIES AND CULTURAL PRACTICES OF KUPUNA (ELDERS) AND RENOWNED CULTURAL EXPERTS IN A VIDEO DOCUSERIES. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE OF THE TRADITIONAL AND CONTEMPORARY SCIENCE OF NATIVE HAWAIIAN HALE BUILDING PRACTICES WHILE SUPPORTING INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN CULTIVATING STRATEGIES TO DEVELOP CULTURALLY RELEVANT AND INFORMED STEM EXPERIENCES.
description.3976: THE MILLE LACS BAND OF THE MINNESOTA CHIPPEWA TRIBE WILL COLLECT AND PRESERVE ORAL HISTORIES AND PERSONAL STORIES FROM APPROXIMATELY 500 TRIBAL ELDERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN ORDER TO ADDRESS THE DISRUPTION OF TRADITIONAL MODES OF CULTURAL TRANSMISSION CAUSED BY THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE HIRING A NEW ARCHIVES ASSISTANT POSITION, PURCHASING RECORDING SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT, DEVELOPING A STANDARDIZED LIST OF INTERVIEW QUESTIONS, AND ENGAGING TRIBAL MEMBERS TO RECORD ORALLY TRANSMITTED STORIES AND HISTORIES ACCORDING TO PROTOCOLS THAT ADDRESS GENEALOGICAL, CULTURAL, AND PERSONAL HISTORY. THE ORAL HISTORIES WILL BE CATALOGED IN THE TRIBAL ARCHIVES, RESULTING IN A NEW ORAL HISTORY COLLECTION THAT WILL HELP PRESERVE, PROTECT, AND SHARE TRIBAL HISTORY AND CULTURE FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS.
description.3977: THE PUEBLO OF POJOAQUE’S POEH CULTURAL CENTER WILL UNDERTAKE A SHARED STEWARDSHIP AND ETHICAL RETURN PROJECT FOR TEWA OBJECTS TO MAKE THEM AVAILABLE FOR STUDY, INSPIRATION, AND PROPER CARE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RESEARCHING MUSEUMS, INSTITUTIONS, AND INDIVIDUALS IN THE UNITED STATES WHO MAY HAVE TEWA OBJECTS AND COLLABORATING WITH THE IDENTIFIED ENTITIES TO BRING THE OBJECTS BACK TO TEWA COUNTRY IN THE SPIRIT OF RESTORATIVE CULTURAL COLLABORATION. ADDITIONALLY, PROJECT STAFF WILL DEVELOP ETHICAL RETURN POLICIES, GUIDELINES, AND ASSOCIATED TRAINING TO INCREASE CAPACITY FOR ETHICAL RETURNS AND INTER-INSTITUTIONAL COLLABORATION. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT THE PUEBLO OF POJOAQUE AND SURROUNDING PUEBLOS AND WILL INCREASE AWARENESS OF WAYS THAT TRIBES AND MUSEUMS CAN WORK COLLABORATIVELY TO CREATE A SHARED VISION OF AMERICAN HISTORY.
description.3978: THE SEMINOLE TRIBE OF FLORIDA’S AH-TAH-THI-KI MUSEUM WILL COMPLETE A CATALOGING AND REHOUSING PROJECT FOR 16,000 PHOTOGRAPHS IN ITS COLLECTION TO MAKE THEM SEARCHABLE AND ACCESSIBLE TO THE SEMINOLE COMMUNITY. THIS PROJECT WILL FUND A CATALOGING ASSISTANT WHO, ALONG WITH THE COLLECTIONS MANAGER, WILL CATALOG THE PHOTOGRAPHS INTO THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE, REHOUSE THE PHOTOGRAPHS, SHELVE THE NEWLY HOUSED AND CATALOGED PHOTOGRAPHS, AND ADD THEM TO AN ONLINE COLLECTIONS MODULE. ONCE ACCESSIBLE, TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL BE ENGAGED TO HELP PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT THE PHOTOGRAPHS SUCH AS NAMES, PLACES, AND EVENTS. BY DOCUMENTING CONTEMPORARY SEMINOLE LIFE AND MAKING IT MORE ACCESSIBLE, THIS PROJECT WILL HELP PRESERVE THE CULTURE AND HERITAGE OF THE TRIBE.
description.3979: BARONA BAND OF MISSION INDIANS' BARONA CULTURAL CENTER AND MUSEUM WILL CREATE AND INSTALL AN ANIMATED SHORT FILM ENTITLED, “SINYOHOW AND THE TWINS.” THIS FILM WILL SERVE AS A SEQUEL TO THE TRIBE’S AWARD-WINNING MULTI-SENSORY KUMEYAAY/DIEGUEÑO CREATION STORY FILM AND EXHIBIT. USING A COMMUNITY GENERATED MANUSCRIPT, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL HIRE A FILM PRODUCTION COMPANY TO DEVELOP THE SCRIPT AND WORK WITH THE FILMMAKERS TO CREATE AND INSTALL THE FILM IN THE CULTURAL CENTER THEATER. BY MAKING THIS FILM AVAILABLE, THE CULTURAL CENTER WILL CONNECT LOCAL NATIVE YOUTH AND VISITORS WITH ANCIENT KUMEYAAY STORIES AND KNOWLEDGE, FROM THE TRIBE’S PERSPECTIVE. VIEWERS WILL BENEFIT FROM A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF KUMEYAAY HISTORY AND CULTURE, AND YOUNGER GENERATIONS WILL GROW UP WITH THESE STORIES AS A NORMALIZED WAY OF LIFE.
description.3980: THE SEALASKA CORPORATION AND SEALASKA HERITAGE INSTITUTE WILL CREATE SEALASKA LIVING HERITAGE MUSEUM BOXES, PORTABLE KITS COMPRISED OF MUSEUM-QUALITY COLLECTION ITEMS WITH ASSOCIATED LESSON PLANS AND ACTIVITIES, TO BRING CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE AND CULTURALLY SUSTAINING EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES TO SOUTHEAST ALASKA’S ELEMENTARY STUDENTS, MANY OF WHOM ARE UNABLE TO VISIT THE MUSEUM DUE TO ITS LOCATION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ENGAGING ALASKA NATIVE ARTISTS TO CREATE MODELS FOR THE BOXES, CREATING ACCOMPANYING EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS, ASSEMBLING THE BOXES, AND PILOTING TWO MUSEUM BOX EXPERIENCES WITH TEACHERS AND STUDENTS IN GRADES 3-5. THIS PROJECT WILL PROMOTE AND ENHANCE DIVERSITY, INCLUSIVITY, AND CROSS-CULTURAL UNDERSTANDING OF THE TLINGIT, HAIDA, AND TS’MSYEN (TSIMSHIAN) CULTURES AND LANGUAGES AND SUPPORT TEACHERS UNFAMILIAR WITH ALASKA NATIVE CULTURES TO TEACH ABOUT THOSE TRADITIONS, ALLOWING ALASKA NATIVE STUDENTS TO FEEL THAT THEIR CULTURES ARE VALUED.
description.3981: THE JENA BAND OF CHOCTAW INDIANS WILL LAUNCH A STRATEGIC PLANNING INITIATIVE TO GUIDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A CULTURAL CENTER AND MUSEUM THAT WILL HOUSE THE TRIBE'S ARTIFACTS AND DISPLAY ITS HISTORY, CULTURE, AND HERITAGE. TRIBAL LEADERS, MEMBERS, AND STAFF WILL FORM AN ADVISORY PLANNING COMMITTEE AND WILL GATHER INPUT FROM COMMUNITY MEMBERS, PARTICULARLY TRIBAL ELDERS AND YOUTH. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL ENGAGE THE SERVICES OF THREE CONSULTANTS: A PROJECT MANAGER, AN ARCHITECT, AND A PROFESSIONAL MUSEUM CONSULTANT, TO ASSIST IN THE PLANNING PROCESS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL ALSO CONDUCT SITE VISITS TO SEE FIRST-HAND HOW OTHER CHOCTAW COMMUNITIES HAVE DEVELOPED THEIR CULTURAL CENTERS. AS A RESULT, THE TRIBE WILL HAVE A STRATEGIC PATH FORWARD FOR THE SCOPE AND DESIGN OF THEIR CULTURAL CENTER, AND BE BETTER POSITIONED TO PRESERVE JENA CHOCTAW HISTORY, CULTURE, AND HERITAGE.
description.3982: THE METLAKATLA INDIAN COMMUNITY WILL CONDUCT A LANGUAGE PRESERVATION PROJECT TO ADDRESS THE LOSS OF FLUENT SM’ ALGYAX SPEAKERS, WHICH IS NOW A CRITICALLY ENDANGERED LANGUAGE OF THE TS’MSYEN (TSIMSHIAN) PEOPLE, WITH JUST ONE FLUENT SPEAKER REMAINING IN METLAKATLA. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE HIRING A LANGUAGE MENTOR AND A LANGUAGE STUDENT; ACQUIRING THE TECHNOLOGY NEEDED TO ARCHIVE THE LANGUAGE AND LEARNING AIDS; AND PRODUCING AUDIO ARCHIVES, TRAINING, AND EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS. THE MENTOR AND STUDENT WILL PARTICIPATE IN COMMUNITY LANGUAGE CLASSES THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT, AS WELL AS TEACH OTHER PAID AND VOLUNTEER STUDENTS. THE CULTURAL HERITAGE DEPARTMENT WILL ALSO HOST LANGUAGE IMMERSION EVENTS FEATURING INTENSIVE LANGUAGE CLASSES. AS A RESULT OF THESE SERVICES AND PROGRAMMING, TRIBAL MEMBERS WILL HAVE IMPROVED AUDIO ARCHIVES, INCREASED KNOWLEDGE OF THE SM’ ALGYAX LANGUAGE, AND DEEPER CULTURAL CONNECTIONS AND UNDERSTANDING.
