THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CONDUCT ONGOING EVALUATIONS TO DEVELOP AND REFINE A DOCUMENTED MODEL, WHICH THEY WILL SHARE WITH THE LIBRARY AND ARCHIVES COMMUNITIES VIA THE PROJECT WEBSITE AND NATIONAL CONFERENCES. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP DIVERSIFY THE LIBRARY AND ARCHIVES FIELD AND WILL SERVE AS AN EXAMPLE FOR OTHER LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE SCHOOLS IN COHESIVE CURRICULUM INTEGRATION DRAWING ON SOCIAL JUSTICE AND INCLUSIVITY, IMPLEMENTED IN SYNCHRONIZATION WITH AN EXISTING PROGRAM.
description.4223: WEST CHESTER UNIVERSITY, IN COLLABORATION WITH STANFORD UNIVERSITY, THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS AT URBANA-CHAMPAIGN (UIUC), AND OTHER CONSULTANTS, WILL ORGANIZE A VIRTUAL NATIONAL OPEN FORUM WITH DATA EXPERTS FROM DIVERSE BACKGROUNDS AND INDUSTRIES ALONGSIDE ACADEMIC LIBRARIANS TO SHARE THEIR PERSPECTIVES ON IDENTIFYING AND EVALUATING DATA QUALITY. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CREATE A WHITE PAPER, INFOGRAPHIC GUIDES OF A SYNTHESIZED DATA EVALUATION STRATEGY, AND A WEBSITE TO SHARE FORUM DELIVERABLES. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP RAISE ACADEMIC LIBRARIAN AWARENESS OF DATA QUALITY PROBLEMS, FILL THEIR KNOWLEDGE GAPS, AND BUILD THEIR CAPACITY AND CONFIDENCE IN TEACHING DATA EVALUATION, CRITICAL THINKING ABOUT DATA, AND DATA LITERACY. THE PROJECT ALSO WILL DEMONSTRATE LIBRARIES’ IMPACT ON EDUCATING DATA-LITERATE CITIZENS, IMPROVING THE QUALITY AND INTEGRITY OF SCHOLARLY OUTPUT, REDUCING THE SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC COSTS CAUSED BY DATA QUALITY ISSUES, AND IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING. AS SUBRECIPIENTS, STANFORD UNIVERSITY WILL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE, INCLUDING ESSENTIAL PERSPECTIVES FOR DEVELOPING THE SYNTHESIZED DATA EVALUATION STRATEGY AND PROJECT DELIVERABLES; UIUC WILL SUPPORT A GRADUATE STUDENT TO ASSIST IN ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES.
description.4224: THE LIBRARIES AT VIRGINIA TECH AND THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, RIVERSIDE WILL LAUNCH A GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (GENAI) INCUBATOR PROGRAM TO ADDRESS THE CHALLENGE OF LIMITED AI ADOPTION IN UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES. PARTICIPANTS WILL START WITH LEARNING FUNDAMENTALS OF GENAI, ADVANCING THROUGH GUIDED DEMONSTRATIONS, REAL-WORLD EXAMPLES, AND TARGETED TASKS. PARTICIPANTS WILL THEN WORK AS A TEAM ON A CAPSTONE PROJECT TO CREATE A GENAI APPLICATION FOR A LIBRARY USE CASE SPECIFIC TO FOUR LIBRARY THEMES: GENAI LITERACY, COLLECTION, PRESERVATION, AND RESEARCH. THE TARGETED MENTORING WILL FEATURE A MULTI-DAY WORKSHOP, SUPPLEMENTED BY CONSULTATION SESSIONS AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT TOOLS TO ASSIST PARTICIPANTS IN COMPLETING THEIR CAPSTONE PROJECTS. BEYOND THE INITIAL PROJECT PARTICIPANTS, WIDELY SHARED DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE TRAINING MATERIALS, WORKSHOPS, AND THE CAPSTONE PROJECTS. PARTICIPANTS IN THIS INCUBATOR PROGRAM WILL BECOME GENAI PRACTITIONERS, POSSESSING A DEEP UNDERSTANDING, PRACTICAL EXPERTISE, AND THE CAPACITY TO DEMONSTRATE THE POSITIVE IMPACT OF AI WITHIN THE BROADER LIBRARY COMMUNITY.
description.4225: COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES' RARE BOOK & MANUSCRIPT LIBRARY WILL CONVENE A FORUM OF ARCHIVES AND SPECIAL COLLECTIONS CURATORS TO ENHANCE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND INCLUSIVITY IN THIS OFTEN-OVERLOOKED PART OF THE PROFESSION. THE TWO-DAY FORUM WILL GATHER 15–20 BLACK, INDIGENOUS, AND PEOPLE OF COLOR CURATORS TO SHARE KNOWLEDGE, DISCUSS CONTEMPORARY CURATORIAL WORK INCLUDING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT NEEDS AND BARRIERS TO THE FIELD, AND FOSTER CONVERSATIONS ON ETHICAL STEWARDSHIP OF COLLECTIONS. OTHER ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE CREATION OF A CHAPBOOK ON CURATORIAL ETHICS, AN ONLINE COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE, SURVEYS TO ASSESS THE FIELD, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF A MENTORING PIPELINE FOR FUTURE ARCHIVES AND SPECIAL COLLECTIONS CURATORS. THE PROJECT AIMS TO BENEFIT ASPIRING CURATORS, CURRENT CURATORS, AND THE DIRECTORS OF ARCHIVES AND SPECIAL COLLECTIONS WHO SUPERVISE THEM BY FOSTERING AN INCLUSIVE, ETHICAL APPROACH TO CURATORIAL WORK.
description.4226: IN THIS EARLY CAREER RESEARCH DEVELOPMENT PROJECT, DR. PRIYA KUMAR OF PENNSYLVANIA STATE UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP, TEST, AND DISSEMINATE A TOOLKIT THAT EQUIPS LIBRARIANS TO NAVIGATE PRIVACY ISSUES RELATED TO PRETEEN ENGAGEMENT WITH TECHNOLOGY. THE MARYLAND STATE LIBRARY AGENCY, THE WISCONSIN LIBRARY SERVICES TEAM WITHIN THE WISCONSIN DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC INSTRUCTION’S DIVISION FOR LIBRARIES AND TECHNOLOGY, A TEAM OF ADVISORS, AND THE AMERICAN LIBRARY ASSOCIATION WILL BE INVOLVED IN DIFFERENT PHASES OF THE PROJECT. THROUGH CO-DESIGN WORKSHOPS WITH LIBRARIANS, THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL TRANSLATE A THEORY-BASED PRIVACY LITERACY FRAMEWORK DESIGNED BY DR. KUMAR INTO A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE TOOLKIT AND TEST THE TOOLKIT AT FOUR PUBLIC LIBRARIES. IN THE PROCESS, THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL FOSTER A COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE THROUGH WHICH YOUTH SERVICE LIBRARIANS CAN EXCHANGE PRIVACY KNOWLEDGE AND SUPPORT. THE RESEARCH WILL CONTRIBUTE INSIGHTS AND MATERIALS THAT HELP LIBRARIANS DIAGNOSE AND ADDRESS TECHNOLOGY-RELATED PRIVACY ISSUES IN A WAY THAT RESPECTS THE DIVERSE NEEDS OF YOUTH.
description.4227: THE SOCIETY OF AMERICAN ARCHIVISTS (SAA) WILL CONVENE A FORUM TO DEVELOP A STRATEGIC RESEARCH AGENDA FOR THE ARCHIVAL PROFESSION TO ENHANCE THE PROFESSION'S CAPACITY TO SERVE ITS AUDIENCES, DEMONSTRATE SOCIETAL VALUE, AND EXPAND PROFESSIONAL KNOWLEDGE. THE FORUM WILL BRING TOGETHER ARCHIVISTS AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS OVER THE COURSE OF TWO DAYS TO TRANSFORM THE SAA RESEARCH AND INNOVATION ROADMAP INTO A COMPREHENSIVE AND ACTIONABLE RESEARCH AGENDA. ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE FACILITATED DISCUSSIONS, FEEDBACK COLLECTION, AND DISSEMINATION OF THE AGENDA. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE A PUBLISHED PRIORITIZED RESEARCH AGENDA, A COMMUNICATIONS AND OUTREACH PLAN, AND A FRAMEWORK FOR AGENDA MAINTENANCE AND FUTURE UPDATES. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE ARCHIVISTS, GRANT FUNDERS, AND LEADERS OF STANDARD-SETTING ORGANIZATIONS.
description.4228: THE UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA, IN COLLABORATION WITH OLD DOMINION UNIVERSITY, WILL ADDRESS THE KNOWLEDGE GAP THAT MANY SCHOOL LIBRARIANS REPORT IN WORKING WITH STUDENTS WITH AUTISM. THIS PROJECT WILL GATHER PRACTICING SCHOOL LIBRARIANS ACROSS THE NATION TO LEARN VALUABLE INFORMATION FROM AUTISM EXPERTS. THIS PROJECT’S ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE 1) PLANNING A NATIONAL VIRTUAL FORUM TO BRING SCHOOL LIBRARIANS TOGETHER FOR AUTISM EDUCATION; 2) HOSTING THE NATIONAL VIRTUAL FORUM; 3) CREATING RECORDINGS, ABSTRACTS, AND FACT SHEETS FROM THE NATIONAL VIRTUAL FORUM; 4) PUBLISHING INFORMATION ON AN ELEARNING PLATFORM; AND 5) DISSEMINATING VIA PLATFORMS SUCH AS THE PROJECT ENABLE WEBSITE, THE TARGETING AUTISM BLOG, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, AND PRACTITIONER PUBLICATIONS. TOGETHER, THESE LIVE AND RECORDED SESSIONS AND COMPLEMENTARY MATERIALS WILL HELP TO ADDRESS THE NEED FOR MORE AUTISM-INFORMED SCHOOL LIBRARIANS, ULTIMATELY LEADING TO MORE INCLUSIVE AND ACCEPTING SCHOOL LIBRARIES FOR CHILDREN WITH AUTISM.
description.4229: IN THIS EARLY CAREER RESEARCH DEVELOPMENT PROJECT, DR. ALEXANDRA CHASSANOFF WILL INVESTIGATE HOW BORN-DIGITAL STEWARDS DESCRIBE THEIR CURRENT NEEDS AND CHALLENGES; WHAT PROFESSIONALIZATION PATHWAYS EXIST; AND WHAT ROLE, IMPACT, AND VALUE COMMUNITIES OF PRACTICE HAVE IN BORN-DIGITAL STEWARDSHIP. ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE CONDUCTING AN ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN, STUDYING SEVERAL COMMUNITIES OF PRACTICE VIA SITE OBSERVATIONS AND FOCUS GROUP SESSIONS, AND INTERVIEWING OTHER EXPERT COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE STAKEHOLDERS. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE A SYNTHESIS OF CURRENT PROFESSIONALIZATION PATHWAYS, A SUMMATIVE REPORT ON BORN-DIGITAL STEWARDSHIP, AND A GUIDE TO CULTIVATING PROFESSIONAL BORN-DIGITAL STEWARDSHIP COMMUNITIES OF PRACTICE. BY SHARING ACTIONABLE GUIDANCE DERIVED FROM PRACTITIONER EXPERIENCES, THE PROJECT WILL HELP DIMINISH THE WIDENING GAP IN BORN-DIGITAL STEWARDSHIP BETWEEN BEST-IN-PRACTICE THEORIES AND EXISTING REALITIES IN LIBRARIES AND ARCHIVES ACROSS THE NATION.
description.4230: THE SCHOOL DISTRICT OF PHILADELPHIA (SDP), PARTNERING WITH THE PHILADELPHIA ALLIANCE TO RESTORE SCHOOL LIBRARIANS, WILL INVESTIGATE STRATEGIES USED BY LARGE URBAN SCHOOL DISTRICTS TO REINSTATE SCHOOL LIBRARIANS AND DEVELOP A REPLICABLE DISTRICT MODEL OF SCHOOL LIBRARY RENEWAL. THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE GATHERING AND PUBLISHING STRATEGIES FROM URBAN SCHOOL DISTRICTS THAT SUCCESSFULLY RESTORED LIBRARIAN POSITIONS; INVESTIGATING AND PUBLISHING OPTIONS FOR RECRUITING A DIVERSE POOL OF SCHOOL LIBRARIAN CANDIDATES; AND CREATING A REPLICABLE PLAN USING SDP AS A MODEL TO RESTORE EFFECTIVE SCHOOL LIBRARIES WITH CERTIFIED LIBRARIANS. ALL DISTRICTS CAN BENEFIT FROM THE PROJECT’S FINDINGS AND ADAPTABLE TOOLS AND RESOURCES. THIS PROJECT WILL SERVE AS A MODEL AND BE USEFUL TO OTHER SCHOOL AND LIBRARY LEADERS RECOGNIZING THE NEED TO REINSTATE CERTIFIED SCHOOL LIBRARIANS AND EFFECTIVE LIBRARIES AS A SCHOOL IMPROVEMENT STRATEGY FOR THEIR K–12 STUDENTS.
description.4231: THE BOSTON LIBRARY CONSORTIUM, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ALLIANCE OF LIBRARY CONSORTIA, WILL DESIGN, PILOT, AND ASSESS A THREE-DAY LEADERSHIP ACADEMY FOR BIPOC SUPPORT STAFF LIBRARY SUPERVISORS WHO DO NOT HAVE MASTER OF LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE (MLIS) DEGREES. THE LEADERSHIP ACADEMY WILL PROMOTE RETENTION AND DEVELOPMENT OF A LEADERSHIP SKILL SET, AS WELL AS DELIVER TRAINING AND EDUCATION ON CURRENT, FRONT-LINE LIBRARY TOPICS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL USE A CO-DESIGN APPROACH TO DEVELOP THE CURRICULUM BY ENGAGING BIPOC THOUGHT LEADERS, BIPOC LIBRARY SUPERVISORS WITHOUT MLIS DEGREES, EXPERIENCED MANAGEMENT CONSULTANTS, AND MEMBERS OF THE CONSORTIA TO CO-CREATE A CURRICULUM THAT STRIKES A COMPELLING BALANCE BETWEEN BROADER ORGANIZATIONAL ISSUES AND PRACTICAL LEADERSHIP SKILLS. THE INITIAL PILOT WILL DEVELOP AND DELIVER A NATIONAL LEADERSHIP ACADEMY TO 30 LIBRARY STAFF MEMBERS THAT SUPPORT THE LONG-TERM PROFESSIONAL GROWTH OF A VITAL POPULATION OF WORKERS IN LIBRARIES WHOSE NEEDS FOR TRAINING AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ARE CURRENTLY UNMET.
description.4232: THE CONSORTIAL COLLABORATION FOR ACADEMIC LIBRARY LEADERSHIP SUCCESS (CCALLS) PROJECT WILL ENGAGE LIBRARY CONSORTIA IN ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL CONTINUING EDUCATION PROGRAM TO DEVELOP ACADEMIC LIBRARY WORKERS’ ASSESSMENT SKILLS. THE “CARLI COUNTS” CURRICULUM IS A STRONG FOUNDATION FOR SUCH TRAINING, BUT ITS REPLICATION AND SCALING NATIONWIDE REQUIRES SELF-EXAMINATION OF CAPACITY AT EACH INDIVIDUAL PARTICIPATING CONSORTIUM. THIS EXAMINATION IS KICKED OFF WITH A COMMUNITY DIALOGUE AND THEN GUIDED AND SUPPORTED THROUGH A DESIGN SEMINAR. BY THE END OF THE PROJECT, CONSORTIA NATIONWIDE WILL HAVE A GREATER AWARENESS OF THEIR OWN CAPACITY TO PROVIDE ASSESSMENT TRAINING TO THEIR MEMBERS AND THE POTENTIAL BENEFITS OF PURSUING A NATIONAL-SCALE PROGRAM THROUGH CONSORTIAL COLLABORATION. ULTIMATELY, CCALLS AIMS TO ENABLE LIBRARY CONSORTIA TO WORK TOGETHER TO PROPAGATE ASSESSMENT TRAINING FOR ACADEMIC LIBRARY WORKERS THROUGHOUT THE U.S., BENEFITING ACADEMIC LIBRARIES AND THEIR INSTITUTIONS BY DIRECTLY SUPPORTING THEIR STUDENTS AND FACULTY.
description.4233: THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH TEXAS DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION SCIENCE WILL DEVELOP AND DEPLOY AN ONLINE, IMMERSIVE HEALTH SCIENCES LIBRARIANSHIP FELLOWSHIP TRAINING PROGRAM TO BUILD THE COMPETENCIES OF LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE (LIS) GRADUATE STUDENTS AND EARLY CAREER LIBRARIANS. DESPITE THE CRITICAL NEED OF HEALTH SCIENCES LIBRARIANS TO ENHANCE THE QUALITY DELIVERY OF HEALTH CARE, THERE ARE FEW OPPORTUNITIES FOR INDIVIDUALS TO SPECIALIZE IN THIS TYPE OF LIBRARIANSHIP. AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT, 20 INDIVIDUALS WILL INCREASE THEIR COMPETENCE IN HEALTH SCIENCES LIBRARIANSHIP THROUGH THIS SPECIALIZED SUMMER TRAINING. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DEVELOP OPENLY ACCESSIBLE TRAINING MATERIALS TO EDUCATE ENTRY-LEVEL HEALTH SCIENCES LIBRARIANS, WHICH COULD BE USED BY LIS MASTER’S PROGRAMS AND PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATIONS TO ENHANCE THEIR CURRICULA IN THIS AREA. THIS PROJECT WORKS TO FILL THE PRESENT NEED FOR QUALIFIED HEALTH SCIENCES LIBRARIANS IN VARIED WORK SETTINGS ACROSS THE COUNTRY.
description.4234: THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS URBANA-CHAMPAIGN SCHOOL OF INFORMATION SCIENCES AND THE PUBLIC LIBRARY ASSOCIATION WILL IMPLEMENT THE DATA STORYTELLING TOOLKIT FOR LIBRARIES PROJECT TO PROVIDE GUIDANCE AND TOOLS TO HELP PUBLIC LIBRARIES REACH AUDIENCES WITH STORIES BASED ON DATA. THERE IS A GAP BETWEEN AVAILABLE DATA AND USABLE STORIES FOR PUBLIC LIBRARIES; THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE GAP BY GUIDING USERS TO DEVELOP SKILLS TO TRANSLATE DATA INTO EVIDENCE-BASED STORIES. FOLLOWING A PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED BASIC MODEL, THIS PROJECT CONNECTS DATA STORYTELLING TRAINING WITH PUBLIC LIBRARY DATA, TOOLS, AND INFRASTRUCTURE. THROUGH AN ITERATIVE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, THE PROJECT WILL LEAD TO AN ONLINE TOOLKIT WITH TWO INTERACTIVE PATHWAYS AND BUILT-IN GUIDANCE AND STORY TEMPLATES. THE TOOLKIT WILL HELP LIBRARY STAFF LEARN TO BETTER TELL THE STORY OF THEIR IMPACT AND VALUE, POSITIONING LIBRARIES FOR SUCCESS INTO THE FUTURE.
description.4235: THE SOUTH ASIAN AMERICAN DIGITAL ARCHIVE WILL HOST AN INAUGURAL SUMMIT—A NATIONAL FORUM AIMED AT INSPIRING NEW LIBRARY, ARCHIVES, AND MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS TO ADDRESS WELL-DOCUMENTED DIVERSITY GAPS IN THE FIELD. THE SUMMIT WILL CONNECT YOUNG SOUTH ASIAN AMERICANS WITH CURRENT SOUTH ASIAN LIBRARY, ARCHIVES, AND MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS TO EXPLORE CAREER PATHS AND COMMUNITY MEMORY PROJECTS. ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PANEL DISCUSSIONS, ROUNDTABLES, MENTORSHIP SESSIONS, AND COMMUNITY ARCHIVING ACTIVITIES. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED AWARENESS OF CAREERS IN THE LIBRARY, ARCHIVES, AND MUSEUM PROFESSIONS, STRONGER COMMUNITY TIES, AND A MODEL FOR FUTURE SUMMITS. BENEFICIARIES ARE YOUNG SOUTH ASIAN AMERICANS AND CURRENT LIBRARY, ARCHIVES, AND MUSEUM PROFESSIONALS.
description.4236: IN THIS EARLY CAREER RESEARCH DEVELOPMENT PROJECT, DR. SARAH A. EVANS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH TEXAS, DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION SCIENCE, WILL STUDY TEENAGE LEISURE AND INFORMATIONAL READING HABITS WITH COMICS AND GRAPHIC NOVELS, FOCUSING ON GRAPHIC MEDICINE TO ENHANCE INFORMAL LITERACY LEARNING IN PUBLIC LIBRARIES. THIS STUDY WILL EXPLORE HOW ADOLESCENTS USE GRAPHIC NOVELS TO MEET LEISURE READING AND INFORMATION NEEDS; HOW ENGAGEMENT IN GRAPHIC MEDICINE ACTIVITIES FOSTER LITERACY, COMMUNICATION, AND SELF-CARE SKILLS; AND EFFECTIVE LIBRARY PRACTICES TO SUPPORT THIS LEARNING. RESEARCH METHODS WILL INCLUDE CONTENT ANALYSIS, INTERVIEWS, AND FOCUS GROUPS. DR. EVANS WILL COLLABORATE WITH LIBRARIANS AND TEENS IN THREE LIBRARIES TO CREATE GRAPHIC MEDICINE BOOK CLUBS AND CO-DESIGN ACTIVITIES, LEADING TO A PROTOTYPE GRAPHIC MEDICINE TOOLKIT AND PROGRAM CURRICULUM FOR PUBLIC LIBRARIES. THE PROJECT AIMS TO REVEAL CURRENT PATTERNS IN ADOLESCENT USE OF COMICS AND GRAPHIC NOVELS AND PROVIDE PRACTICAL SUPPORT STRATEGIES FOR TEEN-SERVICES LIBRARIANS.
description.4237: CLEMSON UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES, WITH WESTERN CAROLINA UNIVERSITY AND PURDUE UNIVERSITY, WILL CONDUCT A TWO-YEAR, MIXED METHODS WORKFORCE STUDY OF RACIALLY AND ETHNICALLY MINORITIZED ACADEMIC LIBRARY SUPPORT STAFF. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL DEPLOY A NATIONAL SURVEY AND CONDUCT REGIONAL FOCUS GROUPS WITH MINORITIZED LIBRARY STAFF ACROSS THE UNITED STATES TO DESCRIBE BARRIERS TO PATHWAYS TO LIBRARIANSHIP (I.E., TO UNDERSTAND WHY SO MANY MINORITIZED INDIVIDUALS REMAIN IN SUPPORT STAFF ROLES INSTEAD OF BECOMING LIBRARIANS). THIS PROJECT WILL GENERATE NEW INSIGHTS AND UNDERSTANDING OF MINORITIZED ACADEMIC LIBRARY SUPPORT STAFF’S STATUS (NUMBERS, DISTRIBUTION, DEMOGRAPHICS, LEVELS OF EDUCATIONAL ATTAINMENT, ACTIVITIES, ETC.), THEIR PROFESSIONAL INTERESTS AND ASPIRATIONS, AND BARRIERS (FINANCIAL, CULTURAL, PERSONAL, OTHER) THAT MIGHT HINDER RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND ADVANCEMENT OF MINORITIZED POPULATIONS IN THE FIELD. THE RESEARCH WILL INCREASE THE PROFESSION-WIDE UNDERSTANDING OF THE MULTIPLE BARRIERS (SYSTEMIC AND LOCALIZED) TO ACHIEVING GREATER LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE PROFESSIONAL WORKFORCE DIVERSITY.
description.4238: THE AMERICAN LIBRARY ASSOCIATION WILL PLAN AND PROTOTYPE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT RESOURCES FOR LIBRARY WORKERS THAT COVER A WIDE RANGE OF PROGRAMMING SKILLS. THE PROGRAMMING LIBRARIAN LEARNING LAB WILL BE AN ONLINE PROFESSIONAL LEARNING COMMUNITY WHERE PROGRAMMING LIBRARY WORKERS CAN ACCESS FREE LEARNING EXPERIENCES AND RESOURCES THAT BUILD THEIR CAPACITY TO PLAN, DESIGN, AND DELIVER ENGAGING PUBLIC PROGRAMS. THE PROJECT WILL DESIGN AN EFFECTIVE AND ENGAGING ONLINE LEARNING HUB FOR LIBRARY WORKERS; PROTOTYPE MULTIMEDIA CONTENT THAT HIGHLIGHTS OUTSTANDING REAL-WORLD LIBRARY PROGRAMMING; CONDUCT A THOROUGH MIXED-METHODS EVALUATION; AND COMPLETE ALL THE ADVANCE WORK NEEDED TO PROCEED INTO FULL PRODUCTION OF THE PROGRAMMING LIBRARIAN LEARNING LAB. IN ITS FINAL FORM, THIS COMPREHENSIVE SET OF FREE LEARNING MATERIALS, ALL DEDICATED TO THE ADVANCEMENT OF SKILLS-BUILDING FOR LIBRARY PROGRAMMING, WILL PROVIDE MUCH-NEEDED FOUNDATIONAL LEARNING LIBRARY WORKERS NATIONWIDE WHOSE WORK INVOLVES CONCEIVING, PLANNING, AND EXECUTING PROGRAMS FOR THEIR COMMUNITIES
description.4239: THE ASSOCIATION OF MOVING IMAGE ARCHIVISTS, ON BEHALF OF THE AUTISTIC VOICES ORAL HISTORY PROJECT AND IN COLLABORATION WITH THE ASSOCIATION FOR AUTISM AND NEURODIVERSITY, WILL TRAIN ARCHIVISTS ON AUTISTIC COMMUNICATION TO IMPROVE THEIR ABILITY TO INCLUSIVELY SERVE THEIR COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO EQUIP AUTISTIC INDIVIDUALS WITH ORAL HISTORY SKILLS TO ENABLE THEM TO ACTIVELY PARTICIPATE IN DOCUMENTING AND CO-CURATING THEIR LIVED EXPERIENCES TO INCREASE REPRESENTATION OF AUTISTIC NARRATIVES IN THE HISTORIC RECORD. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE TWO WORKSHOPS, A COLLECTION OF 48 ORAL HISTORIES, AND ENHANCED METADATA FOR ACCESSIBILITY. EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE IMPROVED PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES AND INCLUSIVE DOCUMENTATION OF AUTISTIC NARRATIVES. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE MEMORY WORKERS AND THE AUTISTIC COMMUNITY.
description.4240: THE UNIVERSITY CORPORATION FOR ADVANCED INTERNET DEVELOPMENT, INTERNET2 COMMUNITY ANCHOR PROGRAM WILL PARTNER WITH COMMUNITIES TO SCALE THE ADOPTION OF THE TOWARD GIGABIT LIBRARIES TOOLKIT TO SUPPORT THE SELF-TRANSFORMATION OF TRIBAL, NATIVE HAWAIIAN, AND NATIVE ALASKAN LIBRARY STAFF INTO INFORMED CONSUMERS, ADVOCATES, AND PROVIDERS OF TECHNOLOGY, INTERNET ACCESS, AND DIGITAL SERVICES. USING THE TOOLKIT, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE FREE, ACCESSIBLE TECH TRAINING/PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR ALL INDIGENOUS LIBRARY STAFF. TRIBAL, NATIVE HAWAIIAN, AND NATIVE ALASKAN LIBRARIES, ORGANIZATIONS, AND COMMUNITIES WILL HELP OTHER LIBRARIES LEVERAGE LANDMARK INFRASTRUCTURE AND E-RATE FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES TO MAKE TECHNOLOGY AND CONNECTIVITY ADVANCEMENTS.
description.4241: THE ASSOCIATION OF RESEARCH LIBRARIES (ARL) WILL ENGAGE STAKEHOLDERS BY SOCIALIZING A SET OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) FUTURE SCENARIOS FOR RESEARCH LIBRARIES AND THE RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT. SCENARIO PLANNING IS A STRATEGY-RELATED METHODOLOGY THAT EXAMINE LONG-TERM ASSUMPTIONS AND EXPLORE UNCERTAIN LANDSCAPES OF FUTURE ENVIRONMENTS. THIS PROJECT BUILDS ON A JOINT ARL AND COALITION FOR NETWORKED INFORMATION PROJECT WHICH HAS ALREADY DEVELOPED 4 SCENARIOS. LEVERAGING THESE RECENTLY PREPARED SCENARIOS, ARL WILL DEVELOP A SERIES FOR EDUCATIONAL AND OUTREACH EVENTS TO ASSIST SENIOR LEADERS ACROSS THE COUNTRY TO HELP ALL RESEARCH LIBRARIES AND ARCHIVES BE MORE PROACTIVE ABOUT AN AI-INFLUENCED FUTURE. THEY WILL HOST A 2-DAY NATIONAL FORUM, DEVELOP AND PUBLISH AN AI SCENARIO PLANNING TOOLKIT, AND HOST FOUR WORKSHOPS TO TRAIN LIBRARY LEADERS IN HOW TO DEPLOY THE TOOLKIT WITHIN THEIR OWN CONTEXTS. THIS PROJECT WILL ENGAGE LIBRARY LEADERS TO ENSURE THAT ACADEMIC LIBRARIES NATIONWIDE REMAIN RELEVANT AND CRITICAL FOR OUR COMMUNITIES IN THE NEXT DECADE AND BEYOND.
description.4242: THE WYOMING DEPARTMENT OF STATE PARKS AND CULTURAL RESOURCES WILL USE THE FUNDS TO IMPROVE PRESERVATION OF AND EXPAND ACCESS TO THE COLLECTIONS ASSOCIATED WITH THE VORE BUFFALO JUMP ARCHAEOLOGICAL SITE, USED BY NORTHWESTERN PLAINS TRIBES AS A BISON TRAP FROM ABOUT 1550 CE TO THE LATE 1700S. THE COLLECTIONS FROM THIS SITE COMPRISE SOME 23,000 FAUNAL REMAINS AND LITHIC ARTIFACTS, WHICH HAVE BEEN CORE TO CROSS-DISCIPLINARY STUDIES OF THIS HUNTING TECHNIQUE IN ARCHAEOLOGY, GEOLOGY, AND BIOLOGY. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS ISSUES OF COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT, CARE, PRESERVATION, AND ACCESS BY CLEANING, CATALOGING, ASSESSING CONDITIONS OF, CREATING PROPER STORAGE MOUNTS FOR, AND REHOUSING ARTIFACTS CREATING 2D AND 3D HIGH-RESOLUTION IMAGES OF SIGNIFICANT AND DIAGNOSTIC MATERIALS REORGANIZING AND DIGITIZING ARCHIVAL RECORDS LINKING RECORDS TO ARTIFACTS AND SPECIMENS AND MAKING IMAGES AND INFORMATION AVAILABLE ELECTRONICALLY THROUGH A TIERED ACCESS SYSTEM, REFLECTING TRIBAL AND STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION. THE PROJECT WILL BE MATCHED WITH $158,403 IN NON-FEDERAL SHARE.
description.4243: THE MISSISSIPPI DEPARTMENT OF ARCHIVES AND HISTORY WILL PRESERVE ITS ARCHAEOLOGICAL COLLECTIONS, WHICH REPRESENT OVER 14,000 YEARS OF THE STATE'S PAST. THE DEPARTMENT WILL RELOCATE ALL OFFSITE ARTIFACTS TO A NEW STORAGE FACILITY AND CATALOG THE COLLECTIONS FROM THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER DELTA REGION-WHICH IS ESTIMATED TO INCLUDE OBJECTS FROM OVER 500 SITES. THE PROJECT DESIGN WILL ENHANCE COLLECTIONS DOCUMENTATION BY INCORPORATING NATIVE AMERICAN PERSPECTIVES ON THE OBJECTS' CULTURAL USES. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL PREPARE THE COLLECTIONS FOR CURATION BY REHOUSING ALL ARTIFACTS AND RECORDS, AND EXPAND TRIBAL, PUBLIC, AND INSTITUTIONAL ACCESS TO THE COLLECTIONS TO SHARE STORIES FOCUSED ON MISSISSIPPI'S HISTORY AND CULTURE.
description.4244: THE NEVADA NORTHERN RAILWAY FOUNDATION WILL IMPROVE THE LONG-TERM PRESERVATION OF ITS BUSINESS RECORDS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL RENOVATE THE STORAGE SPACE HOUSING THE RECORDS OF THE RAILROAD, PRIMARILY THROUGH INSTALLATION OF COMPACT SHELVING, IN ADDITION TO ORGANIZING AND REHOUSING THE ARCHIVAL MATERIALS. THE COLLECTION INCLUDES CONDUCTOR'S REPORTS, PURCHASING AND ACCOUNTING LEDGERS, COMMISSARY RECORDS, DISPATCHER'S BOOKS, BLUEPRINTS, CORRESPONDENCE, ACCIDENT REPORTS, MAPS, AND TIMETABLES. THE COLLECTION REPRESENTS A COMPREHENSIVE RESOURCE FOR THE STUDY OF THE RAILROAD INDUSTRY IN THE U.S. IN THE TWENTIETH CENTURY, AS WELL AS THE STORIES OF THE INDIVIDUALS WHO WORKED FOR IT BY ENCOMPASSING THE WHOLE HISTORY OF THE NEVADA RAILROAD--FROM PLANNING TO TECHNOLOGICAL CHANGES TO ITS EVENTUAL DISSOLUTION.
description.4245: THE VERMONT DEPARTMENT OF BUILDING AND GENERAL SERVICES WILL CONSERVE SCULPTURE ON THE HIGHWAY, AN OUTDOOR COLLECTION OF SIXTEEN MONUMENTAL MARBLE AND CONCRETE SCULPTURES WHICH WERE CREATED AT TWO INTERNATIONAL SCULPTURE SYMPOSIA HELD IN VERMONT DURING THE SUMMERS OF 1968 AND 1971. THE SYMPOSIA, MODELED AFTER PREVIOUS EVENTS IN EUROPE, SOUTH AFRICA, AND THE MIDDLE EAST, BROUGHT ARTISTS FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD TO THE GREEN MOUNTAINS TO LIVE AND WORK TOGETHER IN AN OPEN STUDIO ENVIRONMENT. THE LARGE-SCALE WORKS WERE CREATED WITH BOTH NATIVE VERMONT MARBLE, AND ALSO FROM LOCALLY MANUFACTURED CONCRETE. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL CLEAN, REPAIR, AND STABILIZE EACH SCULPTURE, TO MITIGATE THE EFFECTS OF CONCRETE DETERIORATION INVOLVING INCLUDES CRACKING, SPALLING, WATER INFILTRATION, AND EXPOSED STEEL REINFORCEMENT.
description.4246: THE FRIENDS OF SUMNER SCHOOL MUSEUM AND ARCHIVES WILL USE FUNDS TO UNDERTAKE CONSERVATION TREATMENTS FOR THE LONG-TERM CARE, PRESERVATION, AND ACCESS OF 11 OBJECTS IN ITS COLLECTION. THE MUSEUM HOLDS APPROXIMATELY 670 OBJECTS ON DISPLAY AND OVER 16,000 LINEAR FEET OF MATERIALS IN STORAGE THAT DOCUMENT THE HISTORY OF D.C. PUBLIC EDUCATION FROM ITS INCEPTION IN 1804 TO THE PRESENT, INCLUDING INFORMATION RELATED TO THE INSTRUCTION OF AFRICAN AMERICAN STUDENTS. AFTER CONSERVATION TREATMENTS ARE COMPLETED, THE MATERIALS WILL BE DIGITIZED, REHOUSED, AND RETURNED TO THE MUSEUM FOR FUTURE USE IN MUSEUM EXHIBITION AND BY SCHOLARS OF D.C. HISTORY.
description.4247: THE HUTCHINGS MUSEUM WILL CATALOG, ARCHIVE, DIGITIZE, AND CREATE 3D MODELS OF NATIVE AMERICAN AND BUFFALO SOLDIER RELATED ARTIFACTS IN ITS COLLECTION. THE COLLECTION INCLUDES A VARIETY OF ARTIFACTS THAT HIGHLIGHT NATIVE AMERICAN AND BLACK HISTORIES IN THE 19TH AND 20TH CENTURIES, AS WELL AS THE HISTORY OF UTAH. FOR THIS PROJECT, MUSEUM STAFF WILL DIGITIZE WAX CYLINDER AUDIO RECORDINGS, UPDATE COLLECTION RECORDS, AND REHOUSE OBJECTS. ADDITIONALLY, STAFF WILL PROVIDE FURTHER INTERPRETATION OF THE OBJECTS THROUGH HISTORICAL RESEARCH AND DISPLAY. AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT, STAFF WILL CREATE PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE IN-PERSON AND DIGITAL EXHIBITS THAT WILL INCLUDE AN INTERACTIVE TIMELINE OF THE OBJECTS IN ITS COLLECTION.
description.4248: THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA, LABORATORY OF ARCHAEOLOGY WILL USE FUNDS TO REHOUSE AND DIGITIZE ITS PALEOENVIRONMENTAL ARCHIVES FROM GEORGIA’S COASTAL ZONE. THE COLLECTIONS INCLUDE ARTIFACTS AND DOCUMENTARY ARCHIVES ABOUT NATIVE AMERICAN HISTORY, REPRESENTED BY EXCAVATIONS ON GEORGIA'S BARRIER ISLANDS AND ADJACENT MAINLAND AREAS AND PERTAINING TO NATIVE AMERICAN SITES FROM 4500 YEARS AGO TO THE 17TH CENTURY. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL WORK WITH TWO GRADUATE STUDENTS, FIVE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, AND A DATABASE CONSULTANT TO INVENTORY, REHOUSE, AND DIGITIZE COLLECTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, STAFF WILL CONSULT WITH MEMBERS OF DESCENDENT COMMUNITIES RELATED TO THE MATERIAL HISTORIES OF THE ARTIFACTS, SUCH AS MEMBERS OF THE GEECHEE (SAPELO ISLAND AND PINPOINT COMMUNITY) AND THE PEOPLE OF THE MUSCOGEE NATION.
description.4249: THE COLLEGE OF NEW JERSEY WILL UNDERTAKE A PROJECT TO PROCESS, REHOUSE, AND DESCRIBE APPROXIMATELY 200 LINEAR FEET OF UNPROCESSED MATERIALS DOCUMENTING THE HISTORY OF THE COLLEGE, WHICH WAS FOUNDED AS NEW JERSEY STATE NORMAL SCHOOL AND IS THE SECOND OLDEST TEACHER TRAINING COLLEGE IN NEW JERSEY. THE COLLECTIONS INCLUDE MATERIALS DEMONSTRATING HOW TEACHING PRE-ELEMENTARY, ELEMENTARY, AND SECONDARY STUDENTS IN THE UNITED STATES HAS CHANGED OVER TIME. FOR THE PROJECT, A NEWLY HIRED PROJECT ARCHIVIST AND GRADUATE ASSISTANT WILL WORK WITH STAFF TO DIGITIZE ARCHIVES AND MIGRATE DATA TO A NEW SERVER. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, DIGITIZED MATERIALS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE THROUGH AN ONLINE COLLECTIONS HUB FOR PUBLIC USE.
description.4250: THE WHARTON ESHERICK MUSEUM WILL UNDERTAKE THE CONSERVATION OF WORKS ON PAPER AND RELATED ARCHIVAL MATERIALS OF WHARTON ESHERICK, A FOUNDATIONAL FIGURE IN TWENTIETH-CENTURY CONTEMPORARY CRAFT AND AMERICAN MODERN DESIGN. FOLLOWING A RECENT CONSERVATION SURVEY OF THE MUSEUM’S ARCHIVAL COLLECTIONS AND WORKS ON PAPER, MUSEUM STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONSERVATION TEAM TO COORDINATE THE TREATMENT AND REHOUSING OF OBJECTS IN THE COLLECTION, INCLUDING SKETCHES, PRINTS, PASTELS, AND WATERCOLORS. ONCE TREATMENT OF THE OBJECTS IN THE COLLECTION IS COMPLETED, STAFF WILL UPDATE COLLECTION RECORDS, AND STABILIZED OBJECTS WILL BE UTILIZED FOR FUTURE RESEARCH PURPOSES.
description.4251: THE INTERNATIONAL MUSEUM OF THE HORSE WILL ADDRESS CONSERVATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS PERTAINING TO THE CARE OF THEIR COLLECTION OF EQUESTRIAN ARTIFACTS. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE AN OBJECTS CONSERVATOR WHO SPECIALIZES IN LEATHER CONSERVATION, AND FIVE CONSERVATION TECHNICIANS WHO WILL TREAT LEATHER ARTIFACTS DAMAGED BY MOLD. THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL REHOUSE OBJECTS AND UPDATE RELEVANT OBJECT DATA AND PHOTO DOCUMENTATION IN THE COLLECTIONS DATABASE. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE THE ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH THESE COLLECTIONS ARE HOUSED THROUGH THE USE OF AIR FILTRATION DEVICES AND CLEANING OF THE COLLECTIONS STORAGE SPACE. CONSERVATION TREATMENTS WILL STABILIZE OBJECTS IN THE COLLECTION SO THAT THEY CAN THEN BE UTILIZED FOR FUTURE EXHIBITION, PROGRAMMING, AND RESEARCH PURPOSES AS WELL AS FOR LOANS TO OTHER MUSEUMS.
description.4252: THE SHELBURNE MUSEUM WILL ASSESS AND RESEARCH A COLLECTION OF NATIVE AMERICAN OBJECTS RECENTLY ACQUIRED BY THE MUSEUM. THE COLLECTION OF APPROXIMATELY 200 ITEMS DATING FROM THE LATE 18TH TO THE MID-20TH CENTURIES INCLUDES POTTERY, GARMENTS, FOOTWEAR, DOLLS, AND OTHER ITEMS PREDOMINANTLY FROM PLAINS, PRAIRIE, AND SOUTHWEST PEOPLES. FOR THE PROJECT, CONSERVATION AND COLLECTIONS STAFF WILL CONDUCT INITIAL OUTREACH TO NATIVE AMERICAN TRIBES REPRESENTED IN THE COLLECTION. STAFF WILL TRAVEL TO CATALOG AND CONDUCT A CONDITION ASSESSMENT OF THE ITEMS. ADDITIONALLY, STAFF WILL ORGANIZE 6 COLLABORATIVE DISCUSSIONS WITH NATIVE AMERICAN PARTNERS TO BE RECORDED AND STORED IN THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTIONS DATABASE.
description.4253: THE MISSISSIPPI DEPARTMENT OF ARCHIVES AND HISTORY WILL USE GRANT FUNDS TO INVENTORY, CATALOG, REHOUSE, AND PREPARE A COLLECTION OF ARCHAEOLOGICAL ARTIFACTS FOR CURATION. THE COLLECTION CONTAINS ARTIFACTS FROM MORE THAN 2,000 DISTINCT SITES ACROSS MISSISSIPPI, REPRESENTING THE 14,000-YEAR HISTORY OF HUMAN OCCUPATION IN THE SOUTHEAST.  STAFF ARCHEOLOGISTS WILL SUPERVISE THE PROJECT, INCLUDING CONSULTATION WITH SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS AND CONSERVATORS. A NEWLY HIRED COLLECTIONS MANAGER WILL CATALOG COLLECTIONS AND CREATE DIGITIZED RECORDS IN A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL PURCHASE NEW COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE, AND UPGRADE EQUIPMENT, INCLUDING THE PURCHASE COMPUTERS, STORAGE FOR SENSITIVE ARTIFACTS, AND A FLOTATION TANK TO PROCESS SOIL SAMPLES WITHIN THE COLLECTION.
description.4254: POETS HOUSE WILL PRESERVE ANALOG AND DIGITAL CONTENT DOCUMENTING THE NATION’S POETIC ACTIVITY OVER THE PAST 80 YEARS. THE ARCHIVAL MATERIALS INCLUDE POETS HOUSE’S OWN PROGRAM HISTORY, HISTORICAL RECORDINGS FROM LIVE EVENTS AT THE NUYORICAN POETS CAFÉ, A NEW YORK VENUE FOR SLAM AND PERFORMANCE POETRY; RADIO BROADCASTS OF POETS READING THEIR WORKS FROM THE 1940S AND 1950S AND RECORDINGS OF OTHER POETRY VENUES FROM THE 1990S AND EARLY 2000S. PROJECT STAFF WILL REPAIR AND DIGITIZE VIDEO AND AUDIO RECORDINGS CURRENTLY HOUSED ON AGING HARD DRIVES AND DIGITIZE HUNDREDS OF ANALOG RECORDINGS. THE MUSEUM WILL INDEX AND CROSS-REFERENCE THE MATERIALS WITH THE REST OF ITS MEDIA COLLECTION AND ADD THEM TO ITS DIGITAL CATALOG. THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT LONG-TERM PRESERVATION, WHILE PROVIDING INSIGHTS INTO POETRY TRADITIONS, AESTHETICS, AND CONTEMPORARY POETRY COLLECTIONS FOR POETS, SCHOLARS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.4255: THE ROCHESTER INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY (RIT) WILL USE FUNDS TO RESTORE AND RE-ASSEMBLE THE SCULPTURE, “GOLDEN DANDELIONS,” CREATED BY THE WORLD-RENOWNED ARTIST HARRY BERTOIA. THE EASTMAN KODAK COMPANY COMMISSIONED THE SCULPTURE TO BE THE CENTERPIECE OF A FOUNTAIN AT THE MAIN ENTRANCE TO ITS PAVILION AT THE 1964 NEW YORK WORLD’S FAIR. AFTER MOVING THE SCULPTURE TO RIT, IT BECAME SEVERELY DETERIORATED OVER TIME IN AN OUTDOOR ENVIRONMENT AND IT CURRENTLY REMAINS UNASSEMBLED AND IN STORAGE. CONSERVATORS WILL THOROUGHLY ASSESS AND RESTORE DAMAGE, RECREATE MISSING ELEMENTS, DEVELOP A NEW BASE, AND PROVIDE FOR ITS DISPLAY IN A PROMINENT INDOOR SETTING ON CAMPUS, WHICH WILL ENSURE ITS LONGEVITY.
description.4256: THE UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH CAROLINA WILL USE FUNDS TO PRESERVE ITS COLLECTION OF ORAL HISTORIES, DOCUMENTS, ARTWORK, AND ARTIFACTS AT THE UNIVERSITY’S NATIVE AMERICAN STUDIES CENTER.  STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTOR TO INSTALL ARCHIVAL SHELVING FOR APPROXIMATELY 2,000 OBJECTS, INCLUDING A COLLECTION OF CATAWBA INDIAN POTTERY. AFTER THE REHOUSING OF OBJECTS IN COMPLETED, STAFF WILL DEVELOP A DISASTER PLAN FOR THE COLLECTION BASED ON NEW STORAGE SPECIFICATIONS. ADDITIONALLY FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WITH CONDUCT INTERVIEWS TO RECORD ORAL HISTORIES OF NATIVE COMMUNITIES IN THE LOW COUNTRY AND WILL CURATE A CORRESPONDING EXHIBIT WITH COMMUNITY MEMBERS FROM TRIBES IN SOUTH CAROLINA. DIGITAL MATERIALS AND RECORDS OF THE COLLECTION WILL BE PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE THROUGH THE ONLINE DATABASE, THE SOUTH CAROLINA NATIVE AMERICA ARCHIVE.
description.4257: THE KENTUCKY GEOLOGICAL SURVEY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY WILL CONSERVE MINERAL CORES FROM THE WESTERN KENTUCKY FLUORSPAR AND SOUTH-CENTRAL KENTUCKY MINERAL DISTRICTS ROCK CORE COLLECTION AT THE EARTH ANALYSIS RESEARCH LIBRARY. THE UNIVERSITY WILL HIRE TWO GEOLOGISTS, A GEOLOGIC ARCHIVE TECHNICIAN, AND A PHOTOGRAPHER TO DOCUMENT, CORRELATE METADATA, AND CONSERVE THE MINERAL CORES. PROJECT STAFF WILL OVERSEE COLLECTIONS CARE TASKS, INCLUDING IDENTIFYING THE GEOLOGIC AND MINERAL MAKEUP OF THE CORES, LABELING, AND REHOUSING. ADDITIONALLY, PROJECT STAFF WILL MAKE EXISTING AND NEW DATA ABOUT THE COLLECTION AVAILABLE ONLINE FOR MINERAL DEPOSIT RESEARCHERS IN INDUSTRY AND THE GEOSCIENCES.
description.4258: THE FIREBOAT FIRE FIGHTER MUSEUM WILL OVERSEE THE INSPECTION AND CONSERVATION OF THE HISTORIC FIRE BOAT AND 1973 GALLANT SHIP AWARD WINNER, FIRE FIGHTER. MUSEUM STAFF AND VOLUNTEERS WILL COORDINATE EFFORTS TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF THE HULL AND MITIGATE FUTURE CORROSION OF THE VESSEL. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE REPLACING FIRE MAIN DISCHARGE PIPING TO RESTORE OPERABILITY AND REPLACING STEEL PLATING TO MITIGATE THREATS OF DETERIORATION AND PREVENT FUTURE LEAKAGE. FRAMING SUPPORTS AND UPDATES TO SAFETY FEATURES WILL ENSURE THE SOUNDNESS OF THE VESSEL FOR ACCESS BY VISITORS TO THE MUSEUM AND ITS CONTINUED USE FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES BY THE MUSEUM.
description.4259: THE ALVIN AILEY DANCE FOUNDATION WILL MAKE BALLET ARCHIVAL MATERIAL ACCESSIBLE FOR RESTAGING BY OTHER DANCE COMPANIES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE CATALOGING AND DIGITIZING THE NECESSARY TECHNICAL INFORMATION TO RESTAGE THE BALLETS, COLLECTING AND ANALYZING DRAMATURGICAL CONTENT ON EACH BALLET FOR HISTORIC PRESERVATION, AND DETERMINING THE RIGHTS HOLDERS FOR EACH WORK FOR FUTURE LICENSING OPPORTUNITIES WITH OTHER PROFESSIONAL DANCE COMPANIES AND EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS. THIS COLLECTED MATERIAL, ALONG WITH A MINI DOCUMENTARY WITH DANCER AND PRODUCTION STAFF INTERVIEWS, WILL COMPRISE A “DANCE CAPSULE” THAT WILL BE AVAILABLE THROUGH A NEW ONLINE PORTAL.
description.4260: THE HISTORICAL MEDICAL LIBRARY OF THE COLLEGE OF PHYSICIANS OF PHILADELPHIA WILL USE FUNDS TO CONSERVE, DIGITIZE, AND INCREASE ACCESS TO ITS HISTORY OF VACCINES COLLECTION. THE COLLECTION CONTAINS MATERIALS RELATED TO THE HISTORY OF VACCINATION BETWEEN 1702 AND 1920, INCLUDING MEDICAL PAMPHLETS AND PROMOTIONAL MATERIALS, GOVERNMENTAL DECREES AND LETTERS FROM PHYSICIANS TO ELECTED OFFICIALS, PHYSICIAN LETTERS AND NOTES, AND SCRAPBOOKS DOCUMENTING THE HISTORY OF BOTH VACCINATION AND ANTI-VACCINATION CAMPAIGNS AND EFFORTS. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONSERVATOR TO TREAT AND REHOUSE OBJECTS IN THE COLLECTION. ADDITIONALLY, STAFF WILL CREATE FINDING AIDS FOR THE COLLECTION AND MAKE DIGITAL VERSIONS OF THE COLLECTION MATERIALS DISCOVERABLE ON ONLINE RESEARCH PLATFORMS.
description.4261: AS IT MARKS ITS 40TH ANNIVERSARY, URBAN BUSH WOMEN WILL IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT, PRESERVATION, AND ACCESSIBILITY OF ITS COLLECTIONS. THE ARCHIVAL COLLECTION ENCOMPASSES FOUR DECADES OF RICH HISTORY, DOCUMENTING JAWOLE ZOLLAR’S RESEARCH, CHOREOGRAPHIC NOTES, PERFORMANCE SCRIPTS, SHEET MUSIC, AND DIRECTORS’ NOTES WHICH ZOLLAR ENSURED WERE RETAINED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF HER MANY WORKS. JAWOLE ZOLLAR’S CHOREOGRAPHY WAS AN INFLUENTIAL MOVEMENT IN AMERICAN DANCE HISTORY AND BROUGHT ATTENTION TO RACIAL EQUITY AND SOCIAL JUSTICE. ARCHIVAL FORMATS FROM 1984 TO PRESENT DAY INCLUDE AUDIO/VISUAL MATERIALS, PRINT MATERIALS, PERFORMANCE COSTUMES, TEXTILES, AND MAGNETICS (FLOPPY DISKS AND HARD DRIVES).  A PART-TIME ARCHIVAL ASSISTANT WILL WORK WITH PROJECT STAFF TO PROPERLY DOCUMENT, REHOUSE, AND DIGITIZE THE MATERIALS ACCORDING TO ARCHIVAL STANDARDS.
description.4262: THE COLBURN SCHOOL WILL IMPROVE THE CARE, PRESERVATION, AND ACCESSIBILITY OF THE HERBERT AND TRUDL ZIPPER ARCHIVE, THE ZIPPERS WERE AUSTRIAN-BORN IMMIGRANTS TO THE UNITED STATES, RENOWNED AS INNOVATIVE PERFORMING ARTISTS AND TEACHERS WHO MADE A DEEP IMPACT ON THE CLASSICAL MUSIC, DANCE, AND EDUCATION FIELDS. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE THE SCHOOL’S INTELLECTUAL CONTROL OVER THE COLLECTION BY CREATING ARTIFACT DESCRIPTIONS AND A FINDING AID. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DIGITIZE AND REHOUSE A MAJORITY OF THE COLLECTION, WHICH CONTRIBUTES TO THE NATION’S HISTORY OF CLASSICAL MUSIC EDUCATION AND MODERN DANCE, AS WELL AS HOLOCAUST HISTORY AND THE JEWISH IMMIGRANT STORY.
description.4263: THE ARHOOLIE FOUNDATION WILL PRESERVE ITS COLLECTION OF MATERIALS RELATED TO THE FOUNDER OF ARHOOLIE RECORDS, CHRIS STRACHWITZ (1931–2023). THE COLLECTION IS COMPRISED OF APPROXIMATELY 500 POSTERS, AND 700 AUDIOVISUAL RECORDINGS DOCUMENTING THE HISTORY OF ARHOOLIE RECORDS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PRIORITIZING MATERIALS FOR DIGITIZATION, DEVELOPING DIGITIZATION STANDARDS, PROCESSING, DIGITIZATION, AND IDENTIFYING A DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR ONLINE DELIVERY OF THE COLLECTION. ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE A DETAILED FINDING AID, A COLLECTION INVENTORY, REHOUSING, AND PLANS FOR DIGITIZATION AND A DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM.
description.4264: THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, BERKELEY’S ART MUSEUM AND PACIFIC FILM ARCHIVE WILL UNDERTAKE A CONSERVATION PROJECT FOR APPROXIMATELY 1,800 QUILTS, PIECED FRAGMENTS, AND TEXTILE OBJECT IN ITS AFRICAN AMERICAN QUILTS COLLECTION. THE COLLECTION CONTAINS WORKS BY MORE THAN 500 INDIVIDUAL QUILTERS AND NINE INTERGENERATIONAL FAMILIES. CONSERVATION WORK FOR THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE TREATMENTS TO REMOVE MICROBIAL, MOLD AND INSECT INFESTATIONS, CAREFUL CLEANING AND DRYING, AND REHOUSING OF OBJECTS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE QUILTS AND RELATED MATERIAL FROM THE COLLECTION WILL BE PRESERVED FOR FUTURE RESEARCH, EDUCATIONAL, AND EXHIBITION PURPOSES.
description.4265: THE NATIONAL MODEL AVIATION MUSEUM WILL HIRE A COLLECTIONS MANAGER TO DIGITIZE, CATALOG, AND REHOUSE THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION OF AVIATION MODELS AND RELATED MATERIALS, INCLUDING MAGAZINES, DOCUMENTS, PHOTOGRAPHS, AND NEGATIVES. THE NEW HIRE WILL HELP IMPROVE THE MUSEUM’S STEWARDSHIP OF THEIR COLLECTION AND INCREASE THE MUSEUM’S INTELLECTUAL CONTROL OF THE MATERIAL. STAFF WILL ENTER COLLECTIONS INFORMATION INTO A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE AND MAKE DIGITIZED MATERIALS ACCESSIBLE ONLINE FOR RESEARCH PURPOSES.
description.4266: INDEPENDENCE COMMUNITY COLLEGE WILL CREATE AND MAKE PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE A COMPREHENSIVE ONLINE CATALOG OF ARCHIVAL ASSETS FEATURING SIGNIFICANT PLAYWRIGHTS, PERFORMING ARTISTS, AND ORIGINAL MANUSCRIPTS FROM THE WILLIAM INGE COLLECTION. THE COLLECTION INCLUDES TWO FOCUS AREAS: OVER 400 WORKS WRITTEN AND CREATED BY PLAYWRIGHT AND SCREEN WRITER WILLIAM INGE AND APPROXIMATELY 400 RECORDED INTERVIEWS WITH LEADING PLAYWRIGHTS AND STAGE ARTISTS WHO HAVE TAKEN PART IN THE WILLIAM INGE THEATRE FESTIVAL. WILLIAM INGE (1913-1973) WAS AN AWARD-WINNING WRITER WHOSE WORK WAS PRIMARILY SET IN SMALL TOWNS. ONCE COMPLETE, THE ONLINE RESOURCE WILL INCREASE PUBLIC ACCESSIBILITY TO HISTORIC MATERIALS RELATED TO THEATRICAL WRITERS AND PERFORMERS.
description.4267: THE CAPITAL CITY MUSEUM WILL REHOUSE ITS COLLECTION OF APPROXIMATELY 20,000 OBJECTS DOCUMENTING THE HISTORY OF FRANKFORT AND FRANKLIN COUNTY, KENTUCKY. MUSEUM STAFF WILL INVENTORY AND REHOUSE COLLECTIONS IN ARCHIVAL-QUALITY CONTAINERS AND WITH STORAGE FURNITURE AS WELL AS PURCHASE A FREEZER FOR MOLD MITIGATION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL MITIGATE RISKS AND PROLONG THE USEFUL LIFE OF COLLECTIONS, WHICH THE MUSEUM SHARES WITH THE PUBLIC THROUGH EXHIBITS AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING. FOLLOWING THE COMPLETION OF THE PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL OFFER VISITOR TOURS OF STORAGE AREAS TO PROMOTE EDUCATION ABOUT COLLECTION STEWARDSHIP.
description.4268: THE SPECIAL COLLECTIONS AND ARCHIVES OF THE ROLVAAG LIBRARY AT ST. OLAF COLLEGE WILL PRESERVE AND DIGITIZE ITS COLLECTION OF NORWEGIAN-AMERICAN IMPRINTS, WHICH REFER TO THE “THE GREAT SETTLING,” WHEN ONE-THIRD OF THE NORWEGIAN POPULATION EMIGRATED TO THE UNITED STATES IN THE LATE 19TH TO EARLY 20TH CENTURY. THE COLLECTION INCLUDES MONOGRAPHS, ANNUALS, MONTHLY PERIODICALS, AND DAILY OR WEEKLY NEWS PUBLICATIONS COMPRISING OF APPROXIMATELY 4,000 TITLES AND 7,700 CATALOG ITEMS. THE COLLEGE WILL HIRE A COLLECTIONS ASSOCIATE POSITION TO WORK WITH CONSERVATORS TO PREPARE CONDITION REPORTS, TREAT THE MATERIALS, AND DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION.
description.4269: THE ASHEVILLE ART MUSEUM WILL CONSERVE, PRESERVE, AND DIGITIZE A PORTION OF ITS COLLECTION OF ARTWORKS RELATED TO WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA, SOUTHERN APPALACHIA, AND THE SOUTHEASTERN REGION. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES 148 OBJECTS OF APPALACHIAN HISTORICAL AND CONTEMPORARY WORK, INCLUDING WORKS BY BLACK MOUNTAIN COLLEGE STUDENTS AND FACULTY AND SELF-TAUGHT ARTISTS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE CLEANING AND REPAIR OF PAINTINGS AND WORKS ON PAPER AND REPAIRING CHIPPED OR BROKEN CERAMICS, IN ADDITION TO PHOTOGRAPHY AND DIGITIZATION. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT VISITORS, STUDENTS, AND SCHOLARS AND INCREASED DIGITAL ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION FOR THE PUBLIC.
description.4270: THE QUEENS MUSEUM OF ART WILL CARRY OUT A CONSERVATION PROJECT FOR THE PANORAMA OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK, A LARGE-SCALE MODEL OF NEW YORK CITY THAT WAS BUILT FOR THE 1964-1965 NEW YORK WORLD’S FAIR.  THE MODEL WAS CREATED BY MORE THAN 100 ARTISANS, COVERS AN AREA OF 9,335 SQUARE FEET, AND CONTAINS 895,000 BUILDINGS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE AN OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE MODEL’S 272 PANELS AS WELL AS REPAINTING AND REINFORCEMENT OF THE STRUCTURAL SUPPORT. CONSERVATORS WILL ALSO REPAIR THE LIGHTING SYSTEM WITHIN THE MODEL, WHICH CODES FOR DIFFERENT BUILDING FUNCTIONS. WHEN RESTORED, THE MODEL WILL BE A RESOURCE FOR HISTORIANS AND RESEARCHERS OF NEW YORK CITY HISTORY.
description.4271: THE MUSEUM OF THE BIG BEND AT SUL ROSS STATE UNIVERSITY WILL IMPROVE THE STORAGE OF ITS COLLECTION OF HISTORIC MAPS. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A CURATOR OF CARTOGRAPHIC COLLECTIONS TO SUPERVISE THE PROJECT AND WORK WITH A CARTOGRAPHIC CONSULTANT. THE CURATOR WILL RESEARCH COLLECTION PROVENANCE, ENGAGE IN PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES WITH PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND DEVELOP A CATALOG OF THE COLLECTION. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES IN THE COLLECTIONS STORAGE AREA THAT THREATEN THE CONDITION OF THE COLLECTION. IMPROVED LONG-TERM COLLECTIONS STORAGE WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED PRESERVATION FOR THE COLLECTION, ADDITIONAL STUDY SPACE, AND INCREASED ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION FOR THE PURPOSES OF EXHIBITION AND RESEARCH.
description.4272: THE LEWIS GINTER BOTANICAL GARDEN WILL REHOUSE AND STORE THE LORA M. ROBINS LIBRARY COLLECTIONS AND ARCHIVES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE INSTALLATION OF A COMPACT STORAGE SYSTEM WITH CLOSED STORAGE FOR RARE BOOKS, CABINETS FOR WORKS ON PAPER, SHELVING FOR OBJECTS AND ARCHIVAL BOXES, AND ART RACKS FOR HANGING FRAMED WORKS. THE COLLECTION CONTAINS ORIGINAL WATERCOLOR BOTANICAL ILLUSTRATIONS, HERBARIUM SPECIMENS, AND WATERCOLORS FROM THE LEE MEMORIAL PARK WILDFLOWER AND BIRD SANCTUARY, AND APPROXIMATELY 300 VOLUMES OF BOTANICAL AND HORTICULTURAL BOOKS WITH AN EMPHASIS ON THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION. THE REHOUSING PROCESS WILL ALLOW STAFF TO ASSESS THE CONDITION AND DOCUMENTATION OF EACH COLLECTION ITEM AS IT IS PROCESSED, WHILE THE OVERALL PROJECT WILL INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY TO THE COLLECTIONS FOR RESEARCH, EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING, DIGITIZATION, AND EXHIBITION PURPOSES.
description.4273: THE VIRGINIA DEPARTMENT OF HISTORIC RESOURCES WILL CONSERVE ARTIFACTS RECOVERED FROM EXCAVATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ENSLAVED PEOPLE LIVING AT KINGSMILL AND ASSOCIATED 17TH AND 18TH CENTURY PLANTATION SITES. INFORMED BY A COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT, THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE CREATING A CONSERVATION PLAN FOR OBJECTS, THE MAJORITY OF WHICH ARE MADE OF METAL. CURATORIAL AND CONSERVATION STAFF WILL CONSERVE DETERIORATING ARTIFACTS, REHOUSE OBJECTS WITH ARCHIVAL MATERIALS, AND CATALOGUE THE COLLECTION. STAFF WILL UTILIZE THE COLLECTION FOR EXHIBITION PURPOSES AND WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO THE COLLECTION FOR RESEARCHERS, STUDENTS, AND EDUCATORS. PROJECT STAFF WILL ALSO SHARE THE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT AT A PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCE.
description.4274: THE HENRY ART GALLERY WILL IMPROVE THE STORAGE OF AND ACCESS TO ITS ART COLLECTION. DURING THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL REHOUSE TWO SUBSETS OF THE HENRY’S COLLECTION: 107 PAINTINGS IN THE FOUNDER'S COLLECTION BY ARTISTS SUCH AS WINSLOW HOMER, GEORGE INNESS, AND MARIE ROSALIE BONHEUR AS WELL AS 250 RECENTLY ACQUIRED LARGE-SCALE FRAMED PHOTOGRAPHS AND WORKS ON PAPER BY ARTISTS, INCLUDING NAN GOLDIN, EIRIK JOHNSON, AND ANDY WARHOL. INFORMED BY A PREVIOUS COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE THE INSTALLATION OF A HIGH-DENSITY MOBILE ART RACK SYSTEM. ONCE COMPLETE, THE ARTWORKS WILL BE LESS VULNERABLE TO DAMAGE AND MORE AVAILABLE FOR EXHIBITION, WORKSHOP, AND RESEARCH PURPOSES.
description.4275: THE WISCONSIN HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL PRESERVE AND PROVIDE ACCESS TO AT-RISK MATERIALS IN 26 COLLECTIONS DOCUMENTING THE MODERN AMERICAN CIVIL RIGHTS MOVEMENT. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF SELECTED MATERIALS FOR CONSERVATION AND DIGITIZATION THAT ARE MOST FREQUENTLY REQUESTED FOR RESEARCH PURPOSES, INCLUDING APPROXIMATELY 490 CUBIC FEET OF ARCHIVES WHICH INCLUDE 2,412 AUDIO RECORDINGS, 445 MOVING IMAGES, 101 MICROFILM REELS, AND MORE THAN 22 CUBIC FT OF GRAPHIC MATERIALS, SUCH AS PHOTOGRAPHS, POSTERS, AND EPHEMERA. THE HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL STABILIZE, REHOUSE, AND PERFORM CONSERVATION TREATMENTS ON AT-RISK PHYSICAL ITEMS. STAFF WILL DIGITIZE COLLECTION ITEMS AND MAKE THEM ACCESSIBLE ONLINE FOR PUBLIC USE.
description.4276: THE PHILBROOK MUSEUM OF ART WILL SAFEGUARD AND PRESERVE ITS NATIVE ART COLLECTION, WHICH INCLUDES WORKS OF 20TH-CENTURY BASKETRY, POTTERY, PAINTINGS, AND JEWELRY. STAFF WILL WORK WITH CONSULTANTS TO COORDINATE THE INSTALLATION OF FIRE SUPPRESSION AND NEW SMOKE DETECTION SYSTEMS, AS WELL AS OUTFITTING STORAGE AND GALLERY AREAS WITH SECURITY CAMERAS AND ACCESS CONTROL PANELS. THE PRESERVATION OF THE MUSEUM’S NATIVE HOLDINGS WILL ENSURE THE COLLECTION IS AVAILABLE FOR VISITORS AND CULTURAL RESEARCHERS AND WILL CONTINUE TO INFORM EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING AND FUTURE EXHIBITIONS.
description.4277: THE PALEY CENTER FOR MEDIA WILL DIGITIZE AND CATALOG APPROXIMATELY 2,500 ITEMS FROM ITS COLLECTION PERTAINING TO AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY. THE COLLECTION HOLDS RARE AND AT-RISK TELEVISION MEDIA AND HISTORIC PROGRAMMING FEATURING FIGURES SUCH AS NAT KING COLE, BAYARD RUSTIN, BERNARD SHAW, TONI MORRISON, CONGRESSWOMAN BARBARA JORDAN, AND OPRAH WINFREY. THE PALEY CENTER FOR MEDIA WILL WORK WITH MULTIPLE VENDORS TO PRESERVE AND DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION. THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL MAINTAIN ASSOCIATED COLLECTION METADATA. ONCE DIGITIZED, THESE MATERIALS WILL BE USED BY THE PALEY EDUCATION STAFF FOR ITS K-12 MEDIA EDUCATION PROGRAM AND FOR PUBLIC EXHIBITS.
description.4278: THE BLACKWATER DRAW MUSEUM AT EASTERN NEW MEXICO UNIVERSITY WILL UPDATE ITS INVENTORY AND REHOUSE MATERIAL FROM THE BLACKWATER DRAW ARCHAEOLOGY SITE, WHICH DOCUMENTS CULTURAL ACTIVITY FROM CLOVIS TIMES (OVER 13,000 YEARS AGO) THROUGH THE RECENT HISTORIC PERIOD. THE COLLECTION INCLUDES ARTIFACTS, STONE TOOL TECHNOLOGY, DOCUMENTS, AND PHOTOS FROM THE LAST 94 YEARS OF RESEARCH AT THE SITE. THIS PROJECT WILL PRESERVE APPROXIMATELY 2,790 ARTIFACTS, 870 PHOTOGRAPH NEGATIVES, AND 1,356 35 MM NEGATIVE FILM STRIPS. STAFF AND STUDENT EMPLOYEES WILL UPDATE COLLECTIONS RECORDS WITH ASSOCIATED PHOTOGRAPHIC DOCUMENTATION.
description.4279: THE GREATER HUDSON HERITAGE NETWORK WILL WORK WITH 10 SMALL AND MID-SIZE MUSEUMS IN NEW YORK STATE TO CONSERVE OBJECTS FROM THEIR COLLECTIONS. THE OBJECTS INCLUDE 35 ITEMS OF HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE AND A WIDE RANGE OF MATERIALS, WHICH, AFTER A PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT, WERE SELECTED AS OBJECTS MOST IN NEED OF CONSERVATION TREATMENTS. A PANEL OF CONSERVATORS WILL WORK ON THE OBJECTS OVER THE COURSE OF THE PROJECT AND WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT CONSERVATION WORKSHOPS AT EACH MUSEUM. THE CONSERVATION WORKSHOPS WILL PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL TRAINING FOR PARTICIPATING MUSEUM STAFF AND ADDRESS CONSERVATION TOPICS SPECIFIC TO INDIVIDUAL MUSEUM COLLECTIONS.
description.4280: CHROMADIVERSE WILL PRESERVE, DIGITIZE, AND MAKE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC MARGARET ELIZABETH “MARBETH” SCHNARE’S PHOTOGRAPHS OF DANCE THEATRE OF HARLEM. STAFF WILL INVENTORY, TRANSPORT, DIGITIZE, AND REHOUSE THE COLLECTION, WHICH INCLUDES 6,000 PHOTOGRAPHS IN PRINT AND 35MM NEGATIVE FORMATS, AS WELL AS APPROXIMATELY 100 DOCUMENTS. THE PROJECT WILL INVOLVE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A CURATED WEBSITE, ALONG WITH THE CREATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A MARKETING STRATEGY TO SHOWCASE THE COLLECTION TO AUDIENCES ONLINE. ONCE PRESERVED AND MADE ACCESSIBLE, THE COLLECTION WILL BE A RESOURCE FOR GENERAL AUDIENCES AND SCHOLARS INTERESTED IN DANCE THEATRE OF HARLEM, CLASSICAL BALLET, AFRICAN AMERICAN HISTORY, AND THE CULTURAL LIFE OF HARLEM AND NEW YORK CITY.
description.4281: THE AMERICAN JEWISH HISTORICAL SOCIETY WILL PRESERVE RECORDS OF THE ANTI-DEFAMATION LEAGUE’S CIVIL RIGHTS INFORMATION CENTER AND ITS CENTER ON EXTREMISM. THE RECORDS DOCUMENT THE ANTI-DEFAMATION LEAGE’S INITIATIVES TO EXPOSE AND MITIGATE ANTISEMITISM, RACISM, AND OTHER FORMS OF HATE. PROJECT STAFF WILL REHOUSE AND CREATE A FINDING AID FOR APPROXIMATELY 100 LINEAR FEET OF RECORDS, INCLUDING CORRESPONDENCE, RECORDS OF COURT CASES AND LEGISLATION, PERIODICALS, REPORTS, AND RESEARCH FILES. THE SOCIETY WILL HIRE A PROJECT ARCHIVIST TO PROCESS AND DIGITIZE THE COLLECTION, MAKING IT AVAILABLE TO RESEARCHERS BOTH ON-SITE AND ONLINE.
description.4282: THE UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH CAROLINA WILL REHOUSE ARCHAEOLOGICAL MATERIAL FROM ITS CATAWBA-WATEREE COLLECTIONS, WHICH REPRESENT APPROXIMATELY 400 ARCHAEOLOGICAL ASSEMBLAGES FROM EIGHT COUNTIES IN SOUTH CAROLINA THAT PROVIDE DOCUMENTATION OF SITES FROM ALL PERIODS OF HUMAN HABITATION IN THE REGION. IN PREPARATION FOR A MOVE TO A NEW FACILITY ON CAMPUS, PROJECT STAFF WILL SURVEY THE COLLECTIONS AND REPLACE DETERIORATING HOUSING WITH PRESERVATION-QUALITY BAGS, BOXES, AND LABELS. PROJECT STAFF WILL WORK WITH GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE ASSISTANTS TO CATALOG COLLECTIONS IN A COLLECTIONS MANAGEMENT DATABASE. DIGITIZED OBJECTS IN THE NATIVE AMERICAN COLLECTIONS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO DESCENDANT COMMUNITIES.
description.4283: THE NATIONAL BUILDING MUSEUM WILL PRESERVE THE NORTHWESTERN TERRA COTTA COLLECTION, ONE OF THE LARGEST ARCHITECTURAL TERRA COTTA COLLECTIONS IN THE UNITED STATES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PHOTOGRAPHING, CATALOGUING, AND DIGITIZING DRAWINGS, FOCUSING ON DRAWINGS PRODUCED FROM 1924 TO 1956.  FOR THE PROJECT, THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE NEW STAFF TO CONDUCT CONSERVATION ASSESSMENTS AND REHOUSE AT-RISK ITEMS, WORK WITH CONSULTANTS, AND FORM PARTNERSHIPS TO MANAGE THE PRESERVATION AND ACCESSIBILITY OF THE COLLECTION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL IMPROVE PRESERVATION, ACCESSIBILITY, AND KNOWLEDGE OF THE COLLECTION, BENEFITING RESEARCHERS, EDUCATORS, AND THE PUBLIC.
description.4284: THE WOODMERE ART MUSEUM WILL CARRY OUT A PROJECT TO STABILIZE AND CONSERVE SIGNIFICANT WORKS IN THEIR COLLECTION BY PHILADELPHIA ARTISTS. THE WOODMERE’S COLLECTION, RANGING FROM THE 18TH CENTURY TO THE PRESENT, IS DEDICATED TO TELLING THE STORY OF PHILADELPHIA'S ART AND ARTISTS FROM GENERATION TO GENERATION. THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH AND CONFIGURE NEW STORAGE SPACES TO RELIEVE COLLECTION OVERCROWDING AS WELL AS IMPLEMENT UPDATED ART STORAGE PRACTICES. STAFF WILL UPDATE THE CATALOGUING SYSTEM AND MOVE, CATALOGUE, AND DIGITIZE WORKS IN THE COLLECTION. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, WORKS BY PHILADELPHIA ARTISTS WILL BE MORE AVAILABLE FOR USE IN EXHIBITIONS AS WELL AS FOR PUBLIC RESEARCH PURPOSES.
description.4285: THE STATEN ISLAND MUSEUM WILL INVENTORY AND REHOUSE APPROXIMATELY 185 LINEAR FEET OF ARCHIVAL MATERIAL IN PREPARATION TO MOVE THE COLLECTIONS INTO A NEW CLIMATE-CONTROLLED STORAGE SPACE. THE COLLECTIONS INCLUDE THE PAPERS OF RENOWNED SCIENTISTS INCLUDING NATHANIEL LORD BRITTON, JOHN J. CROOKE, AND MATHILDE WEINGARTNER. THE ARCHIVES ALSO INCLUDE ARCHAEOLOGICAL DESCRIPTIONS OF LENAPE SITES ON STATEN ISLAND. THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE PURCHASE OF ARCHIVAL SUPPLIES, AS WELL AS A PART-TIME PROJECT ARCHIVIST AND MUSEUM FELLOW, WHO WILL CARRY OUT THE COLLECTION INVENTORY AND REHOUSING ACTIVITIES. ADDITIONALLY, THE MUSEUM WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTOR TO CONSERVE AND DIGITIZE 11 JOURNALS OF WILLIAM T. DAVIS, A PROMINENT NATURALIST, ENTOMOLOGIST, AND HISTORIAN. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED PRESERVATION OF THE COLLECTION, ENHANCED INTELLECTUAL CONTROL, AND THE CREATION OF NEW FINDING AIDS THAT WILL INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY OF THE COLLECTION FOR STAFF AND RESEARCHERS.
description.4286: CLEARY UNIVERSITY WILL PRESERVE AND ENHANCE A COLLECTION OF OVER 800 PIECES BY AMERICAN ARTIST ARTHUR SECUNDA. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE CATALOGING, DIGITIZING, RESTORING, AND FRAMING ARTWORKS, AND CREATING A STABLE STORAGE ENVIRONMENT FOR THE PROTECTION AND ACCESSIBILITY OF OBJECTS. THE UNIVERSITY WILL HIRE A CURATOR, ENGAGE WITH CONSULTANTS, AND ESTABLISH PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL MUSEUMS AND ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS TO FACILITATE RESTORATION AND CONSERVATION EFFORTS. THE CURATOR WILL WORK WITH INTERNS TO CREATE A LONG-TERM PRESERVATION PLAN FOR THE SECUNDA COLLECTION, WHICH WILL INFORM FUTURE IMPROVEMENTS TO THE COLLECTION FOR STUDENTS AND SCHOLARS.
description.4287: MARTHA’S VINEYARD PRESERVATION TRUST WILL UNDERTAKE RESTORATION OF THE FLYING HORSES CAROUSEL, A NATIONAL HISTORIC LANDMARK AND THE OLDEST PLATFORM CAROUSEL IN THE UNITED STATES. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE REPAIR AND RESTORATION OF 16 OF THE CAROUSEL’S 20 HORSES, RESTORATION AND REPLACEMENT OF THE CAROUSEL’S MECHANICAL COMPONENTS, AND RESTORATION OF ITS FOUR SCENIC PANELS. THE PROJECT WILL ENGAGE A STRUCTURAL ENGINEER, RESTORATION CONTRACTORS, AND A PAINTING RESTORATION SPECIALIST TO PROTECT AND PRESERVE THE CAROUSEL WHILE MAINTAINING ITS HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE CAROUSEL WILL BE MORE STRUCTURALLY STABLE AND AVAILABLE FOR USE BY VISITORS.
description.4288: THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS, CHICAGO LIBRARY WILL DIGITIZE, PRESERVE, AND MAKE ACCESSIBLE 781 AUDIO AND VIDEO RECORDINGS FROM THEIR CHICAGO IN THE CITY2000 COLLECTION. THE CITY2000 COLLECTION DOCUMENTS CHICAGO AND ITS INHABITANTS AND NEIGHBORHOODS DURING THE YEAR 2000 THROUGH PHOTOGRAPHS, INTERVIEWS, AND SOUNDSCAPES. PROJECT STAFF AND STUDENT EMPLOYEES WILL ADDRESS PRESERVATION NEEDS FOR COLLECTIONS AT RISK OF DETERIORATION, SUCH AS DIGITAL AUDIO TAPE AND MAGNETIC TAPE. THE UNIVERSITY WILL CONTRACT WITH A VENDOR TO REFORMAT THE MATERIALS, AND PROJECT STAFF WILL MAKE THE MATERIALS AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY’S DIGITAL COLLECTIONS PORTAL. DIGITIZED FILES WILL BE ENHANCED WITH METADATA AS WELL AS AUDIO TRANSCRIPTS FOR INCREASED ACCESSIBILITY.
description.4289: THE NATIONAL MINING HALL OF FAME AND MUSEUM WILL IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT AND CARE OF ITS COLLECTION OF OBJECTS THAT DOCUMENT AMERICAN MINING HISTORY. INFORMED BY A RECENT COLLECTIONS ASSESSMENT FOR PRESERVATION (CAP) REPORT, PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PURCHASING AND INSTALLING NEW DISPLAY CASES, STORAGE SHELVES, BLACKOUT WINDOW BLINDS, AND TOOLS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING OF THE COLLECTION SPACE. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN ENVIRONMENTALLY MONITORED COLLECTIONS SPACES THAT WILL ENABLE THE MUSEUM TO COLLECT TEMPERATURE AND HUMIDITY LEVELS FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE MUSEUM’S HISTORY. WITH THE ADDITION OF BLACKOUT BLINDS IN ALL THE COLLECTIONS SPACES, THE OBJECTS WILL NO LONGER BE AT RISK OF LIGHT DAMAGE AND THE OBJECTS’ STORAGE IN MORE STABLE CONDITIONS WILL BETTER PRESERVE THEM FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS.
description.4290: THE LIVINGSTON COUNTY HISTORICAL MUSEUM WILL IMPROVE THE STORAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 30,000 ARTIFACTS RELATING TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLE AND HABITANTS OF THE POST-COLONIAL FINGER LAKES REGION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE PURCHASING AND INSTALLING NEW COLLECTIONS STORAGE AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS, SECURITY, AND FIRE PREVENTION MEASURES. BUILDING UPON A DETAILED ASSESSMENT OF STORAGE NEEDS CONDUCTED BY AN INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM, PROJECT STAFF WILL ENGAGE EXPERTS TO ENSURE THAT THE EQUIPMENT WILL PROPERLY STORE COLLECTIONS AND MITIGATE FURTHER DAMAGE. THE REHOUSED MATERIAL WILL FACILITATE THE CREATION OF FUTURE EXHIBITS AND ALLOW STAFF TO ROTATE AND REST OBJECTS FROM THE COLLECTION.
description.4291: THE MUSEUM OF GLASS WILL ENSURE LONG-TERM CARE AND PUBLIC ACCESS TO BORN-DIGITAL AND DIGITIZED COLLECTIONS RELATED TO THE HISTORY OF GLASS AS A CONTEMPORARY ART MEDIUM. THE MUSEUM WILL HIRE A DIGITAL ARCHIVIST WHO WILL WORK WITH A CURATORIAL ASSISTANT TO DIGITIZE A PORTION OF THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTION, INCLUDING PHOTOGRAPHS AND VIDEO FOOTAGE OF GLASS ARTISTS. PROJECT STAFF WILL CREATE INSTITUTIONAL DIGITAL PRESERVATION PLANS AND IMPLEMENT A NEW DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. PROJECT STAFF WILL MAKE DIGITIZED COLLECTIONS ACCESSIBLE ONLINE FOR THE BENEFIT OF HISTORIANS, ART EDUCATORS, AND GLASS ARTISTS.
description.4292: THE MICHIGAN TECHNOLOGICAL UNIVERSITY ARCHIVES WILL UNDERTAKE A DATA MANAGEMENT PROJECT TO PRESERVE HISTORIC MINING RECORDS. THE UNIVERSITY ARCHIVES PRESERVE PAPER-BASED DRILLING DATA AND GEOLOGICAL CORE DESCRIPTIONS OF THE KEWEENAW COPPER MINING DISTRICT FOR AN ESTIMATED 600,000 FEET OF CORE FROM OVER 650 HOLES DRILLED FROM 1899 TO 1970. THE PROJECT WILL MATCH DESCRIPTIVE RECORDS WITH EXISTING CORES, ENHANCING THEIR HISTORICAL VALUE AND SCIENTIFIC USEFULNESS. THE PROJECT WILL WORK WITH A LONG-TIME PARTNER, GEOLOGIC PROFESSIONALS, UNIVERSITY STAFF, AND PAID GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO IDENTIFY, SCAN, AND PRESERVE THE ARCHIVED RECORDS. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THE INCREASED ACCESSIBILITY OF DIGITAL IMAGES ONLINE FOR A PUBLIC AUDIENCE, ENHANCED UTILITY OF DATA, AND THE PRESERVATION OF PRIMARY SOURCE MATERIALS.
description.4293: THE NEW YORK CITY LANDMARKS PRESERVATION COMMISSION WILL MAKE OBJECTS FROM ITS ARCHAEOLOGICAL COLLECTIONS ACCESSIBLE TO THE PUBLIC. THE COLLECTIONS INCLUDE TWO ARCHAEOLOGICAL EXCAVATIONS IN LOWER MANHATTAN EXCAVATED IN THE LATE 1970S AND EARLY 1980S: THE STADT HUYS BLOCK SITE AND 7 HANOVER SQUARE. FOR THE PROJECT, STAFF AND PAID GRADUATE INTERNS WILL PROCESS AND DIGITIZE APPROXIMATELY 20,595 DOCUMENTS. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, STAFF WILL CREATE TWO ONLINE EXHIBITIONS AND MAKE THE DIGITIZED COLLECTIONS AVAILABLE FOR USE BY THE PUBLIC AND RESEARCHERS.
description.4294: THE PROVIDENCE PERFORMING ARTS CENTER WILL CARRY OUT A RESTORATION OF ITS 1927 WURLITZER OPUS 1587 THEATER ORGAN. KNOWN AS THE VOICE OF PROVIDENCE, THE ORGAN IS ONE OF ONLY THREE INSTRUMENTS THE RUDOLPH WURLITZER COMPANY EQUIPPED (OUT OF MORE THAN 2,200 BUILT) WITH 21 RANKS AND AN ORNATE FIVE-MANUAL CONSOLE. STAFF WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTED RESTORATION FIRM TO CONDUCT A CONDITION ASSESSMENT, CLEAN AND VOICE EACH ORGAN PIPE, RESTORE THE RELAYS AND WINDING SYSTEM, AND REPAIR CLOTH AND LEATHER PARTS AS NEEDED. AS A RESULT OF THE PROJECT, THE ORGAN WILL BE FULLY RESTORED AND OPERABLE FOR COMMUNITY PERFORMANCE EVENTS.
description.4295: THE NATIONAL MUSEUM OF FOREST SERVICE HISTORY WILL INSTALL STORAGE CABINETRY, ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS, AND PHYSICAL SECURITY SYSTEMS IN ITS NEW NATIONAL CONSERVATION LEGACY CENTER, WHICH HAS A DEDICATED SPACE DESIGNED TO ENSURE PRESERVATION OF THE COLLECTION. THE MUSEUM’S 50,000 ITEM COLLECTION INCLUDES ARTIFACTS, LETTERS, REPORTS, MAPS, PHOTOGRAPHS, TOOLS, INSTRUMENTS AND PUBLISHED BOOKS THAT RELATE TO THE HISTORY OF THE NATIONAL FOREST SERVICE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE THE INSTALLATION OF A NEW HVAC SYSTEM AND MICROCLIMATE GENERATORS, FIRE DETECTION AND SUPPRESSION SYSTEMS, A SECURITY AND VIDEO SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM, AND A SPACE SAVING COLLECTION STORAGE SYSTEM. THE PROJECT WILL RESULT IN SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED STORAGE CONDITIONS FOR THE MUSEUM’S COLLECTIONS.
description.4335: THIS EDA INVESTMENT SUPPORTS THE CITY OF JACKSBORO WITH MAKING ROAD AND WATER INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS TO SUPPORT BUSINESS GROWTH IN THE JACKSBORO BUSINESS PARK IN JACK COUNTY, TEXAS.  THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT LOCAL BUSINESS EXPANSION WHILE ATTRACTING NEW EMPLOYERS TO THE REGION.  ONCE COMPLETED, THE PROJECT WILL HELP BETTER SERVE EXISTING INDUSTRIES AND CREATE GOOD-PAYING JOBS, WHICH WILL SPUR PRIVATE INVESTMENT AND STRENGTHEN THE REGIONAL ECONOMY.
description.4336:
CORRECTIONS AGENCIES ARE GRAPPLING WITH HOW TO CREATE SAFE AND HUMANE ENVIRONMENTS FOR PEOPLE WHO WORK, VISIT, AND ARE INCARCERATED IN PRISON; TO RECRUIT AND RETAIN STAFF; AND TO SUSTAIN EFFORTS THAT PROMOTE INCARCERATED PEOPLES SUCCESSFUL REENTRY TO THE COMMUNITY. TRANSFORMING THE CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES IN PRISONS IS ESSENTIAL TO ENHANCE SAFETY, IMPROVE THE DYNAMICS BETWEEN STAFF AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE, CREATE COMMUNITY AND A SENSE OF PURPOSE BEYOND CUSTODY AND CONTROL, AND SHAPE A CULTURE THAT CENTERS THE DIGNITY OF BOTH STAFF AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE. TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL PROBLEM OF TRANSFORMING PRISON CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES, THE VERA INSTITUTE OF JUSTICE (VERA) IS EXPANDING ITS GROUNDBREAKING WORK OF RESTORING PROMISE THROUGH A NEW PROJECT, DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY.

VERA WILL INSPIRE AND BROADLY SUPPORT THE CORRECTIONS FIELD TO TRANSFORM ITS CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES BY SELECTING EIGHT DIVERSE AGENCIES TO USE THE DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY FRAMEWORKTO ASSESS AND TRANSFORM THEIR POLICIES, TRAINING, AND RESOURCE ALLOCATIONS SO THEY ARE BETTER ALIGNED WITH DIGNITY AND TO ACHIEVE THEIR MISSION-CRITICAL GOALS.

THE TRANSFORMATION PROCESS WILL BE SUCCESSFUL BY LEVERAGING THE LEADERSHIP OF TRAINED CORRECTIONS PROFESSIONALS AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE AND PROCEEDING IN THREE STAGES: LEARNING AND STRATEGY DESIGN, CHANGE MANAGEMENT, AND SUSTAINABILITY. BEYOND THE EIGHT AGENCIES SELECTED TO GET SUPPORT WITH THE DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY FRAMEWORK, VERA WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT TO THE FIELD BY DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING RESOURCES AND RESPONDING TO AD HOC REQUESTS. VERA WILL PROACTIVELY BUILD FIELD KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY THROUGHOUT THE COURSE OF THE PROJECTMAINTAINING AN UP-TO-DATE REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE, BEST PRACTICES IN CORRECTIONS, AND INNOVATIONS IN CORRECTIONS CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES.

BY COMBINING THE EXPERTISE OF CORRECTIONS PROFESSIONALS AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE WITH VERA'S EXPERIENCE IN ON THE GROUND, EVIDENCE-BASED PRISON TRANSFORMATION WORK, DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY WILL BRING ABOUT MEANINGFUL AND SUSTAINABLE CHANGES IN THE PARTICIPATING CORRECTIONAL AGENCIES AND BUILD FIELD KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY FOR TRANSFORMING PRISON CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES.DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY WILL RESULT IN GREATER SAFETY FOR ALL, SUCCESSFUL RE-ENTRY FOR INCARCERATED PEOPLE, AND STAFF WHO ARE WELL AND HAVE PURPOSE.
description.4337: THE VERA INSTITUTE OF JUSTICE (VERA) WILL UTILIZE THIS FUNDING TO IMPLEMENT MUNICIPAL SAFETY HUBS, A NEW MODEL OF COMMUNITY-CENTERED SAFETY INFRASTRUCTURE IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT. VERA WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND SUBAWARDS TO THE ALBUQUERQUE (NEW MEXICO) COMMUNITY SAFETY DEPARTMENT AND THE CITY OF RICHMOND (CALIFORNIA) COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT, OFFICE OF NEIGHBORHOOD SAFETY TO CREATE AND SUSTAIN CIVILIAN-LED SAFETY HUBS. THESE SAFETY HUBS WILL UTILIZE A DATA-INFORMED, COMMUNITY-CENTERED, NEEDS-BASED PUBLIC HEALTH APPROACH TO ADDRESS PUBLIC SAFETY AND SOCIAL NEEDS, WITHOUT RELYING SOLELY ON TRADITIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT RESPONSES. THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON REFINING A CIVILIAN-LED PUBLIC SAFETY PLAN, EXPANDING CAPACITY FOR COLLECTING AND ANALYZING PUBLIC SAFETY DATA, AND FOSTERING ENGAGEMENT AND ACCOUNTABILITY TO SYSTEM IMPACTED COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS. THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON HIGH-NEED AREAS, ADDRESSING INCIDENTS RELATED TO MENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ISSUES, DISTURBANCES, AND SURVIVAL BEHAVIORS THAT TOO OFTEN BECOME CRIMINALIZED WHEN THE ONLY AVAILABLE RESPONSE IS LAW ENFORCEMENT (E.G. BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES, PUBLIC DISTURBANCES, LOITERING, UNWANTED PERSONS, PUBLIC INTOXICATION, AND TRESPASSING). ALSO, VERA WILL ENGAGE A DIVERSE CROSS-SECTION OF SYSTEM-IMPACTED RESIDENTS, CIVILIAN GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS TO DEVELOP STRATEGIES, MECHANISMS, AND MEASURES OF SUCCESS FOR GREATER COORDINATION, INTEGRATION, AND ACCOUNTABILITY TO SYSTEM-IMPACTED COMMUNITIES IN ADVANCING A SHARED VISION OF PUBLIC SAFETY.
description.4338:
THE VERA INSTITUTE OF JUSTICES (VERA) RESHAPING PROSECUTION INITIATIVE SEEKS FUNDING TO ADDRESS INEQUITIES IN ACCESS TO DIVERSION PROGRAMS FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED COMMUNITIES. VERA WILL PARTNER WITH PROSECUTORS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS THAT SERVE JUSTICE-INVOLVED COMMUNITIES TO BUILD OR EXPAND A DIVERSION PROGRAM THAT ADDRESSES A HEALTH AND SAFETY NEED IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY AND INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING FEATURES: (1) HAS NO AUTOMATIC EXCLUSIONS BASED ON CRIMINAL HISTORY, (2) HAS NO MANDATORY FINES OR FEES, (3) ADOPTS A NEEDS-BASED PUBLIC HEALTH APPROACH (AS OPPOSED TO AN OFFENSE-BASED APPROACH), (4) PROVIDES PROGRAMMING AND CASE MANAGEMENT THROUGH A COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATION, AND (5) CONSULTS JUSTICE-INVOLVED COMMUNITIES TO CREATE METRICS TO EVALUATE THE DIVERSION PROGRAM. EACH PARTNERSHIP WILL INCLUDE THREE MAIN COMPONENTS: COLLABORATION WITH A COMMUNITY PARTNER TO IMPLEMENT AND SUPPORT THEIR DIVERSION PROGRAM THROUGH RESEARCH SUPPORT AND OTHER RESOURCES, COLLABORATION WITH THE PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE TO IMPLEMENT RACIALLY EQUITABLE PROCESSES FOR DIVERSION REFERRALS, AND QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE RESEARCH TO COLLECT DATA FOR PROCESS AND OUTCOME EVALUATIONS OF DIVERSION PROGRAMS. VERA WILL ALSO PROVIDE SUBGRANTS TO THE COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO SUPPORT INCREASING DIVERSION CAPACITY.

EXPECTED PRODUCTS INCLUDE IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION TOOLS SUCH AS GUIDES AND FACT SHEETS FOR BUILDING AND EVALUATING THE SUCCESS OF THE PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED DIVERSION PROGRAMS; A REPORT TO SHARE LESSONS LEARNED AND QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE RESEARCH COLLECTED FROM THE PARTNERSHIPS, INCLUDING AROUND RECIDIVISM AND METRICS CHOSEN BY THE LOCAL COMMUNITY; AND A VERA-LED LEARNING COMMUNITY OF PAST PARTNERS TO SUPPORT SUSTAINABILITY AND HELP SPREAD SIMILAR DIVERSION PROGRAMS ACROSS THE FIELD.

description.4341:
CONTROL #: 2784-1745 NEW AWARD TO NEW MEXICO (LEAD-LOS ALAMOS NATIONAL LABORATORY)
FUNDING OPPORTUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT DE-FOA-0002784: EXPLORATORY TOPIC G: PRODUCTION OF GEOLOGIC HYDROGEN THROUGH STIMULATED MINERALOGICAL PROCESSES (STIMULATION)
PROJECT TITLE: GEOCHEMICAL AND HYDROMECHANICAL STIMULATION FOR REACTION ACCELERATION (GEOHYDRA) OF SERPENTINIZATION FOR IN SITU HYDROGEN PRODUCTION

THIS PROJECT AIMS TO MAXIMIZE HYDROGEN GENERATION BY SERPENTINIZATION OF ULTRAMAFIC ROCKS THROUGH A SYSTEMATIC STUDY THAT COMBINES LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS, HYDRO-CHEMICAL MODELS, AND THEORY DEVELOPMENT FOR UPSCALING. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROJECT WILL HELP TO UNLOCK THE VAST POTENTIAL OF GEOLOGICAL HYDROGEN GENERATION, PROVIDING A KEY TECHNOLOGY FOR CLEAN ENERGY TRANSITION.
